“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the six supernormal powers and sport with sovereign mastery, traveling from one buddha-field to another. In all the buddha-lands they pass through, there is no mention of the names ‘śrāvaka’ or ‘pratyekabuddha’; there are only those who practice the single vehicle (ekayāna) of true purity.”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva makes offerings to, reveres, honors, and praises the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all buddha-fields; as they practice the perfection of wisdom, it gradually increases, whereby they purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the six supernormal powers and sport with sovereign mastery, traveling from one buddha-field to another; the lifespan of the sentient beings in the buddha-lands they pass through is beyond calculation.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva makes offerings to, reveres, honors, and praises the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all buddha-fields; as they practice the perfection of wisdom, it gradually increases, whereby they purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, endowed with the six supernormal powers, travel through various worlds. There are worlds where even the names of the Three Jewels do not exist; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas go to those places to praise the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, causing sentient beings to give rise to profound pure faith, whereby they bring benefit and peace for a long night.”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, having passed away from this life, will be reborn in a buddha-field, where they will practice the bodhisattva path until attaining unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. “Śāriputra!

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, practice with courageous diligence; they attain the first dhyāna up to the fourth dhyāna; they attain the immeasurable of loving-kindness up to the immeasurable of equanimity; they attain the concentration of the sphere of infinite space up to the concentration of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; and they cultivate the ten powers of a buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is not born in the desire realm, is not born in the form realm, and is not born in the formless realm; rather, they are constantly born in places where they can benefit sentient beings, bringing them profit, peace, and happiness.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have already cultivated the six pāramitās and, from the moment they first resolve their minds [on awakening], enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (samyaktva-niyāma), and even attain the stage of non-retrogression.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, having previously cultivated the six pāramitās, are able from the very first production of the thought of awakening to successively realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes, and enter parinirvāṇa within the realm of great nirvāṇa without remainder.”
"After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma he has taught shall remain for one kalpa, or even for more than one kalpa, bringing benefit and happiness to boundless sentient beings. Śāriputra!"

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have already previously cultivated the six pāramitās; from the very first production of the thought of enlightenment, they are able to be in accord with the prajñāpāramitā. Surrounded before and behind by immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they travel through various buddha-fields, going from one buddha-field to another, making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, while maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom and attain the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; sporting therein, they first enter the first dhyāna.”
Emerging from the first dhyāna, one enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, one enters the second dhyāna;
emerging from the second dhyāna, one enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, one enters the third dhyāna;
emerging from the third dhyāna, one enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, one enters...
From the fourth dhyāna, he emerges and enters the attainment of cessation; from the attainment of cessation, he emerges and enters the sphere of infinite space;
from the sphere of infinite space, he emerges and enters the attainment of cessation;
from the attainment of cessation, he emerges and enters the sphere of infinite consciousness; from the sphere of infinite consciousness, he emerges and enters the attainment of cessation.
Emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the sphere of nothingness; emerging from the sphere of nothingness, he enters the attainment of cessation;
emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
emerging from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the first dhyāna.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, through the skillful means of practicing the perfection of wisdom, exercises mastery in entering, emerging from, proceeding in forward and reverse order, and leaping over the various sublime concentrations at will.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have already attained the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and although they have already cultivated the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), yet do not grasp at the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor the fruit of a once-returner, nor the fruit of a non-returner, nor the fruit of an arhat, nor the enlightenment of a solitary buddha, nor unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they cause sentient beings to give rise to the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, enabling them to attain the fruit of stream-entry up to the fruit of arhatship or pratyekabuddha enlightenment;
or they cause sentient beings to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha up to all-aspect omniscience, enabling them to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra! This wisdom of the fruits of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is itself the patience of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Śāriputra!
"You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells on the stage of non-retrogression; being in union with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are capable of such deeds. Śāriputra!"

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six pāramitās, purify the Tuṣita heaven; it should be known that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will certainly become buddhas within this Bhadrakalpa.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom who, although they have already attained the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; who have already attained the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and who have already cultivated the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); whose minds are directed toward awakening and are never weary or negligent; yet they have not yet fully realized the noble truths in the present or the future.”
"Śāriputra, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by only one more birth. Śāriputra!"

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections, traveling from one buddha-field to another throughout all worlds, purifying buddha-lands and establishing sentient beings in unexcelled enlightenment.
"Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva must pass through immeasurable and incalculable great kalpas before they realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. Śāriputra!"

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in the six perfections, constantly and diligently exerting themselves to benefit sentient beings; they never speak words that lead to what is meaningless, nor do they give rise to actions of the body or mind that lead to what is meaningless.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections, constantly and diligently exerting themselves to benefit sentient beings; they travel from one buddha-field to another, severing for all sentient beings the paths to the three evil realms.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although fully established in the six pāramitās, always take the perfection of generosity as their foremost practice. They courageously cultivate all the bodhisattva deeds, bestowing upon sentient beings every requisite for happiness without ever ceasing. To those who need food, they give food; to those who need drink, they give drink; to those who need vehicles, they give vehicles; to those who need clothing, they give clothing. Flowers, incense, necklaces, dwellings, bedding, couches, lamps, wealth, grain, and precious gems—whatever articles for sustaining life they require, they provide and bestow them all.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although fully dwelling in the six pāramitās, always take the śīla-pāramitā as their preeminent guide. They courageously cultivate all bodhisattva practices, possessing the sublime discipline of body, speech, and mind, and they exhort all sentient beings to likewise cultivate such discipline so that it may be swiftly perfected.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, while fully abiding in the six pāramitās, always take the pāramitā of patience as their foremost guide. They courageously cultivate all bodhisattva practices, remain far removed from all states of mind such as anger and resentment, and exhort all sentient beings to likewise cultivate such patience so that they may swiftly bring it to full perfection.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they fully abide in the six pāramitās, always take the pāramitā of diligence as their preeminent guide. They courageously cultivate all bodhisattva practices and fully practice all wholesome dharmas; they also exhort all sentient beings to cultivate such diligence, causing them to swiftly reach fulfillment.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although fully established in the six pāramitās, always take the dhyāna-pāramitā as their foremost; they courageously cultivate all bodhisattva practices and fully cultivate all supreme śamatha, while also exhorting all sentient beings to practice such sublime samādhi so that they may swiftly reach fulfillment.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although fully abiding in the six pāramitās, always take the prajñāpāramitā as their foremost guide. They courageously cultivate all bodhisattva practices and fully cultivate all forms of vipaśyanā. They also exhort all sentient beings to cultivate such supreme wisdom, causing them to swiftly reach fulfillment.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, manifest emanation bodies like those of a Buddha and enter throughout the realms of hell, animals, the hungry ghosts, humans, and devas, preaching the true Dharma to them in accordance with their respective languages.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), manifest transformation bodies like those of a Buddha that travel throughout the worlds of the Ganges-sand in the ten directions, proclaiming the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields;

they listen to the sublime Dharma at the abodes of various Buddhas, making offerings, paying respect, honoring, and praising them; and having thoroughly surveyed the subtle, pure characteristics of the most excellent buddha-fields in the ten directions, they themselves give rise to supremely adorned and pure buddha-fields, wherein they establish great bodhisattvas bound to only one more birth (*ekajāti-pratibaddha*), instructing them to swiftly realize unsurpassed awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six pāramitās, achieve the thirty-two marks of a great man, and possess faculties that are sharp, pure, and dignified. All sentient beings who see them feel love and respect; through this, they provide guidance according to their faculties and inclinations, leading them to gradually realize the nirvāṇa of the three vehicles.”
In this way, Śāriputra,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should train in the purification of the actions of body, speech, and mind.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections; although they have attained sharp and keen faculties, they do not hold themselves in high regard nor disparage others.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, constantly abide in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline; until they attain the stage of non-retrogression, they never fall into the evil destinies at any time.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their initial generation of the mind of awakening until they have attained the stage of non-retrogression, never abandon the ten paths of wholesome action.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfections of generosity and ethical discipline, become wheel-turning kings endowed with the seven treasures. They transform beings through the Dharma and not through what is contrary to the Dharma, establishing sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action and also relieving the destitute with material wealth.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfection of generosity and ethical discipline, become universal monarchs for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of lifetimes. They encounter immeasurable hundreds of thousands of buddhas, making offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them, and they give away both internal and external things without regarding it as difficult.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), constantly act as lamps of Dharma for sentient beings blinded by false views. They also maintain this illumination to constantly illuminate themselves, and until they reach unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), they never abandon this illumination of Dharma.”
By these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly brings forth all the buddha-dharmas in the present. Therefore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, there is no possibility for any blameworthy karma of body, speech, or mind to arise even for a moment.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
what are called the faulty bodily, verbal, and mental actions of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Buddha said:
“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:”
"This is the body; it is because of this that I initiate bodily action.
This is speech; it is because of this that I initiate verbal action.
This is the mind; it is because of this that I initiate mental action."
“Śāriputra! These are called the faulty bodily, verbal, and mental actions of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Śāriputra!”

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the body or bodily action, they do not apprehend speech or vocal action, and they do not apprehend the mind or mental action.

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom were to obtain a body, speech, and mind, as well as the actions of body, speech, and mind, and should then give rise to a mind of stinginess and greed, a mind of violating the precepts, a mind of anger and resentment, a mind of laziness, a mind of distraction, or a mind of evil wisdom—if such minds arise, they are not called bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Therefore, Śāriputra, it is impossible for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom to give rise to such a thought. Śāriputra!
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections are able to purify the three types of coarse heaviness of body, speech, and mind.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying,
“World-Honored One!”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness (dauṣṭhulya) of body,
speech, and mind? The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!”

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the body nor the bodily dysfunctions; they do not apprehend speech nor the vocal dysfunctions; they do not apprehend the mind nor the mental dysfunctions.
Śāriputra! In this way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are able to purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness of body, speech, and mind.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first production of the thought of enlightenment, constantly and fully upholds the ten paths of wholesome action, does not give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha, and always gives rise to great compassion toward sentient beings."
"Śāriputra! I also say that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness (dauṣṭhulya) of body, speech, and mind. Śāriputra!"
Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) to purify the path to enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"What is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s path to awakening?
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend any physical, verbal, or mental actions, nor the three types of coarse heaviness (*dausthulya*). They do not apprehend the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, or the perfection of wisdom. They do not apprehend the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or the vehicle of the bodhisattvas’ perfectly complete awakening.
Śāriputra! This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s path to awakening. Why is this?
Because one does not apprehend anything among all phenomena by means of the path to enlightenment.
"Śāriputra, furthermore,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections and proceed upon the path to enlightenment such that no one can obstruct them."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
for what reason is it that when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, no one is able to obstruct them as they proceed upon the path to enlightenment?”
The Buddha said: “Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they do not cling to the aggregate of form (rūpa-skandha), nor do they cling to the aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness (vedanā-, saṃjñā-, saṃskāra-, and vijñāna-skandha).”
They do not cling to the sense-base of the eye, nor to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
they do not cling to the sense-base of forms, nor to the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;

they do not cling to the eye-element, the form-element, or the eye-consciousness-element; they do not cling to the ear-element, the sound-element, or the ear-consciousness-element; they do not cling to the nose-element, the odor-element, or the nose-consciousness-element; they do not cling to the tongue-element, the taste-element, or the tongue-consciousness-element; they do not cling to the body-element, the tangible-element, or the body-consciousness-element; they do not cling to the mind-element, the mental-phenomena-element, or the mind-consciousness-element.
They do not cling to the noble truth of suffering, nor do they cling to the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, or the path;

they do not cling to ignorance, nor do they cling to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

they do not cling to the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they cling to the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.

They do not cling to the perfection of generosity; they do not cling to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. They do not cling to the ten powers of a Buddha;

they do not cling to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects.

They do not cling to the fruit of stream-entry; they do not cling to the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; they do not cling to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; they do not cling to any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and they do not cling to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Śāriputra! By these causes and conditions, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, they increase and blaze forth upon the path to enlightenment, such that none can obstruct them.
“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfection of wisdom, are able to swiftly fulfill all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).”

Because they have accomplished supreme wisdom, they never fall into the various perilous and evil realms, nor do they receive the bodies of lowly humans or devas; they are forever free from poverty, their physical forms are endowed with all faculties and their countenances are upright and handsome, and they are revered and loved by devas, humans, asuras, and others.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the supreme wisdom accomplished by a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

By accomplishing this wisdom, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; they hear all the true Dharma taught by those Buddhas; they see all the assemblies of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and the Saṅgha therein; and they also see the signs of the adornments of those lands.”

By virtue of accomplishing this wisdom, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not give rise to the notion of a world, do not give rise to the notion of a Buddha, do not give rise to the notion of the Dharma, do not give rise to the notion of the Śrāvaka Saṃgha, do not give rise to the notion of the Bodhisattva Saṃgha, do not give rise to the notion of a Pratyekabuddha, do not give rise to the notion of a self, do not give rise to the notion of a non-self, and do not give rise to the notion of the adornment of a buddha-field.

By virtue of accomplishing this wisdom, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, although they practice the perfection of generosity, do not apprehend the perfection of generosity; although they practice the perfection of ethical discipline, they do not apprehend the perfection of ethical discipline;
although they practice the perfection of patience, they do not apprehend the perfection of patience;
and although they practice the perfection of diligence, they do not apprehend the perfection of diligence.
Although they practice the perfection of meditative concentration, they do not apprehend the perfection of meditative concentration;
although they practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the perfection of wisdom;
although they practice the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not apprehend the four foundations of mindfulness.
Even though they practice the eight branches of the noble path, they do not apprehend the eight branches of the noble path;
even though they practice the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not apprehend the ten powers of a Buddha;
and so on, up to even though they practice the knowledge of all aspects, they do not apprehend the knowledge of all aspects.
Śāriputra! This is called the supreme wisdom attained by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

By attaining this wisdom, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to swiftly fulfill all Buddha-dharmas; although they know all dharmas, they do not apprehend any dharma, because their intrinsic nature is empty.

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, are able to purify the five eyes, namely: the flesh eye, the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the dharma eye, and the buddha eye.”
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the pure fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who see a hundred yojanas with their fleshly eyes; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas...”
Some bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see two hundred yojanas with their fleshly eyes; some bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see three hundred yojanas with their fleshly eyes;
some bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, and even up to a thousand yojanas with their fleshly eyes;
and some bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see one Jambudvīpa with their fleshly eyes.
On one continent, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eyes see two great continents;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eyes see three great continents; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eyes see four great continents;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eyes see a small thousand-world system; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas... [and so forth].
While some bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see a medium chiliocosm with their physical eyes, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who see a trichiliocosm with their physical eyes. Śāriputra!
"This is called the pure fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is the pure divine eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!..."

The divine eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Four Great Kings; it sees everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin heavens; it sees everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Brahmakāyika heaven, and so on, up to seeing everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who see with the divine eye what cannot be seen by the divine eyes of any being from the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.

Śāriputra! With their divine eye, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to see sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions passing away from here and being reborn there.
“Śāriputra! This is called the pure divine eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the pure eye of wisdom of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Buddha said:
"Śāriputra!

The wisdom-eye of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma—whether conditioned or unconditioned, with outflows or without outflows, mundane or supramundane, faulty or faultless, defiled or pure, with form or formless, resistant or non-resistant, past, future, or present, bound to the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm, wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate, to be abandoned by seeing, to be abandoned by cultivation, or not to be abandoned, whether it be of the stage of training, the stage beyond training, or neither training nor beyond training—even down to all dharmas in their intrinsic nature or their specific distinctions.
Śāriputra! With this wisdom-eye, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma that can be seen, heard, sensed, or cognized.
"Śāriputra! This is called the pure eye of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Buddha said:
“Śāriputra! The Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva can know, as they truly are, the various distinctions among individuals:
this one is a follower by faith (śraddhānusārin), this one is a follower by dharma (dharmānusārin), and this one practices the signless (animitta).”
"This dwells in emptiness; this dwells in signlessness; this dwells in wishlessness. This gives rise to the five faculties by means of the gate of liberation of emptiness;

from the five faculties, it gives rise to uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from uninterrupted concentration, it gives rise to the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*). By means of the knowledge and vision of liberation, one eternally severs the three fetters—namely, the view of a self-identity (*satkāya-dṛṣṭi*), adherence to precepts and observances (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), and doubt (*vicikitsā*). Because of the eternal severance of these three fetters, one attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*).
Through the path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one attenuates sensual desire and ill-will to attain the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmi-phala*)."
Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one permanently abandons sensual desire and ill-will to attain the fruit of a non-returner (*anāgāmiphala*).

Furthermore, by means of the further superior path of cultivation, one permanently abandons the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*)—namely, desire for the realm of form (*rūparāga*), desire for the formless realm (*ārūpyarāga*), ignorance (*avidyā*), pride (*māna*), and restlessness (*auddhatya*)—and because of this permanent abandonment of the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms, one attains the fruit of an arhat (*arhattvaphala*).

This occurs by means of the door of signless liberation (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*) giving rise to the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*), and from the five faculties giving rise to the uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*), until the permanent abandonment of the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms results in the attainment of the fruit of an arhat.

This arises from the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha), whereby the five faculties (pañcendriya) are produced; from the five faculties, the immediate concentration (ānantarya-samādhi) is produced, and so on until the five higher fetters (pañcordhvabhāgīya-saṃyojana) are permanently severed and the fruit of arhatship is attained.
It is likewise by means of two or three [faculties].
"Śāriputra! This is called the pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
The Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva can know, as they truly are, that all phenomena subject to origination are phenomena subject to cessation; by knowing this, he attains the five faculties.
“Śāriputra! This is called the pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”

The Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva can know, as it truly is, that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has first resolved upon the mind of awakening, practices the perfection of generosity up to the practice of the perfection of wisdom, and has accomplished the faculty of faith and the faculty of diligence; through skillful means, their mental experience and physical existence increase in wholesome dharmas.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva may be born into a great kṣatriya clan, or a great brāhmaṇa clan, or a great householder clan, or a great merchant clan; or they may be born among the gods of the Four Great Kings, up to and including being born among the gods who control the creations of others. Abiding in those realms, they bring sentient beings to maturity; according to what sentient beings delight in, they bestow various supreme and wonderful articles of enjoyment to purify buddha-fields. They make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and do not fall into the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, never regressing until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
"Śāriputra! This is called the pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

The Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva can know, as it truly is, that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already received the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while that bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet received the prediction;

that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained non-retrogression regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while that bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained non-retrogression;
and that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already reached the stage of non-retrogression, while that bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet reached the stage of non-retrogression.
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already perfected the supernormal powers; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet perfected the supernormal powers.

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has perfected the supernormal powers, he is able to travel to Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; whereas because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet perfected the supernormal powers, he is unable to travel to Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained the supernormal powers; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained the supernormal powers."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained superior faculties; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained superior faculties.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already purified a buddha-field; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet purified a buddha-field.
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already matured sentient beings; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet matured sentient beings.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained great vows; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained great vows.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already been praised by all Buddhas; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet been praised by all Buddhas."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already drawn near to the Buddhas; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet drawn near to the Buddhas.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has an immeasurable lifespan; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has a measurable lifespan.
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains awakening, the community of bhikṣus will be immeasurable; when this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains awakening, the community of bhikṣus will be measurable.
When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva attains awakening, there will be a community of bodhisattvas; when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva attains awakening, there will be no community of bodhisattvas.
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva exclusively cultivates practices for the benefit of others; this bodhisattva-mahāsattva concurrently cultivates practices for his own benefit.
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva undergoes difficult and arduous practices; this bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not undergo difficult and arduous practices.
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by only one more birth; this bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by many births.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already entered his final existence; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet entered his final existence.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already sat upon the seat of sublime awakening; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet sat upon the seat of sublime awakening."
“Śāriputra, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will have Māras come to test him; that bodhisattva mahāsattva will not have Māras come to test him.
Śāriputra, this is called the pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the pure Buddha-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”

The Buddha said, “Śāriputra! Immediately following the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, they enter the diamond-like samādhi (vajropama-samādhi), attain all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā), and achieve the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, unobstructed and unimpeded liberation, and the buddha-eye.”

By means of this Buddha-eye, the bodhisattva mahāsattva transcends the sphere of wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; there is nothing he does not see, nothing he does not hear, nothing he does not perceive, and nothing he does not cognize, as he perceives all characteristics within all phenomena.
Śāriputra! This is called the pure Buddha-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Śāriputra!
“Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they then obtain such a pure Buddha-eye.”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain such pure five eyes, they should diligently cultivate the six pāramitās. Why is this?
Because these six pāramitās encompass all wholesome dharmas—namely, all the wholesome dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas.
“Śāriputra! Suppose someone were to ask the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha:
‘Speaking in truth, what dharma is able to encompass all wholesome dharmas?’”
The Buddha answered directly:
"It is what is called Prajñāpāramitā. Why is this so?
This Prajñāpāramitā is the mother of all wholesome dharmas, for it is able to give birth to the five pāramitās, the five eyes, and all other meritorious qualities.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain the five pure eyes, they should study the perfection of wisdom;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, they should study these five pure eyes in this way.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in these five pure eyes in this way, they will certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

“Śāriputra, furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are able to bring forth the perfection of the six superknowledges (abhijñā), namely: the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of supernormal powers; the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of the divine ear; the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of others’ minds; the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of recollecting past lives; the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of the divine eye; and the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows.”
Then, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,

what is the supernormal power of the realization of knowledge (ṛddhividhi-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) that a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings forth when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
The Buddha said: “Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of miraculous feats (*ṛddhividhi-jñāna-sākṣātkriyā-abhijñā*), capable of performing various great miraculous transformations. These include: shaking the earth and all other things throughout the worlds of the ten directions, each as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā; transforming one into many and many into one; appearing and disappearing with rapidity and without obstruction; passing straight through mountain precipices, walls, and barriers as if through space; traveling through the air like a flying bird; emerging from and submerging into the earth as if in water; walking upon water as if on land; emitting smoke and flames from the body like a blazing high plateau; pouring forth streams of water from the body like melting snow-capped peaks; eclipsing the light of the sun and moon—whose divine merit and majestic power are otherwise difficult to withstand—by stroking them with the hand; and even attaining mastery over rebirth in the Śuddhāvāsa heavens. Such miraculous transformations are infinite in number.

"Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such supernormal powers of the knowledge of miraculous transformations, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal power of the realization of miraculous transformations, nor to the phenomena of the supernormal power of the realization of miraculous transformations, nor to the one who can attain such supernormal power of the realization of miraculous transformations. He is without attachment in both clinging and non-clinging."
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are detached from intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form this thought:
"I shall now manifest the supernormal power of the knowledge of psychic travel for my own amusement," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).

"Śāriputra! This is called the supernormal power of the realization of knowledge of the sphere of psychic power (ṛddhividhi-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) that a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings forth when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

What is the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine ear (divyaśrotra-abhijñā) that is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear-knowledge, which is supremely pure and surpasses that of humans and devas; they are able to hear, as it truly is, the various sounds of sentient and insentient beings throughout worlds in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”

That is to say, they are able to hear everywhere, without obstruction or hindrance, all such sounds—whether great or small—as the sounds of all hells, animals, the realm of hungry ghosts, humans, and devas; the sounds of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and all Buddhas; the sounds of censuring and reviling birth-and-death (saṃsāra), praising and extolling nirvāṇa, turning one’s back on the conditioned (saṃskṛta), and proceeding toward enlightenment (bodhi); the sounds of loathing the outflows (āsrava) and rejoicing in the outflow-free (anāsrava); the sounds of extolling the Triple Gem, subduing false paths, debating and discerning the truth, chanting the sūtras, exhorting the severance of unwholesome dharmas, causing the cultivation of wholesome dharmas, rescuing from suffering and calamity, and offering congratulations and comfort with joy. All such sounds, whether large or small, they can hear universally, free from any impediment.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such a function of the divine ear, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal power of the realization of knowledge of the divine ear, nor does he cling to the matters of the supernormal power of the realization of knowledge of the divine ear, nor does he cling to the one who can attain such a supernormal power of the realization of knowledge of the divine ear. He is without attachment in both attachment and non-attachment.”
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are detached from intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form the thought:
"I shall now manifest the supernormal power of the divine ear for my own amusement," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Śāriputra! This is called the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine ear, which is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

What is the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of others' minds (paracittajñāna-abhijñā) that a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings forth when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal power of the knowledge of others’ minds, and are able to know, as it truly is, each of the ten directions...”
Regarding the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—namely, he thoroughly knows the minds of other sentient beings:
if they have a mind with attachment, he knows it as it truly is, as a mind with attachment; if they are free from attachment, he knows it as it truly is, as a mind free from attachment;
if they have a mind with aversion, he knows it as it truly is, as a mind with aversion; if they are free from aversion...

He knows truly when the mind is free from hatred; if there is a deluded mind, he knows truly that there is a deluded mind, and if it is free from delusion, he knows truly that it is free from delusion.

If there is a mind of craving, he knows truly that there is a mind of craving, and if it is free from craving, he knows truly that it is free from craving. If there is a mind of grasping, he knows truly that there is a mind of grasping.
If the mind is free from grasping, one knows the mind as it truly is, free from grasping; if the mind is concentrated, one knows the concentrated mind as it truly is;
if the mind is scattered, one knows the scattered mind as it truly is; if the mind is small, one knows the small mind as it truly is;
if the mind is great, one knows the great mind as it truly is; if the mind is uplifted, one knows the uplifted mind as it truly is; if the mind is depressed...
He knows the inferior mind as it truly is; he knows the tranquil mind as it truly is as a tranquil mind;
he knows the untranquil mind as it truly is as an untranquil mind; he knows the agitated mind as it truly is as an agitated mind;
he knows the non-agitated mind as it truly is as a non-agitated mind; he knows the concentrated mind as it truly is as a concentrated mind; and if...
He knows an unconcentrated mind as an unconcentrated mind; he knows a liberated mind as a liberated mind, and an unliberated mind as an unliberated mind;
he knows a tainted mind as a tainted mind, and an untainted mind as an untainted mind; he knows a flawed mind as a flawed mind...
He knows, as it truly is, a mind that has a flaw; he knows, as it truly is, a mind without a flaw;
he knows, as it truly is, a mind that is surpassed; he knows, as it truly is, a mind that is unsurpassed.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such an application of the knowledge of others’ minds, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of others’ minds, nor to the phenomena of realizing the knowledge of others’ minds, nor to the one who is able to attain such a realization of the knowledge of others’ minds. He is without attachment in both clinging and non-clinging.”
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because their intrinsic nature is detached, and because their intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form the thought:
"I shall now induce the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds for my own amusement," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Śāriputra! This is called the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of others' minds, which is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom."

In the fourth section of the third chapter, "The Chapter on Contemplation," of the second division,
Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“What is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives when practicing the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of the realization of recollecting past lives, and are able to truly and accurately recollect all the various events of past lives of all sentient beings throughout as many worlds in each of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.

That is to say, one recollects the past lives of oneself or others for the duration of one moment of mind, ten moments of mind, a hundred moments of mind, a thousand moments of mind, or many hundreds of thousands of moments of mind;

or again, one recollects the past lives for the duration of one day, ten days, a hundred days, a thousand days, or many hundreds of thousands of days; or again, one recollects for the duration of one...
He recollects his various past lives—whether for one month, ten months, a hundred months, a thousand months, or many hundreds of thousands of months;
or again, he recollects his various past lives for one year, ten years, a hundred years, a thousand years, or many hundreds of thousands of years;
or again, he recollects his various past lives for one eon, ten eons, a hundred eons, or a thousand eons.
...the events of former abodes spanning many hundreds of thousands of kalpas, even up to immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas; or again,
recollecting as they wish all the events of former abodes belonging to the past limit—
namely, at such a time, in such a place, with such a name, such a clan, of such a kind, and such a...
They ate such food, dwelt for such a long time, had such a life span, lived for such a duration,
experienced such pleasure, and underwent such suffering; they passed away from that place and were reborn here,
and having passed away from here, they were reborn there— with such physical appearance and such speech.
Whether briefly or in detail, whether concerning himself or others, he is able to recollect all matters of past lives.

"Śāriputra, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such power of knowledge regarding past lives, he does not exalt himself therein. He does not cling to the nature of the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives; he does not cling to the objects of the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives; he does not cling to the one who attains the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives. Regarding both clinging and non-clinging, he is entirely without attachment."
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because their intrinsic nature is detached, and because their intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form this thought:
"I shall now induce the supernormal power of knowledge of past lives for my own amusement," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).
"Śāriputra! This is called the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives, which is induced when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom."
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the supernormal power of the realization of the divine eye-wisdom that a bodhisattva mahāsattva elicits when practicing the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the superknowledge of the realization of the divine eye, which is most excellent, pure, and surpasses that of human eyes. They are able to see, as it truly is, the various forms and appearances of sentient and non-sentient beings throughout worlds in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. That is to say, they universally see all classes of sentient beings at the time of death and at the time of birth—their beautiful forms and coarse forms, their rebirth in happy realms or miserable realms, whether superior or inferior—and all such various forms and appearances.”

Therefore, one further understands that sentient beings undergo various distinctions in birth according to the power and function of their karma: there are those who have accomplished misconduct of body, accomplished misconduct of speech, and accomplished misconduct of mind; who, due to the causes and conditions of slandering the noble ones and holding wrong views, at the dissolution of the body after death, shall fall into the evil destinies—either being born in hell, or as an animal, or in the realm of hungry ghosts, or among the base and wicked sentient beings of the borderlands, where they undergo various sufferings.

Likewise, there are those who have accomplished good conduct of body, accomplished good conduct of speech, and accomplished good conduct of mind; who, due to the causes and conditions of praising the noble ones and holding right views, at the dissolution of the body after death, shall ascend to the happy destinies—either being born in the heavens or among human beings, where they experience various joys.
In this way, he knows as they truly are the various distinctions in the fruits received by sentient beings according to their diverse types of karma.

"Śāriputra, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such functions of the divine eye, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal knowledge of realizing the divine eye, nor to the matters of the supernormal knowledge of realizing the divine eye, nor to the one who is able to attain such supernormal knowledge of realizing the divine eye. He is without attachment to either attachment or non-attachment."
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because their intrinsic nature is detached, and because their intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form this thought:
"I shall now manifest the supernormal power of the divine eye for my own amusement," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Śāriputra! This is called the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine eye, which is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

What is the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows (āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) that is induced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?"
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣaya-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā*), and are able to know, as it truly is, whether the outflows of all sentient beings— whether themselves or others— in all worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have been exhausted or not.”
This supernormal power relies upon the diamond-like concentration (*vajropama-samādhi*); it is only when the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of all obstacles are severed that it becomes perfected.
When the stage of a non-retrogressive Bodhisattva is attained, it is also termed the "exhaustion of all outflows" (*āsrava-kṣaya*), because they never again arise or manifest.

Although the bodhisattva has attained this supernormal power of the exhaustion of outflows, they do not fall to the level of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but proceed solely toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, as they no longer seek any other benefit or purpose.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such application of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣayajñāna*), he does not exalt himself therein; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the exhaustion of outflows, nor to the matter of realizing the exhaustion of outflows, nor to the one who is able to attain such realization of the exhaustion of outflows. He is without attachment in both attachment and non-attachment.”
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form this thought:

"I shall now induce the supernormal power of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows for my own enjoyment," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).

"Śāriputra! This is called the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the exhaustion of outflows (āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are able to fulfill and purify the six perfections of supernatural power (ṣaḍ-abhijñā-pāramitā). Because these six perfections of supernatural power are fulfilled and purified, they then realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfection of generosity and purify the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, because through ultimate emptiness they do not give rise to a mind of either giving or stinginess.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline and purify the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, because through ultimate emptiness they do not give rise to thoughts of either upholding or violating ethical discipline.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfection of patience and purify the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, because through ultimate emptiness they do not give rise to thoughts of compassion, anger, or resentment.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfection of diligence to purify the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, because they do not give rise to thoughts of exertion or indolence due to ultimate emptiness.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*) and purify the path of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), because they do not give rise to a mind of either tranquility or distraction due to ultimate emptiness (*atyantaśūnyatā*).”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfection of wisdom and purify the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, because through ultimate emptiness they do not give rise to a mind of either wisdom or delusion.

“Śāriputra! “Śāriputra! “Śāriputra! “Śāriputra, furthermore,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfections of generosity and meditative concentration, purifying the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, because through ultimate emptiness they do not give rise to thoughts of stinginess regarding giving or distraction from tranquility.”

“Śāriputra! “Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, and patience, purifying the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects; for, by means of ultimate emptiness, they do not give rise to thoughts of giving or stinginess, observing precepts or violating them, or compassion or anger.”

“Śāriputra! This is because, through ultimate emptiness, they do not give rise to thoughts of giving versus stinginess, compassion versus anger, or diligence versus indolence.”

This is because, through ultimate emptiness, they do not give rise to thoughts of giving or stinginess, observing precepts or violating them, compassion or malice, or vigor or indolence.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfections of generosity, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration, purifying the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects. This is because, through ultimate emptiness, they do not give rise to thoughts of observing precepts or violating precepts, loving-kindness or malice, diligence or indolence, tranquility or distraction, or wisdom or delusion.”

“Śāriputra! Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, thereby purifying the path of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects. This is because, through ultimate emptiness, they do not give rise to thoughts of giving or stinginess, observing precepts or violating them, loving-kindness or malice, compassion or anger, diligence or laziness, tranquility or distraction, or wisdom or delusion.”
"Thus it is, Śāriputra!"

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they abide in the six perfections and purify the path of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). Because of ultimate emptiness, they are without giving or parsimony; without observance or violation of precepts; without compassion or malice; without diligence or laziness; without tranquility or distraction; and without wisdom or delusion. They do not cling to giving or parsimony; they do not cling to observance or violation of precepts; they do not cling to compassion or malice; they do not cling to diligence or laziness; they do not cling to tranquility or distraction; and they do not cling to wisdom or delusion.

Śāriputra! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not become attached to those who practice generosity or to those who are stingy; he does not become attached to those who maintain the precepts or to those who violate them; he does not become attached to those who possess loving-kindness and compassion or to those who harbor anger and malice; he does not become attached to those who are diligent and energetic or to those who are lazy and indolent; he does not become attached to those who are tranquil and composed or to those who are distracted and agitated; and he does not become attached to those who possess wisdom or to those who are foolish and ignorant.
Śāriputra! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is attached to neither attachment nor non-attachment. Why is this?
Because all phenomena are ultimately empty,
Śāriputra, at that time,
this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not cling to revilement or praise, does not cling to harm or benefit, and does not cling to contempt or respect.
Why is this? Because within ultimate emptiness, there are no phenomena of reviling or praising; no phenomena of harming or benefiting; and no phenomena of contempt or respect.

Śāriputra! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not become attached to those who revile or praise him; he does not become attached to those who harm or benefit him; and he does not become attached to those who treat him with contempt or respect.
Why is this? Because within ultimate emptiness, there is no one who reviles or praises; there is no one who harms or benefits; and there is no one who treats with contempt or reverence.
Śāriputra! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is attached to neither attachment nor non-attachment. Why is this?
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* forever severs all attachment and non-attachment. "Śāriputra!
When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the *prajñāpāramitā*, the merit they obtain is supreme and most wondrous, such that it is not possessed by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

Śāriputra! Once this bodhisattva mahāsattva has thus perfected these merits, he is further able to bring all sentient beings to maturity through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) and to purify the buddha-fields. He thereby attains the purification of the path of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and is swiftly able to realize the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom practices the perfection of wisdom, they give rise to a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings. Having given rise to a mind of equanimity, they give rise to a mind of benefit and happiness toward all sentient beings. Having given rise to a mind of benefit and happiness, they attain equanimity regarding the nature of all phenomena (*dharmatā*). Having attained equanimity regarding the nature of phenomena, they establish all sentient beings within the state of equanimity regarding the nature of all phenomena."

“Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, in this present life, receives the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas of the ten directions, and is also held in the respect and affection of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.”

Śāriputra! In whatever place these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are born, their eyes shall never see unpleasant forms; their ears shall never hear unpleasant sounds; their noses shall never smell unpleasant odors; their tongues shall never taste unpleasant flavors; their bodies shall never feel unpleasant tangibles; and their minds shall never apprehend unpleasant phenomena.
“Śāriputra! These bodhisattva mahāsattvas shall never regress from unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.

When the Buddha spoke these words regarding the benefits obtained by those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom, three hundred bhikṣus in the assembly immediately rose from their seats, took the robes they were wearing and offered them to the Buddha, and all resolved to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled, and from his mouth issued rays of light of various colors.
Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his left shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"For what cause and for what reason do you manifest this smile?
When a Great Sage manifests a smile, there must surely be a cause and condition. We pray that you will look upon us with compassion and deign to explain it for us!
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“Three hundred bhikṣus rose from their seats; from this point forward, during sixty-one kalpas known as the Star-like Kalpas, they shall all become buddhas with one and the same name: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān—namely, Mahādhvajaketu.”
"After these bhikṣus have cast off this body, they shall be reborn in the eastern land of Akṣobhya Buddha, where they will cultivate the bodhisattva practices under that Buddha.
Furthermore, sixty thousand devaputras, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, all resolved to attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

The World-Honored One prophesied that he would, within the Dharma of the Tathāgata Maitreya, leave the household life with pure faith and exclusively cultivate the holy life; the Tathāgata Maitreya will then grant him a prophecy that he shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

At that time, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, the entire assembly here was able to see in each of the ten directions a thousand buddha-fields and their respective World-Honored Ones, along with those assemblies and the pure, adorned, subtle, and extraordinary splendor of those buddha-fields—a magnificence that the signs of adornment and purity in this Sahā world could not equal.
At that time, ten thousand sentient beings in this assembly each made a vow, saying:
"By means of all the pure deeds we have cultivated, may we be reborn in those various Buddha-fields."
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the aspiration in his mind, again smiled, and from his face issued forth rays of light of various colors.
Venerable Ānanda rose again from his seat and respectfully asked the Buddha about the cause and conditions for his smile.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"Do you now see these ten thousand sentient beings? Ānanda replied:
"Yes, indeed! We have seen it.
The Buddha said:

“Ānanda! When these ten thousand sentient beings have exhausted their lifespans here, they shall each attain rebirth in ten thousand Buddha-fields by the power of their vows. Until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they shall never be separated from a Buddha in whatever place they are born; they shall make offerings, show reverence, respect, and praise [the Buddhas], and practice the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*). Having attained perfection, they shall all simultaneously become Buddhas, all bearing the same name: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān—namely, the Tathāgata Śrīkūṭarāja (King of Adornment).”

Chapter Four: The Peerless (Asamasama), Second Part. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the Venerable Subhūti, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, the Venerable Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, and other such renowned great bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, upāsakas, and upāsikās, all rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha together, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
The great *pāramitā* is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the vast *pāramitā* is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the foremost *pāramitā* is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the supreme *pāramitā* is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
This prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is the supreme pāramitā; this prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is the unsurpassed pāramitā;
this prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is the exquisite pāramitā.
The perfection of wisdom is a lofty perfection; this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The perfection of wisdom is an ultimate perfection; this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The perfection of wisdom is an unsurpassed perfection; this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The supreme among the supreme pāramitās is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the peerless pāramitā is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the pāramitā equal to the unequaled is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The perfection of space is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of non-opposition is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of the emptiness of self-characteristics is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The perfection of the emptiness of mutual non-existence is the Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of the emptiness of all phenomena is the Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of the emptiness of the unapprehendable is the Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Maitreya, the perfection of the emptiness of non-arising is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of the emptiness of non-cessation is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of the emptiness of non-existence is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Maitreya, the perfection of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is the Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of the emptiness of both non-existence and existence is the Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and the perfection of śamatha is the Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The perfection of dhyāna is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection that develops all merits is the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection that accomplishes all merits is the... of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The Prajñāpāramitā of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is the pāramitā that cannot be overcome;
the Prajñāpāramitā of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is the pāramitā that can shatter all [other] pāramitās.
“World-Honored One!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are most honored and supreme, possessing great power; they are able to perform peerless giving, able to fulfill peerless giving, and able to perfect the perfection of peerless giving;
they are able to attain a peerless self-body, namely, a body exquisitely adorned with boundless marks and signs.”
They are able to realize the peerless Dharma, namely, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"World-Honored One!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are most honored and supreme, possessing great power; they are able to uphold the peerless precepts, fulfill the peerless precepts, and perfect the peerless perfection of pure ethical discipline."
One can attain an unequaled self-nature, namely, a body exquisitely adorned with boundless marks and signs;
one can realize the unequaled Dharma, namely, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are most honored and supreme, possessing great power; they are able to cultivate the peerless patience, able to fulfill the peerless patience, and able to perfect the peerless perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā);
they are able to attain a peerless self-nature, namely, a body exquisitely adorned with boundless marks and signs.”
They are able to realize the peerless Dharma, namely, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"World-Honored One!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are most honored and supreme, possessing great power; they are able to give rise to peerless diligence, fulfill peerless diligence, and possess the peerless perfection of vigor."
One is able to attain the peerless self-body, namely the wondrously adorned body with boundless marks and signs;
one is able to realize the peerless Dharma, namely unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are most honored and supreme, possessing great power; they are able to give rise to the unequaled samādhi, are able to fulfill the unequaled samādhi, and are able to perfect the unequaled dhyāna-pāramitā;
they are able to attain an unequaled self-body, namely, a body wonderfully adorned with boundless marks and signs.”
They are able to realize the peerless Dharma, namely, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"World-Honored One!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are most honored and supreme, possessing great power; they are able to cultivate peerless wisdom, able to fulfill peerless wisdom, and able to be endowed with the peerless perfection of wisdom."
One is able to attain a self-nature that is unequaled, namely, a body wonderfully adorned with boundless marks and signs;
one is able to realize a dharma that is unequaled, namely, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Regarding other various and sublime qualities, it is likewise in accordance with what is appropriate.
“World-Honored One!

Because the World-Honored One also practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, is able to cultivate, abide in, fulfill, and perfect sublime qualities, he attains form that is unequaled and peerless; he attains feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness that are unequaled and peerless; he realizes enlightenment that is unequaled and peerless, and turns the wheel of Dharma that is unequaled and peerless. It is the same for all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to reach the ultimate further shore of all dharmas, they should practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
“World-Honored One!
