‘In such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a world, there is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva of such-and-such a name who, for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, has donned the great armor of merit; he purifies Buddha-fields, matures sentient beings, and sports with supernormal powers while performing what is to be done.’”
Thus, as the sound spread from one to another throughout the ten directions, humans, devas, and others who heard it were all filled with great joy and said:
"This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva will before long realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment he seeks, bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings."
At that time, Śāriputra asked Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra:
"In what way does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings?"
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra said: “Śāriputra!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having donned the great armor of the six pāramitās for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, further, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to those beings, become detached from desires and unwholesome states; with directed thought and sustained thought, born of detachment, they enter and dwell in the first dhyāna, characterized by joy and bliss. [This is] explained at length until: having abandoned pleasure and abandoned pain, with the prior disappearance of joy and grief, they enter and dwell in the fourth dhyāna, which is neither painful nor pleasant, and is purified by equanimity and mindfulness.”

Furthermore, relying upon meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), he gives rise to a mind accompanied by loving-kindness (*maitrī*), whose mental aspect (*ākāra*) is vast, non-dual, and immeasurable; it is free from enmity, harm, resentment, and affliction. Having thoroughly cultivated this state until it is pervasive, his resolute conviction (*adhimokṣa*) is universal, overflowing throughout the ten directions, exhausting the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. He dwells fully endowed with this resolute conviction of a loving mind.
The same applies to the mental aspects and resolute convictions arising from minds accompanied by compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*).

Relying on this preparatory application, he further transcends all perceptions of form, extinguishes perceptions of resistance, and does not attend to perceptions of diversity; he enters the sphere of infinite space and dwells fully therein.
This is explained at length until: having transcended the sphere of nothingness, he enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and dwells fully therein.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, taking these meditative concentrations, immeasurables, and formless attainments, employs the method of non-apprehension to dedicate them together with all sentient beings toward omniscience.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Śāriputra!

For the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas first personally abide in these dhyānas, immeasurables, and formless attainments, skillfully discerning and knowing the modes of entering, abiding, and emerging from them, as well as their various activities, characteristics, and signs.
Having attained mastery, he further reflects:

"I shall now, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and taking great compassion as my primary motive, for the sake of severing the afflictions of all sentient beings, teach the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*). I shall analyze and reveal them so that they may thoroughly understand the gratification (*āsvāda*), the disadvantage (*ādīnava*), and the escape (*niḥsaraṇa*) regarding these meditative absorptions, as well as the modes of entry, abiding, and emergence, along with their activities, characteristics, and signs."

"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfection of meditative concentration, practices the perfection of generosity, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings."

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, teaches the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, they are not interrupted by the mental states of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or others."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfection of meditative concentration, practices the perfection of ethical discipline, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, teaches the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, they have faith, patience, desire, and delight in such dharmas."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfection of meditative concentration, practices the perfection of patience, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of bringing universal benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, cultivates the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, they dedicate their own roots of virtue for the sake of sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, diligently cultivating those roots of virtue without ceasing."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfection of meditative concentration, practices the perfection of diligence, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, relies upon the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*), and thereby brings forth superior meditative absorptions (*samāpatti*), meditative stabilizations (*samādhi*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), and bases of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*), attaining mastery over entering, abiding in, and emerging from them, yet does not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfection of meditative concentration and practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and taking great compassion as the foremost, cultivates the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, they correctly observe those meditative concentrations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and their constituent factors through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, and non-self, as well as through the aspects of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; thus, they do not abandon great compassion and do not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.”

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfection of meditative concentration, practices the perfection of wisdom, and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of bringing universal benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva,

with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and with great compassion as the foremost, cultivates the concentration of loving-kindness (*maitrī-samādhi*), he forms this thought:
'I shall provide relief for all sentient beings and cause them all to attain happiness.'"
When cultivating the concentration of compassion, one forms this thought:
"I shall rescue and deliver all sentient beings, causing them all to be free from suffering.
When cultivating the concentration of sympathetic joy, one forms this thought:
"I shall encourage and inspire all sentient beings so that they may all attain liberation.
When practicing the meditative concentration of equanimity, one forms this thought:
"I shall benefit all sentient beings equally so that they may all exhaust their outflows."

"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the immeasurable, practices the perfection of generosity and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings."

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, enters, abides in, and emerges from the four immeasurables, never seeks the state of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, but seeks only unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the immeasurable, practices the perfection of ethical discipline and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, enters, dwells in, and emerges from the four immeasurables without mixing in the mental engagements of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but possesses only faith, patience, desire, and delight for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the immeasurable, practices the perfection of patience and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of bringing universal benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, diligently abandons all evils and diligently cultivates all virtues at the times of entering, abiding in, and emerging from the four immeasurables, seeking to advance toward enlightenment without ever abandoning it for even a moment."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the immeasurable, practices the perfection of diligence and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, enters, abides in, and emerges from the four immeasurables, can induce various meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) and attainments (*samāpatti*), and is able to attain great mastery therein, such that he is not led away or carried off by those states of concentration, nor does he undergo rebirth under their influence."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the immeasurable, practices the perfection of meditative concentration and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, at the time of entering, abiding in, and emerging from the four immeasurables, observes them as they truly are through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, and non-self, as well as the aspects of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, yet does not abandon great compassion, they do not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the immeasurable, practices the perfection of wisdom and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“Śāriputra! By relying on such skillful means as these, bodhisattva mahāsattvas cultivate the six perfections and set out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, cultivates all aspects of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; cultivates all aspects of the three doors of liberation; and even cultivates all aspects of the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—using the method of non-apprehension and dedicating it together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes."
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, gives rise to the wisdom of internal emptiness, up to and including the wisdom of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and through the method of non-apprehension, dedicates this together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, gives rise toward all phenomena to a sublime wisdom that is neither distracted nor concentrated; a sublime wisdom that is neither permanent nor impermanent; a sublime wisdom that is neither pleasant nor painful; a sublime wisdom that is neither self nor non-self; a sublime wisdom that is neither pure nor impure; a sublime wisdom that is neither empty nor non-empty; a sublime wisdom that is neither with signs nor signless; a sublime wisdom that is neither with vows nor vowless; a sublime wisdom that is neither tranquil nor non-tranquil; and a sublime wisdom that is neither detached nor non-detached—employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.”
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, does not engage with the past, future, or present, yet is not ignorant of the phenomena of the three times;
Wisdom does not function within the realms of desire, form, or formlessness, yet it is not that it does not know the phenomena of these three realms;
wisdom does not function within the wholesome, the unwholesome, or the indeterminate, yet it is not that it does not know the phenomena of these three natures;
wisdom does not function within the mundane or the supramundane, yet it is not that it does not know mundane or supramundane phenomena.
Wisdom does not engage with the conditioned or the unconditioned, yet it is not that it is ignorant of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena;

wisdom does not engage with the outflowing or the non-outflowing, yet it is not that it is ignorant of outflowing and non-outflowing phenomena. Wisdom takes non-apprehension as its skillful means and, together with all sentient beings, dedicates [merit] toward omniscience.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings. Śāriputra!

Because Bodhisattvas, by means of such skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), set out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, they are further called "Great Beings" (*mahāsattva*).

“Śāriputra! Thus, for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to sentient beings, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have set out in the Great Vehicle are joyfully praised by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, amidst their great assemblies, who speak thus:

‘In such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a world, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named so-and-so, who has set out in the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings; he purifies buddha-fields, brings sentient beings to maturity, and performs his duties by sporting with supernormal powers.’”
Thus, as the sound spread from one to another throughout the ten directions, humans, devas, and others who heard it were all filled with great joy and spoke these words:
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment he seeks, bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings."
Chapter 14: The Vehicle of the Mahāyāna, Part Two. At that time, Śāriputra asked Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra:
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva mount the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings?"
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra said: “Śāriputra!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, although they ride upon the perfection of giving, they do not apprehend the perfection of giving; nor do they apprehend the giver, the recipient, the gift, or the phenomena that are excluded.”

Although they ride upon the perfection of pure ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), they do not apprehend the perfection of pure ethical discipline; they do not apprehend the one who maintains the precepts, the one who violates them, nor the factors that are prohibited.

Although they ride upon the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), they do not apprehend the perfection of patience; they do not apprehend the one who is able to endure, the object of endurance, nor the factors that are prohibited.

Although they ride upon the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*), they do not apprehend the perfection of diligence; they do not apprehend the one who is diligent, the one who is indolent, nor the factors that are prohibited.

Although one mounts the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*), one does not apprehend the perfection of meditative concentration; one does not apprehend the cultivation of concentration or distraction, nor does one apprehend the objects of concentration or the phenomena to be excluded.

Although one mounts the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*), one does not apprehend the perfection of wisdom; one does not apprehend the cultivation of insight or delusion, nor does one apprehend wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate phenomena; one does not apprehend mundane or supramundane phenomena, nor conditioned or unconditioned phenomena, nor tainted or untainted phenomena, nor the phenomena to be excluded.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employing non-apprehension as a skillful means, cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path for the sake of relinquishing cultivation; cultivates the three doors of liberation; and likewise cultivates up to the ten powers of a buddha and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), observes according to reality that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation (*prajñapti*), a conventional establishment (*saṃvṛti*), and a verbal expression (*vyavahāra*), because both "bodhi" and "sattva" are unapprehendable;
and that from form (*rūpa*) up to consciousness (*vijñāna*) exist only as mere designations, conventional establishments, and verbal expressions, because they are unapprehendable;
and that from the eye (*cakṣus*) up to the mind (*manas*) exist only as mere designations, conventional establishments, and verbal expressions, because they are unapprehendable.
From form up to mental phenomena (*dharma*), there are only provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable;
from the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element, there are only provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable;
from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, there are only provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable.
From internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, these exist only as provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable;

to speak extensively, up to the Tathāgata’s ten powers and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, these exist only as provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable;

true suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, and the limit of reality exist only as provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable.
The subject that awakens and the object awakened to exist merely as provisional names, designations, and verbal expressions, for they are unattainable;
likewise, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas exists merely as a provisional name, designation, and verbal expression, for it is unattainable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), constantly cultivates and perfects non-retrogressive supernatural powers from the first generation of the mind of awakening until the realization of the knowledge of all modes; matures sentient beings and purifies buddha-fields; travels from one buddha-field to another, making offerings, paying respect, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; and having heard and received the sublime Dharma associated with the Great Vehicle from those Buddhas, reflects upon it according to principle and diligently practices and studies it.
“Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings. Śāriputra!”

Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ride upon the Great Vehicle, traveling from one buddha-field to another to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; and although they listen to and receive the sublime Dharma from those Buddhas, bringing sentient beings to maturity and adorning and purifying buddha-fields, their minds are entirely free from any conceptualization of "buddha-fields" and so forth.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the stage of non-duality; observing which body among all sentient beings should be used to bring them to liberation, he immediately manifests and assumes such a body.

Śāriputra! From this point until they realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas shall never be separated from the true Dharma of the Mahāyāna in whatever place they may be born.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long attain the knowledge of all modes; he shall turn the wheel of the true Dharma for gods, humans, and others—a wheel of Dharma that cannot be turned by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, gods, Māras, Brahmās, or anyone else.

"Śāriputra! Because all bodhisattvas universally seek to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, and because they ride upon the Great Vehicle, they are further called Mahāsattvas. Śāriputra!"

Thus, for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to sentient beings, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who have mounted the Great Vehicle are joyfully praised by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, amidst their great assemblies, who speak these words:

"In such-and-such a direction, within such-and-such a world, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named so-and-so, for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, has mounted the Great Vehicle; before long, he shall attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and turn the wheel of the true Dharma for gods, humans, and others—a wheel that none of the śrāvakas in the world can turn."
Thus, as the sound spread from one to another throughout the ten directions, humans, devas, and others who heard it were all filled with great joy and said:
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long attain the knowledge of all modes; he shall turn the sublime wheel of Dharma and deliver immeasurable multitudes."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 412; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Fascicle 413.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Fifteen: On Being Neither Bound Nor Liberated. Part Two, Chapter Fifteen: On Being Neither Bound Nor Liberated. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
As it was said, "A bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who has donned the armor of the Great Vehicle. How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva don the armor of the Great Vehicle?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don the armor of everything from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to have donned the armor of the Great Vehicle."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don the armor of the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don the armor of inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don the armor of the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don the armor of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*).

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can transform his own body into the form of a Buddha, emitting great radiance that illuminates the trichiliocosm and even the Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, performing beneficial deeds for all sentient beings, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons such armor of merit as these, emitting a great radiance that illuminates the trichiliocosm and even the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and causes the six types of threefold earthquakes in those worlds—namely, shaking, intense shaking, and equal intense shaking—and so forth, thereby performing great benefit for all sentient beings."
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don the great armor of merit of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), universally transforming the trichiliocosm into the likeness of vaidūrya, and likewise transforming his own body into that of a great wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*) with a retinue of the seven treasures all perfectly complete, he shall give to all sentient beings whatever they require: food to those who need food, drink to those who need drink, clothing to those who need clothing, and vehicles to those who need vehicles; he shall provide ointments, powdered incense, burning incense, flower garlands, dwellings, bedding, medicinal requisites, lamps, pearls, gold, silver, and various other kinds of precious goods and utensils, bestowing them all according to their needs.

Having performed such giving, he further proclaims for them the Dharma associated with the six *pāramitās*, so that upon hearing it, they shall never fall away, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never abandoning the Dharma associated with the six *pāramitās*.
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

It is like a master illusionist or his disciple who, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures various impoverished sentient beings and magically creates and bestows upon them whatever they require.
"What do you think?
Is such an illusory phenomenon real? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! The Buddha told Subhūti:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also like this: they can don the great armor of the perfection of giving (dāna-pāramitā), transforming worlds into vaidūrya or manifesting themselves as universal monarchs (cakravartin) and so forth, bestowing upon sentient beings whatever they require and proclaiming for them the dharmas associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā). Although such bodhisattvas perform these deeds, they possess no substantial reality.”
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having donned the great armor of the merit of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*) for the sake of sentient beings, is born into the family of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) and succeeds to the rank of a universal monarch with sovereign wealth and power, he establishes immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings in the ten paths of wholesome action, or in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; or in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; or in the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; or in the ten powers of a buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. He also proclaims such teachings for them so that they may abide therein, never abandoning these dharmas until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Mahāyāna. Subhūti!"

It is like a master illusionist or his disciple who, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures up hundreds of thousands of immeasurable sentient beings and causes them to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

"So too, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, for the sake of sentient beings, are born into the family of a wheel-turning monarch; having inherited the rank of a wheel-turning monarch with its wealth, nobility, and sovereignty, they establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings in the ten paths of wholesome action, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha."
Thus, although a bodhisattva has that which they do, there is no reality to it.
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like an illusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva personally dons the great armor of the merit of the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*), and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the perfection of patience."

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva themselves don the great armor of the merit of the perfection of patience, and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the perfection of patience?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first generation of the mind of awakening until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, dons the armor of patience and constantly reflects:

'Even if all classes of sentient beings were to come with swords and clubs to inflict harm upon me, I shall never, for even a single moment, give rise to a mind of resentment, malice, or anger; furthermore, I shall exhort all sentient beings to cultivate this same patience.'"

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to accomplish everything according to what the mind intends, until the attainment of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). He never abandons such patience, and he also causes sentient beings to cultivate such patience."
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

It is like a master illusionist or his disciple who, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures various kinds of sentient beings; some brandish swords and staves to harm one another, while others exhort each other to practice the conduct of patience.
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

"So too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: they themselves don the great armor of the merit of the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), and they likewise encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the perfection of patience. Thus, although these bodhisattvas have something to do, there is no [inherent] reality to it."
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva personally dons the great armor of the meritorious perfection of diligence, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the meritorious perfection of diligence.

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva themselves don the great armor of the perfection of diligence, and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the perfection of diligence?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, takes great compassion as the foremost priority and applies physical and mental diligence, thereby abandoning all unwholesome dharmas and cultivating all wholesome dharmas; and if they also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to practice such physical and mental diligence until they realize the knowledge of all modes—never forsaking such right effort throughout."
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

Just as a master illusionist or his disciple, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure various kinds of sentient beings and then personally cultivate diligence while also encouraging others to do so.
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also like this: with mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, and taking great compassion as their foremost priority, they personally cultivate diligence and also encourage sentient beings to cultivate diligence; yet, although such bodhisattvas have things they do, there is no [inherent] reality in them.”
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva personally dons the great armor of the merit of the dhyāna-pāramitā, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the dhyāna-pāramitā.

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva don for themselves the great armor of the merit of the dhyāna-pāramitā, and also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the dhyāna-pāramitā?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in the samādhi of the equality of all phenomena, they do not perceive any phenomenon as being either concentrated or distracted; yet they constantly cultivate this perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), and also encourage sentient beings to cultivate such equal meditative concentration, never abandoning this meditative concentration until they realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)."
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

It is like a master illusionist or his disciple who, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures various kinds of sentient beings and causes them to cultivate the meditative concentration on the equality of all phenomena, while also exhorting them to cultivate such concentration.
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

"So too it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas: dwelling in the samādhi of the equality of all phenomena, they also exhort sentient beings to cultivate such a samādhi; thus, although these bodhisattvas perform actions, there is no substantial reality to them."
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva personally dons the great armor of the merit of the prajñāpāramitā, they also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the prajñāpāramitā.

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva personally don the great armor of the merit of the prajñāpāramitā, and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to don the great armor of the merit of the prajñāpāramitā?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in this profound *prajñāpāramitā* free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*), they do not perceive any distinction among phenomena—whether arising or ceasing, defiled or purified, or as 'this' and 'that. Furthermore, they encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings to abide in such wisdom free from conceptual proliferation."
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

Just as a master illusionist or his apprentice, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure various kinds of sentient beings and cause them to abide in the wisdom free from conceptual proliferation, and likewise encourage others to abide in such wisdom.
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

“So too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: they themselves are able to abide in wisdom free from conceptual proliferation, and they also encourage sentient beings to abide in such wisdom. Thus, although these bodhisattvas have things they do, there is no reality to them.”
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the various merits described above and observes all sentient beings in the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

There are sentient beings who embrace false teachings and engage in various evil deeds; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by means of their supernormal powers, transform their own bodies so as to pervade all such buddha-worlds, manifesting themselves according to the inclinations of those sentient beings. They personally manifest the practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and they likewise exhort others to practice generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Having exhorted all sentient beings to practice this path, he further speaks the Dharma associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) in accordance with their various languages and sounds, so that upon hearing it, they may eventually realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), never abandoning such sublime Dharma.
"Subhūti! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

It is like a master illusionist or his disciple who, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures forth various kinds of sentient beings and causes them to abide securely in the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), and likewise encourages others to abide in this Dharma.
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also like this: they manifest their own bodies throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; they dwell in the six pāramitās according to what is appropriate, and they also exhort sentient beings to abide in these practices, never abandoning them. Although such bodhisattvas have things they do, there is no reality to them.”
Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the aforementioned virtues, attends with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, takes great compassion as the foremost, employs the non-apprehension of phenomena as the skillful means, and brings benefit and happiness to all sentient beings without mixing in the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form such a thought:
"I shall establish this many sentient beings in the perfections, such as generosity, while I shall not establish that many sentient beings."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the perfections (pāramitās) such as giving.
One should not form this thought:
"One should not think, 'I shall establish so many sentient beings in the emptiness of the internal and so forth, while I shall not establish so many others.
Rather, one should simply form this thought:
'I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the emptiness of the internal and so forth.'"
They do not form such a thought:
"I shall establish this many sentient beings in the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, but I shall not establish that many sentient beings."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth.
One does not form such a thought [of self-reference]:
"I shall establish all those sentient beings in the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and yet there are no sentient beings to be established"—
he merely forms this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and so forth."
They do not form such a thought as:
"I shall establish this many sentient beings in the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth, while I shall not establish that many sentient beings."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth.
One does not form this thought:
"One should not think, 'I shall establish so many sentient beings in the fruit of stream-entry and so forth, while I shall not establish so many others.
Rather, one should simply form this thought:
'I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the fruit of stream-entry and so forth.'"
They do not form this thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in the Buddha's unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while so many sentient beings I shall not establish."
"But one should simply form this thought:
'I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the Buddha's unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Subhūti!"
This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to don the armor of the Great Vehicle. "Subhūti!

It is like a master illusionist or his apprentice who, standing at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures forth various kinds of sentient beings in immeasurable numbers; according to their needs, he employs skillful means to establish them in generosity, and so on, up to establishing them in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas."
"What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! The Buddha told Subhūti:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also like this: with mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as their foremost priority, and employing the method of non-apprehension, they establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless classes of sentient beings, causing them to abide in everything from generosity up to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; yet although such bodhisattvas have something for which they act, there is no actual reality therein.”
"Why is this? Because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, it should be known that those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who do not don the armor of merit are truly donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.”
Why is this? Because all dharmas are empty of their own characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*). For what reason?
World-Honored One!
Form up to consciousness—the characteristics of form up to consciousness are empty; the eye-base up to the mind-base—the characteristics of the eye-base up to the mind-base are empty;
the form-object-base up to the phenomena-object-base—the characteristics of the form-object-base up to the phenomena-object-base are empty.
The eye-element up to the mind-element are empty of the characteristics of the eye-element up to the mind-element;
the form-element up to the phenomena-element are empty of the characteristics of the form-element up to the phenomena-element;

the eye-consciousness-element up to the mind-consciousness-element are empty of the characteristics of the eye-consciousness-element up to the mind-consciousness-element; and eye-contact up to mind-contact... [are empty].

The contact of the mind is empty of intrinsic characteristics; the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are empty of the characteristics of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition;
and the perfection of generosity, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, [are likewise empty]. The perfection of generosity... [is empty].
The *pāramitās*, up to and including the *prajñāpāramitā*, are empty of the characteristic of the *pāramitās*;
the four applications of mindfulness, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are empty of the characteristic of the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;

internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, are empty of the characteristic of internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature. Thus it is.

Up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
the bodhisattva mahāsattva is empty of the characteristics of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and the donning of the great armor of merit is empty of the characteristics of donning the great armor of merit.
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, you should know that when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas do not don the armor of merit, they are truly donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.”
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.

Subhūti, you should know that omniscience is without creation or action, and all sentient beings are likewise without creation or action; it is for this purpose that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas don the armor of the Great Vehicle."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,

for what reason is the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) without creation or activity, and all sentient beings likewise without creation or activity, yet bodhisattva-mahāsattvas don the armor of the Great Vehicle for this very purpose?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“Because no agent can be apprehended, the knowledge of all modes is neither created nor fashioned, and all sentient beings likewise are neither created nor fashioned.”

Why is that? "Subhūti, form is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade."
Why is this? Because from form through to consciousness, they are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

The sense base of the eye is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the sense base of the eye, up to and including the sense base of the mind, is ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

The sense base of form is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), they are ultimately unobtainable. "Subhūti!..."
The eye-element is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the eye-element, up to and including the mind-element, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!
The realm of form is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) up to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they are ultimately unattainable. "Subhūti!..."

The eye-consciousness element is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the mind-consciousness element, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

Eye-contact is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact are likewise neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because eye-contact, up to and including mind-contact, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

The various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

I neither create nor do not create; neither act nor do not act. Sentient beings, life-principles, born beings, nourished beings, persons, individuals, mind-born beings, youthful ones, agents, experiencers, knowers, and seers neither create nor do not create; neither act nor do not act.
Why is this? Because from the self up to the seer, none are ultimately to be found. "Subhūti!..."

The dream-state is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; likewise, echoes, reflections, illusions, shadows, light-rays, flowers in the sky, cities of Gandharvas, and transformations are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because dream-objects and even matters of transformation are ultimately unobtainable. "Subhūti!..."

Internal emptiness is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, they are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

The four foundations of mindfulness are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!

In this way, even up to the ten powers of the Tathāgata are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.

Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are ultimately unattainable. "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is for this reason that they are called 'Buddhas']."

Suchness is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the dharma-constancy, the dharma-abiding, and the limit of reality are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from true suchness (tathatā) up to the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), they are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!..."

The bodhisattva mahāsattva neither constructs nor does not construct, neither acts nor does not act; the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha neither constructs nor does not construct, neither acts nor does not act.
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva and a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!..."

All-knowledge is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade; the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.

Why is this? Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are ultimately unattainable. "Subhūti!..."

For this reason, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is neither created nor fashioned, and all sentient beings are likewise neither created nor fashioned; it is for this purpose that the bodhisattva mahāsattvas don the armor of the Great Vehicle.
"Subhūti! By this meaning, you should know that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not don the armor of merit, they are said to have donned the armor of the Mahāyāna.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, form is neither bound nor liberated; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.”
At that time, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra asked Subhūti:
"Venerable One, do you say that form is neither bound nor liberated? Do you say that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated?"
Subhūti replied, “So it is! So it is!”
"I say that form is neither bound nor liberated; I say that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra asked:
"In what way is form neither bound nor liberated?"
"In what way are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness neither bound nor liberated? Subhūti replied:
"Just as form in a dream is neither bound nor liberated, so too are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness in a dream neither bound nor liberated."

Like an echo, like a reflection, like a shadow, like a mirage, like a magical illusion, like a flower in the sky, like a city of Gandharvas, and like a transformation—form is neither bound nor liberated. Like an echo, and so on, up to like a transformation, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because all these things, from form (*rūpa*) up to consciousness (*vijñāna*), do not exist; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are detached; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are quiescent; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are unarisen; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are unceasing; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are undefiled; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are unpurified; therefore, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
Past form is neither bound nor liberated; past feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Future and present form are neither bound nor liberated; future and present feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because all these things, from form up to consciousness, are non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are detached, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are quiescent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated; and because they are unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

Wholesome form is neither bound nor liberated; wholesome feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated. Unwholesome and indeterminate form is neither bound nor liberated;
unwholesome and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because all these things, from form (*rūpa*) up to consciousness (*vijñāna*), are non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are detached, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are quiescent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
Worldly form is neither bound nor liberated; worldly feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Supramundane form is neither bound nor liberated; supramundane feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because all these things, from form up to consciousness, do not exist, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are detached, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are quiescent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated; and because they are unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
Conditioned (sāsrava) form is neither bound nor liberated; conditioned feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Unconditioned (anāsrava) form is neither bound nor liberated; unconditioned feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because all these things, from form (*rūpa*) up to consciousness (*vijñāna*), being non-existent, are neither bound nor liberated; because they are detached, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are quiescent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are undefiled, they are neither bound nor liberated; and because they are unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
All dharmas are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
Because all phenomena are non-existent, detached, quiescent, unarisen, unceasing, undefiled, and unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
The perfection of generosity is neither bound nor liberated; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are neither bound nor liberated."
Why is this? Because the perfections such as giving are non-existent, remote, quiescent, unarisen, unceasing, unstained, and unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra! Inner emptiness is neither bound nor liberated;

outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because inner emptiness and so forth are non-existent, because they are detached, because they are tranquil, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are neither defiled nor pure, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

The four foundations of mindfulness are neither bound nor liberated; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are neither bound nor liberated."
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are non-existent, detached, quiescent, unarisen, unceasing, unstained, and unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

In this way, even up to the ten powers of the Tathāgata are neither bound nor liberated; the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because the ten powers and so forth are non-existent, because they are detached, because they are quiescent, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are neither defiled nor pure, and thus there is neither bondage nor liberation.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
All practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are neither bound nor liberated; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because the practices of a bodhisattva are equal to non-existence, because they are detached, because they are tranquil, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are unstained, and because they are unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

All-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is neither bound nor liberated; the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
Because all-knowledge and so forth are non-existent, detached, quiescent, unarisen, unceasing, unstained, and unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

Suchness is neither bound nor liberated; the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, and the limit of reality are all neither bound nor liberated."

Why is this? Because true suchness (tathatā) and so forth are non-existent, because they are detached, because they are quiescent, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are neither defiled nor pure, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are neither bound nor liberated; Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva and the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent, detached, quiescent, unarisen, unceasing, unstained, and unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
"Furthermore, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
All conditioned phenomena are neither bound nor liberated; all unconditioned phenomena are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

Because conditioned phenomena and so forth are non-existent, because they are remote, because they are quiescent, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are neither defiled nor pure, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, regarding this subtle dharma-gate that is neither bound nor liberated, should understand it as it truly is by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method.”
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

All bodhisattva mahāsattvas should diligently train in this perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom, and in the four applications of mindfulness up to all-aspect omniscience, by means of the expedient of non-apprehension.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

By means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should abide in this way—in the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, and in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the knowledge of all aspects, which are neither bound nor liberated.”
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

By taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should bring to maturity sentient beings who are neither bound nor liberated; they should purify buddha-fields that are neither bound nor liberated; they should draw near to, serve, and make offerings to Buddhas who are neither bound nor liberated; and they should listen to and receive the dharma-gates that are neither bound nor liberated.

“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is never separated from the Buddhas who are neither bound nor liberated; he is never separated from the supernormal powers that are neither bound nor liberated; he is never separated from the five eyes that are neither bound nor liberated; he is never separated from the dhāraṇīs that are neither bound nor liberated; and he is never separated from the samādhis that are neither bound nor liberated.”
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva shall give rise to the knowledge of the aspects of the path that is neither bound nor liberated; he shall realize the all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects that are neither bound nor liberated; he shall turn the wheel of Dharma that is neither bound nor liberated; and he shall establish all sentient beings in the essential teachings of the three vehicles that are neither bound nor liberated.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās that are neither bound nor liberated, they are able to realize the nature of all phenomena as neither bound nor liberated—because they are non-existent, because they are detached, because they are quiescent, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are unstained, and because they are unpurified; thus they are neither bound nor liberated.”
"Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is called one who has donned the great armor of neither bondage nor liberation.
Chapter Sixteen: Samādhi, Part Two, Section One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
To what extent should one know that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has set out upon the Great Vehicle?”
From where does such a Mahāyāna emerge? Where does it abide?
And in what does such a Mahāyāna reside?
"Who, moreover, will mount this Great Vehicle and depart?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"As for your initial question, 'What is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?'"
"Subhūti, these six perfections are the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
What are the six? They are as follows:"

Namely: the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! What is the perfection of giving?

It is when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension, personally relinquishes all internal and external possessions, and likewise encourages others to relinquish their internal and external possessions, dedicating these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.”
"Subhūti! This is the perfection of giving of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"
What is the perfection of pure ethical discipline?

It is when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension, personally undertakes the ten paths of wholesome action and also encourages others to undertake them, dedicating these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.
"Subhūti! This is the perfection of ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"
What is the perfection of patience?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, personally possesses superior patience and also encourages others to possess superior patience, and dedicates these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.
"Subhūti! This is the perfection of patience of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"
What is the perfection of diligence?

It is when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, personally and untiringly cultivates the five perfections without abandoning them, and likewise encourages others to untiringly cultivate the five perfections without abandoning them, dedicating these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.
"Subhūti! This is the perfection of vigor of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"
What is the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*)?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), enters through skillful means into the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), yet never takes birth under the influence of those states; and furthermore, being able to exhort others through skillful means to enter the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, so that they do not take birth under the influence of the power of those absorptions, and dedicates these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.
"Subhūti! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā). Subhūti!"
What is the perfection of wisdom?

It is when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employing non-apprehension as the means, observes the nature of all phenomena as it truly is; remaining without grasping or attachment toward the nature of all phenomena, they also exhort others to observe the nature of all phenomena as it truly is, remaining without grasping or attachment toward the nature of all phenomena, and dedicate these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward the knowledge of all modes.
Subhūti! This is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti, you should know this!
This is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of:

internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
"What is internal emptiness?
'Internal' refers to internal phenomena, namely the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

One should know that herein, the eye is empty of the eye because it is neither permanent nor subject to destruction; and so on, up to the mind being empty of the mind because it is neither permanent nor subject to destruction."
Why is this? Because such is their intrinsic nature, Subhūti!
This is internal emptiness.
What is external emptiness?
The external refers to external phenomena, namely: form, sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.

It should be understood that herein, form is empty of form, being neither permanent nor subject to destruction; and so on, up to: phenomena are empty of phenomena, being neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
Why is this? Because such is their intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti! This is called external emptiness.
What is internal-and-external emptiness?
"Internal and external" refers to internal and external phenomena, namely the six internal bases and the six external bases.

It should be understood that herein, internal phenomena are empty of external phenomena—being neither permanent nor subject to destruction—and external phenomena are empty of internal phenomena—being neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
Why is this? Because such is their intrinsic nature, Subhūti!
This is internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*). What is the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*)?
Emptiness refers to the emptiness of all phenomena; this emptiness, in turn, is empty of emptiness, being neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
Why is this? Because such is their intrinsic nature, Subhūti!
This is the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*). What is the great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*)?
"Great" refers to the ten directions: namely, east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.

It should be understood that herein, the eastern direction is empty of the eastern direction, being neither permanent nor subject to destruction; this continues up to the downward direction, which is empty of the downward direction, being neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is this so?
Because it is of such an inherent nature, Subhūti,
this is called the great emptiness.
"What is the emptiness of the ultimate (paramārtha-śūnyatā)?
