“Subhūti, you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, Subhūti!”
The characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refer to the four fearlessnesses.
What are the four? "Subhūti!

If, having attained nothing, one employs skillful means and claims for oneself, "I am a perfectly awakened one (samyaksambuddha)," then even if there should be a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a deva, a Māra, a Brahmā, or anyone else in the world who, according to the Dharma, raises an objection or brings it to mind, saying that regarding this Dharma one is not a perfectly awakened one, I see no grounds for such an objection.

Because he has seen that there is no cause for such challenges, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he proclaims himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he rightly roars the lion’s roar and turns the sublime Brahma-wheel.
That wheel is pure, authentic, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, devas, māras, brahmās, or anyone else in the world, there is none who is able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma.
This is the first. "Subhūti!

If one takes non-apprehension as the means, and declares of oneself, 'I have eternally exhausted all outflows,' then even if there should be a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a deva, a Māra, a Brahmā, or anyone else in the world who, according to the Dharma, raises an objection or calls for recollection, saying that such outflows have not been eternally exhausted, I see no grounds for that objection."

Because he has seen that those [objections] are without cause, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he declares himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he rightly roars the lion’s roar and turns the sublime Brahma-wheel.

That wheel is pure, upright, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, Brahmās, or anyone else in the world, there is none who is able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma.
This is the second. "Subhūti!

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one teaches the dharmas that obstruct the path to the disciples, and if there should be any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world who, relying on the Dharma, raises an objection or attempts to cause recollection, saying that 'practicing these dharmas cannot obstruct the path,' I see no grounds for such an objection."

Because he has seen that there is no such challenge regarding the absence of a cause, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he declares himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage among the great assembly, and he rightly roars the lion’s roar, turning the sublime Wheel of Brahma.

That wheel is pure, correct, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, whether brāhmaṇas, devas, Māras, Brahmās, or anyone else in the world, there is none who is able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma.
This is the third. "Subhūti!

If one employs the skillful means of non-apprehension to teach the path for the exhaustion of suffering to the disciples, then should any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world, according to the Dharma, raise an objection or cause one to reflect, saying that 'cultivating this path cannot exhaust suffering,' I see no grounds for such an objection."

Because he has seen that there is no cause for such challenges, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he declares himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he rightly roars the lion’s roar and turns the sublime Brahma-wheel.

That wheel is pure, upright, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, Brahmās, or anyone else in the world, there is none who is able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma.
This is the fourth. "Subhūti,
you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*). What are the four?
1. The analytical knowledge of meaning (arthapratisaṃvid).
2. The analytical knowledge of phenomena (dharmanirukti-pratisaṃvid).
3. The analytical knowledge of expression (niruktipratisaṃvid).
The four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*). Subhūti!
These four analytical knowledges, when practiced by way of non-apprehension, should be known as the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*).
What are these eighteen?
"Subhūti!"

That is to say, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas are always free from error; they have no harsh or violent speech; they have no loss of mindfulness; they have no manifold perceptions; they have no unconcentrated mind; they have no equanimity lacking discernment; their aspiration never regresses, their diligence never regresses, their mindfulness never regresses, their wisdom never regresses, their liberation never regresses, and their knowledge and vision of liberation never regress. All their bodily actions are preceded by wisdom and follow after wisdom; all their verbal actions are preceded by wisdom and follow after wisdom; all their mental actions are preceded by wisdom and follow after wisdom. Their knowledge and vision regarding the past are unattached and unimpeded; their knowledge and vision regarding the future are unattached and unimpeded; their knowledge and vision regarding the present are unattached and unimpeded.

"Subhūti! These eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are all without exception characterized by the method of non-apprehension; you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the gateways of dhāraṇī.
What are these gateways of dhāraṇī?"
This refers to entering the gateways of all syllables through the equality of syllables and the equality of speech.
What is meant by entering the gateways of all syllables through the equality of syllables and the equality of speech?

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they enter the gateway of the syllable *ṅa*, realizing that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen;
they enter the gateway of the syllable *la*, realizing that all phenomena are free from dust and defilement.”
One enters the gateway of the letter *pa*, for it awakens one to the teaching on the ultimate meaning (*paramārtha*) of all phenomena;
one enters the gateway of the letter *dha*, for it awakens one to the fact that all phenomena are without birth or death;
one enters the gateway of the letter *na*, for it awakens one to the fact that all phenomena are far removed from names and signs, and are without gain or loss.
One enters the letter-door *la*, for one awakens to the fact that all phenomena transcend the world, as the causal conditions of craving and its branches have been forever destroyed;
one enters the letter-door *ḍha*, for one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are tamed, tranquil, true thusness, equal, and non-conceptual;
one enters the letter-door *ba*, for one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are free from bondage and liberation.
Entering the gateway of the letter *ca*, one realizes that all phenomena are free from feverish affliction and corruption, thereby attaining purity;
entering the gateway of the letter *ṣa*, one realizes that all phenomena are without obstruction;
entering the gateway of the letter *ba*, one realizes that the path of vocal expression is severed in all phenomena.
Entering the gateway of the letter *ḍha*, one realizes that all phenomena are the immovable true suchness (*tathatā*);
entering the gateway of the letter *ya*, one realizes that all phenomena are non-arising according to reality;
entering the gateway of the letter *ṣṭa*, one realizes that the characteristics of the subduing and sustaining of all phenomena are unapprehendable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Ka, for one realizes that an agent of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Sa, for one realizes that the temporal equality of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Ma, for one realizes that the nature of grasping at "mine" in all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Ga, realizing that the nature of movement, activity, and grasping in all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Tha, realizing that the nature of the locus upon which all phenomena depend is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Ja, realizing that the nature of the producer and the produced in all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Śva, realizing that the nature of peace and security of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Dha, realizing that the nature of the sustaining elements of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Śa, realizing that the nature of quiescence of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Kha, for one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are like the nature of space and are ungraspable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Chaṃ, for one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are of an exhausted nature and are ungraspable;

one enters the gateway of the letter Sthā, for one awakens to the fact that all phenomena, in their capacity to sustain what is possible and what is impossible, are of a nature that is immovable and ungraspable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ja*, realizing that the nature of all phenomena as that which is known is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *sta*, realizing that the nature of all phenomena as objects of attachment is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ha*, realizing that the nature of all phenomena as being able to act as causes is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ba*, for one realizes that the destructible nature of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *bha*, for one realizes that the nature of all phenomena being shrouded by desire and pleasure is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *sma*, for one realizes that the nature of all phenomena being subject to recollection is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the syllable *kha* because one realizes that the summonable nature of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the syllable *ca* because one realizes that the courageous and robust nature of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the syllable *ga* because one realizes that the thick and impartial nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ca*, for one realizes that the accumulated nature of all phenomena is unattainable;

one enters the gateway of the letter *ṇa*, for one realizes that all phenomena are free from all clamor and contention, and that going, coming, walking, standing, sitting, and reclining are unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *pha*, for one realizes that the pervasive fruition of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the letter-gateway *ṣa*, realizing that the nature of the accumulation and aggregation of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the letter-gateway *va*, realizing that the characteristics of decay and aging in all phenomena are unattainable;
one enters the letter-gateway *ja*, realizing that the traces of the gathering of all phenomena are unattainable.
One enters the *ṭha*-gate, realizing that the nature of all phenomena as being driven and pressured is unapprehendable;
one enters the *ca* (or *cha*)-gate, realizing that the ultimate locus of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

This gateway of the letter ‘ca’ (ca) is the means for entering the limit of the emptiness of phenomena; apart from these letters that express the emptiness of all phenomena, nothing further can be found.”

Why is this? Because the meanings of these syllables cannot be proclaimed, cannot be displayed, cannot be written down or maintained, cannot be grasped, and cannot be observed, for they are free from all signs (*nimitta*).

"Subhūti! For example, just as space is the destination to which all things return, so too are these gateways of syllables; it is only by entering these gateways that the meaning of the emptiness of all phenomena becomes fully manifest."
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Entering this syllable *kṣa* and others is called entering the gateways of all syllables.
Suvikrāntavikrāmin!”

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain skillful wisdom by entering such gates of letters, they will encounter no obstruction regarding all that is expressed or indicated by speech and sound; they will be able to fully realize and maintain the equal emptiness of all phenomena, and they will achieve skillfulness in all vocal expressions.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to hear such seal-marks and seal-words that enter the gates of all syllables, and having heard them, receives, maintains, recites, masters, and explains them to others—without pursuing fame, gain, or honor—he will, by virtue of these causes and conditions, obtain twenty kinds of meritorious benefits.”
What are the twenty? They are: attaining powerful mindfulness; attaining superior shame and remorse; attaining firm strength; attaining the essential meaning of the Dharma;
attaining superior awakening; attaining distinguished wisdom; attaining unimpeded eloquence; and attaining the gateways of dhāraṇī.

They attain freedom from doubt; they attain the state where neither anger nor attachment arises toward speech that is either contrary or compliant; they attain dwelling in equanimity, free from high or low;

they attain skillfulness regarding the vocal expressions of sentient beings; and they attain skillfulness regarding the aggregates (*skandha*), skillfulness regarding the elements (*dhātu*), skillfulness regarding the sense bases (*āyatana*), skillfulness regarding the truths (*satya*), skillfulness regarding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), and skillfulness regarding causes (*hetu*).
Through skill in conditions and skill in phenomena, one attains skill in the knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of faculties,
skill in the knowledge of others' minds, skill in the observation of stellar chronology, skill in the knowledge of the divine ear, skill in the knowledge of recollecting past lives,
skill in the knowledge of supernormal powers, skill in the knowledge of death and rebirth, and attains the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows.
He is skillful; he attains skill in the knowledge of what is possible and what is impossible, skill in the knowledge of coming and going, and skill in the modes of deportment. Subhūti!
These are the twenty kinds of meritorious benefits obtained. "Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they obtain such dhāraṇī-doors; you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
Chapter 18: Purifying the Grounds, Part Two, Chapter 18, Section One. "Furthermore, Subhūti, as to what you asked:
'To what extent should one know that a bodhisattva mahāsattva has set out upon the Great Vehicle?'"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) and proceeds from one stage (bhūmi) to the next, it should be understood that up to this point, the bodhisattva mahāsattva has set out upon the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna).
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the six perfections, proceed from one stage to the next? Subhūti!
It is when a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all phenomena come from nowhere and go nowhere.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because all phenomena neither go nor come, and have no point of departure or destination, for those phenomena are devoid of transformation or decay.

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely upon or dwell upon the ground from which he has proceeded; although he cultivates the activities for purifying that ground, he does not perceive that ground."
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the six perfections, proceeds from one stage to the next.
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the activities of the stages?
"Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the first stage, they should skillfully cultivate ten kinds of superior deeds.
What are these ten?"

First, by taking non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates and purifies the activity of the superior intention (*adhyāśaya*), because the characteristics of beneficial things cannot be apprehended.
Second, by taking non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates and purifies the activity of a mind of equality toward all sentient beings, because all sentient beings cannot be apprehended.
Third, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the karma of giving; for the giver, the receiver, and the gift are all unapprehendable.
Fourth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the practice of attending upon spiritual friends, because one has no attachment to those spiritual friends.
Fifth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the practice of seeking the Dharma, because all dharmas sought are unapprehendable.
Sixth, by taking non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the practice of always delighting in leaving the home life, because the home that is abandoned cannot be apprehended.
Seventh, by taking non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the practice of loving the Buddha’s body, because the causes for the primary marks and secondary signs cannot be apprehended.

Eighth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and elucidates the activity of the Dharma teachings, because the dharmas that are conceptually distinguished cannot be apprehended.
Ninth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the activity of destroying pride, because all phenomena of worldly prosperity cannot be apprehended.
Tenth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the karma of truthful speech, because all words and speech are unapprehendable. Subhūti!
"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the first stage, they should skillfully cultivate and purify these ten superior activities. Furthermore, Subhūti,
when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the second stage, they should contemplate and practice eight dharmas so that they may be swiftly perfected."
What are the eight?
First, pure ethical discipline (*śīla*).
Second, recognizing kindness and repaying it.
Third, abiding in the power of patience;
fourth, experiencing supreme joy;
fifth, not abandoning sentient beings.
Sixth, to constantly give rise to great compassion.
Seventh, to serve, honor, and provide for one's teachers and elders with a mind of reverence and faith, as if attending upon the Buddhas themselves.
Eighth, to diligently seek and practice the pāramitās.
"Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the second bhūmi, they should contemplate and train in these eight dharmas so that they may be swiftly perfected.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dwell in the third stage, they should abide in five dharmas. What are these five?
First, they should diligently seek out extensive learning without ever becoming weary or satisfied, and regarding the teachings they have heard, they should not cling to the literal words.
Second, they constantly practice the gift of Dharma with a mind free from attachment; though they extensively transform and guide others, they do not exalt themselves.
Third, they plant various roots of goodness to adorn and purify the Buddha-land; though they employ the dedication of merit, they do not praise themselves.
Fourth, although they do not weary of the boundless cycle of birth and death for the sake of transforming sentient beings, they remain free from arrogance and indolence.
Fifth, although they abide in a sense of shame and remorse, they are without attachment.
"Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the third bhūmi, they should always abide securely in these five dharmas.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the fourth stage, they should uphold and not abandon ten dharmas. What are these ten?
First, dwelling in an araṇya, they should never forsake it.
Second, they always delight in having few desires.
Third, they always delight in contentment.
Fourth, they never abandon the virtues of the dhūta ascetic practices.
Fifth, never abandoning any of the precepts;
sixth, generating a profound sense of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures;
seventh, always delighting in giving rise to a mind associated with tranquility.
Eighth, relinquishing all things.
Ninth, the mind not being stagnant or submerged.
Tenth, always being without attachment or longing for any thing.
"Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the fourth stage, they should uphold these ten dharmas and not abandon them.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the fifth stage, they should distance themselves from ten things. What are these ten?
First, they should distance themselves from household life.
Second, one should distance oneself from bhikṣuṇīs.
Third, one should distance oneself from stinginess regarding households.
Fourth, one should distance oneself from anger and strife within assemblies.
Fifth, one should distance oneself from praising oneself and disparaging others.
Sixth, one should distance oneself from the ten unwholesome paths of action.
Seventh, one should distance oneself from excessive arrogance.
Eighth, one should distance oneself from perversions.
Ninth, one should distance oneself from hesitation.
Tenth, one should distance oneself from greed, hatred, and delusion.
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the fifth stage, they should always remain far removed from these ten dharmas.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the sixth stage, they should fulfill six dharmas.
What are these six? They are the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), namely, from generosity (dāna) up to wisdom (prajñā).
Furthermore, one should distance oneself from six things. What are these six?
First, the mind of a śrāvaka.
Second, the mind of a solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha*).
Third, the mind of feverish affliction.
Fourth, the mind that is neither joyful nor sorrowful when seeing a beggar approach.
Fifth, the mind of regret and longing for all things one has relinquished.
Sixth, the mind of employing skillful means to deceive those who come seeking. Subhūti!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the sixth stage, they should constantly fulfill the six dharmas previously mentioned and should remain far removed from the six dharmas subsequently mentioned.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the seventh stage, they should distance themselves from twenty things.
What are these twenty?
First, one should distance oneself from the grasping at a self up to the grasping at a viewer.
Second, one should distance oneself from the grasping at annihilation.
Third, one should distance oneself from the grasping at permanence.
Fourth, one should distance oneself from attachment to the perception of signs.
Fifth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views.
Sixth, one should distance oneself from attachment to name-and-form.
Seventh, one should distance oneself from attachment to the aggregates (*skandha*).
Eighth, one should distance oneself from attachment to the sense bases (*āyatana*).
Ninth, one should distance oneself from attachment to the elements (*dhātu*).
Tenth, one should distance oneself from clinging to [the notion of] truth.
Eleventh, one should distance oneself from clinging to dependent origination.
Twelfth, one should distance oneself from clinging to and dwelling within the three realms.
Thirteenth, one should remain far removed from all attachment to phenomena (*dharmagrāha*).
Fourteenth, one should remain far removed from attachment to phenomena as being either conformable or non-conformable to reality.
Fifteenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views based on the Buddha.
Sixteenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views based on the Dharma.
Seventeenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views based on the Sangha.
Eighteenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views based on the precepts.
Nineteenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views based on emptiness.
Twentieth, one should distance oneself from aversion and fear toward emptiness.
"Furthermore, one should fulfill twenty dharmas.
What are the twenty?
First, one should fulfill the thorough penetration of emptiness."
Second, one should fulfill the realization of signlessness (*animitta*).
Third, one should fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness (*apraṇihita*).
Fourth, one should fulfill the purity of the three spheres (*trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi*).
Fifth, one should fulfill compassion for sentient beings and non-attachment toward sentient beings.
Sixth, one should fulfill the vision of the equality of all phenomena and non-attachment within that regard.
Seventh, one should fulfill the impartial view toward all sentient beings and remain without attachment therein.
Eighth, one should fulfill the thorough penetration of the principle of reality and remain without attachment therein.
Ninth, one should fulfill the wisdom of the patience regarding non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Tenth, one should fulfill the exposition of the principle that all phenomena have a single characteristic (*eka-lakṣaṇa-naya*).
Eleventh, one should fulfill the elimination of conceptual discrimination (*vikalpa*).
Twelfth, one should fulfill the complete distancing from all conceptualizations.
Thirteenth, one should fulfill the complete distancing from all views.
Fourteenth, one should fulfill the complete distancing from all afflictions.
Fifteenth, one should fulfill the stage of śamatha and vipaśyanā.
Sixteenth, one should fulfill the taming of the mental continuum.
Seventeenth, one should fulfill the pacification of the mental continuum.
Eighteenth, one should fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom.
Nineteenth, one should fulfill freedom from all attachment and defilement.
Twentieth, one should fulfill the ability to manifest one's own body within the assemblies of Buddhas in any Buddha-field according to one’s heart’s desire.

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the seventh stage, they should always remain far removed from the twenty kinds of dharmas previously mentioned, and they should bring to perfection the twenty kinds of dharmas subsequently mentioned.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the eighth stage, they should fulfill four dharmas. What are these four?
First, one should fulfill the thorough comprehension of the mental activities of all sentient beings.
Second, one should fulfill the playful mastery of the various supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
Third, one should fulfill the vision of all Buddha-fields and, according to that vision, personally adorn and purify various Buddha-fields.
Fourth, they should fulfill the service and offering to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and the contemplation of the Tathāgata’s body as it truly is.
Subhūti! When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the eighth stage, they should diligently fulfill these four dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When bodhisattva mahāsattvas abide in the ninth stage, they should fulfill four dharmas. What are these four?
First, one should fulfill the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties of sentient beings.
Second, one should fulfill the purification of Buddha-fields.
Third, one should fulfill the frequent entry into various meditative absorptions through the illusion-like samādhi.

Fourth, they should fulfill the practice of manifesting through spontaneous birth within the various realms of existence in order to bring the roots of virtue of all sentient beings to maturity according to their needs. Subhūti!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the ninth stage, they should diligently fulfill these four dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the tenth stage, they should fulfill twelve dharmas.
What are these twelve?
First, one should fulfill the great vow to encompass infinite realms, causing whatever is aspired to be realized.
Second, one should fulfill the knowledge of the various languages of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and other diverse classes of beings.
Third, one should fulfill unimpeded eloquence in teaching.
Fourth, one should fulfill the perfection of entering the womb.
Fifth, one should fulfill the perfection of birth.
Sixth, one should fulfill the perfection of family.
Seventh, one should fulfill the perfection of lineage.
Eighth, one should fulfill the perfection of retinue.
Ninth, one should fulfill the perfection of the excellence of the birth-body.
Tenth, one should fulfill the perfection of the excellence of renunciation.
Eleventh, one should fulfill the perfection of the excellence of adorning the Bodhi tree.
Twelfth, they should fulfill the complete accomplishment and perfection of all merits. Subhūti!
When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the tenth stage, they should diligently fulfill these twelve dharmas.
“Subhūti, you should know this!
Once a bodhisattva mahāsattva has dwelled in the tenth stage, they should be said to be no different from the Tathāgatas.
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, employing the method of non-apprehension, cultivate and purify the karma of the superior intention?”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mental orientation associated with the knowledge of all modes, cultivates and accumulates all supreme roots of goodness, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation and purification of the activity of the superior intention by means of non-apprehension."
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivate and purify the karma of a mind of equality toward all sentient beings?
Subhūti!...”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, brings forth the four immeasurable minds of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the karma of an impartial mind toward all sentient beings by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method.
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the practice of generosity by taking non-apprehension as the means? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices generosity toward all sentient beings without making any conceptual distinctions, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivating the practice of generosity by taking non-apprehension as the means."
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivate the practice of attending upon spiritual friends? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees spiritual friends exhorting and transforming sentient beings, causing them to cultivate the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), he immediately attends upon, reveres, makes offerings to, honors, praises, and inquires about the true Dharma from them, serving them day and night with a mind free from weariness. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivates the practice of attending upon spiritual friends."
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, taking non-apprehension as the means, cultivate the activity of seeking the Dharma? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes, diligently seeks the unsurpassed true Dharma of the Tathāgata and does not fall into the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivating the activity of seeking the Dharma by taking non-apprehension as the means.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivate the practice of always delighting in going forth? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in all places of birth, constantly feels aversion toward the household life with its clamor, crowding, and confinement as if it were a prison, and always rejoices in the pure renunciation of the Buddha-dharma, which is tranquil, unconditioned, and unimpeded like space—this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivates the practice of always delighting in going forth.”
“What is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the practice of loving the Buddha’s body by taking non-apprehension as the means? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon seeing the physical form of the Buddha even for a single moment, never abandons the mental attention directed toward the Buddha until they realize all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the practice of loving the Buddha’s body by taking non-apprehension as the means.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivate the activity of expounding and clarifying the Dharma teachings? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, whether while the Buddha is in the world or after his parinirvāṇa, expounds and clarifies the Dharma teachings for the sake of all sentient beings—teachings that are excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, skillful in both letter and meaning, pure, complete, and the pristine holy life—namely, from the sūtras up to the treatises (upadeśas)—this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivating the activity of expounding and clarifying the Dharma teachings by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivate the practice of destroying pride? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva always maintains humility and respect, subduing the mind of pride, and because of this is not born into a low caste or inferior lineage—this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivates the practice of destroying pride.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivate the karma of truthful speech? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva speaks in accordance with what they know, such that their words and actions correspond, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, cultivates the karma of truthful speech.”
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the first bhūmi, they should skillfully cultivate these ten superior deeds.
What is the pure ethical discipline (*śīla*) of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor any other factors that violate the precepts and obstruct enlightenment, this is the pure ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva."
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva recognize kindness and repay it? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the sublime conduct of all bodhisattvas, if they receive even a small kindness from another, they are still able to repay it with great weight; how much more so for a great favor, which they would certainly not fail to requite!”
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva recognizes kindness and repays it.
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva abide in the power of patience? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, even when all sentient beings should harm them, is able to maintain a mind free from anger and malice toward them, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva abiding in the power of patience.
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva experience supreme joy? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees sentient beings who have already achieved accomplishment in the practices of the three vehicles, he experiences profound joy in his heart; this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva experiencing supreme joy.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not abandon sentient beings?
Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva desires to universally rescue and deliver all sentient beings, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva not to abandon sentient beings.”
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly give rise to great compassion?
Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the various supreme practices of a bodhisattva, they always form this thought:"

"For the benefit of each and every sentient being, even if I must remain in the great hells for as many immeasurable and innumerable *gaṅgā* sands of kalpas as there are beings, undergoing various heavy sufferings—whether being burned, boiled, cut, or severed; whether being impaled, suspended, ground, or pounded—I shall endure such immeasurable miseries until all those classes of sentient beings have mounted the Buddha-vehicle and entered parinirvāṇa. Even when the entire realm of sentient beings has thus been exhausted, my heart of great compassion shall never grow weary or desist."
This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva constantly gives rise to great compassion.

"How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, with a mind of reverence and faith toward their teachers and elders, consult them, receive their instructions, and make offerings to them as if they were the Buddhas?"

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, seeking unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, reveres and obeys their teachers and elders without any attachment or longing, this is for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to serve, attend to, and make offerings to all teachers and elders with a mind of reverence and faith, as if serving the Buddhas."
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seek to practice the pāramitās? Subhūti,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva single-mindedly seeks to study all the pāramitās without regard for other matters, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seeking to practice the pāramitās."
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the second bhūmi, they should contemplate and train in these eight dharmas so as to bring them quickly to fulfillment.
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s diligent pursuit of extensive learning with constant insatiability, and their non-attachment to the literal words of the teachings they have heard?”
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts diligent effort and forms this thought:

'Whether in this buddha-field or in the worlds of the ten directions, whatever true Dharma is taught by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, I shall hear it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and study it to the ultimate point so that nothing is left out; yet, within it, I shall not be attached to words.'"

"This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to diligently seek extensive learning without ever becoming weary or satisfied, and not to become attached to the words of the teachings they have heard.
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly practice the gift of Dharma with an undefiled mind, extensively transforming and guiding others without becoming self-exalting?"

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva proclaims the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, they do not even hold these roots of goodness for themselves and dedicate them toward enlightenment, much less seek any other matter!"

Although they extensively transform and guide others, they do not rely on this as a basis for self-conceit; this is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s constant practice of the gift of Dharma with an undefiled mind, whereby they widely open the way to enlightenment yet remain free from self-exaltation.
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva plant various roots of goodness for the purpose of adorning and purifying a buddha-field, yet, although they dedicate these roots, do not exalt themselves? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices various roots of goodness with courageous diligence, desiring to adorn the pure lands of all buddhas and to purify the mental lands of both self and others, and though they act for this purpose, do not become haughty—this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to plant various roots of goodness for the purpose of adorning and purifying a buddha-field, yet, although they dedicate them, do not exalt themselves.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, neither grow weary of the boundless cycle of birth and death nor become arrogant or indolent? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring all sentient beings to fulfillment, plants roots of goodness and purifies Buddha-fields, and until they have perfected the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), undergoes the diligent hardships of boundless birth and death without weariness and without self-exaltation—this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, neither grows weary of the boundless cycle of birth and death nor becomes arrogant or indolent.”
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell in shame and modesty yet remain unattached? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva seeks exclusively for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they possess shame and modesty regarding the mental orientations of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas such that they never give rise to them even for a moment; furthermore, they remain unattached even toward those [orientations]. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in shame and modesty yet remains unattached."
“Subhūti! When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the third stage, they should constantly abide in these five dharmas.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 415, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter 18: Cultivating the Stages, Part Two. “What is meant by a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwelling in an araṇya (forest hermitage) and never abandoning it?”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seeks unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and transcends the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to dwell in an araṇya and never abandon it."
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delight in having few desires? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not even seek great enlightenment for their own sake, much less do they desire the affairs of the world or those of the two vehicles!”
This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to always delight in having few desires.
"What is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delighting in contentment? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, solely for the sake of realizing all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), has no attachment to other matters, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who always delights in contentment.
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandon the qualities of ascetic purification (dhūtaguṇa)? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly gives rise to the patient acceptance that investigates the profound Dharma, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandons the qualities of ascetic purification.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandon the precepts? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains steadfast and unshakable in the points of training, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to never abandon the precepts.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to a desire-thought toward exquisite sensual pleasures, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva developing a profound sense of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delight in generating a mind associated with quiescence? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all phenomena have never arisen or been produced, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to always delight in generating a mind associated with quiescence.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquish all things? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp at any internal or external phenomena whatsoever, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishing all things.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind not become stuck or submerged? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva never gives rise to a thought regarding any station of consciousness, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind not to become stuck or submerged.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain free from attachment toward all things? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva never entertains thoughts regarding any phenomena, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to always remain free from attachment toward all things.”
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the fourth stage, they should uphold and not abandon these ten dharmas.
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s way of remaining far removed from the household life?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva travels through the buddha-fields and, wherever he is born, always delights in leaving the household life, shaving off his hair and beard, donning the dharma robes, and manifesting as a śramaṇa—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who should remain far removed from the household life."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from bhikṣuṇīs? Subhūti!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from all bhikṣuṇīs, not dwelling with them even for the duration of a finger-snap, nor giving rise to any improper thoughts toward them; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from bhikṣuṇīs."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from stinginess regarding households? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects in this way:”

"I ought to bring long-term benefit and happiness to all sentient beings; now that this sentient being has, through the power of their own merit, encountered such a noble family of donors, I should not harbor stinginess or envy toward them."
Having reflected thus, one distances oneself from stinginess regarding one's home; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance themselves from stinginess regarding their home.
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance themselves from anger and strife within assemblies?"
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva thinks thus:

'If there are śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas within an assembly, or if the essential teachings corresponding to their vehicles are being expounded therein, it may cause me to fall away from the mind of great enlightenment; therefore, I must certainly distance myself from such assemblies.'"

He further thought: "Those who engage in anger and strife cause sentient beings to give rise to hatred and harm, thereby committing various kinds of evil and unwholesome karma; this already violates the path to the happy realms, let alone the Great Enlightenment!"
"Therefore, one must certainly distance oneself from anger and contention.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance themselves from anger and contention within assemblies.
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance themselves from self-praise and the disparagement of others?"

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any internal or external phenomena at all, they should therefore remain far removed from praising themselves and disparaging others; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva remaining far removed from praising themselves and disparaging others."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the ten unwholesome paths of action?
Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects in this way:”

"These ten types of unwholesome courses of action can even obstruct rebirth in the happy realms of humans and devas; how much more so will they act as obstacles to the Noble Path and Great Enlightenment!"
"Therefore, I must certainly distance myself from them.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance himself from the ten unwholesome paths of action.
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from overweening pride and arrogance?"

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma capable of giving rise to such pride and arrogance, he should therefore distance himself from it; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s distancing himself from overweening pride and arrogance."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from perversions? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives that the objects of perversion are entirely unapprehendable, for this reason they must certainly remain far removed from perversions; this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to remain far removed from perversions.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from hesitation? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva observes that the objects of hesitation are entirely unapprehendable, for this reason they must certainly remain far removed from hesitation; this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to remain far removed from hesitation."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion?

Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive at all any phenomenon of greed, hatred, or delusion, they should therefore remain far removed from these three dharmas; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion."
"Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the fifth stage, they should always remain far removed from these ten dharmas.
How should a bodhisattva-mahāsattva fulfill the six pāramitās?"

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; furthermore, by abiding in these six perfections, the Buddhas and those of the two vehicles are able to cross over the shoreless ocean of the five kinds of objects of knowledge."
What are the five? First, the past; second, the future.
Third, the present; fourth, the ineffable;
fifth, the unconditioned.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the six pāramitās.
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the mind of a śrāvaka?
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'The minds of śrāvakas are not those that realize the path to unsurpassed great bodhi, and therefore they should be shunned.'"
Why is this? Because they are weary of birth and death.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the mind of a śrāvaka.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the mind of a pratyekabuddha?
Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought as this:”
"The minds of the pratyekabuddhas should be avoided, for they do not constitute the path for realizing unsurpassed great bodhi. Why is this?
Because they delight in nirvāṇa."
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from a mind of feverish affliction?"
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'This tormented mind cannot realize the path to unsurpassed great bodhi; therefore, it should be abandoned.'"
Why is this? Because they fear birth and death.
This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should remain far removed from a mind of feverish affliction.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid the state of mind characterized by displeasure and dejection when seeing a beggar approach? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:”
"This mind of sorrow and distress does not serve as a means for realizing the unsurpassed Great Bodhi; therefore, it should be abandoned.
Why is this? Because it is contrary to loving-kindness and compassion."
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from a mind of displeasure and dejection when seeing a beggar approach.
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from a mind of regret and sorrowful attachment after giving away all one's possessions?"
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'This mind of regret is not the path for realizing unsurpassed great enlightenment, and therefore it should be abandoned.'"
Why is this? Because it violates my original vow.
That is to say, when I first resolved to attain bodhicitta, I made this vow:
"Whatever I possess that is requested by seekers, I have never given it away fruitlessly according to their desires.
Why, then, would I now feel regret after having already given?
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance themselves from the mind of attachment, longing, and remorse regarding all things they have relinquished.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid the mind of deceitful guile toward those who come seeking [their help]?
Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought as this:”
"This deceitful mind is not the path for realizing unsurpassed great bodhi and should therefore be abandoned.
Why is this? Because it contradicts one's original vow."
It means that when I first resolved upon bodhicitta, I made this vow:
"Whatever I possess, I shall not let it go empty-handed to those who come seeking it according to their desires.
How could I now deceive them with hypocrisy?
“This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance themselves from the mind of artful deception toward those who come seeking [their help]. Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the sixth stage, they should constantly fulfill the six dharmas previously mentioned, as well as distance themselves from the six dharmas subsequently mentioned.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the grasping at a self, up to and including the grasping at a viewer? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that from the self up to the viewer they are ultimately non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the grasping at a self, up to and including the grasping at a viewer.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the attachment to annihilation? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all phenomena are ultimately unarisen because they lack the meaning of annihilation, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the attachment to annihilation.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the attachment to permanence? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is neither produced nor subject to impermanence, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the attachment to permanence.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the perception of signs? Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that afflictions such as greed are non-existent, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the perception of signs.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the grasping at views?
Subhūti, because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the intrinsic nature of any views whatsoever, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the grasping at views.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*)? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of name-and-form is entirely non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to name-and-form."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to the aggregates? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all aggregates is entirely non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to the aggregates.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to the sense-bases (*āyatana*)? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all sense-bases is entirely non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to the sense-bases.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to the elements (*dhātu*)? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all elements is entirely non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to the elements.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from clinging to the truths? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all truths is utterly non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from clinging to the truths.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to dependent origination? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of dependent origination is entirely non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to dependent origination.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to and grasping at the three realms? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of the three realms is entirely non-existent and unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to and grasping at the three realms.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from all attachment to phenomena? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is like space and is thus unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from all attachment to phenomena.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to all phenomena as being either conformable or non-conformable to reality? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is utterly unapprehendable, because there is neither that which is conformable nor that which is non-conformable to reality, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to all phenomena as being either conformable or non-conformable to reality."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to views based on the Buddha? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that attachment to views based on the Buddha does not lead to seeing the Buddha, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to views based on the Buddha."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to views based on phenomena? Subhūti,

because a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is invisible, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to views based on phenomena."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to views based on the Saṃgha? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the harmonious assembly is signless, unconditioned, and invisible, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to views based on the Saṃgha."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to views based on the precepts? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the natures of both transgression and merit are neither existent nor non-existent, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to remain far removed from attachment to views based on the precepts.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from the attachment to views based on emptiness? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all empty phenomena are entirely non-existent and invisible, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance himself from the attachment to views based on emptiness.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from aversion and fear toward emptiness?

Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, they will see that emptiness does not conflict with or harm emptiness; therefore, neither aversion nor fear can be found. For this reason, one should not feel aversion or fear toward the dharma of emptiness. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from aversion and fear toward emptiness."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the thorough penetration of emptiness? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the thorough penetration of emptiness."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the realization of the signless?
Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not mentally engage with any signs, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the realization of the signless."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to any cognition regarding the phenomena of the three realms, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the purity of the three spheres? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is fully endowed with the ten paths of wholesome action that are completely pure, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the purity of the three spheres.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill compassion for sentient beings and remain unattached to sentient beings? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained great compassion and the purification of the buddha-field, yet remains entirely without attachment, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill compassion for sentient beings and remain unattached to sentient beings."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the equal vision of all phenomena, as well as remain without attachment therein? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither increases nor decreases any phenomena and has no attachment whatsoever to them, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the vision of the equality of all phenomena, as well as non-attachment therein.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the equal vision toward all sentient beings, as well as remain without attachment therein? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither increases nor decreases [the perception of] sentient beings and has no attachment whatsoever, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the equal vision toward all sentient beings, as well as being without attachment therein.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the thorough penetration of the principle of reality, and remain without attachment therein? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the true principle of all phenomena, thoroughly penetrates it as it truly is, yet has nothing to penetrate and no attachment whatsoever, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the thorough penetration of the true principle and non-attachment therein.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the knowledge of the patience regarding non-arising? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is patient with all phenomena as being without arising, without cessation, and without volitional construction, and understands that name-and-form are ultimately unarisen, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the knowledge of the patience regarding non-arising.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the principle of the single characteristic of all phenomena? Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the non-dual characteristic regarding all phenomena, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the principle of the single characteristic of all phenomena.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the eradication of conceptualization? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to conceptualization regarding any phenomena, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the eradication of conceptualization.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete relinquishing of all perceptions?

Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes the perception of the small, the great, and the immeasurable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the complete relinquishing of all perceptions.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete distancing from all views? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva distances themselves from the views of the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the complete distancing from all views.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete distancing from afflictions?

Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva abandons all outflows, afflictions, and the continuity of habitual tendencies, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfilling the complete distancing from afflictions.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the stage of śamatha and vipaśyanā? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the stage of śamatha and vipaśyanā.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the taming of the mind? Subhūti,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not cling to the three realms, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the taming of the mind.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the state of a tranquil mind? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva skillfully restrains the six sense faculties, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the state of a tranquil mind.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates and attains the Buddha-eye, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill non-attachment? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes the six sense bases, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill non-attachment.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the ability to go to any buddha-field at will and manifest his own body within the assemblies of those buddhas?
Subhūti!...”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates supreme supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), travels to various buddha-fields to serve and make offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and requests them to turn the wheel of Dharma to deliver sentient beings—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of going to any buddha-field at will and manifesting his own body within the assemblies of those Buddhas.
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the seventh stage, they should always remain far removed from the former twenty dharmas and should bring the latter twenty dharmas to fulfillment.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the thorough entry into the mental activities of all sentient beings? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva,

by means of a single moment of wisdom, knows as they truly are the minds and mental factors of all sentient beings, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfilling the thorough entry into the mental activities of all sentient beings.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the mastery of the various supernormal powers? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva plays with the various sovereign supernormal powers, desiring to approach and make offerings to the Buddhas, he travels from one buddha-field to another buddha-field, yet is able to remain free from the thought that he is traveling through buddha-fields."
“Subhūti! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the mastery of the superknowledges.
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the vision of all buddha-fields, and, according to what they see, personally adorn and purify various buddha-fields?”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in a single buddha-field, they are able to see the infinite buddha-fields of the ten directions and can manifest them as well, yet they never give rise to the notion of 'buddha-fields.'"

Furthermore, for the sake of maturing all sentient beings, he manifests and dwells in the position of a universal monarch (cakravartin) over a trichiliocosm, adorning himself therewith; yet he is also able to relinquish it without any attachment. This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of beholding all buddha-fields and, according to what he has seen, personally purifying various buddha-fields.
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the worship and service of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and observe the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, correctly discerns the meaning and intent of the Dharma, this is called serving the Buddhas with the offering of the Dharma; furthermore, to contemplate the *dharmakāya* of the Buddhas is what constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of serving and making offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, by contemplating the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is.
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the eighth stage, they should diligently fulfill these four dharmas.
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties?”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, abiding in the ten powers of a buddha, understands as they truly are the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties."
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete purification of the buddha-field? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, purifies the mental activities of all sentient beings, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the complete purification of the buddha-field."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the meditative stabilization like an illusion and repeatedly enter various concentrations? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this meditative stabilization, although they can accomplish all activities, the mind does not waver at all regarding phenomena; furthermore, because they have fully matured the cultivation of this meditative stabilization, it manifests repeatedly without the need for deliberate application. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the meditative stabilization like an illusion and repeatedly enter various concentrations.”

"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the entry into all states of existence by manifesting through spontaneous birth, in accordance with the ripening of the roots of goodness of sentient beings?
Subhūti!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring sentient beings to maturity, enters into various states of existence and manifests birth according to what is appropriate for their superior roots of goodness, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva entering into various states of existence and manifesting spontaneous birth (upapāduka) in accordance with the ripening of the roots of goodness of sentient beings.
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the ninth stage, they should diligently fulfill these four dharmas.
What are the ways in which bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should fulfill the encompassing of great vows for boundless locations, so that whatever they vow, all may be realized?”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already fully cultivated the six pāramitās to the point of ultimate perfection, they will be able to realize whatever they wish for—whether it be for the purpose of purifying the buddha-fields or for the purpose of maturing sentient beings. This is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the great vow to encompass infinite locations, such that whatever they aspire to, they cause to be realized."
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the knowledge of the diverse languages of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and so forth? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme analytical knowledge of language (nirukti-pratisaṃvid), he is able to thoroughly understand the distinctions among the speech and sounds of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the knowledge of the diverse languages of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and so forth.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill unimpeded eloquence? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme analytical knowledge of eloquence, so as to be able to teach inexhaustibly for the sake of all sentient beings, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill unimpeded eloquence.”
“What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of entering the womb? Subhūti!

Although a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is in fact always born by transformation in all places of birth, for the benefit of sentient beings they manifest entry into a womb, wherein they fully possess boundless superior qualities. This is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of entering the womb.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of birth? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva is born from the womb, they manifest various rare and sublime events, causing all sentient beings who see them to rejoice and obtain great benefit and happiness. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the perfection of birth.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of family lineage? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is born into a great kṣatriya clan or a great brāhmaṇa clan, with parents who are truly pure—this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the perfection of family lineage.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of the excellence of lineage? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is always born within the lineage of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the excellence of lineage.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of having a retinue? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has as his retinue exclusively an immeasurable and innumerable assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of having a retinue.”
“What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of the birth-body?

Subhūti, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is first born, his body is endowed with all the marks and signs; he emits a great radiance that pervasively illuminates boundless Buddha-worlds and causes those worlds to tremble in six ways. Sentient beings who encounter this light all receive benefit. This is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of the birth-body.”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of renunciation?

Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva goes forth from home, surrounded by immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings who follow, honor, and praise him, he proceeds to the site of enlightenment, shaves off his hair and beard, dons the three dharma robes, and takes up the alms bowl; leading immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, he causes them to ride upon the three vehicles toward parinirvāṇa. This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the perfection of renunciation.”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of adorning the bodhi tree? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through the power of their preeminent roots of goodness and vast vows, brings forth such a great bodhi tree—having lapis lazuli for its trunk and pure gold for its roots, with branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all composed of the seven supreme jewels; a tree so tall and wide that it completely covers the trichiliocosm, its radiance shining throughout the worlds of the Ganges-sand number of Buddhas in the ten directions—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfilling the perfection of adorning the bodhi tree."
“What is the fulfillment and perfection of all qualities for a bodhisattva mahāsattva? Subhūti,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the sublime provisions of merit and wisdom, brings sentient beings to maturity, and purifies the buddha-fields— this is the fulfillment and perfection of all qualities for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the tenth stage, they should diligently fulfill these twelve dharmas.
How is it that once bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have dwelt in the tenth stage, they may be said to be no different from all Tathāgatas?”

Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already perfected the six pāramitās, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; having attained all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, if they further sever the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies, they abide in the stage of a buddha.
For this reason it is said:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already dwelled in the tenth stage, one should say that they are no different from the Tathāgatas.
"Subhūti! [the Buddha continued.]
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling in the tenth stage, proceed to the stage of a Tathāgata? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, through skill in means, practices the six pāramitās and the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. He transcends the stage of pure observation, the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having seen the truths, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the pratyekabuddha, and the stage of the bodhisattva. Furthermore, he eternally severs the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies, and thus becomes a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, abiding in the stage of a Tathāgata.
"Subhūti! In this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwelling in the tenth stage proceeds toward the stage of a Tathāgata. Subhūti!"
Based on this, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva has set out upon the Mahāyāna.
Chapter 19: Departing from Abiding, Part One “Furthermore, Subhūti!
Regarding your question, "From where does such a Great Vehicle emerge, and where does it abide?
