Subhūti, such a Great Vehicle emerges from within the three realms and abides within the knowledge of all modes; yet, because it employs non-duality as its means, there is neither emergence nor abiding.
Why is that? Subhūti!

Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the knowledge of all modes—these two dharmas are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
Why is this? Subhūti!
A signless dharma does not abide having already emerged, does not abide about to emerge, and does not abide emerging now.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Those who wish for uncharacterized phenomena (*animitta-dharma*) to have emergence or abiding would likewise wish for the emptiness of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu-śūnyatā*) to have emergence or abiding; yet the emptiness of the dharma-realm cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is empty; the dharma-realm is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!

If anyone wishes to claim that the signless dharma has emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that suchness-emptiness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the secure realm, the peaceful realm, the realm of abandonment, the realm of detachment, and the realm of cessation-emptiness also have emergence and abiding; yet, from the emptiness of suchness up to the emptiness of cessation, these cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because true thusness is empty; true thusness is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on, up to the realm of cessation being empty; the realm of cessation is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that phenomena which are signless have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of form also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of form cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because form is empty;
the emptiness of form is itself empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that the signless dharma has emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty; feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that phenomena which are signless have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of the sense-base of the eye also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the sense-base of the eye cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the eye-base is empty; the eye-base is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that phenomena which are without marks (animitta) have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, would likewise wish for the emptiness of the form-base (*rūpāyatana*) to have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the form-base cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).”
Why is this? Because the sphere of form is empty; the sphere of form is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone should wish for the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish for the emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena to also have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty; the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, would likewise wish for the emptiness of the eye-faculty to have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the eye-faculty cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
Why is this? Because the eye-element is empty; the eye-element is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that phenomena which are signless (animitta) have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements (śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, and manaḥ-dhātu-śūnyatā) also has emergence and abiding; yet, the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty; the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for signless phenomena to have emergence and abiding, would likewise wish for the emptiness of the form realm (*rūpadhātu-śūnyatā*) to have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the form realm cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).”
Why is this? Because the realm of form is empty; the realm of form is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that the signless dharma has emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are empty; the emptiness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena is the emptiness of their own intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, would likewise wish for the emptiness of the eye-consciousness element to have emergence or abiding; yet the emptiness of the eye-consciousness element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
Why is this? Because the eye-consciousness element is empty; the eye-consciousness element is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone should wish for a signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish for the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements to also have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness are empty; the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness are empty because their intrinsic nature is empty.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, would likewise wish for the emptiness of eye-contact to have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of eye-contact cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
Why is this? Because eye-contact is empty; eye-contact is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that signless phenomena have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty; the emptiness of the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for unconditioned phenomena (*animitta-dharma*) to emerge or abide are likewise wishing for the emptiness of the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition to also emerge and abide; yet the emptiness of the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).”

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty; the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone should wish for the dharma of signlessness to have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish for the emptiness of the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions to also have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are empty; the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are empty of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for uncharacterized phenomena (*animitta-dharma*) to emerge from or abide within [the world] are likewise wishing for the emptiness of dream-objects (*svapna-śūnyatā*) to have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of dream-objects cannot emerge from the triple world (*traidhātuka*), nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).”
Why is this? Because dream-objects are empty; dream-objects are empty because their intrinsic nature is empty. "Subhūti!

If anyone wishes to claim that phenomena which are without marks (animitta) have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that illusions, mirages, echoes, reflections, shadows, flowers in the sky, and transformations—which are themselves empty—also have emergence and abiding. Yet, from illusions being empty up to transformations being empty, these cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the wisdom of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because illusory things are empty; illusory things are empty of their own intrinsic nature, and even transformations are empty; transformations are empty of their own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to maintain that signless phenomena have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to maintain that the emptiness of the perfection of giving also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the perfection of giving cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the perfection of giving is empty, the perfection of giving is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

Those who wish for the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding would likewise wish for the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom to also have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty; and because the emptiness of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is itself empty of intrinsic nature.

"Subhūti! Those who wish for signless dharmas to have emergence and abiding, would thereby wish for internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) itself to have emergence and abiding; yet internal emptiness cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*)."
Why is this? Because internal emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that the signless (*animitta*) dharma has emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of the non-dispersal of dispersion, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature also have emergence and abiding. However, from the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, these cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the external is empty of the emptiness of the external, and its own nature is empty; and so on, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, which is empty of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and its own nature is empty.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharmas to have emergence and abiding, would likewise wish for the emptiness of the four applications of mindfulness to have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the four applications of mindfulness cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all aspects.”
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty; the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness is the emptiness of their own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!

If anyone should wish for the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish for the emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path to also have emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the four right efforts, up to the emptiness of the eightfold noble path, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the four right efforts are empty, and the four right efforts are empty of their own intrinsic nature; and so on, up to the eightfold noble path being empty, and the eightfold noble path being empty of its own intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharmas to have emergence or abiding, would likewise wish for even the emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha to have emergence or abiding; yet the emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).”
Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha are empty; the ten powers of a Buddha are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone were to claim that phenomena which are signless have emergence or abiding, they would likewise be claiming that the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.

Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses are empty; the self-nature of the four fearlessnesses is empty, and so on, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha being empty; the self-nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is empty.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharmas to have emergence or abiding would likewise wish for stream-enterers to have birth in the evil destinies, once-returners to have repeated births, non-returners to have birth in the desire realm, great bodhisattvas to have births for their own benefit, and arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and tathāgatas to have further births; yet such things do not exist.”
Why is this? Because for those such as the stream-enterers, rebirth in the evil destinies and so forth cannot be found. "Subhūti!

If anyone wishes to claim that dharmas which are signless have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of a stream-enterer also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of a stream-enterer cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the stream-enterer is empty; the emptiness of the stream-enterer is empty of its own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that phenomena which are signless have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that the emptiness of the once-returner, the non-returner, the arhat, the pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva, and the Tathāgata also has emergence and abiding; yet the emptiness of the once-returner, up to the emptiness of the Tathāgata, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the once-returner is empty, and the once-returner is empty of its own intrinsic nature; up to and including the Tathāgata, who is empty, and the Tathāgata is empty of his own intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."

If anyone wishes to claim that dharmas which are signless have emergence and abiding, they would likewise wish to claim that names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions—which are empty—also have emergence and abiding; yet names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions, being empty, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).

Why is this? Because names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions are empty; names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions are empty of their own intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Those who wish for the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding, would likewise wish for that which is unborn and unceasing, unstained and unpurified, signless, unconditioned, and empty to also have emergence and abiding. Yet, that which is unborn and unceasing, unstained and unpurified, signless, unconditioned, and empty cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).”

Why is this? Because it is unarisen and unceasing, unstained and unpurified, signless and unconditioned; because emptiness—unarisen, unceasing, unstained, unpurified, signless, and unconditioned—is itself empty of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! For this reason, this Great Vehicle emerges from within the three realms and abides in the knowledge of all modes; yet, because it employs non-duality as its skillful means, there is neither emergence nor abiding.”
Why is this? Because the signless dharma is without movement or change.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 416, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Two of the Nineteenth Chapter, "Emergence and Abiding," Section Two: "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
As for your question, "In what does such a Great Vehicle abide?", Subhūti!
Such a Great Vehicle abides nowhere at all.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are without any place of abiding.
For what reason?
Because the abiding place of all phenomena cannot be apprehended, Subhūti,
this Great Vehicle dwells in non-dwelling by means of non-apprehension as its expedient.
“Subhūti! Just as the dharma-realm neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm is empty of an intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.

“Subhūti! Just as suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the secure realm, the tranquil realm, the realm of abandonment, the realm of detachment, and the realm of cessation neither abide nor do not abide;”
Why is this so? Because the self-nature of true suchness (*tathatā*), up to and including the self-nature of the realm of cessation (*nirodhadhātu*), neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?

Because the self-nature of *tathatā* is empty of the self-nature of *tathatā*, and so on up to the self-nature of the realm of cessation being empty of the self-nature of the realm of cessation, the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as form neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Form, by its own nature, neither abides nor does it not abide.
Why is this? Because the self-nature of form is empty of the self-nature of form; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.
"Subhūti! Just as feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness neither abide nor do not abide. Why is that?
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no abiding in their own-being, nor do they not abide. Why is this?

Because the own-being of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is empty of the own-being of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the eye-base neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The sense base of the eye, by its very nature, neither abides nor does it not abide.
Why is this? Because the sense base of the eye is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense base of the eye; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this?
The self-nature of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind neither abides nor does it not abide.

Why is this? Because the self-nature of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty of the self-nature of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the sphere of form neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
The sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is, by its very nature, neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why?
Because the nature of the sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena neither abide nor do not abide. Why is that?
The intrinsic nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the eye-element neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
The nature of the eye-faculty neither abides nor does not abide.
Why? Because the nature of the eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.
"Subhūti! Just as the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements neither abide nor do not abide. Why is that?
The nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?

Because the nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements is empty of the nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the form realm neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this? Because...”
The intrinsic nature of the realm of form neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the realm of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realm of form; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this so?
The intrinsic nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the eye-consciousness element neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
The nature of the eye-consciousness element neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-consciousness element is empty of the nature of the eye-consciousness element; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this? Because...”
Because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness elements neither abide nor do not abide.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness elements is empty of the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness elements; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as eye-contact neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The intrinsic nature of eye-contact neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of eye-contact is empty of the intrinsic nature of eye-contact; the Mahāyāna is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
The self-nature of contact through the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the self-nature of contact through the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty of the self-nature of contact through the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition neither abide nor do not abide. Why is that?
The nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is empty of the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the various feelings produced with ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact as conditions neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this?
The various feelings produced with conditions of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact are by nature neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?

Because the self-nature of the various feelings produced with conditions of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact is empty of the self-nature of the various feelings produced with conditions of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as a dream-object neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The intrinsic nature of dream-objects neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of dream-objects is empty of the intrinsic nature of dream-objects; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as a magical illusion, a mirage, an echo, a reflected image, a shadow, a flower in the sky, and a transformation are neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this so?
Because the nature of illusory phenomena, up to and including transformations, neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the nature of illusory phenomena, up to and including transformations, is empty of the nature of illusory phenomena, up to and including transformations; so too is the Great Vehicle—neither abiding nor not abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the perfection of giving neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this? Because...”
The intrinsic nature of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?

Because the intrinsic nature of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as internal emptiness neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this? Because...”
Because the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.

“Subhūti! Just as external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, their intrinsic nature neither abides nor does it not abide. Why is that?

Because the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, is itself empty of the nature of the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does it not abide.
“Subhūti! Just as the four foundations of mindfulness neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this?
The four foundations of mindfulness abide neither in their own nature nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the own-nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is empty of the own-nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path neither abide nor do not abide;”
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

Because the intrinsic nature of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path is empty of the intrinsic nature of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path, so too is the Mahāyāna; it neither abides nor does it not abide.
"Subhūti! Even the ten powers of a Buddha neither abide nor do not abide. Why is that? Because..."
The self-nature of the Buddha’s ten powers neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the self-nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is empty of the self-nature of the Buddha’s ten powers; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.

“Subhūti! Just as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are by their very nature neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?

Because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as for a stream-enterer, birth in the evil destinies is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
For one who has entered the stream (*srotāpanna*), birth in the woeful realms is by its very nature neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?

Because the nature of birth in the woeful realms for one who has entered the stream is empty of the nature of birth in the woeful realms for one who has entered the stream; the Great Vehicle is likewise, being neither abiding nor non-abiding.

“Subhūti! Just as a once-returner is born again and again, and a non-returner is born in the desire realm, so too the great bodhisattva is born for the sake of their own benefit; whereas the arhat, the pratyekabuddha, and the tathāgata have no further birth, being neither abiding nor non-abiding.”

Why is this? Because for one who has come once, or for those who come again and again, up to and including the Tathāgata, there is no self-nature in subsequent existence that abides, nor is there any that does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the once-returner who returns to birth repeatedly, up to the Tathāgata who has no further births, is empty, so too is the Mahāyāna: neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as a stream-enterer neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The nature of a stream-enterer neither abides nor does not abide.
Why? Because the nature of a stream-enterer is empty of the nature of a stream-enterer; the Great Vehicle is likewise, neither abiding nor not abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, a pratyekabuddha, a bodhisattva, and a tathāgata neither abide nor do not abide. Why is that?
From the once-returner up to the Tathāgata, their intrinsic nature neither abides nor does it not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of those from the once-returner up to the Tathāgata is empty; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
"Subhūti! Just as names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this so?
Names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions have a nature that neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions is empty of the nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without marks and unconditioned, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this so?
Because it is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without marks and unconditioned, its self-nature neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the self-nature that is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without marks and unconditioned, is empty of arising and cessation, defilement and purity, and marks and conditioning; the Great Vehicle is likewise: it neither abides nor does not abide.
“Subhūti! For this reason, although this Great Vehicle has no abiding place, it dwells in non-abiding by means of the expedient of non-duality.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti! As for your question, 'Who, moreover, rides upon this Great Vehicle and departs?'— Subhūti!"
There is no one at all who, by means of this Great Vehicle, goes forth.
Why is that? Subhūti!
Whether it be the vehicle being ridden, the rider, the time, or the place—all such things are non-existent and cannot be apprehended. Why is this so?
Since all dharmas are non-existent and entirely unattainable, how can it be said that there is a vehicle to be mounted, one who mounts it, the time of mounting, or the place of mounting?
Therefore, it cannot be said that there is a vehicle which truly exists as a Great Vehicle from which one departs.
Why is this? "Subhūti!..."
Because "I" does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
In this way, because sentient beings up to and including those who see do not exist and cannot be apprehended, even one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.

Since true thusness (*tathatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), the realm of peace (*kṣemadhātu*), and so forth are likewise non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is also unobtainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because form is non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Since the eye-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because they are ultimately pure.
The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind likewise do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, even one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because the sense-field of form does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Since the eye-faculty does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
Since the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise non-existent and unattainable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unattainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because the non-existence of the form realm cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Because the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmadhātu) likewise do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Since the eye-consciousness element does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because they are ultimately pure.
Since the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!
Because eye-contact is non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
Because ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact likewise do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure. "Subhūti!
Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.

Since the various feelings produced with the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as conditions are likewise non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unobtainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because the perfection of generosity is non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because internal emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self- and common-characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is that? Because it is ultimately pure. "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is so]."
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

Because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unapprehendable.
Why is that? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha, because they are non-existent and unobtainable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unobtainable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

Because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is also unattainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because the stream-enterer is non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
Because the once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, and tathāgata do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because the fruit of stream-entry is non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is also unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because all-knowledge is non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!

Because there is no arising and no cessation, no defilement and no purity, no marks and no unconditioned, and because nothing exists and is unapprehendable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unapprehendable."
Why is that? Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti!..."
Because the past, future, and middle limits do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because going and coming do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Since whether one is practicing or abiding, there is nothing that exists and nothing that can be apprehended, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Because it is ultimately pure. "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is so]."
Because neither death nor birth exists and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle likewise cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because neither increase nor decrease exists and cannot be apprehended, one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "
Because it is ultimately pure.
Furthermore, Subhūti, regarding this matter,
what dharma is it that cannot be apprehended such that one says it is "unapprehendable"?

"Subhūti! In this context, because the dharma-realm cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable; likewise, because true thusness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, also cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this so? Because the dharma-realm is equal [to all things], it cannot be obtained in the past, cannot be obtained in the future, and cannot be obtained in the present, for it is ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom also cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity and the others cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, also cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because internal emptiness and the others are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable, they are said to be unapprehendable; because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are also unapprehendable, they are said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! It is because even the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended that they are said to be unapprehendable; it is because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, also cannot be apprehended that they are said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this so? Because the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because a stream-enterer cannot be apprehended, it is said that they are unapprehendable; because those from a once-returner up to a Tathāgata also cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because those such as the stream-enterers and others are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable; because the fruit of once-returning, up to and including the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because the fruit of stream-entry and so forth cannot be attained in the past, cannot be attained in the future, and cannot be attained in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without marks and unconditioned cannot be apprehended, it is said to be ‘unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because non-arising and so forth are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the first stage is unobtainable, it is said to be unobtainable; likewise, up to the tenth stage, because it is unobtainable, it is said to be unobtainable."
Why is this? Because the first stage and the others are not already attained, not yet to be attained, and not currently being attained, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! In this context, what are the ten stages? They are:

the stage of pure observation, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of possessing vision, the stage of attenuation, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of having completed what was to be done, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, and the stage of the Tathāgata. These are the ten stages.”

“Subhūti! Because the first bhūmi cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, it is said to be unapprehendable; up to and including because the first bhūmi cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said to be unapprehendable.

Because the second bhūmi through to the tenth bhūmi cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, they are said to be unapprehendable; up to and including because the second bhūmi through to the tenth bhūmi cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this so? Because within this, the first stage and the others are not already obtainable, not yet to be obtained, and not currently obtainable, for they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti! Because sentient beings to be matured cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, they are said to be unapprehendable; up to and including, because sentient beings to be matured cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within this, the maturation of sentient beings cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as yet to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being attained in the present, for it is ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the purification of the Buddha-field cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said to be unapprehendable; and so on, up to: because the purification of the Buddha-field cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, it is said to be unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because within this, the adornment and purification of the Buddha-field is not something that has been attained, will be attained, or is being attained now, for it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti! Because the five eyes cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, they are said to be unapprehendable; up to and including, because the five eyes cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are said to be unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because within this, the five eyes are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

"So it is, Subhūti! When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, although they contemplate that all phenomena are non-existent and utterly unobtainable because they are ultimately pure, there is no one who departs by means of the Great Vehicle and remains [elsewhere]. Nevertheless, taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, they mount the Great Vehicle, emerge from the birth and death of the triple world, and abide in the knowledge of all modes, benefiting and gladdening sentient beings until the end of the future."
Chapter 20: The Chapter on Surpassing Excellence, Part Two, Chapter Twenty of the Section on Surpassing Excellence, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Regarding the term "Mahāyāna": Mahāyāna transcends all those in the world—devas, humans, asuras, and so forth; it is the most honored, the most supreme, the highest, and the most wondrous.
“World-Honored One!

This Great Vehicle is equal to space; just as space can universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Great Vehicle universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.”
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is precisely the vehicle of the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One! [he continued.]

Furthermore, just as space cannot be seen to come, go, or abide, so too is the Mahāyāna: it cannot be seen to come, go, or abide; because it is without movement and without abiding, it is called the Mahāyāna.
"World-Honored One!

Furthermore, just as the past, future, and middle limits of space are all unapprehendable, so too is the Great Vehicle; its past, future, and middle limits are all unapprehendable. Because it is equal throughout the three times and transcends the three times, it is called the 'Great Vehicle.'"
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said, Subhūti!

The Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas consists of the six pāramitās, namely: the pāramitā of giving, the pāramitā of ethical discipline, the pāramitā of patience, the pāramitā of diligence, the pāramitā of meditative concentration, and the pāramitā of wisdom."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas refers to inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

The Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas refers to all the gates of dhāraṇī, all the gates of samādhi, and all samādhis—namely, the Samādhi of Heroic Progression (*śūraṅgama-samādhi*) up to the Samādhi of Non-attachment like Space (*ākāśa-asakta-samādhi*).
Furthermore, Subhūti,
the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas consists of the four applications of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. Subhūti!
One should know that such immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless merits are all the Mahāyāna of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
You have said: "The Mahāyāna surpasses all the world—including devas, humans, and asuras; it is the most honored, the most excellent, the highest, and the most sublime."
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
Subhūti! In this context, what is meant by "all the worlds of gods, humans, and asuras"?
It refers to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.

“Subhūti! If the desire realm were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if its nature as it is were eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of a substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or exquisite, and it could not transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the desire realm is that which is conceptualized, a mere composite, subject to transition and movement, and because everything up to the limit of all things is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and alteration, and entirely devoid of a real nature—therefore, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends and surpasses all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If form and the formless realm were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed the nature of being as it is, eternally constant, immutable, and possessed of a real essence—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would not be able to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the realms of form and formlessness are objects of conceptualization, being mere provisional aggregations subject to transition and movement—and because everything up to the ultimate is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If form were suchness—non-illusory, unchanging, non-perverted, real, and true; if its nature as it is were eternal, permanent, immutable, and possessed of a substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because form is that which is conceptually imputed, a mere composite, subject to change and movement, and because everything up to the ultimate is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation and alteration, and entirely devoid of a real intrinsic nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! If feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if their nature as it is were eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of a substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are objects of conceptualization, are merely provisional aggregations subject to change and movement, and because they are entirely impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation and alteration, and devoid of any real intrinsic nature—even unto all phenomena—this Great Vehicle is honored, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the eye base were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if it possessed an intrinsic nature that was eternal, constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout its entire existence—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the eye-base is that which is conceptually imputed, a mere composite, subject to transition and movement, and because everything up to all phenomena is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and alteration, and entirely devoid of a real intrinsic nature—therefore, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed an intrinsic nature that was eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout all time—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are objects of conceptualization, are merely provisional combinations subject to flux, and because they are all impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—therefore this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the sphere of form were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if its nature as it is were eternal, constant, unalterable, and possessed of a substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the sphere of form is that which is conceptualized, a mere composite, subject to change and movement, and so on, up to being entirely impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation and alteration, and devoid of any intrinsic nature—therefore this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed an intrinsic nature that was eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout all existence, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are conceptualized as such, are merely provisional combinations subject to change and movement, and because they are all impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation and alteration, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, transcending all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the eye-element were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-perverted, real, and true; if its 'as-it-is-ness' were eternally constant, immutable, and possessed of a substantial nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the eye-element is that which is conceptualized, a mere composite, subject to change and movement, and because everything up to [the other elements] is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation and alteration, and entirely devoid of a real nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind constituents were suchness—unfailing, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed a nature that was eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable, and possessed a substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it could not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are conceptualized as such, being merely provisional combinations subject to flux, and because they are all impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, transcending all worlds including the devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the form realm were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if it possessed an intrinsic nature that is eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout its entire existence—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, nor supreme, nor superior, nor sublime, and it would not be able to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the realm of form is an object of conceptualization, a provisional aggregation subject to transition and movement, and because everything up to all phenomena is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature; therefore, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed an intrinsic nature that was eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout all time, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are objects of conceptualization, are composite, and are subject to change—indeed, because all things are impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation, subject to alteration, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the eye-consciousness element were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if its nature as it is were eternal, constant, unalterable, and possessed of a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, superior, or sublime, and it would not be able to transcend all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of visual consciousness is that which is conceptualized, a mere composite, subject to transition and movement—and because everything up to all phenomena is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and alteration, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.”

“Subhūti! If the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness elements were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed an intrinsic nature that was eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout all time—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, superior, supreme, or sublime, and it would not be able to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are conceptualized as such, being composite, subject to change, and even unto all that is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation, subject to alteration, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—therefore this Mahāyāna is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If eye-contact were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if its nature as it is were eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of a real essence—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, superior, supreme, or sublime, and it would not be able to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because eye-contact is that which is conceptualized, a mere provisional combination subject to transition and movement, and because everything up to [the other sense-bases] is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if, by its very nature, it were eternally constant, immutable, and possessed of a real essence, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact are conceptualized as such, being merely provisional combinations subject to movement and change—and because everything up to all phenomena is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to transformation and alteration, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed a nature that is as-it-is, eternally constant, immutable, and possessed of a substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, supreme, preeminent, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are conceptualized, are merely provisional combinations, and are subject to movement—indeed, because they are all impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, real, and true; if they possessed an intrinsic nature that was eternally constant, immutable, and unalterable throughout all time—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it could not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the various feelings produced with the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as conditions are conceptualized, are merely provisional combinations, and are subject to movement—indeed, because they are all impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends and surpasses all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the dharma-realm were a truly existent entity rather than a non-existent one, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is not substantially existent and is of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If true suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, and the realm of peace are not substantially existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the perfection of giving were something truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would be unable to transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity is not truly existent—it is of a non-existent nature—this Great Vehicle is honored, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, transcending all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable, superior, supreme, or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not substantially existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If internal emptiness were a real existence and not a non-existence, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would be unable to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because inner emptiness is not truly existent and is of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras."

“Subhūti! If external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of the non-dispersal and dispersal of phenomena, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would not be able to transcend all worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are not truly existent—and because they are of a non-existent nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the four foundations of mindfulness were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to surpass all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are not truly existent and are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path were substantially existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are not substantially existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If even the ten powers of a Buddha were substantially existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are not substantially existent and are of the nature of non-existence, this Great Vehicle is honored, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would not be able to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not truly existent, being of a nature that is non-existent, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 417. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter Twenty: Surpassing Excellence (Part Two). "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
