If the nature of the lineage were a truly existent reality rather than something non-existent, then this Mahāyāna would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would be unable to transcend and surpass all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti! Because the dharma of the lineage is not truly existent and is of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the dharma of the eighth person, the dharma of a stream-enterer, the dharma of a once-returner, the dharma of a non-returner, the dharma of an arhat, the dharma of a pratyekabuddha, the dharma of a bodhisattva, and the dharma of a tathāgata were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or superior, nor supreme or sublime; it would not be able to transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

"Subhūti! Because the eighth dharma, up to and including the Tathāgata-dharma, are not substantially existent and are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the lineage-possessing person (gotrabhū-pudgala) were a real entity and not a non-entity, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it could not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because the person of the lineage is not truly existent, being of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it surpasses all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the individuals—the eighth-rank practitioner, the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, the arhat, the pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva, and the tathāgata—were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or superior, nor supreme or sublime; it would be unable to surpass all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Subhūti! Because the eighth person up to the Tathāgata person do not exist as real entities, and because they are of the nature of non-existence, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras—were truly existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime, and it would be unable to transcend all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras—are not truly existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it transcends all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the various immeasurable kinds of minds that arise within a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first generation of the mind of awakening until sitting upon the seat of sublime enlightenment, were substantially existent and not non-existent, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or excellent; it would not be able to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! From the first generation of the mind of awakening until sitting upon the seat of sublime enlightenment, the immeasurable varieties of minds that arise therein are not truly existent; because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, transcending all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the diamond-like wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva were a real existence and not a non-existence, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor superior or sublime; it would not be able to transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the vajra-like wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not truly existent, and because it is of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime; it surpasses all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the vajra-like wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva were a real entity and not non-existent, then the bodhisattva mahāsattva would not be able to use this vajra-like wisdom to realize that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, to forever sever the continuity of all afflictions and habitual tendencies, to attain the knowledge of all modes, nor would they be able to surpass all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the vajra-like wisdom of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not a real existence and is of a non-existent nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas employ this vajra-like wisdom to realize that the self-nature of all phenomena is empty; they forever sever the continuity of all afflictions and habitual tendencies, realize the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), and are likewise able to surpass all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the bodies of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs—were truly existent and not non-existent, then the majestic splendor and sublime virtues of those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not be able to surpass all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because the bodies of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs—are not substantially existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, the majestic radiance and sublime virtues of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas surpass all those in the world, including devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the light rays emitted by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were truly existent and not non-existent, then those light rays emitted by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would be unable to universally illuminate worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, nor would they be able to surpass all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because the light rays emitted by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are not substantially existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, the light rays emitted by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are able to universally illuminate as many worlds in each of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, and are also able to surpass all those in the world, including devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the sixty melodious qualities of the voice possessed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were truly existent and not non-existent, then those sixty melodious qualities of the voice possessed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would be unable to universally address the sentient beings to be converted throughout the immeasurable and innumerable worlds of the ten directions, nor would they be able to surpass all the worldlings, including devas, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti! Because the sixty melodious qualities of speech possessed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are not truly existent, and because they are of a non-existent nature, these sixty melodious qualities of speech possessed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are able to proclaim themselves throughout the immeasurable and innumerable worlds of the ten directions to the sentient beings to be converted, and are also able to surpass all those in the world, including devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were a real entity and not a non-entity, then that wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not be utterly pure; nor would it be such that no śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas of the entire world could turn it, nor could it surpass all the gods, humans, and asuras of the entire world."

Subhūti! Because the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is not a real existence, but is of the nature of non-existence, the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is utterly pure; no śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas in all the world are able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma, and it also surpasses all the world’s devas, humans, and asuras.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the sentient beings emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were truly existent and not non-existent, then the wheel of Dharma turned by those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not be able to cause those classes of sentient beings to attain parinirvāṇa in the realm of the wondrous nirvana without remainder, nor would it be able to surpass all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

"Subhūti! Because the sentient beings emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are not truly existent, but are of the nature of non-existence, the wheels of Dharma turned by those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are able to cause all those classes of sentient beings to attain parinirvāṇa in the realm of the wondrous nirvana without remainder, and they are also able to surpass all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras."
"Subhūti! For these various reasons and conditions, it is said that the Great Vehicle is venerable, supreme, preeminent, and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
21. Chapter on Non-existence, Part Two, Chapter Twenty-one, Section One: "Furthermore, Subhūti, you have said:
'The Great Vehicle is equal to space.'"
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
Why is this so? "Subhūti!

For example, just as the spatial dimensions of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below cannot be apprehended in space, so it is with the Great Vehicle: the spatial dimensions of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below cannot be apprehended. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space all forms and colors—long and short, high and low, square and round, crooked and straight—are unapprehendable, so too it is with the Great Vehicle: long and short, high and low, square and round, crooked and straight—all such forms and colors are unapprehendable. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space the manifest colors—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, azure, green, and so forth—all cannot be apprehended, so it is with the Great Vehicle: the manifest colors—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, azure, green, and so forth—all cannot be apprehended. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither past, nor future, nor present, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) neither past, nor future, nor present; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space neither increases nor decreases, neither advances nor recedes, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither increases nor decreases, neither advances nor recedes; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”
“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither defiled nor pure, so too is the Great Vehicle neither defiled nor pure; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is without arising, without cessation, without abiding, and without alteration, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) without arising, without cessation, without abiding, and without alteration; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither determinate nor indeterminate, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither determinate nor indeterminate. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is without seeing, without hearing, without sensing, and without cognizing, so too is the Great Vehicle without seeing, without hearing, without sensing, and without cognizing; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is not something to be known, not something to be attained, not something to be fully understood, not something to be permanently abandoned, not something to be realized, and not something to be cultivated, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is not something to be known, not something to be attained, not something to be fully understood, not something to be permanently abandoned, not something to be realized, and not something to be cultivated. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither a fruit nor a dharma that possesses a fruit, neither a maturation nor a dharma that possesses maturation, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither a fruit nor a dharma that possesses a fruit, neither a maturation nor a dharma that possesses maturation; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither a dharma characterized by desire nor a dharma free from desire, neither a dharma characterized by hatred nor a dharma free from hatred, neither a dharma characterized by delusion nor a dharma free from delusion, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither a dharma characterized by desire nor a dharma free from desire, neither a dharma characterized by hatred nor a dharma free from hatred, neither a dharma characterized by delusion nor a dharma free from delusion. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space one cannot find an initial generation of the mind of awakening, nor can one find anything up to and including the tenth generation of the mind of awakening, so it is with the Great Vehicle: one cannot find an initial generation of the mind of awakening, nor can one find anything up to and including the tenth generation of the mind of awakening. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space one cannot find the stage of pure observation, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having seen the truths, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, or the stage of the Tathāgata, so it is with the Great Vehicle: one cannot find the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space does not fall within the desire realm, does not fall within the form realm, and does not fall within the formless realm, so too is the Great Vehicle: it does not fall within the desire realm, does not fall within the form realm, and does not fall within the formless realm. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space one cannot find those entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry, those entering the once-returning stage or the fruit of once-returning, those entering the non-returning stage or the fruit of non-returning, those entering the stage of arhatship or the fruit of arhatship, those entering the stage of pratyekabuddhahood or the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood, nor a bodhisattva or a Tathāgata, so it is with the Great Vehicle: one cannot find those entering the stream up to and including a Tathāgata. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space the stage of a śrāvaka, the stage of a pratyekabuddha, the stage of a bodhisattva, and the stage of a tathāgata cannot be found, so it is with the Great Vehicle: the stage of a śrāvaka, the stage of a pratyekabuddha, the stage of a bodhisattva, and the stage of a tathāgata cannot be found therein. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant, neither associated nor dissociated, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant, neither associated nor dissociated. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, and neither pure nor impure, so too is the Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna): it is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, and neither pure nor impure. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither empty nor non-empty, neither characterized by marks nor markless, and neither with vows nor vowless, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna): it is neither empty nor non-empty, neither characterized by marks nor markless, and neither with vows nor vowless. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither remote nor non-remote, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither remote nor non-remote; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”
"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither dark nor light, so too is the Great Vehicle neither dark nor light; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna); it is neither obtainable nor unobtainable. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither the aggregates, elements, or sense bases, nor is it apart from the aggregates, elements, or sense bases, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither the aggregates, elements, or sense bases, nor is it apart from the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither expressible nor inexpressible, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna); it is neither expressible nor inexpressible. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”
“Subhūti! For these and various other such reasons, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”

You have said: "Just as space can universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Mahāyāna universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings."
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Because sentient beings do not exist, you should know that space, too, does not exist.
Because space is non-existent, one should know that the Great Vehicle is also non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Great Vehicle is universally able to contain immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether it be sentient beings, or space, or the Great Vehicle—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because sentient beings are immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless, you should know that space is also immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless;
because space is immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless, you should know that the Great Vehicle is also immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless."
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of accommodating immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?

Whether it be sentient beings who are immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless; or space which is immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless; or the Great Vehicle which is immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless—all such things are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because sentient beings do not exist, you should know that space also does not exist.
Because space does not exist, you should know that the Great Vehicle also does not exist."
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is also non-existent.
Because "the incalculable" does not exist, one should know that "the boundless" also does not exist.
Because "the boundless" does not exist, one should know that all phenomena (*dharmas*) also do not exist.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally able to accommodate immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?
Whether it be sentient beings, space, the Great Vehicle, the immeasurable, the innumerable, the boundless, or all phenomena—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the self does not exist, you should know that sentient beings also do not exist.
Because sentient beings do not exist, you should know that the life-principle also does not exist."
Because the "life-principle" (jīva) does not exist, one should know that the "one who is born" (jāta) also does not exist.
Because the "one who is born" does not exist, one should know that the "nourisher" (poṣa) also does not exist.
Because the nourisher does not exist, one should know that the person (*puruṣa*) also does not exist.
Because the person does not exist, one should know that the individual (*pudgala*) also does not exist.
Because the *pudgala* does not exist, one should know that the mind-born (*manomaya*) also does not exist.
Because the mind-born does not exist, one should know that the youth (*māṇava*) also does not exist.
Because the "Child of the Sages" (Mañjuśrī) is non-existent, one should know that the agent is also non-existent.
Because the agent is non-existent, one should know that the recipient is also non-existent.
Because the experiencer does not exist, one should know that the knower also does not exist.
Because the knower does not exist, one should know that the seer also does not exist.
Because the seer does not exist, one should know that space also does not exist.
Because space does not exist, one should know that the Great Vehicle also does not exist.
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is also non-existent.
Because the "innumerable" does not exist, one should know that the "boundless" also does not exist.
Because the "boundless" does not exist, one should know that all phenomena (*dharmas*) also do not exist.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of accommodating immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?

Whether it be "I" up to "the seer," or space, or the Great Vehicle, or the immeasurable, or the innumerable, or the boundless, or all dharmas—all such things as these are non-existent, because they cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Because everything from the self up to the viewer does not exist, you should know that the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) also does not exist.
Because the dharma-realm does not exist, you should know that space (*ākāśa*) also does not exist."
Because space is non-existent, one should know that the Great Vehicle is also non-existent.
Because the Great Vehicle is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the incalculable is also non-existent.
Because the incalculable is non-existent, one should know that the boundless is also non-existent.
Because the infinite is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena are likewise non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of accommodating immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite sentient beings.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether it be from the self up to the perceiver, or the dharma-realm, or space, or the Great Vehicle, or the immeasurable, or the innumerable, or the boundless, or all dharmas—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Because everything from 'self' up to 'seer' is non-existent, you should know that True Suchness (*tathatā*), the Reality Limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), the realm of peace (*kṣemadhātu*), and so forth, are likewise mutually non-existent."
Because suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth are non-existent, one should know that space is also non-existent.
Because space is non-existent, one should know that the Great Vehicle is also non-existent.
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is also non-existent.
Because the "innumerable" is non-existent, one should know that the "boundless" is also non-existent.
Because the "boundless" is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena (*dharmas*) are also non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of accommodating immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?

Whether it be "I" up to "the seer," or suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth; or whether it be space, the Great Vehicle, the immeasurable, the innumerable, the boundless, or all phenomena—since all such things as these are non-existent and unapprehendable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Because everything from the self up to the perceiver does not exist, one should know that form (*rūpa*) also does not exist.
Because form does not exist, one should know that space (*ākāśa*) also does not exist."
Because space is non-existent, one should know that the Great Vehicle is also non-existent.
Because the Great Vehicle is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable is also non-existent.
Because the innumerable is non-existent, one should know that the boundless is also non-existent.
Because the infinite is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena are likewise non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally able to accommodate immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite sentient beings.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether it be the self up to the perceiver, or form, or space, or the Great Vehicle, or the immeasurable, or the innumerable, or the boundless, or all dharmas—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because from 'self' up to 'perceiver' there is nothing whatsoever, you should know that feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are likewise successively non-existent."
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-existent, one should know that space is also non-existent.
Because space is non-existent, one should know that the Great Vehicle is also non-existent.
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is also non-existent.
Because the "innumerable" is non-existent, one should know that the "boundless" is also non-existent.
Because the "boundless" is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena (*dharmas*) are also non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally able to accommodate immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?

Whether it be "I" up to "the seer," or feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; or space, or the Great Vehicle, or the immeasurable, or the innumerable, or the boundless, or all dharmas—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Because that which ranges from 'I' to the 'seer' does not exist, you should know that the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) also does not exist.
Because the eye-base does not exist, you should know that space (*ākāśa*) also does not exist."
Because space is non-existent, one should know that the Great Vehicle is also non-existent.
Because the Great Vehicle is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable is also non-existent.
Because the innumerable is non-existent, one should know that the boundless is also non-existent.
Because the infinite is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena are likewise non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of accommodating immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite sentient beings.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether it be from "self" up to "seer," or the sense-base of the eye, or space, or the Great Vehicle, or the immeasurable, or the innumerable, or the boundless, or all phenomena—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because from 'self' up to 'perceiver' there is nothing existent, you should know that the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise successively non-existent."
Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not exist, one should know that space also does not exist.
Because space does not exist, one should know that the Great Vehicle also does not exist.

Because from 'self' up to 'perceiver' there is nothing existent, you should know that the once-returner, the non-returner, the arhat, the pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva, and the Tathāgata are likewise non-existent."
Because the once-returner, up to and including the Tathāgata, do not exist, one should know that space also does not exist.
Because space does not exist, one should know that the Great Vehicle also does not exist.
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is also non-existent.
Because the "countless" is non-existent, one should know that the "boundless" is also non-existent.
Because the "boundless" is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena (*dharmas*) are also non-existent.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally able to accommodate immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?

Whether it be from "self" up to "seer," or from "once-returner" up to "Tathāgata," or whether it be space, the Great Vehicle, the immeasurable, the innumerable, the boundless, or all phenomena—since all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because everything from the self up to the perceiver does not exist, you should know that the śrāvaka also does not exist.
Because the śrāvaka does not exist, you should know that the pratyekabuddha also does not exist."
Because the pratyekabuddha is non-existent, one should know that the samyaksaṃbuddha is also non-existent.
Because the samyaksaṃbuddha is non-existent, one should know that the Mahāyāna is also non-existent.
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the Pratyekabuddhayāna is also non-existent.
Because the Pratyekabuddhayāna is non-existent, one should know that the Śrāvakayāna is also non-existent.
Because the Śrāvaka vehicle does not exist, one should know that the Tathāgata also does not exist.
Because the Tathāgata does not exist, one should know that the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) also does not exist.
Because all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) does not exist, one should know that space (*ākāśa*) also does not exist.
Because space does not exist, one should know that the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) also does not exist.
Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) is also non-existent.
Because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the innumerable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is also non-existent.
Because "the incalculable" does not exist, one should know that "the boundless" also does not exist;
because "the boundless" does not exist, one should know that all phenomena (*dharmas*) also do not exist.
For this reason, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of accommodating immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Why is this so, Subhūti?

Whether it be "I" up to "seer," or a śrāvaka, or a pratyekabuddha, or a perfectly awakened one (samyaksaṃbuddha), or the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna), or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or the vehicle of the śrāvakas, or a Tathāgata, or all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā), or space, or the Great Vehicle, or the immeasurable, or the innumerable, or the boundless, or all phenomena (dharmas)—all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as the realm of nirvāṇa can universally accommodate immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Great Vehicle universally accommodate immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings."
For this reason, it is said:

just as space can universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Mahāyāna universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! You have said:
'Just as space cannot be seen to come, go, or abide, so too is the Great Vehicle; it cannot be seen to come, go, or abide.'"
"It is so! It is so! It is just as you have said."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Because all phenomena neither come nor go, and furthermore, they do not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because all phenomena—whether moving or stationary—are unapprehendable, for this reason, the Great Vehicle likewise has no place from which it comes, no place to which it goes, and no place where it abides that can be apprehended.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere.
Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; [the same applies to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness].
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are by nature nowhere from which they come, nowhere to which they go, and nowhere in which they abide.
Subhūti! The suchness of form is nowhere from which it comes, nowhere to which it goes, and nowhere in which it abides;
The suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Subhūti!
The intrinsic nature of form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no intrinsic nature from which they come, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere.
Subhūti! Form, in its own characteristic, has no place from which it comes, nor does it go anywhere, nor does it abide anywhere.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no intrinsic nature from which they come, nor do they go anywhere,
nor do they abide anywhere.
Why is this so, Subhūti?
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of form, up to and including consciousness, cannot be apprehended whether they are moving or stationary.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The sense-base of the eye comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere.
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the sense-base of the eye comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the eye-base comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The intrinsic nature of the sense base of the eye comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere.”
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of the eye-base comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of the sense base of the eye, up to and including the sense base of the mind, cannot be apprehended whether they move or remain still.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The sphere of form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The intrinsic nature of the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere.”
"Subhūti! The suchness of the sense-base of form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena also comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the sense-base of form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of the sense-base of form up to the sense-base of phenomena—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The eye-element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the eye-element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the eye-element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the eye-element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of the eye-element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of the eye-element up to the mind-element—whether moving or abiding—are unapprehendable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The realm of form (rūpadhātu) comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmadhātu) come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the realm of form comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the form realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic characteristic of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic characteristics of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of the realm of form, up to the realm of phenomena, cannot be apprehended as either moving or abiding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The eye-consciousness element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the visual consciousness element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the eye-consciousness element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of the eye-consciousness element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of the visual consciousness element, up to and including the mental consciousness element, cannot be apprehended as either moving or abiding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Eye-contact comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of eye-contact comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of eye-contact comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of eye-contact comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact likewise comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of eye-contact comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristics of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of visual contact, up to and including mental contact, cannot be apprehended whether they are moving or abiding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere;
the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are by nature neither coming from anywhere, nor going anywhere, nor abiding anywhere;
the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise by nature neither coming from anywhere, nor going anywhere, nor abiding anywhere."
Subhūti! The suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere.
Subhūti! The various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition have no intrinsic nature from which they come, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere;

the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions likewise have no intrinsic nature from which they come, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere.
"Subhūti! The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition have no self-characteristic from which they come, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere;

the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions likewise have no self-characteristic from which they come, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended whether they move or remain still.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The earth element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements also come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the earth element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the earth element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements also comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the earth element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic characteristic of the earth element comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of the earth element up to the consciousness element—whether in motion or at rest—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The dharma-realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, true suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of suchness, the reality-limit, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, also comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The dharmadhātu and suchness come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere;
suchness, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth—suchness comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, the intrinsic nature of true suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of the dharma-realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, the self-characteristics of suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of the dharma-realm, up to and including the realm of peace and security, cannot be apprehended whether they move or remain still.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The perfection of giving comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
“Subhūti! The suchness of the perfection of generosity comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom also comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere.”
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of the perfection of generosity comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristics of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended, whether in motion or at rest.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The four foundations of mindfulness come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere;

the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path likewise come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, the suchness of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The specific characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness do not come from anywhere, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere;
likewise, the specific characteristics of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path do not come from anywhere, nor do they go anywhere, nor do they abide anywhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended, whether in motion or at rest.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
In this way, even up to the ten powers of a Buddha come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere;

the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere."
Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
likewise, the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere.
"Subhūti! The suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha, in their own characteristics, come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere;
the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, in their own characteristics, come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and self-characteristic of the Buddha’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Awakening comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the Buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of bodhi comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of a Buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of awakening comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of a Buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of bodhi comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of a Buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The self-characteristic of awakening comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the self-characteristic of a Buddha comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the awakening of a Buddha, its fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and intrinsic characteristics—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The conditioned realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the unconditioned realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the conditioned realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the unconditioned realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The suchness of the conditioned realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the suchness of the unconditioned realm also comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of the conditioned realm comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the intrinsic nature of the unconditioned realm also comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
"Subhūti! The conditioned realm (saṃskṛtadhātu), by its own characteristic, comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere;
the unconditioned realm (asaṃskṛtadhātu), by its own characteristic, comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the intrinsic nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics of the conditioned realm and the unconditioned realm—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Subhūti! For this reason, it is said that the Great Vehicle has no coming, no going, and no abiding that can be perceived, being just like space.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
You have said: "Furthermore, just as the past, future, and present limits of space are all unapprehendable, so too is the Great Vehicle; its past, future, and present limits are all unapprehendable.
It is equal throughout the three periods of time and transcends the three periods of time; therefore, it is called the 'Great Vehicle.'"
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."

Why is this so? Subhūti! The past world is empty of the past world; the future world is empty of the future world; the present world is empty of the present world. The equality of the three times is empty of the equality of the three times; that which transcends the three times is empty of that which transcends the three times; the Great Vehicle is empty of the Great Vehicle; the bodhisattva is empty of the bodhisattva.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Emptiness possesses no distinguishing characteristics such as one, two, three, four, or five; therefore, the Great Vehicle is equal throughout the three periods of time and transcends the three periods of time.

“Subhūti! Within this Great Vehicle, neither the characteristic of equality nor the characteristic of inequality can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of desire nor the characteristic of freedom from desire can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of hatred nor the characteristic of freedom from hatred can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of delusion nor the characteristic of freedom from delusion can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of pride nor the characteristic of freedom from pride can be apprehended. In this way, up to and including neither the characteristic of the wholesome nor the characteristic of the unwholesome can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of the determinate nor the characteristic of the indeterminate can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of permanence nor the characteristic of impermanence can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of pleasure nor the characteristic of suffering can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of self nor the characteristic of non-self can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of purity nor the characteristic of impurity can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of the desire realm nor the characteristic of transcendence from the desire realm can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of the form realm nor the characteristic of transcendence from the form realm can be apprehended; neither the characteristic of the formless realm nor the characteristic of transcendence from the formless realm can be apprehended.”
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because within this Great Vehicle, the intrinsic nature of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Past form is empty of past form; future and present form are empty of future and present form.

Past feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty of past feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; future and present feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty of future and present feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, past form cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Past form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is also empty; within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone past form being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, future and present form cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "

Future and present form are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is empty; within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone future and present form being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, past feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

Past feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone past feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness being found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, future and present feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

Future and present feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone future and present feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The past eye-base is empty of the past eye-base; the future and present eye-bases are empty of the future and present eye-bases.

The past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases are empty of the past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases; the future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases are empty of the future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past eye-base cannot be apprehended. Why is that?
The past eye-base is itself empty; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone a past eye-base that could be apprehended within emptiness!
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within emptiness, the future and present eye-base cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The eye-base of the future and present is itself empty; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the apprehension of a future or present eye-base within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The past spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The future and present spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the future and present spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind that could be found within emptiness!
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The past sphere of form is empty of the past sphere of form; the future and present spheres of form are empty of the future and present spheres of form.

The past spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are empty of the past spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects; the future and present spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are empty of the future and present spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past sphere of form cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

Past form-objects are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone a past form-object that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present bases of form (rūpāyatana) cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The sphere of form (rūpāyatana) of the future and present is itself emptiness; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the apprehension of a sphere of form of the future and present within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended. Why is that?"

The past bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena being apprehendable within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are unapprehendable. Why is this? "

The future and present spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the future and present spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena that could be found within emptiness!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The past eye-element is empty of the past eye-element; the future and present eye-elements are empty of the future and present eye-elements.

The past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are empty of the past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements; the future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are empty of the future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements."
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past eye-element cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
The past eye-element is itself empty; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone a past eye-element that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present eye-element cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The future and present eye-element is itself empty; even emptiness is empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone a future or present eye-element that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements are unapprehendable. Why is this?"

The past ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements are unapprehendable. Why is this?"

The future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone a future or present ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind element that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The past realm of form is empty of the past realm of form; the future and present realms of form are empty of the future and present realms of form.

The past realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the past realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the future and present realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the future and present realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past form realm cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
The past form realm is itself emptiness, and emptiness is also empty; within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the past form realm being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present form realm cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because..."

The future and present form-realm (*rūpadhātu*) is itself emptiness, and emptiness is also empty; within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the future and present form-realm being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are unapprehendable. Why is this?"

The past realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmadhātu) cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The future and present realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the future and present realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The past eye-consciousness element is empty of the past eye-consciousness element; the future and present eye-consciousness elements are empty of the future and present eye-consciousness elements.

The past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are empty of the past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements; the future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are empty of the future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements."
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The past eye-consciousness element is itself emptiness; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone a past eye-consciousness element that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The eye-consciousness element of the future and present is itself empty; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone an eye-consciousness element of the future or present that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are unapprehendable. Why is this?"

The past realms of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone a past realm of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mental consciousness that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness elements are unapprehendable. Why is this? "

The future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone a future or present ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Past eye-contact is empty of past eye-contact; future and present eye-contact are empty of future and present eye-contact.

Past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are empty of past ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact; future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are empty of future and present ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, past eye-contact cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Past eye-contact is itself empty; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone past eye-contact being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, future and present eye-contact cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

Future and present eye-contact are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone future and present eye-contact being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, past auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental contacts are unapprehendable. Why is that?"

Past contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself empty; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone past contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present contacts of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "

The future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are themselves empty; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the apprehension of future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact within emptiness.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The various feelings produced with past eye-contact as condition are empty of the various feelings produced with past eye-contact as condition; the various feelings produced with future and present eye-contact as condition are empty of the various feelings produced with future and present eye-contact as condition.

The various feelings produced with past ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition are empty of the various feelings produced with past ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition; the various feelings produced with future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition are empty of the various feelings produced with future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the various feelings produced with past eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The various feelings produced with past eye-contact as a condition are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the various feelings produced with past eye-contact as a condition that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the various feelings arising with eye-contact as a condition in the future and present cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition in the future and present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the possibility of finding the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition in the future and present within that emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the various feelings produced with past auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental contact as conditions cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The past feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the various feelings arising with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions cannot be apprehended in the future or the present. Why is this? "

The feelings produced with conditions of future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the possibility of finding feelings produced with conditions of future and present ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact within emptiness!

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Four Hundred and Nineteen. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Two, Chapter Twenty-One: On Non-Existence (3). "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

The perfection of generosity of the past is empty of the perfection of generosity of the past; the perfection of generosity of the future and present is empty of the perfection of generosity of the future and present.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of the past are empty of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of the past; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of the future and present are empty of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of the future and present.
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The past perfection of generosity is itself emptiness; emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, so how much less could the past perfection of generosity be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) of the future and the present cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "

The perfection of generosity of the future and present is emptiness, and emptiness itself is empty; within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, so how much less could the perfection of generosity of the future and present be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the past perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The past perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves empty; emptiness itself is empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because the future and present perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the future and present perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom that could be found within emptiness!
