"Furthermore, Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness of the past are empty of the four foundations of mindfulness of the past; the four foundations of mindfulness of the future and present are empty of the four foundations of mindfulness of the future and present.

The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path of the past are empty of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path of the past; the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path of the future and present are empty of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path of the future and present."
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the four applications of mindfulness of the past cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "

The past four foundations of mindfulness are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past four foundations of mindfulness being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the four applications of mindfulness of the future and the present are unapprehendable. Why is this? "

The four foundations of mindfulness of the future and present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the four foundations of mindfulness of the future and present that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The four right efforts of the past, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the four right efforts of the past, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, being apprehended within emptiness!
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within emptiness, the four right efforts of the future and present, up to the eight branches of the noble path, are unapprehendable. Why is this?

The four right efforts of the future and present, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the four right efforts of the future and present, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, which could be apprehended within emptiness.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

In this way, even up to the ten powers of the past Buddhas are empty of the ten powers of the past Buddhas; the ten powers of the future and present Buddhas are empty of the ten powers of the future and present Buddhas.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha of the past are empty of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha of the past; the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha of the future and present are empty of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha of the future and present."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the ten powers of the Buddhas of the past cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The ten powers of the past Buddhas are emptiness; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the ten powers of the past Buddhas being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the ten powers of future and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The ten powers of the Buddhas of the future and the present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the ten powers of the Buddhas of the future and the present being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because..."

The four fearlessnesses of the past, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are themselves emptiness; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the four fearlessnesses of the past, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, which could possibly be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the four fearlessnesses of the future and present, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The four fearlessnesses of the future and present, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are themselves emptiness; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the four fearlessnesses of the future and present, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, which could be apprehended within emptiness.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Ordinary beings of the past are empty of ordinary beings of the past; ordinary beings of the future and present are empty of ordinary beings of the future and present.

Śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas of the past are empty of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas of the past; śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas of the future and present are empty of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas of the future and present."
“Subhūti! Within emptiness, past ordinary beings cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Past ordinary beings are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone past ordinary beings being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, future and present ordinary beings cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "

Ordinary beings of the future and present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone ordinary beings of the future and present being apprehended within emptiness!
Because the self, sentient beings, and even the knower and the viewer are all non-existent and unapprehendable.
Subhūti! Within emptiness, past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are unapprehendable.

Why is this? The past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas that might be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the future and present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because..."

Future and present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the apprehension of future and present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas within emptiness!
Because the self, sentient beings, and even the knower and the viewer are all non-existent and unapprehendable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Form at the prior limit is unapprehendable;
form at the posterior limit and the middle limit is unapprehendable; and form within the equality of the three limits is also unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, form is unapprehendable in the past, the future, and the present.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can form be apprehended as having a prior limit, a subsequent limit, or a middle limit within that equality! Subhūti!

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable in the past limit; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable in the future limit and the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise unapprehendable.
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are all unapprehendable in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be apprehended within equality, whether in the past, the future, or the present!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The eye-base cannot be apprehended in the past limit; the eye-base cannot be apprehended in the future limit or the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three limits, the eye-base cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the eye-base cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the eye-base be apprehended within equality as having a prior limit, a subsequent limit, or a middle limit!

"Subhūti! The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases (*āyatana*) of the past limit are unapprehendable; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases of the future limit and the middle limit are unapprehendable; and even within the equality of the three limits, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases be apprehended as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit within that equality!

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the sphere of form cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three limits, the sphere of form cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) is unapprehendable in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the form-base (rūpāyatana) of the prior, subsequent, or middle limits be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three limits, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be the spheres of sound, fragrance, taste, touch, or mental phenomena—whether past, future, or present—to be found within that equality!

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The眼界 (cakṣurdhātu) of the past limit cannot be apprehended; the眼界 of the future limit and the middle limit cannot be apprehended; and even within the equality of the three limits, the眼界 cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the eye-element cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the eye-element be apprehended within equality as having a prior limit, a subsequent limit, or a middle!

"Subhūti! The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present limits of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind element be apprehended within that equality, as having prior, subsequent, or intermediate limits!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The form realm (*rūpadhātu*) cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the form realm cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, the form realm likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the form realm of the past, the future, and the present is entirely unobtainable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the form realm (rūpadhātu) be apprehended as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit within that equality!

"Subhūti! The sound, odor, taste, tangible object, and dharma-element of the past limit are unapprehendable; the sound, odor, taste, tangible object, and dharma-element of the future and middle limits are unapprehendable; and within the equality of the three limits, the sound, odor, taste, tangible object, and dharma-element are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be the sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects of the past, future, or present limits within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three limits, the eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the eye-consciousness element is entirely unapprehendable in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the eye-consciousness element be apprehended within equality, in terms of its prior, subsequent, or middle limits!

"Subhūti! The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three limits, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present limits of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element be apprehended as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Eye-contact cannot be apprehended at the prior limit;
eye-contact cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; nor can eye-contact be apprehended within the equality of the three limits."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, eye-contact is unapprehendable in the past, the future, or the present.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can eye-contact be apprehended within equality as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit!

"Subhūti! The contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind at the prior limit is unapprehendable; the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind at the posterior limit and the middle limit is unapprehendable; and within the equality of the three limits, the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact of the past, future, and present limits are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can one apprehend the past, future, or present limits of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended in the past; they cannot be apprehended in the future or the middle [present]; nor can the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition be apprehended within the equality of the three times."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions cannot be apprehended in the past limit; they cannot be apprehended in the future or middle limits; and within the equality of the three limits, the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental contact as conditions—whether in the past, the future, or the present interval—are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could one apprehend the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions within that equality, whether in the past, future, or present!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The perfection of giving in the past limit is unapprehendable; the perfection of giving in the future limit and the middle limit is unapprehendable; and even the perfection of giving within the equality of the three limits is unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the perfection of generosity be apprehended within equality as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit!

"Subhūti! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended in the past limit; the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended in the future limit or the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three limits, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the pure precepts, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can one find the purity of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or the perfection of wisdom within that equality, whether in the past, future, or present!

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable in the past; the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable in the future and the present; and even within the equality of the three times, the four foundations of mindfulness are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four foundations of mindfulness are unattainable in the past, the future, and the present.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the four foundations of mindfulness be apprehended within equality as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit!

"Subhūti! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit or the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the four right efforts, up to the eightfold noble path, be apprehended as having a prior, middle, or subsequent limit within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

In this way, even the ten powers of a Buddha are unapprehendable in the past limit; they are unapprehendable in the future limit or the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, the ten powers of a Buddha are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the ten powers of a Buddha be apprehended within the past, future, or present limits of that equality!

"Subhūti! The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are unapprehendable in the past limit. They are unapprehendable in the future limit and the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four fearlessnesses and even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended throughout the past, the future, or the present.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the four fearlessnesses, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, be apprehended within that equality, whether in the past, the future, or the present!

"Furthermore, Subhūti! An ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) cannot be apprehended in the past limit; an ordinary person cannot be apprehended in the future limit or the middle limit; and within the equality of the three limits, an ordinary person likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, neither the past, the future, nor the present can be apprehended as distinct from ordinary beings.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be any distinction between the prior, the subsequent, or the intermediate limits within that equality!
This is because the self, sentient beings, and so forth, up to the knower and the viewer, are all non-existent and cannot be apprehended. Subhūti!

A śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata cannot be apprehended in the past; a śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata cannot be apprehended in the future or the present; and within the equality of the three times, a śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata likewise cannot be apprehended.
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present limits of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be the sounds of "prior," "subsequent," or "intermediate" limits for śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas within that equality!
Because the self, sentient beings, and even the knower and the viewer are all non-existent and unapprehendable.

"In this way, Subhūti, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they abide within this equality of the three periods of time; by diligently training in the knowledge of all aspects without grasping or attachment, they swiftly attain its fulfillment."
"Subhūti! This is called the Great Vehicle of the equality of the three periods for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in such a Great Vehicle, they surpass all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras—and are swiftly able to realize the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, excellent! Excellent!”
Excellent! The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has skillfully and correctly expounded the Mahāyāna of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
World-Honored One!

Thus, this Mahāyāna is most honored, most supreme, most exalted, and most wondrous. In the past, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas trained in this and were already able to realize all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
In the future, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will train in this and shall be able to realize all-aspect omniscience, thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.

At present, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions train in this and are now able to realize all-aspect omniscience, thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.

Therefore, the Mahāyāna is most honored and supreme, most exalted and wondrous; it serves as the true and excellent basis for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, enabling them to swiftly realize all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) and to bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Subhūti!

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, future, and present rely upon the Great Vehicle to practice with diligent effort, swiftly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings."
Therefore, the Mahāyāna is the most honored, the most supreme, the highest, and the most wondrous; it surpasses all those in the world, including devas, humans, and asuras.
Chapter 22: Chapter on Accordance, Part Two. At that time, the Venerable Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
The Tathāgata previously instructed the Venerable Subhūti to proclaim the *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; why, then, does he now speak of the Mahāyāna?
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha,
saying: “Blessed One,
will the meanings of the Great Vehicle that I have previously explained not contradict the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"All the meanings of the Great Vehicle that you have previously expounded are entirely in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā and do not deviate from it in any way."
Why is this? Subhūti!

All wholesome dharmas, the factors of enlightenment—whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of tathāgatas—all such things are without exception subsumed within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How are all wholesome dharmas—the factors of enlightenment, whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas—all entirely subsumed within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?”
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"Whether it be the perfection of generosity, or the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

whether it be the four applications of mindfulness, or the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;"
Whether it be the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;

whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha, or the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
or whether it be all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects.
Subhūti, whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant abiding in equanimity—

all such wholesome dharmas, factors of enlightenment, whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas— all these are entirely subsumed within the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the perfection of wisdom, or the perfections of concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;
whether it be form, or feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;"
Whether it be the eye-base, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases;
whether it be the form-base, or the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases;
or whether it be the eye-element, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements.
Whether it be the realm of form, or the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena;
whether it be the realm of eye-consciousness, or the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness;
or whether it be eye-contact, or the contacts of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind;
Whether it be the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or those produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition;
whether it be the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments;
whether it be the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, or the ten totalities;

Whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness, or the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
whether it be the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
whether it be wholesome dharmas or unwholesome dharmas.
Whether they be determinate dharmas or indeterminate dharmas;
whether they be outflowing dharmas or non-outflowing dharmas;
whether they be conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas.
Whether mundane phenomena or supramundane phenomena;
whether the noble truth of suffering, or the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
whether the desire realm, or the form and formless realms.

Whether it be internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
whether it be the dharma-realm, suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth;
or whether it be dhāraṇīs or samādhis.

Whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
whether it be the Tathāgatas themselves, or the Dharma and Vinaya realized and taught by the Buddhas;
whether it be awakening, or nirvāṇa.
All such phenomena as these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.
"Subhūti! For this reason, all the meanings of the Great Vehicle that you have previously explained are entirely in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā and do not deviate from it in any way."

Why is this? "Subhūti, the Great Vehicle is not different from the perfection of wisdom, and the perfection of wisdom is not different from the Great Vehicle; [they are not two, nor are they distinct]."

The Mahāyāna is not different from the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity; nor are the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity different from the Mahāyāna.

Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.
“Subhūti! The Great Vehicle is not different from the four foundations of mindfulness, and the four foundations of mindfulness are not different from the Great Vehicle;

the Great Vehicle is not different from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are not different from the Great Vehicle.”

Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, or even the eight branches of the noble path, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“Subhūti! The Great Vehicle is not different from the ten powers of a Buddha, and the ten powers of a Buddha are not different from the Great Vehicle;

the Great Vehicle is not different from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not different from the Great Vehicle.”

Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna, the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, or even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.

“Subhūti! For this reason, all the meanings of the Great Vehicle that you have previously explained are entirely in accord with the *prajñāpāramitā* and do not deviate from it. To speak of the Great Vehicle is to speak of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and to speak of the *prajñāpāramitā* is to speak of the Great Vehicle; for there is no difference in meaning between these two names.”
Chapter 23: On the Boundless (Anantapāramitā). Part Two, Chapter Twenty-three, Section One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and entirely unobtainable; all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit are non-existent and entirely unobtainable; all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the middle limit are non-existent and entirely unobtainable.
“World-Honored One!
Because form (*rūpa*) is without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit;
because feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the sphere of the eye is without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also without limit;
because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also without limit.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the sphere of form is without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the eye-element is without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects (*dharmadhātu*) are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the eye-consciousness element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because eye-contact is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;
because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.”
“Bhagavān, because the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) is limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless;
because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because internal emptiness is without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit.

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are without limit, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also without limit.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the dharma-realm is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because true thusness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also limitless;
because the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also limitless.”
“World-Honored One!
Within form itself, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from form, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Within feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness themselves, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!

Within the sense-base of the eye, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the sense-base of the eye, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Within the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!

Within the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the sphere of form, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Within the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
The eye-element itself is non-existent and unobtainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the eye-element, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.

Likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements themselves are non-existent and unobtainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!

Within the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and cannot be apprehended; apart from the realm of form, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Within the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and cannot be apprehended; apart from the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!

Within the visual consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the visual consciousness element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Likewise, within the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements (*manovijñānadhātu*), the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“Bhagavān! Eye-contact itself is non-existent and unattainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from eye-contact, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unattainable.

Likewise, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact themselves are non-existent and unattainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unattainable.”
“World-Honored One!

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Likewise, the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
“World-Honored One!
The perfection of giving itself is non-existent and unattainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the perfection of giving, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unattainable.

Likewise, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom themselves are non-existent and unattainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unattainable.”
“World-Honored One!

The four foundations of mindfulness themselves are non-existent and unobtainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the four foundations of mindfulness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.

Likewise, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path themselves are non-existent and unobtainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!

Within the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Within the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*), the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
The ten powers of a Buddha are non-existent and unobtainable as a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the ten powers of a Buddha, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.

The four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-existent and unobtainable as a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!

Within internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from internal emptiness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Likewise, within external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
Within the dharma-realm itself, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the dharma-realm, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Within true thusness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from true thusness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
Within the Śrāvaka vehicle, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the Śrāvaka vehicle, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.

Within the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!

Regarding all these dharmas, though I seek for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in every way, in every place, and at every time, I see none at all and cannot find them. How then am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas by means of the perfection of wisdom?”
"Bhagavān! These so-called 'bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' have only conventional designations and possess no intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*).

Just as it is said that 'self' and so forth are ultimately unarisen, having only conventional designations and no intrinsic nature, so too are all phenomena: they are ultimately unarisen, having only conventional designations and no intrinsic nature."
“World-Honored One!
What is form that is ultimately non-arising?
What are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are ultimately non-arising?”
“World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, then it is not called form, nor is it called feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
World-Honored One!”
What is the sense-base of the eye that is ultimately unarisen?
What are the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind that are ultimately unarisen?
World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, it is not called the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*), nor is it called the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base (*manas-āyatana*).
"World-Honored One,
what is the form-base (*rūpa-āyatana*) that is ultimately non-arising?"
What are the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena that are ultimately non-arising?
World-Honored One, if they are ultimately non-arising, then they cannot be called the sphere of form, nor can they be called the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
What is the eye-element that is ultimately non-arising?
What are the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements that are ultimately non-arising?”
“World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be called the eye-element, nor can it be called the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element.
World-Honored One!”
What is the ultimate non-arising of the form realm?
What is the ultimate non-arising of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena?
World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, it is not called the form-element (*rūpa-dhātu*), nor is it called the sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, or mental-object-element (*śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-,
dharma-dhātu*). "World-Honored One,
what is the eye-consciousness-element that is ultimately non-arising?"
"What is it that the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are ultimately non-arising?
World-Honored One!
If they are ultimately non-arising, then they are not called the eye-consciousness element, nor are they called the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements."
“World-Honored One!
What is eye-contact that is ultimately non-arising?
What are ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact that are ultimately non-arising?”
“World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, then it is not called eye-contact, nor is it called ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
World-Honored One!”
What are those feelings produced with eye-contact as condition that are ultimately non-arising?
What are those feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions that are ultimately non-arising?
World-Honored One!

If there is ultimate non-arising, then it cannot be called "the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition," nor can they be called "the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions."
“Bhagavān, what is the perfection of giving that is ultimately non-arising?
What are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom that are ultimately non-arising?”

"Bhagavān! If there is ultimately no arising, then it cannot be called the perfection of generosity, nor can it be called the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom."
“World-Honored One!
What are the four foundations of mindfulness that are ultimately non-arising?
What are the four right endeavors, and so on, up to the eight branches of the noble path that are ultimately non-arising?”
“World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, then it cannot be called the four foundations of mindfulness, nor can it be called the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path.
World-Honored One!”
"World-Honored One, what is the emptiness gate of liberation that is ultimately unarisen?
What are the signless and wishless gates of liberation that are ultimately unarisen?"
If they are ultimately non-arising, they cannot be called the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor can they be called the gates of liberation of signlessness or wishlessness.
"World-Honored One,
what are the ten powers of a Buddha that are ultimately non-arising?"
"What is it that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are ultimately non-arising?
World-Honored One!

If they are ultimately non-arising, then they cannot be called the ten powers of a Buddha, nor can they be called the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."
“World-Honored One!
What is the ultimate non-arising of internal emptiness?
What is the ultimate non-arising of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-nature?”
“World-Honored One!
If there is ultimate non-arising, then it cannot be called internal emptiness, nor can it be called external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
World-Honored One!”
What is the dharmadhātu that is ultimately unarisen?
What is suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, that are ultimately unarisen?
World-Honored One!
If there were ultimate non-arising, it would not be called the Dharma-realm, nor would it be called True Suchness, the Reality-limit, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth.
“World-Honored One!
What is it that is ultimately non-arising in the Śrāvaka vehicle?
What is it that is ultimately non-arising in the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna?”
"Bhagavān! If there is ultimate non-arising, then it is not called the Śrāvaka-yāna, nor is it called the Pratyekabuddha-yāna or the Mahāyāna. Bhagavān!"
How could I possibly instruct and admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of a prajñāpāramitā that is ultimately unarisen?
“World-Honored One!
Apart from ultimate non-arising, there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
World-Honored One!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such a teaching, does not sink into despondency nor feel regret, and their mind is neither startled, terrified, nor afraid, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 423. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter on the Boundless, Part Two, Twenty-three. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"For what reason do you say that Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit are non-existent and unobtainable, and Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the middle limit are non-existent and unobtainable?"

For what reason is it said that because form (*rūpa*) is limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless; and because feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless;

and even up to the point that because the vehicle of the śrāvaka is limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless; and because the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha and the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless?

For what reason is it said that, with respect to form itself, a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended; and apart from form, a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended?

Likewise, with respect to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness themselves, a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended; and apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended.

This extends even to the vehicle of the śrāvakas: with respect to the vehicle of the śrāvakas itself, a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended; and apart from the vehicle of the śrāvakas, a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended.

Is it that within the vehicle of the solitary realizers (pratyekabuddhayāna) and the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna), a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; and apart from the vehicle of the solitary realizers and the Great Vehicle, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended?

For what reason do you say that, regarding all these dharmas, I have sought Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas in every way, in every place, and at every time, yet have seen none at all and cannot find them; how then am I to instruct and admonish the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*?
For what reason do you say that "bodhisattva-mahāsattvas" are merely provisional designations and lack any intrinsic nature?
For what reason do you say that just as "self" and so forth are ultimately unarisen, they are merely provisional designations and lack any intrinsic nature?
For what reason is it said that all phenomena are likewise, being ultimately unarisen, existing only as provisional designations and entirely lacking intrinsic nature?
For what reason is it said that whatever form there may be is ultimately unarisen?
What is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are ultimately non-arising?
What, furthermore, is the Śrāvaka vehicle that is ultimately non-arising?
What is the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna that are ultimately non-arising?

For what reason is it said that if something is ultimately non-arising, it is not called form (*rūpa*), nor is it called feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*);

and so on, up to: if something is ultimately non-arising, it is not called the vehicle of the śrāvakas (*śrāvakayāna*), nor is it called the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas (*pratyekabuddhayāna*) or the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*)?
For what reason do you say: "How could I possibly instruct and admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of the perfection of wisdom which is ultimately unarisen?"
For what reason is it said that, being ultimately unarisen, there is also no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening?

For what reason is it said that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such a teaching, their mind does not sink, nor do they feel sorrow or regret, and their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?
“Virtuous one, you should now explain this fully for me.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied to Śāriputra:

“Regarding what the Venerable asks—‘For what reason is it said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unapprehendable; bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit are non-existent and unapprehendable; and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the middle limit are non-existent and unapprehendable?’”
"Śāriputra, because sentient beings do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because sentient beings are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended."
Because sentient beings are remote, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because sentient beings lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
The non-existence and unobtainability of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the future limit and the middle limit are likewise so. “Śāriputra,
because form is non-existent, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable;”
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because form is empty, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because form is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because form has no intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit: they do not exist and cannot be apprehended. "Śāriputra!
Because the eye-base does not exist, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended."
Because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the sense base of the eye is empty, bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty, bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the sense-base of the eye is detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the sense base of the eye lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for the future limit and the middle limit that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-existent and unapprehendable.
"Śāriputra, because the sphere of form is non-existent, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unapprehendable; [the same applies to the future and middle limits]."
Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not exist, the prior limits of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the sphere of form is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the sphere of form is detached, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are detached, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the sense-base of form lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit: they are non-existent and cannot be apprehended. "Śāriputra!
Because the eye-element is non-existent, all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended."
Because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements do not exist, the prior limits of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the eye-element is empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the eye-element is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the eye-element lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit, who are non-existent and unobtainable. "Śāriputra!
Because the realm of form is non-existent, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable."
Because the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the realm of form is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the realm of form is detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the form realm lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit, who are non-existent and unobtainable. "Śāriputra!
Because the eye-consciousness element is non-existent, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable."
Because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the eye-consciousness element is empty, bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are empty, bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the eye-consciousness element is detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and unapprehendable;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and unapprehendable.
Because the visual consciousness element lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
The same is true for the non-existence and unobtainability of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the future limit and the middle limit. “Śāriputra,
because eye-contact is non-existent, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable;”
Because ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact are non-existent, the prior limits of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because eye-contact is empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because eye-contact is detached, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are detached, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because visual contact lacks intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental contact lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit, who are non-existent and unobtainable. "Śāriputra,
because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-existent, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable."

Because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are detached, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;

because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are detached, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;

because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit that they are non-existent and unobtainable. "Śāriputra,
because the perfection of generosity is non-existent, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable."

Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the perfection of giving is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the perfection of generosity is remote, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are remote, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the perfection of generosity lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit: they do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
"Śāriputra, because internal emptiness does not exist, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended."

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because internal emptiness is empty, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is empty, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because internal emptiness is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because internal emptiness lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;

because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities, lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for the future limit and the middle limit that all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are non-existent and unapprehendable.
"Śāriputra, because the four foundations of mindfulness are non-existent, all bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unapprehendable."

Because the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the four foundations of mindfulness lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit: they do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
"Śāriputra, in this way, because even the ten powers of a Buddha do not exist, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended."

Because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended;
because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit do not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Because the ten powers of a Buddha lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended;
because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha lack intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.
It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit and the middle limit that they are non-existent and unobtainable. “Śāriputra,
because the dharmas of the śrāvakas are non-existent, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit are non-existent and unobtainable;”
