Śāriputra! Because the Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna are empty of intrinsic nature, if a dharma is empty of intrinsic nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be designated as either the Pratyekabuddhayāna or the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Because emptiness is neither the Pratyekabuddhayāna nor the Mahāyāna.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
if there is ultimate non-arising, then it is not called form, nor is it called feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, if there is ultimate non-arising, it is not designated as the Śrāvaka Vehicle, nor is it designated as the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, nor the Mahāyāna. "Moreover, Śāriputra..."

As for the Venerable One’s question: "For what reason do you say, 'How could I possibly instruct and admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of the Prajñāpāramitā which is ultimately unarisen'?"
"Śāriputra, that which is ultimately non-arising is itself the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the perfection of wisdom is itself ultimate non-arising."
Why is this? Because ultimate non-arising and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual and have no distinction between them. Śāriputra!
Ultimate non-arising is itself the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva is himself ultimate non-arising. Why is this?
Because ultimate non-arising and the bodhisattva mahāsattva are neither two nor distinct.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
How could I possibly instruct and admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of a prajñāpāramitā that is ultimately unarisen?
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, regarding what the Venerable One asked:
'For what reason is it said that because there is no ultimate non-arising, there is also no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?'"

"Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive a perfection of wisdom apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive a bodhisattva-mahāsattva apart from ultimate non-arising."
Why is this? Because the perfection of wisdom and the bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and there is no distinction between them, as they are both ultimately unarisen.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any form apart from that which is ultimately unarisen, nor do they perceive any feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness apart from that which is ultimately unarisen.
Why is this? Whether it be form, or feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, they are non-dual with and inseparable from ultimate non-arising. Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive an eye-base apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive an ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, or mind-base apart from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because whether it be the sense base of the eye, or the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any place where form exists apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive any place where sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena exist apart from ultimate non-arising.

Why is this? Because whether it be the sphere of form, or the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, they are non-dual with ultimate non-arising, and there is no distinction between them.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive an eye-element apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive an ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element apart from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because whether it be the eye-element, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive a form-realm apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive a sound, odor, taste, tangible, or mental-object realm apart from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because whether it be the realm of form, or the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive an eye-consciousness element apart from that which is ultimately unarisen, nor do they perceive ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness elements apart from that which is ultimately unarisen.
Why is this? Because whether it be the eye-consciousness element, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive an eye-contact that is apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive an ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact that is apart from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Whether it be eye-contact, or ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from absolute non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any feeling produced with eye-contact as a condition that is apart from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive any feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions that are apart from ultimate non-arising.

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition, are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive a perfection of giving that is separate from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom that are separate from ultimate non-arising.

Why is this? Because whether it be the perfection of generosity, or the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness as being apart from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being apart from ultimate non-arising.

Why is this? Because whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, or even the eight branches of the noble path, they are non-dual with and inseparable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive anything apart from ultimate non-arising, up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha; nor do they perceive anything apart from ultimate non-arising that constitutes the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, or even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any gateways of samādhi as existing apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive any gateways of dhāraṇī as existing apart from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because all gateways of samādhi and all gateways of dhāraṇī are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as being apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as being apart from ultimate non-arising.

Why is this? Because whether it be all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are non-dual with ultimate non-arising (*atyantānutpāda*) and there is no distinction between them.

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive a śrāvaka vehicle apart from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive a pratyekabuddha vehicle or a mahāyāna apart from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because whether it be the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the Mahāyāna, they are non-dual and indistinguishable from ultimate non-arising. Śāriputra!
For this reason, I say: apart from that which is ultimately unarisen, there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, regarding what the Venerable One asked:

'For what reason is it said that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such an exposition, does not sink in spirit nor feel regret, and his mind is not startled, terrified, or afraid, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?'"

"Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive any real activity in phenomena; rather, they see all phenomena as being like a dream, like an illusion, like an echo, like a reflection, like a mirage, like a shadow, like a city of gandharvas, and like a magical transformation—appearing to exist yet lacking practical utility. Hearing it said that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is emptiness, they give rise to profound joy and remain free from despondency and other such states."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say this:

if, upon hearing such a teaching, the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not sink, nor does he feel regret; if his mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 420–423. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter on the Boundless, Part Four. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and contemplates all phenomena, at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp, does not take up, does not dwell upon, and does not cling to form; nor does he designate it as "self.

Likewise, with regard to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, he does not grasp, does not take up, does not dwell upon, and does not cling to them; nor does he designate them as "self."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form, nor even consciousness.
"In the sense-base of the eye, there is no grasping, no appropriation, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self.
In the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, there is no grasping, no appropriation, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor are they designated as 'self.'"
Why is this? World-Honored One!
Because at that time, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the sense base of the eye, nor even the sense base of the mind.
"In the sphere of form, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';
in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor are they designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the sphere of form, nor even the sphere of mental phenomena.
"In the eye-element, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';
likewise, in the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor are they designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-element, nor even the mind-element.
"In the realm of form, there is no feeling, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';
likewise, in the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, there is no feeling, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the realm of form, nor even the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
"In the visual consciousness element, there is no grasping, no appropriation, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';

likewise, in the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements, there is no grasping, no appropriation, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor are they designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the eye-consciousness element, nor even the mind-consciousness element.
"In eye-contact there is no feeling, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment; nor is it designated as 'self.
In ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact there is no feeling, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment; nor is it designated as 'self.'"
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive eye-contact, nor even mind-contact.
"Regarding the various feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact, there is no feeling, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self.
Regarding the various feelings arising conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, there is no feeling, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self.'"
Why is this? World-Honored One!

It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including any feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.
"In the perfection of generosity, there is no receiving, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'mine.

In the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, there is no receiving, no grasping, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor are they designated as 'mine.'"
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the perfection of giving, up to and including the perfection of wisdom.
"In inner emptiness there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';

likewise, in outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self and common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive anything from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature.
"In the four foundations of mindfulness, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';

likewise, in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the eightfold noble path.
"In this way, up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha, there is no grasping, no appropriation, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';

likewise, regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, there is no grasping, no appropriation, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
"Regarding all doors of samādhi, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';
regarding all doors of dhāraṇī, there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self.'"
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any gateways of samādhi or any gateways of dhāraṇī.
"Up to and including omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self';

likewise, regarding the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), there is no grasping, no seizing, no dwelling, and no attachment, nor is it designated as 'self'."
Why is this? World-Honored One!

It is because at that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive form (rūpa), nor do they perceive feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), or consciousness (vijñāna).”
Why is this? Because the nature of form and so forth is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the sense-base of the eye, nor does one perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of the eye is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the sense-base of form, nor does one perceive the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of form and so forth is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the eye-element, nor does one perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-elements.
Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-element and so forth is empty, being without arising or cessation.
One does not perceive the form-element, nor does one perceive the elements of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because the nature of the realm of form and so forth is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the eye-consciousness element, nor does one perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-consciousness element and so forth is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive eye-contact, nor does one perceive ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
Why is this? Because the nature of eye-contact and so forth is empty, being without arising or ceasing.

One does not perceive the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor does one perceive the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.
Why is this? Because the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature, being without arising or cessation.
One does not perceive the perfection of generosity, nor does one perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) and the others is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive internal emptiness, nor does one perceive external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*).
Why is this? Because the nature of internal emptiness and so forth is empty, being without arising or cessation.
One does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does one perceive the four right endeavors, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path.
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are empty of intrinsic nature and are without arising or ceasing.

In this manner, up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha, one does not perceive them, nor does one perceive the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth are empty of intrinsic nature, being without arising or cessation.
One does not perceive any gateways to samādhi, nor does one perceive any gateways to dhāraṇī.
Why is this? Because all gateways to samādhi are equal in their emptiness of intrinsic nature, being without arising or cessation.
One does not perceive the dharma-realm, nor does one perceive true suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm is equal emptiness, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive any bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice, nor does one perceive the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
Why is this? Because all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are equal to the emptiness of intrinsic nature, being without arising or cessation.
Thus, one does not perceive omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), nor does one perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Why is this? Because all-knowledge and its nature are empty, being without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"

That form is neither produced nor extinguished is itself not form; that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither produced nor extinguished are themselves not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because form and so forth are non-dual with that which is neither born nor extinguished, and there is no distinction between them.
For what reason?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of form is not form; the non-arising and non-ceasing of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“World-Honored One!

The sense base of the eye, being neither arising nor ceasing, is not the sense base of the eye; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, being neither arising nor ceasing, are also not the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
Why is this so? Because the sense-base of the eye and so forth are non-dual with that which is neither arising nor ceasing; they are not two distinct things. Why is this?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the eye-base is not the eye-base; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.
“World-Honored One!

The sense-base of form is neither produced nor extinguished, and thus it is not the sense-base of form; the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise neither produced nor extinguished, and thus they are not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
Why is this so? Because the sphere of form and so forth are non-dual with non-arising and non-ceasing; they are not two distinct things. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the sphere of form is not the sphere of form; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are also not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
“World-Honored One!

The eye-element that is neither produced nor extinguished is not the eye-element; likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements that are neither produced nor extinguished are also not the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.”
Why is this? Because the eye-sphere and so forth are non-dual with that which is neither arising nor ceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is this?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the eye-element that is non-arising and non-ceasing is not the eye-element; likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements that are non-arising and non-ceasing are also not the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.
“World-Honored One!

That which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of the realm of form is not the realm of form; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are also not the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena.”
Why is this? Because the realm of form and so forth are non-dual with non-arising and non-ceasing, and there is no distinction between them.
For what reason?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is not one, not two, not many, and not distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the realm of form is not the realm of form; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the realms of sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are also not the realms of sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental phenomena.
“World-Honored One!

The eye-consciousness element, being neither arising nor ceasing, is not the eye-consciousness element; likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements, being neither arising nor ceasing, are also not the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.”
Why is this? Because the eye-consciousness element and so forth are non-dual with, and have no distinction from, the unborn and unceasing. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the eye-consciousness element that is non-arising and non-ceasing is not the eye-consciousness element; likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements that are non-arising and non-ceasing are also not the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.
“World-Honored One!

The non-arising and non-ceasing of eye-contact is not itself eye-contact; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are also not themselves ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.”
Why is this? Because eye-contact and so forth are non-dual with, and have no distinction from, that which is neither born nor extinguished. Why is this?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of eye-contact is not itself eye-contact; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are also not themselves ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
“World-Honored One!

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition that are neither arising nor ceasing are not, in fact, feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions that are neither arising nor ceasing are likewise not feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.”
Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual with, and have no distinction from, the unarisen and unceasing. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is not one, not two, not many, and not distinct.

Therefore, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, being non-arising and non-ceasing, are not themselves the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; likewise, the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions, being non-arising and non-ceasing, are also not themselves the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.

“Bhagavān! The non-arising and non-ceasing of the perfection of generosity is not itself the perfection of generosity; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not themselves the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Why is this so? Because the perfection of generosity and the others are non-dual with, and have no distinction from, non-arising and non-ceasing.
For what reason?
Because the dharmas of non-arising and non-ceasing are neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) is not itself the perfection of generosity; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are also not themselves the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

The non-arising and non-ceasing of internal emptiness is not itself internal emptiness; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are not themselves external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
Why is this? Because inner emptiness and so forth are non-dual with the unarisen and the unceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of internal emptiness is not itself internal emptiness; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, is also not itself external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-nature.
“World-Honored One!

The non-arising and non-ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness are not themselves the four foundations of mindfulness; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are not themselves the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are non-dual with non-arising and non-ceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is that?
Because the dharmas that are neither arising nor ceasing are not one, not two, not many, and not distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness are not themselves the four foundations of mindfulness; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are also not themselves the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

Thus, even up to the ten powers of a Buddha, their non-arising and non-ceasing are not the ten powers of a Buddha; likewise, the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, their non-arising and non-ceasing are also not the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
Why is this? Because the ten powers of the Buddha and so forth are non-dual with the unborn and the unceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the Buddha’s ten powers, being non-arising and non-ceasing, are not the Buddha’s ten powers; likewise, the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, being non-arising and non-ceasing, are also not the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

That all gateways of samādhi are neither produced nor extinguished is itself not the gateways of samādhi; that all gateways of dhāraṇī are neither produced nor extinguished is also not the gateways of dhāraṇī.”
Why is this? Because all gateways of samādhi and so forth are non-dual with the unborn and unceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is that?
Because the dharmas of non-arising and non-ceasing are neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of all samādhi-gates are not themselves all samādhi-gates; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of all dhāraṇī-gates are also not themselves all dhāraṇī-gates.
“World-Honored One!

That the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is neither produced nor extinguished is not itself the dharma-realm; that true thusness (tathatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), and the realm of peace (kṣemadhātu) are neither produced nor extinguished is likewise not itself true thusness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, or the realm of peace.”
Why is this so? Because the dharma-realm and such are non-dual with the unarisen and the unceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of non-arising and non-ceasing is not itself the dharma-realm; likewise, true thusness (tathatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the inconceivable realm, and the realm of peace, when non-arising and non-ceasing, are also not themselves the dharma-realm, true thusness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, or the realm of peace.
“World-Honored One!

That which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not itself the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; likewise, that which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is not itself the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”
Why is this? Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual with, and have no distinction from, the unborn and unceasing. Why is that?
Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, the non-arising and non-ceasing of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not itself the practice of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is not itself the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
“World-Honored One!

That which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is not itself all-knowledge; that which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is likewise not itself the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.”
Why is this? Because all-knowledge and the like are non-dual with the unarisen and the unceasing, and there is no distinction between them. Why is that?

Because the dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing is not one, not two, not many, and not distinct, therefore that which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of all-knowledge is not itself all-knowledge;

likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are also not themselves the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

Form is non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, and that which is non-dual is also not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

The sense-base of the eye is non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the sense-base of the eye; the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, and that which is non-dual is also not the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”

The non-duality of the sense-field of form is itself not the sense-field of form; the non-duality of the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is likewise not the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

The non-duality of the eye-element is itself not the eye-element; the non-duality of the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is likewise not the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

The non-duality of the form-element is itself not the form-element; the non-duality of the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is likewise not the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

The non-duality of the visual consciousness element is itself not the visual consciousness element; likewise, the non-duality of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements is itself not the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness element.
The non-duality of eye-contact is itself not eye-contact; likewise, the non-duality of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is itself not ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.

The non-duality of all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself not all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; likewise, the non-duality of all sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is itself not all sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.

The non-duality of the perfection of generosity is not itself the perfection of generosity; the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is also not itself the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

The non-duality of internal emptiness is not itself internal emptiness; the non-duality of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is also not itself external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities.

The non-duality of the four applications of mindfulness is not itself the four applications of mindfulness; the non-duality of the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is also not itself the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path.

In this way, up to the ten powers of a Buddha, non-duality is not the ten powers of a Buddha; the four fearlessnesses, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, non-duality is also not the four fearlessnesses, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
All doors of samādhi, non-duality is not all doors of samādhi; all doors of dhāraṇī, non-duality is also not all doors of dhāraṇī. The dharma-realm, non-duality is not the dharma-realm;

true suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth—non-duality is also not true suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth.

The non-duality of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is not itself all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices; the non-duality of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is not itself the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.

The non-duality of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is not itself omniscience; likewise, the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is also not itself the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!
Form enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness enter into the category of non-dual dharmas;
the eye-base enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.”
The sphere of form enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.
The eye-element enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; the elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.
The form-element enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; the elements of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.
The eye-consciousness element enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.
Eye-contact enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.

All feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition enter into the category of non-dual dharmas; all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.

The perfection of generosity enters into the category of non-dual phenomena; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom enter into the category of non-dual phenomena;
internal emptiness enters into the category of non-dual phenomena, and external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence enter into the category of non-dual phenomena;
the four foundations of mindfulness enter into the category of non-dual phenomena, and the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path enter into the category of non-dual phenomena.

In this way, even up to the ten powers of a Buddha enter the category of non-dual dharmas; the four fearlessnesses, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, enter the category of non-dual dharmas;
all doors of samādhi enter the category of non-dual dharmas; all doors of dhāraṇī enter the category of non-dual dharmas;
the dharma-realm enters the category of non-dual dharmas; and suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, enter the category of non-dual dharmas.

The practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter into the category of non-dual dharmas; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas enters into the category of non-dual dharmas;
omniscience enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; and the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.
Chapter 24: On Detachment, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"As you have said, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and contemplates all phenomena, what is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"What is the perfection of wisdom?
How does one observe all phenomena?
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied:
"Regarding what the Venerable One asked, 'What is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

Śāriputra, one is called a *bodhisattva* because they diligently seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings; and they are further called a *mahāsattva* because they possess the realization of reality as it is, being able to thoroughly know the characteristics of all phenomena without any attachment."
At that time, Śāriputra again asked Subhūti:
"How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can fully comprehend the characteristics of all phenomena without any attachment?"
Subhūti replied, “Śāriputra!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas truly understand all characteristics of form without grasping; they truly understand all characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness without grasping.”

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all eye-bases (cakṣur-āyatana) without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases without grasping.

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all form-bases (rūpa-āyatana) without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases without grasping.

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all eye-elements (cakṣurdhātu) without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements without grasping.

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all form-realms without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all sound, odor, taste, tactile, and mental-object realms without grasping;

they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all eye-consciousness realms without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness realms without grasping;

they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all eye-contact without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact without grasping.

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and remain without attachment; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, and remain without attachment;

they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*), and remain without attachment; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and remain without attachment;

they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*), and remain without attachment; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and remain without attachment.

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all four foundations of mindfulness without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path without grasping.

Likewise, up to and including, they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all ten powers of a Buddha without grasping; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha without grasping;
they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all doors of samādhi without grasping; and they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all doors of dhāraṇī without grasping.

They understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all dharma-realm without any attachment; they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of all suchness, the limit of reality, the inconceivable realm, the realm of peace, and so forth, without any attachment;

even up to understanding, as they truly are, the characteristics of all-knowledge without any attachment, and understanding, as they truly are, the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects without any attachment.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"Furthermore, what is meant by the 'characteristics of all phenomena'? Subhūti replied:

“Śāriputra! If, by means of such formations, characteristics, and signs, one discerns that these phenomena are form, sound, odor, taste, tangible object, or mental phenomenon; internal or external; with outflows or without outflows; conditioned or unconditioned—these are called the characteristics of all phenomena.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, regarding what the Venerable One asked— 'What is the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?'—
Śāriputra, [listen to this:]..."
"Because it possesses supreme and wondrous wisdom that is distantly removed from all things, it is named Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra asked: "From what phenomena is it able to remain distantly removed?"
Subhūti replied, “Because it is able to distance one from all aggregates, bases, elements, afflictions, views, and the six destinies, it is called the perfection of wisdom.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Because this supreme and wondrous wisdom reaches far, it is called Prajñāpāramitā. Śāriputra said:
"To what phenomena is this able to reach far? Subhūti replied:

"This is called the perfection of wisdom because it reaches far beyond everything from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; this is called the perfection of wisdom because it reaches far beyond everything from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; this is called the perfection of wisdom because it reaches far beyond everything from the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; likewise, it is called the perfection of wisdom because it reaches far beyond everything from the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and it is called the perfection of wisdom because it reaches far beyond everything from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects."
"Śāriputra! For these reasons, it is called the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
Regarding the Venerable’s question, "How does one observe all phenomena? Śāriputra,

when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe form and so forth, up to consciousness, as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached.

“Observe the sense base of the eye, up to and including the sense base of the mind, as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither secluded nor non-secluded.”

"Contemplate the sphere of form, up to and including the sphere of mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor untranquil, and neither secluded nor unsecluded."

"Contemplate the eye-element up to the mind-element as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspiration nor without aspiration, neither tranquil nor untranquil, and neither detached nor undetached."

"Observe the realm of form, up to and including the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspiration nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached."

“Observe the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached.”

“Observe eye-contact, and so on up to mind-contact, as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspiration nor without aspiration, neither tranquil nor untranquil, and neither detached nor undetached.”

“Observe that all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither secluded nor non-secluded.”

"Contemplate the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached."

"One contemplates internal emptiness, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached."

"One contemplates the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eight factors of the noble path as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached."

"In this way, up to and including the examination of the Buddha’s ten powers and even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with vows nor vowless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached."

“Observe that all samādhi-gates and all dhāraṇī-gates are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with vows nor vowless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached.”

"In this way, one contemplates that all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with aspirations nor aspirationless, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, and neither detached nor non-detached."
“Śāriputra! These are called the examination of all phenomena. Śāriputra!”
"When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should observe all phenomena in this manner.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason, worthy one, do you speak thus?"

If form is neither arising nor ceasing, it is not form; if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither arising nor ceasing, they are also not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness. Likewise, up to and including omniscience—if omniscience is neither arising nor ceasing, it is not omniscience; and if the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are neither arising nor ceasing, are they also not the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects?
Subhūti replied, "Śāriputra!

Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is neither arising nor ceasing, and there is no form, up to and including consciousness."
For this reason it is said:

that form is neither produced nor extinguished is itself not form; that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither produced nor extinguished are themselves not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Śāriputra! In this way, even up to omniscience, the nature of omniscience is empty; the knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty. Within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor ceasing, nor is there omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects.
For this reason it is said:

that which is the non-arising and non-ceasing of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is not itself all-knowledge; likewise, the non-arising and non-ceasing of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are not themselves the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"Virtuous one, for what reason do you say: 'Form is non-dual and is not form;

feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are non-dual and are not feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness'; and so on, up to: 'Omniscience is non-dual and is not omniscience; the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual and are not the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects'?"
Subhūti replied, “Śāriputra!

Whether it be form or non-duality, whether it be feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness or non-duality—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
For this reason it is said:
form is non-dual and is not form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual and are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Śāriputra! Thus, whether it be omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) or non-duality, whether it be the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), or their non-duality—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics (*alakṣaṇa*).
For this reason it is said:

omniscience is non-dual and yet is not omniscience; the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual and yet are neither the knowledge of the paths nor the knowledge of all aspects.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Subhūti: "Virtuous one, for what reason do you say this:
that form enters into the category of non-dual phenomena;

that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness enter into the category of non-dual phenomena; and so on, up to omniscience entering into the category of non-dual phenomena, and the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects entering into the category of non-dual phenomena?"
Subhūti replied, “Śāriputra!

Form is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from form. Form itself is non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing themselves are form.”

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
For this reason it is said:
"The sphere of form enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness enter into the category of non-dual dharmas, Śāriputra."

In this way, even up to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), it is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from omniscience. Omniscience is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves omniscience.

The knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
"For this reason it is said:
'The knowledge of all modes enters into the category of non-dual dharmas; the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects enter into the category of non-dual dharmas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and contemplates all phenomena, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives the non-arising of a self because it is ultimately pure; likewise, they perceive the non-arising of the ‘seer’ because it is ultimately pure;
they perceive the non-arising of form because it is ultimately pure, up to and including the perception of the non-arising of consciousness because it is ultimately pure.”

One sees that the sense-base of the eye is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; likewise, one sees that the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.

One sees that the sense-base of forms is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; likewise, one sees that the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena (*dharma*) are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.

One sees that the eye-element is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; likewise, one sees that the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, mind, and mental phenomena are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.
They see that the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; even unto seeing that the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;

they see that the realm of eye-consciousness (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; even unto seeing that the realm of mind-consciousness (*manovijñānadhātu*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;
they see that eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; even unto seeing that mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure.

He sees that all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are non-arising because they are ultimately pure; and so on, up to seeing that all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.

He sees that the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; and so on, up to seeing that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure.

He sees that internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; and so on, up to seeing that the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure.

One sees that the four foundations of mindfulness are non-arising because they are ultimately pure; likewise, one sees that even the eight branches of the noble path are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.

In this way, one sees that even the ten powers of a Buddha are non-arising because they are ultimately pure, and one sees that even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.
One sees that all doors of samādhi are non-arising because they are ultimately pure, and one sees that all doors of dhāraṇī are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.

In this way, up to and including the vision of the non-arising of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), because it is ultimately pure; the vision of the non-arising of the knowledge of the paths and their aspects (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), because they are ultimately pure;

the vision of the non-arising of the dharmas of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*), because they are ultimately pure; the vision of the non-arising of ordinary beings themselves, because they are ultimately pure;

the vision of the non-arising of the dharmas of stream-enterers (*srotāpanna*), because they are ultimately pure; and the vision of the non-arising of stream-enterers themselves, because they are ultimately pure.
One sees that the dharma of the once-returner is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; one sees that the once-returner is non-arising because it is ultimately pure.
One sees that the dharma of the non-returner is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; one sees that the non-returner is non-arising because it is ultimately pure.
One sees that the dharma of the arhat is non-arising because it is ultimately pure; one sees that the arhat is non-arising because it is ultimately pure.
One sees that the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure; one sees that the pratyekabuddhas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
one sees that all the dharmas of the bodhisattvas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure; one sees that all the bodhisattvas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
one sees that the dharmas of all the Buddhas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure; and one sees that all the Buddhas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.
"One sees that all sentient beings are non-arising dharmas because they are ultimately pure; one sees that all sentient beings are unborn because they are ultimately pure.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 423, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter on Detachment, Twenty-four, Part Two. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed Subhūti, saying:

"As I understand the meaning of what you have said, from myself up to the 'seer' (draṣṭṛ), there is ultimate non-arising; from form (*rūpa*) up to consciousness (*vijñāna*), there is ultimate non-arising. Likewise, up to the dharmas of all Buddhas and the Buddhas themselves, there is ultimate non-arising; the dharmas of all sentient beings and all sentient beings themselves are ultimately non-arising."

If this were so, there would be no distinction in taking birth within the six destinies; one would not attain the fruit of a stream-enterer through being a stream-enterer, nor would one attain the fruit of a once-returner through being a once-returner, nor the fruit of a non-returner through being a non-returner, nor the fruit of an arhat through being an arhat; one would not attain pratyekabuddha-enlightenment as a pratyekabuddha, nor would a bodhisattva attain the knowledge of all aspects.

Furthermore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas would not experience profound weariness toward the cycle of birth and death in the six destinies, nor would they attain the five kinds of enlightenment for the sake of delivering others.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If all dharmas are ultimately unarisen, how is it that a stream-enterer, for the sake of the fruit of stream-entry, diligently cultivates the path to eternally sever the three fetters?"
How does a once-returner, for the sake of the fruit of once-returning, diligently cultivate the path that forever abandons greed, hatred, and delusion?
How does a non-returner, for the sake of the fruit of non-returning, diligently cultivate the path that forever abandons the fetters pertaining to the lower realm?
How does an arhat, for the sake of the fruit of arhatship, diligently cultivate the path that leads to the permanent abandonment of the higher fetters?
How does a pratyekabuddha, for the sake of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, diligently cultivate the path of independently awakening to the principle of dependent origination?

How is it that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for the sake of delivering immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, practice hundreds of thousands of difficult and painful ascetic practices, fully undergoing immeasurable and unbearable heavy sufferings?
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
And how do the Buddhas turn the sublime wheel of Dharma for the sake of delivering immeasurable sentient beings from suffering?
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied to Śāriputra:
"It is not that within those dharmas of non-arising I perceive any differentiation in rebirth within the six destinies;
nor is it that within those dharmas of non-arising I perceive anyone who is able to enter the clear realization of the truths."

It is not that within those phenomena of non-arising (*anutpāda-dharma*), I see one who has entered the stream attaining the fruit of stream-entry, one who returns once attaining the fruit of once-returning, one who does not return attaining the fruit of non-returning, or an arhat attaining the fruit of arhatship; nor do I see one who is a pratyekabuddha attaining pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, nor one who is a bodhisattva attaining the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
It is not that within those phenomena of non-arising, I see a bodhisattva mahāsattva weary of birth and death and attaining the five types of enlightenment;
nor do I see a śrāvaka practicing the path to sever the fetters, nor a pratyekabuddha diligently cultivating the path of the dependent origination of solitary awakening.

It is not that, within those phenomena of non-arising, I perceive any bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing manifold asceticisms or undergoing various heavy sufferings for the sake of liberating sentient beings; rather, these bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not give rise to the notion of "difficult practices" or "suffering."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
if one gives rise to the notion of difficult and painful practices, one will ultimately be unable to bring great benefit to immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings.

Śāriputra! All bodhisattvas, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension, give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings. Abiding in the perception of them as their own parents, brothers, wives, children, and even themselves, they resolve to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to deliver them, thereby being able to bring about their great benefit.
“Śāriputra! All bodhisattvas should form this thought:

‘Just as my own self-nature cannot be found when sought through all modes, in all places, and at all times among all phenomena, so too it is with internal and external phenomena; they are entirely non-existent and unobtainable.’”

If one abides in this perception, one will not perceive any difficulty in performing arduous and ascetic practices; by means of this, one is able to perform hundreds of thousands of arduous and ascetic practices for the sake of immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, thereby bringing them great benefit.
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have no grasping or appropriation toward any phenomena, any sentient beings, in any manner, at any location, or at any time.

Śāriputra! It is not that within those dharmas of non-arising I perceive a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who has realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and turned the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because all phenomena and all sentient beings are unapprehendable.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti: "What do you think?
Is there something to be realized by means of phenomena that arise, or is there something to be realized by means of phenomena that do not arise?"
Subhūti replied, "I do not wish to realize anything by means of dharmas that arise, nor do I wish to realize anything by means of dharmas that do not arise."
Śāriputra said: "If this is so, is there then absolutely no attainment and no clear realization? Subhūti replied:
"Although there is attainment and there is clear realization, in reality they are not realized by means of two dharmas.

Śāriputra! It is only in accordance with worldly convention that attainment and clear realization are provisionally established; in the ultimate sense, there is neither attainment nor clear realization."

Śāriputra! It is only in accordance with worldly convention that one designates the existence of stream-enterers and the fruit of stream-entry; the existence of once-returners and the fruit of once-returning; the existence of non-returners and the fruit of non-returning; the existence of arhats and the fruit of arhatship; the existence of pratyekabuddhas and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the existence of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the conduct of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva; and the existence of buddhas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a buddha. In the ultimate sense, there are no such things as stream-enterers and so forth.

Śāriputra said: "If it is the case that 'attainment,' 'clear realization,' and 'stream-entry' are merely designated according to worldly convention and are not the ultimate truth, then are the distinctions among the six realms of existence also merely designated according to worldly convention and not the ultimate truth?"
Subhūti replied: “So it is! So it is!”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because within the ultimate truth (paramārtha), there is neither the maturation of karma (karmavipāka) nor defilement and purification.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti: "What do you think?
Is it intended to cause unarisen phenomena to arise, or is it intended to cause already arisen phenomena to arise?"
Subhūti replied, “I do not wish for unarisen phenomena to arise, nor do I wish for already arisen phenomena to arise. Śāriputra said:
“What are those dharmas that have not yet arisen, which you, O Venerable One, do not wish to cause to arise?
Subhūti replied: “Śāriputra!...”
Form is an unarisen phenomenon; I do not wish for it to arise.
Why? Because its intrinsic nature is empty.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are dharmas that have not yet arisen; I do not wish for them to arise.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
Even up to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, these are dharmas that have not yet arisen, and I do not wish for them to arise.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
Śāriputra asked: "What are those dharmas that have already arisen, which you, Venerable One, do not wish to cause to arise? Subhūti replied:
“Śāriputra! Form is a dharma that has already arisen; I do not wish for it to arise. Why is this?
Because they are empty of intrinsic nature.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are dharmas already arisen; I do not wish for them to arise. Why is this?
Because they are empty of intrinsic nature.
Even up to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, which is a dharma already arisen, I do not wish for it to arise. Why is that?
"Because its intrinsic nature is empty.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti: "What do you think?"
"Do you wish for that which has already arisen to arise again, or do you wish for that which has not yet arisen to arise? Subhūti replied,
"I do not wish for that which has already arisen to arise, nor do I wish for that which has not yet arisen to arise."

Why is this? Śāriputra, these two dharmas—arising and non-arising—are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.
"For this reason, I do not wish to cause birth to arise, nor do I wish to cause non-birth to arise.
Then, Śāriputra asked Subhūti again:
"Venerable one, do you delight in discoursing upon the characteristics of non-arising within the dharma of non-arising that you have explained?"
Subhūti replied: "Śāriputra!
Regarding the dharmas of non-arising that have been taught, I do not even delight in discoursing upon the characteristics of non-arising."

Why is this? Śāriputra, whether it be non-arising dharmas, the characteristic of non-arising, or the delight in eloquent exposition—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
At that time, Śāriputra again asked Subhūti:
"Regarding the non-arising of dharmas, one utters the word 'non-arising'; is this word 'non-arising' itself also non-arising?"
Subhūti replied: “So it is! So it is!”
It is exactly as you have said.
When one utters the word "non-arising" with respect to dharmas that do not arise, both this dharma and this word are devoid of the meaning of arising. Why is this so?
Śāriputra! Form is unarisen;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also unarisen. Why is this?
Because their intrinsic nature is empty,
