If good sons and good daughters regarding this Prajñāpāramitā listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated, then these good sons and good daughters will always be protected by the Four Great Heavenly Kings of the trichiliocosm, Śakra Devendra, Mahābrahmā the Lord of the Sahā World, the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, and others—such as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras, as well as other benevolent spirits—who will all come to guard them, preventing any calamities or afflictions from invading them, and ensuring that whatever they seek in accordance with the Dharma shall not fail to be fulfilled."

In all Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas also constantly protect and keep in mind these good sons and good daughters, causing their evils to gradually diminish and their wholesome dharmas to increase.
That is to say, it causes the increase of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension;
it also causes the increase of the contemplation of internal emptiness up to the contemplation of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, by means of non-apprehension;
and it also causes the increase of the four applications of mindfulness, as explained at length, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, by means of non-apprehension.
They also cause all gateways of samādhi and all gateways of dhāraṇī to increase, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient;
they also cause all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects to increase, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient.

Kauśika! Because of these causes and conditions, the speech of these sons and daughters of good family is majestic and solemn, such that all who hear it receive it with respect; their discourse is measured and their words are free from error or confusion; they well understand how to repay kindness and steadfastly serve virtuous friends; and they are not obscured by stinginess, envy, anger, resentment, concealment, vexation, flattery, deception, or hypocrisy.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family themselves abstain from taking life and also encourage others to abstain from taking life; they correctly praise the dharma of abstaining from taking life and joyfully extol those who abstain from taking life. This extends even to their own abstention from wrong views, as well as encouraging others to abstain from wrong views, correctly praising the dharma of abstaining from wrong views, and joyfully extolling those who abstain from wrong views.”

They themselves practice the perfection of generosity and also encourage others to practice the perfection of generosity; they unerringly extol the method of practicing the perfection of generosity and joyfully praise those who practice it. This continues up to them themselves practicing the perfection of wisdom, encouraging others to practice the perfection of wisdom, unerringly extolling the method of practicing the perfection of wisdom, and joyfully praising those who practice it.

They themselves practice inner emptiness and also encourage others to practice inner emptiness; they correctly extol the dharma of practicing inner emptiness and joyfully praise those who practice inner emptiness. This extends even to their own practice of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as encouraging others to practice the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; they correctly extol the dharma of practicing the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence and joyfully praise those who practice the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They themselves are able to cultivate all gateways of samādhi and also encourage others to cultivate all gateways of samādhi; they unerringly praise the method of cultivating all gateways of samādhi and joyfully extol those who cultivate all gateways of samādhi.

They themselves are able to cultivate all gateways of dhāraṇī and also encourage others to cultivate all gateways of dhāraṇī; they unerringly praise the method of cultivating all gateways of dhāraṇī and joyfully extol those who cultivate all gateways of dhāraṇī.

They themselves are able to cultivate the four dhyānas and also encourage others to cultivate the four dhyānas; they unerringly extol the method of cultivating the four dhyānas and joyfully praise those who cultivate the four dhyānas.

They themselves are able to cultivate the four immeasurables and also encourage others to cultivate the four immeasurables; they unerringly extol the method of cultivating the four immeasurables and joyfully praise those who cultivate the four immeasurables.

They themselves are able to cultivate the four formless attainments and also encourage others to cultivate the four formless attainments; they unerringly extol the method of cultivating the four formless attainments and joyfully praise those who cultivate the four formless attainments.

They themselves are able to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness and also encourage others to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness; they unerringly praise the method of cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness and joyfully extol those who cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness.

This extends even to their own ability to cultivate the eight branches of the noble path, as well as encouraging others to cultivate the eight branches of the noble path, unerringly praising the method of cultivating the eight branches of the noble path, and joyfully extolling those who cultivate the eight branches of the noble path.

One personally cultivates the three gates of liberation, encourages others to cultivate the three gates of liberation, unerringly extols the method of cultivating the three gates of liberation, and joyfully praises those who cultivate the three gates of liberation.

They themselves are able to cultivate the eight liberations and also encourage others to cultivate the eight liberations; they unerringly extol the dharma of cultivating the eight liberations and joyfully praise those who cultivate them.

They themselves are able to enter the nine successive meditative attainments in both forward and reverse order and also encourage others to enter the nine successive meditative attainments in both forward and reverse order; they unerringly extol the dharma of entering the nine successive meditative attainments in both forward and reverse order and joyfully praise those who enter them.

They themselves are able to cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha and also encourage others to cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha; they unerringly praise the method of cultivating the ten powers of a Buddha and joyfully extol those who cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha.

This extends even to their own cultivation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and their encouragement of others to cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they unerringly praise the method of cultivating the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and joyfully extol those who cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

One personally cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, and also encourages others to cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity; one unerringly extols the dharma of cultivating non-forgetfulness and constant equanimity, and joyfully praises those who cultivate non-forgetfulness and constant equanimity.

They themselves cultivate omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); they also encourage others to cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; they unerringly praise the practice of omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; and they joyfully extol those who cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.

"Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family practice the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, and dedicate them together with all sentient beings equally toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family constantly reflect:

‘If I do not practice the perfection of generosity, I shall be born into a poor and lowly family; lacking even basic influence, how could I possibly bring all sentient beings to maturity or purify a Buddha-field?’”
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I do not protect the perfection of pure ethical discipline, I shall be reborn in the various evil destinies; I would not even obtain the body of a lowly human being, so how could I mature all sentient beings or purify a Buddha-field?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I do not cultivate the perfection of patience, my faculties will be impaired and my physical appearance will be ugly; I shall not possess the perfect body of a bodhisattva. If I were to obtain the perfect body of a bodhisattva and practice the bodhisattva conduct, sentient beings who see me would feel deep joy and would faithfully accept what I say, and I would certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If I do not obtain this perfect body, how can I mature all sentient beings and purify the buddha-fields?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I were to be indolent and fail to arouse the perfection of vigor, I would not even be able to attain the supreme path of a bodhisattva; how then could I bring all sentient beings to maturity or purify the Buddha-fields?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If my mind were distracted and I did not enter the perfection of meditative concentration, I would not even be able to give rise to the sublime samādhis of a bodhisattva; how then could I mature all sentient beings or purify the buddha-fields?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I were without wisdom and did not study the *prajñāpāramitā*, I would not even be able to attain the skillful means to transcend the stages of the two vehicles; how then could I mature all sentient beings or purify the Buddha-fields?
"How much less could they possibly attain the knowledge of all-knowledge! "Kauśika,
these sons and daughters of good family constantly maintain this thought:"
"I should not follow the power of stinginess and greed; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of generosity would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of immoral conduct; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of ethical discipline would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of anger and resentment; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of patience would not be fulfilled."
I should not follow the power of indolence; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of diligence would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of mental distraction; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of meditative concentration would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of faulty wisdom; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of wisdom would not be fulfilled.

If my cultivation of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were not fulfilled, I would ultimately never be able to attain the knowledge of all modes.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), shall—regarding this Prajñāpāramitā—hear it with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, transcribe it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated; they will certainly obtain such meritorious benefits in both the present life and the future.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 427. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Two: Chapter Twenty-nine on Embracing, Section Two. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

Thus, this perfection of wisdom is exceedingly rare; it tames the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they do not become conceited, while enabling them to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: "Kauśika,
how does the perfection of wisdom discipline the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they do not become conceited, yet are able to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes?"
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the mundane perfection of giving, if they give a gift to the Buddha, they form this thought:”
"I am able to give to the Buddha.
If one practices giving toward bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, the destitute, the aged and infirm, travelers on the road, or beggars, one then forms this thought:
"I am able to give to the bodhisattvas, and so forth, down to the beggars."
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva lacks skillful means, although they practice giving, they give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate it toward the knowledge of all modes.
“Bhagavān, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the worldly perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they think:
‘I am able to practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.’”
They also form this thought:
"I am able to fulfill the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva lacks skillful means, although they practice from pure ethical discipline up to wisdom, they give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four foundations of mindfulness of the world, they think:
‘I am able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness.’”
They also form this thought:
"I am able to fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means, although they practice the four foundations of mindfulness, they give rise to a conceited mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to practice the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.’”
Or they may think: "I am able to fulfill the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path.

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva lacks skillful means, although they practice the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, they give rise to a conceited mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.’”
Or they may think: "I am able to fulfill the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means, although they practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, they give rise to a conceited mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice all the gateways of samādhi and the gateways of dhāraṇī, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to practice all the gateways of samādhi and the gateways of dhāraṇī.’”
Or they may think: "I am able to fulfill all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means, although they practice all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī, they give rise to a conceited mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to practice the ten powers of a buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.’”
Or they may think: "I am able to fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means, although they practice the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to practice all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.’”
Or they may think: "I am able to fulfill all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), although they practice all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects, they give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bring sentient beings to maturity and purify Buddha-fields, if they should think:
‘I am able to bring sentient beings to maturity and purify Buddha-fields; no others have this ability,’ [they fall into a conceited state].”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means, although they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, they give rise to a conceited mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!

Thus, when the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practices various wholesome dharmas by relying on a worldly mind, because they lack skillful means and their minds are disturbed by the grasping at ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ although they practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not attain it; consequently, they cannot truly subdue their arrogant minds, nor can they truly dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of giving, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend a giver, a recipient, or the gift. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom while practicing giving, they are able to truly subdue the haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.”

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, or any phenomena. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom to practice ethical discipline up to wisdom, they are able to truly subdue the haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the four applications of mindfulness that transcend the world, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the four applications of mindfulness, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects, nor any phenomena whatsoever. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom while practicing the four applications of mindfulness, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects, they are able to truly subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings sentient beings to maturity and purifies buddha-fields, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the maturing of sentient beings, the purification of buddha-fields, or any phenomena whatsoever. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom to bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, they are able to truly subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).”
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, I say: This Prajñāpāramitā is most rare;
it subdues the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they do not become arrogant, yet enables them to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
Chapter 30: Stūpas, Part Two. Chapter Thirty: Stūpas. At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters are able to wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, these good sons and good daughters will always possess peace and security in body and constant joy in mind, and shall not be afflicted by any calamities or misfortunes.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, with sincere hearts, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, attend upon, make offerings to, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, then when these sons or daughters of good family are amidst the ranks of an army engaged in battle, if they sincerely recite this *Prajñāpāramitā*, they will be protected by compassion for all sentient beings; they shall not be harmed or killed by blades or weapons, and their adversaries will all give rise to thoughts of loving-kindness. Even if those adversaries harbor evil intentions, they will naturally retreat and be defeated."
It is impossible that such sons and daughters of good family should lose their lives or be wounded by swords and arrows in the midst of military campaigns. Why is this?

Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family, employing the method of non-apprehension, have for a long night cultivated the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. Thus, they are able to subdue the weapons of greed within themselves and likewise remove the weapons of greed from others;
they are able to subdue the weapons of hatred within themselves and likewise remove the weapons of hatred from others.
One is able to subdue the weapons of ignorance within oneself and likewise remove the weapons of ignorance from others;
one is able to subdue the weapons of arrogance within oneself and likewise remove the weapons of arrogance from others;
one is able to subdue the weapons of evil views within oneself and likewise remove the weapons of evil views from others.
One is able to subdue the weapons of latent tendencies within oneself, and is also able to remove the weapons of latent tendencies in others;
one is able to subdue the weapons of the defilements of active outbursts within oneself, and is also able to remove the weapons of the defilements of active outbursts in others;
one is able to subdue the weapons of evil karma within oneself, and is also able to remove the weapons of evil karma in others.

Kauśika! For this reason, even if these sons and daughters of good family should enter the midst of a military array, they will not be wounded or killed by swords or weapons; all their adversaries will give rise to thoughts of loving-kindness, and should any harbor evil intentions, they will naturally retreat and be defeated.

Because of the majestic power of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* recited with a sincere mind by these sons and daughters of good family, it is simply impossible that they would lose their lives or be wounded by swords and arrows even while amidst a military array.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they constantly listen with a sincere heart to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to principle, make offerings to it, revere and respect it, praise it, copy it, explain it, and cause it to spread widely. Such good sons and good daughters cannot be harmed by any poisons, sorcery, malevolent spirits, curses, incantations, or spells; water cannot drown them, fire cannot burn them, and they cannot be injured by weapons, wild beasts, enemies, thieves, evil deities, various heterodoxies, or malevolent ghosts.

Why is this so? Kausika! This Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is a great illuminating mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the mantra of the unequaled; this Prajñāpāramitā is the king of all mantras, supreme and most wondrous, with none able to equal it. Possessing great majestic power, it can subdue all things and cannot itself be subdued by anything.
These sons and daughters of good family who diligently practice and study this king of mantras will not harm themselves, nor will they harm others, nor will they harm both.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family who study this Prajñāpāramitā realize that neither self nor other can be apprehended.

Kauśika! When these sons and daughters of good family study this great king of spells, the Prajñāpāramitā, they do not apprehend a self, nor do they apprehend sentient beings, up to and including those who know and those who see;

they do not apprehend form, nor do they apprehend feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, up to and including all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Because there is nothing to be apprehended in these things, they do not bring harm to themselves, do not bring harm to others, and do not bring harm to both. "Kauśika!

When these sons of good family and daughters of good family study this Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, although they apprehend neither me nor the Dharma, they realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. They observe the differences in the mental activities of all sentient beings and, according to what is appropriate for them, turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, causing all who practice as taught to obtain benefit and happiness."
Why is this? Kauśika!

In the past, the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas diligently studied this great king of dhāraṇīs, the Prajñāpāramitā; they have already realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and have turned the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.

In the future, the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who diligently study this great king of dhāraṇīs, the Prajñāpāramitā, shall realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.

At present, in the infinite worlds of the ten directions, there are assemblies of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, diligently practicing and studying this great king of dhāraṇīs, the Prajñāpāramitā, have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and are turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, with sincere hearts, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, then in whatever lands, cities, or towns these good sons and good daughters may dwell, humans and non-humans alike shall not be harmed by any calamities, misfortunes, or epidemics."
Why is this? Kausika!

Wherever these sons and daughters of good family dwell, all the gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, as well as the nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras of this trichiliocosm and the infinite worlds of the ten directions, will constantly come to protect them, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising them, so that no obstacles shall arise for the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters write down this Great Divine Mantra King of the Prajñāpāramitā and place it in a pure location, making offerings to it, honoring, respecting, and praising it—even if they do not hear it, nor receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, or contemplate it according to principle, nor explain or analyze it for others—the humans and non-humans in that dwelling place, city, district, or royal capital shall not be harmed by any calamities, misfortunes, or epidemics."
Why is this? Kausika!

Wherever this Great Dharani King of the Perfection of Wisdom resides, all the gods from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akanistha Heaven, as well as the nagas, asuras, and others throughout this trichiliocosm and the infinite worlds of the ten directions, will constantly come to protect, make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise it, so that no obstacles may arise for this Great Dharani King of the Perfection of Wisdom.

Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family merely write down this great king of divine mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, and place it in a pure location to offer worship, honor, respect, and praise, they still obtain such benefits in the present life; how much more so for those who can hear it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the truth, and extensively explain and analyze it for others!
"You should know that such individuals possess boundless merit; they will swiftly realize Bodhi and bring benefit and happiness to all. Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good men or good women fear enemies, wild beasts, calamities, malevolent incantations, epidemics, poisons, spells, and the like, they should write out this Great Divine Spell-King, the Prajñāpāramitā, in portions however large or small, place it in a fragrant sachet, and keep it within a precious casket, constantly carrying it with them. By making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it, all causes for fear will naturally vanish, for devas, nāgas, spirits, and ghosts will constantly protect them."

Kauśika! For example, if a person or even an animal of the animal realm enters the precincts of the Bodhi tree, or merely reaches the vicinity of those precincts, neither humans nor non-humans will be able to harm them.
Why is this? Kauśika!

All Buddhas of the past, future, and present have sat in this very place to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Having attained enlightenment, they bestow upon all sentient beings freedom from fear, freedom from dread, freedom from enmity, and freedom from harm, such that their bodies and minds dwell in peace and happiness.
He establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to abide in the sublime conduct of human and celestial nobility;
he establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to abide in the blissful sublime conduct of the three vehicles;

he establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to realize and attain, in this very life, either the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship.
They establish immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings so that they may realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Such supreme matters are all due to the majestic power of the perfection of wisdom; therefore, all devas, nāgas, asuras, and others here together protect, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise it.

It should be known that it is likewise with this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*: wherever it resides, all devas, nāgas, asuras, and others will constantly come to protect it, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising it, so that no obstacles shall arise for the *Prajñāpāramitā*.

“Kauśika! Wherever this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā may be located, you should know that this place is a true caitya; all sentient beings should pay homage to it, and they should make offerings with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags and canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters were to write down this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and were to adorn, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise it in various ways; and furthermore, were to make offerings with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps—[how much merit would they generate]?”

There may be sons and daughters of good family who, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, erect stūpas adorned with the seven precious gems, place the Buddha’s śarīras within them contained in jeweled caskets, and offer them worship, reverence, respect, and praise; furthermore, they provide offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps.
"Between these two resulting merits, which is greater?
The Buddha told Kauśika, "I shall question you in return; answer as you see fit."
"What do you think?
By training in and learning from what dharmas does the Tathāgata attain all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) and the body adorned with the marks and signs?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“World-Honored One!

The Tathāgata’s attainment of all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) and his body adorned with the marks and signs (*lakṣaṇavyañjana*) is acquired by training in this profound sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).”
The Buddha said,
“Kauśika, it is so! It is thus!”
So it is! It is as you have said.

Because I have studied and trained in this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, I have attained the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) and the body endowed with the marks and signs of excellence.
Why is this? Kausika!
It is impossible for one who does not study the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Kauśika! It is not merely by attaining a body endowed with the marks and signs that one is called a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; rather, it is because of having realized all-aspect wisdom (sarvākārajñatā) that one is called a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Kauśika! The omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) attained by the Tathāgata arises with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) as its cause;
the Buddha’s body of marks and signs (lakṣaṇavyañjana-kāya) serves merely as its basis. If one does not rely upon the Buddha’s body of marks and signs, omniscience would have no means of arising.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is the direct cause for the arising of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna); and because one desires to bring this knowledge into manifestation and maintain its continuity, one further cultivates and accumulates the marks and signs of a Buddha’s body.

If this body of marks and signs were not the basis for the Buddha’s omniscience, then all devas, nāgas, humans, and non-humans would not offer it sincere worship and respect; however, because this body of marks and signs serves as the support for the Buddha’s omniscience, the various devas, nāgas, spirits, humans, and non-humans offer it worship and respect.
For this reason, after my parinirvāṇa, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others will offer worship and reverence to my śarīra relics. Kausika!

If sons or daughters of good family merely offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā, they thereby offer worship to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), to the Buddha’s body adorned with the marks and signs (*lakṣaṇavyañjana*) upon which that knowledge relies, and to the Buddha’s relics (*śarīra*) after his parinirvāṇa.
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because all-aspect omniscience, as well as the body endowed with the marks and signs and the śarīra relics, all have the perfection of wisdom as their root.

Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters merely offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to the body of the Buddha and his śarīras, they are not offering worship to the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) nor to this Prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because the physical remains of the Buddha’s body are not the root of this *prajñāpāramitā* and its knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Kauśika! For this reason, if sons or daughters of good family wish to make offerings to the Buddha’s body, his mind, or his other merits, they should first hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, and explain such profound sūtras as this Prajñāpāramitā; thereafter, they should further honor them with various kinds of excellent and sublime offerings.

"For this reason, Kauśika, if any sons or daughters of good family write down this profound sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, and honor, revere, respect, and praise it with various adornments and offerings; and furthermore, offer to it various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain great merit]."

Suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, erect a stūpa adorned with the seven precious jewels, place the Buddha’s śarīra relics within it contained in a jeweled casket, and offer them worship, reverence, respect, and praise; furthermore, they provide offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps.
Of the two resulting merits, the former is greater by an immeasurable number of times.
Why is this so, Kauśika?
Thus, this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* is able to give rise to the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*;
it is able to manifest internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*);
and it is able to give rise to the four applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), as explained at length, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*).
Because it can give rise to all gateways of samādhi and gateways of dhāraṇī;
because it can accomplish the maturation of sentient beings and the purification of Buddha-fields;

because it can accomplish the perfection of the lineage of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the perfection of physical form and strength, the perfection of wealth and treasures, and the perfection of retinues; it can accomplish...
Because of great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity toward all, one is able to bring about the great clans of the kṣatriyas,
the great clans of the brāhmaṇas, the great clans of the householders, and the great clans of the lay-merchants in the world,
as well as the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; because of this, one is able to bring about the emptiness of the world.
Because it pertains to the gods of the [four] spheres of infinite space up to the gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
because it can accomplish the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
because it can accomplish the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas; because it can accomplish that which is most supreme and...
“Because it surpasses all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas by means of their knowledge of all aspects.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

As for those people of Jambudvīpa who do not offer worship, respect, honor, or praise to this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, do they perhaps not know that by offering worship, respect, honor, and praise to the profound Prajñāpāramitā, one obtains such meritorious benefits?
The Buddha said to Kauśika:
"I shall now question you; answer as you see fit.
What do you think?"
Within Jambudvīpa, how many people have attained verified confidence in the Buddha, verified confidence in the Dharma, and verified confidence in the Saṅgha?
How many people are free from doubt regarding the Buddha, free from doubt regarding the Dharma, and free from doubt regarding the Saṅgha?
How many people have reached the ultimate realization of the Buddha, the ultimate realization of the Dharma, and the ultimate realization of the Saṅgha?
How many people have attained the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment?
How many people have attained the three gates of liberation?
How many people have attained the eight liberations?
How many people have attained the nine successive meditative absorptions?
How many people have attained the six supernormal powers?
How many have attained the four analytical knowledges?
How many have permanently severed the three fetters and attained the fruit of stream-entry?
How many people have thinned out greed, hatred, and delusion to attain the fruit of once-returning?
How many people have severed the five lower fetters to attain the fruit of non-returning?
How many people have severed the five fetters of the higher realms and attained the fruit of arhatship?
How many people have resolved their minds and are certain to attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha?
How many people have resolved their minds and are certain to attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
“World-Honored One!

Within Jambudvīpa there are a few people who have attained pure faith in the Buddha, pure faith in the Dharma, and pure faith in the Saṃgha; even there are a few people who have resolved their minds and are certain to proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

Within Jambudvīpa, there is an extremely small number of people who attain pure confidence in the Buddha, pure confidence in the Dharma, and pure confidence in the Saṅgha. Even fewer are those who have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha. Even fewer still are those who resolve their minds to definitely proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Even fewer are those who, having resolved their minds, diligently practice and proceed toward the conduct of enlightenment. And even fewer are those who, having diligently practiced the conduct of enlightenment, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Kauśika!

Among the classes of sentient beings wandering in saṃsāra, throughout immeasurable lifetimes, they have for the most part not seen the Buddha, not heard the True Dharma, not drawn near to the Saṅgha, not practiced giving, not maintained pure precepts, not cultivated patience, not aroused diligence, not practiced meditative concentration, and not studied wisdom.

They do not hear of internal emptiness and do not cultivate internal emptiness; likewise, they do not hear of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence and do not cultivate the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They do not hear of the four foundations of mindfulness and do not cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness; this is explained at length up to: they do not hear of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and do not cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. They do not hear of all the doors of samādhi and do not cultivate all the doors of samādhi;
they do not hear of all the doors of dhāraṇī and do not cultivate all the doors of dhāraṇī.

They do not hear of all-knowledge, nor do they cultivate all-knowledge; they do not hear of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects, nor do they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.

Kauśika! By this cause and condition, you should know that among those in this Jambudvīpa, there are only a very small number of people who attain verified clarity regarding the Buddha, verified clarity regarding the Dharma, and verified clarity regarding the Saṅgha. Even fewer are those who have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha. Even fewer still are those who resolve their minds to definitely proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Even fewer, having already resolved their minds, diligently cultivate the practices leading to enlightenment. And even fewer, having diligently cultivated the practices for enlightenment, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! I shall now question you; answer as you see fit. Kauśika!"
What do you think?
Setting aside all the human beings of Jambudvīpa, how many sentient beings in this trichiliocosm offer worship and respect to their parents and teachers?
How many sentient beings honor and revere śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas?
How many sentient beings practice giving, observe the precepts, undertake the fast, and cultivate merit?

How many sentient beings dwell amidst various desires with the perception of weariness, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of impurity, the perception of revulsion toward food, and the perception that all worlds are not to be delighted in?
How many sentient beings cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?
How many sentient beings, having even resolved their minds, are certain to proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas?
How many sentient beings, having already generated the resolve, are diligently practicing the conduct that leads to enlightenment?
How many sentient beings are refining and nurturing the mind directed toward enlightenment?
How many sentient beings skillfully practice the perfection of wisdom?
How many sentient beings abide in the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva?
"How many sentient beings will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
"World-Honored One!"

In this trichiliocosm, there are few sentient beings who offer worship and respect to their parents and teachers, and even fewer sentient beings who swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Buddha said,
“Kauśika, it is so! It is thus!”
So it is! It is just as you have said, Kauśika!

In this trichiliocosm, there are very few sentient beings who offer worship and respect to their parents and teachers; even fewer sentient beings offer worship and respect to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; even fewer sentient beings attain the stage of non-retrogression as bodhisattvas; and even fewer sentient beings swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

With my pure, unsurpassed Buddha-eye, I survey all worlds throughout the ten directions. Although there are immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings who have resolved their minds to definitely proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and who diligently cultivate the practices leading to enlightenment, because they are far removed from the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), only one, two, or three of those sentient beings manage to reach the stage of non-retrogression as bodhisattvas; for the most part, they fall back into the inferior stages of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."
Why is this? Kauśika!

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is extremely difficult to attain; for it cannot be realized by those with evil wisdom, the indolent, those of inferior diligence, inferior resolve, or inferior sentient beings.

“Kauśika! For this reason, if sons or daughters of good family resolve their minds upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, diligently practice the conduct leading to enlightenment, and desire to abide on the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattvas so as to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without hindrance, they should repeatedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, inquire of their teachers, and delight in explaining it to others—this very profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Having performed these deeds, one should further transcribe [the text], adorning it with various precious objects, and offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise; furthermore, one should make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags and canopies, as well as various wonderful, rare, musical instruments, and lamps.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should also hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, inquire of their teachers, and delight in explaining to others those other excellent and wholesome dharmas that are subsumed within this profound perfection of wisdom.”
What are the other superior wholesome dharmas that are subsumed within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*? They are: from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of meditative concentration;

the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; all doors of samādhi and doors of dhāraṇī; the four foundations of mindfulness, as explained at length, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas. These are called the other superior wholesome dharmas subsumed within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should also hear, receive, uphold, recite, and reflect upon as they truly are the other immeasurable dharma-gates that accord with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, such as the aggregates (*skandha*), bases (*āyatana*), and elements (*dhātu*); they should not disparage them, thereby creating obstacles to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
For what reason?
Kausika! These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:

"When the Tathāgata formerly dwelt in the stage of a bodhisattva, he constantly and diligently cultivated and studied the dharmas that accord with enlightenment—namely, from the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity; from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; all the doors of samādhi and dhāraṇī; the four foundations of mindfulness, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, as well as other immeasurable dharma-gates such as the aggregates, bases, and elements that accord with this profound perfection of wisdom. By means of these, he realized the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
We who now seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment should likewise train ourselves accordingly.
Such dharmas as this perfection of wisdom are certainly our great teachers; by training in them, our aspirations shall be fulfilled.

Such dharmas as this perfection of wisdom are certainly the Dharma-seals of all Buddhas; for by training in them, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have realized, are realizing, and will realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Likewise, these dharmas such as the *prajñāpāramitā* are also the seal of the Dharma for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; because all stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas have studied them, they have reached, are reaching, and will reach the further shore of nirvāṇa.
"For this reason, Kauśika, whether the Buddha remains in the world or has entered parinirvāṇa,
all sons and daughters of good family should rely upon the *prajñāpāramitā*— from its extensive exposition up to the knowledge of all aspects— and constantly and diligently practice and study it."
Why is this so? Kauśika!

It is because this Prajñāpāramitā, extensively explained up to and including the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), is that upon which all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and others—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth—rely and take refuge.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! Suppose there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgatas, erect stūpas for the relics of the Buddhas out of the seven precious substances as offerings. These are adorned with various rare and wonderful jewels; they are one yojana in height and half a yojana in width. Furthermore, throughout their entire lives, they offer, revere, honor, respect, and praise them with various celestial and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags, canopies, various rare and wonderful musical instruments, and lamps."
"What do you think?
By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very much so,
World-Honored One!
Very much so!”
“Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha said to Kauśika:

“If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) to hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this *prajñāpāramitā* in accordance with reality; and if they widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it, adorning it in various ways, and offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise; furthermore, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain great merit].”
“By this causal condition, the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family is far greater than that [previous merit], immeasurable and boundless. Furthermore, Kauśika!”

Setting aside this one matter, suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of various Tathāgatas, erect stūpas for the relics of those Buddhas made of the seven exquisite precious gems, adorned with an intermixture of various rare and wonderful treasures. These are one yojana in height, and half that in width. Suppose they fill an entire Jambudvīpa, or the four continents, or a small thousand-world system, or a medium thousand-world system, or even a great trichiliocosm, and throughout their entire lives, they honor, revere, respect, and praise them with all kinds of celestial flowers, garlands, and even lamps.
"What do you think?
By reason of this, would those sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very much so,
World-Honored One!
Very much so!”
“Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha said to Kauśika:

“If sons and daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) to listen with a sincere heart to this Prajñāpāramitā, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and contemplate it according to reality; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or write it down, adorning it in various ways, and offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise, further making offerings of various exquisite flower garlands up to lamps and lights.”
“By this cause and condition, the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family is far greater than that, immeasurable and boundless. Furthermore, Kauśika!”

Setting aside one trichiliocosm, suppose that all the sentient beings within a trichiliocosm, after the Tathāgata has entered parinirvāṇa, were each to erect stūpas for the Buddha’s śarīra out of exquisite seven precious gems, adorned with various rare and wonderful ornaments, measuring one yojana in height and half a yojana in width, filling the entire trichiliocosm without any gaps; and furthermore, throughout their entire lives, they were to offer worship, honor, respect, and praise with various celestial flower garlands, up to lamps and lights.
"What do you think?
Would the multitude of sentient beings in this great trichiliocosm gain much merit by reason of this cause and condition?
Śakra, Lord of Devas, replied:
“Very many, World-Honored One! Very many!”
"Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha said to Kauśika:

"If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) to hear, receive, uphold, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this Prajñāpāramitā according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they write it down, adorning it in various ways, and offer it with worship, reverence, respect, and praise, further making offerings of various exquisite flower garlands up to lamps and lights."
"The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this cause and condition is far greater than that, immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying: "So it is!"
"So it is, World-Honored One!
So it is, Sugata!"

If sons or daughters of good family offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to this Prajñāpāramitā, it should be known that they are thereby offering worship, honor, respect, and praise to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present.

Suppose that all sentient beings in worlds throughout the ten directions, each as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, were to erect stūpas made of the seven precious jewels after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa for the purpose of making offerings to his relics; these stūpas would be adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures, measuring one yojana in height and half a yojana in width, filling the entire trichiliocosm without any empty space. Furthermore, they would offer various celestial flower garlands, up to lamps and lights, for an eon or even more than an eon, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them.
“World-Honored One!
By this cause and condition, would these sentient beings acquire much merit?
The Buddha said:
"Their merit shall be immeasurable and boundless.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

"If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and with sincere hearts listen to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they write it down, adorning it in various ways, and offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise, further making offerings of various exquisite flower garlands up to lamps and lights; [their merit shall likewise be immeasurable and boundless]."

The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this cause and condition is far greater than that [previous merit], being immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because this *prajñāpāramitā* can comprehensively encompass and store all wholesome dharmas, namely the ten...
The wholesome paths of action; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
the contemplation of the four noble truths; the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment;
the three doors of liberation; the six supernormal powers; the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments; and the perfection of generosity.

From the many up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), whether it be from internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*),
or the various doors of samādhi and dhāraṇī, or the ten powers of a Buddha (*buddha-bala*), the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*),
the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), great compassion (*karuṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and great equanimity (*upekṣā*).
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether it be all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*),
or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, are all subsumed within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the true Dharma-seal of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; it is also the true Dharma-seal of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.”
“World-Honored One!

Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have constantly and diligently studied this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they have realized, are realizing, and will realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
and because all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas have also constantly and diligently studied this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they have reached, are reaching, and will reach the further shore of Nirvāṇa.”
“World-Honored One!

For this reason, if sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as their skillful method, listen with sincere hearts to this *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it with various adornments, even making offerings of lamps and light—the mass of merit thus produced will be immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 428; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Fascicle 429.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter 31: The Arising of Merit. Part Two, Chapter Thirty-one: The Arising of Merit. At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"It is so! It is thus!"
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Kauśika!"

If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) to wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this *prajñāpāramitā* in accordance with reality; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or transcribe it with various adornments, making offerings to it with reverence, respect, honor, and praise; and further, make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps—then the mass of merit produced will be immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.
For what reason? Kausika!

By means of this *prajñāpāramitā*, one can accomplish the all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; it also accomplishes the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*; it also accomplishes inner emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*); it also accomplishes the four foundations of mindfulness, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*); it also accomplishes the five eyes and the six superknowledges (*abhijñā*); it also accomplishes all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) and doors of dhāraṇī; it also accomplishes the maturation of sentient beings and the purification of Buddha-fields; it also accomplishes the vehicles of all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Unsurpassed Vehicle; and it also accomplishes the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi*) realized by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
"For this reason, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yoga*), they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this *prajñāpāramitā* according to the truth; and if they widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or even transcribe it with various adornments, up to making offerings of lamps and illumination.

Compared to this mass of merit, the merit from the stūpas previously constructed does not approach even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part; it does not even approach a single *upaniṣad* fraction.
Why is this? Kauśika!

If this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā is circulated among human beings, then in this world the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṃgha of Bhikṣus shall never disappear.
If this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* were to abide among human beings,
the world would constantly possess the ten paths of wholesome action; likewise, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments,
the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*, and from internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*)...

Up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence; whether it be the four applications of mindfulness, explained at length up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; or all the doors of samādhi and dhāraṇī;
or omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; or the great clans of kṣatriyas and the great [clans] of brahmins...

clans, great clans of elders, and great clans of householders; or the gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception; or those of the Śrāvaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, and the Unsurpassed Vehicle;
or stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas; or bodhisattvas...
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva brings sentient beings to maturity and purifies Buddha-fields; whether it be the Tathāgatas, Arhats,
Samyaksaṃbuddhas who realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes—
such supreme matters shall never perish.

Chapter 32: On Merit, Part Two, Chapter Thirty-Two. At that time, all the gods from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven within the trichiliocosm raised their voices in unison and addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
“O Great Sage!
Therefore, this profound *prajñāpāramitā* should be accepted, maintained, read, recited, diligently studied, correctly contemplated, and honored, revered, respected, and praised.
Why is this? Great Seer!

If one upholds, recites, diligently practices, reflects upon according to the principle, makes offerings to, reveres, honors, and praises this Prajñāpāramitā, it will cause all unwholesome dharmas to diminish and all wholesome dharmas to increase; it will also cause the hosts of devas to increase and the factions of the asuras to diminish; furthermore, it will ensure that the Buddha-eye, Dharma-eye, and Saṅgha-eye do not perish, and that the lineage of the Buddha, the lineage of the Dharma, and the lineage of the Saṅgha shall never be interrupted.

“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there exist in the world the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; there also exist internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; there also exist the four foundations of mindfulness, as extensively explained, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; there also exist all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī; there also exist omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; there also exist the fruit of stream-entry up to the fruit of arhatship; there also exists the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; there also exists the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and there also exists unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Therefore, O Great Sage!
You should receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the truth, honor, revere, respect, and praise this Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
You should receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, and offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
For what reason?
Kausika! If the asuras and their evil factions should give rise to such a thought:
"We shall engage in battle and conflict with the celestial armies of Śakra, Lord of Devas.

At that time, you, the retinues of the devas, should each with utmost sincerity recite this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it; then the evil intentions arising from the asuras and their factions will immediately be extinguished.
“Kauśika! If any sons of the gods or daughters of the gods manifest the five signs of decline, their hearts will become terrified and fearful of falling into the evil destinies.
At that time, you and your celestial retinues should stand before them and, with utmost sincerity, recite and contemplate this Prajñāpāramitā.”

At that time, those devas or devīs, by virtue of the power of the roots of goodness of this *prajñāpāramitā* and because they have conceived pure faith in this *prajñāpāramitā*, will see the five signs of decay vanish and their bodies and minds become tranquil. Even if their lives should end, they will be reborn in their original realm, where they will enjoy celestial wealth and pleasures twice as superior as before.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because the merit and power of hearing and having faith in the Prajñāpāramitā are exceedingly vast and great.

“Kauśika! If any sons of good family, daughters of good family, or any devaputras and devakanyās should hear this profound Prajñāpāramitā even once, by the power of their roots of goodness, they will certainly and gradually realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

All Buddhas of the past, future, and present, along with their disciples, have all studied this very Prajñāpāramitā, thereby realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and entering the realm of nirvana without remainder.
Why is this? Kauśika!

This Prajñāpāramitā universally encompasses all factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*), for it fully includes all the dharmas of the Buddhas, the dharmas of the Bodhisattvas, the dharmas of the Pratyekabuddhas, and the dharmas of the Śrāvakas.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra, a great illuminating mantra, the unsurpassed mantra, the unequaled mantra, and the king of all mantras. It is the most honored, the most supreme, the highest, and the most wondrous; it can subdue all things and cannot itself be subdued by anything.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is able to eliminate all evil and unwholesome dharmas, and is able to encompass all supreme wholesome dharmas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said. Why is this? Kausika!

All Buddhas of the past, future, and present have, by means of this profound Great Dharani King of Prajñāpāramitā, realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turned the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
Why is this? It is because, by relying upon and depending on this great king of mantras, the profound Prajñāpāramitā,
there come to exist in the world the ten paths of wholesome action, as well as the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Whether it be the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; whether it be internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature;
whether it be the four applications of mindfulness, as extensively explained, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
or whether it be suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the reality-limit, or the non-falsity of phenomena;
The unchanging nature, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, and the inconceivable realm;
whether it be the four noble truths, the five eyes, or the six supernormal powers; whether it be the fruit of stream-entry up to the fruit of arhatship;
whether it be the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, the conduct of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the unsurpassed, perfect... [enlightenment] of a Buddha.
"Equal to enlightenment— namely, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*),
and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Furthermore, Kauśika,
it is because of the bodhisattva mahāsattva that there exist in the world the ten paths of wholesome action, and so on, up to the knowledge of all aspects."
Just as all the stars and constellations attain increased brilliance by depending on the full moon,
so too do the ten paths of wholesome action, and everything up to the knowledge of all aspects, become manifest by depending on the bodhisattvas.

When the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have not yet appeared in the world, it is only the Bodhisattvas who, endowed with various skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), correctly proclaim all mundane and supramundane dharmas for the sake of sentient beings; all such skillful means possessed by Bodhisattvas arise and grow from this very profound Prajñāpāramitā.

Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), they are able to practice the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*); they are able to practice inner emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*); and they are able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛty-upasthāna*)—as extensively explained—up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*). Without realizing the stages of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields. They fully acquire the perfection of lifespan, the perfection of the buddha-field, the perfection of the retinue, the perfection of requisites, and the perfection of physical form and strength, and even the realization of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), all of which are accomplished through the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, they shall achieve the sublime merits of both the present and the future."
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How do these sons and daughters of good family accomplish the preeminent merits of the present and the future?"
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, these sons and daughters of good family shall, in the present life, not be harmed by poison, wounded by weapons, burned by fire, or drowned by water; they shall not even meet an untimely death from the four hundred and four diseases, except for those karmic results already fixed that must be experienced in the present life.”

Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family should encounter legal troubles or be oppressed by enemies and bandits, and they recite this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere mind, then when they arrive at such places, they shall ultimately not be subjected to punishment or harm by them.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because such is the majestic power and influence of this Prajñāpāramitā that it causes things to be so.

Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family wish to go into the presence of a sovereign, a prince, or a high minister, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere heart, they will certainly be greeted with joy by the king and others, who will offer them sustenance, respect, honor, esteem, and praise.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family constantly give rise to the minds of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity toward all sentient beings.
