Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall always achieve such present merits as these. Kauśika!
If good sons or good daughters, with sincere hearts, hear, receive,
uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain,
and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, then these good sons and good daughters, accordingly—
In whatever place they are born, they are never separated from the ten paths of wholesome action;
nor from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; nor from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
nor from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; nor from the four foundations of mindfulness, as explained at length...
Up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether it be all the gateways of samādhi or dhāraṇī,
or omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, they do not fall into the realms of hell,
the animal kingdom, or the hungry ghosts, except when they intentionally go there by vow to mature sentient beings.

In whatever place they are born, they shall always possess all their faculties and limbs without deficiency; they shall never be born into families that are impoverished, lowly, or of craftsmen, nor among those of mixed castes, butchers, hunters, thieves, prison guards, *pukkasas*, *caṇḍālas*, or the base *śūdras* who engage in trade.

In whatever place they are born, they will be fully adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs; all sentient beings who see them will rejoice. They will mostly be reborn in the pure lands of Buddhas, arising by transformation from lotus flowers, committing no evil, and never being separated from the supernormal powers of a bodhisattva. Following their heart’s wishes, they will travel through various Buddha-lands, proceeding from one Buddha-field to another, drawing near to and making offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. They will bring sentient beings to maturity, adorn and purify Buddha-fields, hear the true Dharma, and practice according to what they have heard, gradually realizing the knowledge of all modes.
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall achieve such future merits as these. For this reason, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family wish to attain such superior merits in the present and future, even unto unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should never be separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*). Taking non-apprehension as their means, they should—with sincere hearts—listen to, receive and uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*. Furthermore, they should make offerings with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, musical instruments, and lamps.
Chapter 33: On the Non-Buddhists (Tīrthika-varga), Part Two. Chapter Thirty-three: At that time, there were many non-Buddhist brahmans who, seeking the Buddha, came to the place where he was.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having seen this, thought to himself:
"Now these many non-Buddhist brahmins have come to this Dharma assembly seeking to find fault with the Buddha; could this not be an obstacle created by Prajñā?"
"I shall recite and contemplate the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as I received it from the Buddha, so that those followers of heterodox paths may retreat back to their own places.

Having thought this, he then recited the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Thereupon, the many non-Buddhist brahmins, extending gestures of respect from afar, circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right and departed by the same path they had come.
At that time, having seen this, Śāriputra thought to himself:
"For what reason has he just come and now departed?
Then the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:
“Those non-Buddhists came seeking my faults, but because Śakra, Lord of the Devas, recited the Prajñāpāramitā, they were made to depart. Śāriputra! ”
I do not see even the slightest white dharma in those non-Buddhist brahmins; they have come to me only with malicious intent, seeking to find fault with me. Śāriputra!

I do not see anyone in the entire world—whether among gods, Māras, Brahmās, or any class of sentient beings such as śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas—who, when the Prajñāpāramitā is being taught, would harbor a malicious intent or come seeking an opportunity to find fault.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because all those from the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven in this trichiliocosm— including śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and buddhas— as well as all nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others endowed with great power, together protect this Prajñāpāramitā so that no evils may cause obstacles.
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because all these devas are born through the power of the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others, throughout as many worlds in each of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, all together protect this Prajñāpāramitā, so that no evils may cause obstacles."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all those Buddhas arise through the power of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
At that time, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:

"Now the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is surrounded by the fourfold assembly, and all the devas and humans of the desire and form realms have gathered together to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā. Within this assembly, there will certainly be Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who shall receive the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; I shall go there to destroy their vision."
Having formed this thought, he manifested four armies and, displaying fierce prowess and sharp valor, approached the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw this and thought to himself:
"Could it be that the Evil Māra has manifested these things to come and disturb the Buddha, and to create obstacles for the Prajñāpāramitā?"

Why is this? Because these four armies are so magnificently adorned that none of the four armies belonging to Chāyabala, the Śākya royal lineage, the Licchavis, or the Mallas can equal them; by this, one certainly knows they have been conjured by Māra.

For a long night, Māra has been watching for a weakness in the Buddha and seeking to destroy the sublime accomplishments cultivated by sentient beings; I shall now recite and contemplate the profound Prajñāpāramitā as received from the Buddha, so that this evil Māra may be driven back to his own abode.
Having reflected thus, he then recited the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; thereupon, the evil Māra departed by way of his path, compelled by the power of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

At that time, all those present in the assembly—from the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven—each miraculously manifested various celestial flowers, fragrant garlands, and other exquisite offerings. Leaping into the air, they scattered them over the Buddha, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha in unison:
"May this Prajñāpāramitā long abide among the people of Jambudvīpa."
Why is this so? World-Honored One!

As long as this profound Prajñāpāramitā is circulated among the people of Jambudvīpa, you should know that in this place the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Bhikṣu Saṃgha will abide for a long time without perishing.

It is likewise so for this trichiliocosm and even for the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions; by means of this, the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and their sublime practices can also be fully understood.

"Bhagavān! In whatever region there may be sons of good family or daughters of good family who, with pure faith, write down and uphold this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who honor, revere, respect, and praise it, one should know that in that place there will be a wondrous radiance that dispels darkness and gives rise to manifold benefits."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the other hosts of devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

As long as this profound Prajñāpāramitā continues to circulate among the people of Jambudvīpa, you should know that in those places the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus will abide for a long time without perishing.

In this trichiliocosm, and likewise throughout the infinite, countless, and boundless worlds of the ten directions, it is by means of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and their sublime practices that [all things] can be fully understood.

In whatever regions there may be sons of good family or daughters of good family who, with pure faith, write down, uphold, honor, revere, respect, and praise this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that in those places there will be sublime radiance that dispels darkness and gives rise to manifold benefits.
At that time, the hosts of devas again each manifested various celestial flowers, fragrant garlands, and other offerings, scattering them over the Buddha, and addressed him once more:

"If good sons and good daughters, regarding this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, transcribe and explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated—then Māra and his armies shall be unable to find an opportunity against these good sons and good daughters. We, the hosts of devas, shall also constantly follow them and diligently provide protection so that they suffer no harm or affliction."
For what reason?
World-Honored One!
These sons and daughters of good family are honored and served by us devas as if they were the Buddha, or because we revere the Dharma as if it were the Buddha.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha:

“These sons and daughters of good family cannot accomplish this matter through meager roots of virtue; they must have accumulated many roots of virtue, made many true aspirations, made many offerings to the Buddhas, and served many spiritual friends in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas in previous lives, and are thus able to listen with a sincere heart to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated.”
"Bhagavān! If sons or daughters of good family wish to attain the knowledge of all aspects of all Buddhas, they should seek the perfection of wisdom;
if they wish to attain the perfection of wisdom, they should seek the knowledge of all aspects of all Buddhas."
Why is this? Because all the knowledge of all aspects attained by the Buddhas arises from the perfection of wisdom;
and all perfections of wisdom arise from the knowledge of all aspects of the Buddhas.

Why is this? The omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) attained by all Buddhas is not different from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and all perfection of wisdom is not different from the omniscience attained by all Buddhas;
one should know that the omniscience attained by all Buddhas and this perfection of wisdom are non-dual and have no distinction between them.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.
Therefore, the merit and majestic power of the *prajñāpāramitā* are most honored and most supreme.
Chapter 34: The Arrival of the Gods, Part Two, Chapter 34-1. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One, for what reason do the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas not extensively praise the five pāramitās beginning with generosity, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, but instead extensively praise only the sixth, the prajñāpāramitā?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“Because the sixth, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), serves as the sovereign and the guide for the first five perfections up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma), I have praised only the perfection of wisdom extensively.”
Furthermore, Ānanda! What do you think?

If one practices generosity, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, without dedicating them toward omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), can that be called truly practicing the perfection of generosity, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
Ānanda replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The Buddha said:

“Ānanda! It is only by dedicating [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) that one practices from generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; only then can it be called the true practice of the perfection of generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

Therefore, because the Perfection of Wisdom is able to act as the sovereign and the guide for the first five perfections up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, I have praised only the Perfection of Wisdom extensively.
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“In what way does one dedicate toward omniscience while practicing giving, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, so that it may truly be called the practice of the perfection of giving, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?”
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-aspect omniscience while practicing from generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. When one thus dedicates toward all-aspect omniscience while practicing from generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, this is called truly practicing the perfection of generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“By means of what non-duality as the skillful means, what non-arising as the skillful means, and what non-apprehension as the skillful means, does one dedicate [merit] toward all-aspect omniscience while practicing from generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, such that it is called the true cultivation of the perfection of generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?”
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

By means of the non-duality of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension—when one dedicates [the merit] toward all-aspect omniscience and practices from generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, only then can it be called the true cultivation of the perfection of generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
The Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How is it that by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-aspect omniscience while practicing from generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—how is this called truly practicing the perfection of generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

Form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; even up to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, which is empty of the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Why is this? Because form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to and including unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, are empty of intrinsic nature; and because these are non-dual and without distinction from the perfection of generosity up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of the perfection of wisdom that one can dedicate [merit] toward omniscience; and because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to bring the perfection of generosity, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, to ultimate fulfillment.”

Therefore, because the Prajñāpāramitā is the most honored and the guide for the five preceding pāramitās, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, I have praised only the Prajñāpāramitā extensively.
"Ānanda, you should know this:

it is like when seeds are scattered upon the great earth; through the convergence of various conditions, they attain growth. You should understand that the great earth serves as the basis for the growth of the seeds and acts as their support."

In this way, the perfection of wisdom and the omniscience toward which it is dedicated serve as the basis for, and the foundation upon which, the previous five perfections up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are established, enabling them to grow and flourish.

Because this Prajñāpāramitā is the most honored and the guide among the five preceding pāramitās up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, I have extensively praised only the Prajñāpāramitā, and not dāna and the others.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Even now, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has not yet finished expounding all the merits of this Prajñāpāramitā.”

Why is this? The merit of the *prajñāpāramitā* as received by me from the World-Honored One is profound, vast, immeasurable, and boundless. Any sons or daughters of good family who, regarding this *prajñāpāramitā*, listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, shall likewise obtain boundless merit.

If one were to transcribe such profound sūtras as this Prajñāpāramitā and adorn them in various ways, and further make offerings with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps, the merit obtained would likewise be boundless.
“World-Honored One! If good sons and good daughters, regarding this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*,
listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and apply themselves according to the principle...”
By reflecting upon, copying, explaining, and widely disseminating [this], through these causes and conditions, there come to exist in the world the ten paths of wholesome action;
as well as the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom; and internal emptiness.
...up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness, extensively explained up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
whether it be the fruit of stream-entry up to the fruit of arhatship; whether it be the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; whether it be the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas;
whether it be the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha; or whatever [other dharmas there may be]—all these...
"Whatever excellent things exist in the world, there are none that do not appear therein.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: "Kauśika!"
I do not say that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses only the merits previously described.
Why is this? Kausika!

Kauśika, because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is endowed with boundless and supreme merits, I do not say that those sons or daughters of good family who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this profound *sūtra* of the *prajñāpāramitā* according to the Dharma; who extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; and who write it down, adorn it in various ways, and further make offerings to it with immeasurable, exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps—possess only the merits previously described. Rather, they possess even greater merit.
Why is this so? Kausika!

If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, widely proclaiming and disseminating it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they further transcribe it with various adornments and make offerings to it with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, up to lamps and lights—then these good sons and good daughters will achieve immeasurable and preeminent aggregates of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*), concentration (*samādhiskandha*), wisdom (*prajñāskandha*), liberation (*vimuktiskandha*), and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha*).
“Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family are like the Buddha. Why is this?

Because it upholds the unsurpassed path of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present; because it leads with certainty toward the enlightenment of a Buddha; because it brings about inexhaustible benefit, welfare, and happiness for all sentient beings; and because it transcends the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

Kauśika! Compared to the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to these sons and daughters of good family do not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor even an *upaniṣad* (infinitesimal) part.
Why is this? Kausika!

These sons and daughters of good family transcend all inferior mental states associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; they never praise the vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, for there is nothing among all phenomena that they do not know—meaning they are able to correctly know that "nothing exists."

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā—listening to it with a sincere heart, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, diligently practicing and studying it, reflecting upon it according to the principle, and widely proclaiming and disseminating it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they further transcribe it, adorning it in various ways, and furthermore make offerings to it with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, even down to lamps—I declare that they will obtain immeasurable and boundless meritorious benefits in both the present and the future.”
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“We devas shall constantly follow and protect these sons and daughters of good family, so that they may not be afflicted or harmed by any humans, non-humans, or various adverse conditions.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension, should receive, uphold, read, and recite this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, then at that time immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras will gather together for the sake of hearing the Dharma; they will rejoice and leap for joy, reverently receiving this profound Prajñāpāramitā.”

Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension, proclaim such dharmas corresponding to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, at that time immeasurable devaputras will all assemble; through their celestial power, they will cause the Dharma-preacher’s eloquence to increase and his exposition to flow forth inexhaustibly.

Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension, proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā, at that time immeasurable devaputras will assemble there out of reverence for the Dharma. By their celestial power, they will cause the eloquence of the Dharma-preacher to be unimpeded, such that even if obstacles or difficulties arise, they cannot be obstructed or severed.

Kauśika! Those sons and daughters of good family who, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen to, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra according to the principle of reality; and who extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or even transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and further make offerings to it with diverse, exquisite flower garlands up to lamps—these shall, in the present life, obtain boundless merit and benefits, and neither Māra nor his hosts shall be able to disturb or afflict them.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* among the fourfold assembly, their minds will be free from fear and they shall not be overcome by any form of debate."
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because they are sustained by the empowerment of this very profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Furthermore, within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, all phenomena are extensively analyzed; that is to say, wholesome phenomena (*kuśala-dharma*), unwholesome phenomena (*akuśala-dharma*), determinate phenomena (*vyākṛta-dharma*), indeterminate phenomena (*avyākṛta-dharma*), tainted phenomena (*sāsrava-dharma*), untainted phenomena (*anāsrava-dharma*), mundane phenomena (*laukika-dharma*), supramundane phenomena (*lokottara-dharma*), conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta-dharma*), unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*), the phenomena of śrāvakas, the phenomena of pratyekabuddhas, the phenomena of bodhisattvas, and the phenomena of tathāgatas—all such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of distinct categories of dharma-gates are subsumed herein.

Furthermore, because these sons and daughters of good family are well-established in the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they do not perceive anyone who can raise an objection, nor do they perceive anything that is being objected to, nor do they perceive any Prajñāpāramitā that is being taught.

For this reason, Kauśika, these sons and daughters of good family, because they are sustained by the great majestic power of this Prajñāpāramitā, shall not be overcome by the debates of heterodox teachers nor by any enemies.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, regarding this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated—these good sons and good daughters will have minds that are never startled, terrified, or afraid; their minds will not sink, nor will they feel sorrow or regret."
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family do not perceive anything that could cause alarm, fear, terror, sinking, or regret.

Kauśika! If sons and daughters of good family wish to attain these present, boundless merits and benefits, they should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, write down, explain, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā; they should offer it worship, honor, respect, and praise, never abandoning it for even a moment.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension, should with sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, write down, explain, widely disseminate, honor, revere, respect, and praise this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā."

These sons and daughters of good family will always be loved and respected by their parents, teachers, elders, friends, kings, ministers, and all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; they will also be cherished and remembered by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Arhats, Anāgāmins, Sakṛdāgāmins, and Srotāpannas throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions; furthermore, they will be protected by the devas, māras, Brahmās, humans, non-humans, asuras, and others of the world.

These sons and daughters of good family achieve the most supreme and uninterrupted eloquence; at all times they practice the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; they abide in the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; they practice the four foundations of mindfulness, and so on, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they practice all gateways of samādhi and dhāraṇī; they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields; and they practice all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, never flagging or ceasing.

These sons and daughters of good family cannot be overcome by any heterodox arguments of external paths or by any enemies; rather, they are able to overcome the heterodox arguments of external paths and all enemies.

Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family wish to attain such benefits and merits as these—uninterrupted and inexhaustible in both the present and the future—they should, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect according to the principle, write down, explain, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā; and they should offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
If good sons and good daughters write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, adorn it in various ways, and place it in a pure location, making offerings to it, honoring, respecting, and praising it."

At that time, all those from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Vast Fruit within this trichiliocosm, as well as in the infinite worlds of the ten directions—who have already resolved upon unexcelled bodhicitta—constantly come to this place to behold, pay homage to, read, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā; they offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise, circumambulate it to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and then depart.

All the gods of the Pure Abodes—namely, the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha—heavenly beings—likewise constantly come here to behold, pay homage to, read, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā; they offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise, circumambulate it to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and then depart.

At that time, from this trichiliocosm as well as from the boundless worlds of the ten directions, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans of great majesty and virtue would also constantly come here to behold and pay homage to, recite and study, offer worship, show reverence, honor, and praise this Prajñāpāramitā; they would circumambulate it to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and then depart.
“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:

‘Now, all those from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, as well as other immeasurable nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans of great majesty and virtue who constantly come here to behold, pay homage to, read, recite, and worship this profound Prajñāpāramitā that I have written down—honoring, respecting, revering, and praising it, circumambulating it to the right, prostrating, and departing with palms joined—I shall thereby have provided them with the gift of Dharma.’”
Having formed this thought, they will rejoice and leap for joy, causing the merit they have obtained to increase twofold. "Kauśika!

Because of this, all those from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven within this trichiliocosm, as well as in other boundless worlds throughout the ten directions—including immeasurable nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans of great majesty and virtue—will constantly come here to follow and protect these sons and daughters of good family. They shall not be harmed by any humans or non-humans, except for the ripening of fixed evil karmic causes from past lives that must manifest in the present, or for heavy karma that is transformed to be experienced lightly in the present life."

Kauśika! By the great majestic power of this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, these sons and daughters of good family shall obtain such various merits and benefits in the present life as follows: those among the devas who have already resolved upon unexcelled bodhicitta, or those who, relying on the Buddha-dharma, have attained extraordinary benefit and happiness, will constantly come here out of reverence for the Dharma; they will follow, protect, and increase their power.
Why is this? Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family have already resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they do so constantly for the sake of rescuing and delivering all sentient beings, constantly for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity, constantly for the sake of never abandoning all sentient beings, and constantly for the sake of benefiting and gladdening all sentient beings.
Those devas are likewise; by this cause and condition, they constantly come to protect these good men and good women, ensuring they are free from affliction and harm.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 429. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Two, Chapter Thirty-Four: The Arrival of the Gods (Part Two). At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”

How do these sons and daughters of good family perceive that all the gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha realm, as well as other immeasurable nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans of great majesty and virtue, come to their place to behold and pay homage to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it is written, to read and recite it, to make offerings, revere, honor, and praise it, and to circumambulate it with palms joined in joyous mindfulness?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: "Kauśika!

If these sons and daughters of good family see a sublime radiance wherever this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is located, or if they hear a wondrous fragrance or sounds like celestial music, you should know that at such a time, devas, nāgas, and others of great supernormal power and blazing majesty have come to that place. They observe, pay homage to, read, recite, copy, offer worship, respect, revere, and praise this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; with palms joined, they circumambulate it to the right, and with joy, they protect and keep it in mind."
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

When these sons and daughters of good family cultivate pure conduct and adorn their dwelling, and with a sincere mind make offerings to such profound sūtras as this *Prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that at that time, devas, nāgas, and others of great supernormal power and blazing majesty will come to that place. They will observe and pay homage to, read and recite, and make offerings to, revere, respect, honor, and praise the profound *Prajñāpāramitā* that has been written down; they will join their palms, circumambulate it to the right, and joyfully protect and keep it in mind."

Kauśika! Whenever gods, nāgas, and others who possess such great supernormal powers and blazing majesty come to that place, all the malevolent spirits and evil ghosts therein will be struck with terror and disperse, none daring to remain.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, the minds of these sons and daughters of good family will give rise to vast and expansive pure resolve; the wholesome karma they cultivate will increase manifold, and all their undertakings will be free from obstacles.
For this reason, Kauśika!

Wherever this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā may be located, one should clear away all impurities from the surrounding area, sweep and scrub it clean, apply fragrant ointments, and sprinkle scented water. One should arrange a precious throne and place the scripture upon it, burning incense, scattering flowers, and spreading canopies and awnings. Adorn the interior with precious banners, pennants, and bells, as well as various exquisite and rare garments, necklaces, gold, silver, precious vessels, musical instruments, and lamps. Thus, one should embellish that place with all manner of colorful decorations.

If one can make such offerings to the *prajñāpāramitā*, then immeasurable devas, nāgas, and others—possessing great supernatural powers and blazing with majestic virtue—will come to that place. They will behold, pay homage to, read, and recite the profound *prajñāpāramitā* written there; they will offer worship, respect, honor, and praise, and with palms joined and circumambulating to the right, they will joyfully protect and keep it in mind.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If these sons and daughters of good family can thus make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will certainly attain freedom from weariness of body and mind, physical and mental bliss, lightness of body and mind, flexibility of body and mind, and tranquility of body and mind. With their thoughts fixed upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, when they sleep at night, they shall have no evil dreams but only auspicious ones; that is to say, they shall see the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, his body of true golden color, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and fully adorned with the eighty secondary signs, emitting great radiance that universally illuminates all things, surrounded before and behind by Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas, and standing amidst the assembly.

They heard the Buddha teach the dharmas associated with the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they further heard him teach the dharmas associated with inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the detailed exposition from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

Furthermore, they heard him analyze the meanings associated with the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; and they further heard him analyze the meanings associated with inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the detailed exposition from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

Furthermore, in a dream he saw a Bodhi tree, vast in height and breadth and adorned with various jewels; a great bodhisattva approached the Bodhi tree, sat in the full lotus posture, subdued the hosts of Māra, realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turned the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.

Furthermore, he saw immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas debating and discerning the various meanings of the Dharma, namely: how one should thus bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, cultivate the bodhisattva practices, subdue the armies of Māra, forever sever the habitual tendencies of the obstructions, and proceed toward the realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Furthermore, he again saw in his dream immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas in the ten directions, and he also heard their voices, saying: "In such-and-such a world, there is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, who, surrounded and honored by several hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and several hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Śrāvaka disciples, is preaching the Dharma for them."

Furthermore, he again saw in a dream immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas from the ten directions entering parinirvāṇa. After each of those Buddhas had entered parinirvāṇa, there were donors who, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha’s śarīra, erected with the seven precious jewels immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of stūpas. Moreover, at each and every stūpa, they offered worship, respect, honor, and praise for immeasurable kalpas, using immeasurable supreme and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family who see such auspicious dream-omens will experience peace and happiness in body and mind whether asleep or awake; the devas and other celestial beings will augment their vital energy, causing them to feel their own bodies become light and agile.”

By reason of these causes and conditions, one does not become excessively attached to food, drink, medicine, clothing, or bedding; the mind remains light and subtle regarding these four types of offerings. Just as a yogācāra enters a sublime meditative concentration (*samādhi*), and by the power of that concentration his body and mind are nourished and moistened, so that even upon emerging from meditation he remains light and subtle in mind despite encountering fine delicacies—this is likewise the case here.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

It is because these sons and daughters of good family are protected and mindful of by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, Śrāvakas, Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all those possessed of great supernormal powers and supreme majesty—throughout this trichiliocosm and the infinite worlds of the ten directions. These beings infuse their bodies and minds with subtle, refined vital energy, thereby causing their resolve to be courageous and their physical strength to flourish.

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family wish to obtain all such present meritorious benefits as these, they should give rise to the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), and with sincere hearts listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, although unable to hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, or reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra as it truly is, nor able to extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, nevertheless writes it down and adorns it with various jewels, and further makes offerings to it with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, rare and wonderful treasures, music, and lamps—honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it—they too shall obtain the various merits and benefits previously described.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family are able to extensively bring benefit and happiness to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension, should with sincere hearts hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā according to the truth; and if they should widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or even write it down, adorning it with various jewels, and further make offerings to it with diverse, exquisite flower garlands up to lamps—then the mass of merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless."

It surpasses the merit of one who, for the duration of their entire life, honors, reveres, respects, and praises all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their assemblies of disciples throughout the worlds of the ten directions with immeasurable kinds of superior and exquisite food, drink, clothing, bedding, medicine, and requisites;

it also surpasses the merit of one who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddhas of the ten directions and their disciples, constructs stūpas made of the seven precious gems—high, vast, and magnificent—to enshrine their relics (śarīra), and further honors, reveres, respects, and praises them for the rest of their life with immeasurable celestial flower garlands, up to lamps and lights.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because all the Buddhas of the ten directions and their assemblies of disciples are born from such profound Prajñāpāramitā.

35. Chapter on the Relics, Part Two, Chapter Thirty-Five: "Furthermore, Kauśika, suppose one portion were filled with the relics of the Buddha throughout this Jambudvīpa, and another portion were this profound Prajñāpāramitā written down; of these two portions, which would you take?"
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
“World-Honored One!
Between these two portions, my mind would rather take the profound Prajñāpāramitā.”

Why is this? It is not that I lack faith in or acceptance of the *śarīra* of the Buddhas, nor that I do not delight in making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising them; rather, it is because the bodies of the Buddhas and their *śarīra* are all produced from this very profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and are all cultivated by the power of the merit of this very profound *prajñāpāramitā*, that they are thus honored, respected, revered, and praised with immeasurable kinds of sublime flower garlands up to lamps by all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
At that time, Śāriputra said to Śakra: “Kauśika!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics (*animitta*). Since a dharma that is without characteristics cannot be grasped, how can you grasp it?”

Why is this? Kauśika! The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without taking up and without discarding; without increase and without decrease; without accumulation and without dispersion; without benefit and without harm; without defilement and without purity. It does not bestow the dharmas of the Buddhas, nor the dharmas of the Pratyekabuddhas, nor the dharmas of the Arhats, nor the dharmas of those in training (*śaikṣa*). It does not discard the dharmas of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*), nor does it bestow the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*), nor does it discard the conditioned realm (*saṃskṛtadhātu*). It does not bestow the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*), nor does it bestow the four applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*)—expounded at length up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—nor does it discard the dharmas of affliction (*saṃkleśadharma*).
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied to the Venerable Śāriputra: “So it is! So it is!”
It is exactly as you have said, Venerable One!

If one knows the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it truly is— neither grasping nor abandoning, and so forth, neither bestowing the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) nor discarding the defilements— this is the true grasping of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and this is the true practice of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

However, this perfection of wisdom does not follow two courses, because it is devoid of dual characteristics; likewise, from the perfection of meditative concentration down to the perfection of generosity, they too do not follow two courses, because they are devoid of dual characteristics.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
It is as you have said:
from the profound *prajñāpāramitā* down to the *dānapāramitā*, none of them follow a dualistic course. Why is this?
Kauśika! This is because these six perfections are all devoid of dualistic characteristics. Kauśika!

Whoever wishes to attribute two distinct characteristics to the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and even to the *dānapāramitā*, would likewise wish to attribute two distinct characteristics to the *dharmadhātu*, *tathatā*, *dharmatā*, *bhūtakoṭi*, and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because from the profound *prajñāpāramitā* down to the *dānapāramitā*, they are all non-dual and without distinction from the *dharmadhātu* down to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* should be wholeheartedly prostrated to, circumambulated from the right, and honored, revered, respected, and praised by all the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others.”
Why is this? Because all the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas rely upon the Prajñāpāramitā, diligently practicing and studying it to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

When I am seated upon the throne of Śakra, Lord of Devas, in the Sudharmā Hall of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, preaching the True Dharma for the assembly of devas, immeasurable sons of the gods come to where I am, making offerings, paying homage, honoring, and praising me; they circumambulate me to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and depart.”

If I am not present at that Dharma-seat, the sons of the gods will also come to that place; although they do not see me, they will pay homage and make offerings just as they did when I was there, all saying:

"This is the seat where Śakra, Lord of the Devas, teaches the Dharma to the gods; we should all act as if the Lord of the Devas were present, making offerings, circumambulating to the right, and prostrating before departing."
“World-Honored One!

Regarding this *prajñāpāramitā*, wherever it is written down, upheld, recited, or widely proclaimed and disseminated for the sake of sentient beings, one should know that this place will always be visited by the gathering of the countless and immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans from this land and the infinite worlds of the ten directions. Even if there is no one to preach it, because they revere the Dharma, they will likewise offer worship, pay homage, show respect, and praise it at that place before departing.”

Why is this? Because all the requisites for happiness belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all sentient beings, exist by depending upon the Prajñāpāramitā; and because even the *śarīra* relics of the Buddha receive offerings through being permeated by the merit of the Prajñāpāramitā.

“Bhagavān! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* serves as the cause, the condition, the basis of reliance, and the means of elicitation for the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and for the omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) they realize.”

Therefore, I say: suppose one portion consisted of the relics of the Buddha filling this entire Jambudvīpa, and another portion consisted of this profound Prajñāpāramitā written down; between these two portions, my intention would rather be to take this Prajñāpāramitā.
“World-Honored One!
When I uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, because my mind accords with the Dharma, I do not perceive any signs of fear whatsoever.”
Why is this so? World-Honored One!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without marks, without characteristics, without words, and without speech. Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is without marks, without characteristics, without words, and without speech, the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* *pāramitās*, and so forth, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), are likewise without marks, without characteristics, without words, and without speech.

"Bhagavān! If this Prajñāpāramitā possessed characteristics and verbal expression, rather than being without characteristics and verbal expression, then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha would not have realized that all dharmas are without characteristics, without marks, without words, and without speech; nor would he have attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and taught his disciples that all dharmas are without characteristics, without marks, without words, and without speech."

"Bhagavān! Because this Prajñāpāramitā is expressed through the discourse of signlessness and not through the discourse of having signs, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has realized that all phenomena are signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible; having attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he teaches his disciples that all phenomena are signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible."
World-Honored One!

For this reason, the Prajñāpāramitā is worthy of receiving offerings, honor, respect, and praise from devas, humans, asuras, and others, with immeasurable varieties of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and illuminations.
“Bhagavān! If there should be those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold,
read and recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this profound Prajñāpāramitā according to the truth, and extensively proclaim it for the sake of sentient beings...”
They shall circulate it, or again, transcribe it adorned with various jewels, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it;
they will certainly never again fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts, nor among the borderlands, the barbarians, or the mlecchas;
they will not fall into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but will surely proceed toward [Buddhahood].
Regarding supreme perfect enlightenment, they constantly see all Buddhas and perpetually hear the true Dharma;
they never part from virtuous friends, purify Buddha-fields, and bring sentient beings to maturity;
proceeding from one Buddha-field to another, they make offerings, show reverence, respect, and praise to the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

Suppose one portion were the relics of the Buddha filling this trichiliocosm, and another portion were this profound *prajñāpāramitā* written down; between these two portions, my intention would be to take this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the Buddha-śarīras of the trichiliocosm, are all born from the Prajñāpāramitā.

Furthermore, the *śarīra* relics of the Buddhas throughout the three thousandfold world system all derive from being permeated by the power of the merit of the *prajñāpāramitā*; therefore, they receive offerings, reverence, respect, and praise from devas, humans, asuras, and others.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, sons and daughters of good family who offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise to the Buddha’s *śarīra* will certainly not fall into the three evil realms; they will always be born among gods and humans to enjoy various riches and pleasures, and according to their aspirations, they shall proceed toward *nirvāṇa* by means of the Three Vehicles.
“Bhagavān! Whether one beholds the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, or beholds this profound Prajñāpāramitā written down, these two merits are equal and without distinction.”
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is equal to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, being non-dual and without any state of duality.

“Bhagavān! If there is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who abides in the three bases of miraculous power (*prātihārya*) and proclaims the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings—namely, from the Sūtras up to the Upadeśas—and if a son or daughter of good family were to receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain this Prajñāpāramitā to others, these two merits would be equal and without distinction.”

Why is this? Because whether it be those Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, or their three modes of miraculous manifestation, or the twelvefold teachings they have proclaimed, all arise in dependence upon the Prajñāpāramitā.

“Bhagavān! If all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā, were to abide in the three types of miraculous displays and proclaim the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings—namely, from the sūtras up to the upadeśas—and if a son or daughter of good family were to receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain this Prajñāpāramitā to others, these two merits would be equal and without distinction.”

Why is this? Because all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions—as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā—as well as their three types of miraculous displays and the twelvefold teachings they proclaim, all arise in dependence upon the Prajñāpāramitā.

“Bhagavān! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to offer, revere, respect, and praise all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the worlds of the ten directions—as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—with immeasurable varieties of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps;

and if another son of good family or daughter of good family were to transcribe the Prajñāpāramitā and likewise offer, revere, respect, and praise it with immeasurable exquisite offerings—the merit of these two would be equal and without distinction.”
Why is this? Because all those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are born in dependence upon the Prajñāpāramitā.
“World-Honored One!... [text continues]”

If sons or daughters of good family should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this Prajñāpāramitā according to the principle of reality, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, they shall in future lives not fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts, nor shall they fall into the stages of the Śrāvaka or the Pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family will certainly abide in the stage of non-retrogression, remaining far removed from all calamities, epidemics, and afflictions.
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, and honor, revere, respect, and praise it with immeasurable kinds of sublime offerings, they will certainly and forever sever all fears.”
Just as a debtor who fears his creditor immediately approaches and serves a king, relying on the king’s power to escape that fear;
so it is, World-Honored One!
The king is a metaphor for the *prajñāpāramitā*; those debtors are metaphors for sons and daughters of good family who, by relying upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, attain freedom from fear.
“World-Honored One!
It is just as when a person, by relying upon a king and being protected by that king, is honored, revered, respected, and praised by all people of the world;
so too are the relics of the Buddha. Because they have been permeated by this Prajñāpāramitā, they are honored, revered, respected, and praised by devas, humans, asuras, and others.”
“World-Honored One!
The king is a metaphor for the Prajñāpāramitā; the Buddha’s śarīra is a metaphor for that which relies upon the king.
“World-Honored One! [he continued.]

The omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) attained by all Buddhas is likewise accomplished in reliance upon the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). For this reason, I say that even if one portion were the relics of the Buddha filling this trichiliocosm, and another portion were the writing of such profound perfection of wisdom, between these two portions, my intention would rather be to take the profound perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because the Buddha’s relics are as firm as adamant and possess various colors; because the body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary characteristics, the Tathāgata’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and even the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all aspects, are all accomplished through the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!
It is by virtue of the majestic spiritual power of this Prajñāpāramitā that the five perfections, such as giving and the rest, are also designated as "pāramitās. Why is this so?
"Bhagavān! If there were no prajñāpāramitā, giving and the other perfections could not reach the further shore. Furthermore, Bhagavān!"

Whether in this trichiliocosm or in other worlds, in whatever royal capitals, cities, towns, or villages there may be, if anyone therein upholds, recites, copies, explains, makes offerings to, honors, respects, and praises this *prajñāpāramitā*, the sentient beings in those places shall not be harmed by any humans or non-humans, except for those who must experience the results of their fixed evil karma. Therein, these sentient beings will gradually train in the correct practice of the Three Vehicles, and according to their aspirations, they shall even swiftly realize the nirvana of the Three Vehicles.
“World-Honored One!
In this way, the perfection of wisdom brings great benefit to this trichiliocosm.
World-Honored One!”

Thus, this Prajñāpāramitā possesses great supernormal power; wherever it resides, there is a Buddha performing the various works of a Buddha, namely, bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
World-Honored One!

It is like a priceless great divine jewel that possesses immeasurable kinds of sublime and wondrous majestic power; wherever this divine jewel resides, humans and non-humans alike are free from all afflictions and harms.

Suppose there is a man or a woman who is possessed by a ghost and suffers physical and mental distress; if someone were to show them this divine jewel, the ghost would immediately depart due to the power of the jewel.
Whether one suffers from fevers caused by wind, phlegm, or heat, or from a combination of wind and phlegm, if this divine bead is tied to the body, none of these ailments will fail to be cured.

This jewel can provide illumination in the dark; it cools when it is hot and warms when it is cold. Wherever this divine jewel is located, the seasons remain harmonious, being neither too cold nor too hot.
If this divine jewel is present in a particular location, venomous creatures such as snakes and scorpions will not dare to remain there.

Should a man or a woman be struck by poison and suffer from agonizing pain and delirium, if someone displays this divine jewel to them, the poison will be instantly neutralized by the power of the jewel.

If sentient beings suffer from leprosy, malignant sores, swellings, pustules, or eye diseases such as vertigo and cataracts, or from diseases of the ears, nose, tongue, throat, body, or various ailments of the limbs and joints, all these illnesses will be healed by wearing this divine pearl.

If the waters in various ponds, pools, springs, or wells are turbid and foul, or are on the verge of drying up, when this jewel is cast into them, the water immediately becomes full, fragrant, pure, and clear, endowed with the eight meritorious qualities;

if one wraps this divine jewel in garments of various colors—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, azure, or green—and casts it into the water, the water follows the hues of the cloth, each becoming identical to its color.

Thus, this priceless great jewel, the divine pearl, possesses boundless majesty and virtue that cannot be fully extolled; even when placed within a chest or casket, it causes that vessel to be fully endowed with boundless majesty and virtue.
"Even if an empty box or casket once held a jewel, that vessel will still be cherished and esteemed by all people.
At that time, Ānanda asked Śakra:
"Is such a divine jewel possessed only by the devas, or do humans also have it?"
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
"This jewel exists both among humans and in the heavens. If it is among humans, its form is small and heavy; if it is in the heavens, its form is large and light."

Furthermore, while the jewel-marks among humans are incomplete, those on the celestial realms are perfectly round; the majestic power and virtue of the divine jewels in heaven surpass those possessed by humans by immeasurable multiples.
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is likewise so; it is the root of all virtues and can extinguish immeasurable evil and unwholesome dharmas. In whatever place it resides, it causes the physical and mental suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings to be entirely eliminated, such that humans and non-humans alike cannot cause them harm.”

“World-Honored One! The priceless great jewel of divine pearls you have described is not merely a metaphor for the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; it is also a metaphor for the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and for the *dhyānapāramitā* up to the *dānapāramitā*. It is also a metaphor for internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*). It is also a metaphor for the four foundations of mindfulness, as extensively explained, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*). It is also a metaphor for the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), suchness (*tathatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
Such merits as these are all brought forth and manifested by the great majestic spiritual power of the Prajñāpāramitā; these merits are profound, vast, immeasurable, and boundless.

Because the Buddha’s relics have been perfumed and cultivated by all manner of meritorious qualities, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, they are worthy of receiving the offerings, veneration, respect, and praise of all the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others.

"Furthermore, World-Honored One! The *śarīra* of the Buddha is the most perfect and supremely pure *prajñāpāramitā*, extending even to the *dānapāramitā*; it is the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*); it is the four foundations of mindfulness, as extensively explained up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*); it is all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); it is great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; it is the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*); and because it is the vessel that serves as the basis for the permanent severance of the continuity of the habitual tendencies of afflictions (*kleśavāsanā*) and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, it is worthy of receiving the offerings, veneration, respect, and praise of all the world, including devas, humans, and asuras."
“World-Honored One!

Because the *śarīra* of the Buddha is the vessel that supports the perfection of the most perfect, supreme, and pure merit-treasures, it is worthy of receiving the offerings, veneration, respect, and praise of all the worlds, including devas, humans, and asuras.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the Buddha’s *śarīra* is the vessel that serves as the basis for the *pāramitās*—which are utterly perfect, most supreme, pure, unstained, and neither purified nor impure; which are without arising or ceasing, without entering or exiting, without increase or decrease, without coming or going, without movement or stillness, and without this or that—it is worthy of receiving all the offerings, reverence, respect, and praise from the worlds of gods, humans, and *asuras* after the Buddha’s *parinirvāṇa*.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the Buddha’s *śarīra* (relics) are the vessel that supports the perfection of the ultimate, most excellent, and utterly pure true nature (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena, they are worthy of receiving the offerings, respect, honor, and praise of all the world—including gods, humans, and asuras—after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa.”
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

Setting aside the Buddha-śarīras that would fill a trichiliocosm, suppose there were one portion consisting of the Buddha-śarīras filling as many worlds in each of the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River, and another portion consisting of the transcription of this profound Prajñāpāramitā; between these two portions, my inclination would be to take this Prajñāpāramitā."
Why is this so? World-Honored One!

It is because all the *śarīras* of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are born from this very profound *prajñāpāramitā*; they are all cultivated by this very profound *prajñāpāramitā*; and they serve as the vessel upon which this very profound *prajñāpāramitā* relies; thus they are worthy of receiving the offerings, veneration, respect, and praise of all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
“World-Honored One!
If good men and good women, etc., make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the *śarīra* of the Buddha, they will receive inexhaustible wealth and joy among devas and humans.”

Among humans, this refers to the great clans of kṣatriyas, the great clans of brahmins, the great clans of householders, and the great clans of lay devotees; among the gods, it refers to those from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations. By means of such distinguished roots of goodness, one reaches the final body and attains the end of suffering.
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters, with a sincere mind, listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, copy, explain, and contemplate according to principle this Prajñāpāramitā, they will, by means of this Prajñāpāramitā, swiftly attain its full perfection.”

Because the perfection of wisdom is thus brought to fulfillment, it further causes the perfection of meditative concentration, and so on down to the perfection of generosity, as well as the four foundations of mindfulness, and so forth up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, to also reach fulfillment.

By means of this, one is further able to transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and freedom from birth (samyaktvaniyāma), and attain the bodhisattva’s sublime supernormal powers (abhijñā).

Riding upon these supernormal powers, they travel through all Buddha-fields, going from one Buddha-land to another, making offerings to and revering the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-fields, and manifest various bodies through the arousal of supreme thoughts and vows.

For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, they may become universal monarchs (*cakravartin*), or other minor kings; they may become kṣatriyas, or brahmins; they may become Vaiśravaṇas, or Śakras, the Lord of Devas; they may become Brahmā kings, or other types of beings, thereby bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.

Therefore, World-Honored One, it is not that I lack faith and acceptance toward the śarīras of the Buddhas, nor that I do not delight in making offerings to, revering, honoring, and praising them; yet, the merit obtained from making offerings to, revering, honoring, and praising this profound Prajñāpāramitā is far greater than that. For this reason, my mind would rather take up this profound Prajñāpāramitā.
“World-Honored One!

If sons or daughters of good family offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise to this *prajñāpāramitā*, they thereby increase all Buddha-dharmas and also acquire mastery over worldly and world-transcending wealth and happiness; thus, they have already offered worship, respect, reverence, and praise to the *śarīra* relics of the Buddha.”
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If there are those who wish to constantly behold the form bodies and dharma bodies of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions, they should with a sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā."

Because they see all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions through their two kinds of bodies, they gradually cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) so that it may be swiftly perfected; at that time, they should practice the recollection of the Buddha (buddhānusmṛti) by means of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
“World-Honored One!
The nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is twofold.
The first is the conditioned (saṃskṛta).”
The second is the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). In this context, what is meant by the nature of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma-tā*)?

It refers to the knowledge of internal emptiness up to the knowledge of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; the knowledge of the four applications of mindfulness up to the knowledge of the eightfold noble path; the knowledge of the three doors of liberation; the knowledge of the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the knowledge of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena; the knowledge of determinate and indeterminate phenomena; the knowledge of contaminated and uncontaminated phenomena; the knowledge of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena; the knowledge of mundane and supramundane phenomena; the knowledge of defiled and purified phenomena—all such knowledges of immeasurable categories are collectively termed the nature of conditioned phenomena.
In this context, what is meant by the unconditioned nature of phenomena (*asaṃskṛta-dharmatā*)?

It refers to the self-nature of all phenomena, which is without arising and without cessation, without abiding and without change, without defilement and without purity, without increase and without decrease, and without marks—this is the unconditioned nature of all phenomena.
"What is called the intrinsic nature of all phenomena?
It is that all phenomena have no intrinsic nature; this is what is called the unconditioned nature of phenomena.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."

Kauśika! All Buddhas of the past, future, and present, relying upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, have realized, will realize, and are currently realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

All disciples (*śrāvaka*) of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, relying upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, have attained, will attain, and are currently attaining the fruits of stream-entry (*srotāpanna*), once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmin*), non-returning (*anāgāmin*), and arhatship (*arhat-phala*).
The Pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, and present all rely upon the Prajñāpāramitā to have realized, will realize, and are currently realizing the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha. Why is this?
Kauśika! It is because within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the teachings corresponding to the three vehicles are extensively expounded.

Furthermore, that which is here taught takes non-apprehension as its expedient means; it takes the absence of intrinsic nature and the absence of marks as its expedient means; it takes non-arising and non-ceasing as its expedient means; it takes non-defilement and non-purity as its expedient means; it takes non-creation and non-action as its expedient means; it takes non-entry and non-exit as its expedient means; it takes non-increase and non-decrease as its expedient means; and it takes non-grasping and non-rejection as its expedient means.
All that has been thus explained is by way of conventional truth, not by way of the ultimate truth.

Why is this so? This Prajñāpāramitā is neither this shore nor the other shore; it is neither dry land nor the middle of the stream; it is neither high nor low; it is neither equal nor unequal; it is neither with marks nor without marks; it is neither mundane nor supramundane; it is neither with outflows (*sāsrava*) nor without outflows; it is neither conditioned (*saṃskṛta*) nor unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*); it is neither wholesome nor unwholesome; it is neither determinate (*vyākṛta*) nor indeterminate (*avyākṛta*); it is neither past, nor future, nor present.
