although he teaches sentient beings to realize the fruit of arhatship, he does not realize it himself;
although he teaches sentient beings to realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, he does not realize it himself.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally practices the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;

he himself dwells on the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to dwell on the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva;
he himself exerts diligence to adorn and purify buddha-fields, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to exert diligence to adorn and purify buddha-fields.

They themselves diligently apply effort to bring sentient beings to maturity, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to diligently apply effort to bring sentient beings to maturity;

they themselves diligently initiate the spiritual powers of a bodhisattva, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to diligently initiate the spiritual powers of a bodhisattva;
they themselves diligently purify the gates of dhāraṇī, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to diligently purify the gates of dhāraṇī.

They themselves diligently cultivate and purify the gateways of samādhi, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to diligently cultivate and purify the gateways of samādhi;
they themselves are able to realize perfect eloquence, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to realize perfect eloquence;
they themselves are able to assume a perfect physical body, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to be able to assume a perfect physical body.

He himself is able to fully embrace the perfection of the primary and secondary marks, and he also exhorts immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to be able to fully embrace the perfection of the primary and secondary marks;

he himself is able to fully embrace the stage of youthful purity (*kumārabhūmi*), and he also exhorts immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to be able to fully embrace the stage of youthful purity.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, and also encourages others to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;

personally abides in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and also encourages others to abide in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature;

personally cultivates the ten powers of a buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and also encourages others to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

They personally cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and they also encourage others to cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;

they personally sever the continuity of the habitual tendencies of all afflictions (*kleśavāsanā*), and they also encourage others to sever the continuity of the habitual tendencies of all afflictions;

they personally realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to benefit and bring joy to all, and they also encourage others to realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and perform such deeds.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How extraordinary,
World-Honored One!"
"How marvelous!
Well-Gone One!

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished such a great mass of merit; for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, they practice this profound perfection of wisdom, seeking to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to bring benefit and happiness to all."
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom so that it may be swiftly fulfilled?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive form as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as increasing or decreasing.
They do not perceive the sense-base of the eye as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as increasing or decreasing.
They do not perceive the sense-base of forms as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena as increasing or decreasing."
One does not perceive the eye-element as increasing or decreasing; one does not perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element as increasing or decreasing.
One does not perceive the form-element as increasing or decreasing; one does not perceive the sound, odor, taste, tangible-object, or mental-object-element as increasing or decreasing.
One does not perceive the eye-consciousness-element as increasing or decreasing; one does not perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness-element as increasing or decreasing.
They do not perceive an increase or decrease in eye-contact; they do not perceive an increase or decrease in ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.

They do not perceive an increase or decrease in any feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; they do not perceive an increase or decrease in any feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition.

They do not perceive an increase or decrease in the perfection of generosity; they do not perceive an increase or decrease in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

One does not perceive inner emptiness as increasing or decreasing; one does not perceive outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of limits, emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as increasing or decreasing.

One does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness as increasing or decreasing; one does not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as increasing or decreasing.

Furthermore, they do not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as increasing or decreasing.
They do not perceive any dharani-doors as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive any samadhi-doors as increasing or decreasing.

They do not perceive all-knowledge as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as increasing or decreasing. When a bodhisattva mahasattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they will swiftly attain its fulfillment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive this as a dharma, nor do they perceive this as a non-dharma; they do not perceive this as the past, nor do they perceive this as the future."
One sees this as the present, yet one does not see it as wholesome, nor does one see it as unwholesome;
one does not see it as determinate, nor does one see it as indeterminate; one does not see it as conditioned, nor does one see it as unconditioned;
one does not see it as belonging to the desire realm, nor does one see it as belonging to the form realm, nor does one see it as belonging to the formless realm. Not...
One does not perceive this perfection of giving, up to and including the non-perception of this perfection of wisdom;
one does not perceive this internal emptiness, up to and including the non-perception of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature;
one does not perceive these four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the non-perception of the eightfold noble path; and so on, up to and including the non-perception of suchness.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ten powers, nor even the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
when they do not perceive all the doors of dhāraṇī, nor all the doors of samādhi;
and when they do not perceive all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the knowledge of all aspects—this is a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
One will swiftly bring the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) to full completion.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because all phenomena are without intrinsic nature or characteristics; because they lack functional activity; because they cannot be transmuted; because they are false, deceptive, unsubstantial, and lacking self-mastery; because they are devoid of sensation; and because they are free from a self, a sentient being, a life-principle, a nourisher, and so forth, up to a knower or a viewer.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
that which the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable.”
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
What the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable, Subhūti!"

Because form is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;

because the eye-base is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;

because the form-base is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and phenomena-bases are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

Because the eye-element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;

because the form-element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, and mental-object-elements are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;

because the eye-consciousness-element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; and because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-elements are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

Because eye-contact is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;

because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;

because the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; and so on, up to: because the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

Because internal emptiness is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; up to and including because the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; up to and including because the eightfold noble path is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

Likewise, up to and including because the ten powers of a Buddha are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; up to and including because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

Because all dharani-doors are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathagata is inconceivable; because all samadhi-doors are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathagata is inconceivable;

because all-knowledge is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathagata is inconceivable; and because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathagata is inconceivable.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they understand as it truly is that form is inconceivable, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are inconceivable, and so on up to omniscience (sarvajñatā) being inconceivable, and the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) being inconceivable. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly bring it to full completion.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the notion that form is either conceivable or inconceivable; they do not give rise to the notion that feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are either conceivable or inconceivable.

They do not give rise to the notion that the eye base is either conceivable or inconceivable; they do not give rise to the notion that the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind bases are either conceivable or inconceivable."

One does not give rise to thoughts—whether conceivable or inconceivable—with respect to the sphere of form; one does not give rise to thoughts—whether conceivable or inconceivable—with respect to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

One does not give rise to thoughts—whether conceivable or inconceivable—with respect to the eye-element; one does not give rise to thoughts—whether conceivable or inconceivable—with respect to the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

One does not give rise to thoughts—whether conceivable or inconceivable—with respect to the element of form; one does not give rise to thoughts—whether conceivable or inconceivable—with respect to the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

He does not give rise to the notion of the conceivable or the inconceivable regarding the eye-consciousness element; he does not give rise to the notion of the conceivable or the inconceivable regarding the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.

He does not give rise to the notion of the conceivable or the inconceivable regarding eye-contact; he does not give rise to the notion of the conceivable or the inconceivable regarding ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact.

He does not give rise to the notion of the conceivable or the inconceivable regarding the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; he does not give rise to the notion of the conceivable or the inconceivable regarding the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.

One does not give rise to the thought that the perfection of generosity is either conceivable or inconceivable, nor does one give rise to such thoughts regarding anything up to the perfection of wisdom;

one does not give rise to the thought that inner emptiness is either conceivable or inconceivable, nor does one give rise to such thoughts regarding anything up to the emptiness of non-existence and intrinsic nature;

one does not give rise to the thought that the four foundations of mindfulness are either conceivable or inconceivable, nor does one give rise to such thoughts regarding anything up to the eightfold noble path.

In this way, up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not give rise to the notion that they are either conceivable or inconceivable; up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they do not give rise to the notion that they are either conceivable or inconceivable.

They do not give rise to the notion that any of the doors of dhāraṇī are either conceivable or inconceivable, nor do they give rise to the notion that any of the doors of samādhi are either conceivable or inconceivable.

They do not give rise to the notion that omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is either conceivable or inconceivable, nor do they give rise to the notion that the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are either conceivable or inconceivable. When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) in this manner, they will swiftly attain its fulfillment.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 438. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Two, Chapter Forty-three on the Northeast, Section Two. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Such is the profound meaning and intent of this Prajñāpāramitā; who is able to believe and understand it?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

The Buddha told Subhūti:

He does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the intrinsic nature of the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; he does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the intrinsic nature of the feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.

One does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding internal emptiness, up to and including non-existence-of-nature-intrinsic-nature emptiness;

one does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristic of internal emptiness, up to and including the characteristic of non-existence-of-nature-intrinsic-nature emptiness;

one does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, up to and including the intrinsic nature of non-existence-of-nature-intrinsic-nature emptiness.
He does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path;

he does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the characteristics of the eight branches of the noble path;

he does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the eight branches of the noble path.

In this way, up to and including the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation; up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation.

Regarding the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation; up to and including the characteristics of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation.

Regarding the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation; up to and including the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation.

One does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding all-knowledge; one does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

One does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of all-knowledge; one does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

One does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge; one does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Subhūti! It is because form is inconceivable;

feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable; and so on, up to omniscience being inconceivable, and the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects being inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; has long planted roots of virtue; has made many offerings to the Buddhas; and has served many spiritual friends."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
this Prajñāpāramitā is exceedingly profound.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!

Because form is profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound.”

Because the sense base of the eye is profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound.

Because the sense base of form is profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound.

Because the eye constituent is profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; because the constituents of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound.

Because the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is profound, the *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound; because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmadhātu*) are profound, the *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound;

because the realm of eye-consciousness (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*) is profound, the *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound; because the realms of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness are profound, the *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound;

because eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*) is profound, the *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound; because the contacts of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are profound, the *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound.

Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are profound, the Perfection of Wisdom is extremely profound; because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are profound, the Perfection of Wisdom is extremely profound.

Because the perfection of generosity is profound, the Perfection of Wisdom is extremely profound; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are profound, the Perfection of Wisdom is extremely profound.

Because internal emptiness is profound, the Perfection of Wisdom is extremely profound; and so on, up to: because the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence is profound, the Perfection of Wisdom is extremely profound.

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; and so on, up to: because the eightfold noble path is profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound. Likewise, up to:

because the ten powers of a Buddha are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; and up to: because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound.

Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound; and because the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are profound, the perfection of wisdom is exceedingly profound.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is a great treasury of jewels.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For it is able to bestow the jewels of merit upon sentient beings."
Subhūti! In this way,
the great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the ten paths of wholesome action,
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges— this great treasure.
Because it is a treasure, it is able to bestow upon sentient beings the great, precious jewels of the perfections of generosity,
ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; because it is able to bestow upon sentient beings internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.

Because they are great treasures— the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*),

the emptiness of self and common characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-sāmānyalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*),
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*)— they are able to bestow upon sentient beings the four [reliances].

Because they are the great jewels of the foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
because they can bestow upon sentient beings the great jewels of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and because they can bestow upon sentient beings the eight liberations and the eight bases of mastery...
Because they are great treasures of the [four] foundations, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases;
because they can bestow upon sentient beings the great treasure of suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the limit of reality, and the inconceivable realm;
and because they can bestow upon sentient beings the great treasure of the four noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Because they are able to bestow upon sentient beings the great jewels of the ten bodhisattva stages, the gateways of dhāraṇī, and the gateways of samādhi;
because they are able to bestow upon sentient beings the great jewels of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
because they are able to bestow upon sentient beings the Tathāgata’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and great compassion;
Because they are the great jewels of the three immeasurables—great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity—and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
because they can bestow upon sentient beings the great jewel of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;

and because they can bestow upon sentient beings the great jewels of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). They are able to...
Because it bestows upon sentient beings the great jewels of the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship,
and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; and because it bestows upon sentient beings the great jewels of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, and the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
this perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.”
The Buddha said: “So it is, Subhūti!”
Because form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.
Because the eye-base is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.
Because the form-base is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is a mass of purity; because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because the form-element (*rūpadhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because the sound-, odor-, taste-, tangible-, and phenomena-elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.
Because eye-contact is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; up to and including because the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; up to and including because the eightfold noble path is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Likewise, up to and including because the ten powers of the Tathāgata are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity; up to and including because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity.

Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is a collection of purity; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are pure, the perfection of wisdom is a collection of purity.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “How marvelous,
World-Honored One!
"How marvelous!
O Sugata! This Prajñāpāramitā is so exceedingly profound that it encounters many obstacles; yet now, as you expound it extensively, no obstacles arise."
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is just so!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles; however, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, although it is now being extensively taught, no obstacles shall arise."

Therefore, because they cherish the Dharma, sons and daughters of good family in the Mahāyāna who wish to transcribe this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā should transcribe it swiftly; those who wish to read and recite it should read and recite it swiftly; those who wish to receive and uphold it should receive and uphold it swiftly; those who wish to practice it should practice it swiftly; those who wish to contemplate it should contemplate it swiftly; and those who wish to proclaim it should proclaim it swiftly.
Why is this? Subhūti!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles; one must ensure that no difficulties arise to hinder its transcription, recitation, upholding, cultivation, contemplation, or exposition to others, so that these practices may reach their ultimate fulfillment.

“Subhūti! If these sons of good family or daughters of good family wish to complete the transcription of this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in one month, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven months, or even up to a year, they should transcribe it with diligent vigor and focused mindfulness, so that it may be completed within that time.”

"Subhūti! If these sons of noble family or daughters of noble family wish to master such a profound sūtra as this Prajñāpāramitā by upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and explaining it to others for one month, or two, three, four, five, six, or seven months, or even for a year, they should apply themselves with diligent vigor, maintaining mindfulness while upholding and so forth until they have explained it, so that they may achieve mastery within that allotted time."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because this profound Prajñāpāramitā, a priceless jewel, encounters many obstacles.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary,
World-Honored One!
"How marvelous!
Well-gone One!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā*, a priceless jewel, encounters many obstacles; yet there are those who write it down, read and recite it, receive and uphold it, contemplate it, cultivate it, and explain it to others. Against them, Māra seeks to create hindrances, so that they may not write it down, nor even expound it."
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"Although Māra, the Evil One, may wish to create obstacles so that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is not written down, recited, upheld, contemplated, cultivated, or explained to others, he lacks the power to obstruct this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s activities of writing, reciting, upholding, and so forth, such that they do not reach completion."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By whose spiritual power is it that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as they write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively expound such profound sūtras as this Prajñāpāramitā?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“It is through the spiritual power of the Buddha that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct or hinder Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in writing down, upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and extensively expounding such profound sūtras as this Perfection of Wisdom.”
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

It is also through the spiritual power of all the Buddhas in all worlds of the ten directions that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct or hinder Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in writing down, receiving and upholding, reading and reciting, practicing, contemplating, and extensively expounding such profound sūtras as this Perfection of Wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, because all Tathāgatas, Arhats,

and Samyaksaṃbuddhas collectively protect and keep in mind those bodhisattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they cause those evil Māras to be unable to obstruct or hinder those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, so that they do not prevent them from copying, receiving, upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and extensively explaining to others such profound sūtras as this perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Śāriputra, all Tathāgatas, Arhats,

and Samyaksaṃbuddhas collectively protect and keep in mind the wholesome deeds performed by those bodhisattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom, so that those evil Māras cannot create obstacles for them.

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, it is the natural law that they shall be protected and remembered by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—those who dwell in peace, maintain their presence, and currently teach the Dharma—in the infinite, countless, and boundless worlds of the ten directions. If one is protected and remembered by the Buddhas, it is the natural law that evil Māras will be unable to cause them hindrance.”

Śāriputra! If good sons and good daughters are able to copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, they should form this thought:

"That I now copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain for others this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā* is entirely due to the power of the protection and mindfulness of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless—who dwell in peace throughout the ten directions and currently teach the Dharma, causing these wholesome deeds of mine to not be obstructed by evil Māras."
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“If sons or daughters of good family are able to copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, all such acts are due to the protective mindfulness of the power of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, which ensures that no evil Māras can obstruct any of those excellent and wholesome deeds they perform.”
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

If sons or daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that they are all protected and sustained by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“If sons or daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, then all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions—who dwell in peace, maintain themselves, and currently teach the Dharma—all recognize these sons and daughters of good family who write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. By virtue of this cause and condition, they rejoice and protect them with their mindfulness.”

"Bhagavān! If sons or daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, these sons and daughters of good family will constantly be beheld by the Buddha-eye of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently dwelling in peace and teaching the Dharma throughout the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions. By virtue of this cause and condition, they will be protected and mindful of with compassion, and whatever wholesome deeds they perform will all be successfully accomplished."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

If sons or daughters of good family write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and expound such profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā*, these sons and daughters of good family will always be observed, known, and protected by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently dwelling in peace and teaching the Dharma throughout the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions. With their Buddha-eyes, those Buddhas behold them, recognize them, and keep them in mind, ensuring that no evil Māras can harass or disturb them, and causing the virtuous deeds they perform to be swiftly accomplished.

Śāriputra! If sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that these individuals have already drawn near to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and the armies of all Māras will be unable to obstruct them.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle are able to write out this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra with various adornments, and uphold, read, and recite it, you should know that these individuals have generated deep faith and understanding in this *prajñāpāramitā*. They are able to offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra by means of various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense scents, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, music, and lamps."

These sons and daughters of good family are constantly observed, known, and mindful of by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha with his Buddha-eye; by virtue of this cause and condition, they will certainly obtain great wealth, great benefit, great fruit, and great maturation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Because these sons and daughters of good family possess the power of the roots of goodness derived from writing down, upholding, reading, reciting, making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising the profound Prajñāpāramitā, they shall attain the stage of non-retrogression; until then, they will never be separated from the Buddhas, will constantly hear the True Dharma, and will never fall into the evil realms."

Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family, by virtue of these roots of goodness, shall until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment never be separated from the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they shall never be separated from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence; they shall never be separated from the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; and likewise, they shall never be separated from the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they shall never be separated from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; and they shall never be separated from all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas. By means of this, they will swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek.

Śāriputra! For this reason, those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should diligently copy, receive, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, explain to others, revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, never abandoning it for even a moment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā will, after my parinirvāṇa, gradually flourish in the southeastern direction."

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle and are able to conceive deep faith and joy in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, copying it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, practicing it, contemplating it, and expounding it; furthermore, they honor, revere, respect, and praise this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme and wholesome roots, they will never fall into the various perilous and evil destinies; instead, they will be born among the gods or among humans, enjoying wealth, honor, and happiness. Through this power, their practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom will progressively increase and swiftly reach fulfillment. Relying upon these, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Subsequently, according to what is appropriate for them, they will gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles and proceed toward liberation.
Some attain the nirvāṇa of the śrāvaka; some attain the nirvāṇa of the pratyekabuddha; and some attain the unsurpassed nirvāṇa of ultimate peace and bliss.
“Śāriputra! This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall spread from the southeast to the south and gradually flourish there.”

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and are able to develop deep faith and joy in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, copying it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, practicing it, reflecting upon it, and expounding it; furthermore, they honor, revere, respect, and praise this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will ultimately never fall into the various miserable realms; instead, they will be born among the gods or among humans, enjoying wealth and honor. Through this power, their practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom will progressively increase until they are swiftly brought to fulfillment. Relying on this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Subsequently, according to what is appropriate for them, they will gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles and proceed toward liberation.
Some attain the nirvāṇa of śrāvakas, some attain the nirvāṇa of pratyekabuddhas, and some attain the unsurpassed nirvāṇa of ultimate peace and happiness.
“Śāriputra! This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall further flourish, spreading from the south to the southwest.”

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and are able to develop deep faith and joy in this profound Prajñāpāramitā; they copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice and contemplate it, and explain it to others. Furthermore, with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps, they make offerings, pay homage, revere, and praise this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will never again fall into the perilous and evil realms; instead, they will be born in the heavens or among humans, enjoying wealth, nobility, and happiness. Through this power, their practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom will progressively increase and swiftly reach fulfillment. Relying on this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, honor, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Subsequently, according to what is appropriate for them, they will gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles and proceed toward liberation.
Some attain the nirvāṇa of śrāvakas; some attain the nirvāṇa of pratyekabuddhas; and some attain the unsurpassed nirvāṇa of ultimate peace and bliss.
“Śāriputra! This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā will, after my parinirvāṇa, gradually flourish as it spreads from the southwest to the northwest.”

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle and are able to develop deep faith and joy in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, copying it, receiving and maintaining it, reading and reciting it, practicing it, contemplating it, and expounding it; furthermore, they honor, revere, respect, and praise this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will never again fall into the perilous and evil realms; instead, they will be born among the gods or among humans in states of wealth, nobility, and happiness. Through this power, their practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom will progressively increase and swiftly reach fulfillment. Relying on this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Thereafter, according to what is appropriate for them, they will gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles and proceed toward liberation.
Some attain the nirvāṇa of the śrāvaka; some attain the nirvāṇa of the pratyekabuddha; and some attain the unsurpassed nirvāṇa of ultimate peace and bliss.
“Śāriputra! This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish as it moves from the northwest to the north.”

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and are able to develop deep faith and joy in this profound Prajñāpāramitā; they copy, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound it. Furthermore, with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps, they make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will ultimately never fall into the various perilous and evil realms; instead, they will be born in the heavens or among humans to enjoy wealth, nobility, and happiness. Through this power, their practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom will progressively increase and swiftly reach fulfillment. Relying on this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, honor, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Subsequently, according to what is appropriate for them, they will gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles and proceed toward liberation.
Some attain the nirvāṇa of the śrāvaka; some attain the nirvāṇa of the pratyekabuddha; and some attain the unsurpassed nirvāṇa of ultimate peace and happiness.
“Śāriputra! This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall further flourish, spreading gradually from the north to the northeast.”

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and are able to develop profound faith and delight in this very profound *prajñāpāramitā*. They copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and expound it; furthermore, they offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, music, and lamps, thereby making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will ultimately never fall into the perilous and evil realms; instead, they will be born among the gods or among humans in states of wealth and nobility where they experience happiness. Through this power, their practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom will progressively increase and swiftly reach fulfillment. Relying on this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Thereafter, according to what is appropriate for them, they will gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles and proceed toward liberation.
Some attain the nirvana of a śrāvaka; some attain the nirvana of a pratyekabuddha; and some attain the unsurpassed nirvana of ultimate peace and bliss.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years, this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā will perform great Buddha-work in the northeastern region."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
that which is the Dharma revered by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is precisely this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra, this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā is protected and sustained by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats,
and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

The unsurpassed true Dharma of the Vinaya that is not attained by the Buddhas does not possess the characteristic of extinction or disappearance; rather, the unsurpassed true Dharma of the Vinaya attained by all Buddhas is precisely this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.

Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family in the northeastern direction who are able to have faith in, delight in, uphold, recite, study, contemplate, and explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, I shall constantly protect and keep those sons and daughters of good family in mind, so that they may be free from harm and affliction.
“Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family in the northeastern direction who are able to write down such profound sūtras as this Perfection of Wisdom,
and furthermore [honor them] with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands,..."
By offering and honoring such profound sūtras as this Perfection of Wisdom with incense, powders, and other fragrances, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps,
I definitively declare that those sons and daughters of good family, by virtue of...
These roots of goodness will ultimately never fall into the various perilous and evil realms; one will be born among gods and humans, constantly experiencing sublime bliss.

By the power of this, one increases the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) and, based upon them, is able to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Thereafter, according to what is appropriate, one shall rely on the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.
They gradually practice and train until they attain parinirvāṇa.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
With my Buddha-eye, I behold, realize, extol, and praise the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family.

Likewise, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas dwelling in peace throughout the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir—who are currently teaching the Dharma—also behold, realize, extol, and praise the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family with their Buddha-eyes.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Will this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā be widely disseminated in the northeastern region after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, during the later period, the latter part, and the final five hundred years?”
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra, it is so! It is thus!”
It is so! It is so!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years, shall be widely disseminated in the northeastern region.
Śāriputra! After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years,
those sons and daughters of good family in the northeastern direction who shall hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*...
Those who, having conceived deep faith and joy in the Prajñāpāramitā, write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it,
contemplate it according to the principle, and explain it to others— know that those sons and daughters of good family have long since resolved their minds upon unsurpassed,
perfect enlightenment and have long practiced the conduct of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, making offerings [to the Buddhas].
Having encountered many Buddhas and served many virtuous friends, they have long cultivated bodily discipline, mental concentration, and wisdom;

their planted roots of goodness have all reached maturity. By the power of this merit, they are able to hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, develop deep faith and joy, and further transcribe, uphold, recite, and practice it.
...contemplate it, and explain it to others.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, how many sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the north-eastern region who have set out upon the Bodhisattva vehicle will hear such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and give rise to deep faith and joy? Will their minds be without alarm, fear, or terror, and free from anxiety or regret, and furthermore, will they be able to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it to others?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, although there may be immeasurable sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle in the northeast, few will hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and give rise to deep faith and delight. Their minds will not be startled, terrified, or fearful, nor will they feel regret; furthermore, they will be able to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it to others.”

Śāriputra! When those sons and daughters of good family hear this profound sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, their minds are not startled, not terrified, and not afraid; nor do they feel anxiety or regret. They give rise to deep faith and joy, and they copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and expound it—this is truly most rare.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

these sons and daughters of good family have already approached, made offerings to, honored, respected, and praised immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, and have inquired about the meaning and intent associated with such profound Prajñāpāramitā.

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; before long, they will certainly fulfill inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; before long, they will certainly fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; before long, they will certainly fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and before long, they will certainly fulfill all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”

Śāriputra! Because those sons and daughters of good family are protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; because they are sustained by immeasurable spiritual friends; because they are upheld by sublime roots of goodness; and because they desire to bring benefit and happiness to many sentient beings, they seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Why is this? Śāriputra, I constantly teach the Dharma associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) to those sons and daughters of good family; likewise, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past also constantly taught the Dharma associated with the knowledge of all aspects to those sons and daughters of good family.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, those sons and daughters of good family will, in future lives, be able to seek and advance toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and they will also be able to teach the Dharma to others as appropriate, leading them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family possess such stability of body and mind that even the Evil Māra and his retinue cannot destroy their aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; how much less could others who delight in evil deeds and slander the *prajñāpāramitā* obstruct their minds and cause them to cease striving for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 439. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Order. Second Division, Chapter on the Northeast, Part 43-3. "Śāriputra!

In this way, these sons and daughters of good family of the Mahāyāna, upon hearing me teach this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will attain a vast and sublime joy and bliss of mind in the Dharma; they will also be able to establish immeasurable sentient beings in the supreme wholesome dharmas and cause them to advance toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family have now made a great vow before me, saying:

"I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and inspiring them, lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, until they receive the prediction of non-retrogression and abide on the stage of a bodhisattva’s non-retrogression."
"Śāriputra! I deeply rejoice in that vow. Why is this?

Śāriputra! I observe that these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle have made such great vows, and their minds and words are in accord. Those sons and daughters of good family will certainly, in future ages, be able to establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and inspiring them, lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, until they receive the prediction of non-retrogression and abide on the stage of the non-retrogressive bodhisattva.
“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family have also, in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, made this great vow:

‘I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), to cultivate the practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and by manifesting, exhorting, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, cause them to attain the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and to abide in the stage of non-retrogression of a Bodhisattva.’”
"Śāriputra! The Buddhas of the past also gave their profound sympathetic joy toward that vow. Why is this?"

Śāriputra! The Buddhas of the past also observed that when these sons and daughters of good family who have set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle make such great vows, their minds and words are in accord. Those sons and daughters of good family will certainly, in future ages, be able to establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by manifesting, exhorting, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, lead them to unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even to the point of receiving the prediction of non-retrogression and abiding on the stage of irreversible bodhisattvahood.

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family possess vast faith and understanding; they are able to practice vast giving based upon excellent forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles. Having practiced this giving, they are further able to plant vast roots of goodness, and by means of these roots of goodness, they are able to gather vast karmic fruits. Having gathered such vast fruits, they dedicate them solely for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, and are able to relinquish all internal and external possessions to those sentient beings.”

They dedicate these roots of merit thus: may they be reborn in the buddha-fields of other directions where Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently reside, proclaiming this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound Prajñāpāramitā.

Having heard this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is further able to establish countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings within that Buddha-field, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) and to practice the deeds of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. By demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, he causes them to attain non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; thereby fulfilling their great vows, they shall swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How marvelous!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is able [to know] all dharmas of the past, future, and present.”

There is nothing he does not realize and know; regarding the suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the reality-limit, and the space-element of all phenomena, there is nothing he does not realize and know;
regarding the various distinctions among the teachings on all phenomena, there is nothing he does not realize and know;
regarding the distinctions in the mental activities of all sentient beings, there is nothing he does not realize and know; and regarding the past...
There are no bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who do not realize and know; there are no past Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas whom they do not realize and know;
there are no disciples of the Buddhas of the past nor any Buddha-fields whom they do not realize and know;
and there are no bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future whom they do not realize.
He knows that there is nothing among all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of future ages that he does not realize and know;
he knows that there is nothing among the disciples of those Buddhas and the various Buddha-fields of future ages that he does not realize and know;
and he knows that there is nothing regarding the differences in the practices of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas currently dwelling in the worlds of the ten directions who do not realize and know.

In the present world, there is nothing that he does not realize and know regarding all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who dwell in peace and maintain their presence while preaching the Dharma in the infinite, countless, and boundless worlds of the ten directions; likewise,
there is nothing among the disciples of those Buddhas or within those Buddha-fields in the present world that he does not realize and know.

"Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva applies courageous diligence and constantly seeks the six pāramitās without ceasing, will there be times when they attain these six pāramitās and times when they do not?"
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

Those sons and daughters of good family who constantly apply themselves with courageous diligence to these six pāramitās, seeking them with joyful perseverance without ceasing, will at all times attain them; there shall be no time when they do not attain them.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because those sons and daughters of good family constantly seek these six pāramitās with courageous diligence and without ceasing, and because all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas always protect and keep them in mind.
Śāriputra said: “World-Honored One!
If those sons and daughters of good family do not obtain sūtras associated with the six pāramitās, how can it be said that they have attained these six pāramitās?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

If those sons and daughters of good family always seek these six pāramitās with courageous faith, disregarding even their own bodies and lives, it is impossible that they should at any time fail to obtain this corresponding sūtra.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, those sons and daughters of good family, seeking unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, manifest themselves to instruct, encourage, inspire, and gladden all sentient beings, causing them to receive, uphold, recite, contemplate, and practice these sūtras associated with the six pāramitās. By virtue of these roots of goodness, wherever they are born, they will always encounter these sūtras associated with the six pāramitās; they will receive, uphold, and recite them, practicing with courageous diligence according to the teachings, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields, never for a moment ceasing until they have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Chapter 44: On the Deeds of Māra. Part Two, Chapter Forty-four: On the Deeds of Māra. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

The Buddha has already praised and described the merit accomplished by those sons and daughters of good family who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and who practice with vigor the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields.
"Bhagavān! When these sons and daughters of good family set out for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and practice the various deeds, how should one recognize the obstructing works of Māra?"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in proclaiming the essential points of the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, yet eloquence does not quickly manifest at the appropriate time, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.”
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,

for what reason is it considered an activity of Māra when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, though desiring to proclaim the essential points of the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, finds that the eloquence of speech does not manifest promptly?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, because the perfections from the perfection of wisdom down to the perfection of generosity are difficult to bring to fulfillment through such causes and conditions, it is declared that when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva delights in proclaiming the essential teachings for the sake of sentient beings, the eloquence of their timely speech does not quickly manifest; this is considered a work of Māra.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who delights in practicing sublime conduct suddenly finds eloquence arising, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
for what reason is it said that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in practicing sublime deeds, if eloquence suddenly arises, this is a work of Māra?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, because they lack skillful means, eloquence suddenly arises and they abandon the cultivation of those practices. Therefore, it is said that when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva delights in cultivating superior practices and eloquence suddenly arises, this is considered a work of Māra.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle are copying this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if they yawn frequently, engage in groundless joking and laughter, treat one another with contempt, have their bodies and minds agitated, misarrange the words and phrases, become confused regarding the meaning and principles, fail to find its flavor, or if sudden obstacles arise so that the copying is not completed—know that these are the deeds of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, cultivate, explain, or listen to this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* Sūtra, if they yawn frequently, engage in groundless joking and laughter, treat one another with contempt, have their bodies and minds agitated, misarrange the words and phrases, become confused regarding the principles, fail to find its flavor, or if untoward events suddenly arise such that what they undertake is not accomplished—know that these are the works of Māra for a bodhisattva."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

for what reason do sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing this profound sūtra on the perfection of wisdom being preached, suddenly form such a thought as this?”
"I find no flavor in this sutra; what is the use of listening to it with such diligent toil?
Having thought thus, he immediately departs.
It is the same for those who [fail to] receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, practice, transcribe, or explain it.
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

These sons and daughters of good family have not practiced the perfection of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity for long in past lives; therefore, when they hear and receive this profound perfection of wisdom, they find no flavor in it, and unable to endure it in their hearts, they immediately depart.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra being taught, if they should think:
'I have not received the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; what is the use of listening to and receiving such a sūtra? "

"Due to these conditions, his mind becomes unpurified and he finds no flavor [in the teaching]; he then rises from his seat, abandons it with distaste, and departs. You should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
Then, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, for what reason,

within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, are these sons and daughters of good family not granted the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such that they become unable to endure it, grow weary, and depart?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

A bodhisattva who has not yet entered the state of right determination (samyaktva-niyāma) should not be granted the prediction of great enlightenment (mahābodhi-vyākaraṇa). If one were to grant such a prediction, it would increase their arrogance and negligence; since this would cause harm rather than benefit, no prediction is given.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra being taught, if they should think:
'Our names are not mentioned herein; what is the use of listening? "
"With a mind that is not pure, one finds no flavor [in the teaching]; thus, rising from one's seat, one becomes weary and departs. You should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason, within this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, is the name of that bodhisattva not recorded or proclaimed?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
It is the natural law that a bodhisattva who has not yet received the prophecy of great enlightenment should not have their name proclaimed. "Furthermore, Subhūti,
when those sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra being taught, if they should think:
"In this [teaching], our birthplaces—cities, towns, and villages—are not mentioned; what is the use of listening?
With an impure mind, they find no flavor [in the teaching], and rising from their seats, they depart in weary rejection. One should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
for what reason and by what causal conditions is the birthplace— whether city, town, or village— of those bodhisattvas not recorded or declared within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra?"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If the name of that bodhisattva has not yet been prophesied, one should not speak of the distinctions regarding their place of birth.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* being preached, does not attain purity of mind or find their taste in them, and thus departs, then according to the number of steps they take while harboring that impure mind of aversion and abandonment toward this sūtra, they shall lose an equal number of kalpas of merit. They shall incur an equal number of kalpas of karmic obstacles to awakening. Only after undergoing those offenses for that same duration must they again exert diligent effort to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and practice the difficult and painful austerities of a bodhisattva, before they may restore their original state."
Therefore, if a bodhisattva wishes to swiftly realize unsurpassed awakening, they should not feel weary of or abandon the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
