You should swiftly apply yourself with diligence to study those dharmas that all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study those dharmas that Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will soon sit firmly upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimanda), realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the Devaputra Sunirmitarati, leading a host of the Nirmanarati devas, came to where he was, made offerings, paid homage, showed respect, and offered praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should swiftly apply yourself with diligence to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will soon sit securely upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the devaputra Nirmāṇarati, leading a host of Nirmāṇarati devas, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect,
and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should swiftly apply yourself with diligence to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will soon sit peacefully upon the sublime seat of awakening, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the divine son Subhakṛtsna, leading a host from the Heaven of Making Use of Others’ Transformations, came to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should swiftly apply yourself with diligence to study those dharmas that all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study those dharmas that Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will soon sit peacefully upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, leading the hosts of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmakāyika devas, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should swiftly apply yourself with diligence to study those dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study those dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will quickly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). I shall then go beneath the Bodhi tree and earnestly entreat you to turn the unexcelled wheel of Dharma, for the benefit and happiness of infinite sentient beings."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in order to constantly train in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the gods of the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, and the Ābhāsvara-kāyika gods come to his presence to make offerings,

pay homage, show respect, and offer praise. The gods of the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, and the Śubhakṛtsna-kāyika gods come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise.”

The gods of the Bṛhatphala Heaven, along with the hosts of the Bṛhat, Parīttabṛhat, and Apramāṇabṛhat heavens, came to where he was, making offerings, paying homage, showing respect, and praising him;

the gods of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, along with the hosts of the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, and Sudarśana heavens, also came to where he was, making offerings, paying homage, showing respect, and praising him, each saying: "Excellent!"
"O Mahāsattva!

You should swiftly apply yourself with diligence to study those dharmas that all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study those dharmas that Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will soon sit securely upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."

“Monks, you should know that because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom as it has been taught, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, along with the devas, nāgas, asuras, and others, constantly follow, protect, and keep them in mind.”
By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be harmed by any worldly perils, dangers, or calamities, nor by any physical or mental afflictions and sufferings.
"Bhikṣus, you should know this!"

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) exactly as it has been taught, all diseases arising from the mutual conflict of the four great elements in the world shall not afflict them.

That which is called eye disease, ear disease, nose disease, tongue disease, body disease, and diseases of the various limbs and joints—all such four hundred and four diseases are forever non-existent within his body, except for the maturation of heavy karma being manifested as light suffering.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) according to how it is taught, they obtain such immeasurable and boundless merits in both the present life and future lives, which all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are able to know, see, and awaken to.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 454. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter Sixty-one on Fellow Students, Part Two. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda had this thought to himself:

"Is it by his own eloquence that Śakra, Lord of the Devas, proclaims such profound Prajñāpāramitā and praises the merits and benefits of such profound Prajñāpāramitā, or is it through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata?"
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, immediately understood what Ānanda was thinking in his mind and said:
"Venerable One,

this profound *prajñāpāramitā* that I have proclaimed, and these meritorious benefits of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* that I have praised, are all due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata."
At that time, the World-Honored One said to Ānanda: "So it is! So it is!"

Today, when Śakra, Lord of the Devas, proclaims and praises the merits and benefits of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that these are entirely due to the spiritual power of the Tathāgata, and not his own eloquence.
Why is this? The meritorious benefits and supreme virtues of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* certainly cannot be known or expounded by any in the world—whether devas, humans, or asuras.

Ānanda, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva studies, contemplates, and practices this profound perfection of wisdom, all the evil Māras in this trichiliocosm will give rise to doubt and uncertainty, thinking to themselves:

"Will this bodhisattva mahāsattva realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and thereby regress to attain the fruit of a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; or will he proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

"Furthermore, Ānanda! Whenever a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from such profound prajñāpāramitā, all evil Māras give rise to great anguish and distress, their bodies and minds pierced with pain as if struck by poisoned arrows."
Furthermore, Ānanda!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, various evil Māras come to where he is and manifest all kinds of terrifying things, desiring to cause the bodhisattva’s body and mind to be struck with alarm and fear, to lose the mind of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and to feel despondency regarding the practice they are cultivating, even to the point of giving rise to a single thought of distraction, thereby obstructing the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment—this is the deep-seated wish of those evil Māras.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound prajñāpāramitā, are they all afflicted and disturbed by Māra, or are there some who are disturbed and others who are not?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"It is not the case that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* are troubled and disturbed by Māra; rather, there are those who are troubled and disturbed, and those who are not."
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Which bodhisattva mahāsattvas, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, are harassed and disturbed by evil māras?"
“What kind of bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, is not troubled or disturbed by Māra?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom in previous lives, did not believe or understand it, but instead reviled and slandered it, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will be troubled and disturbed by various evil māras.”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, has believed in, understood, and praised it, and has not given rise to slander, then when that bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be troubled or disturbed by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom in a previous life, harbors doubt and hesitation, thinking:
'Does it exist, or does it not exist?'"
"Is it real or unreal?
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will be vexed and disturbed by various evil māras.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, does not give rise to doubt or hesitation in their mind but believes with certainty that it truly exists, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be troubled or disturbed by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is separated from virtuous friends and is instead influenced by evil associates, they will not hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they do not hear it, they cannot comprehend the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; because they do not comprehend it, they cannot cultivate the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; because they do not cultivate it, they cannot inquire about the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; because they do not inquire about it, they do not practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the teaching; and because they do not practice according to the teaching, they cannot realize the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are tormented and distracted by various evil Māras.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva associates with virtuous friends and is not influenced by evil friends, they will hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they hear it, they are able to comprehend the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; because they comprehend it, they are able to cultivate the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; because they cultivate it, they are able to inquire about the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; because they inquire about it, they are able to practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the teaching; and because they practice according to the teaching, they are able to realize the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and instead embraces and praises what is not the true, sublime Dharma, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will be harassed and disturbed by Māras when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva stays close to the perfection of wisdom and does not embrace or praise what is not the true, sublime Dharma, then when that bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they will not be troubled or disturbed by Māra.

"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), slanders and reviles the sublime and true Dharma, at that time Māra, the Evil One, thinks thus:

'Now this bodhisattva is my companion; because he slanders the sublime and true Dharma, there will be immeasurable individuals (pudgala) dwelling in the bodhisattva vehicle who will likewise give rise to slander toward the sublime and true Dharma. By this cause and condition, my wish shall be fulfilled.'"

If such a person belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, despite diligently applying effort to cultivate all wholesome dharmas, falls into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha—and causes others to fall as well—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will be harassed and disturbed by evil māras.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), praises and accepts the sublime true Dharma, and likewise causes immeasurable individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle to praise and accept the sublime true Dharma, the evil Māra will become sorrowful, anxious, and terrified. Even if such an individual of the bodhisattva vehicle does not apply themselves with diligence to cultivate the various wholesome dharmas, they will nonetheless certainly not cause themselves or others to fall back into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha; they will surely realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they cannot be disturbed or confused by the evil Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears the profound sūtras spoken on the *prajñāpāramitā*, they speak these words:

'The principle of this *prajñāpāramitā* is so profound that it is difficult to see and difficult to realize; what is the use of proclaiming, hearing, receiving and upholding, reading and reciting, contemplating, diligently practicing, writing down, or disseminating this sūtra?'"
"I cannot even fathom its source or its bottom, much less others of meager merit and shallow wisdom!

At that time, immeasurable individuals abiding in the vehicle of the Bodhisattvas, upon hearing these words, were all struck with alarm and fear; they then withdrew from the mind set on unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and fell to the level of the two vehicles. It is when such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* that they are thus afflicted and disturbed by evil Māras.
If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears the profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they speak these words:

"The principle of this *prajñāpāramitā* is so profound that it is difficult to see and difficult to realize; if it is not proclaimed, heard, received, upheld, recited, contemplated, diligently practiced, written down, and circulated, it is impossible for one to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

At that time, immeasurable individuals abiding in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, having heard what was said, were filled with joy and exultation; they all took constant delight in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, thoroughly mastering, reflecting upon according to the principle, diligently practicing, explaining to others, and transcribing and disseminating this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as they practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on his own accumulated merit and roots of goodness, disparages other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, saying:
'I am able to practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, whereas you are not able.'"
I am able to dwell in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, whereas you are not able.
I am able to dwell in suchness up to the inconceivable realm, whereas you are not able.
I am able to dwell securely in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; you are not able to do so.
I am able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; you are not able to do so.
"I am able to practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the eight liberations up to the ten totalities, whereas you are not."
I am able to practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice from the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the wisdom of the Stage of Pure Contemplation up to the wisdom of the Tathāgata Stage, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), whereas you are not.
I am able to purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity, whereas you are not.
I am able to contemplate the factors of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order, whereas you are not.
I am able to observe specific and general characteristics, whereas you are not.
I am able to cultivate the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi, whereas you are not.
"I am able to cultivate all the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, whereas you are not.
At that time, the evil Māra, filled with joy and exultation, said:
"This bodhisattva is my ally; he will wander in birth and death without any prospect of escape."
"When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will be harassed and disturbed by evil Māras.

However, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely on their own meritorious roots of goodness to disparage other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and although they constantly and diligently cultivate all wholesome dharmas, they do not cling to the marks of those wholesome dharmas, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be harassed and disturbed by evil Māras."

"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on his own renowned name and lineage, looks down upon other bodhisattvas who cultivate goodness; if he constantly praises his own virtues and disparages the faults of others; if, though lacking in reality the practices, marks, and signs of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva, he claims they truly exist; and if, giving rise to various afflictions, he praises himself and disparages others, saying:
'You all lack the name and lineage of a bodhisattva; I alone possess the name and lineage of a bodhisattva.'"
Because they, out of overweening pride, treat other bodhisattva mahāsattvas with contempt and disparagement,
at that time the evil Māra, having seen this, thinks to himself:
"Now this bodhisattva makes my realm and palaces not empty, thereby increasing the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts."

At that time, the evil Māra assisted him with his supernatural power, causing his majesty, influence, and eloquence to increase even further. Consequently, many people believed and accepted his words, and because of this, they were exhorted and incited to share in those same evil views.

Having shared in those same evil views, they follow that false learning; having followed that false learning, their afflictions blaze intensely. Because their minds are inverted, all the physical, verbal, and mental actions they initiate are capable of bringing about undesirable, ruinous, and painful results.

By reason of these causes and conditions, the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts increase, causing the palaces and lands of Māra to become filled; consequently, the evil Māras rejoice and leap for joy, and whatever they do is accomplished according to their will and at their own disposal. Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are harassed and disturbed by these evil Māras.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely on their own false name and lineage to despise other bodhisattvas who cultivate goodness, possesses no overweening pride regarding their merits, never praises themselves nor disparages others, and is able to skillfully recognize the deeds of evil Māras, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be troubled or disturbed by evil Māras.
"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva should engage in mutual disparagement, slander, and contention with those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the pratyekabuddhas."
At that time, having seen this event, the Evil Māra thought to himself:
"Now this bodhisattva has distanced himself from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and has drawn near to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts."

Why is this? To mutually disparage, revile, and contend with one another is not the path to bodhi; rather, it is the perilous path to the miserable realms of hell, the animal kingdom, and the realm of hungry ghosts.

Having formed this thought, they leap for joy and exult, causing the power of this bodhisattva to increase further so that immeasurable people may grow in evil karma; thus, when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is harassed and disturbed by various wicked Māras.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not revile, disparage, or engage in strife with those seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but instead employs skillful means to guide them toward the Mahāyāna or to encourage them to diligently cultivate the wholesome dharmas of their own respective vehicles, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be troubled or disturbed by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva engages in conflict, dispute, slander, and mutual disparagement with other bodhisattvas who seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment through patience and gentleness."
At that time, having seen this event, the Evil Māra thought to himself:

"These two bodhisattvas have both distanced themselves from the sought-after knowledge of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and have drawn near to the various perilous evil destinies, such as those of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, and asuras."

Why is this so? Strife, contention, slander, and mutual disparagement are not the path to Bodhi; they are merely the perilous roads leading to the miserable realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, and asuras.

At that time, having formed this thought, Māra the Evil One rejoiced and leaped for joy, increasing his own power and causing the two factions to fight and quarrel without ceasing; thus, when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is troubled and disturbed by all the evil Māras.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, together with a community of bodhisattvas seeking unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, does not engage in strife, contention, slandering, or disparagement, but instead exhorts and leads one another to cultivate sublime practices so as to swiftly proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of unexcelled great enlightenment should give rise to a mind of anger and resentment toward other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of unexcelled great enlightenment, and should quarrel with them, treat them with contempt, revile them, or slander them—then for as many moments of such unbeneficial thought as he has produced, that bodhisattva-mahāsattva shall regress from his previously cultivated sublime practices for that many eons; for that long he shall remain far removed from virtuous friends, and for that long he shall again undergo the bonds of birth and death."

If one does not abandon the great bodhicitta, then for that many eons one shall don the armor and diligently cultivate sublime practices without interruption; only thereafter will one restore the merit that had been lost.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the suffering of birth and death resulting from the evil thoughts generated by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, must they necessarily wander through saṃsāra for such a long duration, or can they also attain liberation in the interim?”

Regarding the superior practice from which this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has regressed: must he necessarily exert diligent effort for that many kalpas before it is restored, or is there a way to recover the original state in the interim?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"I have taught for bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas the existence of dharmas for the restoration of virtue through the expiation of offenses.
Ānanda, you should know this!"

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, not yet having received the prediction of unsurpassed great enlightenment, gives rise to a mind of anger and resentment toward those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of unsurpassed great enlightenment—quarreling with them, treating them with contempt, reviling, and slandering them—and subsequently lacks shame and remorse, harbors malice without relinquishing it, and is unable to confess and repent according to the Dharma, I declare that for such a person there is no sense of emerging from the offense or restoring their virtue during that interval; they must instead wander through birth and death for that many eons, separated from virtuous friends and bound by manifold sufferings.

If one does not abandon the mind of great enlightenment (*mahābodhicitta*), then for that many eons, while donning the armor and diligently cultivating sublime practices without interruption, one shall subsequently restore whatever merits were lost.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having not yet received the prediction of unsurpassed great awakening, gives rise to a mind of anger and resentment toward other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of unsurpassed great awakening—engaging in strife, disparagement, abuse, and slander—and subsequently feels shame and remorse, ensuring that his mind is no longer bound by evil, and is able to immediately confess and repent according to the Dharma, thinking:
"I have now obtained this human body so difficult to find; how could I allow myself to again give rise to such faults and evils as to lose this great and wholesome benefit?"
I ought to benefit all sentient beings; how could I allow myself to instead cause them harm?
I ought to revere all sentient beings as a servant serves his master; how could I allow myself to instead give rise to arrogance, reviling and despising them?
"I ought to endure all the beatings and rebukes of sentient beings; how could I permit myself to retaliate against them with violent or harsh physical or verbal acts?
I ought to reconcile all sentient beings so that they may respect and love one another; how could I permit myself to again give rise to angry or malicious speech to provoke conflict with them?"
I ought to endure being trodden upon by all sentient beings for a long time, like a road or a bridge; how could I possibly respond to them with further insult?

I seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in order to uproot the great suffering of birth and death for sentient beings and enable them to attain ultimate peace and bliss in nirvana; how could I possibly wish to inflict further suffering upon them?

From this day forth until the end of the future, I shall be like one who is dull-witted, mute, deaf, and blind; I shall not engage in any discrimination toward sentient beings. Even if my head, feet, hands, and arms were to be severed, or my eyes plucked out, my ears cut off, my nose sliced away, my tongue cut out, or any other part of my body or limbs were to be mangled, I would never give rise to malice toward those sentient beings.

If I give rise to evil thoughts, I shall immediately fall away from and destroy the unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening mind I have generated; I shall obstruct the omniscience I seek and be unable to bring benefit, peace, and happiness to sentient beings.

"Ānanda, you should know that for these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, I say there is also the meaning of emerging from transgressions and restoring their virtue even in the interim; they do not necessarily have to undergo the cycle of birth and death for so many kalpas, and Māra, the evil one, cannot disturb them; they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Ānanda! Sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should not engage in social interaction with those seeking the vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas; even if they do engage in such interaction, they should not dwell together with them; and even if they dwell together with them, they should not engage them in discussion or dialectical analysis."

Why is this so? If one were to engage in debate or definitive analysis with such persons, it might provoke thoughts of anger and resentment, or lead to the utterance of harsh and abusive speech. However, a bodhisattva should not give rise to thoughts of anger and resentment toward sentient beings, nor should they produce harsh or abusive speech.
Even if one's head, feet, or limbs are severed, one should not give rise to anger or harsh speech. Why is this?
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should form this thought:

"I seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to uproot the manifold sufferings of birth and death for sentient beings and enable them to attain ultimate benefit and peace; how could I possibly turn this into an evil deed toward them?"
"Ānanda, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of anger toward sentient beings and utters harsh and evil words, they will thereby obstruct unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and also destroy the boundless dharmas of the bodhisattva practices."
Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment should not harbor anger toward sentient beings, nor should they utter harsh or evil speech.
The Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how should Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell together with other Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell together with other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they should regard one another as they would the Great Teacher. Why is this? Because...”
These bodhisattvas, looking at one another in turn, should form this thought:

"They are all my true spiritual friends; they are my companions, riding upon the same vessel. As for the training, the time of training, and the dharmas to be learned—if one trains by means of these, there is no difference whatsoever."
Just as they should train in the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in true thusness up to the inconceivable realm, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the eight liberations up to the ten spheres of totality, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the stages from the Ground of Supreme Joy up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in all the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields, so too should I train.

"Just as they should train in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), so too should I train. Furthermore, he thinks:
"These bodhisattvas teach us the path to great enlightenment; they are my true companions and my teachers."

If that bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in distracted mental attention and is separated from mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes, I shall not train in accordance with him therein.

If those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas remain free from distracted mental engagements and do not depart from mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all modes, I shall likewise train in accordance with them in every respect.
"Ānanda, you should know this!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this way, they will swiftly bring the provisions for awakening (bodhi-sambhāra) to full completion.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are said to be training as one of the same course as the assembly of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas."
62. Chapter on Similarity, Part Two, Chapter Sixty-Two on Similarity, Section One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"What is the commonality (*sabhāgatā*) of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by virtue of which bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in this training are called 'fellow students'?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"Internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is the commonality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*) is the commonality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in training therein, they are called 'fellow students. By means of this fellowship, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*)."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Form is empty of the nature of form;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. This is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."

The sense base of the eye is empty of the nature of the sense base of the eye, and so on, up to the sense base of the mind being empty of the nature of the sense base of the mind; this is the common nature of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The sense base of form is empty of the nature of the sense base of form, and so on, up to the sense base of phenomena being empty of the nature of the sense base of phenomena; this is the common nature of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The eye-element is empty of the nature of the eye-element, and so on, up to the mind-element being empty of the nature of the mind-element; this is the common nature of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The form-element is empty of the nature of the form-element, and so on, up to the phenomena-element being empty of the nature of the phenomena-element; this is the common nature of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The eye-consciousness element is empty of the nature of the eye-consciousness element, and so on up to the mind-consciousness element, which is empty of the nature of the mind-consciousness element; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Eye-contact is empty of the nature of eye-contact, and so on up to mind-contact, which is empty of the nature of mind-contact; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition have the nature of emptiness; even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition have the nature of emptiness—this is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element, and so on, up to the consciousness element being empty of the nature of the consciousness element; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance, and so on, up to old age and death being empty of the nature of old age and death; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The perfection of generosity is empty of the nature of the perfection of generosity, and so on, up to the perfection of wisdom being empty of the nature of the perfection of wisdom; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature being empty of the nature of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness, and so on up to the inconceivable realm, which is empty of the nature of the inconceivable realm; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering, and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, which are empty of the nature of the eight branches of the noble path; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments. This is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations; even up to the ten spheres of totality, they are empty of the nature of the ten spheres of totality—this is the same nature as that of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness—this is the same nature as that of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The Stage of Pure Observation is empty of the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Pure Observation, up to and including the Stage of the Tathāgata, which is empty of the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Tathāgata; this is the commonality of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

The Stage of Supreme Joy is empty of the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Supreme Joy, up to and including the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, which is empty of the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma; this is the commonality of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

The gateways of dhāraṇī are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī; the gateways of samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gateways of samādhi; this is the common nature of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes; the six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers—this is the same nature as that of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The ten powers of the Tathāgata are empty of the nature of the ten powers of the Tathāgata, and so on up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, which are empty of the nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—this is the same nature as that of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge; the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects. This is the commonality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The fruit of stream-entry is empty of the nature of the fruit of stream-entry, up to and including the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, which is empty of the nature of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; this is the commonality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva practice, its nature is emptiness; this is the same nature as that of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of a buddha is empty of the nature of the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of a buddha; this is the same nature as that of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

"Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in training together, they are called 'those who train together'; by virtue of this shared training, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of form, and trains for the sake of the exhaustion of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
Is one training for the sake of detachment from form, and for the sake of detachment from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, training in the knowledge of all modes?
Is one training for the sake of the cessation of form, and for the sake of the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, training in the knowledge of all modes?

"If one trains for the sake of the non-arising of form, and trains for the sake of the non-arising of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna),
World-Honored One?"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains thus, even to the extent of training for the sake of the exhaustion of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, and for the sake of the exhaustion of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If one trains for the sake of the detachment of a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, and trains for the sake of the detachment of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If one trains for the sake of the cessation of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, and trains for the sake of the cessation of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If one trains for the sake of the non-arising of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, and trains for the sake of the non-arising of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "As you have said:
'If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of form, its detachment, its cessation, and its non-arising, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?'"
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion, detachment, cessation, and non-arising of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If one trains in this way, even unto the exhaustion, detachment, cessation, and non-arising of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?

If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion, detachment, cessation, and non-arising of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Is the suchness of form exhausted, detached, ceased, or severed?"
Are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness exhausted, detached from, ceased, and abandoned within their suchness?
Likewise, up to and including the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice, are they exhausted, detached from, ceased, and abandoned within their suchness?
"Is the suchness of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment exhausted,
detached from, ceased, or abandoned? Subhūti replied, "No!"
"No, World-Honored One! No, Sugata!"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in suchness in this way, they are training in the knowledge of all aspects.
Subhūti, you should know this!”
Suchness is inexhaustible, undivided, unceasing, and uninterrupted; it cannot be realized as an object.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in suchness in this manner, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
they are training in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature."
This is training in suchness up to the inconceivable realm; this is training in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
this is training in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
this is training in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; this is training in the eight liberations up to the ten totalities.
This is training in the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
this is training in the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma; this is training in all doors of dhāraṇī and doors of samādhi;
this is training in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; this is training in the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
The common dharmas are the training in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity;
they are the training in all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; they are the training in all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
and they are the training in the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the perfection of generosity up to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, you should know that they are training in the knowledge of all aspects."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they reach the ultimate perfection of all training; they cannot be overcome by any celestial Māras or any followers of external paths; they swiftly reach the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattvas; they practice that which was practiced by their own ancestors—the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas; they correctly follow and turn toward the protection of the Dharma; they are able to perform the deeds appropriate for one who has departed from darkness; they are well able to bring all sentient beings to maturity; and they are skillfully able to purify their own Buddha-field. This is called being well-trained in great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma with its three turnings and twelve aspects; they are training to establish hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder and lead them to parinirvāṇa; they are training in the sublime practice of not severing the lineage of the Buddhas; they are training in the opening of the gate of ambrosia by all Buddhas; they are training in establishing immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the vehicles of the Three Dharmas; they are training in manifesting the ultimate, quiescent, and truly unconditioned realm for all sentient beings. This is the training for the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna); those of inferior capacity cannot train in such a manner."
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to skillfully rescue all sentient beings from the great suffering of birth and death, they should train in this way.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they will certainly not fall into the realms of hell, animals, or the world of hungry ghosts; they will certainly not be born in border regions, among the Dàxù or Mièlìchē; they will certainly not be born into the families of caṇḍālas or pukkasas, nor into any other various impoverished, lowly, or undisciplined households. They will never be blind, deaf, mute, or crippled; their faculties will never be deficient; they will never be hunchbacked, epileptic, afflicted with boils, scabies, leprosy, hemorrhoids, or malignant sores. They will be neither too tall nor too short, neither too dark-skinned nor too pale, and will be free from all manner of foul, loathsome diseases and sores.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, in every birth they shall always obtain a perfect retinue; their physical appearance will be dignified and handsome, and their speech will be majestic and authoritative, such that all people love and respect them. In whatever place they are born, they will abstain from taking life up to and including wrong views; they will never embrace false or heterodox teachings, nor will they sustain themselves by means of such heterodox teachings. Furthermore, they will not accept those who break the precepts, hold evil views, or slander the Dharma as their friends."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they will never be born in the long-lived heavens of the gods who delight in pleasure and possess meager wisdom."

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*); by virtue of this power of skillful means, although they are able to repeatedly enter the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), they do not undergo rebirth under the influence of those states.

Because they are sustained by the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they achieve such skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) that, although they constantly attain mastery in entering and emerging from all meditative concentrations (*samādhi*), they do not, under the influence of those concentrations, take birth in the long-lived heavens (*dīrghāyuṣka-deva*) and thereby neglect the cultivation of the bodhisattva’s supreme and wondrous practices.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they attain purification in all the immeasurable and boundless sublime dharmas of the Buddhas, including the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."
"Because of its purity, one does not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“If all phenomena are pure by their very nature, how do bodhisattva mahāsattvas further attain purity regarding the sublime Dharma of the Buddhas?
The Buddha told Subhūti: “It is so! It is so!”
So it is! It is as you have said:
all phenomena are by their very nature pure from the beginning.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, within the original purity of all phenomena, diligently practices and studies the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, attaining realization according to reality without sinking or stagnation, and remaining far removed from all defilements and attachments; therefore, it is said that the bodhisattva further attains purification.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Although all phenomena are pure by nature, foolish ordinary beings do not know, see, or realize this.
Therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices generosity in order to cause them to know, see, and realize it."
They practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
they abide in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; they abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
they abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; and they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path.
They practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they practice the eight liberations up to the ten spheres of totality; they practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
they practice from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Stage of Dharma Clouds; and they practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
They cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity; they cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;
and they cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way in the fundamental purity of all phenomena, they attain purity in the Buddha’s ten powers, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, as well as other immeasurable and boundless buddha-dharmas; they do not fall into the stages of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.

Regarding the diverse mental activities of all sentient beings, he is able to penetrate them all to the ultimate further shore; through skillful means, he causes all sentient beings to realize the inherent purity of the nature of all phenomena and to attain the ultimate peace and bliss of nirvana.
“Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, on the great earth, precious things such as gold and silver appear in few places, whereas sand, stones, and rubble appear in many places. It is the same with all sentient beings: only a small portion are able to study the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, namely those bodhisattvas who abide in the Great Vehicle; most, however, study the dharmas of the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, namely those seeking their own benefit through the inferior and middling vehicles.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, among those in the human realm, only a small portion are able to cultivate the karma of a universal monarch (cakravartin), while the vast majority practice the karma of minor kings; so it is with all sentient beings: only a small portion are able to cultivate the path to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), while the vast majority practice the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that among the bodhisattvas who seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, few realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while many fall into the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that a person belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who does not distance themselves from the profound perfection of wisdom and skillful means will certainly enter the stage of non-retrogression.”
If one is devoid of skillful means regarding the profound perfection of wisdom, they will certainly regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattvas and wish to enter the ranks of those bodhisattvas who do not retrogress, should diligently practice and study the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), never allowing them to be neglected even for a moment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus trains in the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom,
they will never give rise to stinginess, greed, immoral conduct, anger, laziness, or distraction."
He does not give rise to a mind accompanied by agitation or unwholesome wisdom;
nor does he give rise to a mind accompanied by greed, hatred, delusion, or pride; nor does he give rise to a mind accompanied by negligence, error, or other faults;
nor does he give rise to a mind that clings to form, feeling, perception, or mental formations.

He does not give rise to a mind that accompanies consciousness and clings to it; nor does he give rise to a mind that accompanies the sense bases from the eye base up to the mind base and clings to them;
nor does he give rise to a mind that accompanies the sense fields from the form field up to the phenomena field and clings to them;
nor does he give rise to a mind that accompanies the elements from the eye element up to the mind element and cling to them; nor...
They do not give rise to a mind that clings to that which accompanies the form realm up to the dharma realm;
nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to that which accompanies the eye-consciousness realm up to the mental-consciousness realm;
nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to that which accompanies eye-contact up to mental-contact; nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to that which is conditioned by eye-contact...

Regarding all feelings born of conditions, up to and including all feelings born with mind-contact as condition, they do not give rise to a mind that clings to the earth element, nor to any clinging to the elements up to consciousness;
they do not give rise to a mind that clings to ignorance, nor to any clinging to the factors up to old age and death; they do not give rise to clinging.
They do not give rise to a mind attached to the practice of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
nor do they give rise to a mind attached to the practice of inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature;
nor do they give rise to a mind attached to the practice of suchness up to the inconceivable realm; nor do they...
They do not give rise to a mind that clings to and is associated with the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to and is associated with the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments;
nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to and is associated with the eight liberations up to the ten totalities.
Nor does he give rise to a mind that clings to the practice of the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
nor does he give rise to a mind that clings to the practice of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
nor does he give rise to a mind that clings to the practice of the stage of pure observation up to the stage of a Tathāgata.
Nor does he give rise to a mind attached to and associated with the stages from the Ground of Utmost Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma;
nor does he give rise to a mind attached to and associated with the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
nor does he give rise to a mind attached to and associated with the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor...
They do not give rise to a mind attached to that which is accompanied by the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics;
nor do they give rise to a mind attached to that which is accompanied by the qualities of non-forgetfulness and constant abiding in equanimity;
nor do they give rise to a mind attached to that which is accompanied by the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi. Furthermore, they do not...

They do not give rise to a mind that clings to being accompanied by omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to being accompanied by the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) up to the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddhabodhi*);
nor do they give rise to a mind that clings to being accompanied by any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Nor does he give rise to a mind that clings to the practice of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Why is this?

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, does not perceive any dharma that can be apprehended; since there is nothing to be apprehended, he does not give rise to a mind that clings to the practice of dharmas such as form and so forth.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 455. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Two, Chapter Sixty-Two (Part Two): "On Sameness. Furthermore, Subhūti:

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus trains in the profound perfection of wisdom, by the power of their skillful means and majestic virtue, they encompass all perfections, increase all perfections, and lead all perfections.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because within the profound perfection of wisdom all perfections are contained.

"Subhūti! Just as the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*) can fully contain all sixty-two views, so too is it with the profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*); it contains all the perfections."

"Subhūti! For example, just as when all who die their life-faculty ceases and all other faculties accordingly perish, so it is with the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā): the five perfections, such as generosity, all follow along with it. If there were no perfection of wisdom, there would likewise be no perfections at all."
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to reach the ultimate further shore of all pāramitās, they should train in this profound prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are the most honored and most supreme among all sentient beings."
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already been able to train in and study the supreme state.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"
"What do you think?
Are the sentient beings within this trichiliocosm many? Subhūti replied:
"The sentient beings within Jambudvīpa alone are already countless; how much more so must those in the trichiliocosm not be numerous!"
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said, Subhūti!

Suppose all the sentient beings in the trichiliocosm were to simultaneously attain human bodies; having attained human bodies, they were to simultaneously resolve upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and practice the deeds of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and having completed their practice, they were to simultaneously realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete buddhahood."

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, for the full duration of their lives, are able to provide offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, streamers, canopies, music, lamps, dwellings, bedding, food and drink, and medicines, thereby honoring, revering, respecting, and praising these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
"What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit? Subhūti replied:
“Very much so,
World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to constantly and joyfully hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, master, reflect upon according to principle, practice in accordance with the teaching, transcribe, and disseminate such profound prajñāpāramitā, the mass of merit they obtain will be infinitely many times greater than the former.”

Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses great purpose and function, enabling the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to stand as the foremost among all sentient beings; wishes to universally benefit all sentient beings; wishes to act as a protector for those without protection, a refuge for those without refuge, a destination for those without a destination, eyes for those without eyes, and light for those without light; wishes to show the correct path to those who have lost it, and to lead those who have not attained nirvāṇa to attain nirvāṇa—he should train in this profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; wishes to practice within the sphere of activity of the Tathāgatas; wishes to sport in the places where the Buddhas sport; wishes to let out the great lion’s roar of a Tathāgata; wishes to beat the unsurpassed Dharma drum of all Buddhas; wishes to strike the unsurpassed Dharma bell of all Buddhas; wishes to blow the unsurpassed Dharma conch of all Buddhas; wishes to ascend the unsurpassed Dharma throne of all Buddhas; wishes to proclaim the unsurpassed Dharma meaning of all Buddhas; wishes to resolve the net of doubts of all sentient beings; wishes to enter the wondrous nectar realm of all Buddhas; wishes to experience the subtle and sublime Dharma-bliss of all Buddhas; and wishes to realize the supreme merits of a Tathāgata—such a one should study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), there is no root of merit or virtue that they cannot encompass, and there is no root of merit or virtue that they cannot attain.”
"Why is this? It is because the profound perfection of wisdom is the locus upon which all kinds of meritorious virtues and roots of goodness depend.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed [the Buddha], saying:
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to study such profound prajñāpāramitā, can they thereby encompass and attain all the merits and roots of goodness of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva is also able to gather and attain all the merits and roots of goodness of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; yet, within these, he dwells in nothing and clings to nothing."

Having observed correctly with superior wisdom and vision, they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth; therefore, there is not a single root of merit or virtue that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not acquire.

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they will draw near to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they become a true field of merit for all the world—including its gods, humans, and asuras—surpassing the fields of merit of all worldly śramaṇas, brahmins, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas. They will swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*). In whatever place they are born, they will not abandon the perfection of wisdom, will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom, and will constantly practice the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, you should know that they have attained non-retrogression regarding all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), are able to correctly awaken to all phenomena, have distanced themselves from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and are close to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought as this:

‘This is the perfection of wisdom; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation; I am able to cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom; by means of this profound perfection of wisdom, I shall abandon those dharmas that ought to be abandoned, and I shall certainly realize the knowledge of all modes!’”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom, nor can they comprehend the perfection of wisdom. Why is this?
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not form such thoughts as:

"I am the *prajñāpāramitā*; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation; this is the cultivator; these are the phenomena from which the *prajñāpāramitā* is detached; these are the phenomena illuminated by the *prajñāpāramitā*; and this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by the *prajñāpāramitā*."
"If one knows in this way, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought:"

"This is not the perfection of wisdom; this is not the time for cultivation; this is not the place for cultivation; this is not the cultivator. It is not by means of the perfection of wisdom that one becomes remote from all dharmas that should be abandoned, nor is it by means of the perfection of wisdom that one is definitively able to realize the knowledge of all modes."

Why is this? Because all phenomena abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; herein, there is no differentiation whatsoever.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice in this way, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Chapter 63: Non-conceptualization, Part Two, Chapter Sixty-three: Non-conceptualization. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had this thought to himself:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity,
abides in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, abides in suchness up to the inconceivable realm,
and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, [and] practices...”
They practice the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
they cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; they cultivate the eight liberations up to the ten totalities;
they cultivate the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and they cultivate the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma.
They practice all *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates; they practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
they practice the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity; and they practice all-knowledge and the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
If even the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path and the practice for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—
which involve the knowledge of all aspects— already transcend all sentient beings, how much more so once one has attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment!

"If sentient beings, upon hearing the name of the knowledge of all modes, give rise to faith and understanding, they will already attain the excellent benefits of human life and the most supreme lifespan in the world; how much more so for those who resolve their minds upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, or who constantly hear such profound sūtras as this Prajñāpāramitā!

If any sentient beings are able to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and hear this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, all other sentient beings should aspire to rejoice in them, for the merit they obtain cannot be equaled by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having formed this thought, immediately took celestial flowers of exquisite sound and scattered them as an offering over the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and the assembly of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas.
Having scattered the flowers, they made this aspiration:

"If sons and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, by means of the roots of merit and virtue I have accumulated, may they swiftly bring to full completion all that they seek—the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma and the knowledge of all modes."

By means of the roots of merit and goodness accumulated by me, may they swiftly attain the perfection of the dharmas of the self-enlightened ones (pratyekabuddhas) and the true, untainted dharmas (anāsrava-dharma) that they seek.
By means of the roots of merit and goodness accumulated by me, may all the dharmas they wish to hear be swiftly and completely fulfilled.
"By the roots of merit and virtue I have accumulated, may those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the pratyekabuddhas also swiftly fulfill their aspirations.
Having made this vow, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are sons or daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who have already resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, I shall never, even for a single thought-moment, give rise to a contrary intention that would cause them to retreat from the mind of great bodhi.

I shall not give rise to even a single thought of a contrary intention that would cause the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas to become weary of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and to retreat and dwell on the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already conceived a desire for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I pray that their mind may further increase and advance, so that they may swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

May those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having witnessed the various sufferings within birth and death, give rise to various firm great vows for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others, [vowing]:
"Since I have already crossed the great ocean of birth and death myself, I shall also diligently cross over those who have not yet crossed."
Since I have already liberated myself from the fetters of birth and death, I shall also diligently strive to liberate those who are not yet liberated.
Since I have already attained peace and security amidst the various terrors of birth and death, I shall also diligently strive to bring peace and security to those who have not yet found it.
“Since I have personally realized ultimate *nirvāṇa*, I shall also diligently strive to cause those who have not yet realized it to likewise attain it.
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward the roots of goodness and merit of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has first resolved upon enlightenment, how much merit will they obtain?”

If one gives rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward the roots of merit and virtuous deeds of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have long since resolved their minds [on enlightenment], how much merit will they obtain?
If one gives rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward the roots of merit and virtuous deeds of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, how much merit will they obtain?
“If one gives rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward the roots of merit and wholesome qualities of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is bound to only one more birth, how much merit will be obtained?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
The number of the four great continents can be known, but the measure of the merit produced by the mind of sympathetic joy of these sons and daughters of good family cannot be known.

Kauśika! Even if one could know the number of two things within a trichiliocosm, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sons and daughters of good family who rejoice together cannot be known.

Kauśika! Suppose the trichiliocosm were a single great ocean, and someone were to take a single hair, split it into one hundred parts, and use the tip of one part to dip into the waters of that great ocean; the number of drops could be known, but the merit produced by the mind of sympathetic joy of these sons and daughters of good family is immeasurable and cannot be known.
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are sentient beings who do not rejoice in the roots of goodness and merits of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, one should know that they are all possessed by Māra.”
“World-Honored One!
