If there are sentient beings who do not rejoice in the meritorious roots of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, you should know that they are all part of the faction of Māra, the Evil One.”

"Bhagavān! If there are sentient beings who do not rejoice in the meritorious roots of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, you should know that they have all passed away from the realm of Māra and have come to be born here."

Why is this? If a bodhisattva mahāsattva seeks to proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening and cultivates the various practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, then any sentient beings who rejoice in and dedicate the roots of virtue and merits of those bodhisattva mahāsattvas will all be able to destroy all the armies, palaces, and retinues of Māra.
“World-Honored One!

If there are sentient beings who, with deep hearts of reverence and love, honor the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha Jewels, and who, wherever they are born, always desire to see the Buddha, always desire to hear the Dharma, and always desire to encounter the Sangha, they should give rise to sympathetic joy toward the merits and roots of goodness of all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
Having thus rejoiced, one should dedicate [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, yet should not give rise to notions of duality or non-duality.
If one can act in this way, one will swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings, and destroying the hosts of Māra.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said,

Kauśika! If sentient beings, with deep resolve, rejoice in the roots of goodness and virtues of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, those sentient beings will swiftly fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

If any sentient beings, with deep hearts, rejoice in the roots of virtue and merits of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, those sentient beings will possess great power; they will always be able to serve all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and spiritual friends, constantly hear the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā, and skillfully understand their meaning and intent.

Kauśika! These sentient beings, having accomplished such roots of goodness through the merit of sympathetic joy and dedication, will, in whatever place they are born, always be honored, revered, respected, and praised by all the worlds—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth. They shall not behold unpleasant forms, hear unpleasant sounds, smell unpleasant odors, taste unpleasant flavors, experience unpleasant tactile sensations, or contemplate unwholesome dharmas. They shall never be separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; passing from one Buddha-field to another, they shall draw near to the Buddhas, plant various roots of goodness, mature sentient beings, and adorn and purify Buddha-fields.
Why is this? "Kauśika!

These sentient beings are able to rejoice with a profound heart in the roots of merit and virtues of countless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have first resolved their minds toward awakening, and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

They are able to deeply rejoice in the roots of merit and virtuous deeds of the countless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in the first through the tenth stages, and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

One is able to deeply rejoice in the roots of merit and wholesome roots of countless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bound to one more birth, and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, the roots of goodness of all these sentient beings will increase, and they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

Having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they will be able to bring about true benefit and happiness for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings until the end of the future, causing them to abide in the realm of nirvana without remainder (*anupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇadhātu*).

For this reason, Kauśika, all sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should, with sympathetic joy, rejoice in the roots of merit and virtues of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have first resolved upon awakening, in those who have long since resolved, in those on the stage of non-retrogression, and in those bound to only one more birth; they should dedicate these toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

When rejoicing in [the merit of] arising and dedicating it, one should not cling to rejoicing and dedication as being identical to the mind or separate from the mind; one should not cling to practice as being identical to the mind or separate from the mind.

If one can thus remain without attachment, rejoicing in and dedicating [merit] while practicing the various deeds of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; one will be able to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings throughout the future, causing them all to abide in ultimate nirvāṇa.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

As the Buddha has taught, all dharmas are like illusions, even unto all dharmas being like magically conjured things. How can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of an illusory mind, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Do you perceive the illusory-like mind of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"I do not perceive illusion, nor do I perceive a mind that is like an illusion.
The Buddha said to Subhūti, "What do you think?"
"If there were no illusion and no mind that is like an illusion, would you see such a mind as being able to realize unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment? Subhūti replied, "No!"
"Bhagavān! I do not see any place where there is no illusion and no illusion-like mind, yet there is a mind capable of realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: “What do you think?
Apart from illusion and apart from a mind that is like an illusion, do you perceive any such dharma that can realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"I do not see any place apart from illusion or a mind that is like an illusion where there is any further dharma capable of realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!
World-Honored One!"
I do not perceive any dharma that is either identical to or separate from the mind; therefore, what dharma could I say exists or does not exist? For all dharmas are ultimately detached.
If all dharmas are ultimately detached, it is impossible to designate that "this dharma exists" or "this dharma does not exist."

If a phenomenon cannot be established as either existent or non-existent, then it cannot be said to be able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; for it is not the case that a non-existent phenomenon can realize enlightenment.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are non-existent; their intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended, being neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure. Why is this so?
“World-Honored One!
Because the *prajñāpāramitā* up to the *dānapāramitā* are ultimately detached;
because the *adhyātmaśūnyatā* up to the *abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā* are ultimately detached; because the *tathatā* up to [the *anupalambhaśūnyatā*]...”
Because the realm of thought is ultimately detached; because the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are ultimately detached;
because the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are ultimately detached;
because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the eight liberations are ultimately detached.
...up to the ten spheres of totality (*daśa-kṛtsnāyatana*), because they are ultimately detached; because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are ultimately detached;
because the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) up to the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) are ultimately detached;
because all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi are ultimately detached; [and] the five eyes...
Because the six supernormal powers are ultimately detached; because the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are ultimately detached;
because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity are ultimately detached;
and because omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are ultimately detached.
Because all practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are ultimately secluded, because the unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is ultimately secluded, and because the knowledge of all modes is ultimately secluded.
“World-Honored One!

If a dharma is ultimately detached, that dharma should not be cultivated, nor should it be discarded, nor should anything be brought forth by it. Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is also ultimately detached, one should not bring forth anything regarding dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

Since the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is ultimately detached, how can it be said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by relying on the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is also ultimately secluded; how could a dharma that is secluded realize a dharma that is secluded?
Therefore, it should be said that the perfection of wisdom cannot be described as realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Buddha said to Subhūti: “Excellent! Excellent!”
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā*, up to and including the *dānapāramitā*, is ultimately detached; likewise, everything up to the conduct of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is ultimately detached; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all buddhas is ultimately detached; and even the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is ultimately detached.

"Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity are ultimately secluded, it can be said that bodhisattva mahāsattvas realize the ultimately secluded unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

In this way, up to and including the ultimate seclusion of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one may say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes the ultimately secluded unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti! If the profound perfection of wisdom, up to and including the perfection of generosity, were not ultimately secluded, it would not be the perfection of wisdom, up to and including the perfection of generosity; likewise, up to and including if the knowledge of all aspects were not ultimately secluded, it would not be the knowledge of all aspects.

Subhūti, because the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity is ultimately secluded, it is designated as the "perfection of wisdom" up to the "perfection of generosity"; likewise, up to the point that the knowledge of all modes is ultimately secluded, it is designated as the "knowledge of all modes."
Therefore, Subhūti, it is not that bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not rely upon the profound perfection of wisdom to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti! Although it is not by means of a dharma that is detached that one can realize a dharma that is detached, yet one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; it is not without relying upon the profound perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should always diligently practice and study this profound perfection of wisdom.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The dharmas and meanings practiced by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are all exceedingly profound.”
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"

The dharmas and meanings practiced by all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are profoundly deep, difficult to see, and difficult to realize; they are beyond discursive thought and transcend the sphere of conceptualization, being personally realized within by those of subtle and secret wisdom, and incapable of being expressed in words.

"Subhūti, you should know that bodhisattva mahāsattvas perform what is difficult to do: although they practice such profound meanings of the Dharma, they do not realize the states of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha levels."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, there is nothing difficult for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to accomplish; one should not say that they are able to perform a difficult task.”

Why is this? Because the dharmas and meanings realized by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are entirely unapprehendable; the prajñāpāramitā that realizes them is also unapprehendable; and the dharma being realized, the one who realizes it, the place of realization, and the time of realization are likewise unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
Since all dharmas are found to be unobtainable when examined by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, what dharma-meaning could there be to be realized?
What *prajñāpāramitā* could there be to serve as the means of realization?”
Furthermore, what is there that can be designated as the dharma to be realized, the one who realizes, the place of realization, or the time of realization?
This being so, how can it be maintained that by means of this one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Even unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment cannot be realized, much less the dharmas of the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas!

World-Honored One, practicing in this manner is called the bodhisattva’s practice of non-apprehension; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice such a practice of non-apprehension, they will be without obstruction or hindrance regarding all dharmas.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing these words spoken, their mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, not distressed, not regretful, does not sink, and does not become despondent, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Bhagavan! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this manner, they do not perceive any signs; they do not perceive that 'I am practicing,' nor do they perceive 'not practicing. They do not perceive that the prajñāpāramitā is what they are practicing, nor do they perceive that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is what they are realizing. Furthermore, they do not perceive the time, the place, or any other such conditions of realization."
“World-Honored One!
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts as:
‘I am far from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.’”
“World-Honored One!
It is like space, which does not form the thought:
‘I am far from or near to those dharmas.’”
Why is this? Because space is without movement and without distinction, being free from conceptual differentiation.
It is in this same way that the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, without forming such thoughts:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.
“World-Honored One, it is as if, for example, an illusory person does not form such a thought:
‘The illusionary base, the illusionist, or the spectators are far from or near to me.’”
Why is this? Because the conjured person is without discrimination.
It is the same for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
For example, an image does not form the thought:
‘I am far from or near to my original substance or its basis.’”
Why is this? Because the manifested images are devoid of conceptual discrimination.
It is the same for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such thoughts as:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without conceptual discrimination regarding all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom have neither attachment nor aversion. Why is this?
Because in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, neither love nor hatred, nor the intrinsic nature of objects, can be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!

Just as all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have neither love nor hatred toward any phenomena, so too it is for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*: they likewise have neither love nor hatred toward any phenomena.”
Why is this? Because the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have severed both attachment and aversion regarding the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]

Just as all conceptualization, various conceptualizations, and pervasive conceptualizations have been utterly severed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, so too it is with the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom: all conceptualization, various conceptualizations, and pervasive conceptualizations have been utterly severed.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is non-discriminatory toward all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!...”
Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not form this thought:
"I am far from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
"So too it is for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such thoughts as:
'I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and I am near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.'"
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!...”
Just as those who are emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not form this thought:
"I am far from the levels of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; I am near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their emanations are without conceptual discrimination.
It is likewise for Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
Just as when the Buddhas and others wish to perform some task, they manifest a transformation being and have that being perform that task, yet the manifested being does not form this thought:
‘I am able to carry out such a deed.’”
Why is this? Because those who are emanated have no conceptual discrimination regarding the actions they perform.

It is just so with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*: although one diligently cultivates it for a specific purpose, and once cultivated it can accomplish the task at hand, yet there is no conceptual discrimination regarding that which is accomplished.
Why is this? Because it is the nature of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to be without conceptual discrimination regarding phenomena.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

It is like a skilled craftsman or his apprentice who, for some purpose, constructs various mechanical devices—whether female or male figures, or elephants, horses, and the like. Although these mechanical devices perform their respective functions, they possess no discrimination regarding those activities.
Why is this? Because the nature of a mechanical device is inherently non-conceptual.

It is the same with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*: it is established for a specific purpose, and once established, although it can accomplish what is to be done and what is to be taught, within it there is no conceptualization whatsoever.
"Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is, by its very nature, non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed Subhūti, saying:

“Is it only the perfection of wisdom that is without conceptual differentiation, or are the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity also without conceptual differentiation?”

Subhūti replied, “It is not only the perfection of wisdom that is without conceptual differentiation; the perfections of concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are likewise without conceptual differentiation.”

Śāriputra said: "Is it only the six pāramitās that are without conceptual differentiation, or are form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness also without conceptual differentiation?
Or are the sense bases, from the eye base up to the mind base, also without conceptual differentiation?"
The sphere of form up to the sphere of mental phenomena is also without conceptual differentiation; the eye-element up to the mind-element is also without conceptual differentiation;
the form-element up to the mental-phenomena-element is also without conceptual differentiation;
the eye-consciousness-element up to the mind-consciousness-element is also without conceptual differentiation; and the eye-contact up to the mind-contact is also without conceptual differentiation.
There is no conceptual differentiation regarding the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition;

there is no conceptual differentiation regarding the earth element, up to and including the consciousness element; there is no conceptual differentiation regarding ignorance, up to and including old age and death;
and there is no conceptual differentiation regarding inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature.
There is no conceptual differentiation; even with respect to suchness up to the inconceivable realm, there is no conceptual differentiation.

Even with respect to the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, there is no conceptual differentiation. Even with respect to the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, there is no conceptual differentiation.
Even with respect to the eight liberations up to the ten spheres of totality, there is no conceptual differentiation.
Furthermore, there is no conceptual differentiation regarding the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path;
there is no conceptual differentiation regarding the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;

there is no conceptual differentiation regarding the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; and there is no conceptual differentiation regarding the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the Dharma-cloud.
It is non-conceptual; it is non-conceptual with respect to all *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates;

it is non-conceptual with respect to the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; it is non-conceptual with respect to the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
and it is non-conceptual with respect to the quality of non-forgetfulness and the constant abiding in equanimity.

Intrinsic nature is also without conceptual differentiation; omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are also without conceptual differentiation;
the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are also without conceptual differentiation;

the conduct of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also without conceptual differentiation; and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is also without conceptual differentiation.

"Bodhi is also without conceptual differentiation; the conditioned realm is also without conceptual differentiation, and the unconditioned realm is also without conceptual differentiation? Subhūti replied:

"Not only are the six pāramitās non-conceptual, but form is also non-conceptual; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also non-conceptual; even the conditioned realm is non-conceptual, and the unconditioned realm is also non-conceptual."

Śāriputra said: "If all phenomena are entirely without conceptual differentiation, how can one differentiate the distinctions among the five destinies, namely: this is the hell realm, this is the animal realm, this is the realm of hungry ghosts, this is the human realm, and this is the celestial realm?"

How does one differentiate the distinctions among noble ones—namely, that this is a stream-enterer, this is a once-returner, this is a non-returner, this is an arhat, this is a pratyekabuddha, this is a bodhisattva, and this is a tathāgata?

Subhūti replied: "Sentient beings, due to the causes and conditions of their inverted afflictions, initiate various actions of body, speech, and mind. By means of these, they bring about the ripening fruit of karma rooted in desire; based upon this, the distinctions between the five destinies—hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and gods—are established."
Furthermore, regarding your question, "How are the distinctions among the noble ones differentiated?
Śāriputra, it is because they are non-conceptual that the designation of "stream-enterer" and the "fruit of stream-entry" is established.
Because they are non-conceptual, one designates the once-returner and the fruit of once-returning;
because they are non-conceptual, one designates the non-returner and the fruit of non-returning;
because they are non-conceptual, one designates the arhat and the fruit of arhatship.
Because they are non-conceptual, one designates the Pratyekabuddha and the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha;
because they are non-conceptual, one designates the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and the conduct of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva;
because they are non-conceptual, one designates the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Śāriputra! Because past Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were without conceptualization and had severed conceptualization, various distinctions can be provisionally established;

likewise, because future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas will also be without conceptualization and will have severed conceptualization, various distinctions can be provisionally established.”

Likewise, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions are also without conceptual discrimination, for discrimination has been severed; yet, various distinctions may be provisionally established.

Śāriputra! By this cause and condition, you should know that all phenomena are without discrimination, because the non-discriminatory *tathatā*, the *dharmadhātu*, and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), serve as the definitive standard.
“Śāriputra! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice this profound *prajñāpāramitā* which is free from conceptual differentiation.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva can practice this profound *prajñāpāramitā* free from conceptual differentiation, they will be able to realize the non-conceptual, subtle, and unsurpassed *samyak-saṃbodhi*, awakening to the non-conceptual nature of all phenomena and bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings until the end of the future.”
Chapter 64: On the Firm and the Non-firm, Part Two, Section One of Chapter Sixty-four: "On the Firm and the Non-firm. At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, do they practice a firm dharma?"
“Is it that they practice non-solid dharmas?
Subhūti replied, “When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they practice non-solid dharmas; they do not practice solid dharmas.”
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because the perfection of wisdom, up to and including the perfection of generosity, are not solid phenomena. Internally...
Because emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, is not a solid dharma;
because suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is not a solid dharma; because the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are not solid dharmas;
because the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are not solid dharmas; [and] the four meditative concentrations, the four [immeasurables]...
Because the [four] immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not enduring phenomena; because the eight liberations up to the ten totalities are not enduring phenomena;
because the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not enduring phenomena;
because the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma are not enduring phenomena; and because all the gateways of dhāraṇī and the three...
Because the doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) are not solid phenomena; because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) are not solid phenomena;
because the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) are not solid phenomena;

because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) are not solid phenomena; [and] because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and all-...
Because the knowledge of marks is not a solid phenomenon; because all the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are not solid phenomena;
because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is not a solid phenomenon; and because the knowledge of all modes is not a solid phenomenon.

Why is this? When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not perceive even that which is non-solid as being obtainable within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, much less do they perceive anything solid as being obtainable!

In this way, even when practicing the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), one does not perceive even the slightest lack of solidity within that knowledge of all modes, much less perceive any solidity therein!
At that time, immeasurable devas of the desire and form realms all had this thought:

"Those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and are able to give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, practicing according to the meaning as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, yet do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) or the nature of equality, and do not fall into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas—for these reasons, these sons and daughters of good family are most rare and perform what is difficult to do; they are worthy of veneration."
At that time, Subhūti, knowing the thoughts in the minds of those devas, addressed them, saying:

"It is not at all rare, nor is it difficult, for these sons and daughters of good family not to realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) within the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) of equality, and thus not to fall into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all phenomena and all sentient beings are unapprehendable, yet gives rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, dons the armor of diligence, and vows to deliver immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, causing them to enter the realm of nirvana without remainder—this bodhisattva mahāsattva is truly most rare, for they are able to perform what is difficult to do.
“O devas, you should know!

Although a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that sentient beings do not exist at all, they nevertheless resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and don the armor of diligence with the desire to discipline all classes of sentient beings—just as if one were desiring to discipline empty space.”
Why is this? Because space is detached, one should know that all sentient beings are also detached;
because space is empty, one should know that all sentient beings are also empty.
Because space is not solid or substantial, one should know that all sentient beings are likewise not solid or substantial;
because space is non-existent, one should know that all sentient beings are likewise non-existent.
For this reason, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are truly most rare and are able to perform what is difficult to do.
"O devas, you should know!

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas don the armor of great compassion, desiring to subdue all sentient beings; yet, since no sentient beings exist at all, it is as if they were donning armor to battle with space."
“O devas, you should know!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the armor of great compassion (mahākaruṇā) for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings; yet both those sentient beings and the armor of great compassion are ultimately unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because sentient beings are detached, one should know that this armor of great compassion is also detached;
because sentient beings are empty, one should know that this armor of great compassion is also empty.
Because sentient beings are not solid, this armor of great compassion should be known as not solid;
because sentient beings do not exist, this armor of great compassion should be known as non-existent.
“O devas, you should know!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s activity of taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness to all sentient beings is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because sentient beings are detached, empty, insubstantial, and non-existent, one should know that these matters of taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness are likewise detached, empty, insubstantial, and non-existent.
“O devas, you should know!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent. Why is this?
Because sentient beings are detached, empty, insubstantial, and non-existent, one should know that the bodhisattva is likewise detached, empty, insubstantial, and non-existent.
"O devas, you should know!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such matters as these, does not become startled, alarmed, terrified, distressed, regretful, despondent, or submerged, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."

"Why is that? Because the detachment from all forms is the detachment from sentient beings; the detachment from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the detachment from sentient beings;

the detachment from the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind is the detachment from sentient beings; and the detachment from the sense base of forms up to the sense base of phenomena is [the detachment from sentient beings]."
That is, the detachment of sentient beings; the detachment of the eye-element up to the mind-element is the detachment of sentient beings;

the detachment of the form-element up to the phenomena-element is the detachment of sentient beings; the detachment of the eye-consciousness-element up to the mind-consciousness-element is the detachment of sentient beings;
the detachment of eye-contact up to mind-contact is the detachment of sentient beings; [and that which arises] conditioned by eye-contact...
The arising of all sensations, up to and including those sensations produced with mental contact as a condition, is the detachment from sentient beings;

the earth element, up to and including the consciousness element, is the detachment from sentient beings; the causal conditions, up to and including the dominant conditions, are the detachment from sentient beings;
ignorance, up to and including old age and death, is the detachment from sentient beings; the perfection of giving...
The detachment from the *pāramitās*, up to and including the *prajñāpāramitā*, is itself the detachment from sentient beings;

the detachment from the emptinesses, from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is itself the detachment from sentient beings; the detachment from suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is itself the detachment from sentient beings;
and the detachment from the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, is itself the detachment from sentient beings.
The four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are detached from sentient beings;
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are detached from sentient beings; the eight liberations up to the ten totalities are detached from sentient beings;
and the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are detached from sentient beings.
The detachment from sentient beings is the detachment from the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata;
the detachment from the Joyous Stage up to the Cloud of Dharma Stage is the detachment from sentient beings;

the detachment from all doors of dhāraṇī and doors of samādhi is the detachment from sentient beings; and the detachment from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers is the detachment from sentient beings.
The Tathāgata’s ten powers, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are detached from sentient beings;
the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks are detached from sentient beings;
the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity are detached from sentient beings; omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and all...

The detachment from the marks of wisdom is the detachment from sentient beings; the detachment from the fruit of stream-entry up to the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the detachment from sentient beings;
the detachment from all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the detachment from sentient beings;

the detachment from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of the Buddhas is the detachment from sentient beings; and the detachment from the knowledge of all modes is the detachment from sentient beings.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 456. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Second Division, Chapter Sixty-Four Part Two: "The Firm and the Non-firm. "O devas, you should know!

The detachment from all forms is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the detachment from all forms is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes; the detachment from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes.
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment of the sense bases of the eye is itself the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, up to: the detachment of the sense bases of the eye is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*); the detachment of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment from the sense-bases of form is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the detachment from the sense-bases of form is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the detachment from the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment of the eye-element is itself the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements is itself the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, up to the detachment of the eye-element is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the detachment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know this!

The detachment from the realm of forms is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from the realms of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the detachment from the realm of forms is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all modes; the detachment from the realms of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all modes.”
"O devas, you should know!

The detachment of the eye-consciousness element is itself the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements is itself the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to the point that the detachment of the eye-consciousness element is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and the detachment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes."
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment from all eye-contact is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the detachment from all eye-contact is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*); the detachment from ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

All feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, even up to this: all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are detached from the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*); all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are detached from the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment from the earth element is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to the point that the detachment from the earth element is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the detachment from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes.”
"O devas, you should know!

The separation from all causal conditions is the separation from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the separation from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition is the separation from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the separation from all causal conditions is the separation from the knowledge of all modes; the separation from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition is the separation from the knowledge of all modes."
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment from ignorance is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from volitional formations up to aging and death is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to the point that the detachment from ignorance is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*), and the detachment from volitional formations up to aging and death is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all aspects.”
“O gods, you should know this!

The detachment of the various *pāramitās* of giving is the detachment of inner emptiness, up to and including the detachment of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*). The detachment of the *pāramitās* of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is the detachment of inner emptiness, up to and including the detachment of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature. In this way, up to and including the detachment of the various *pāramitās* of giving is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and the detachment of the *pāramitās* of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know this!

The detachment of the various internal emptinesses is itself the detachment of the *pāramitās*, from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the detachment of the *pāramitās*, from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, up to the point that the detachment of the various internal emptinesses is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the detachment of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O gods, you should know!

That which is the detachment of all *tathatā* (suchness) is the detachment of the *pāramitās*, from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom; that which is the detachment of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm) up to the inconceivable realm is the detachment of the *pāramitās*, from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom. Thus, even unto the detachment of all *tathatā* is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and the detachment of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
"O devas, you should know!

The noble truth of suffering is detached from, and thus detached from, the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are detached from, and thus detached from, the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, up to: the noble truth of suffering is detached from, and thus detached from, all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna); the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are detached from, and thus detached from, all-knowledge."
“O gods, you should know!

The four applications of mindfulness are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to this point, the four applications of mindfulness are detached from the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are detached from the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The four dhyānas are detached from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are detached from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the four dhyānas are detached from the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are detached from the knowledge of all modes.”
"O devas, you should know this!

The detachment from the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) is the detachment from the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). The detachment from the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive meditative attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to the point that the detachment from the eight liberations is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā), and the detachment from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is the detachment from the knowledge of all modes."
"O devas, you should know!

The detachment from the gates of liberation of emptiness is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, even up to: the detachment from the gates of liberation of emptiness is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); the detachment from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the detachment from the knowledge of all aspects."
“O devas, you should know this!

The detachment of the stage of pure observation (*śuddhādhyāśaya-bhūmi*) from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom is itself the detachment of the stage of lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*) up to the stage of the Tathāgata from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. In this same way, up to the point that the detachment of the stage of pure observation from omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) is itself the detachment of the stage of lineage up to the stage of the Tathāgata from omniscience.”
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment of the Stage of Utmost Joy from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom is itself the detachment; the detachment of the Stage of Stainless up to the Stage of Dharma-Cloud from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom is itself the detachment. Likewise, up to the detachment of the Stage of Utmost Joy from the knowledge of all modes is itself the detachment; the detachment of the Stage of Stainless up to the Stage of Dharma-Cloud from the knowledge of all modes is itself the detachment.”
“O devas, you should know this!

The detachment of the various *dhāraṇī* gates is the detachment of the *pāramitās*, from the *dāna-pāramitā* up to the *prajñā-pāramitā*. The detachment of the *samādhi* gates is the detachment of the *pāramitās*, from the *dāna-pāramitā* up to the *prajñā-pāramitā*. In this way, even up to the detachment of all *dhāraṇī* gates, which is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), and the detachment of the *samādhi* gates, which is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The detachment of the five eyes is the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the detachment of the six superknowledges is the detachment of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to this point, the detachment of the five eyes is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes; the detachment of the six superknowledges is the detachment of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know this!

The ten powers of the Tathāgatas are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to this point, the ten powers of the Tathāgatas are detached from the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are detached from the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The absence of the thirty-two marks of a great man is the absence of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the absence of the eighty secondary signs is the absence of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to the point that the absence of the thirty-two marks of a great man is the absence of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), and the absence of the eighty secondary signs is the absence of the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

The dharmas of non-forgetfulness are detached from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is detached from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, up to: the dharmas of non-forgetfulness are detached from the knowledge of all modes; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is detached from the knowledge of all modes.”
“O devas, you should know!

That which is the detachment of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is the detachment of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). That which is the detachment of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is the detachment of the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom. In this way, up to: that which is the detachment of all-knowledge is the detachment of the knowledge of all-knowledge; that which is the detachment of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the detachment of the knowledge of all-knowledge.”
“O devas, you should know!

The fruit of stream-entry is detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the fruit of once-returning up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, up to the point that the fruit of stream-entry is detached from all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and the fruit of once-returning up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is detached from all-knowledge.”
“O devas, you should know!

The practice of detachment by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the detachment from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; likewise, it is the detachment from everything up to the detachment from the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
"O devas, you should know this!

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is detached from the perfection of giving, up to and including the perfection of wisdom; likewise, it is detached from everything up to and including the detachment from the knowledge of all modes."
“O gods, you should know!

That which is the detachment of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is the detachment of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), up to and including the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Likewise, up to and including that which is the detachment of all-knowledge is the detachment of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi) of all Buddhas.”
“O devas, you should know!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing it said that all dharmas are without anything not to be relinquished, their mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, not sorrowful, not regretful, does not sink, and does not despair—you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”
At that time, the Blessed One addressed Subhūti, saying:
"For what reason and by what causal conditions do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas neither sink nor become despondent regarding the profound perfection of wisdom?"
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Because all dharmas are non-existent, because they are detached, because they are quiescent, because they are nothingness, and because they are without arising or ceasing, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not sink or become despondent regarding the profound perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
By means of these various causes and conditions, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not sink or become despondent regarding the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

Why is this? Because for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, regarding all phenomena—whether that which causes one to sink, that which is sunk, the time of sinking, the place where one sinks, or the one who sinks—all these cannot be apprehended through such sinking, because all phenomena are unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such an exposition as this, does not become startled, terrified, or afraid, and does not feel sorrow, regret, despondency, or discouragement, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that all phenomena are unapprehendable and cannot be conceptually designated; namely, that which causes one to sink, that which is sunk, the time of sinking, the place of sinking, and the one who sinks by means of this sinking.
For this reason, when the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear such a teaching, their minds are not startled, not terrified, not afraid, not distressed, not remorseful, not dejected, and not submerged.
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this manner, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, Mahābrahmā, and the Lords of Beings will constantly pay him homage together.”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will not only be constantly honored and venerated by Śakra, the Lord of Devas, Mahābrahmā, and the Lords of Beings; these bodhisattva mahāsattvas will also be constantly honored and venerated by those who have transcended this realm, such as the gods of the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, and all other hosts of devas."

Furthermore, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are constantly protected and remembered by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently preaching the Dharma in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions.
“Subhūti, you should know that because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way,
they will swiftly bring to full completion the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom.”
They also cause the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature to be swiftly perfected;
they also cause true thusness up to the inconceivable realm to be swiftly perfected; they also cause the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path to be swiftly perfected;
and they also cause the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path to be swiftly perfected.
They attain fulfillment, and they also cause the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions to be swiftly fulfilled;
they also cause the eight liberations up to the ten totalities to be swiftly fulfilled;
they also cause the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—to be swiftly fulfilled; and they also cause the Ground of Extreme Joy to be swiftly fulfilled.
They will swiftly attain full perfection up to the stage of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*);
they will also cause all gateways of dhāraṇī and gateways of samādhi to be swiftly perfected; they will also cause the five eyes and the six supernormal powers to be swiftly perfected;
and they will also cause the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), to be swiftly perfected.
They also cause the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity to be swiftly perfected;
they also cause omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects to be swiftly perfected;
they also cause all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to be swiftly perfected; and they also cause the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas [to be swiftly attained].
They will swiftly attain fulfillment, and they will also cause the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) to be swiftly fulfilled.

"Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in this way, they are constantly protected and remembered by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they will swiftly fulfill all meritorious qualities. Because such a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the sphere of action appropriate for a Buddha and correctly practices the conduct of a Buddha, this bodhisattva is like a Buddha, a World-Honored One."

“Subhūti, you should know that the mind of this bodhisattva mahāsattva is firm and steadfast. Even if all sentient beings in as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges were to become evil Māras, and each of those evil Māras were further to manifest as just as many evil Māras—all these evil Māras possessing immeasurable and boundless supernormal powers—even with all their supernatural might, these evil Māras could not obstruct this bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor prevent him from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor stop him from realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already attained the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and have realized that all phenomena are ungraspable.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes two dharmas, no evil Māras will be able to create obstacles, preventing them from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
What are these two?
First, contemplating that all phenomena are ultimately empty.
Second, not abandoning any sentient beings.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes two dharmas, no evil Māras will be able to create obstacles, preventing them from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
What are these two? First, they are able to accomplish everything exactly as it has been taught.
Second, they are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this way, the devas and other celestial beings will constantly come to pay homage, draw near to offer worship, inquire, and exhort them, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Mahāsattva!
If you wish to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, you should diligently abide in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is this so?"
"O Great Being!

If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva diligently abides in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, they can act as a protector for all sentient beings who have no protector; they can act as a refuge for those who have no refuge; they can act as a rescuer for those who have no rescuer; they can act as a destination for those who have no destination; they can act as an island for those who have no island; they can act as a dwelling for those who have no dwelling; they can provide light to those in darkness; and they can provide eyes and ears to those who are deaf and blind."
Why is this? O Mahāsattva!

To abide thus in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness is itself to dwell securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; if one can dwell securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can abide in this way within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then when the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently residing in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions preach the true Dharma amidst their great assemblies, they will spontaneously rejoice and proclaim the name, clan, and various merits of that bodhisattva mahāsattva—namely, the subtle and wondrous merits of abiding in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

just as I now proclaim the profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the assembly, I spontaneously rejoice before this great multitude and extol and praise the names, lineages, and various merits of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas such as Ratnaketu and Uṣṇīṣa, as well as those other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who currently dwell in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha, purifying their brahma-conduct and abiding in the *prajñāpāramitā*. These are the subtle and sublime merits of those who abide in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

At present, in all the Buddha-worlds of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas proclaim the profound Prajñāpāramitā to the assemblies; therein also dwell Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have purified their conduct and abide in the Prajñāpāramitā.

Each of those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, in the presence of their respective assemblies, spontaneously and joyfully proclaimed and praised the names, lineages, and various merits of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—namely, the subtle and wondrous merits of abiding in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

In the Buddha-worlds of the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir—worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas proclaim the profound Prajñāpāramitā to the assemblies; therein also dwell Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have purified their conduct and abide in the Prajñāpāramitā.

Each of those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, in the presence of their respective assemblies, spontaneously and joyfully proclaimed and praised the names, lineages, and various merits of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—namely, the subtle and wondrous merits of abiding in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Subhūti, you should know that there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), gradually perfecting the path to great awakening and gradually perfecting the profound perfection of wisdom, until they attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna). Furthermore, when all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges are preaching the true Dharma, they will spontaneously rejoice and praise the names, lineages, and various merits of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas before the great assemblies—namely, the subtle and wondrous merits of practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to perform what is difficult: they do not sever the lineage of the Buddhas and bring great benefit to sentient beings.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, which bodhisattva mahāsattvas,

when the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas preach the sublime Dharma, have their names, clans, and various merits spontaneously proclaimed, extolled, and praised before the great assembly— those who are in the stage of non-retrogression or those in the stage of retrogression?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abiding in the stage of non-retrogression who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, have their names, clans, and various merits spontaneously proclaimed, extolled, and praised by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas when they preach the true Dharma before great assemblies."

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have not yet received their prediction, practice the perfection of wisdom; when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha teaches the sublime Dharma, he spontaneously rejoices and extols their names, clans, and various merits before the great assembly.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Who is this bodhisattva of whom you have spoken?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who train by following the conduct of Akṣobhya when he was a bodhisattva; having already attained stable abiding on the stage of non-retrogression, when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas teach the sublime Dharma before the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, they naturally rejoice and extol his name, lineage, and various merits in the midst of the great assembly.”

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who train by following the conduct of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as Ratnaketu and Śikhin; although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet received their prediction, they practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* with diligent vigor, and when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha teaches the true Dharma, he spontaneously rejoices and extols their names, clans, and various merits before the great assembly.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; although they have deep faith and understanding regarding the non-arising nature of all phenomena,
they have not yet realized the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) within this profound perfection of wisdom."
Although they have deep faith and understanding in the pāramitās, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti);
although they have deep faith and understanding in the ultimate emptiness of all phenomena, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
although they have deep faith and understanding in the quiescent nature of all phenomena, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena. At [this stage],...

Although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are by nature detached, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*);
although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are by nature illusory, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are by nature empty, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena.

Although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are non-existent in nature, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*);
although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena lack self-mastery in nature, they have not yet attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are not solid or substantial in nature, they have not yet attained [the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena].
The patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena. "Subhūti!

When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha teaches the sublime Dharma, he likewise naturally rejoices and extols the names, clans, and various merits of such bodhisattva mahāsattvas before the great assembly."

"Subhūti! If, when the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas preach the sublime Dharma, they spontaneously rejoice and extol the names, clans, and various merits of a bodhisattva mahāsattva before the great assembly, that bodhisattva mahāsattva has transcended the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, and when the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas preach the true Dharma, they spontaneously rejoice before the great assembly and extol and praise his name, clan, and various merits, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will certainly abide in the stage of non-retrogression; having abided in this stage, he will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing this teaching of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, have no doubt, no confusion, no delusion, and no distress regarding its meaning and intent, but instead think:
'As the Buddha has taught this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, its principle is necessarily so and is certainly free from error.'"

These sons and daughters of good family, through hearing the *prajñāpāramitā*, will give rise to profound pure faith; they shall gradually hear the *prajñāpāramitā* extensively from the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha and the various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and will develop deep faith and understanding in its meaning and intent.

"Once they have attained such faith and understanding, they shall abide on the stage of non-retrogression; having abided on this stage, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Subhūti!"

If these sons and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle merely hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and without doubt or confusion, without delusion or error, develop deep faith and understanding, and do not engage in slander, they shall yet obtain immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous roots of goodness; how much more so for those who can receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it, contemplating and reflecting upon it by means of the principle of *tathatā* (suchness), and dwelling in *tathatā* with diligent cultivation!

These sons and daughters of good family shall swiftly abide in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Since the true nature of all phenomena is ultimately unapprehendable, how can it be said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, dwelling in suchness, diligently practice and train, will swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"Just as a transformation being created by a Buddha abides in suchness while practicing the bodhisattva path, they will swiftly abide in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."

So too it is with all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: dwelling securely in suchness while practicing the bodhisattva path, they shall swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"That which is emanated by the Tathāgata is entirely non-existent, and a phenomenon apart from suchness is also unobtainable; who then abides in suchness to cultivate the bodhisattva practice?"
Who will abide in the stage of non-retrogression?
Who will realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Who will turn the wheel of Dharma, preach what Dharma, and deliver what assembly?

"Bhagavān! Since even suchness cannot be apprehended, how much less could there be one who, abiding in suchness, practices the bodhisattva path, swiftly dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turns the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings?"
"If this were truly existent, it would be impossible.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "It is so!"
"So it is! It is as you have said.
That which is emanated by the Tathāgata does not exist at all; even dharmas apart from suchness cannot be found. Who, then, could abide in suchness to cultivate the bodhisattva practice?"
Who will abide in the stage of non-retrogression?
Who will realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Who will turn the wheel of Dharma, preach what Dharma, and deliver what assembly?

Subhūti! Since even suchness cannot be apprehended, how much less could there be one who dwells in suchness to practice the bodhisattva path, who would swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings?
If this were truly existent, it would be impossible. Why is that? Subhūti!
Whether Buddhas appear in the world or do not appear, the nature of all phenomena remains as it is, never departing from suchness, and so on, up to the inconceivable realm. Subhūti!
It is certain that there is no abiding in suchness while practicing the bodhisattva path, nor, as explained at length, bringing sentient beings to liberation.
Why is this, Subhūti?
The suchness of all phenomena is without arising and without cessation, nor can even the slightest portion of abiding or alteration be found. Subhūti!
If a phenomenon is without arising and without cessation, and not even the slightest portion of abiding or alteration can be found, who would abide therein to practice the bodhisattva path?
Who will abide in the stage of non-retrogression?
