those with impaired wisdom abide in the aggregate of wisdom (*prajñāskandha*); those without liberation abide in the aggregate of liberation (*vimuktiskandha*); and those without the knowledge and vision of liberation abide...
Abiding in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, those who have not yet seen the truths should train in the perfection of wisdom in order to attain the fruit of a stream-enterer,
or the fruit of a once-returner, or the fruit of a non-returner, or the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha,
or else to gradually realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to train in the sublime deportment of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—so that all sentient beings, upon beholding it, never tire of looking and thereby eliminate evil and give rise to goodness—they should train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they form this thought:

'When shall I attain the gaze of a dragon-elephant, with a solemn and dignified bearing as I preach the Dharma to the assembly; when shall my actions of body, speech, and mind all follow wisdom and be entirely pure; and while walking in meditation, when shall my feet not touch the ground for a distance of four finger-widths?'"
"To accomplish this matter, one should train in the *prajñāpāramitā*.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*, forms such a thought:"

"When shall I be surrounded by a retinue of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of gods from the Realm of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmakāyika-sabhā Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara-śuddha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, so that they may come to the Bodhi tree as my attendants?"

"May these hosts of devas prepare a seat of celestial raiment beneath the Bodhi tree; upon this seat, may I sit cross-legged and, with my hand adorned with all manner of wondrous marks, touch the great earth, causing the Earth Goddess and her retinue to appear simultaneously to subdue the hosts of Māra and realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. From that time forth, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, may every place where I am located become adamantine?"
"To accomplish this matter, one should study the *prajñāpāramitā*.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the *prajñāpāramitā* forms this thought: 'When shall I abandon my kingdom and go forth into homelessness?

On that very day, may I realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; on that very day, may I turn the sublime wheel of Dharma; and on that very day, may immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings become free from dust and free from defilement, giving rise to the pure Dharma-eye.'"

Furthermore, you cause immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings to forever exhaust all outflows, attaining liberation through both mind and wisdom; you also cause immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings to attain non-retrogression in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
"To accomplish this matter, one should train in the *prajñāpāramitā*.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the *prajñāpāramitā* forms this thought:

'When shall I attain unsurpassed enlightenment, with immeasurable and incalculable śrāvakas and bodhisattvas as my assembly of disciples, such that at the time of a single teaching, immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, without rising from their seats, shall become arhats;'"
Furthermore, how can one cause immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, without rising from their seats, to attain non-retrogression in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
To accomplish this matter, one should study the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) forms this thought: 'When shall I attain an inexhaustible lifespan and boundless radiance, adorned with the marks and signs such that those who behold me never tire;

and even when walking, may a thousand-petaled lotus support each of my feet, causing a thousand-spoked wheel to appear upon the ground as I lift my steps and traverse the earth; and though the great earth trembles, may I not disturb the sentient beings dwelling therein; and when I wish to turn back, may my entire body rotate; and wherever my feet tread, may they reach as far as the vajra-limit, with the ground turning beneath them like the circumference of a chariot wheel; and from every limb and joint of my body, may light be emitted, illuminating the infinite worlds of the ten directions, and wherever it shines, may I bring great benefit to all sentient beings?'"
"To accomplish this matter, one should train in the *prajñāpāramitā*.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the *prajñāpāramitā* forms this thought:

'When I attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, may there not be even the names of any greed, hatred, or delusion in the land where I dwell; may the sentient beings therein achieve sublime wisdom, and by the power of that wisdom, engage in such reflection:'"

Practicing generosity, self-discipline, patience, diligence, tranquility, and discernment; remaining free from negligence and diligently cultivating the holy life; and maintaining loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity without harming sentient beings—how excellent this would be, just like other Buddha-fields!
"Once the work of transformation is complete and after his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall have no time of extinction, and he will constantly bring great benefit to sentient beings.
To accomplish this matter, one should study the Prajñāpāramitā.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, forms this thought:

'When I attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings in immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who hear my name, necessarily attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.'"
"To accomplish these matters, one should study the Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain these immeasurable and boundless, preeminent qualities should study the Prajñāpāramitā."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 479. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three: The Chapter on Śāriputra, Second, Part Two. "Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and has already been able to bring forth such merits,
at that time, the Four Great Kings of the trichiliocosm will leap for joy and think:
"We should now offer four bowls to this bodhisattva, just as the heavenly kings of old offered bowls to the previous Buddhas."
At that time, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin heavens within this trichiliocosm leaped for joy and thought:
"We should all attend upon and make offerings to such a bodhisattva, so that the fierce hosts of the asuras may diminish and the assembly of the devas and their retinues may increase."

At that time, the Brahma-kāyika devas up to the Mahābrahmās, the Ābhāsvara devas up to the Śubhakṛtsnas, the Śuddhāvāsa devas up to the Śubhakṛtsnas, the Bṛhatphala devas up to the Akaniṣṭhas, and the Avṛha devas up to the Akaniṣṭhas, were filled with joy and delight, and they thought:
"We should entreat such a bodhisattva to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma for the benefit of all."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they increase the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, as well as other wholesome dharmas."
At that time, the sons and daughters of good family in that world were filled with joy and exultation, and they thought:
"We shall act as parents, brothers, wives, children, kinsmen, acquaintances, and friends to such bodhisattvas."

At that time, the gods from the Realm of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Control over Others' Emanations; from the Heaven of Brahma’s Retinue up to the Great Brahma Heaven; from the Heaven of Radiance up to the Heaven of Utmost Purity of Radiance; from the Heaven of Purity up to the Heaven of Universal Purity; from the Vast Heaven up to the Heaven of Vast Results;

and from the Heaven Free from Strife up to the Heaven of the Ultimate Form—were filled with joy and delight, and thought to themselves: "We shall employ various skillful means to cause this bodhisattva to remain free from the dharma of sexual desire. From the first generation of the mind of enlightenment until the realization of the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, he shall always practice the holy life (brahmacarya) and not give rise to greedy attachment toward dharmas that accord with the fetters."
Why is this? Engaging in non-celibate conduct acts as an obstacle even to rebirth in the Brahma heavens, let alone to realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, it is by severing desire, leaving the household life, and practicing celibacy that a bodhisattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and not by failing to leave the household life and engaging in non-celibate conduct.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Must all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas necessarily have parents, wives, children, and various kinsmen and friends?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra,
there are some bodhisattvas who possess parents, wives, children, and kinsmen, yet they cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;”

There are some bodhisattvas who have no wives or children; from the first generation of the mind of enlightenment until their attainment of Buddhahood, they constantly practice the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*) without losing their state of perpetual youth.

There are also some bodhisattvas who, through skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), first manifest the enjoyment of the five kinds of sublime sensory desires, and only afterwards renounce them to diligently practice the pure conduct, thereby attaining unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Śāriputra! It is like a master illusionist or his disciple skilled in the arts of illusion who creates various manifestations of the five kinds of sublime sensual pleasures, and therein indulges at will in merriment and the enjoyment of pleasure.”
"What do you think?
Does that which is produced by illusion have any reality? Śāriputra replied:
"No, World-Honored One! The Buddha said:

“Śāriputra! It is the same for the bodhisattva mahāsattva: through skillful means, desiring to bring sentient beings to maturity, he manifests the experience of the five desires while remaining truly free from defilement.”

Why is this? Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have developed a profound sense of weary revulsion toward the five sensual desires; they are not defiled by their faults, and through immeasurable means they censure and disparage all desires, thinking:
"Desires are like a blazing fire; desires are like filth; desires are like a butcher; desires are like an enemy; desires are like a vessel of poison; desires are like a dark well."
"Śāriputra! Since bodhisattva-mahāsattvas thus censure and revile all desires through such immeasurable doors of fault, how could there be any genuine engagement with the experience of desires?"
"It is solely for the sake of skillfully benefiting sentient beings and causing them to obtain profit and happiness that he has manifested this matter through transformation.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"How, Śāriputra, should the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said: "Śāriputra!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should contemplate in this way:
they do not perceive a truly existent bodhisattva, nor do they perceive the name "bodhisattva";
they do not perceive the perfection of wisdom, nor do they perceive the name "perfection of wisdom."
One does not perceive practice, nor does one perceive non-practice.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
The Bodhisattva is empty of intrinsic nature, and the name "Bodhisattva" is empty.
Why is this? Form is empty of intrinsic nature, not by virtue of emptiness; [and so on for the other aggregates].
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of intrinsic nature; this is not by means of emptiness.
The emptiness of form is not form; the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Form is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Form is emptiness, and emptiness is form; sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are emptiness, and emptiness is sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

This so-called "bodhi" is merely a name; this so-called "sattva" is merely a name; this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a name; and this so-called "emptiness" is merely a name. Thus, their intrinsic nature is without arising, without cessation, without defilement, and without purity.

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this way, they do not perceive arising, they do not perceive cessation, they do not perceive defilement, and they do not perceive purity. Why is this?

Śāriputra! It is only by provisionally establishing adventitious names that one gives rise to conceptual discrimination regarding various phenomena; having provisionally established these adventitious names, one follows them with verbal expression, and according as there is such verbal expression, so too does attachment arise.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any such names or the referents of those names; because they do not perceive them, they give rise to no attachment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should contemplate in this way:

'Bodhisattva' is merely a name; 'Buddha' is merely a name; 'perfection of wisdom' is merely a name; 'form' (rūpa) is merely a name; 'feeling,' 'perception,' 'volitional formations,' and 'consciousness' (vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārāḥ, vijñāna) are merely names; and all other phenomena (dharmas) are merely names."

Śāriputra! Just as "I" is merely a name, such that what is called "I" is in reality unfindable, so too are "sentient being," "life-principle," "born one," "nourisher," "person," "pudgala," and so forth, up to "knower" and "seer"—these are also merely names, such that what is called a "sentient being" up to a "seer" is in reality unfindable.
Because of the emptiness of non-apprehension, one merely follows worldly convention to provisionally establish adventitious names; all phenomena are likewise such that they should not be clung to.
Therefore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive a self, nor even a "seer," nor do they perceive the intrinsic nature of any phenomenon.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, it cannot be equaled by the wisdom of any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, with the sole exception of the wisdom of the Buddhas.”
Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva finds nothing to be apprehended in either the name or that which is named, for they do not perceive them and have no attachment to them.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, it is called practicing the profound perfection of wisdom well.

"Śāriputra! Suppose all the great śrāvakas were to fill Jambudvīpa like a forest of bamboo, reeds, rice, millet, sugarcane, hemp, and groves; even the combined wisdom of all these would not equal one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part of the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of prajñāpāramitā. It would not even equal a fractional part, a calculable part, or even an *upaniṣad* part."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all the wisdom possessed by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enables all sentient beings throughout the ten directions to attain nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
the wisdom cultivated in a single day by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of prajñāpāramitā cannot be equaled by the combined wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
“Śāriputra! Let alone Jambudvīpa.

Suppose all of you great śrāvakas were to fill the four great continents like bamboo, reeds, rice, millet, sugarcane, various types of hemp, and forests; even the combined wisdom of all such beings would not equal one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part of the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). It would not even equal a numerical fraction, a calculable fraction, or even a *upaniṣad* fraction.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all the wisdom possessed by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enables all sentient beings throughout the ten directions to attain nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
The wisdom cultivated by a single bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of prajñāpāramitā in a single day cannot be equaled by the combined wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

“Śāriputra! Setting aside the four great continents, suppose all of you great śrāvakas were to fill a trichiliocosm like bamboo, reeds, rice, millet, sugarcane, hemp, and forests; even the wisdom possessed by all of you compared to the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the *prajñāpāramitā* would not equal a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any numerical fraction, nor any calculable fraction, nor even a *upaniṣad* fraction.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all the wisdom possessed by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enables all sentient beings throughout the ten directions to attain nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
the wisdom cultivated in a single day by a single bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of prajñāpāramitā cannot be equaled by the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
“Śāriputra! Set aside for a moment a single trichiliocosm.

Suppose all of you great śrāvakas were to fill as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River, packed together like bamboo, reeds, rice, millet, sugarcane, sesame, and forests; even the combined wisdom of all such beings would not equal a hundredth part of the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any numerical fraction, nor any calculable fraction, nor even a fraction of the infinitesimal (upaniṣad).”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all the wisdom possessed by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enables all sentient beings throughout the ten directions to attain nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
the wisdom cultivated by a single bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of prajñāpāramitā in a single day cannot be equaled by the combined wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the wisdom of those in the Śrāvaka vehicle—stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, and arhats—the wisdom of those in the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, the wisdom of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—all such wisdom is without distinction, not mutually contradictory, without arising or ceasing, and empty by its very nature.”

If phenomena are without distinction, non-contradictory, without arising or ceasing, and empty of intrinsic nature, then the principle of differentiating these phenomena cannot be apprehended. Why, then, does the Blessed One say that the wisdom cultivated by a single bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom in a single day cannot be equaled by the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra, what do you think?”

Regarding the work accomplished by the wisdom cultivated in a single day by a single bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom—does the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas possess such a function?
Śāriputra said: “No, World-Honored One!”
“Furthermore, Śāriputra, what do you think?

Regarding the wisdom cultivated in a single day by a single bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom—which is fully capable of eliciting the subtle knowledge of all aspects, omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; which benefits and brings peace and happiness to all sentient beings, awakening them to all aspects of all phenomena; and which skillfully establishes all sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder—does the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas possess such efficacy?”
Śāriputra said: “No, World-Honored One!”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, what do you think?
Can all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas form such a thought as this: [that they will attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment]?"
"Did you not think, 'I shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and skillfully establish all sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder'? Śāriputra replied:
"No, World-Honored One! Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
"What do you think?
Could any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha conceive such a thought as this:

'I shall practice the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; I shall bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields; I shall fulfill the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; and having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, I shall through skillful means establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder'?"
"Is it not so? Śāriputra replied, "It is not."
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!
All bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) form this thought:

"I shall practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; I shall bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields; I shall fulfill the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; and having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I shall through skillful means establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder."
“Śāriputra! For example, a firefly does not form this thought:
‘My light can illuminate the entire Jambudvīpa and cause it to be universally and brightly lit.’”
The Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas are likewise; they have never, even for a single moment of mind, conceived such a thought as:

"I shall cultivate the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), bring sentient beings to maturity, and adorn and purify Buddha-fields; I shall fulfill the ten powers (daśabala) of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses (catvāri vaiśāradyāni), the four analytical knowledges (catasraḥ pratisamvidah), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ); I shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ), and through skillful means (upāya), establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder (nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇadhātu)."
“Śāriputra! For example, when the orb of the sun rises with its light blazing intensely, it immediately illuminates the entire continent of Jambudvīpa.
It is just so for all bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom; they all form this thought:”

"I shall cultivate the six perfections, bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-fields, fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I shall through skillful means establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and is able to attain the pure path to enlightenment of the bodhisattva’s stage of non-retrogression?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,

from their first generation of the mind of awakening, practice the six perfections and abide in the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, they transcend the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and are able to attain the pure path to awakening of the bodhisattva’s stage of non-retrogression.”
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Abiding in what stage can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas serve as a truly pure field of merit for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

From their first generation of the mind of awakening, bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the six perfections until they sit upon the sublime seat of awakening; throughout this time, they are always the truly pure field of merit for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that all wholesome dharmas appear in the world. That is to say: all ten paths of wholesome action; the five precepts for lay devotees (*upāsaka*); the eight precepts for temporary abstinence (*upavāsa*); the four dhyānas; the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*); the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*); the knowledge of the four noble truths; the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*); the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*); the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*); the five faculties (*indriya*); the five powers (*bala*); the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*); the eight branches of the noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*); the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*); the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*); the ten powers of a Tathāgata (*tathāgatabala*); the six perfections (*pāramitā*); and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*). It is through such immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless wholesome dharmas that they appear in the world.

Due to these various wholesome dharmas of the bodhisattvas, there appear in the world great clans of kṣatriyas, great clans of brāhmaṇas, great clans of householders, and great clans of lay-merchants; the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods who Control the Creations of Others; the gods of the Brahmā Assembly up to the Mahābrahmās; the Ābhāsvara gods up to the Śubhakṛtsnas; the Śuddhāvāsa gods up to the Vaihāyasa gods; the Vast gods up to the Bṛhatphalas; the gods of Non-percipient Beings, the Avṛhas up to the Akaniṣṭhas; and the gods of the Sphere of Infinite Space up to the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception.

Furthermore, it is due to the various wholesome dharmas of bodhisattvas that there appear in the world stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas further purify their own fields of merit?"
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas no longer need to purify their own fields of merit.”
Why is this? Because it is already utterly pure.
For what reason?
Śāriputra! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are great donors because they bestow upon sentient beings many wholesome dharmas, both mundane and supramundane.

That is to say, they bestow upon sentient beings the ten paths of wholesome action, the five precepts of a lay follower (*upāsaka*), the eight precepts of the fast-day (*upoṣadha*), the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the wisdom of the four noble truths, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eight branches of the noble path, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, the six perfections, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Because they bestow such immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless wholesome dharmas, bodhisattvas are called great donors.
"By this, one has already purified one's own field of merit and brought forth an immeasurable mass of worldly merit.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"With what dharmas do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas associate such that they may be said to associate with the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of form, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom;
because they are in accord with the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of the sense base of the eye, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom;
because they are in accord with the emptiness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of the sense base of form, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because they are in accord with the emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*), they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

because they are in accord with the emptiness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements (*śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, manodhātu*), they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of the realm of form, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom;
because they are in accord with the emptiness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of the visual consciousness element, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom;
because they are in accord with the emptiness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom;
because they are in accord with the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of ignorance (*avidyā*), they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

because they are in accord with the emptiness of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), clinging (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*), they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of all phenomena, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom;
because they are in accord with the emptiness of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
Śāriputra, because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with the emptiness of intrinsic nature, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Śāriputra!
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with these seven kinds of emptiness, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom. "Śāriputra!..."

When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are in accord with these seven kinds of emptiness, they do not perceive form as being either conjoined or unconjoined; they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either conjoined or unconjoined.

They do not perceive form as being either a phenomenon that arises or a phenomenon that ceases; they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either phenomena that arise or phenomena that cease.

They do not perceive form as being either a defiled phenomenon or a pure phenomenon; they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either defiled phenomena or pure phenomena.

One does not see form conjoined with feeling; one does not see feeling conjoined with perception; one does not see perception conjoined with formations; one does not see formations conjoined with consciousness. Why is this?
"Śāriputra! There is not even the slightest dharma that is conjoined with any other dharma, because the intrinsic nature of all dharmas is empty. Śāriputra!"
All forms are empty; they are not form.
All feelings, perceptions, mental formations, and consciousnesses are empty; they are not feeling, perception, mental formation, or consciousness. Why is this?
Śāriputra! All forms are empty; they do not possess the characteristic of resistance.
All sensations are empty; they do not possess the characteristic of experiencing.
All perceptions are empty; they do not possess the characteristic of grasping images.
All formations are empty; they do not possess the characteristic of volitional construction.
All consciousnesses are empty; they do not possess the characteristic of discernment.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form. Form is itself emptiness; emptiness is itself form. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also thus.

“Śāriputra! This emptiness of all phenomena is characterized by neither arising nor ceasing, neither defilement nor purity, neither increase nor decrease; it is not of the past, not of the future, and not of the present.”
Thus, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
no eye-base, no ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base;
no form-base, no sound, odor, taste, tangible object, or mental-object-base.
There is no earth element; there is no water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element.
There is no eye element; there is no ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind element.
There is no form element; there is no sound, odor, taste, tangible object, or mental phenomenon element.
There is no eye-consciousness element, nor ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements;
there is no ignorance, nor the cessation of ignorance;

there is no volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or aging-and-death, nor the cessation of volitional formations up to the cessation of aging-and-death.
There is no noble truth of suffering, nor the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
there is no attainment and no clear realization;
there is no stream-enterer and no fruit of stream-entry.
There is no once-returner, and no fruit of once-returning;
there is no non-returner, and no fruit of non-returning; there is no arhat, and no fruit of arhatship.
There is no solitary realizer, nor is there the enlightenment of a solitary realizer;
there is no bodhisattva, nor is there the conduct of a bodhisattva;
there is no perfectly awakened one, nor is there the enlightenment of a perfectly awakened one.
“Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) as either associated or dissociated; they do not perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as either associated or dissociated.

They do not perceive form (rūpa) as either associated or dissociated; they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness (vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskāra, vijñāna) as either associated or dissociated."

One does not perceive the sense-base of the eye as either associated or dissociated; one does not perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as either associated or dissociated. One does not perceive the sense-base of forms as either associated or dissociated;
one does not perceive the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena as either associated or dissociated.

One does not perceive the eye-element as either associated or dissociated; one does not perceive the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as either associated or dissociated. One does not perceive the form-element as either associated or dissociated; one does not perceive the elements of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena as either associated or dissociated.

He does not perceive the eye-consciousness element as either associated or dissociated; he does not perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements as either associated or dissociated.
He does not perceive the noble truth of suffering as either associated or dissociated; he does not perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path as either associated or dissociated.

He does not perceive ignorance as either associated or dissociated; he does not perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or aging-and-death as either associated or dissociated.

They do not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness as either associated or dissociated; they do not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as either associated or dissociated;
they do not perceive the six superknowledges as either associated or dissociated;

they do not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha as either associated or dissociated; and they do not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as either associated or dissociated.

One does not perceive whether the subtle wisdom that perceives no signs is associated or dissociated, nor does one perceive whether the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is associated or dissociated.
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive emptiness as uniting with emptiness, nor do they perceive it as corresponding with emptiness; they do not perceive signlessness as uniting with signlessness, nor do they perceive it as corresponding with signlessness; they do not perceive wishlessness as uniting with wishlessness, nor do they perceive it as corresponding with wishlessness. Why is this?
Śāriputra! Emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are neither conjoined nor disjoined, and because they are neither associated nor dissociated. Śāriputra!
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and are thus associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, having entered into the emptiness of the intrinsic characteristics of all phenomena, they do not perceive form as either conjoined or dispersed; they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as either conjoined or dispersed."
One does not observe form as being either conjoined with or dispersed from the prior limit. Why is this?
Because one does not perceive a prior limit.
One does not contemplate whether form is joined with or separated from the future limit. Why?
Because one does not perceive a future limit.
One does not contemplate whether form and the middle limit are joined or dispersed. Why?
Because one does not perceive a middle limit.
One does not contemplate feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either conjoined with or separate from the prior limit.
Why is this? Because one does not perceive a prior limit.
One does not contemplate feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either conjoined with or separate from the future limit. Why?
Because one does not perceive a future limit.
One does not contemplate whether feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness are conjoined with or separated from the middle limit.
Why is this? Because one does not perceive a middle limit.
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not contemplate the past limit as being either joined with or separate from the future limit; they do not contemplate the past limit as being either joined with or separate from the middle limit; they do not contemplate the future limit as being either joined with or separate from the past limit; they do not contemplate the future limit as being either joined with or separate from the middle limit; they do not contemplate the middle limit as being either joined with or separate from the past limit; they do not contemplate the middle limit as being either joined with or separate from the future limit; they do not contemplate the past limit, the future limit, and the middle limit as being either joined with or separate from one another; they do not contemplate the future limit, the past limit, and the middle limit as being either joined with or separate from one another; they do not contemplate the middle limit, the past limit, and the future limit as being either joined with or separate from one another; nor do they contemplate the past limit, the future limit, and the middle limit as being either joined with or separate from one another. Why is this?"
Śāriputra, because the three periods of time are empty,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and accord with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe all-knowledge as being either conjoined with or dissociated from the past."
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the past, how much less could one observe all-knowledge as either conjoined with or separate from the past!
One does not observe all-knowledge as either conjoined with or separate from the future.
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the future, how much less could one observe all-knowledge as either conjoined with or separate from the future!
One does not observe all-knowledge as either conjoined with or separate from the present.
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the present, how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the present!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from form.
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive form, how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either conjoined with or separate from form!
One does not observe all-knowledge as being either conjoined with or separate from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, much less observe omniscience as being either conjoined with or separate from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the sense-base of the eye. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the sense-base of the eye, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from it!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or dissociated from the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or dissociated from them!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the sense-base of form. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the sense-base of form, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from it!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from them!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge and the eye-element are conjoined or dispersed. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the eye-element, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge and the eye-element are conjoined or dispersed!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind element. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind element, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from them!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the realm of form. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the realm of form, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from it!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from them!
One does not observe whether omniscience and the eye-consciousness element are joined or dispersed. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the eye-consciousness element, how much less could one observe whether omniscience and the eye-consciousness element are joined or dispersed!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element, how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from them!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or separated from the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the noble truth of suffering, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or separated from it!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or separate from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or separate from them!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge and ignorance are joined or dispersed. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive ignorance, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge and ignorance are joined or dispersed!

One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the factors from volitional formations up to old age and death, much less observe whether omniscience is joined with or separated from volitional formations up to old age and death!
One does not observe whether omniscience is joined with or separated from the perfection of generosity.
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the perfection of generosity, much less observe whether omniscience and the perfection of generosity are joined or separated!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is joined with or separated from the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. Why is that?

One does not even perceive the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom; how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either conjoined with or separate from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge and the four foundations of mindfulness are conjoined or dispersed. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge and the four foundations of mindfulness are conjoined or dispersed!

One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is conjoined with or separate from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path; how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either conjoined with or separate from the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge and the six supernormal powers are joined or dispersed. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the six supernormal powers, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge and the six supernormal powers are joined or dispersed!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge and the ten powers of a Buddha are joined or dispersed. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the ten powers of a Buddha, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge and the ten powers of a Buddha are joined or dispersed!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are joined or dispersed. Why is this?

Since one does not even perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, how much less could one observe omniscience as being either conjoined with or separate from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge and the Buddha are joined or dispersed, nor does one contemplate whether the Buddha and all-knowledge are joined or dispersed.
Why is this? Because all-knowledge is itself the Buddha, and the Buddha is himself all-knowledge.
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge and awakening are joined or dispersed, nor does one contemplate whether awakening and all-knowledge are joined or dispersed. Why is this?
Omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is itself awakening (*bodhi*), and awakening is itself omniscience. Śāriputra,
because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not cling to form as being either existent or non-existent; they do not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either existent or non-existent.
They do not cling to form as being either permanent or impermanent; they do not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either permanent or impermanent."
He does not cling to form as either pleasant or painful; he does not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as either pleasant or painful.

He does not cling to form as either self or non-self; he does not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as either self or non-self. He does not cling to form as either tranquil or untranquil; he does not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as either tranquil or untranquil.
He does not cling to form as either empty or non-empty; he does not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as either empty or non-empty.
One does not cling to form, whether it has signs or is signless; one does not cling to feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, whether they have signs or are signless.

One does not cling to form, whether it has aspirations or is aspirationless; one does not cling to feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, whether they have aspirations or are aspirationless.
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form this thought:
'I am practicing the perfection of wisdom.'"
They do not form this thought:
"I am not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
They do not form this thought:
"I neither practice nor do not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*.
They do not form this thought:
"I neither practice nor do not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*."
"Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of giving; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

They do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of entering the bodhisattva’s state of certainty (samyaktvaniyāma); they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of attaining the bodhisattva’s stage of non-retrogression."
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of maturing sentient beings, nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of purifying the Buddha-fields;

one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four applications of mindfulness, nor for the sake of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;

one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ten powers of a Buddha, nor for the sake of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of internal emptiness; nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of limits, emptiness of dispersion and non-dispersion, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics and common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-existence, or emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of suchness; nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, or the limit of reality.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive any differentiation in the nature of phenomena (dharmas).
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of the divine eye; nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal powers of the divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of past lives, miraculous powers, or the realization of the exhaustion of outflows."
Why is this? Śāriputra,

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not even perceive the perfection of wisdom, much less perceive the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, or their six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā)!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form this thought:

'By means of the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine eye, I shall universally observe all sentient beings in Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, distinguishing their various categories of death here and birth there.'"
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine ear, I shall hear everywhere throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all the various sounds and speech of sentient beings."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds, I shall fully know the distinctions in the minds and mental factors, as well as their objects of cognition, of all sentient beings throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal knowledge of recollecting past lives, I shall universally remember all the various past lives of all sentient beings in Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of miraculous feats, I shall go everywhere throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, to proclaim the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of my supernormal knowledge of the destruction of the outflows, I shall thoroughly examine whether all sentient beings in all Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have destroyed their outflows or not."
"Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and is in accord with the perfection of wisdom, they are able through skillful means to universally establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder. No evil Māras or their retinues can find an opportunity against them; all afflictions are completely subdued and extinguished, and all worldly affairs they desire are accomplished."

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and the assemblies of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, together protect and mind such Bodhisattvas, ensuring they do not fall back into the stages of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.

In each of the ten directions, throughout realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; the gods from the Cāturmahārājika-kāyika up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin; from the Brahmakāyika up to the Mahābrahmā; from the Ābhāsvara up to the Ābhāsvara-śubha; from the Śubhakṛtsna up to the Śubhakṛtsna-vibhūta; from the Bṛhatphala up to the Bṛhatphala-vibhūta; from the Avṛha up to the Akaniṣṭha—all these together protect and guard this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Whatever they undertake shall be free from obstacles and swiftly accomplished; all various physical and mental ailments and sufferings shall be completely healed and eliminated; and even if there are karmic offenses that would otherwise result in bitter retribution in future lives, these shall be transformed so that they are experienced only lightly in the present.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness and compassion.

“Śāriputra! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, possessing great power and requiring little application of effort, they are able to bring forth all the most excellent dhāraṇī-doors and all the most excellent samādhi-doors, causing them all to manifest.”

By the power of this, one will, according to one's wish, bring forth various mundane and supramundane merits; wherever one is born, one will always encounter and serve the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, and until reaching unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, one shall never be separated from the Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas during that interval.

Śāriputra, you should know that because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and is in accord with the perfection of wisdom, they attain such immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable benefits and merits as these.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts as:
'There are phenomena that are either associated or dissociated with other phenomena, or equal or unequal. "
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive any dharma that is either associated or dissociated with another dharma, nor any that is equal or unequal.
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 483. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three: The Chapter on Śāriputra, Section Two, Part Three. "Furthermore, Śāriputra!..."
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts as:
"I shall swiftly manifest perfect awakening in the dharma-realm," or "I shall not swiftly manifest perfect awakening."
Why is this? Śāriputra, because there is not even the slightest dharma that can manifest equal enlightenment within the dharmadhātu.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive even the slightest dharma as being separate from the dharmadhātu, nor does he perceive the dharmadhātu as being separate from the existence of all dharmas.
He does not perceive even the slightest dharma as being identical to the dharmadhātu, nor does he perceive the dharmadhātu as being identical to the existence of all dharmas.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because phenomena (dharma) and the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) are neither identical nor separate.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form the thought:
"The dharma-realm can act as the causal condition for all phenomena."
They do not form the thought:
"These dharmas can realize the dharma-realm. Why is this?
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive even the slightest dharma; how much less could there be a dharma that can realize the dharmadhātu! Śāriputra!

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not perceive the dharma-realm as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the dharma-realm; it is the same for all buddhas.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
emptiness and the dharma-realm are neither associated nor dissociated, neither identical nor distinct.
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the dharma-realm as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the dharma-realm."
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with form;

he does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sense-base of the eye as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the sense-base of the eye;

he does not perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sphere of form as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the sphere of form;

he does not perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-element as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the eye-element;

he does not perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element as being conjoined with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the realm of form as being associated with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being associated with the realm of form;

he does not perceive the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as being associated with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being associated with the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-consciousness element as being associated with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being associated with the eye-consciousness element;

he does not perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements as being associated with emptiness, nor does he perceive emptiness as being associated with the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.
“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom can correspond in this way, this is the foremost correspondence with emptiness.”

Śāriputra! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is thus associated with emptiness, they do not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; rather, they bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Śāriputra! Among all the applications of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, the application with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is the foremost, the most honored, the most excellent, the highest, the most sublime, the supreme, the unsurpassed, the unsurpassable, the peerless, and the equal to the unequaled.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because that which corresponds to this prajñāpāramitā corresponds to emptiness, corresponds to signlessness, and corresponds to wishlessness.

“Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas are thus associated with this perfection of wisdom, you should know that they have either received the prediction of enlightenment or are close to receiving it.”
Śāriputra! By means of this correspondence, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring great benefit to immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings. Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form the thought:
"I am associated with the perfection of wisdom.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I have already received the prediction of enlightenment, or I am close to receiving it.
They do not form such thoughts as:
"I can adorn and purify a buddha-field," or "I can bring sentient beings to maturity."
They do not form this thought:
"I shall realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes. Why is this?

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma apart from the dharmadhātu; he does not perceive the dharmadhātu as existing apart from all dharmas. He does not perceive any dharma that can practice the prajñāpāramitā; he does not perceive any dharma that receives the Buddha’s prediction; he does not perceive any dharma that can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; he does not perceive any dharma that can adorn and purify a buddha-field; and he does not perceive any dharma that can bring sentient beings to maturity.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they ultimately do not give rise to the notion of a "sentient being" or similar concepts.

Why is this? Because all sentient beings are ultimately neither born nor do they perish; since they are ultimately neither born nor do they perish, how could they possibly practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?
Just as sentient beings are neither born nor extinguished, so too are all phenomena.

"Śāriputra, it is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the birth of sentient beings or phenomena that they practice the perfection of wisdom; because they do not perceive the extinction of sentient beings or phenomena that they practice the perfection of wisdom; because they realize that sentient beings and phenomena are empty that they practice the perfection of wisdom; because they realize that sentient beings and phenomena are non-self that they practice the perfection of wisdom; because they realize that sentient beings and phenomena are unapprehendable that they practice the perfection of wisdom; and because they realize that sentient beings and phenomena are utterly secluded that they practice the perfection of wisdom."

“Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being in accord with emptiness is foremost; being in accord with the perfection of wisdom is most venerable and most supreme, such that none can equal it.”

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they are able to correctly bring forth great loving-kindness, great compassion, and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas. By the power of this, they ultimately never give rise to minds of stinginess and greed, violation of precepts, anger and resentment, laziness, distraction, or corrupt wisdom.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is in union with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), from where did this bodhisattva mahāsattva pass away to be reborn here?”
"From where did he pass away, and where will he be reborn?
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is in union with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), that bodhisattva mahāsattva has either passed away from another buddha-field to be reborn here, or passed away from Tuṣita Heaven to be reborn here, or passed away from among human beings to be reborn here."

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being in union with the perfection of wisdom, passes away from another buddha-field and is reborn here, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly become united with the perfection of wisdom.”

By virtue of these causes and conditions, as soon as they are reborn, profound and wondrous Dharma gates will swiftly manifest before them. From that time forth, they will always be in rapid accord with the *prajñāpāramitā*, and in whatever place they are born, they will constantly encounter the Buddhas, making offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them, never allowing such encounters to pass in vain.

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being in union with the perfection of wisdom, passes away from Tuṣita Heaven and is reborn here, that bodhisattva mahāsattva never forgets and constantly brings before them the six perfections; they also never forget and constantly bring before them all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi.

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), passes away from among humans and is reborn here, that bodhisattva mahāsattva—except for those who have attained the stage of non-retrogression—is of dull faculties; they cannot quickly become associated with the perfection of wisdom, nor do they possess mastery over the gateways of dhāraṇī or the gateways of samādhi, such that these do not frequently manifest before them.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra! Regarding what you have asked:
'If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is in union with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), where will this bodhisattva mahāsattva be reborn after passing away from this world?'"

"Śāriputra, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having passed away from here, will be born in other buddha-fields, traveling from one buddha-field to another. In whatever place they are born, they will always encounter Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas; until they realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening they seek, they will never be separated from a Buddha."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, because they lack skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), although able to manifest the four dhyānas and practice the six pāramitās, by virtue of attaining those dhyānas are reborn in the long-lived heavens. When their lifespan there is exhausted, they are reborn in the human world, where they encounter various Buddhas and provide them with offerings, respect, honor, and praise, and practice the six kinds of pāramitās; yet their faculties are dull and not at all sharp."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,

although they have attained meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), because they lack skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), abandon meditative concentration and are reborn in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*)."
It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s faculties are dull and not extremely sharp.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who,
although able to enter the four dhyānas and also able to enter the four immeasurables, [do not attain the fruit of arhatship].
They are also able to enter the four formless absorptions, and they are also able to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path,
the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, and great compassion.
Possessing great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, because they possess skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*),
they are not reborn by the power of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), or the formless attainments (*ārūpya*). Rather,
they are born only in worlds where a Buddha resides, constantly encountering Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, never being separated from the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
“Maitreya, you shall certainly become a Buddha within this Bhadrakalpa.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although capable of giving rise to the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, do not take birth according to the power of those dhyānas, immeasurables, or formless states because they possess skillful means. Instead, they are reborn in the desire realm—whether among a great kṣatriya clan, a great brāhmaṇa clan, a great householder clan, or a great merchant clan—for the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they manifest entry into the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, do not take birth according to the power of those dhyānas, immeasurables, or formless states because they possess skillful means.
