Instead, they are reborn in the desire realm, or among the Cāturmahārājika devas, or the Trāyastriṃśa devas, or the Yāma devas, or the Tuṣita devas, or the Nirmāṇarati devas, or the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas. This is for the sake of maturing sentient beings and for the sake of purifying their own buddha-fields; they constantly encounter all Buddhas, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising them, never allowing such encounters to pass in vain."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they are able to manifest entry into the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, yet by virtue of their skillful means, pass away from this place and are reborn in the Brahma-world as Great Brahmā Kings. Possessing majestic power and sovereignty, they travel through various buddha-fields, going from one buddha-field to another, and exhort those bodhisattvas therein who have not yet realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to realize that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi."
"Since you have already realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, we pray that you turn the wheel of Dharma for the benefit of all beings. Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bound to one more birth who practice the perfection of wisdom; because they possess skillful means, although they manifest the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, the concentration of emptiness, the concentration of signlessness, and the concentration of wishlessness, they do not revolve according to the influence of these dhyānas, immeasurables, or formless states. They manifest before, serve, attend upon, and make offerings to the present Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; having diligently practiced the holy life in the presence of these Buddhas, they pass away from this world and are reborn in Tuṣita Heaven.

Throughout the full span of their lifetimes, with all faculties unimpaired, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, they will be surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of immeasurable and countless celestial beings who pay them homage; then, being reborn among humans, they will realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, and deliver immeasurable multitudes.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*). They are not born in the desire realm, nor are they born in the form realm, nor are they born in the formless realm. They travel through various buddha-fields to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, while practicing the bodhisattva path until they realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) they seek."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the six supernormal powers and sport with mastery, traveling from one buddha-field to another. In the buddha-fields they pass through, there is no mention of the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; there is only the Single Vehicle (ekayāna) and the assembly of bodhisattvas."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the six supernormal powers and sport with mastery, traveling from one buddha-field to another; the lifespan of the sentient beings in the buddha-fields they pass through is incalculable."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, having attained the six supernormal powers, travel through various worlds, going from one world to another.

There may be worlds where the names of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha are not heard; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas go to those places to praise the merits of the Triple Gem, causing all sentient beings to give rise to deep pure faith, whereby they obtain great benefit throughout the long night [of saṃsāra]."

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva passes away from here, they will be reborn in a buddha-field where they cultivate the bodhisattva practices, gradually realizing the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from the first production of the thought of awakening, attain the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and they cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is not born in the desire realm, nor is he born in the form realm, nor is he born in the formless realm; rather, he is always born in places where he can benefit sentient beings, bringing them profit, peace, and happiness.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,
from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, are able to enter the bodhisattva’s stage of correct determination, and even able to abide in the stage of non-retrogression."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from the very first production of the thought of enlightenment, are able to successively realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening; they turn the sublime wheel of Dharma and deliver immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, enabling them to obtain supreme benefit and peace, and finally enter parinirvāṇa in the realm of nirvana without remainder."
"After my parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma that I have taught shall remain for one kalpa, or even for more than one kalpa, benefiting boundless classes of sentient beings. Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, are able to be in accord with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Surrounded by respectful attendance of immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they travel through various buddha-fields, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, while bringing sentient beings to maturity and purifying buddha-fields.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom and attain the four dhyānas,
the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions, being able to sport with mastery therein; that is to say, first— "
Entering the first dhyāna, arising from the first dhyāna and entering the meditative attainment of cessation (*nirodha-samāpatti*);
arising from the meditative attainment of cessation and entering the second dhyāna; arising from the second dhyāna and entering the meditative attainment of cessation;
arising from the meditative attainment of cessation and entering the third dhyāna; arising from the third dhyāna and entering the meditative attainment of cessation; arising from...
Emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the fourth dhyāna; emerging from the fourth dhyāna, he enters the attainment of cessation;
emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the sphere of infinite space; emerging from the sphere of infinite space, he enters the attainment of cessation;
emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the sphere of infinite consciousness; emerging from the sphere of infinite consciousness...
Entering the attainment of cessation, he arises from the attainment of cessation and enters the sphere of nothingness;
arising from the sphere of nothingness, he enters the attainment of cessation; arising from the attainment of cessation, he enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
and arising from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he enters the attainment of cessation.
In this way, Śāriputra,

the bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom through skillful means sports with mastery, proceeding in direct and reverse order, and returning, through the successive stages of meditative attainments.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have already attained the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and who have also cultivated the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—yet do not take up the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor the fruit of a once-returner, nor the fruit of a non-returner, nor the fruit of arhatship, nor pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, nor the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a buddha."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they cause sentient beings to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, so that they may attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;

they also cause sentient beings to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, so that they may realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra! This wisdom of the fruits of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is itself the patience of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Śāriputra!

It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already dwelled in the stage of non-retrogression; abiding securely in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are capable of performing such deeds.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the six pāramitās, purify the Tuṣita heaven; they shall become buddhas within this Bhadrakalpa, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Although they have already attained the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), and the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti); although they have cultivated the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda), the five faculties (indriya), the five powers (bala), the seven factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga), and the eightfold noble path (āryāṣṭāṅgamārga); and although they have also cultivated the ten powers of a buddha (buddhabala), the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma)—constantly and diligently training in the conduct that leads to awakening—they have not yet fully realized the Four Noble Truths (catvāri āryasatyāni) in the present."
You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by only one more birth before attaining unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!..."
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the six perfections, travel through various worlds to establish sentient beings in unsurpassed enlightenment and to purify buddha-fields.
It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva must pass through immeasurable and incalculable great eons before attaining unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide securely in the six perfections, constantly and diligently exerting themselves to benefit sentient beings; they never utter speech that leads to what is meaningless, nor do they give rise in body or mind to actions that invite what is meaningless.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who constantly take the six perfections as their primary practice while cultivating the bodhisattva path. They bestow upon all sentient beings every kind of requisite for happiness: they give food to those who need food, drink to those who need drink, clothing to those who need clothing, vehicles to those who need vehicles, fragrant garlands to those who need fragrant garlands, bedding to those who need bedding, dwellings to those who need dwellings, wealth and grain to those who need wealth and grain, precious jewels to those who need precious jewels, ornaments to those who need ornaments, and servants to those who need servants. They provide whatever else is required, exhorting them to cultivate all that is wholesome and instructing them to abandon all that is unwholesome, so that all may realize the eternal bliss of nirvāṇa."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who manifest emanation bodies like those of a Buddha and enter throughout the realms of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and devas; they preach the true Dharma using the vocal sounds appropriate to each class of being, causing them to obtain supreme benefit, peace, and happiness."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), manifest emanation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*) like those of a Buddha that travel throughout the worlds of the Ganges-sand in the ten directions, proclaiming the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields (*buddhakṣetra*).

In the presence of these Buddhas, they listen to the sublime Dharma, making offerings with reverence, honoring, and praising them. They fully grasp the characteristics of the most excellent, unsurpassed, subtle, and pure buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, and thereby personally bring forth their own most excellent, unsurpassed, purified buddha-fields. Within these fields, they establish great bodhisattvas bound to one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*), causing them to swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) they seek."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six pāramitās and are endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, adorning their bodies. Their faculties are sharp and unsurpassedly pure; all sentient beings who see them feel nothing but reverence and affection. They gradually guide and transform them, causing them to swiftly realize the nirvāṇa of the three vehicles."
In this way, Śāriputra, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train in the purification of their physical, verbal, and mental actions for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom; although they have attained the most excellent and sharp faculties, they do not exalt themselves or disparage others."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, constantly abide in the pāramitās of generosity and ethical discipline; until they attain the stage of non-retrogression, they never fall into the evil destinies at any time."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,
from their first generation of the mind until they have attained the stage of non-retrogression, never abandon the ten paths of wholesome action."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, abiding in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, become wheel-turning kings endowed with great majesty and power; they constantly bestow wealth and treasures upon sentient beings, causing them to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, gather the karmic retribution of hundreds of thousands of universal monarchs (*cakravartin*). By means of this, they encounter immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, making offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them, such that none of these acts go to waste."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), constantly acting as a light for sentient beings, never departing from the radiance of the Buddha-dharma, and thus proceeding by stages until they realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi)."
Śāriputra! By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is always able to manifest all the Buddha-dharmas. Therefore, Śāriputra!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should never give rise to faulty actions of body, speech, or mind.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
what are called blameworthy bodily actions, verbal actions, and mental actions?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought: ‘What is this body?’”
"By means of this body, I initiate bodily action.
What is speech? By means of this speech, I initiate vocal action."
"What is this mind?
It is by means of this mind that I give rise to mental karma. Śāriputra!
These are called faulty actions of body, speech, and mind.

"Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the body or bodily action; they do not apprehend speech or vocal action; they do not apprehend the mind or mental action."

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom were to perceive a self in body, speech, mind, and their respective actions, they would then give rise to thoughts of stinginess and greed, violation of precepts, anger and resentment, laziness, distraction, and corrupt wisdom.
Śāriputra! It is impossible for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom to give rise to such a thought.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
It is impossible that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom would give rise to the three kinds of grossness of body, speech, and mind.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, they are able to purify the three types of coarse heaviness (*dauṣṭhulya*) of body, speech, and mind.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness of body, speech, and mind?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the body nor the bodily dysfunctions; they do not apprehend speech nor the verbal dysfunctions; they do not apprehend the mind nor the mental dysfunctions, Śāriputra!”
In this way, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to purify the three types of coarse heaviness (*dauṣṭhulya*) of body, speech, and mind. Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva,

from the first generation of the mind of awakening, is able to fully undertake and maintain the ten paths of wholesome action, does not give rise to the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and constantly keeps in mind the deliverance of all sentient beings.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called one who is able to purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness (*dauṣṭhulya*). Furthermore, Śāriputra!
“There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections to purify the path to enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying,
“World-Honored One!”
"What is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s path to awakening?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva conduct, they do not apprehend physical action, they do not apprehend verbal action, they do not apprehend mental action; they do not apprehend the perfection of generosity, nor do they apprehend the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom; they do not apprehend śrāvakas, they do not apprehend pratyekabuddhas, they do not apprehend bodhisattvas, they do not apprehend tathāgatas, and they do not apprehend any phenomena whatsoever."
Śāriputra! This is the path to enlightenment for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Śāriputra!
"When the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, no one can obstruct them on their path to enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason, Śāriputra, can no one obstruct a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the six perfections and proceeds upon the path to enlightenment?
The Buddha said: "Śāriputra!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, they do not grasp at form; they do not grasp at feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

They do not grasp at the sense base of the eye or the sense base of forms; they do not grasp at the sense base of the ear or the sense base of sounds; they do not grasp at the sense base of the nose or the sense base of odors; they do not grasp at the sense base of the tongue or the sense base of tastes; they do not grasp at the sense base of the body or the sense base of tangibles; they do not grasp at the sense base of the mind or the sense base of phenomena.
They do not grasp at the eye element, the form element, or the eye-consciousness element.

They do not grasp the ear element, the sound element, or the ear-consciousness element; they do not grasp the nose element, the odor element, or the nose-consciousness element; they do not grasp the tongue element, the taste element, or the tongue-consciousness element; they do not grasp the body element, the tangible-object element, or the body-consciousness element; they do not grasp the mind element, the mental-object element, or the mind-consciousness element.
They do not grasp the earth element, nor the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

They do not grasp the four foundations of mindfulness, nor the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
They do not grasp at the perfection of generosity; they do not grasp at the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
They do not grasp at the ten powers of a Buddha; they do not grasp at the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They do not grasp at the fruit of stream-entry; they do not grasp at the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.
They do not grasp at the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, they do not grasp at the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and they do not grasp at unsurpassed,

perfect, and complete enlightenment. Śāriputra, for this reason, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, their growth and blazing intensity as they proceed toward the path to enlightenment cannot be obstructed by anyone.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,
dwelling securely in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are able to swiftly fulfill the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)."

Because they have accomplished supreme wisdom, they close the gates to all perilous and evil realms; they receive human and celestial bodies that are never impoverished or lowly, their faculties are complete, and their physical appearance is dignified and majestic, such that they are revered and loved by all gods and humans in the world.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the supreme wisdom accomplished by a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

By accomplishing this wisdom, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas universally behold all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions; they universally hear the sounds of the Dharma preached by those Buddhas; they universally see all the assemblies of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas therein; and they universally see the signs of the majestic purity of those lands.”

“Śāriputra! By accomplishing this wisdom, bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not give rise to the notion of a world, do not give rise to the notion of a Buddha, do not give rise to the notion of the Dharma, do not give rise to the notion of the Śrāvaka Saṃgha, do not give rise to the notion of the Bodhisattva Saṃgha, do not give rise to the notion of a Pratyekabuddha, do not give rise to the notion of a self, do not give rise to the notion of another, and do not give rise to the notion of the adornment and purification of a Buddha-field.”
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas have accomplished this wisdom, although they practice the perfection of generosity, they do not apprehend the perfection of generosity;

although they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they do not apprehend the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.
Although they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not apprehend the four foundations of mindfulness;

although they cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they do not apprehend the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path;
although they accumulate the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not apprehend the ten powers of a Buddha.

Although they assemble the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they do not apprehend the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Śāriputra! This is the supreme wisdom attained by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
By attaining this wisdom, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to swiftly fulfill all Buddha-dharmas; yet, although they fulfill all Buddha-dharmas, they do so without any grasping.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the six perfections, attain the purification of the five eyes, namely: the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the Dharma eye, and the Buddha eye."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure fleshly eye?”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see one hundred *yojana*s; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see two hundred *yojana*s; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see three hundred up to a thousand *yojana*s; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see the realm of Jambudvīpa; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see the realm of two great continents; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can even see the realm of four great continents; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see a small thousand-world system; there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see a medium thousand-world system; and there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas whose fleshly eye can see a trichiliocosm.”
"Śāriputra! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to attain the pure fleshly eye.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure divine eye?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"The divine eye of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Four Great Kings,
the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
it can also see all the gods of the Brahmakāyika Heaven and the Brahmapurohita Heaven."
What is seen by the divine eye of the gods of the Heaven of the Retinue of Brahmā and the Great Brahmā Heaven, he can also see;
what is seen by the divine eye of all the gods of the Heaven of Limited Light, the Heaven of Infinite Light, and the Heaven of Luminous Sound, he can also see;
and what is seen by the gods of the Heaven of Purity, the Heaven of Limited Purity, the Heaven of Infinite Purity, and the Heaven of Universal Purity, he can also see.
With his own eyes, he can see everything that is seen by the divine eyes of the Bṛhatphala devas—
including the Bṛhat, Parīttabṛhat, Apramāṇabṛhat, and Bṛhatphala devas— as well as everything seen by the divine eyes of the Asaṃjñisattva devas,
and everything seen by the divine eyes of the Avṛha, Atapa, and Sudṛśa devas.
...the gods of Sudarśana and the Akaniṣṭha heaven see with their divine eye. Śāriputra!
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who see with their divine eye what the divine eyes of all the gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven cannot see.

Śāriputra! With their divine eye, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to see, as they truly understand them, all sentient beings in each of the worlds of the ten directions—as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—dying here and being reborn there.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure divine eye.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure eye of wisdom?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess the pure eye of wisdom; they do not perceive any phenomenon—whether conditioned or unconditioned, wholesome or unwholesome, faulty or faultless, with outflows or without outflows, defiled or free from defilement, mundane or supramundane, or afflicted or purified.”
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, with the wisdom-eye, does not see any dharma that can be seen, heard, sensed, or cognized. Śāriputra!
"This is what constitutes the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s attainment of the pure eye of wisdom.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure Dharma-eye?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"The Dharma-eye of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas can know, as they truly are, the various distinctions among individuals (pudgala)."
That is to say, knowing them as they truly are:
this is one who follows by faith, this is one who follows the Dharma, this is one who practices the signless;
this one dwells in emptiness, this one dwells in the signless, this one dwells in the wishless.

From these three gates of liberation arise the five faculties; from the five faculties arises the uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from the uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*). By means of this knowledge and vision of liberation, one permanently abandons the three fetters—namely, the view of a self-identity (*satkāya-dṛṣṭi*), attachment to precepts and observances (*śīla-vrata-parāmarśa*), and doubt (*vicikitsā*). Because of abandoning these, one attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*).
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga*) first attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion to attain the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmi-phala*).
Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion to attain the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmi-phala*).

Furthermore, by means of this very superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one exhausts the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañcordhvabhāgīya-saṃyojana*), namely: attachment to the realm of form (*rūparāga*), attachment to the formless realm (*ārūpyarāga*), ignorance (*avidyā*), pride (*māna*), and restlessness (*auddhatya*).

Through the exhaustion of these, one attains the fruit of arhatship. This occurs by means of the door of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) giving rise to the five faculties (*pañcendriya*); from the five faculties arises the uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from the uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñānadarśana*); and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one permanently abandons the three fetters (*trisaṃyojana*), attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*), and so on, as extensively described, up to the attainment of the fruit of arhatship.

Likewise, by means of the door of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), the five faculties arise; from the five faculties arises the uninterrupted concentration; from the uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation; and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one permanently abandons the three fetters, attaining the fruit of stream-entry, and so on, as extensively described, up to the attainment of the fruit of arhatship.

This arises from the door of liberation of wishlessness, giving rise to the five faculties; from the five faculties, one gives rise to the uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from the uninterrupted concentration, one gives rise to the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one eternally severs the three fetters, attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpanna*), and so on in detail until the attainment of the fruit of arhatship.

This occurs by way of the doors of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā*) and signlessness (*animitta*); this by way of the doors of liberation of emptiness and wishlessness (*apranihita*); and this by way of the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness—the detailed explanation is likewise for each.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Dharma-eye.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
The Dharma-eye of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is able to know, as it truly is, that all phenomena of origination are phenomena of cessation; by knowing this, they attain the five faculties.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Dharma-eye. Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

The Dharma-eye of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enables them to know, as it truly is, that this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has first generated the mind of awakening, practices the perfections of generosity and ethical discipline, and has accomplished the faculty of faith and the faculty of diligence; through skillful means, they contemplate receiving a body for the sake of increasing wholesome dharmas.

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas may be born into great kṣatriya clans, up to and including great householder clans; or they may be born among the gods of the Four Great Kings, up to and including the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods. Abiding in those realms, they bring sentient beings to maturity, bestow various articles of pleasure upon all sentient beings, and purify buddha-fields. They serve, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, never falling into the stages of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and remaining non-regressive until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Dharma-eye. Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

The Dharma-eye of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can know, as it truly is, that this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has already received the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while that bodhisattva-mahāsattva has not yet received the prediction;
that this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has already attained non-retrogression, while that bodhisattva-mahāsattva has not yet attained non-retrogression;
and that this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has already perfected the supernormal powers, while that bodhisattva-mahāsattva has not yet perfected the supernormal powers.

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to travel to Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions to make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; while these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are unable to travel to Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions to make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already attained the supernormal powers (abhijñā); these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet attained the supernormal powers.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already purified their Buddha-fields; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet purified their Buddha-fields.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already matured sentient beings; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet matured sentient beings.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already been praised by all buddhas; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet been praised by all buddhas.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already drawn near to all buddhas; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet drawn near to all buddhas.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s lifespan is immeasurable; this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s lifespan is measurable.
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains awakening, the community of bhikṣus will be immeasurable; when this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains awakening, the community of bhikṣus will be measurable.
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains awakening, there will be a community of bodhisattvas; when this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains awakening, there will be no community of bodhisattvas.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas engage in difficult practices and ascetic austerities; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not engage in difficult practices and ascetic austerities.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already reached their final existence; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet reached their final existence.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already sat upon the seat of enlightenment; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet sat upon the seat of enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva may have Māras come to harass him, or this bodhisattva mahāsattva may have no Māras come to harass him.
Śāriputra, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to have attained the pure Dharma-eye.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure Buddha-eye?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“Immediately following the bodhicitta of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they enter the diamond-like samādhi (vajropama-samādhi), attain all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā), and realize the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, thereby attaining the pure buddha-eye.”
By attaining this eye, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see nothing that is not seen, hear nothing that is not heard, perceive nothing that is not perceived, and cognize nothing that is not cognized.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Buddha-eye. Śāriputra!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain such pure five eyes, they should train in the six perfections.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

In this way, these six perfections encompass all sublime virtuous dharmas, namely: all the virtuous dharmas of śrāvakas, the virtuous dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the virtuous dharmas of bodhisattvas, and the virtuous dharmas of tathāgatas.
“Śāriputra! If anyone were to say that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can encompass all supreme wholesome dharmas, this would be the correct statement.”
Why is this so? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the mother of all wholesome dharmas; it is able to give birth to all *pāramitās*, the five eyes, and other such sublime merits.
“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain such pure five eyes, they should study the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Śāriputra!”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should train in the five eyes.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the five eyes, they will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 481. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Śāriputra, Section Two, Part Four. "Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
"There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, are able to bring forth the perfection of the six superknowledges. Śāriputra!"

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the realm of miraculous feats (*ṛddhividhi-jñāna-sākṣātkriyā-abhijñā*), capable of performing various great miraculous transformations.

These include: shaking the great earth and all things within as many worlds of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges; transforming one into many and many into one; appearing and disappearing with swift and unimpeded ease; passing straight through mountain cliffs and walls as if through empty space; traveling through the air like a flying bird; emerging from and submerging into the earth as if in water; walking upon water as if on land; emitting smoke and flames from the body as if burning a high plateau; pouring forth streams of water from the body as if melting the Snow Mountains (*Himavat*); eclipsing the light of the sun and moon—whose divine merit and majestic power are otherwise difficult to withstand—by rubbing them with their hands; and even attaining mastery over the transformation of the body in the Śuddhāvāsa heavens. Such miraculous transformations are infinite in number.

Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such supernormal powers of the knowledge of the realm of phenomena, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not grasp at the nature of the superknowledge of the realization of supernormal powers, nor does he grasp at the activities of the realization of supernormal powers.
One who does not grasp at the supernormal knowledge of the realization of such psychic powers has no grasping whatsoever, whether toward grasping or non-grasping.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra,

this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not manifest such supernormal power of the knowledge of bases for the sake of amusement, except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).

Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the supernormal knowledge of the realization of psychic powers (ṛddhividhi-jñāna-sākṣātkriyābhijñā) brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine ear, which is supremely pure and surpasses that of humans and devas; they are able to hear, as it truly is, the various sounds of sentient and non-sentient beings throughout worlds in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”

That is to say, they universally hear the sounds of all the hells, the sounds of animals, the sounds of the realm of hungry ghosts, the sounds of humans, the sounds of devas, the sounds of śrāvakas, the sounds of pratyekabuddhas, the sounds of bodhisattvas, and the sounds of tathāgatas, as well as all other sounds of sentient and non-sentient beings—whether great or small—without obstruction or hindrance.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such application of the divine ear’s wisdom, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not grasp at the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the divine ear’s wisdom, nor does he grasp at the phenomena of realizing the divine ear’s wisdom.”
One who does not grasp at the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear wisdom has no grasping whatsoever toward either grasping or non-grasping.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable.

Śāriputra, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not bring forth such supernormal power of the divine ear for the sake of amusement; he does so solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of knowing (sarvajñajñāna).
Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear-wisdom, which is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal power of the knowledge of others’ minds, and are able to know, as they truly are, the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings throughout each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”

That is to say, he thoroughly knows other classes of sentient beings as they truly are: whether their minds are possessed of greed or free from greed; whether their minds are possessed of hatred or free from hatred; whether their minds are possessed of delusion or free from delusion; whether their minds are possessed of affection or free from affection; whether their minds are possessed of grasping or free from grasping; whether their minds are concentrated or scattered; whether their minds are narrow or vast; whether their minds are uplifted or depressed; whether their minds are tranquil or untranquil; whether their minds are agitated or unagitated; whether their minds are concentrated or unconcentrated; whether their minds are liberated or unliberated; whether their minds are with outflows or without outflows; whether their minds have fissures or are without fissures; and whether their minds are superior or not superior. All such things he knows as they truly are.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such applications of the knowledge of others' minds, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not grasp at the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of others' minds, nor does he grasp at the phenomena involved in realizing the knowledge of others' minds.”
One who does not grasp at the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of others' minds as being thus, has no grasping whatsoever regarding either grasping or non-grasping.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable.

Śāriputra, these bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not manifest such supernormal knowledge of others' minds for the sake of amusement; they do so solely for the purpose of attaining the knowledge of all modes.
Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of others' minds, which is brought forth by bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of recollecting past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā*), which enables them to accurately recollect all the past life events of every sentient being throughout as many world-systems in each of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.”

That is to say, he recollects, with respect to himself or others, the various past abodes for a duration of one moment of mind up to a hundred moments of mind; or again, he recollects, with respect to himself or others, the various past abodes for a duration of one day up to a hundred days; or again, he recollects, with respect to himself or others, the various past abodes for a duration of one month up to a hundred months; or again, he recollects, with respect to himself or others, the various past abodes for a duration of one year up to a hundred years; or again, he recollects, with respect to himself or others, the various past abodes for a duration of one *kalpa*, a hundred *kalpas*, a thousand *kalpas*, many hundreds of thousands of *kalpas*, even up to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* *kalpas*; or again, he recollects all the various past abodes belonging to the prior limit of existence.

That is to say: at such a time, in such a place, with such a name, such a clan, such a class, such food, such a duration of stay, such a lifespan, such suffering and pleasure; having passed away from that place, they were born here; and having passed away from here, they will be born there—with such physical appearance and such speech.
Whether briefly or in detail, he is able to recollect all matters of former existences.

Śāriputra, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such various applications of the knowledge of recollecting former existences, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not grasp at the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of recollecting former existences, nor does he grasp at the objects realized through that supernormal power of recollecting former existences.
One who does not grasp at the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives has no grasping whatsoever, whether toward grasping or non-grasping.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable. Śāriputra,

these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not manifest the supernormal power of the recollection of past lives for the sake of amusement, except solely for the purpose of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the superknowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives, which is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine eye, which is supremely pure and surpasses that of humans and devas. They are able to see, as it truly is, the various forms and appearances of sentient and non-sentient beings throughout each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. They see all sentient beings at the time of death and at the time of birth—whether of beautiful or ugly appearance, in happy or miserable realms, inferior or superior—and how they undergo the distinctions of rebirth according to the power and function of their karma:

namely, how these sentient beings have accomplished the three kinds of sublime conduct of body, speech, and mind, and by virtue of praising the holy ones and right view, at the dissolution of the body after death, shall ascend to happy realms, being born either in the heavens or among humans to experience various pleasures.”

In this way, sentient beings who commit the three types of misconduct of body, speech, and mind, and who, due to the causes and conditions of slandering the noble ones and holding wrong views, will at the dissolution of the body after death fall into the evil destinies; they may be born in hell, or among animals, or in the realm of hungry ghosts, or among the lowly, base, and defiled sentient beings in borderlands, where they undergo various sufferings and afflictions.

Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such a pure divine eye that he perceives the distinctions of cause and effect as sentient beings pass away from here and are reborn there throughout the realms of the ten directions, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not grasp at the nature of the supernormal power of the realization of divine-eye wisdom, nor does he grasp at the phenomena of the supernormal power of the realization of divine-eye wisdom.
One who does not grasp at the supernormal knowledge of realization through such divine eye wisdom has no grasping whatsoever, whether toward grasping or non-grasping.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable.

Śāriputra, it is not for the sake of amusement that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bring forth such supernormal knowledge of the divine eye; they do so solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of knowing.
Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the superknowledge of the realization of the divine eye-wisdom, brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā*), and are able to know, as it truly is, whether all sentient beings in each of the worlds of the ten directions—as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—have exhausted their outflows or have not yet exhausted them.”

Although a bodhisattva attains this supernormal power of the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣayābhijñā*), they do not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but proceed solely toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, because they no longer seek any other benefit or goal.

Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such application of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not grasp at the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the exhaustion of outflows, nor does he grasp at the phenomena of realizing the exhaustion of outflows.

One who does not grasp at the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows (āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) has no grasping whatsoever regarding either grasping or non-grasping.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Because their intrinsic nature is empty, because they are devoid of intrinsic nature, and because intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable.

Śāriputra, it is not for the sake of amusement that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bring forth such supernormal knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows; they do so solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes of being (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, brings forth the perfection of the superknowledge of the realization of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows.

"In this way, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they are swiftly able to fulfill the purity of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*). By means of the fulfillment of the purity of these six supernormal powers, they are swiftly able to realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, abide in the perfection of generosity and purify the path to the knowledge of all modes, because they are ultimately empty and free from stinginess;

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, abide in the perfection of ethical discipline and purify the path to the knowledge of all modes, because they are ultimately empty and free from transgressions."

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, abide in the perfection of patience and purify the path to the knowledge of all modes, because through ultimate emptiness they are free from anger;

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, abide in the perfection of diligence and purify the path to the knowledge of all modes, because through ultimate emptiness they are free from indolence;

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, abide in the perfection of meditative concentration and purify the path to the knowledge of all modes, because through ultimate emptiness they are free from distraction.

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom and abide in the perfection of wisdom, purifying the path to the knowledge of all modes, because through ultimate emptiness they are devoid of unwholesome wisdom.

“In this way, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they abide in the six perfections—whether individually or collectively—and purify the path to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Because of ultimate emptiness, because there is no coming or going, and because there is no grasping or abandoning, they provisionally designate generosity and stinginess, ethical discipline and immorality, patience and anger, diligence and laziness, meditative concentration and distraction, and wisdom and false wisdom; yet, within these, they remain without any attachment.”

Śāriputra! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp at generosity, does not grasp at stinginess, does not grasp at pure ethical discipline, does not grasp at transgression of ethical discipline, does not grasp at patience, does not grasp at anger, does not grasp at diligence, does not grasp at laziness, does not grasp at meditative concentration, does not grasp at distraction, does not grasp at wisdom, and does not grasp at false wisdom.
Śāriputra! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp at abuse or revilement, does not grasp at praise, does not grasp at contempt, and does not grasp at reverence.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
within the dharma of non-arising, there is neither reviling nor praise, neither contempt nor reverence.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* forever severs all objects of attachment. "Śāriputra!..."
When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, the merit they obtain is supreme and most sublime, such that it is not possessed by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Śāriputra! These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with their merits perfected, bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, and are thus able to swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they give rise to a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings."
Once this bodhisattva mahāsattva has given rise to a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings, they attain the equality of all sentient beings and the equality of all phenomena.
Having attained the equality of all sentient beings and attained the equality of all phenomena, this bodhisattva mahāsattva establishes all sentient beings within the equality of all phenomena.

In this present life, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas obtain the shared protection and mindfulness of all buddhas, the shared love and respect of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the shared veneration of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

In whatever place this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is born, his eyes shall never see unpleasant forms; his ears shall never hear unpleasant sounds; his nose shall never smell unpleasant odors; his tongue shall never taste unpleasant flavors; his body shall never feel unpleasant tactile sensations; and his mind shall never grasp unpleasant mental objects.
“Śāriputra! These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to never regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

When the Buddha spoke these words concerning the supreme merits of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom, many hundreds of bhikṣus rose from their seats, each removed his upper robe to offer it to the World-Honored One; having made their offerings, they all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled, and from his mouth issued rays of light of various colors.
Then, Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his left shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what cause and for what reason do you manifest this smile?
The manifestation of a smile by the Buddhas is never without cause or condition.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:

"These many hundreds of bhikṣus who have risen from their seats shall, after this, during the sixty-first kalpa known as the Star-like Kalpa, all become buddhas with one and the same name: Mahādhvajaketu Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān."
"After these bhikṣus have cast off this body, they shall be reborn in the eastern land of Akṣobhya Buddha, where they will cultivate the bodhisattva practices in the presence of that Buddha.

At that time, there were also sixty thousand devaputras who, hearing the Dharma corresponding to the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as taught by the Buddha, received it with joy and faith. The World-Honored One prophesied that they would, within the Dharma of the Tathāgata Maitreya, leave the household life with pure faith, diligently practice the holy life (*brahmacarya*), sever all afflictions, and realize parinirvāṇa.

At that time, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, the entire assembly in the gathering saw, in each of the ten directions, a thousand buddha-fields, as well as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas together with their respective assemblies.
Those buddha-fields were adorned with manifold virtues and were most delightful, such that the marks of adornment and purity in this Sahā world could not compare to them.
At that time, ten thousand beings in this assembly each made a vow, saying:
"By the merit we have cultivated, may we be reborn in those various Buddha-lands.
Then, the World-Honored One, knowing their aspirations, smiled once more, and from his face issued forth rays of light of various colors.
Then, Ānanda rose again from his seat and respectfully asked the Buddha about the cause and conditions for his smile.
At that time, the Buddha said to him:
"Do you now see these ten thousand people?"
Ānanda said: “Indeed! I have seen it.”

The Buddha said: "Now these ten thousand beings, when their lives here end, shall each attain rebirth in ten thousand buddha-fields in accordance with their vows. From that time forth, they shall never be separated from the Buddhas, and they shall constantly offer them worship, respect, honor, and praise. Having fully cultivated the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) until they are perfected, they shall realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). They shall all bear the same name: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān—namely, the Tathāgatas named Śrīkūṭarāja."

At that time, among the assembly, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, the Venerable Subhūti, and other great bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs well-known to all, as well as bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, upāsakas, and upāsikās, all rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, and together addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The perfection of wisdom attained by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is the great perfection,
the vast perfection, the foremost perfection, the honored perfection,
the supreme perfection, the wondrous perfection, and the most subtle perfection.
The pāramitās are the high pāramitās, the ultimate pāramitās, the superior pāramitās,
the unsurpassed pāramitās, the unsurpassably unsurpassed pāramitās, the equal pāramitās, the unequaled pāramitās, the peerless...
These pāramitās are the space-like pāramitā; they are the pāramitā without counterpart;
they are the pāramitā of the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are the pāramitā of the emptiness of common characteristics;
they are the pāramitā that accomplishes all meritorious qualities; they are the pāramitā that cannot be overcome.
The *pāramitā* is that which can subdue all other *pāramitās*. “World-Honored One!

Those Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who practice the *prajñāpāramitā* are the most honored, the most supreme, the most excellent, and the most wondrous; they possess great power and are able to practice the unequaled *dāna*, *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitā*; they are able to fulfill the unequaled *dāna*, *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitā*; they are able to perfect the unequaled *dāna*, *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitā*; and they are able to attain the unequaled self-body, namely, the body wonderfully adorned with boundless marks and signs.”
One is able to realize the peerless Dharma, namely, unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. World-Honored One,

it is also because of the complete perfection of the practice of the *prajñāpāramitā* that one attains peerless form, attains peerless feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, realizes peerless enlightenment, turns the peerless wheel of Dharma, and brings benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.

The Buddhas of the past, future, and present have also been able to realize, will realize, and are currently realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by practicing this profound perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to reach the ultimate further shore of all dharmas, they should study the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

"Bhagavān! All those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and so forth—should revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the disciples, bodhisattvas, and others, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.
All those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and so forth—should revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise all bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom.

Why is this? It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that humans and devas appear in the world; that is to say, great clans of kṣatriyas, great clans of brahmins, great clans of householders, and great clans of lay elders; as well as universal monarchs (*cakravartin*) and various minor kings who possess wealth, nobility, and sovereignty; and from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception, all appear in the world.
It is because of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there appear in the world the stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and all buddhas.
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the Jewels of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha appear in the world.

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that various means of livelihood and articles of comfort appear in the world, namely: food and drink, clothing, bedding, requisites for the sick, medicine, wealth, grain, precious gems, lamps, and other such things.
In brief, all the happiness of humans, devas, and others in the world, as well as the bliss of nirvana, do not exist without being due to such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections themselves and also encourage others to do so; therefore, by virtue of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom, all sentient beings obtain supreme benefit and happiness.
At that time, the World-Honored One manifested the mark of his tongue-organ, which completely covered the trichiliocosm.

From this tongue-mark, there further issued forth immeasurable rays of light of various colors, universally illuminating the Buddha-lands of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such that there was nowhere they did not pervade.

At that time, in each of the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there were immeasurable and innumerable great bodhisattvas. Seeing this great light, they felt uncertainty in their hearts and each went to the Buddha of their own realm, prostrated with reverence, and said:
"World-Honored One!..."
"By whose spiritual power is this?
And for what reason does this great radiance illuminate all these Buddha-lands?
At that time, each of those Buddhas replied in turn:

“In such-and-such a direction there is a buddha-field named Sahā; its Buddha is named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān. He is now proclaiming the Prajñāpāramitā for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, manifesting the mark of his tongue-root which completely covers the trichiliocosm.”

From that mark on the tongue, there further issued forth immeasurable rays of light of various colors, universally illuminating the Buddha-lands of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such that none were left untouched.
“The light we now behold is that which has manifested from the tongue-mark of that Buddha.
At that time, immeasurable and innumerable great bodhisattvas in those various realms, having heard this, were filled with joy and each addressed their respective Buddhas, saying:

“We wish to go to the Sahā world to behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and the various bodhisattvas, and furthermore to hear the Prajñāpāramitā. We only pray that the World-Honored One will compassionately grant us leave to go!”

Then, each of those Buddhas replied, "Now is the very time; go as you wish. At that time, the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, having received the Buddhas' permission, prostrated at their feet, circumambulated them to the right, and took their leave.

They prepared various jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, robes, necklaces, fragrant garlands, rare treasures, flowers of gold and silver, and so forth. They played and struck various kinds of sublime music, and in a mere moment, they arrived at the presence of this Buddha. Having made offerings, paid homage, and praised the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas with respect and reverence, they circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

At that time, the gods from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven each brought immeasurable varieties of fragrant garlands and immeasurable kinds of exquisite celestial flowers to the place where the Buddha was. Having made offerings, paid their respects, and honored and praised the Buddha and the bodhisattvas, they circumambulated them hundreds of thousands of times, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.

At that time, the various jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, robes, necklaces, fragrant flowers, rare treasures, and musical instruments offered by the great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions and the countless devas of the desire and form realms, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, soared into the air and merged into a single platform-canopy. Its dimensions equaled those of a trichiliocosm, and at each of the four corners of the platform’s summit stood a jeweled banner, adorned with every kind of ornament, most lovely and delightful to behold.

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing that the mental dispositions of the bodhisattvas and the assembly of devas who had come from the worlds of the ten directions were pure, and that they had already attained the patience of the non-arising of all phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), realizing that all phenomena are unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), without action (*anabhisaṃskāra*), neither arising nor ceasing, immediately smiled, and from his face issued forth rays of light of various colors.
Then Ānanda rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
For what cause and for what reason do you manifest this smile? The Great Sage does not manifest a smile without a cause or a condition."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:

“In this assembly now, hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings have already attained the patience regarding the non-arising of all phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti); they have realized that all phenomena are unconditioned and inactive, neither arising nor ceasing, and their aspirations are pure.”

By this cause and condition, the flowers and other various articles of offering that were presented leaped up into the air and formed a tiered canopy; at each of the four corners of the canopy's summit stood jeweled banners, adorned in myriad ways and most delightful to behold.
At that time, hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings in the assembly rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, and said to the World-Honored One:
“World-Honored One!

"In the future, we vow to become Buddhas, possessing the majestic power, marks, and signs of excellence just like the World-Honored One now; may our lands be adorned in the same manner, and may our assemblies of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, humans, and devas, as well as the wheels of Dharma we turn, all be identical to those of the present Buddha."
At that time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:

“These hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings who have risen from their seats shall, in a future age, practice the bodhisattva path for sixty-eight koṭis of great kalpas. During the Flower Accumulation Kalpa (Puṣpasaṃcaya-kalpa), they shall all attain buddhahood with one and the same name: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān—namely, the Tathāgata named Bodhyaṅgapuṣpa.”
3. The Chapter on Subhūti, Part Three: The First Section of the Chapter on Subhūti. At that time, the Bhagavān addressed Subhūti, saying:

“By means of your eloquence, you should proclaim the *prajñāpāramitā* for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; instruct and admonish those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they may reach the ultimate consummation of the *prajñāpāramitā*.”
At that time, the assembly of bodhisattvas, great disciples, and sons of gods all conceived this doubt:
"Will the Venerable Subhūti, by his own power, expound the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?"
"Is this by virtue of the World-Honored One’s majestic spiritual power?

At that time, Subhūti, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual strength, understood the doubts in the minds of the assembly of great śrāvakas and the sons of the gods, and addressed the venerable Śāriputra:
"Whatever the disciples of the Buddhas may dare to speak, there is nothing that does not rely upon the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power."

Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because the Buddha first proclaims the essential teachings for others; they then rely on the Buddha’s instructions to practice with diligent effort until they realize the true nature of all phenomena. Subsequently, when they in turn proclaim these teachings for others, provided that what they say does not contradict the nature of phenomena, all such instances are the skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) of the Tathāgata.

Śāriputra! It is by relying on the empowerment of the Buddha’s spiritual power that I shall proclaim the perfection of wisdom for the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is not through my own eloquence that I am able to perform this task.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the profound perfection of wisdom is not the domain of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Regarding what the Buddha has said about 'bodhisattvas,' of which dharma is this a designation when one speaks of a 'bodhisattva'?"

"Bhagavān! I do not perceive any dharma that can be called a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, nor do I perceive any dharma that can be called the prajñāpāramitā. How then am I to proclaim the prajñāpāramitā for the sake of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?"
"Bhagavān! By means of which perfection of wisdom do I instruct and admonish which bodhisattva mahāsattvas, so that they may reach the ultimate consummation in the perfection of wisdom?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti:

"There is only a mere designation called 'prajñāpāramitā,' and there is only a mere designation called 'the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Such designations are merely conventional constructs; they are neither born nor extinguished, neither internal nor external nor in between, because they are unapprehendable."

“Subhūti, you should know that just as the ‘self’ in the world exists only as a mere designation and cannot be found in reality, so too this designation is neither born nor extinguished; it is merely a conventional concept established through verbal expression.

Likewise, the sentient being, the life-principle, the creature, the nourisher, the person, the individual, the mind-born, the youth, the agent, the experiencer, the knower, and the seer—all such things exist only as mere designations and cannot be found in reality; thus these designations are neither born nor extinguished, being merely conventional concepts established through verbal expression.”
These various provisional designations do not exist internally, nor externally, nor in between the two, because they cannot be apprehended.
Thus it is, Subhūti!

Whether it be the perfection of wisdom, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or these two names—all are merely provisional phenomena. Such provisional phenomena are neither born nor extinguished; they exist only as provisional designations established by conventional speech, for they do not exist internally, nor externally, nor in between the two, because they cannot be apprehended.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! For example, just as internal form is merely a conventional dharma, so too these conventional dharmas are neither produced nor extinguished; they exist only as designations established by conceptual thought and verbal expression.

Likewise, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also merely conventional dharmas; these conventional dharmas are neither produced nor extinguished; they exist only as designations established by conceptual thought and verbal expression."
All these are merely conventional designations; these conventional designations do not exist internally, nor externally, nor in between the two, because they are unapprehendable.
Thus it is, Subhūti!

Whether it be the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or these two names—they are all conventional dharmas. Such conventional dharmas are neither born nor extinguished; they exist only as provisional designations and verbal expressions, being neither internal, nor external, nor in between, because they are ungraspable.
