“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive internal emptiness, nor do they rely on internal emptiness to contemplate external emptiness;

they do not perceive external emptiness, nor do they rely on external emptiness to contemplate internal emptiness, nor do they rely on external emptiness to contemplate both internal and external emptiness;

they do not perceive both internal and external emptiness, nor do they rely on both internal and external emptiness to contemplate external emptiness, nor do they rely on both internal and external emptiness to contemplate great emptiness.”

Not perceiving great emptiness, one does not, relying on great emptiness, contemplate internal and external emptiness; nor, relying on great emptiness, does one contemplate the emptiness of emptiness.

Not perceiving the emptiness of emptiness, one does not, relying on the emptiness of emptiness, contemplate great emptiness; nor, relying on the emptiness of emptiness, does one contemplate ultimate emptiness.

Not perceiving ultimate emptiness, one does not, relying on ultimate emptiness, contemplate the emptiness of emptiness; nor, relying on ultimate emptiness, does one contemplate the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.

One does not perceive the emptiness of the conditioned, nor does one, relying on the emptiness of the conditioned, contemplate the emptiness of the ultimate; nor, relying on the emptiness of the conditioned, does one contemplate the emptiness of the unconditioned.

One does not perceive the emptiness of the unconditioned, nor does one, relying on the emptiness of the unconditioned, contemplate the emptiness of the conditioned; nor, relying on the emptiness of the unconditioned, does one contemplate the emptiness of the absolute.

One does not perceive the emptiness of the absolute, nor does one, relying on the emptiness of the absolute, contemplate the emptiness of the unconditioned; nor, relying on the emptiness of the absolute, does one contemplate the emptiness of the boundless.

One does not perceive the emptiness of the limitless, nor does one contemplate ultimate emptiness by relying on the emptiness of the limitless, nor does one contemplate the emptiness of non-dispersal by relying on the emptiness of the limitless;

one does not perceive the emptiness of non-dispersal, nor does one contemplate the emptiness of the limitless by relying on the emptiness of non-dispersal, nor does one contemplate the emptiness of intrinsic nature by relying on the emptiness of non-dispersal;

one does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one contemplate the emptiness of non-dispersal by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one contemplate the emptiness of characteristics by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

One does not perceive the emptiness of marks, nor does one, relying on the emptiness of marks, contemplate the emptiness of intrinsic nature; nor, relying on the emptiness of marks, does one contemplate the emptiness of all phenomena.

One does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena, nor does one, relying on the emptiness of all phenomena, contemplate the emptiness of marks; nor, relying on the emptiness of all phenomena, does one contemplate the emptiness of non-existence.

One does not perceive the emptiness of non-existence, nor does one, relying on the emptiness of non-existence, contemplate the emptiness of all phenomena; nor, relying on the emptiness of non-existence, does one contemplate the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

One does not perceive the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nor does one rely on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence to contemplate the emptiness of non-existence. Śāriputra,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, it is called entering the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should train in the profound perfection of wisdom in this way: they should know form and its name, but not be attached to them; they should know feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as their names, but not be attached to them;
they should know the eye-base and its name, but not be attached to them; they should know the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, as well as their names, but not be attached to them."

One should know the sense-base of form and its designation, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharma*) and their designations, yet one should not be attached to them.

One should know the eye-element and its designation, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and their designations, yet one should not be attached to them.

One should know the element of form and its designation, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena and their designations, yet one should not be attached to them.

One should know the eye-consciousness element and its name, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements and their names, yet one should not be attached to them;
one should know the perfection of generosity and its name, yet one should not be attached to them;
one should know the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom and their names, yet one should not be attached to them.

One should know the four dhyānas and their names, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and their names, yet one should not be attached to them;

one should know the four foundations of mindfulness and their names, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, and their names, yet one should not be attached to them;
one should know the five eyes and their names, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the six supernormal powers and their names, yet one should not be attached to them.

One should know the ten powers of a Buddha and their names, yet one should not be attached to them; one should know the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and their names, yet one should not be attached to them.

In this way, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should know the mind of awakening and its name, yet they should not be attached to them; they should know the unequaled mind and its name, yet they should not be attached to them; they should know the vast mind and its name, yet they should not be attached to them.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
this mind is no-mind, because its intrinsic nature is pure.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"In what way is the intrinsic nature of the mind pure? Subhūti replied:

“The nature of this mind is neither associated with nor dissociated from greed; it is neither associated with nor dissociated from hatred; it is neither associated with nor dissociated from delusion; it is neither associated with nor dissociated from the fetters, latent tendencies, views, and hindrances; and it is neither associated with nor dissociated from the minds of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”
"Śāriputra! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that the mind is thus pure by nature.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed Subhūti, saying:
"Does this mind possess a nature that is non-mind?
Subhūti questioned, saying:
"Within a nature that is non-mind, can existence or non-existence be apprehended?"
Śāriputra said: “No, Subhūti!”
Subhūti replied, "Since neither existence nor non-existence can be apprehended within the nature of mind, how can one ask whether this mind exists as the nature of mind or not?"
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"What is meant by 'the nature of non-mind'? Subhūti replied:
"In all phenomena, there is no alteration and no conceptual differentiation; this is called the 'non-mind nature. Śāriputra asked:
"Is it only the mind that is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, or are all other phenomena likewise without alteration and without conceptual differentiation?"

Subhūti replied: "Just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too are form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness without alteration and without conceptual differentiation;

just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too are the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind without alteration and without conceptual differentiation."
Just as the mind is without change and without conceptual differentiation, so too are the sense-bases from form up to mental phenomena without change and without conceptual differentiation;
just as the mind is without change and without conceptual differentiation, so too are the elements from the eye-element up to the mind-element without change and without conceptual differentiation;

just as the mind is without change and without conceptual differentiation, so too are the objective realms from the form-realm up to the mental-phenomena-realm without change and without conceptual differentiation.

Just as the mind is without transformation and without conceptual differentiation, so too the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element is without transformation and without conceptual differentiation;

just as the mind is without transformation and without conceptual differentiation, so too the earth element up to the consciousness element is without transformation and without conceptual differentiation;
just as the mind is without transformation and without conceptual differentiation, so too ignorance up to old age and death is without transformation and without conceptual differentiation.

Just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom are without alteration and without conceptual differentiation;

just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are without alteration and without conceptual differentiation;
just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are without alteration and without conceptual differentiation.

Just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are without alteration and without conceptual differentiation;

just as the mind is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation, so too even unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is without alteration and without conceptual differentiation.
At that time, Śāriputra praised Subhūti, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
It is exactly as you have said.

You are a true son of the Buddha, born from the mind of the Buddha, born from the mouth of the Buddha, born from the Dharma of the Buddha, and born through transformation by the Dharma. Having received a share of the Buddha-Dharma rather than a share of material wealth, you have personally realized the various dharmas within yourself; with the eye of wisdom clearly seeing them, you are able to arise and speak. The Buddha has always declared that among his assembly of śrāvakas, you are foremost in dwelling in the concentration of non-contention (*araṇā-samādhi*); what the Buddha has said is true and not false.
Subhūti! All bodhisattva mahāsattvas should train in the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner. Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this way within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it should be known that they already abide on the stage of non-retrogression, are not separated from the *prajñāpāramitā*, and are able to contemplate the true nature of all phenomena as it truly is.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If sons or daughters of good family wish to train in the stage of a śrāvaka, they should diligently listen to, receive, read, recite, uphold, reflect upon according to principle, and examine with discernment this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, bringing it to ultimate completion.

Those who wish to train in the stage of a pratyekabuddha should likewise diligently listen to, receive, read, recite, uphold, reflect upon according to principle, and examine with discernment this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, bringing it to ultimate completion."

Those who wish to study the bodhisattva stages and the stage of a Tathāgata should likewise diligently listen to, receive, read, recite, firmly uphold, reflect upon according to principle, and scrutinize this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, bringing it to ultimate completion.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because within this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, the three vehicles of the Dharma are extensively explained and revealed.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the perfection of wisdom, they will have studied all the dharmas of the three vehicles in their entirety and will attain skillfulness in them.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Since I neither know nor perceive, and do not even see, either the perfection of wisdom or the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, how can I instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the perfection of wisdom?

“Bhagavān! I neither know nor perceive the *prajñāpāramitā*, nor do I see it; if I were to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas by means of this *prajñāpāramitā*, I would certainly feel regret.”
“World-Honored One!
Regarding all dharmas, I neither know nor attain them, nor do I see them. If I were to instruct or admonish the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas by means of these dharmas, I would certainly feel regret.”
“World-Honored One!

Regarding all dharmas, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything at all; how then can it be said that this is called a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and this is called the prajñāpāramitā?”
“World-Honored One!
The name ‘bodhisattva-mahāsattva’ and the name ‘prajñāpāramitā’ both abide nowhere, nor do they not abide. Why is this?
Since these two meanings do not exist, these two names both have no place of abiding, nor are they non-abiding.
"World-Honored One!
Regarding form up to consciousness, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything; how then can it be said that 'this is form' up to 'this is consciousness'?"
These names such as "form" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of these names—form and so forth—do not exist; therefore, these names for form and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the sense bases from the eye base up to the mind base, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease therein, nor do I see anything at all; how, then, can it be said that ‘this is the eye base’ up to ‘this is the mind base’?”
The names such as "eye-base" (cakṣur-āyatana) and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide. Why is this?
Because the referents of "eye-base" and so forth are non-existent, the names "eye-base" and so forth abide nowhere at all, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the sphere of form up to the sphere of mental phenomena, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything therein; how then can it be said that ‘this is the sphere of form’ up to ‘this is the sphere of mental phenomena’?”
Names such as "the sphere of form" (rūpāyatana) neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents (artha) of "the sphere of form" and so forth do not exist, names such as "the sphere of form" have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the eye-element up to the mind-element, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything therein; how, then, can it be said that ‘this is the eye-element’ up to ‘this is the mind-element’?”
The names such as "eye-element" (cakṣurdhātu) are all neither abiding anywhere nor non-abiding. Why is this?
Because the referents of "eye-element" and so forth do not exist; therefore, the names "eye-element" and so forth abide nowhere at all, yet they are not non-abiding.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the realm of form up to the realm of phenomena, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease therein, nor do I have any vision of them; how, then, can it be said that ‘this is the realm of form’ up to ‘this is the realm of phenomena’?”
Names such as "the realm of form" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of "the realm of form" and so forth do not exist, names such as "the realm of form" have no place of abiding whatsoever, yet they are also not non-abiding.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element, I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I see anything therein; how then can it be said that ‘this is the eye-consciousness element’ up to ‘this is the mind-consciousness element’?”
The names of the eye-consciousness element and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of the eye-consciousness element and so forth are non-existent, the names of the eye-consciousness element and so forth have no abode whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding eye-contact up to mind-contact, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything therein; how, then, can it be said that ‘this is eye-contact’ up to ‘this is mind-contact’?”
Names such as "eye-contact" and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of "eye-contact" and so forth do not exist, names such as "eye-contact" have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I have any vision of them. How, then, can it be said that ‘these are the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition,’ up to ‘these are the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition’?”
The names for all feelings and so forth produced with eye-contact as a condition neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referent-object (artha) of "feelings and so forth produced with eye-contact as a condition" does not exist; therefore, the names for "feelings and so forth produced with eye-contact as a condition" have no abode whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding ignorance up to old age and death, I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I see them; how then can it be said that ‘this is ignorance’ up to ‘this is old age and death’?”
The names "ignorance" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of ignorance and so forth are non-existent, the names "ignorance" and so forth abide nowhere at all, yet they do not not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the cessation of ignorance up to the cessation of old age and death, I do not know it, I do not attain it, nor do I see it, whether in terms of increase or decrease; how then can it be said that ‘this is the cessation of ignorance’ up to ‘this is the cessation of old age and death’?”
The names "the cessation of ignorance" and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of "the cessation of ignorance" and so forth are non-existent, the names "the cessation of ignorance" and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding greed, hatred, delusion, as well as the various fetters, latent tendencies, and views—whether they increase or decrease—I do not know them, I do not attain them, nor do I perceive them; how then can it be said that ‘this is greed’ and so forth?”
These names such as "greed" and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of "greed" and so forth are non-existent, these names for greed and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything at all; how then can it be said that ‘this is generosity’ up to ‘this is the perfection of wisdom’?”
The names "generosity" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of generosity and so forth do not exist, the names "generosity" and so forth abide nowhere at all, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding what is ‘self’ up to and including ‘the seer,’ I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease therein, nor do I see anything at all; how, then, can it be said that ‘this is my self’ up to and including ‘this is the seer’?”
These names "self" and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referent of "self" and so forth does not exist; therefore, these names "self" and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything therein; how, then, can it be said that ‘these are the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path’?”
The names of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are non-existent, the names of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth do not abide at all, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!
Regarding the three gates of liberation, I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I see them; how, then, can it be said that these are the three gates of liberation?”
The names of the three gates of liberation neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the meaning of the three gates of liberation is non-existent, the names of the three gates of liberation do not abide at all, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*), I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I see them; how then can it be said that ‘these are the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments’?”
The names such as "meditative concentration" (dhyāna) and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of meditative concentration and so forth are non-existent, the names of meditative concentration and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding my mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, mindfulness of the Saṅgha, mindfulness of ethical discipline, mindfulness of relinquishment, mindfulness of the devas, mindfulness of breathing, and mindfulness of death—I do not know, nor do I attain, nor do I perceive any increase or decrease in them. How, then, can it be said that ‘this is mindfulness of the Buddha’ up to ‘mindfulness of death’?”
Names such as "recollection of the Buddha" neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of "recollection of the Buddha" and so forth are non-existent, names such as "recollection of the Buddha" have no abode whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, I neither know nor attain their increase or decrease, nor do I see them; how, then, can it be said that ‘these are the five eyes and the six supernormal powers’?”
The names of the five eyes and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of the five eyes and so forth are non-existent, the names of the five eyes and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the Buddha’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I see them; how then can it be said that these are the Buddha’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
The names of the Buddha’s ten powers and so forth neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of the Buddha’s ten powers and so forth are non-existent; therefore, the names of the Buddha’s ten powers and so forth have no abode whatsoever, yet they are not non-abiding.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding these five aggregates of clinging—which are like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a mirage, like an image, like the moon in water, like a magical illusion, and like a transformation—I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease, nor do I see anything at all. How, then, can it be said that ‘these are the five aggregates of clinging which are like a dream and so forth’?”
The names of the five aggregates of clinging, such as "like a dream" and so forth, neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the referents of these five aggregates of clinging, such as "like a dream," are non-existent; therefore, these names of the five aggregates of clinging, such as "like a dream," do not abide at all, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding seclusion, tranquility, non-arising, non-ceasing, non-formation, non-destruction, non-defilement, non-purity, suchness, the dharma-realm, the stability of phenomena, the fixed nature of phenomena, and the limit of reality—I neither know nor attain any increase or decrease therein, nor do I perceive anything. How, then, can it be said that ‘this is seclusion’ up to ‘this is the limit of reality’?”
Terms such as "detachment" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of detachment and so forth do not exist, terms such as "detachment" have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding conditioned and unconditioned, outflowing and non-outflowing, and other such dharmas, I neither know nor perceive their increase or decrease, nor do I see them. How, then, can it be said that these are conditioned or unconditioned, outflowing or non-outflowing, and so forth?”
Names such as "conditioned" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of "conditioned" and so forth do not exist, names such as "conditioned" have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the phenomena of the past, future, and present, I neither know nor perceive them as increasing or decreasing, nor do I see anything of them; how, then, can it be said that ‘these are the phenomena of the past, future, and present’?”
Names such as "the past" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.
Why is this? Because the referents of the past and so forth do not exist, names such as "the past" have no place of abiding whatsoever, nor do they not abide.

“Bhagavān! Regarding all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the Bodhisattvas and the Saṅgha of Śrāvakas in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—I neither know nor perceive any increase or decrease therein, nor do I see anything of it. How, then, can it be said that these are all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the Bodhisattvas and the Saṅgha of Śrāvakas in the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges?”
Names such as the "ten directions" and so forth neither abide anywhere nor do they not abide.

Why is this? Because the meaning of the ten directions and so forth is non-existent; therefore, names such as the ten directions and so forth have no place of abiding whatsoever, yet they are not non-abiding either.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding all the dharmas as described above, I neither know nor obtain them whether they increase or decrease, nor do I perceive them. How, then, can it be said that ‘this is a bodhisattva mahāsattva’ or ‘this is the prajñāpāramitā’?”
“Blessed One!

Since I neither know nor perceive, nor do I see, either the perfection of wisdom or the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, how can I instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!
The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the name of the prajñāpāramitā are both non-abiding and yet not non-abiding. Why is this?

Because these two meanings do not exist, these two names both have no place of abiding, nor are they non-abiding. "World-Honored One! Such a combination of dharmas through causes and conditions is conventionally designated as 'bodhisattva-mahāsattva' and conventionally designated as 'prajñāpāramitā. These conventional designations cannot be expressed within the aggregates, sense bases, and elements, nor can they be expressed even within the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; "World-Honored One! Just as a person who has never before seen an elephant, upon seeing one for the first time, might touch its trunk and say, 'The elephant is like a plow handle,' or touch its ear and say, 'The elephant is like a winnowing basket,' or touch its shoulder and say, 'The elephant is like a mortar,' or touch its back and say, 'The elephant is like a large rock,' or touch its belly and say, 'The elephant is like a large jar,' or touch its tail and say, 'The elephant is like a rope'—World-Honored One, what do you think? Would that person truly know the elephant? Subhūti replied, "No, World-Honored One. The Buddha said, "Subhūti, it is the same for those bodhisattvas who, relying on the perfection of wisdom, practice the six perfections, yet do not understand the true nature of the perfection of wisdom. Because they do not understand the true nature of the perfection of wisdom, they do not understand the true nature of the six perfections. Because they do not understand the true nature of the six perfections, they do not understand the true nature of all dharmas. Because they do not understand the true nature of all dharmas, they do not understand the true nature of the bodhisattva. Because they do not understand the true nature of the bodhisattva, they do not understand the true nature of the Tathāgata. Because they do not understand the true nature of the Tathāgata, they do not understand the true nature of the Dharma. Because they do not understand the true nature of the Dharma, they do not understand the true nature of the Saṃgha. Because they do not understand the true nature of the Saṃgha, they do not understand the true nature of the path. Because they do not understand the true nature of the path, they do not understand the true nature of the fruit. Because they do not understand the true nature of the fruit, they do not understand the true nature of nirvāṇa. Because they do not understand the true nature of nirvāṇa, they do not understand the true nature of the three jewels. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three jewels, they do not understand the true nature of the five precepts. Because they do not understand the true nature of the five precepts, they do not understand the true nature of the ten wholesome paths of action. Because they do not understand the true nature of the ten wholesome paths of action, they do not understand the true nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Because they do not understand the true nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not understand the true nature of the four right efforts. Because they do not understand the true nature of the four right efforts, they do not understand the true nature of the four bases of psychic power. Because they do not understand the true nature of the four bases of psychic power, they do not understand the true nature of the five faculties. Because they do not understand the true nature of the five faculties, they do not understand the true nature of the five powers. Because they do not understand the true nature of the five powers, they do not understand the true nature of the seven factors of enlightenment. Because they do not understand the true nature of the seven factors of enlightenment, they do not understand the true nature of the noble eightfold path. Because they do not understand the true nature of the noble eightfold path, they do not understand the true nature of emptiness. Because they do not understand the true nature of emptiness, they do not understand the true nature of the signless. Because they do not understand the true nature of the signless, they do not understand the true nature of the wishless. Because they do not understand the true nature of the wishless, they do not understand the true nature of the unconditioned. Because they do not understand the true nature of the unconditioned, they do not understand the true nature of the conditioned. Because they do not understand the true nature of the conditioned, they do not understand the true nature of the ultimate truth. Because they do not understand the true nature of the ultimate truth, they do not understand the true nature of the conventional truth. Because they do not understand the true nature of the conventional truth, they do not understand the true nature of the two truths. Because they do not understand the true nature of the two truths, they do not understand the true nature of the three gates of liberation. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three gates of liberation, they do not understand the true nature of the three jewels. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three jewels, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of knowledge. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of knowledge, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of supernormal knowledge. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of supernormal knowledge, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of recollection. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of recollection, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of liberation. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of liberation, they do not understand the true nature of the three doors to liberation. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three doors to liberation, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of patience. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of patience, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of concentration. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of concentration, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of wisdom. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of wisdom, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of cultivation. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of cultivation, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of realization. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of realization, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of attainment. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of attainment, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of liberation. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of liberation, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of turning away. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of turning away, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of cessation. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of cessation, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of peace. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of peace, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of tranquility. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of tranquility, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of bliss. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of bliss, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of purity. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of purity, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of excellence. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of excellence, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of supremacy. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of supremacy, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of sovereignty. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of sovereignty, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of mastery. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of mastery, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-attachment. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-attachment, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-obstruction. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-obstruction, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-discrimination. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-discrimination, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-conceptualization. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-conceptualization, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-grasping. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-grasping, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-clinging. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-clinging, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-desire. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-desire, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-craving. Because they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-craving, they do not understand the true nature of the three kinds of non-thirst. Because they do

It cannot be expressed in terms of the five aggregates of clinging, which are like a dream and even like a magical transformation; it cannot be expressed in terms of tranquility, seclusion, and so forth; nor can it be expressed in terms of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the Bodhisattvas and the Saṅgha of Śrāvakas, throughout as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River.
Why is this? World-Honored One!
As previously stated, the increase and decrease of all dharmas are both unknowable and unobtainable, for there is nothing to be seen.
“World-Honored One!

As it has been taught, the names of the five aggregates and so forth cannot be designated as having any location; likewise, the name of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the name of the *prajñāpāramitā* also cannot be designated as having any location.”

Just as the name "dream" and so forth cannot be designated anywhere, just as the name "space" cannot be designated anywhere, just as the names "earth, water, fire, and wind" cannot be designated anywhere, just as the names "virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation" cannot be designated anywhere, just as the names "stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, tathāgata," and those various dharmas cannot be designated anywhere, just as the names for "wholesome and unwholesome," "permanent and impermanent," "bliss and suffering," "self and non-self," "quiescent and non-quiescent," and so forth—whether existent or non-existent—cannot all be designated anywhere, so too the name "bodhisattva-mahāsattva" and the name "prajñāpāramitā" cannot be designated anywhere.
Why is this so? Because all such names neither abide anywhere, nor do they not abide. Why is this?
Since these various meanings do not exist, these various names have no abode whatsoever, nor are they non-abiding.
“World-Honored One!

It is because of this meaning that I say regarding the Dharma, whether it increases or decreases, one neither knows nor attains it, and there is nothing to be seen. How then can it be said, ‘This is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva,’ or ‘This is called the prajñāpāramitā’?”

“Bhagavān! Since I neither know nor attain the meaning or the names of these two, and have no vision of them either, how am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, if one were to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas by means of this teaching, they would certainly come to feel regret.
World-Honored One!”

If, when the *prajñāpāramitā* is being proclaimed through these characteristics, a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind does not sink, is not distressed, and feels no regret; and if they likewise do not tremble, fear, or become terrified, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has definitely already dwelled in the stage of non-retrogression, dwelling by means of the skillful means of non-dwelling and remaining free from all attachment.

"Furthermore, World-Honored One, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in form (rūpa) up to consciousness (vijñāna); they should not abide in the sense base of the eye (cakṣur-āyatana) up to the sense base of the mind (mana-āyatana); they should not abide in the sense base of forms (rūpa-āyatana) up to the sense base of phenomena (dharma-āyatana); they should not abide in the element of the eye (cakṣurdhātu) up to the element of the mind (manodhātu); they should not abide in the element of forms (rūpadhātu) up to the element of phenomena (dharmadhātu); they should not abide in the element of eye-consciousness (cakṣurvijñānadhātu) up to the element of mind-consciousness (manovijñānadhātu); they should not abide in eye-contact (cakṣuḥ-saṃsparśa) up to mind-contact (manaḥ-saṃsparśa); they should not abide in the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; they should not abide in the earth element (pṛthivī-dhātu) up to the consciousness element (vijñāna-dhātu); and they should not abide in ignorance (avidyā) up to old age and death (jarāmaraṇa)."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
Form is empty of the nature of form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
“World-Honored One!

This form is empty, yet it is not separate from emptiness; emptiness does not exist apart from form. Form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also like this.”

For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not abide in form, nor even in consciousness; and so it is likewise for everything up to old age and death.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma)."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness.
“World-Honored One!

These four foundations of mindfulness are empty and are not the four foundations of mindfulness; the four foundations of mindfulness are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the four foundations of mindfulness. This is likewise true for everything up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not abide in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor even in the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,
when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in anything from the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
Giving is empty of the nature of giving.
World-Honored One!

This giving is empty and is not giving; giving does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from giving. Giving is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself giving. It is even so for the *prajñāpāramitā*.
For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not abide in anything from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not dwell upon syllables, nor should they dwell upon what is conveyed by syllables— whether conveyed by one, by two, or by many."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
All syllables are empty of the intrinsic nature of syllables.
“World-Honored One!

These syllables are empty, yet they are not the syllables themselves. The syllables do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the syllables. The syllables are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the syllables; it is likewise for that which is induced by the syllables.”
For this reason, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not dwell upon syllables nor upon that which is induced by syllables.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in the supernormal powers (abhijñā). Why is this?
World-Honored One!
The supernormal powers are empty of the nature of supernormal powers.
World-Honored One!

These supernormal powers are empty, yet they are not separate from supernormal powers; supernormal powers do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from supernormal powers. Supernormal powers are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself supernormal powers.
For this reason, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in the supernormal powers (abhijñā).
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not abide in form, nor even in consciousness, as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either empty or non-empty, as either with signs or signless, as either with aspirations or aspirationless, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.
Why is this? World-Honored One!
The dharmas such as form, whether permanent or impermanent, are empty of the nature of permanence or impermanence.
World-Honored One!

These dharmas such as form are empty of permanence and impermanence; it is not that there are dharmas other than form, etc., which are permanent or impermanent. Form and the other dharmas, whether permanent or impermanent, are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from form and the other dharmas, whether permanent or impermanent. Form and the other dharmas, whether permanent or impermanent, are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is form and the other dharmas, whether permanent or impermanent.

For this reason, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in form (rūpa) up to consciousness (vijñāna) as either permanent or impermanent; the same applies to whether these dharmas such as form are pleasant or painful, and so on, up to being distant or not distant.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,

when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the fixed nature of dharmas (dharmasthititā), or the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi)."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
True Suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness.
World-Honored One!

This suchness is emptiness, yet it is not separate from suchness; suchness does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from suchness. Suchness is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself suchness.

For this reason, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should not abide in suchness (tathatā); the same applies to the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the dharma-stability (dharmasthititā), and the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi).
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not abide in any of the dhāraṇī-doors or samādhi-doors."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
All dharani-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of dharani-doors.
World-Honored One!

This dharani-gate is empty and is not the dharani-gate; the dharani-gate is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the dharani-gate. The dharani-gate is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the dharani-gate.
For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they should not abide in any of the dhāraṇī-doors; the same applies to the samādhi-doors as well.
"Furthermore, Blessed One,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because their mind is entangled by the grasping at 'I' and 'mine,' they dwell upon form, and they dwell upon feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."
Because of dwelling in this state, one applies effort toward form, and applies effort toward feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.
Due to such application of effort, one is unable to practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because they, by means of their preparatory application (*prayoga*), are unable to embrace the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to study the profound *prajñāpāramitā* correctly, unable to bring the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because their mind is entangled by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, they may even abide in all the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi.”
Because of dwelling in this state, one applies oneself to the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi;
yet, because of such application, one is unable to practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because they are unable, through their application of effort, to embrace the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to study the profound *prajñāpāramitā* correctly, unable to bring the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).
"Why is this so? World-Honored One!
Form should not be grasped; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness should not be grasped."

Because form should not be grasped, it is not form; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness should not be grasped, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of form, up to and including consciousness, is empty,
World-Honored One.
One should not grasp at any of the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor should one grasp at the gateways of samādhi;
because the gateways of dhāraṇī are not to be grasped, they are not gateways of dhāraṇī, and because the gateways of samādhi are not to be grasped, they are also not gateways of samādhi.
Why is this? Because both the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi are empty by their very nature.
World-Honored One!
The perfect and profound *prajñāpāramitā* of right training that is thus grasped should also not be grasped; because it should not be grasped, it would not be *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they should contemplate all phenomena through the emptiness of intrinsic nature. When making this contemplation, the mind has no place of activity; this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s samādhi of non-appropriation."
This samādhi is subtle, sublime, vast, and immeasurable; it can accumulate boundless and unimpeded activities, and cannot be diverted or stolen away by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
That which is accomplished as the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) should also not be grasped; because it should not be grasped, it would not be the knowledge of all modes. Why is this?
This is because of inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence. Why is this so,
World-Honored One?
This knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is not attained through cultivation based on grasping at signs. Why is this?
Because all grasping at signs is affliction (kleśa).

“What are these marks? They are the marks of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; the marks of the eye up to the mind; the marks of visible forms up to mental phenomena; the marks of eye-consciousness up to mind-consciousness; the marks of the applications of mindfulness up to the factors of the path; the marks of the perfections, the superknowledges, and written characters; the marks of the ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the marks of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the marks of conditioned activity and suchness; the marks of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the fixed nature of dharmas, and the reality-limit; and the marks of the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi.”
To grasp at and become attached to these various signs is called affliction; therefore, one should not cultivate the attainment of the knowledge of all modes by grasping at signs.
If one were to cultivate the attainment of the knowledge of all modes by grasping at signs, then the brahmin Jayasena would not have had faith and understanding in the knowledge of all modes.
"What is called the characteristic of that resolute belief?

It is to generate pure faith in the *prajñāpāramitā* and, by the power of superior understanding (*adhimukti*), to contemplate and examine the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*). One does not take signs (*nimitta*) as a means, nor does one take the absence of signs as a means, because both signs and the absence of signs are ungraspable."

"Although this brahmin Jayasena has turned toward the Buddha-dharma through the power of faith and understanding, and is thus called a 'follower by faith,' he is nonetheless able to enter into the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) by means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature."

Having thus entered into realization, one does not grasp at the marks of form, nor does one grasp at the marks of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, up to and including the marks of the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of their own characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*), and thus neither the grasper (*grāhaka*) nor the grasped (*grāhya*) can be apprehended. Why is that so?

For this reason, the brahmin does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by means of an internal realization; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by means of an external realization; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by means of an internal-and-external realization; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by means of a realization through non-knowledge; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by means of a realization through something else; nor does he contemplate the knowledge of all modes by means of a realization through non-attainment.

Why is this? Such a brahmin does not perceive the omniscient wisdom that is observed, nor does he perceive the prajñā that observes, nor does he perceive the observer, the place of observation, or the time of observation.

Likewise, such a brahmin does not observe omniscient wisdom within internal form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; nor does he observe omniscient wisdom externally, or both internally and externally, within form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; nor does he observe omniscient wisdom apart from form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. This is likewise true for the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi.
Why is this? Whether internal, external, both internal and external, or apart from the internal and external, all are empty and unobtainable.

For these reasons, through various such gateways of detachment, the brahmin Jayasena conceived deep faith and understanding in the knowledge of all modes of knowing (*sarvajñajñāna*); he was without grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, because the true nature of all phenomena (*dharmatā*) is unobtainable.

Thus, when the brahmin had attained faith and understanding in the knowledge of all modes through the gateway of the signless, he did not grasp at signs in any phenomena, nor did he contemplate signlessness, because both phenomena with signs and phenomena without signs are ultimately unapprehendable.

In this way, by the power of resolute conviction (*adhimukti*), that brahmin neither grasps nor rejects any phenomena, for within the reality of the true nature (*dharmatā*) there is no grasping or rejecting.
At that time, that brahmin did not even cling to his own conviction, up to and including nirvāṇa itself.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty and cannot be grasped.
*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 484, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Subhūti, Section Four. "World-Honored One!..."
The Prajñāpāramitā realized by the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is likewise: it has no grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, for it enables one to go from this shore to the other shore;
if there were even the slightest grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, one would not be able to reach that other shore.

For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not grasp at form, nor even at consciousness, nor even at the doors of dhāraṇī or the doors of samādhi.
Why is this? Because all dharmas are ungraspable.
"World-Honored One!..."

Although all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not grasp at any phenomena, because the applications of mindfulness up to the factors of the path practiced through their original vows have not yet been perfected, and because the ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha realized through their original vows have not yet been accomplished, they do not enter parinirvāṇa in the interim by way of non-grasping at the characteristics of phenomena.
World-Honored One!

Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fulfill the applications of mindfulness they practice up to the factors of the path, and are able to accomplish the ten powers they realize up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they do not perceive them as such.

Why is this so? Because the applications of mindfulness that are practiced are not applications of mindfulness; even the factors of the path are not factors of the path; the ten powers that are realized are not the ten powers; and even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. This is because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is neither phenomenon nor non-phenomenon.

"Bhagavān! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, although they have no grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, they are nevertheless able to accomplish all supreme tasks."
"Furthermore, World-Honored One,
when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should carefully examine:
'What is this perfection of wisdom?'"
For what reason is it called *prajñāpāramitā*? Whose *prajñāpāramitā* is it?
And what is the function of this *prajñāpāramitā*?
“Blessed One! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should carefully observe this:
if phenomena are non-existent and unapprehendable, then within this non-existence of the perfection of wisdom, what is there to be questioned or scrutinized?”
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"In this context, what dharma is called 'non-existent' and 'unobtainable'? Subhūti replied:

"It is because from the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity are non-existent and cannot be apprehended."

“Śāriputra! Form up to consciousness is non-existent and unapprehendable; internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature is non-existent and unapprehendable; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path is non-existent and unapprehendable; the five eyes and six supernormal powers are non-existent and unapprehendable; the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-existent and unapprehendable; suchness up to the limit of reality is non-existent and unapprehendable; the stream-enterer up to the pratyekabuddha is non-existent and unapprehendable; the bodhisattva and all Buddhas are non-existent and unapprehendable; and omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent and unapprehendable—this is because of internal emptiness, and so on, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature.”

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and is able to conduct such a thorough investigation that all phenomena are found to be non-existent and unapprehendable, if their mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, does not sink, does not despair, and is neither sorrowful nor regretful, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is never separated from the perfection of wisdom.”
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"By what means is it known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to never abandon the perfection of wisdom?"

Subhūti replied: “This bodhisattva mahāsattva knows, as it truly is, that form up to consciousness is devoid of the intrinsic nature of form and so forth; he knows, as it truly is, that generosity up to the perfection of wisdom is devoid of the intrinsic nature of generosity and so forth; and so on, up to knowing, as it truly is, that the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and even knowing, as it truly is, that the limit of reality is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the limit of reality.”
"Śāriputra! By this you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to never abandon the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed Subhūti, saying:
"What is the intrinsic nature of form?
And so on, what is the intrinsic nature of the limit of reality? Subhūti replied:

"Form has non-existence as its intrinsic nature, and so on, up to the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), which has non-existence as its intrinsic nature. From this it should be known that form is devoid of the intrinsic nature of form, and so on, up to the limit of reality being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the limit of reality."
Śāriputra! Form is also devoid of the characteristic of form, and so on, up to the limit of reality, which is also devoid of the characteristic of the limit of reality. Śāriputra!

“Characteristics are also devoid of intrinsic nature, and intrinsic nature is also devoid of characteristics; characteristics are also devoid of characteristics, and intrinsic nature is also devoid of intrinsic nature.
At that time, Śāriputra said to Subhūti:
“If bodhisattvas train in this, they will swiftly be able to accomplish the knowledge of all modes.”
Subhūti replied: “So it is! So it is!”
If bodhisattvas train in this, they will swiftly accomplish the knowledge of all modes.
Why is that? Śāriputra!
"This is because these bodhisattvas know that all phenomena are without arising or ceasing. Śāriputra asked,
"For what reason are all phenomena without arising and without ceasing?"

Subhūti replied: "Because the intrinsic nature of form up to consciousness is empty, neither arising nor ceasing can be apprehended; and so on, because the intrinsic nature of the limit of reality is empty, neither arising nor ceasing can be apprehended."

“Śāriputra! If bodhisattvas can train in the perfection of wisdom in this way, they draw closer to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Just as they draw closer to the knowledge of all modes, so too do they attain purity of body, speech, mind, and marks.

As they attain these four kinds of purity—of body, speech, mind, and marks—so too do they give rise to no thoughts accompanied by greed, hatred, delusion, pride, flattery, deceit, stinginess, or dogmatic views.”

Because these bodhisattvas never give rise to thoughts of greed and the like, they ultimately do not fall into the wombs of women; they always undergo miraculous birth and remain free from the perilous evil realms, except when acting as a means to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.

These bodhisattvas travel from one buddha-field to another, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, and until they realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek, they are never separated from the Buddhas.

Śāriputra! Because these bodhisattvas study the perfection of wisdom without ever becoming weary or indolent, you should know that they are in close proximity to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattvas, lacking skillful means, practice the perfection of wisdom while coursing in form up to consciousness, they are coursing in its signs and are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to form, up to and including consciousness, as being either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, detached or not detached, or tranquil or not tranquil, such practice of their characteristics is not the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

If bodhisattvas, lacking skillful means, practice the perfection of wisdom, whether they practice the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, or practice the five eyes and six supernormal powers, or practice the ten powers of a buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—this is practicing their signs, not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
"If, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, bodhisattvas lack skillful means and form this thought:
'I am practicing the perfection of wisdom.'"
Because there is something apprehended, one is practicing its characteristics.
If one forms this thought: "I am a bodhisattva."
Because there is something apprehended, this is practicing its marks.
If one should form this thought:
"There is one who can thus practice the perfection of wisdom; this is the bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom," [then they are practicing with marks].
“Because there is something apprehended, this is practicing its marks.
World-Honored One!

If bodhisattvas engage in such various conceptual discriminations while practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), one should know that those bodhisattvas lack skillful means (upāyakauśalya) and are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
At that time, Subhūti said to Śāriputra:

"If bodhisattvas, lacking skillful means, practice the perfection of wisdom while dwelling upon conceptions and convictions regarding form up to consciousness, they apply themselves to those very things."
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, grief, despair, and various forms of suffering.
If one dwells upon the sphere of the eye up to the sphere of the mind with perception and conviction, then one applies oneself to those;
if one dwells upon the sphere of visible forms up to the sphere of mental phenomena with perception and conviction, then one applies oneself to those.
If one dwells in the conceptual resolve regarding the eye-element up to the mind-element, one applies effort toward them;
if one dwells in the conceptual resolve regarding the form-element up to the phenomena-element, one applies effort toward them;
if one dwells in the conceptual resolve regarding the eye-consciousness-element up to the mind-consciousness-element, one applies effort toward them.
If one dwells with perception and resolve regarding eye-contact, up to and including mind-contact, then one applies effort toward them;

if one dwells with perception and resolve regarding all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, then one applies effort toward them.
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, grief, despair, and various forms of suffering.

If Bodhisattvas, when practicing the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, dwell upon the conceptualization of and resolve for the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, they apply themselves to those;

if they dwell upon the conceptualization of and resolve for the five eyes, the six supernormal powers, the six perfections, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the ten powers of a Buddha, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they apply themselves to those.

If one forms a conceptualization of and resolves upon the states of a stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata, then one applies oneself to those [states].
"Because of their application [of effort], they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, grief, affliction, and various forms of suffering. Śāriputra!
Because these bodhisattvas lack skillful means, they cannot even attain the stages where śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas abide, much less attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!"
Śāriputra! If bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner, you should know that they are called those lacking skillful means; whatever they undertake will not be accomplished.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"How should one know when bodhisattva mahāsattvas possess skillful means while practicing the perfection of wisdom?"
Subhūti replied: "When bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage with form up to consciousness, nor do they engage with their characteristics;

they do not engage with form up to consciousness as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as empty or non-empty, as with signs or signless, as with aspirations or aspirationless, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached, nor do they engage with their characteristics."

Why is this? Śāriputra, these forms and so forth are empty, yet they are not [separate from] forms and so forth; forms and so forth are not apart from emptiness, and emptiness is not apart from forms and so forth. Forms and so forth are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself forms and so forth. It is likewise for the aggregates, the sense bases, the elements, dependent origination, the factors of awakening, the perfections, the five eyes, the six supernormal powers, the ten powers, and even the unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Śāriputra, you should know that when these bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they possess skillful means (upāyakauśalya).
Because these bodhisattvas possess skillful means, they are able to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).”

Śāriputra! When these bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not grasp at practicing the perfection of wisdom, nor do they grasp at not practicing it; they do not grasp at both practicing and not practicing, nor do they grasp at neither practicing nor not practicing; they do not even grasp at this non-grasping itself—how much less would they grasp at any other phenomena!
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason do these bodhisattvas not grasp even at the perfection of wisdom?"
Subhūti replied: “Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom is also unapprehendable. Why is this? Because...”
Śāriputra! It is because this Prajñāpāramitā likewise has non-existence as its intrinsic nature. Śāriputra!

For this reason, when bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they apprehend the practice of the perfection of wisdom, or its non-practice, or both practice and non-practice, or neither practice nor non-practice, or even the apprehension of non-apprehension—in all such cases, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because all phenomena take non-existence as their intrinsic nature, there is absolutely nothing to be grasped and nothing to which one may become attached.
Śāriputra! This is called the bodhisattva’s samādhi of non-attachment to all phenomena, of the absence of intrinsic nature, and of non-arising.
This samādhi is subtle, sublime, vast, and immeasurable; it can accomplish boundless and unimpeded activities, and is not shared by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
"If bodhisattvas are able to abide constantly and never forsake such a supreme samādhi, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"Do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by abiding constantly and never forsaking only this one supreme samādhi, or are there others as well?"

Subhūti replied: "It is not only by means of this one sublime samādhi that he constantly dwells without forsaking it, enabling all bodhisattvas to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; there are others as well."
Śāriputra asked: "What is this 'remainder'? Subhūti replied:
“Śāriputra! Furthermore,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess the *vikrāntagāminī* samādhi, the *ratnamudrā* samādhi, the *siṃhavikrīḍita* samādhi,
the *candraprabha* samādhi, the *candraketudhvaja* samādhi, and the *sarvadharmasāgara* samādhi.”
The Samādhi of Holding, the Samādhi of Contemplating the Summit, the Samādhi of Certainty in the Dharma-realm,
the Samādhi of the Determined Banner-Mark, the Samādhi of the Vajra Simile, the Samādhi of Entering the Seal of All Dharmas, the Samādhi of Abiding in Concentration,
the Samādhi of the King’s Seal, the Samādhi of the Power of Diligence, the Samādhi of Equal Emergence, and the Samādhi of Entering the Determination of Words.
The samādhi of meditative concentration, the samādhi of entering the designations, the samādhi of observing the directions, the samādhi of the seal of dhāraṇī, the samādhi of non-forgetfulness,
the samādhi of the universal convergence of all phenomena, the samādhi of pervading space, the samādhi of the vajra wheel,
the samādhi of the mark of the supreme banner, the samādhi of the mark of the imperial banner, and the samādhi of the moon.
The concentration of the banner-sign, the concentration of following firmness, the concentration of the lion’s boundless valor, the concentration of wide exposition,
the concentration of relinquishing the dust of craving, the concentration of universal illumination, the concentration of the unblinking eye,
the concentration of abiding in the signless, the concentration of certainty, the concentration of stainless conduct, and the concentration of infinite light.
The samādhi of Equanimity, the samādhi of Radiance, the samādhi of Universal Illumination, the samādhi of the Pure Seat, the samādhi of Stainless Light,
the samādhi of Arising Affection, the samādhi of the Lightning Lamp, the samādhi of the Inexhaustible, the samādhi of the Difficult to Conquer,
the samādhi of Possessing Majestic Splendor, the samādhi of Freedom from Exhaustion, and the samādhi of the Unsurpassed.
...the Samādhi of Manifestation, the Samādhi of the Sun Lamp, the Samādhi of the Pure Moon, the Samādhi of Pure Radiance, the Samādhi of Illuminating Clarity,
the Samādhi of Action and Non-action, the Samādhi of the Marks of Wisdom, the Samādhi of Abiding Mind, the Samādhi of Universal Radiance,
the Samādhi of Excellent Abiding, the Samādhi of Jewel Accumulation, and the Seal of the Sublime Dharma.
The Samādhi of Equality, the Samādhi of Equanimity toward All Phenomena, the Samādhi of Abandoning Attachment and Delight,
the Samādhi of Dharma-Cloud, the Samādhi of Dispersion, the Samādhi of Discerning the Phrases of Dharma, the Samādhi of Entering Equal Letters,
the Samādhi of Being Free from the Marks of Letters, the Samādhi of Severing the Object of Observation, the Samādhi of Non-Alteration, and the Chapter.

The concentration of categories, the concentration of entering the characteristics of meditative absorption, the concentration of signless practice, the concentration free from cataracts and darkness,
the concentration of endowed practice, the immovable concentration, the concentration of the tranquility of objective signs,
