How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seeks out extensive learning without ever becoming weary or satisfied, yet remains unattached to the words of the teachings they have heard?”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts diligent effort and forms this thought:

‘Whether it be this buddha-field or all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the worlds of the ten directions, I shall hear, receive, uphold, read, and recite the True Dharma they have taught; I shall study it to ultimate perfection so that nothing is left out, yet I shall not become attached to the words therein.’”
"This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to diligently seek extensive learning with constant insatiability, yet not to cling to the words of the teachings they have heard.
"World-Honored One!"

“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly practice the gift of Dharma with an undefiled mind, and while extensively transforming and guiding others, remain free from self-exaltation? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when proclaiming the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, does not even dedicate these roots of goodness toward enlightenment for their own sake, much less for the sake of seeking any other matter!

Though he extensively transforms and guides others, he remains free from arrogance and indolence; this is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva constantly practices the gift of Dharma with an unstained mind, widely opening the way for transformation without exalting himself.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva plants various roots of goodness to adorn and purify a buddha-field, and although they dedicate these merits, does not exalt themselves?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all roots of goodness with courageous diligence, desiring to adorn the pure lands of all buddhas and to purify the mental lands of both self and others, yet does not become conceited despite doing these things—this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to plant all roots of goodness to adorn and purify the land, and though employing dedication, not exalting himself.”
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, does not grow weary despite the boundless cycle of birth and death, yet remains free from arrogance and indolence?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, plants various roots of goodness to adorn and purify buddha-fields, and until they have fulfilled the knowledge of all modes and fully accomplished all buddha-dharmas, undergoes the diligent sufferings of boundless birth and death without weariness or self-exaltation—this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in order to transform sentient beings, to not weary of boundless birth and death while remaining free from arrogance and negligence.”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva single-mindedly seeks unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they never for a moment give rise to the mental orientations of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas because they possess a sense of shame and dread; yet, within those states, they harbor no attachment and do not give rise to aversion or disparagement. This is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwelling in shame and dread while remaining without attachment.

“Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the third bhūmi, they should constantly abide in these five dharmas, practicing them with diligence so that they may be swiftly perfected.”
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell in the forest hermitage (araṇya) without ever abandoning it?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, seeking unexcelled perfect enlightenment and in order to transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, never abandons the forest hermitage (āraṇyaka), this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dwelling in the forest hermitage without ever forsaking it.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delight in having few desires?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not even seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment for their own sake, much less worldly affairs or the goals of the two vehicles;
this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly delighting in few desires.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delight in contentment?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of seeking unexcelled, perfect enlightenment exclusively, does not give rise to attachment toward other matters, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is always content and delights in sufficiency.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandon the dhūta qualities?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly gives rise to the patience of discerning the Dharma regarding the profound teachings of the Buddha, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandoning the virtues of *dhūta*.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandon the various points of training?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva firmly maintains the precepts they have studied without wavering, yet is able to remain non-apprehensive of signs therein, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant non-abandonment of the various points of training.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to a mind of desire toward exquisite sensual pleasures, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s profound development of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delight in giving rise to a mind associated with nirvāṇa?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes that all phenomena are eternally without arising or activity, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly and joyfully giving rise to a mind associated with nirvāṇa.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always delight in relinquishing all things? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva never grasps at internal or external phenomena, this is what it means for a bodhisattva-mahāsattva to always delight in relinquishing all things.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind does not sink at any time? “Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s mind is never attached to any station of consciousness, this is what it means for a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s mind to never sink at any time.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain free from attachment toward all things? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage in any mental deliberation regarding any phenomena, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to be constantly free from attachment toward all phenomena.
"Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the fourth stage, they should always uphold these ten dharmas and never abandon them even for a moment."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from household life?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is inclined by nature to travel through the lands of all buddhas, and wherever he is born always delights in leaving the home life—shaving off his hair and beard, holding the alms bowl, donning the three dharma robes, and appearing as a śramaṇa—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s necessary distancing from the household life.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from bhikṣuṇīs?
“Suvīra! [The Buddha replied.]

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should always remain far removed from bhikṣuṇīs, not dwelling with them for even as long as a finger-snap, and furthermore never giving rise to improper thoughts toward them—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva remaining far removed from bhikṣuṇīs.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from stinginess regarding their home?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:

"I should, throughout the long night, bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings; now, these sentient beings have, by the power of their own merit, encountered such a noble householder who is a donor. Therefore, I ought not to harbor stinginess or envy toward them."
“Having reflected thus, he remains far removed from stinginess regarding his home; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from stinginess regarding his home.
“World-Honored One, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from anger and strife within assemblies?”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva thinks thus:

‘If there are śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas within a gathering, or if the essential teachings corresponding to the two vehicles are being expounded therein, it may cause me to fall away from the mind of great enlightenment; therefore, I must certainly distance myself from such gatherings.’”
He further reflects:

"Those who engage in anger and strife cause sentient beings to give rise to hatred and harm, thereby committing various kinds of evil and unwholesome karma; this not only obstructs the happy realms, let alone the Great Enlightenment!"
"Therefore, one must certainly remain far removed from anger and contention.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from anger and contention within assemblies.
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid praising themselves and disparaging others?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives absolutely nothing regarding internal or external phenomena, they should therefore avoid praising themselves and disparaging others; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should avoid praising themselves and disparaging others."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from the ten paths of unwholesome action?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:
"Even these ten unwholesome actions can obstruct rebirth in the happy realms of humans and devas; how much more so would they act as obstacles to the Noble Path and Great Enlightenment!"
"Therefore, I must certainly distance myself from them.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance himself from the ten paths of unwholesome action.
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from overweening pride and arrogance? "Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any internal or external phenomena whatsoever that could give rise to overweening pride and arrogance, they must therefore certainly remain far removed from such overweening pride and arrogance; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from overweening pride and arrogance."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from perversions? “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva observes that perverted phenomena are entirely unobtainable, they must therefore certainly distance themselves from perversion; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s necessary distancing from perversion.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from hesitation?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva observes that matters of hesitation are entirely unfindable, they should therefore resolutely distance themselves from hesitation; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s distancing themselves from hesitation.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive at all the existence of the phenomena of greed, hatred, and delusion, they should therefore remain far removed from these three poisons; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva remaining far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion.
“Subhūti, you should know that when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the fifth stage, they should always remain far removed from these ten dharmas and must not associate with them.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the six pāramitās? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Furthermore, by abiding in these six perfections, the noble assemblies of the three vehicles (triyāna) are able to cross to the further shore of the five kinds of objects of knowledge (pañca-jñeya).
What are the five? First, the past; second, the future.
Third is the present;
fourth is the unconditioned; fifth is the ineffable.
Therefore, a bodhisattva must certainly bring to perfection the six pāramitās, such as generosity; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the six pāramitās.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from the mind of a śrāvaka?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"The mind of the śrāvaka vehicle is not the path for realizing unsurpassed bodhi, and therefore it should be abandoned. Why is that?"
"Because they are weary of birth and death.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the mind of a śrāvaka.
"World-Honored One!"
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the mind of a pratyekabuddha? “Subhūti,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought as this:”
"The mind of the Pratyekabuddhayāna is not the path for realizing unsurpassed bodhi and should therefore be avoided.
Why is this? Because it delights in [personal] nirvāṇa."
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance themselves from the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
"World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance themselves from a mind of feverish affliction?"
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘The mind that fears the heat and affliction of saṃsāra is not the path for realizing unsurpassed bodhi, and therefore it should be abandoned.’”
Why is this? Because they fear birth and death.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from a mind of feverish affliction.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid the mind of displeasure and distress when seeing a beggar approach?
“Suvīra! [the Buddha replied.]
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
"This mind of displeasure and distress is not the path for realizing unsurpassed bodhi, and therefore it should be abandoned."
Why is this? Because it contradicts compassion.
This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should remain far removed from a mind of displeasure and distress when seeing a beggar approach.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid the mind of regret and longing for all things that have been given away? “Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"This mind of regret is not the path for realizing unsurpassed bodhi, and therefore it should be abandoned. Why is that?..."
Because it violates his original vow.
That is to say, when he first resolved upon the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), he made this vow:
"Whatever I possess that is requested by seekers, let it not be in vain, according to their desires."
"Why do you now feel regret after having given?
This is why a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance himself from the mind that feels sorrowful regret and longing for all things once they have been relinquished.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid a mind that uses skillful means to equivocate when someone comes seeking [something]?
“Suvīra! [The Buddha replied.]
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"This deceitful and distracted mind is not the path for realizing unsurpassed bodhi, and therefore it should be abandoned. Why is this so?"
Because it violates my original vow.
That is to say, when I first gave rise to the bodhicitta, I made this vow:
"Whatever I possess that is requested by those who come seeking, I shall not let it go in vain according to their desires."
"How could one now practice such deceptive evasion toward them?
This is why a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance themselves from the mind of using skillful means to evade those who come seeking.

“Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the sixth stage, they should constantly fulfill the six dharmas previously mentioned and should distance themselves from the six dharmas subsequently mentioned, yet without grasping at anything therein.”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 493. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Subhūti, Section Ten: “World-Honored One!”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from the grasping at a self, up to and including the grasping at a viewer? "Subhūti,
it is when a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that from the self up to the viewer, they are ultimately non-existent."

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the self, up to and including the viewer, cannot be apprehended; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to a self, up to and including attachment to a viewer.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from the clinging to annihilation?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena cannot be severed, why is this?
Because all phenomena are ultimately unarisen and thus lack the meaning of severance; this is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should always remain far removed from the attachment to severance.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from the grasping at permanence?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the permanent nature of all phenomena does not exist, why is this?

Because all phenomena are without arising and without cessation, and are neither annihilated nor eternal; thus, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to permanence.

[The Buddha replied: “Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that defiled phenomena (*saṃkleśa-dharma*) are ultimately non-existent.

Why is this? Because defiled phenomena are by nature dissociated from intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-vivikta*). This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from the perception of signs (*nimitta-saṃjñā*).
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from attachment to views? “Excellent One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any intrinsic nature in the various views, why is this?
It is because the dharmas that are perceived cannot be apprehended; thus, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to views.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from attachment to name-and-form?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because a real name-and-form cannot be apprehended; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to name-and-form.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from clinging to the aggregates?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of the aggregates is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because the nature of accumulated phenomena cannot be apprehended; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to the aggregates.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from attachment to a dwelling place? “Excellent One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all sense bases (*āyatana*) is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) of the gates of birth cannot be apprehended; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to the sense bases.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from attachment to the elements?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all elements (*dhātu*) is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because the sustaining nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) cannot be apprehended; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to the elements.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from clinging to [the four] truths? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all truths is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because false dharmas cannot be apprehended; this is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to the truths.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from attachment to dependent origination?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen:]”
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of dependent origination is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because phenomena such as ignorance cannot be apprehended; this is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to dependent origination.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from dwelling in attachment to the grasping of the three realms?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of the three realms is entirely non-existent, why is this?
Because the phenomena bound to the three realms cannot be apprehended. This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment and clinging to the three realms.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from all attachment to dharmas?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is entirely non-existent, why is this?

Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is merely a conventional designation, and like space, it is ungraspable; thus, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from all attachment to phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from all conceptual attachments regarding what is correct and what is incorrect with respect to all phenomena? “Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the nature of all phenomena, they find neither that which is "in accordance with reality" nor that which is "not in accordance with reality. Why is this?

Because such phenomena are unapprehendable. This is why a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to all phenomena as being either in accordance with reality or not in accordance with reality.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from attachment to views based on the Buddha?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that by relying on the view of a Buddha, one cannot see the Buddha.
Why is this? Because the self-nature of the true Buddha is invisible. This is why a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from the attachment to the view that relies upon a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from clinging to views based on phenomena?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that by relying on views regarding phenomena one cannot perceive phenomena, why is this?
Because the intrinsic nature of true phenomena is invisible; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from the attachment to views regarding phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from the clinging to views that rely upon the Saṃgha?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that by relying on the view of the Saṃgha, one cannot see the Saṃgha. Why is this?

Because the true nature of the Saṃgha is signless and unconditioned, and thus it cannot be seen. This is why a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from the attachment to the view of relying on the Saṃgha.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from clinging to views based on the precepts? “Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the natures of both transgression and merit are neither truly existent. Why is this?

Because whether it be transgression or merit, they are merely provisional designations and cannot be apprehended. This is why a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from attachment to views based on the precepts.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from clinging to views based on emptiness?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all empty phenomena as being entirely non-existent and incapable of being perceived—why is this?

Because the intrinsic nature of emptiness is neither existent nor non-existent, and thus cannot be seen; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from the clinging to views based on emptiness.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always remain far removed from weariness and fear regarding emptiness?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, there is no contradiction or conflict between non-emptiness and emptiness; therefore, neither aversion nor fear can be found.

Why is this? Because all phenomena that possess intrinsic nature may be objects of aversion or fear, whereas emptiness is not a phenomenon possessing intrinsic nature and thus should not be an object of aversion or fear; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from aversion and fear toward emptiness.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the thorough penetration of emptiness? “Excellent One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the thorough penetration of emptiness.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the realization of the signless? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize any signs, this is for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to always fulfill the realization of signlessness.
“World-Honored One!”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness?
Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind dwells nowhere among the phenomena of the three realms, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the purity of the three wheels? “Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the ten paths of wholesome action in complete purity, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who should always fulfill the purity of the three wheels.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill compassion for sentient beings, and yet remain without attachment toward sentient beings?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained great compassion and the adornment of a pure land, yet remains entirely without attachment, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who should always fulfill compassionate concern for sentient beings, while remaining without attachment toward those beings.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the vision of the equality of all phenomena, as well as remain without attachment therein?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither increases nor decreases any dharma, and therein neither grasps nor dwells, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who should always fulfill the vision of the equality of all dharmas, and who remains without attachment therein.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the vision of the equality of all sentient beings, and how should they remain without attachment therein?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither increases nor decreases [the nature of] sentient beings, and within this neither grasps nor dwells, this is what is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the vision of the equality of all sentient beings, as well as being without attachment therein.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the ultimate penetration into the true nature of reality, and how should they remain without attachment therein?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the true principle of all phenomena, thoroughly penetrates it as it truly is yet has nothing to penetrate, and within this state neither grasps nor dwells—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the ultimate penetration into the true principle, and being without attachment therein.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the wisdom of the endurance of non-arising?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva endures that all phenomena are without arising and without cessation, without creation and without fabrication, and realizes that name-and-form are ultimately non-arising, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the wisdom of the endurance of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the principle of the single characteristic of all phenomena? “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage in dualistic characteristics regarding all phenomena, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the principle of the single characteristic of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the elimination of conceptual discrimination?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, this constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the elimination of conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the complete distancing from all conceptualizations? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from all notions of smallness, greatness, and immeasurability, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of being far removed from all notions.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the complete distancing from all views? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from the views of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the like, this constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the thorough removal of all views.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the complete distancing from afflictions? “Excellent One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abandons all outflows, afflictions, and the continuity of habitual tendencies, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the distancing from afflictions.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill skillfulness in śamatha and vipaśyanā?
“Excellent One! [The Buddha replied:]
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of skill in śamatha and vipaśyanā.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the taming of the mind-nature?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not cling to nor delight in the phenomena of the three realms, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the subduing of the mental continuum.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the state of a tranquil mind-nature?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva skillfully restrains the six sense faculties, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the nature of a tranquil mind.
"World-Honored One!"
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom?

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates and attains the Buddha-eye, achieving definitive understanding of all phenomena without obstruction, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfilling the nature of unimpeded wisdom."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill being free from attachment?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to skillfully relinquish these six bases, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of being free from attachment.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the ability to go to all buddha-fields according to his heart’s desire, manifesting his own body within the assemblies of those buddhas?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme supernormal powers and travels to the buddha-fields to serve and make offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, requesting them to turn the wheel of Dharma for the benefit of all beings—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfilling the ability to travel to any buddha-field at will and manifesting his own body within the assemblies of those Buddhas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva mahāsattvas abide in the seventh stage, they should always remain far removed from the former twenty dharmas and should bring the latter twenty dharmas to perfection.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the thorough entry into the mental activities of all sentient beings?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with single-minded simultaneous wisdom, knows as they truly are the distinctions among the minds and mental factors and their modes of activity of all sentient beings, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the realization of the mental activities of all sentient beings.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the playful mastery of supernormal powers?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sports with various sovereign supernormal powers, traveling from one buddha-field to another for the sake of approaching and making offerings to the Buddhas, yet is able to remain free from the thought of "traveling through buddha-fields," this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the sport of supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the vision of all buddha-fields, and in accordance with what is seen, personally adorn and purify various buddha-fields?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while dwelling in a single buddha-field, is able to see the boundless buddha-fields of the ten directions and can also manifest them therein, yet never gives rise to the notion of ‘buddha-fields,’ [he is practicing the perfection of wisdom].”

Furthermore, for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity, they manifest themselves in the position of a universal monarch (cakravartin) within a trichiliocosm to adorn themselves; yet they are also able to relinquish it without any attachment. This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of beholding all buddha-fields, adorning and purifying various buddha-fields exactly as they have seen them.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly fulfill the service and offering to all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and observe the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, correctly discriminates the meaning and intent of the Dharma, this is called serving and making offerings to the Buddhas by means of the Dharma; furthermore, to contemplate the Dharma-body of the Buddhas with discernment—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly fulfilling the service and offering to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and contemplating the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is.”
“Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the eighth stage, they should constantly bring these four dharmas to perfection.
“World-Honored One!”
“What is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s wisdom that constantly and perfectly fulfills the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties? ‘Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, abiding in the ten powers of a buddha, knows as they truly are the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s wisdom that constantly and perfectly fulfills the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties.’”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the complete purification of the Buddha-field? “Sudhana!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, purifies the mental activities of all sentient beings without any attachment, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the purification of buddha-fields.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the samādhi of being like an illusion and frequently enter various meditative concentrations?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, although they can accomplish all activities, their mind remains entirely unmoved regarding phenomena.

Furthermore, because they have cultivated this samādhi to full maturity, it manifests repeatedly without the need for deliberate application; this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the illusion-like samādhi and the frequent entry into various meditative absorptions.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the practice of entering into various states of existence by manifesting through spontaneous birth, in order to bring the roots of goodness of all sentient beings to maturity?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring to maturity the sublime roots of goodness in all sentient beings, enters into various states of existence and manifests birth according to what is appropriate for them—this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva entering into various states of existence and manifesting spontaneous birth in accordance with the maturation of the roots of goodness of sentient beings.”
“Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the ninth stage, they should always bring these four dharmas to perfection.
“World-Honored One!”
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the great vow to encompass infinite realms, so that whatever is vowed is all brought to realization? "Excellent One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already cultivated the six perfections to the point of ultimate perfection, whether for the purpose of purifying the buddha-fields or for the purpose of maturing sentient beings, they are able to fulfill all their aspirations according to their wishes without any deficiency; this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the great vow to encompass infinite locations, ensuring that whatever is wished for is fully realized.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the knowledge of the diverse sounds of all classes of beings, from devas and nāgas as extensively described, up to humans and non-humans?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme analytical knowledge of language (*nirukti-pratisaṃvid*) and thoroughly understands the distinctions among the vocal expressions of sentient beings, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the knowledge of the diverse sounds of all classes of beings, from devas and nāgas as extensively described, up to humans and non-humans.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill unhindered eloquence?
“Suvīra! [The Buddha said:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme analytical knowledge of unimpeded eloquence, being able to teach inexhaustibly for the sake of all sentient beings, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of unimpeded eloquent discourse.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is always born into the lineage of the great bodhisattvas of the past, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the perfection of lineage.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the perfection of having a complete retinue?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has as their retinue exclusively an immeasurable and innumerable assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and not other miscellaneous classes of beings, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the perfection of a complete retinue.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the perfection of the birth-body?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

If, at the time of his first birth, a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s body is fully endowed with all the marks and signs of excellence, emits great radiance that universally illumines boundless Buddha-worlds, and causes those worlds to undergo six kinds of movement, such that all sentient beings who encounter it obtain benefit and happiness—this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the perfection of the birth-body.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the perfection of renunciation? “Excellent One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, at the time of going forth, surrounded by immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings who respect and praise him, proceeds to the site of enlightenment, shaves off his hair and beard, dons the three dharma robes, and takes up the alms bowl; and if he guides immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, causing them to ride upon the three vehicles toward parinirvāṇa—this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of the full endowment of going forth, which should always be fulfilled.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the complete adornment of the bodhi tree?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, through the power of their preeminent roots of goodness and vast vows, brings forth such a tree of great enlightenment (bodhivṛkṣa), with lapis lazuli for its trunk and pure gold for its roots, while its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are all composed of the most excellent seven treasures.

That tree is so high and broad that it completely covers the trichiliocosm Buddha-field; its radiance shines forth, pervading the worlds of the Ganges-sand number of Buddhas throughout the ten directions, such that no sentient being who sees it fails to receive benefit. This is the perfection of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of the adornment of the Bodhi tree.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva always fulfill the complete accomplishment and perfection of all merits? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the sublime provisions of merit and wisdom, matures sentient beings, and purifies buddha-fields, this constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant fulfillment of all merits and the complete accomplishment of their endowment.
“Subhūti, you should know that when bodhisattva mahāsattvas abide in the tenth stage, they should always bring these twelve dharmas to perfection.
“World-Honored One!”

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having dwelled in the tenth stage, brings to full perfection all the superior dharmas previously cultivated in the preceding stages, such that he may be said to be no different from the Tathāgatas?
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already perfected the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
he has already perfected the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.”
They have already perfected the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
they have already perfected the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they have already perfected inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature;
they have already perfected suchness up to the inconceivable realm; and they have already perfected suffering, its origin, and its cessation.
...the Noble Truth of the Path; having perfected the eight liberations and the nine successive concentrations;
having perfected all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi; having perfected the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
having perfected the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and being endowed with one—

All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*): if one further permanently severs the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*), one then abides in the stage of a Buddha (*buddhabhūmi*).

For this reason it is said: once a bodhisattva mahāsattva has dwelled in the tenth stage, they have brought to full completion all the superior dharmas previously cultivated in the preceding stages, and they may be said to be no different from the Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwelling in the tenth stage proceed to the stage of a Tathāgata?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

“This bodhisattva mahāsattva, through skillful means, practices the six pāramitās and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment—expounded at length up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—and is endowed with all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Transcending the stage of pure observation, the stage of the lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the pratyekabuddhas, and the stage of the bodhisattvas, he further permanently severs the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*), and thus becomes a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, abiding in the stage of a Tathāgata.”
"Subhūti! In this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwelling in the tenth stage proceeds toward the stage of a Tathāgata.
Thus it is, Subhūti!"
Based on this, one should know that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have set out upon the Great Vehicle.
Furthermore, Subhūti, as to your subsequent question: "From where does such a Great Vehicle emerge, and where does it abide?"
"Subhūti, you should know this:

such a Great Vehicle emerges from within the three realms and abides within the knowledge of all modes; yet, because it employs non-duality as its skillful means, there is neither emergence nor abiding."

Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these two dharmas are neither joined nor dispersed; they are neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
The markless dharma has neither emergence nor abiding.
Why is this? The markless dharma has not already emerged or already abided; it will not emerge or abide in the future; it does not emerge or abide in the present.
“Subhūti, you should know this!

Whoever wishes for signless phenomena to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish for true thusness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm to also have emergence and abiding.”
Why is this? Because from true thusness up to the inconceivable realm, none can emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
Why is this? Because true thusness is empty of the intrinsic nature of true thusness, and so on, up to the inconceivable realm being empty of the intrinsic nature of the inconceivable realm.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, the realm of non-arising, the realm of non-extinction, the realm of non-nature, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, and the realm of the unconditioned to also have emergence and abiding.
Why is this? Because the realm of cessation, up to and including the unconditioned realm, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.

Why is this? Because the realm of cessation is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realm of cessation, and so on, up to the unconditioned realm being empty of the intrinsic nature of the unconditioned realm.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence or abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of form, up to the emptiness of consciousness, to also have emergence and abiding. Why is this so?

From the emptiness of form up to the emptiness of consciousness, none of these can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna). Why is this?
Form is empty; form is empty of its own intrinsic nature. This extends up to consciousness being empty; consciousness is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti, you should know this:

whoever wishes for unconditioned phenomena to have emergence or abiding, would thereby wish for the emptiness of the eye-base, up to the emptiness of the mind-base, to also have emergence and abiding."

Why is this? Because the sense-base of the eye is empty, up to and including the sense-base of the mind, none of them can emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the eye-base is empty; the eye-base is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on, up to the mind-base, which is empty; the mind-base is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the markless dharma to have emergence or abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the sphere of form, up to the emptiness of the sphere of mental phenomena, to have emergence and abiding as well.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the sphere of form up to the emptiness of the sphere of mental phenomena cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.

Why is this? Because the sphere of form is empty; the sphere of form is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on, up to the sphere of phenomena being empty; the sphere of phenomena is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
Subhūti, you should know this!

If one wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence or abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the eye-element up to the emptiness of the mind-element to also have emergence and abiding.
Why is this? Because the eye-element is empty, up to and including the mind-element, none of them can emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.

Why is this? Because the eye-element is empty; the eye-element is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on up to the mind-element, which is empty; the mind-element is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

Should anyone wish to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the form realm, up to the emptiness of the dharma realm, to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the form realm up to the emptiness of the dharma realm cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the realm of form is empty, and the emptiness of the realm of form is the emptiness of its own nature; and so on, up to the realm of phenomena being empty, and the emptiness of the realm of phenomena being the emptiness of its own nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the emptiness of the mind-consciousness element, to have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the eye-consciousness element is empty, up to and including the mind-consciousness element; none of these can emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Why is this? Because the eye-consciousness element is empty; the eye-consciousness element is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on up to the mind-consciousness element, which is empty; the mind-consciousness element is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
whoever wishes for signless phenomena to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the emptiness of eye-contact, up to the emptiness of mind-contact, to also have emergence and abiding.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of eye-contact, up to and including the emptiness of mind-contact, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide in the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because eye-contact is empty; the self-nature of eye-contact is empty. This extends up to: mental contact is empty; the self-nature of mental contact is empty.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence and abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to the emptiness of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, to have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? The various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty, up to and including the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition; none of these can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty; the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of their own intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*). This extends up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, which are empty; the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are empty of their own intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti, you should know this!

Should anyone wish for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish for the emptiness of the earth element, up to the emptiness of the consciousness element, to have emergence and abiding.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the earth element, up to and including the emptiness of the consciousness element, cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the earth element is empty, the space element is empty, and their own-nature is empty; and so on, up to the consciousness element, which is empty and its own-nature is empty.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of causal conditions, up to the emptiness of dominant conditions, to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because from the emptiness of causes and conditions up to the emptiness of the dominant condition, none can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.

Why is this? Because conditioned causes and conditions are empty, and the self-nature of conditioned causes and conditions is empty; even up to dominant conditions being empty, and the self-nature of dominant conditions being empty.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence and abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of ignorance up to the emptiness of old age and death to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because from the emptiness of ignorance up to the emptiness of old age and death, none can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of omniscience.

Why is this? Because ignorance is empty; the emptiness of ignorance is itself empty of intrinsic nature. This continues up to old age and death, which are empty; the emptiness of old age and death is itself empty of intrinsic nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause dreams, illusions, echoes, reflections, shadows, light, mirages, flowers in the sky, cities of Gandharvas, and transformations to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because dream-objects, and even matters of transformation, cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Why is this? Because the nature of dream-objects is empty of the intrinsic nature of dream-objects, and even the nature of transformed phenomena is empty of the intrinsic nature of transformed phenomena.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would thereby wish to cause the emptiness of the perfection of giving, up to the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the perfection of giving, up to and including the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the perfection of giving is empty, the perfection of giving is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on, up to the perfection of wisdom being empty, the perfection of wisdom being empty of its own intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

whoever wishes for signless phenomena to have emergence or abiding, they likewise wish for everything from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-essential nature to have emergence and abiding.”

Why is this? Because from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, none of these can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.

Why is this? Because internal emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, and so on, up to the fact that the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are empty; none of them can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of being.
Why is this? Because the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are empty; the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to the emptiness of the eightfold noble path, to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the emptiness of the eightfold noble path, cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.

Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty; the four foundations of mindfulness are empty of their own intrinsic nature. This extends up to the eightfold noble path being empty; the eightfold noble path is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti, you should know that whoever wishes for signless phenomena to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the emptiness of the four dhyānas to also have emergence and abiding.”
Why is this? The four dhyānas are empty;
none of them can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the four dhyānas are empty; the four dhyānas are empty of their own intrinsic nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence and abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the four immeasurables and emptiness to also have emergence and abiding. Why is this so?
The four immeasurables and emptiness are all unable to emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Because the four immeasurables and emptiness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and emptiness.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the emptiness of the four formless concentrations to also have emergence and abiding.”
Why is this? The four formless absorptions are empty; none of them can lead one out from within the three realms, nor can they lead one to abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Because the four formless absorptions are empty; the four formless absorptions are empty of their own intrinsic nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause emptiness, the signless, and the wishless gates of liberation—which are themselves empty—to have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are themselves empty; they cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes.

Why is this? Because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and their intrinsic nature is empty.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the emptiness of the eight liberations to also have emergence and abiding.”
Why is this? The eight liberations are empty; none of them can emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Because the eight liberations are empty; the eight liberations are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!

If one wishes to cause the dharma of signlessness to have emergence and abiding, then one would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the nine successive attainments to have emergence and abiding. Why is this so?
The nine successive attainments are empty; none of them can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the wisdom of all-knowledge. Why is this?
The nine successive attainments are empty because the self-nature of the nine successive attainments is empty.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

Should anyone wish for the signless dharmas to have emergence or abiding, they would thereby wish for the emptiness of the stage of pure observation, up to and including the emptiness of the stage of the Tathāgata, also to have emergence and abiding."

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the stage of pure observation (*śuddhadarśana-bhūmi*) up to the emptiness of the stage of the Tathāgata cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Why is this? Because the stage of pure observation is empty; the stage of pure observation is empty of its own intrinsic nature, and so on, up to the stage of the Tathāgata, which is empty; the stage of the Tathāgata is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the emptiness of the Stage of Extreme Joy, up to the emptiness of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, to also have emergence and abiding.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the emptiness of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of being.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the Ground of Utmost Joy is the emptiness of the self-nature of the Ground of Utmost Joy, and so on, up to the emptiness of the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma being the emptiness of the self-nature of the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, wishes for all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi—which are empty—to likewise have emergence and abiding.”
Why is this? Because all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi are empty; none can emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Because all dharani-doors and samadhi-doors are empty; all dharani-doors and samadhi-doors are empty because their intrinsic nature is empty.
“Subhūti, you should know this!
Should anyone wish for signless phenomena to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish for the emptiness of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers to have emergence and abiding.”
Why is this? Because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are empty; none of them can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are empty; the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are empty because their own-being is empty.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, up to the emptiness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, up to and including the emptiness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, none of them can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the ten powers of the Tathāgata are empty; the ten powers of the Tathāgata are empty of intrinsic nature. This extends even to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, which are empty; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity—which are empty—to also have emergence and abiding.”

Why is this so? Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are empty; they are all unable to emerge from the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes of being.

Why is this? Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are empty; the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they would likewise wish to cause the emptiness of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects to also have emergence and abiding.

Why is this? Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are empty; none of them can emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Why is this? Because all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are empty; and all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty because their intrinsic nature (svabhāva) is empty.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding, they likewise wish for the stream-enterer to have birth in the miserable realms, the once-returner to have frequent rebirths, the non-returner to have birth in the desire realm, and for the various bodhisattvas, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and tathāgatas to have subsequent births, as well as emergence and abiding.”

Why is this? Because for a stream-enterer, as well as for those up to and including a Tathāgata, any further births—even those in the evil destinies—cannot escape from within the three realms, nor can they abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the rebirth in the evil destinies of a stream-enterer is empty of the intrinsic nature of the rebirth in the evil destinies of a stream-enterer, and so on, up to the subsequent existence of a Tathāgata being empty of the intrinsic nature of the subsequent existence of a Tathāgata.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, wishes for the emptiness of the stream-enterer, up to the emptiness of the Tathāgata, also to have emergence and abiding.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the stream-enterer, up to and including the emptiness of the Tathāgata, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the stream-enterer is empty, the emptiness of the stream-enterer is the emptiness of its own nature; and so on, up to the Tathāgata being empty, the emptiness of the Tathāgata is the emptiness of his own nature.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If one wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence and abiding, then one likewise wishes to cause names, conceptualizations, designations, and verbal expressions to have emergence and abiding as well.

Why is this so? Names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions are all unable to emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Because names, conceptualizations, designations, and verbal expressions are empty of the intrinsic nature of names, conceptualizations, designations, and verbal expressions.
"Subhūti, you should know this:

whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or abiding, they wish for that which is unborn and unceasing, unstained and unpurified, signless and unconditioned to likewise have emergence and abiding."

Why is this? Because that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and without marks and unconditioned, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.

Why is this? Because they are empty of intrinsic nature—being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity, and being signless, unconditioned, without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity, and signless and unconditioned.
"Subhūti, you should know!

For this reason, I say that this Great Vehicle emerges from the triple world and abides within the knowledge of all modes; yet, because it employs non-duality as its skillful means, there is neither emergence nor abiding."
Why is this? Because phenomena that are signless (animitta) are without movement or change; thus, it cannot be said that they have an emergence or a dwelling.
*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 491, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Subhūti, Section Eleven. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Regarding your subsequent question, "In what does such a Great Vehicle abide?",
Subhūti, you should know that such a Great Vehicle abides nowhere at all.
Why is this so? Because all phenomena are entirely without abiding.
For what reason?
Because the abiding place of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
Subhūti, you should know that this Great Vehicle dwells in non-dwelling by means of non-apprehension as its skillful method.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

for example, true thusness (*tathatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm do not abide, nor do they not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because the self-nature of suchness, up to and including the self-nature of the inconceivable realm, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

Because the self-nature of suchness is empty of the self-nature of suchness, and so on, up to the fact that the self-nature of the inconceivable realm is empty of the self-nature of the inconceivable realm.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

For example, the realm of abandonment, the realm of detachment, the realm of cessation, the realm of security, the realm of tranquility, the realm of non-arising, the realm of non-cessation, the realm of non-defilement, the realm of non-purity, the realm of non-action, and the realm of the unconditioned are neither abiding nor non-abiding; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this so? Because the intrinsic nature of the realm of cessation, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the unconditioned realm, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

The nature of the realm of abandonment is empty of the nature of the realm of abandonment, up to and including the fact that the nature of the unconditioned realm is empty of the nature of the unconditioned realm.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, just as the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*) up to the aggregate of consciousness (*vijñānaskandha*) neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*): it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the aggregate of form up to the intrinsic nature of the aggregate of consciousness is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the aggregate of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the aggregate of form, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the aggregate of consciousness being empty of the intrinsic nature of the aggregate of consciousness.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
For example, just as the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the sense base of the eye up to the intrinsic nature of the sense base of the mind is entirely without abiding and without non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-base is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-base, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the mind-base being empty of the intrinsic nature of the mind-base.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

For example, just as the sense-sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the sense-sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*): it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the sense-sphere of form up to the intrinsic nature of the sense-sphere of phenomena is such that there is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the sphere of phenomena being empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of phenomena.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"
For example, the eye-element up to the mind-element neither abides nor does not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-element up to the intrinsic nature of the mind-element is entirely without abiding and without non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-element, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the mind-element being empty of the intrinsic nature of the mind-element.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

For example, just as the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) up to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*): it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the realm of form up to the intrinsic nature of the realm of phenomena is entirely without abiding and without non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the form realm is empty of the intrinsic nature of the form realm, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm being empty of the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

For example, from the visual consciousness element up to the mental consciousness element, they neither abide nor do they not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this so?
