The intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the mind-consciousness element, neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the mind-consciousness element being empty of the intrinsic nature of the mind-consciousness element.
“Subhūti, you should know this!
For example, from visual contact up to mental contact, there is neither abiding nor non-abiding; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of eye-contact, up to and including the intrinsic nature of mind-contact, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The intrinsic nature of eye-contact is empty of the intrinsic nature of eye-contact, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of mind-contact being empty of the intrinsic nature of mind-contact.
"Subhūti, you should know this:

for example, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding."

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including the intrinsic nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is empty of the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and so on, up to the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition being empty of the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.
"Subhūti, you should know this:
just as the element of earth, up to and including the element of consciousness, neither abides nor does not abide, so too the Great Vehicle neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the earth element, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the consciousness element, is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
The earth element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the earth element; this continues up to the consciousness element, which is empty of the intrinsic nature of the consciousness element.
"Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, from the causal condition up to the dominant condition, neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding."
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) up to the sovereign condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
The nature of causal conditions is empty of the nature of causal conditions, up to and including the nature of dominant conditions being empty of the nature of dominant conditions.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!
For example, from ignorance up to old age and death, they neither abide nor do they not abide; the Mahāyāna is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of ignorance, up to the intrinsic nature of old age and death, is entirely without abiding and without non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of ignorance is empty of the intrinsic nature of ignorance, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of old age and death being empty of the intrinsic nature of old age and death.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

For example, just as a dream, an illusion, an echo, a reflection, a shadow, a mirage, a flower in the sky, a city of Gandharvas, and a magical transformation neither abide nor do not abide, so too is the Mahāyāna: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of dream-objects, up to and including the intrinsic nature of transformed phenomena, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

The intrinsic nature of a dream is empty of the intrinsic nature of a dream, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of a transformed phenomenon being empty of the intrinsic nature of a transformed phenomenon.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
For example, from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, neither abides nor does not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom being empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, neither abides nor does not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

The intrinsic nature of internal emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature being empty of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
For example, the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this so?
The noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are by their very nature neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the self-nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path is empty of the self-nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, just as the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path neither abide nor do not abide, so too the Great Vehicle neither abides nor does not abide.”
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to the intrinsic nature of the eightfold noble path, is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?

Because the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the eight branches of the noble path being empty of the intrinsic nature of the eight branches of the noble path.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
For example, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
The four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
"Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are neither abiding nor non-abiding; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding."
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
For example, just as the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
The eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are, by their very nature, neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the self-nature of the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments is empty of the self-nature of the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, from the Stage of Pure Vision up to the Stage of the Tathāgata, they neither abide nor do they not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this so? Because the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Pure Observation, up to the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Tathāgata, is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?

The stage of pure observation is empty of the intrinsic nature of the stage of pure observation, up to and including the stage of the Tathāgata, which is empty of the intrinsic nature of the stage of the Tathāgata.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!"
For example, from the Ground of Utmost Joy up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, there is neither abiding nor non-abiding; the Mahāyāna is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this so?
Because the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Extreme Joy, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Extreme Joy is empty of the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Extreme Joy, and so on, up to the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma being empty of the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma.
“Subhūti, you should know this!
For example, the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
Because the intrinsic nature of the dharani-gates and samadhi-gates is empty of an intrinsic nature of dharani-gates and samadhi-gates.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
For example, the five eyes and six supernormal powers neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the five eyes and six supernormal powers is entirely without abiding and without non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers is empty of the intrinsic nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

For example, just as the ten powers of a Buddha up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha neither abide nor do not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
The intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is empty of the intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers, and so on, up to the fact that the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are, by their very essence, neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?

The quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are empty of the intrinsic nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

For example, just as all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) neither abide nor do not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*): it neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?

Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are empty of the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, the rebirth in the evil destinies of a stream-enterer, the frequent rebirths of a once-returner, the rebirth in the desire realm of a non-returner, the self-benefiting rebirths of bodhisattvas, and the subsequent rebirths of arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and tathāgatas—these are neither abiding nor non-abiding. The Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”

Why is this? Because for a stream-enterer, the inherent nature of birth in the evil realms, up to and including the inherent nature of the Tathāgata’s subsequent birth, is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because for a stream-enterer, the nature of rebirth in the evil destinies is empty of the nature of rebirth in the evil destinies; and so on, up to the fact that for a Tathāgata, the nature of subsequent existence is empty of the nature of subsequent existence.

“Subhūti, you should know this: for example, the state of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; one entering the once-returning stage and the fruit of once-returning; one entering the non-returning stage and the fruit of non-returning; one entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship; one entering the stage of a pratyekabuddha and the fruit of a pratyekabuddha; and the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas—these are neither abiding nor non-abiding. The Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of those who have entered the stream, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because the nature of one who has entered the stream is empty of the nature of one who has entered the stream, and so on, up to the nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas being empty of the nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
“Subhūti, you should know this:
for example, names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions neither abide nor do not abide; the Great Vehicle is likewise neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this so? Because names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions have no abiding in intrinsic nature, nor do they have non-abiding. Why is that?
Because names, designations, conventions, and the intrinsic nature of verbal expression are empty of the intrinsic nature of names, designations, conventions, and verbal expression.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

For example, just as that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without action and without conditioning, neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle—neither abiding nor not abiding.

Why is this? Because, being without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and without action or conditioning, their intrinsic nature abides neither in existence nor in non-existence. Why is that?

Because it is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without action and without conditioning, and because its intrinsic nature is empty—being by nature without arising and cessation, without defilement and purity, and without action and conditioning.
"Subhūti! For this reason, I say that although this Great Vehicle has no abode, it dwells in non-abiding by means of non-duality."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Regarding what you later asked—
'Who, moreover, will set out by means of this Great Vehicle?'—
Subhūti, you should know this!"
There is no one at all who, mounting this Great Vehicle, departs from it. Why is this?
Whether it be the vehicle mounted, the one who mounts, the means by which, the purpose for which, the place, or the time—all such things are non-existent and entirely unobtainable.

Because all phenomena are non-existent and entirely unattainable, it cannot be said that there is a vehicle to be mounted, a rider who mounts it, the means by which one mounts, the purpose for which one mounts, the place where one mounts, or the time at which one mounts.
For this reason, there is absolutely no one who departs by means of this Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Because all dharmas are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because ‘I’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended, one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

Likewise, because sentient beings, life-principles, born beings, nourished beings, persons, individuals, mind-born beings, youths, agents, experiencers, knowers, and seers do not exist and cannot be apprehended, those who ride the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because everything from suchness up to the inconceivable realm is non-existent and unattainable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unattainable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti, you should know that because the realm of abandonment,

the realm of detachment, the realm of cessation, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, the realm of non-arising, the realm of non-cessation, the realm of non-defilement, the realm of non-purity, the realm of non-action, and the realm of the unconditioned are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that because the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the sense-base of form up to the sense-base of mental phenomena are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the eye-element up to the mind-element are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the realm of form up to the realm of phenomena are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the visual consciousness element up to the mental consciousness element are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because eye-contact, up to and including mind-contact, are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are non-existent and unapprehendable, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is unapprehendable.”
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the element of earth up to the element of consciousness are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the causal conditions,
up to and including the dominant conditions, are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because ignorance through to old age and death are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because dream-objects,

illusions, echoes, reflections, shadows, mirages, flowers in the sky, cities of Gandharvas, and transformations are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

Because everything from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable, even one who rides the Great Vehicle is unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that because the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are all non-existent and unapprehendable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this so?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the four dhyānas,
the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are all non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this so?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because from the Stage of Pure Observation up to the Stage of the Tathāgata, all are non-existent and unobtainable, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is unobtainable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that because everything from the Ground of Extreme Joy up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma is non-existent and unobtainable, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is unobtainable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because all dharani-doors and samadhi-doors are non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this so?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are all non-existent and unattainable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unattainable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are all non-existent and unattainable, even one who rides the Great Vehicle is unattainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are both non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*),

the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is likewise unobtainable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

Because the rebirths in the evil destinies of stream-enterers, the frequent rebirths of once-returners, the rebirths in the desire realm of non-returners, the self-benefiting rebirths of bodhisattvas, and the subsequent rebirths of arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and tathāgatas are all non-existent and unapprehendable, those who ride the Great Vehicle are likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

Because the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry; the candidate for the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of once-returning; the candidate for the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of non-returning; the candidate for the fruit of arhatship and the fruit of arhatship; the candidate for the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood and the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood; and the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti, you should know this!

Because the stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, and tathāgata are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

Because names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti,

you should know that because non-arising and non-ceasing, non-defilement and non-purity, and the unconditioned and the uncreated are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the past, future, and middle limits are all non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because going and coming,
moving and staying are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because whether death or birth, increase or decrease, all are non-existent and cannot be apprehended, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that since the purification of Buddha-fields and the maturation of sentient beings are both non-existent and unapprehendable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure. Furthermore, Subhūti!
In this context, because what dharma is it that cannot be apprehended that it is said to be "unapprehendable"?
"Subhūti, you should know:
herein, because the nature of a self up to the nature of a seer cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of a self, up to and including the nature of a seer, cannot be found in the past, cannot be found in the future, and cannot be found in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of true thusness up to the nature of the inconceivable realm cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Because the nature of true thusness, up to the nature of the inconceivable realm, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the realm of abandonment (*prahāṇadhātu*) up to the nature of the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the realm of cessation, up to the nature of the unconditioned realm, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the aggregate of form up to the nature of the aggregate of consciousness cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the aggregate of form, up to the nature of the aggregate of consciousness, is not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and is not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the eye-base up to the nature of the mind-base cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because the nature of the eye-base, up to and including the nature of the mind-base, has not been obtained, will not be obtained, and is not currently being obtained, as it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the nature of the sphere of mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the sense-base of form, up to the nature of the sense-base of mental phenomena, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the eye-element up to the nature of the mind-element cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because the nature of the eye-element, up to and including the nature of the mind-element, has not been obtained, will not be obtained, and is not currently being obtained, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the nature of the dharma realm (*dharmadhātu*) cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because the nature of the form realm, up to the nature of the dharma realm, has not been obtained, will not be obtained, and is not being obtained, as it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the eye-consciousness element up to the nature of the mind-consciousness element cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the nature of the mind-consciousness element, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, being ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of eye-contact up to the nature of mind-contact cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of eye-contact, up to and including the nature of mind-contact, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,

because the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the earth element up to the nature of the consciousness element cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Because the nature of the earth element, up to and including the nature of the consciousness element, has not been obtained, will not be obtained, and is not currently being obtained, as they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) up to the nature of the sovereign condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of causal conditions, up to and including the nature of dominant conditions, is neither obtainable in the past, nor obtainable in the future, nor obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of ignorance up to the nature of old age and death cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of ignorance, up to and including the nature of old age and death, is not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and is not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of dream-objects up to the nature of transformed phenomena cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of dream-visions, up to and including the nature of emanated phenomena, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, as they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the perfection of generosity up to the nature of the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of generosity, up to and including the nature of the perfection of wisdom, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, has not been obtained, will not be obtained, and is not being obtained now, as it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Because the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being about to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being presently attained, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the nature of the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the nature of the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being attained, and cannot be apprehended as being presently attained, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended as having a fixed nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the natures of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because the nature of these gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— is unobtainable,
they are said to be unobtainable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, being ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments cannot be apprehended as having a fixed nature,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments cannot be obtained in the past, cannot be obtained in the future, and cannot be obtained in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the stage of pure observation (*śuklavidarśanā-bhūmi*) up to the nature of the stage of the Tathāgata (*tathāgata-bhūmi*) cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the stage of pure observation, up to the nature of the stage of the Tathāgata, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, being ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the Ground of Extreme Joy up to the nature of the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Because the nature of the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, being ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of all dhāraṇī-doors and samādhi-doors cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because the nature of all dhāraṇī-doors and samādhi-doors is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, being ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers cannot be obtained as having been attained, cannot be obtained as yet to be attained, and cannot be obtained as being presently attained, for they are ultimately pure.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"
In this context, because the nature of the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is that?

Because the nature of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is neither obtainable in the past, nor obtainable in the future, nor obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being about to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being presently attained, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,

because the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) cannot be obtained in the past, cannot be obtained in the future, and cannot be obtained in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of rebirth in the evil destinies of a stream-enterer, up to and including the nature of further rebirth of a Tathāgata, cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because for one who has entered the stream, the nature of rebirth in the evil destinies, up to and including the nature of further rebirth after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, is not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and is not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that herein, because the nature of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship, the stage of entering pratyekabuddhahood and the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood, and all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas cannot be apprehended, they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of one who has entered the stream, up to and including the nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of a stream-enterer up to the nature of a Tathāgata cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of a stream-enterer, up to and including the nature of a Tathāgata, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Because the nature of names, conceptualizations, designations, and verbal expressions cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of non-arising and non-ceasing, non-defilement and non-purity, and non-action and unconditionedness cannot be apprehended, it is said that they are ‘unapprehendable.’”

Why is this? Because it has the nature of being without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and without action and without conditioning; it is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the past, middle, and future limits cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Because its nature at the beginning, middle, and end cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being about to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being currently attained, for it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
In this context, because the nature of going or coming, or of moving or staying, cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable. Why is that?
Because the nature of going or coming, or of moving or staying, has not been apprehended, will not be apprehended, and is not being apprehended in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of death or birth, or increase or decrease, cannot be apprehended, it is said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

Because the nature of whether dead or alive, or whether increasing or decreasing, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that herein,
because the nature of the purification of Buddha-fields and the maturation of sentient beings cannot be apprehended,
they are said to be unapprehendable. Why is this?

The purification of Buddha-fields and the maturation of the nature of sentient beings cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as yet to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being presently attained, because they are ultimately pure.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! Because form through to consciousness cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because herein, from form up to consciousness, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the eye-base through to the mind-base cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from the sense-base of the eye up to the sense-base of the mind, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the eye element up to the mind element cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from the eye-element up to the mind-element, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the form realm up to the dharma realm cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) up to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because eye-contact up to mind-contact cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from eye-contact up to mind-contact, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal and even within the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because herein, all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the earth element up to the consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because within this, from the earth element up to the consciousness element, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the causal conditions (*hetu-pratyaya*) up to the dominant conditions (*adhipati-pratyaya*) cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because within this, the causal conditions (*hetu-pratyaya*) up to the dominant conditions (*adhipati-pratyaya*) are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because ignorance up to old age and death cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, from ignorance up to old age and death, nothing can be apprehended as having existed, nothing can be apprehended as yet to exist, and nothing can be apprehended as existing in the present; for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because herein, from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended; therefore, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because herein, from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, these are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because the four dhyānas,

the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments have not been attained, will not be attained, and are not being attained now, because they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because the doors of liberation—

emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because within this, the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because herein, the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the stage of pure vision up to the stage of the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because within this, from the Stage of Pure Contemplation up to the Stage of the Tathāgata, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, and so forth, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because within this, from the Ground of Utmost Joy up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, they are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because all dhāraṇī-doors and samādhi-doors— from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— are unapprehendable, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable; it is because they are unapprehendable that they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because herein, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein, the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because within this, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity are neither obtainable in the past, nor obtainable in the future, nor obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*),

the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), they are said to be unapprehendable.”

Why is this so? Because herein all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that because the stream-enterer candidate up to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because herein, from the stage of entering the stream up to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, nothing is obtainable in the past, nothing is obtainable in the future, and nothing is obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti, you should know that because the purification of buddha-fields and the maturation of sentient beings cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are said to be unapprehendable."

Why is this? Within this, the purification of Buddha-fields and the maturation of sentient beings are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.
"So it is, Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, although they observe that all phenomena are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable."

Because it is ultimately pure, there is no one who departs by means of the Great Vehicle and remains [elsewhere]; rather, taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one mounts the Great Vehicle to emerge from the birth and death of the triple world, abiding within the wisdom of all-knowledge until the end of the future, continuously and inexhaustibly benefiting and gladdening sentient beings.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 492. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Subhūti, Number Twelve. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Regarding the Mahāyāna: the Mahāyāna universally transcends all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth—and is most honored and supreme. This Mahāyāna is equal to space; just as space can universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Mahāyāna universally contain immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.
Furthermore, just as space cannot be seen to come, go, or abide, so too is the Mahāyāna: it cannot be seen to come, go, or abide.
Moreover, just as space cannot be found in its prior, posterior, or middle limits, so too is the Mahāyāna: its prior, posterior, and middle limits are all unfindable.

Thus, this Mahāyāna is most honored and most supreme; equal to space, it accommodates all, is unmoving, and non-abiding. It is equal throughout the three periods of time and transcends the three periods of time; therefore, it is called the Mahāyāna.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.
A bodhisattva’s Mahāyāna possesses such boundless qualities as these.
Subhūti, you should know this!
The Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas consists of the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), namely, the perfection of generosity (dāna-pāramitā) up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñā-pāramitā).
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas consists of:

internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, non-dispersal emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-existence, and emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is precisely all the gates of dhāraṇī, namely, the gate of dhāraṇīs of syllables and so forth—an immeasurable and incalculable number of gates of dhāraṇī."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

That which is the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas consists of all the gateways to samādhi, namely, the *gaganagañja* samādhi and other such immeasurable and innumerable gateways to samādhi."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

That which is the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas refers to the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three doors of liberation, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha and other immeasurable, boundless, and preeminent virtues; you should know that all these constitute the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
That you say the Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and is the most honored and supreme, is so indeed."
So it is! It is just as you have said.
Subhūti, you should know this!

If the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm were suchness—being non-illusory, unchanging, non-perverted, and not merely provisional; if they were true and real, eternal and constant, immutable and unalterable, and possessed of a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm are conceptually constructed, falsely conjured, and subject to flux; and because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of any real nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not a mere designation; if it were true, real, eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are thoroughly imagined, falsely conjunct, and subject to flux; and because they are entirely impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, not a mere designation, true and real, permanent and eternal, immutable and unalterable, and possessing a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or excellent, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the sense bases from the eye-base up to the mind-base are thoroughly imagined, falsely compounded, and subject to flux; and because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the sphere of form up to the sphere of phenomena were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not merely designated; if they were true and real, eternal and constant, immutable and unalterable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the sense-sphere of form up to the sense-sphere of mental phenomena are conceptually imputed, falsely conjunct, and subject to flux; and because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the eye constituent, up to and including the mind constituent, were suchness—unfalsified, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not merely designated; if they were true and real, eternal and constant, immutable and unalterable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the eye-element up to the mind-element are thoroughly imagined and grasped (*parikalpita*), are false and adventitious composites, and are subject to flux; and because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of any real nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the realm of form up to the realm of phenomena were suchness—neither false, nor subject to change, nor inverted, nor merely provisional; if it were true and real, eternal and constant, unchanging and immutable, possessing a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the realm of form, up to and including the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), is conceptually constructed (*parikalpita*), is a false and provisional conjunction, and is subject to flux; and because everything therein is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the mind-consciousness element, were suchness—unfalsified, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not merely designated; if it were true and real, eternal and constant, immutable and unalterable, and possessed of a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the visual consciousness element, up to and including the mental consciousness element, are conceptually imputed, falsely conjunct, and subject to flux; and because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, and is thus most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If eye-contact, up to and including mind-contact, were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, not merely designated, true, real, permanent, eternal, immutable, and possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including their devas, humans, and asuras."

Because visual contact, up to and including mental contact, is conceptually constructed, is a false and provisional conjunction, and is subject to flux; because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, were suchness—non-false, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not merely provisional; if they were true and real, eternal and constant, immutable and unalterable, and possessed of a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

All feelings produced with visual contact as a condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are conceptually constructed, falsely conjured, and subject to flux; because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of a real nature, this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and is the most honored and supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the earth element, up to and including the consciousness element, were suchness—unfailing, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not a mere designation; if it were true, real, eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the element of earth, up to the element of consciousness, are conceptually constructed, falsely conjunct, and subject to flux; because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of any real nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, and is thus most honored and supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the causal condition, up to and including the sovereign condition, were the *tathatā* (suchness)—if it were not false, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not merely provisional; if it were true, real, eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the gods, humans, and asuras."

Because [phenomena] arise from causes and conditions up to dominant conditions, they are conceptually constructed, falsely conjunct, and subject to flux; because they are entirely impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and utterly devoid of a real nature, this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds—including devas, humans, and asuras—and is thus most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If ignorance up to old age and death were suchness—unfalsified, unchanging, non-erroneous, and not merely conventional; if they were true, real, eternal, constant, immutable, and possessed of a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or excellent, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because ignorance through to old age and death are thoroughly imagined, falsely compounded, and subject to flux—and because everything up to this point is impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If true thusness, up to the inconceivable realm, were a real existent nature rather than a non-existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, and it would not transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because true thusness, up to the inconceivable realm, is neither a nature that truly exists nor a nature that does not exist, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds—including devas, humans, and asuras—and is most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the realm of abandonment, the realm of detachment, the realm of cessation, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, the realm of non-arising, the realm of non-cessation, the realm of non-defilement, the realm of non-purity, the realm of non-action, and the realm of the unconditioned were of a truly existent nature rather than of a non-existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm (asaṃskṛta-dhātu) lack the nature of real existence and are thus non-existent by nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom were of a nature that exists substantially and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or excellent, and it would not transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom are not of a truly existent nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all the worlds of devas, humans, asuras, and others, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature were a truly existent entity rather than a non-existent entity, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or excellent, and it would not transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are not of a truly existent nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds—including devas, humans, and asuras—and is most honored and supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path were of a nature that exists truly and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are not of a nature of real existence, but are of a nature of non-existence, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and is thus most honored and supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path were of a nature that exists substantially and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or excellent, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are not of a truly existent nature, but rather of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments were of a nature that exists as real and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions do not possess a nature of real existence, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—were of a truly existent nature rather than a non-existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not of a truly existent nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments were of a nature that exists as a real entity and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments do not possess a real intrinsic nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds—including devas, humans, and asuras—and is thus most honored and supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi were of a truly existent nature rather than of a non-existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi do not possess a real intrinsic nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and is most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the five eyes and the six supernormal powers were of a nature that exists as a real entity and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the five eyes and six supernormal powers do not possess a real intrinsic nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras, being the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, were of a nature that exists as a real entity and not of a nature that does not exist, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or preeminent, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the ten powers of the Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, do not possess a nature of real existence, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Mahāyāna universally transcends all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and is thus most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the dharmas of the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the dharmas of the Cloud of Dharma were of a truly existent nature and not of a non-existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the dharmas of the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the dharmas of the Stage of the Dharma-Cloud do not possess a real nature, and because they are of a non-existent nature, this Great Vehicle universally transcends all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and is the most honored and most supreme.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the individuals from those on the Stage of Extreme Joy up to those on the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma were of a truly existent nature and not of a non-existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or supreme, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."
