"Furthermore, Subhūti! The eye constituent (*cakṣurdhātu*) up to the mind constituent (*manodhātu*), in their prior, posterior, and middle limits, are all unapprehendable; within the equality of the three limits, the eye constituent up to the mind constituent is likewise unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the eye-element—from its prior, subsequent, and middle limits—up to the intrinsic nature of the mind-element, is entirely unapprehendable. Why is that?

Even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the eye-element, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the mind-element, be apprehended within that equality—whether in its prior, posterior, or middle limits!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The form realm, up to and including the dharma realm, cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, the form realm, up to and including the dharma realm, likewise cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because within equality, the self-nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*)—from its prior, subsequent, and middle limits—up to the self-nature of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), is entirely unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the form realm, up to the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, be apprehended within that equality, whether in the past, future, or present!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; nor can the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element be apprehended within the equality of the three limits."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element from the past, future, and present limits, up to the intrinsic nature of the mind-consciousness element, is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the mind-consciousness element, be apprehended within that equality—whether in the past, future, or present!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Eye-contact, up to and including mind-contact, cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, eye-contact, up to and including mind-contact, likewise cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of eye-contact—from the past, future, and present limits—up to the intrinsic nature of mind-contact, is entirely unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Since even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended, how much less can the intrinsic nature of eye-contact, up to and including the intrinsic nature of mind-contact, be apprehended within that state of equality—whether in the past, future, or present!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including those produced with mind-contact as condition, are all unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; likewise, within the equality of the three limits, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including those produced with mind-contact as condition, are also unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—from those of the past, future, and present limits—up to the intrinsic nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—up to and including the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition—be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The earth element, up to and including the consciousness element, cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, the earth element, up to and including the consciousness element, likewise cannot be apprehended."

Why is this so? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the earth element—from the past, future, and present limits—up to the intrinsic nature of the consciousness element, is entirely unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the earth element, up to the intrinsic nature of the consciousness element, be apprehended within that equality, whether in its prior, subsequent, or middle limit!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Causes and conditions, up to and including dominant conditions, are unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; likewise, causes and conditions, up to and including dominant conditions, are unapprehendable within the equality of the three limits."
Why is this? Because within equality, the self-nature of causes and conditions—from the past, future, and present limits, up to the self-nature of the sovereign condition—is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the self-nature of causes and conditions, or even the self-nature of sovereign conditions, be apprehended within equality—whether in the past, future, or present limits!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Ignorance up to old age and death are all unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, ignorance up to old age and death are likewise unapprehendable."

Why is this so? Because within equality, the self-nature of ignorance from the past, the future, and the present limits, up to the self-nature of old age and death, is entirely unapprehendable. Why is this so?

Since even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended, how much less could the intrinsic nature of ignorance from the prior, posterior, and middle limits, up to the intrinsic nature of old age and death, be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The perfection of generosity, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; likewise, within the equality of the three limits, the perfection of generosity, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving—from its beginning, middle, and end—up to the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity, up to the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, be apprehended within that equality, in terms of its prior, subsequent, or middle limits!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; nor can the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path be apprehended within the equality of the three limits."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness—from the past, future, and present limits—up to the intrinsic nature of the eightfold noble path, is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to the intrinsic nature of the eight branches of the noble path, be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments—whether in their prior, subsequent, or middle stages—be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; likewise, within the equality of these three limits, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are also unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within equality, even the intrinsic nature of the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—regarding the past, future, and present limits cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—within equality be apprehended!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are all unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits. Why is this so?

Since even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended, how much less could the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments—whether in the past, future, or present limits—be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The stages from the Stage of Pure Contemplation up to the Tathāgata stage cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits; within the equality of these three limits, the stages from the Stage of Pure Contemplation up to the Tathāgata stage likewise cannot be apprehended."

Why is this so? Because within equality, the self-nature of the stage of pure observation—from the prior, subsequent, and middle limits—up to the self-nature of the stage of the Tathāgata, is entirely unattainable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the stages from the Ground of Pure Contemplation through the Ground of the Tathāgata be apprehended within equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The initial, middle, and final limits of the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma are all unapprehendable; within the equality of the three limits, the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma are likewise unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the Stage of Great Joy—from the prior, the subsequent, and the intermediate limits—up to the intrinsic nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the Ground of Great Joy, up to the intrinsic nature of the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, be apprehended within that equality—whether in its prior, subsequent, or middle limit!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The dhāraṇī-doors and samādhi-doors of the past, future, and middle limits are all unapprehendable; within the equality of the three limits, the dhāraṇī-doors and samādhi-doors are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the dhāraṇī-gates and samādhi-gates of the past, future, and present limits is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi—whether in the past, future, or present limits—be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The five eyes and six supernormal powers are all unattainable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of these three limits, the five eyes and six supernormal powers are likewise unattainable."
Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the five eyes and six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits. Why is this so?

Even the nature of equality within equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the five eyes and six supernormal powers be apprehended within that equality, whether in the past, future, or present limits!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are all unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are likewise unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of the Tathāgata’s ten powers—whether in the past, future, or present—as well as the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the intrinsic nature of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, or even the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity are both unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity are likewise unapprehendable."

Why is this so? Because within equality, the nature of non-forgetfulness regarding the past, future, and present limits, as well as the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, are all fundamentally unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness regarding the past, future, and present limits, or the state of constant equanimity, be apprehended within equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because within equality, the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) across the past, future, and present limits cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the intrinsic nature of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—whether in the past, future, or present limits—be apprehended within that equality!
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

An ordinary person, a śrāvaka, a pratyekabuddha, a bodhisattva, and a tathāgata are all unapprehendable in the past, future, and middle limits; within the equality of the three limits, from an ordinary person up to a tathāgata, none are apprehendable."

Why is this so? Because within equality, the self-nature of ordinary beings in the past, future, and present limits, up to and including the self-nature of the Tathāgata, is entirely unapprehendable. Why is that?

Even the state of equality within equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can one apprehend the distinct natures of the past, future, and present limits of ordinary beings, up to and including the nature of a Tathāgata, within that equality!
Because a self, a sentient being—and so on, up to a knower and a seer—cannot be apprehended.

"In this way, Subhūti, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas abide in the perfection of wisdom and diligently train in the equality of the three periods of time, they are swiftly able to fulfill all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna). This is called the mark of the Great Vehicle of the equality of the three periods of time for bodhisattva mahāsattvas."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in such characteristics of the Great Vehicle, they will universally transcend all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes, benefiting and bringing happiness to sentient beings until the end of the future.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Excellent!”
Excellent! The Tathāgata has now skillfully expounded for the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such a meaning of the Mahāyāna. This Mahāyāna is most honored and most supreme;

the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past trained in this and were already able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). The assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future will train in this and shall be able to realize the knowledge of all modes. The assembly of all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas throughout the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions in the present are training in this and are currently realizing the knowledge of all modes.
"Therefore, the Mahāyāna is most honored and most supreme; it serves as the true, preeminent basis for the omniscience of the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "It is so!"
So it is! It is just as you have said.

The assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, future, and present all rely upon the Mahāyāna to practice with diligent application; they are thus able to swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and, until the end of the future, bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.

Therefore, the Mahāyāna is most honored and most supreme, universally transcending all worlds—including gods, humans, and asuras—and all assemblies of bodhisattvas should diligently cultivate and study it.
At that time, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Previously, the Tathāgata instructed the Venerable Subhūti to proclaim the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; why is it that he now speaks on the various meanings of the Mahāyāna?”
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Regarding the various meanings of the Great Vehicle that I have previously explained, do they not perhaps contradict the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"All the various meanings of the Mahāyāna that you have previously expounded are in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā and do not deviate from it."

Why is this? Because all wholesome dharmas—whether they be factors of enlightenment, dharmas of the śrāvakas, dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, dharmas of the bodhisattvas, or dharmas of the Tathāgatas—all of these are subsumed within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“What are those called ‘all wholesome dharmas,’ the factors of enlightenment, whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of tathāgatas—all these, without exception, are subsumed within the profound perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha addressed Subhūti:

"Subhūti, you should know that whether it be the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the eight liberations and the nine successive meditative concentrations; the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the Dharma-cloud; all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi; the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity; or omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects."

All such wholesome dharmas as these—the factors of enlightenment, whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas—all of them are without exception subsumed within this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
“Subhūti, you should know this:
whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity;
whether it be the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness; whether it be the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind; or whether it be the sense base of form...”
Reaching the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), whether it be the eye element up to the mind element; the form element up to the phenomenon element;
the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element; eye-contact up to mind-contact;
the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; or the earth [element]...
The element of earth up to the element of consciousness; if it be the causal condition up to the sovereign condition; if it be ignorance up to old age and death;
if it be the realm of desire, the realm of form, or the formless realm; if it be wholesome dharmas or unwholesome dharmas;
if it be dharmas with a definite outcome or indeterminate dharmas; if it be dharmas of those in training, dharmas of those beyond training, or [neither]...
Learning is not a non-learner dharma; it includes the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path,
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments,
the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and the stage of pure observation up to the stage of suchness.
the stages, from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma;
or the gateways of all dhāraṇīs and the gateways of samādhis; or the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
or the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; or the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity; or...
All-knowledge (sarvajñatā), knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā), and knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā);
whether wholesome dharmas or unwholesome dharmas, conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas, dharmas with outflows (sāsrava) or dharmas without outflows (anāsrava),
conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas, worldly dharmas or supramundane dharmas, or suffering (duḥkha).
the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; if it be inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
if it be suchness up to the inconceivable realm; if it be the realm of abandonment up to the unconditioned realm;
if it be the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; or if it be the Dharma and Vinaya realized and taught by the Buddhas.

Whether it be bodhi or nirvāṇa—all such dharmas are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
"For this reason, all the various meanings of the Mahāyāna that you have previously expounded are in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā and do not contradict it."

Why is this? Because the Great Vehicle is not different from the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity, and the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity is not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the Prajñāpāramitā, up to and including the Dānapāramitā, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.

“The Mahāyāna is not different from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, their nature is non-dual because they are not divided into two.

The Great Vehicle is not different from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.

“The Mahāyāna is not different from the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments; the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments are not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the eight liberations, or the nine successive concentrations, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.

The Great Vehicle is not different from the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.

“The Mahāyāna is not different from the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata is not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the Stage of Pure Observation up to the Stage of the Tathāgata, their nature is non-dual because there is no division into two.

"The Great Vehicle is not different from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud; the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud is not different from the Great Vehicle."
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the stages from the Stage of Supreme Joy up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.
The Great Vehicle is not different from the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi; the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the gateways of dhāraṇī, or the gateways of samādhi, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
The Great Vehicle is not different from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the five eyes and six supernormal powers, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.

The Great Vehicle is not different from the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.

“The Great Vehicle is not different from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity; the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity are not different from the Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the state of constant equanimity, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.

The Great Vehicle is not different from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are not different from the Great Vehicle.

Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.

"The Mahāyāna is not different from the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?"
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, their nature is non-dual because they are not divided into two.

The Great Vehicle is not different from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence; internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.
The Great Vehicle is not different from suchness up to the inconceivable realm; suchness up to the inconceivable realm is not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or True Suchness, up to the inconceivable realm, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.
The Great Vehicle is not different from the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm; the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm is not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the realm of cessation, up to the realm of the unconditioned, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.
The Great Vehicle is not different from wholesome and unwholesome dharmas; wholesome and unwholesome dharmas are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or wholesome and unwholesome dharmas, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.
The Great Vehicle is not different from dharmas that are determinate or indeterminate; dharmas that are determinate or indeterminate are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna, or dharmas that are determinate or indeterminate, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.
The Mahāyāna is not different from contaminated (sāsrava) and uncontaminated (anāsrava) dharmas; contaminated and uncontaminated dharmas are not different from the Mahāyāna.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or whether they be contaminated (*sāsrava*) or uncontaminated (*anāsrava*) phenomena, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.

"The Great Vehicle is not different from worldly phenomena (*laukika-dharma*) and supramundane phenomena (*lokottara-dharma*); worldly and supramundane phenomena are not different from the Great Vehicle."
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or mundane phenomena, or supramundane phenomena, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.
The Great Vehicle is not different from conditioned and unconditioned phenomena; conditioned and unconditioned phenomena are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.
The Great Vehicle is not different from the aggregates, bases, and elements; the aggregates, bases, and elements are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the aggregates, sense bases, and elements, their nature is non-dual and indivisible.
Subhūti, you should know this!
For this reason, all the various meanings of the Mahāyāna that you have previously expounded are in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā and do not contradict it.
If one speaks of the Mahāyāna, one speaks of the Prajñāpāramitā; if one speaks of the Prajñāpāramitā, one speaks of the Mahāyāna, for these two names are non-different in meaning.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 495. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Subhūti, Section Fifteen. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
The prior limit of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended, the posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and the middle limit cannot be apprehended.
Because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;
because the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the sense-field of form up to the sense-field of mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) up to the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the form-element (*rūpadhātu*) up to the mental-phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*) are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because eye-contact up to mind-contact is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the element of earth up to the element of consciousness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the causal condition up to the dominant condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because ignorance up to old age and death are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the eight liberations and the nine successive concentrations are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the ten powers of the Tathāgata, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because all doors of dhāraṇī and doors of samādhi are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;
because the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;
because the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma stage are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because true thusness up to the inconceivable realm are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the realm of cessation up to the realm of the unconditioned is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the vehicles of the śrāvaka, the pratyekabuddha, and the mahāyāna are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

From the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the aggregates of form up to the aggregate of consciousness, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

In this way, up to and including the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.
"So be it, World-Honored One!

Regarding all these dharmas, throughout all modes, in all places, and at all times, I have sought a bodhisattva mahāsattva but have seen none at all and cannot find one. How then am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the perfection of wisdom?"
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature at all.

Just as it is said that 'self' and so forth are ultimately unarisen, possessing only provisional names and having no intrinsic nature at all, so too are all dharmas: they are ultimately unarisen, possessing only provisional names and having no intrinsic nature at all."
"Bhagavān! What is form, up to consciousness, that is ultimately non-arising?
If it is ultimately non-arising, it is not designated as 'form' up to 'consciousness. Likewise, what are the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle that are ultimately non-arising?"
If there is ultimate non-arising, then one cannot be designated as a śrāvaka, a pratyekabuddha, or a follower of the Mahāyāna.
“World-Honored One, how could I,
by means of the Prajñāpāramitā that is ultimately non-arising, instruct or admonish a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is ultimately non-arising?”
“World-Honored One!
Apart from ultimate non-arising, there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
World-Honored One!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such an exposition, does not become despondent nor feel regret, and their mind is neither startled, terrified, nor afraid, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked the Venerable Subhūti:
"For what reason do you say that for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the prior limit is unapprehendable, the posterior limit is unapprehendable, and the middle limit is unapprehendable?"
"For what reason is it said that because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless?
Likewise, up to and including the fact that the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle are limitless, for what reason should one know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless?"

"For what reason is it said that within the aggregates from form up to consciousness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; and that apart from the aggregates from form up to consciousness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended?"

In this way, up to and including the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle—wherein the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable—is it because apart from the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable?

"For what reason do I say that, regarding all these dharmas, in every way, in every place, and at all times, I have sought a bodhisattva mahāsattva but have seen none at all and cannot find one; how then am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the perfection of wisdom?"
"For what reason is it said that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have only a provisional name and possess no self-nature?
For what reason is it said that, just as 'self' and so forth are ultimately unarisen, they have only a provisional name and possess no self-nature?"
"For what reason do you say that all dharmas are likewise ultimately unarisen, existing only as provisional names and entirely lacking intrinsic nature?
For what reason do you say that whatever constitutes form, up to and including consciousness, is ultimately unarisen?"
In this way, up to: "What are the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and Mahāyāna that ultimately do not arise?

For what reason is it said that if something ultimately does not arise, it is not called form, up to consciousness; and likewise, up to: if something ultimately does not arise, it is not called a śrāvaka, a pratyekabuddha, or the Mahāyāna?"
"For what reason do you say: 'How could I possibly instruct and admonish a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is ultimately unarisen by means of a perfection of wisdom that is ultimately unarisen?'"
“For what reason do you say that because there is no ultimate non-arising, there is also no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?

For what reason do you say that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears such a teaching and their mind does not sink, nor feel regret, and their mind is not startled, terrified, or afraid, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“Venerable sir, you should now explain this for me.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied to Śāriputra:

“Regarding what the Venerable asked—‘For what reason is it said that the past limit of bodhisattva mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended, the future limit cannot be apprehended, and the middle limit cannot be apprehended?’”
"Śāriputra, because sentient beings do not exist, the past, future, and middle limits of bodhisattva mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, regarding what the Venerable One asked:
'For what reason is it said that because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless? "
"If it is thus that because śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle are limitless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also limitless," [the Buddha said], "Śāriputra!"
The aggregate of form, up to and including the Great Vehicle, are all like space. Why is this?

Just as the past, future, and middle limits of great space cannot be apprehended, and because its center and boundaries are both unapprehendable, it is called "space"; so too it is with the aggregate of form, up to and including the Great Vehicle—their past, future, and middle limits are likewise all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because from the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*) up to the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), all are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāvaśūnya*). Within emptiness, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle limit are all unapprehendable; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless.
In this way, because śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle are limitless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also limitless. Furthermore, Śāriputra!

“Venerable sir, for what reason do you say that the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva neither exists nor can be apprehended as being identical with the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*) up to the aggregate of consciousness (*vijñānaskandha*), nor does he exist nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the aggregates of form up to consciousness;

"Thus it is, Śāriputra!
From the aggregate of form up to the Mahāyāna aggregate of form, all are by nature empty. Why is this?"

Within the emptiness of the aggregate of form up to the Mahāyāna nature, because the aggregate of form up to the Mahāyāna do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas likewise do not exist and cannot be apprehended.

from the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the aggregates of form up to the aggregate of consciousness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

In this way, up to and including the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle—bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Great Vehicle, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The odor-element cannot be apprehended within the odor-element; the odor-element also cannot be apprehended within the form-, sound-, taste-, touch-, or mental-object-element.
The taste-element cannot be apprehended within the taste-element; the taste-element also cannot be apprehended within the form-, sound-, odor-, touch-, or mental-object-element.

The element of tangibility is not to be found within the element of tangibility; the element of tangibility is also not to be found within the elements of form, sound, odor, taste, or mental phenomena.

The element of mental phenomena is not to be found within the element of mental phenomena; the element of mental phenomena is also not to be found within the elements of form, sound, odor, taste, or tangibility.

“Śāriputra! The eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the eye-consciousness element; the eye-consciousness element also cannot be apprehended within the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.”

The auditory consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the auditory consciousness element; the auditory consciousness element also cannot be apprehended within the visual, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness elements.

The nose-consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the nose-consciousness element; the nose-consciousness element also cannot be apprehended within the eye, ear, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.

The tongue-consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the tongue-consciousness element; the tongue-consciousness element also cannot be apprehended within the eye-, ear-, nose-, body-, or mind-consciousness elements.

The body-consciousness element cannot be apprehended within the body-consciousness element; the body-consciousness element also cannot be apprehended within the eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, or mind-consciousness elements.

The consciousness-element cannot be apprehended within the consciousness-element; the consciousness-element also cannot be apprehended within the eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, or body-consciousness-elements.
“Śāriputra! Eye-contact cannot be apprehended within eye-contact; eye-contact also cannot be apprehended within ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
Ear-contact cannot be apprehended within ear-contact; ear-contact also cannot be apprehended within eye-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact.
Nose-contact cannot be apprehended within nose-contact; nose-contact also cannot be apprehended within eye-contact, ear-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact.
Tongue-contact is not to be found in tongue-contact; tongue-contact is also not to be found in eye-, ear-, nose-, body-, or mind-contact.
Body-contact is not to be found in body-contact; body-contact is also not to be found in eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, or mind-contact.
Mental contact cannot be apprehended within mental contact, nor can mental contact be apprehended within visual, auditory, olfactory, gustatory, or tactile contact. "Śāriputra!

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; nor can the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition be apprehended within the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.

The various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; nor can those feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition be apprehended within the various feelings produced with eye-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.

The various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; furthermore, those various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended within the various feelings produced with eye-, ear-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.

The various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; nor can the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition be apprehended within the various feelings produced with eye-, ear-, nose-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.

The various feelings produced with body-contact as condition cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with body-contact as condition; nor can those feelings produced with body-contact as condition be apprehended within the various feelings produced with eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, or mind-contact as condition.

The various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with mental contact as their condition; furthermore, those feelings produced with mental contact as their condition cannot be apprehended within the various feelings produced with eye, ear, nose, tongue, or body contact as their conditions.
“Śāriputra! The earth element cannot be apprehended within the earth element; the earth element cannot be apprehended within the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements either.”
The water element cannot be apprehended within the water element; the water element also cannot be apprehended within the earth, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
The fire element cannot be apprehended within the fire element; the fire element also cannot be apprehended within the earth, water, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
The wind element cannot be apprehended within the wind element; the wind element also cannot be apprehended within the earth, water, fire, space, or consciousness elements.
The space element cannot be apprehended within the space element; the space element also cannot be apprehended within the earth, water, fire, wind, or consciousness elements.

The element of consciousness cannot be apprehended within the element of consciousness; nor can the element of consciousness be apprehended within the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, or space. "Śāriputra!

Conditioned origination cannot be apprehended within conditioned origination; conditioned origination also cannot be apprehended within the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition.

The immediately preceding condition cannot be apprehended within the immediately preceding condition; the immediately preceding condition also cannot be apprehended within the causal condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition.

The object-condition cannot be apprehended within the object-condition; the object-condition also cannot be apprehended within the causal condition, the immediately preceding condition, or the dominant condition.

The dominant condition cannot be apprehended within the dominant condition; the dominant condition also cannot be apprehended within the causal condition, the immediately preceding condition, or the object condition.

“Śāriputra! Ignorance cannot be apprehended within ignorance; ignorance also cannot be apprehended within volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age and death.”

One cannot apprehend the practice of formations; one likewise cannot apprehend the practice of ignorance, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age and death.

Consciousness cannot be apprehended within consciousness; consciousness also cannot be apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age and death.

Name-and-form cannot be apprehended within name-and-form; name-and-form also cannot be apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age and death.

The six sense bases cannot be apprehended within the six sense bases; nor can the six sense bases be apprehended in ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

Contact is not to be found within contact; contact is likewise not to be found within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

Feeling cannot be apprehended within feeling; nor can feeling be apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age and death.

Craving cannot be found within craving; craving also cannot be found within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, clinging, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

Grasping cannot be apprehended within grasping; nor can grasping be apprehended within ignorance, formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

Existence cannot be apprehended within existence; nor can existence be apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, birth, or aging-and-death.

Birth cannot be apprehended within birth; nor can birth be apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, or old age and death.

Old age and death cannot be apprehended within old age and death; old age and death also cannot be apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, or birth.

“Śāriputra! The perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended within the perfection of generosity; the perfection of generosity also cannot be apprehended within the perfections of ethical discipline and so forth. In this way, up to the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended within the perfection of wisdom, nor can the perfection of wisdom be apprehended within the perfections of generosity and so forth.”
“Śāriputra! The four dhyānas cannot be apprehended within the four dhyānas; the four dhyānas also cannot be apprehended within the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.”
The four immeasurables cannot be apprehended within the four immeasurables; the four immeasurables also cannot be apprehended within the four dhyānas or the four formless attainments.
The four formless attainments cannot be apprehended within the four formless attainments; the four formless attainments also cannot be apprehended within the four dhyānas or the four immeasurables.

"Śāriputra! The four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended within the four foundations of mindfulness; the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended within the four right efforts and so forth. Likewise, up to the eightfold noble path, the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended within the eightfold noble path, and the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended within the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth."
“Śāriputra! The eight liberations cannot be apprehended within the eight liberations, nor within the nine successive attainments, nor within the ten totalities;

the nine successive attainments cannot be apprehended within the nine successive attainments, nor can the nine successive attainments be apprehended within the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, or the ten totalities.”

The ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) cannot be apprehended within the ten totalities; the ten totalities also cannot be apprehended within the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), or the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*). "Śāriputra!..."

The liberation door of emptiness cannot be apprehended within the liberation door of emptiness; the liberation door of emptiness also cannot be apprehended within the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

The signless door of liberation cannot be apprehended within the signless door of liberation; the signless door of liberation also cannot be apprehended within the doors of emptiness and wishlessness.

The wishless gate of liberation cannot be apprehended within the wishless gate of liberation; the wishless gate of liberation also cannot be apprehended within the gates of emptiness and signlessness.
“Śāriputra! The five eyes cannot be apprehended within the five eyes; the five eyes also cannot be apprehended within the six supernormal powers.
The six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended within the six supernormal powers; the six supernormal powers also cannot be apprehended within the five eyes.”

"Śāriputra! The ten powers of the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended within the ten powers of the Tathāgata; the ten powers of the Tathāgata also cannot be apprehended within the four fearlessnesses and so forth."

In this way, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), these eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended; nor can the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha be apprehended within the ten powers (*bala*) of a Tathāgata, and so forth.

“Śāriputra! The quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be apprehended within the quality of non-forgetfulness; the quality of non-forgetfulness also cannot be apprehended within the state of constant equanimity.”

The state of constant equanimity cannot be apprehended within the state of constant equanimity, nor can the state of constant equanimity be apprehended within the quality of non-forgetfulness. "Śāriputra!..."
All-knowledge is not to be found within all-knowledge; all-knowledge is also not to be found within the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
The knowledge of the paths is not to be found within the knowledge of the paths; the knowledge of the paths is also not to be found within all-knowledge or the knowledge of all aspects.
All-aspect omniscience cannot be apprehended within all-aspect omniscience; all-aspect omniscience also cannot be apprehended within omniscience or the knowledge of paths.
“Śāriputra! Internal emptiness cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, nor can internal emptiness be apprehended within external emptiness and the others.

In this way, up to and including the fact that the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nor can the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence be apprehended within internal emptiness and the others.”
“Śāriputra! True suchness cannot be apprehended within true suchness; true suchness also cannot be apprehended within the dharma-realm and so forth.

In this way, up to the inconceivable realm, the inconceivable realm cannot be apprehended within the inconceivable realm, and the inconceivable realm also cannot be apprehended within true suchness and so forth.”
“Śāriputra! The realm of cessation cannot be apprehended within the realm of cessation; the realm of cessation also cannot be apprehended within the realm of detachment, and so forth.
Likewise, up to the unconditioned realm cannot be apprehended within the unconditioned realm, and the unconditioned realm also cannot be apprehended within the realm of cessation, and so forth.”

“Śāriputra! The noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended within the noble truth of suffering; the noble truth of suffering also cannot be apprehended within the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

The noble truth of origination cannot be apprehended within the noble truth of origination; the noble truth of origination also cannot be apprehended within the noble truths of suffering, cessation, and the path.

The noble truth of cessation cannot be apprehended within the noble truth of cessation; the noble truth of cessation also cannot be apprehended within the noble truths of suffering, origination, and the path.

The noble truth of the path cannot be apprehended within the noble truth of the path; the noble truth of the path also cannot be apprehended within the noble truths of suffering, origin, and cessation. "Śāriputra!
The gate of dhāraṇī is not to be apprehended within the gate of dhāraṇī, and the gate of dhāraṇī is also not to be apprehended within the gate of samādhi.
The gate of samādhi is not to be apprehended within the gate of samādhi, and the gate of samādhi is also not to be apprehended within the gate of dhāraṇī.

“Śāriputra! The stage of an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana-bhūmi*) cannot be apprehended within the stage of an ordinary person; the stage of an ordinary person also cannot be apprehended within the stage of the lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), and so forth.

Likewise, up to the stage of a Tathāgata (*tathāgata-bhūmi*), it cannot be apprehended within the stage of a Tathāgata, nor can the stage of a Tathāgata be apprehended within the stage of an ordinary person, and so forth.”
“Śāriputra! The Ground of Great Joy cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Great Joy; the Ground of Great Joy also cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Stainless and the others.

In this manner, up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, it cannot be apprehended within the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma; the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma also cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Great Joy and the others.”
“Śāriputra! A stream-enterer cannot be apprehended within the state of a stream-enterer, nor can a stream-enterer be apprehended within the state of a once-returner and so forth.

In this way, up to and including a perfectly awakened one, a perfectly awakened one cannot be apprehended within the state of a perfectly awakened one, nor can a perfectly awakened one be apprehended within the states of a stream-enterer and so forth.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended within a bodhisattva mahāsattva; nor can a bodhisattva mahāsattva be apprehended within the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), its instructions, or its teachings.”

The perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended within the perfection of wisdom; the perfection of wisdom also cannot be apprehended within the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor within the instructions and admonitions.

Instruction and admonition cannot be apprehended within instruction and admonition; instruction and admonition also cannot be apprehended within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
"Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all such things— whether phenomena or a self— are empty of intrinsic nature."
“Śāriputra! For this reason, I say this:

regarding all these dharmas, in every way, in every place, and at every time, I do not perceive a bodhisattva mahāsattva at all, nor can one be found. How then could I instruct or admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the perfection of wisdom?”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 496. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter on Subhūti, Section Sixteen: "Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
Regarding the Venerable’s question, "For what reason is it said that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have only a provisional name and lack any intrinsic nature?"— Śāriputra!
"Because the designation 'bodhisattva mahāsattva' is merely a provisional designation. Then, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason do you say that the designation 'bodhisattva mahāsattva' is merely a provisional designation?"
Subhūti replied: “Just as the names of all phenomena are merely designations, they come from nowhere in the ten directions or the three times, go nowhere, and abide nowhere.”
Among all phenomena there is no name, and within names there are no phenomena; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed, being merely provisional designations. Why is this?

Because both all phenomena and names are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*). Within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be all phenomena or names, both are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus: they are comprised solely of adventitious designations; they come from nowhere, go nowhere, and abide nowhere, being merely conventional designations. For this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as the aggregates from form up to consciousness are designated as merely being comprised of adventitious factors. Why is this so?

The aggregate of form and so forth are not names, and names are not the aggregate of form and so forth; names do not exist within the aggregate of form and so forth, nor do the aggregate of form and so forth exist within names. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the aggregate of form and so forth, together with "name," are empty of intrinsic nature; within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the aggregates of form and so forth nor "name" exist at all, and are entirely unobtainable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious factors; for this reason, it is said that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only a provisional name.
“Śāriputra! Just as the sense bases from the eye base up to the mind base are designated as being merely comprised of adventitious factors. Why is this so?

The sense bases, such as the eye, are not names, and names are not the sense bases, such as the eye. Names do not exist within the sense bases, nor do the sense bases exist within names. They are neither joined nor dispersed, being merely conventional designations. Why is this so?

Because the sense base of the eye and so forth, together with their designations, are empty of intrinsic nature, within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the sense bases such as the eye nor their designations exist at all and are entirely unattainable.

The names of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as the sense-sphere of form, up to the sense-sphere of mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), are designated merely as adventitious designations. Why is this so?

The sense-base of form and so forth are not names, and names are not the sense-base of form and so forth; within the sense-base of form and so forth there are no names, and within names there are no sense-bases of form and so forth. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the sense-base of form (*rūpāyatana*) and so forth, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*). Within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be the sense-base of form and so forth, or the name, both are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious factors; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as the eye-element up to the mind-element are designated merely by adventitious designations. Why is that?

The eye-element and so forth are not names, and names are not the eye-element and so forth; within the eye-element and so forth there are no names, and within names there are no eye-elements and so forth. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the eye-sphere and so forth, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be the eye-sphere and so forth or their names, both are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only conventional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as the names of the form realm up to the dharma realm are comprised merely as adventitious designations. Why is this so?

The form realm and so forth are not names, and names are not the form realm and so forth; within the form realm and so forth there are no names, and within names there is no form realm and so forth. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the realm of form and so forth, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be the realm of form and so forth or the name, both are non-existent and entirely unattainable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious factors; for this reason, it is said that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as the eye-consciousness element, up to and including the mind-consciousness element, are designated merely as adventitious designations. Why is this so?

The eye-consciousness element and so forth are not names, and names are not the eye-consciousness element and so forth. Within the eye-consciousness element and so forth there are no names, and within names there is no eye-consciousness element and so forth. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed; they are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the eye-consciousness element and so forth, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be the eye-consciousness element and so forth or the name, both are non-existent and entirely unobtainable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as visual contact, up to and including mental contact, are designated as merely adventitious. Why is this so?

Eye-contact and so forth are not names, and names are not eye-contact and so forth; names do not exist within eye-contact and so forth, nor do eye-contact and so forth exist within names. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because eye-contact and so forth, together with names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be eye-contact and so forth or names, both are non-existent and entirely unobtainable.

The names of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature at all.

"Śāriputra! All feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are designated as being comprised solely of the adventitious."

Why is this so? The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are not the "name," nor is the "name" the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. Within the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition there is no "name," and within the "name" there are no various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. They are neither joined nor dispersed; they are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, together with name, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, both the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition and name are equally non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only conventional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
"Śāriputra! Just as the elements from the earth element up to the consciousness element are comprised solely of adventitious designations. Why is this so?

The earth element and so forth are not names, and names are not the earth element and so forth. Within the earth element and so forth there are no names, and within names there are no earth elements and so forth. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the earth element and so forth, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, both the earth element and its name are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious factors; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! The names ‘causal condition’ up to ‘dominant condition’ are comprised solely as adventitious designations. Why is this so?

Conditions such as causes and conditions are not names, and names are not conditions such as causes and conditions; within conditions such as causes and conditions there are no names, and within names there are no conditions such as causes and conditions. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because causes, conditions, and so forth, together with names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be causes, conditions, and so forth, or names, both are non-existent and utterly unobtainable.

The names of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only conventional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as ignorance up to old age and death are designated as being merely comprised of adventitious factors. Why is this so?

Ignorance and so forth are not the name, and the name is not ignorance and so forth; the name does not exist within ignorance and so forth, nor do ignorance and so forth exist within the name. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because ignorance and the other factors, together with "name," are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be ignorance and the others or "name," both are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious factors; for this reason, it is said that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature at all.
“Śāriputra! Just as the names of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom are merely comprised of adventitious designations. Why is this so?

The perfections such as the perfection of generosity are not names, and names are not the perfections such as the perfection of generosity; within the perfections such as the perfection of generosity there are no names, and within names there are no perfections such as the perfection of generosity. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity and so forth, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the perfection of generosity and so forth nor the name are anything at all, and are utterly unfindable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious factors; for this reason, it is said that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only provisional names and have no intrinsic nature whatsoever.
“Śāriputra! Just as the names of ‘inner emptiness’ up to ‘emptiness of the nature of non-existence’ are categorized merely as adventitious. Why is this so?

The emptiness of the internal and so forth is not the name; the name is not the emptiness of the internal and so forth. Within the emptiness of the internal and so forth there is no name; within the name there is no emptiness of the internal and so forth. They are neither conjoined nor dispersed, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because internal emptiness and so forth, together with names, are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be internal emptiness and so forth or names, both are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable.

The names of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus, being comprised solely of adventitious designations; for this reason, it is said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess only conventional names and have no intrinsic nature at all.
