Why is this so? Because all phenomena are entirely empty; when subjected to ultimate analysis and investigation, they cannot be apprehended.
— *The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 499.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 503, translated by the Tripitaka Dharma Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part Three, Chapter Four: The Devendra Section, Part Three.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and all those from the gods of the Four Great Kings throughout this trichiliocosm, up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, all had this thought:

"The Venerable Subhūti, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, is raining down a great rain of Dharma for the assembly of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas. For the sake of making offerings, we should each now manifest celestial, exquisite flowers and scatter them over the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the assembly of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, the community of Bhikṣus, the Venerable Subhūti, and the profound Prajñāpāramitā, thereby making offerings."
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the assembly of devas, having formed this thought, each manifested a celestial *divyagandhapuṣpa* (flower of divine fragrance) to offer as an act of worship.

At that time, these flowers completely filled this trichiliocosm; through the Buddha’s supernatural power, they merged in mid-air to form a flower pedestal (*puṣpamaṇḍala*), exquisitely adorned and equal in magnitude to the trichiliocosm.
Having witnessed this event, the Venerable Subhūti thought to himself:

"The flowers now scattered have never been seen before among the realms of the devas; these flowers are so extraordinary and sublime that they certainly were not produced from water, land, grass, or trees, but must have been emanated by the devas from their own minds."
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, knowing the thoughts in Subhūti’s mind, said to him:
"These flowers that have been scattered were not actually produced from water, land, grass, or trees; they are merely manifestations created by the minds of these devas."
At that time, Subhūti said to Śakra:
"These flowers have not arisen; they are therefore not flowers.
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked Subhūti:
"Is it only these flowers that do not arise, or is it the case for other phenomena as well?
Subhūti replied, "It is not only these flowers that do not arise; other phenomena likewise have no sense of arising."
What does this mean? Kausika! Form is also unarisen;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also unarisen. Since these are unarisen, they are not form, nor are they anything up to consciousness.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as form (*rūpa*) or any other such category.

This applies to the sense bases (*āyatana*) from the eye-base up to the mind-base, the sense-object bases from the form-base up to the mental-object base, and the elements (*dhātu*) from the eye-element up to the mind-element.
The form realm up to the dharma realm; the eye-consciousness realm up to the mind-consciousness realm; eye-contact up to mind-contact;
all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition;
the earth element up to the consciousness element; the causal condition up to the sovereign condition; and ignorance.
Up to old age and death; the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm; the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; and the four foundations of mindfulness.
Up to and including the eight branches of the noble path; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions;
the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments; the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
from the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; from the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the cloud of dharma; and the five eyes.
the six supernormal powers, the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha,
the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks, the quality of non-forgetfulness,
the state of constant equanimity, all doors of dhāraṇī, all doors of samādhi, omniscience, and the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
One should know that all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry,
up to the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice and the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas; as well as the stream-enterer,
once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattvas, and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, are likewise [to be understood].
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, thought to himself:
"The Venerable Subhūti possesses profound wisdom; he teaches the nature of phenomena without destroying conventional designations."
The Buddha, knowing his intention, confirmed his words:
"Just as Kauśika has conceived in your mind, the Venerable Subhūti’s wisdom is profoundly deep; he speaks of the nature of all phenomena without destroying conventional designations."
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"In what manner, Venerable Subhūti, do you teach the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) without destroying conventional designations?
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas:

“Kauśika! From form up to consciousness, these are merely provisional designations (*prajñapti*). Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these provisional designations of form and so forth, speaks of the *dharmatā* of form and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of form and so forth is neither destroyed nor undestroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor undestroyed. This should be understood to apply in the same way even unto all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
“Kauśika! The venerable Subhūti teaches the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) without destroying conventional designations.
At that time, Subhūti said to Śakra:
“Kauśika! So it is! So it is!”
As the Buddha has taught, there are no phenomena whatsoever that are not merely provisional designations. Kausika!
Having realized that all phenomena are but provisional designations, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should study the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this manner, they do not train in form, nor do they train in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Why is this? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive form as something in which one can train, nor do they perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as something in which one can train; it should be understood that this is likewise true for all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Subhūti:

"For what reason do bodhisattva mahāsattvas not perceive form, nor perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, nor even perceive all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, such that they might train therein?"
Subhūti replied, “Kauśika! Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form;

feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; even the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is empty of the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.”

Kauśika! By this causal condition, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive form, up to and including consciousness, nor do they perceive anything up to and including all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, within which they might train.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of form as the emptiness of form; one cannot train in the emptiness of form as the emptiness of form. In this same way, up to and including, one cannot see the emptiness of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha as the emptiness of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; one cannot train in the emptiness of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha as the emptiness of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in emptiness, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in emptiness. Why is this?
Because there is no duality, Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of form, nor even train in the emptiness of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of form, and even for the sake of training in the emptiness of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Why is this? Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as the expedient, trains in the emptiness of form, and so on, up to training in the emptiness of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas by means of non-duality as the expedient.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to employ non-duality as a skillful means to train in the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
to train in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence;
to train in suchness up to the inconceivable realm; and to train in the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm.
He trains in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; he trains in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
he trains in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
he trains in the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments; and he trains in the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
They study the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; they study the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the Dharma-cloud;
they study the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; they study the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they study the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary characteristics; they study the quality of non-forgetfulness.
Abiding constantly in equanimity, they train in all dhāraṇī-doors and samādhi-doors;

they train in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); they train in the stage of the stream-enterer candidate and the fruit of stream-entry, up to and including the bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; they train in the stream-enterer...
Stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas,
and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas. Kausika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can take non-duality as their skillful means to train in the perfection of generosity up to the state of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva can take non-duality as their skillful means to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure qualities of a Buddha.

“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, employing the skillful means of non-duality, studies the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing form, nor does he study for the sake of decreasing form; and so on, up to: he does not study for the sake of increasing all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, nor does he study for the sake of decreasing all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because from form up to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, there is no duality.

“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase of form, nor for the sake of its decrease, and so on, up to not training for the sake of the increase of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, nor for the sake of their decrease.”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of grasping at form, nor does he train for the sake of destroying form; likewise, up to and including, he does not train for the sake of grasping at all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, nor does he train for the sake of destroying all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because grasping and destruction are not two distinct things.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"When bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this way, do they not train for the sake of grasping form, nor do they train for the sake of destroying form; and so on, up to: do they not train for the sake of grasping all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, nor do they train for the sake of destroying all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas?"
Subhūti replied, “So it is! So it is!”

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this manner, they do not train for the sake of grasping at form, nor do they train for the sake of destroying form; and so on, up to: they do not train for the sake of grasping at all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, nor do they train for the sake of destroying all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"For what reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this way, do they not train for the sake of grasping at form, nor do they train for the sake of destroying form; and so on, up to: they do not train for the sake of grasping at all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, nor do they train for the sake of destroying all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas?"

Subhūti replied: “When bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this manner, they do not perceive that form is something to be grasped or destroyed, nor do they perceive anyone who can grasp or destroy form; and so on, up to: they do not perceive that any Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is something to be grasped or destroyed, nor do they perceive anyone who can grasp or destroy any Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.”
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because phenomena such as form—
whether as the agent or the object, whether internal or external— are all empty and cannot be apprehended.

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any phenomena as being graspable or subject to destruction, nor perceives anyone who can grasp or destroy them, while training in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly accomplish the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in the perfection of wisdom in this manner, are they able to swiftly accomplish all-knowledge?"
Subhūti replied, “Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in the perfection of wisdom in this way, they are able to swiftly accomplish all-knowledge.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do so for the purpose of neither grasping nor destroying any phenomena.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when training in this way, employs as a skillful means neither the grasping nor the destruction of any phenomena, how can they accomplish the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?"
Subhūti replied:

“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive form, up to and including consciousness, as arising or ceasing, as being grasped or relinquished, as being defiled or purified, as being joined or dispersed, or as increasing or decreasing; and so on, up to not perceiving any Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha as arising or ceasing, as being grasped or relinquished, as being defiled or purified, as being joined or dispersed, or as increasing or decreasing.”
Why is this? Because from form up to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, none possess intrinsic nature and are entirely unapprehendable.
Thus it is, Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not perceive the arising or ceasing, nor even the increase or decrease, of any phenomena. By taking as their skillful means the absence of anything to be learned and the absence of anything to be accomplished, they train in the *prajñāpāramitā* and are thus able to accomplish the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Śāriputra: "Venerable One,
where should one seek the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train?"
Śāriputra said: “Kauśika!
The Prajñāpāramitā in which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train should be sought in the previously explained Subhūti Chapter.”
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to Subhūti:
"Is it by relying upon the supernatural power of the Venerable One that Śāriputra has made this statement?"
Subhūti said: “Kauśika!
It is not by relying on my own spiritual power that Śāriputra has made such a statement.”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked:
"By whose spiritual power and support does Śāriputra speak thus? Subhūti replied:
“It is because the Buddha’s spiritual power serves as a support that Śāriputra has made such a statement.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
“All dharmas are without support; how can it be said that the Buddha’s spiritual power serves as a support for Śāriputra to make such a statement?”
Subhūti replied: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said:
all phenomena are without support.
Therefore, the Tathāgata is neither the supporter nor the supported; it is only for the sake of conforming to conventional truth that he is spoken of as a support.
“Kauśika! One cannot apprehend a Tathāgata in non-reliance;
nor can one apprehend a Tathāgata apart from non-reliance.”
Within the *tathatā* that is without support, the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended; within the Tathāgata, the *tathatā* that is without support cannot be apprehended.
Within the *dharmatā* that is without support, the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended; within the Tathāgata, the *dharmatā* that is without support cannot be apprehended.
“Kauśika! The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended in form;
the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended apart from form.
Within the suchness of form, the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended; within the Tathāgata, the suchness of form cannot be apprehended.
Within the dharma-nature of form, the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended; within the Tathāgata, the dharma-nature of form cannot be apprehended.
In this way, up to and including omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended;
apart from omniscience, the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended.
Within the suchness (*tathatā*) of omniscience, the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended; within the Tathāgata, the suchness of omniscience cannot be apprehended.

Within the dharma-nature of all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended; within the Tathāgata, the dharma-nature of all-aspect omniscience cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

Kauśika! The Tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor separate from form; the Tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor separate from that which is apart from form. The Tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor separate from the suchness of form; the Tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor separate from the suchness of that which is apart from form. The Tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor separate from the dharmatā of form; the Tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor separate from the dharmatā of that which is apart from form.

In this way, even up to the point that the Tathāgata and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the Tathāgata and the knowledge free from all aspects are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the Tathāgata and the suchness (tathatā) of the knowledge of all aspects are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the Tathāgata and the suchness of the knowledge free from all aspects are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the Tathāgata and the dharma-nature (dharmatā) of the knowledge of all aspects are neither conjoined nor dispersed; and the Tathāgata and the dharma-nature of the knowledge free from all aspects are neither conjoined nor dispersed.

“Kauśika! What the Venerable Śāriputra has spoken concerns all phenomena as being neither identical nor separate, neither joined nor dispersed; it is sustained by the Tathāgata’s spiritual power, for he takes that which is without support as his support.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Regarding what you previously asked:
'Where should one seek the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in which all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train?'"

"Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train should not be sought within form, nor should it be sought apart from form; likewise, it should not be sought within the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor should it be sought apart from the knowledge of all aspects."
Why is this? Kausika!

Whether it be form or the departure from form, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects or the departure from the knowledge of all aspects; whether it be the perfection of wisdom, or the bodhisattva mahāsattva—if one seeks such things, they are all neither joined nor dispersed, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of no-characteristic.

Why is this? The perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train is not form, nor is it apart from form; and so on, up to: it is not the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it apart from the knowledge of all aspects.

It is not the suchness of form, nor is it apart from the suchness of form; and so on, up to: it is not the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it apart from the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects.

It is not the dharma-nature of form, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of form; and so on, up to: it is not the dharma-nature of the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Kauśika! Because all these things are non-existent and entirely unobtainable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is not form, nor is it apart from form; and so on, up to: it is not the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor is it apart from the knowledge of all aspects.

It is not the suchness (*tathatā*) of form, nor is it apart from the suchness of form; and so on, up to: it is not the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it apart from the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects.

It is not the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) of form, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of form; and so on, up to: it is not the dharma-nature of the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the knowledge of all aspects.
Then Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed Subhūti, saying:
"The perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is a great perfection, an immeasurable perfection, and a boundless perfection."

Those who are stream-enterers attain the fruit of stream-entry by training in this; those who are once-returners attain the fruit of once-returning by training in this; those who are non-returners attain the fruit of non-returning by training in this; those who are arhats attain the fruit of arhatship by training in this; those who are pratyekabuddhas attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha by training in this; and bodhisattva mahāsattvas, by training in this, are able to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Subhūti replied: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said. Why is this? Kausika!

Because form is great, the Prajñāpāramitā studied by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great; and so on, up to: because all-aspect-knowledge is great, the Prajñāpāramitā studied by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.

Why is this? Because form, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), cannot be apprehended in its prior, posterior, or middle limits; therefore it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also called "great."

“Kauśika! Because form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also immeasurable; and so on, up to: because all-aspect omniscience is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also immeasurable.”

Why is this so? Because the measure of form, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), cannot be apprehended; just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so it is with form and the others. Therefore, they are said to be immeasurable.

Kauśika! Because space is immeasurable, form and the other aggregates are also immeasurable; because form and the other aggregates are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also immeasurable.

“Kauśika! Because form is infinite, the perfection of wisdom in which bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also infinite; and so on, up to: because all-aspect omniscience is infinite, the perfection of wisdom in which bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also infinite.”
Why is this so? Because form, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), cannot be apprehended either in its middle or at its limits.
Just as space cannot be apprehended either in its middle or at its limits, so it is with form and the other aggregates; therefore, they are said to be "boundless."

Kauśika! Because space is boundless, form and the other aggregates are also boundless; because form and the other aggregates are boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless.
"Furthermore, Kauśika, because the objects of focus are limitless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also limitless."
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked:
"In what way is it that because the objects of focus are limitless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also limitless?"
Subhūti replied, “Because the objective referent of the knowledge of all modes is boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika, because the objective referent of the dharma-realm is boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless."
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked:
"In what way is it that because the objective sphere of the dharma-realm is boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless?"

Subhūti replied: "Because the dharma-realm is boundless, its objects of focus are also boundless; because the objects of focus are boundless, the dharma-realm is also boundless. Since both the dharma-realm and its objects of focus are boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is likewise boundless."
"Furthermore, Kauśika, because the objective referent of suchness is boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless."
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked:
"In what way is it that because the object of focus—true suchness—is boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless?"

Subhūti replied, “Because true thusness is boundless, its object of focus is also boundless; because its object of focus is boundless, true thusness is also boundless; and because both true thusness and its object of focus are boundless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also boundless.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika, because sentient beings are infinite,
the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also infinite."
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked:
"In what way is it that because sentient beings are limitless, the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train is also limitless?"
Subhūti replied: "What do you think?
Regarding the term 'sentient being,' what dharma does the expression 'sentient being' designate?"
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

"Sentient beings, sentient beings—this is not a designation for what is dharma, nor is it a designation for what is non-dharma; rather, it is comprised of adventitious designations, comprised of designations without a basis, and comprised of designations without an object."
Subhūti spoke again: "What do you think?
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, is there also revealed any truly existent sentient being?"
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: "No,
Venerable Sir!"

Subhūti replied: "In this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, since no real sentient being is demonstrated to exist, it is said to be 'boundless,' because neither a middle nor an extreme can be apprehended therein."
“Kauśika! What do you think?

If all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were to remain for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River and speak the names of sentient beings, would there, in that regard, be any sentient beings who are born or who perish?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: "No,
Venerable Sir!"
"Why is this? Because all sentient beings are pure by nature, and they have been non-existent from the very beginning. Subhūti replied:
"For this reason, Kausika, I say that because sentient beings are infinite, the perfection of wisdom in which bodhisattva mahasattvas train is also infinite."
For this reason, it should be understood that the perfection of wisdom in which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train should be described as great, immeasurable, and boundless.

Chapter 5: The Manifestation of the Stūpa, Part One of the Third Section. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the other devas of the Desire Realm; Brahmā, King of the Gods, and the other devas of the Form Realm; and the Ṛṣis and celestial maidens of Īśāna, simultaneously cried out three times in a loud voice: “Excellent!”

Excellent! The Venerable Subhūti, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power and with the Buddha as his support, has well analyzed and revealed for us—the devas and humans of the world—the subtle and wondrous nature of phenomena, namely, the Prajñāpāramitā.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice this profound perfection of wisdom as it has been taught and does not depart from it, we shall honor, serve, revere, and praise them just as we do the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.

In this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, no dharma can be apprehended; that is to say, herein form cannot be apprehended, nor can feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be apprehended. In this way, up to and including omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), it cannot be apprehended, nor can the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) be apprehended.

Although no such dharmas can be apprehended, there is the provisional establishment of the holy teachings of the three vehicles, namely: the holy teachings of the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, and the Anuttarayāna.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the devas and others, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.
Within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, although no phenomena such as form can be apprehended, there is the provisional establishment of the holy teachings of the three vehicles.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of the expedient of non-apprehension, is able to practice this Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught and does not depart from it, you gods and others should all with utmost sincerity pay homage, make offerings, respect, and praise them just as you would a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.

Why is this? Within this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, although the noble teachings of the three vehicles are extensively expounded, the Tathāgata is entirely unfindable. The Tathāgata cannot be found as being identical to the perfections from generosity up to wisdom, nor can the Tathāgata be found apart from the perfections from generosity up to wisdom.

The Tathāgata cannot be found as being identical to the emptinesses from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, nor can the Tathāgata be found apart from the emptinesses from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with suchness up to the inconceivable realm, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from suchness up to the inconceivable realm;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments; the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the eight liberations or the nine successive meditative attainments, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the eight liberations or the nine successive meditative attainments;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“O devas and others, you should know!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding all phenomena, takes non-apprehension as their skillful means and diligently trains in the perfection of generosity up to the knowledge of all aspects, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to correctly practice this perfection of wisdom and never abandon it. Therefore, you should with utmost sincerity revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise those bodhisattva mahāsattvas just as you would a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.”
“O devas and others, you should know!

In the past, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dīpaṃkara appeared in the world, I saw that Buddha at the crossroads of the capital city of Padmavati. I offered him five stalks of flowers, spread my hair over the mud, and heard the essential points of the True Dharma. By taking non-apprehension as my skillful means, I was able to remain inseparable from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; and so on, up to the knowledge of all aspects and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas.”
At that time, the Buddha Dīpaṃkara immediately bestowed upon me the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, saying: "Good son!

In a future age, after incalculable eons have passed, within this world during the Bhadrakalpa, you shall become a buddha named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān; you shall proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā and deliver immeasurable multitudes."
At that time, the devas all addressed the Buddha, saying:

“This Prajñāpāramitā is truly rare and marvelous; it enables the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly grasp the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). By taking non-apprehension as the means, they neither grasp nor abandon anything from form (rūpa) through to consciousness (vijñāna), and likewise they neither grasp nor abandon anything from the knowledge of all things (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), up to the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”

At that time, the Buddha surveyed the fourfold assembly, as well as the multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the gods of the Four Great Kings, continuing up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, all of whom had gathered together to serve as witnesses. He then looked toward Śakra, the Lord of Devas, and addressed him, saying: "Kauśika!

Whether they be bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, sons of gods, daughters of gods, or sons and daughters of good family, if they do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and, employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), uphold, recite, diligently practice, correctly contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā* to others, you should know that none of these evil Māras or their retinues will be able to find an opportunity against them.
Why is this? Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of form, and so on, up to dwelling well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the knowledge of all aspects;

One cannot gain advantage through emptiness by means of emptiness; one cannot gain advantage through signlessness by means of signlessness; one cannot gain advantage through wishlessness by means of wishlessness. Why is this so?

Thus, all these phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature; whether it be that which finds the opportunity, that which is found, the time, the place, or the matter of affliction and harm—all are unobtainable.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family, neither humans nor non-humans, shall find any opportunity to harm them. Why is this?

These sons and daughters of good family, employing the method of non-apprehension, constantly and diligently cultivate loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity toward all sentient beings; therefore, no humans or non-humans can harm them.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall never be harmed by various perilous and evil conditions through untimely means, nor shall they die an untimely death."
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family constantly cultivate the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) in order to properly nourish and sustain all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

Among all those in this trichiliocosm, from the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the Vast Fruit (Bṛhatphala), who have already resolved upon unsurpassed bodhicitta—if they have not yet heard, received, upheld, recited, diligently practiced, or reflected upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the principle—they should all remain inseparable from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*), and by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as their expedient, they should with sincere hearts hear, receive, uphold, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the principle."
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind set on omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they will—with sincere hearts—listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice, and reflect according to principle upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Such sons or daughters of good family, whether in an empty house, in a wilderness, on a perilous path, or in a place of danger, shall never feel fear, alarm, or horripilation."

Why is this? It is because these sons and daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they skillfully cultivate inner emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*).
At that time, all the gods from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven within this trichiliocosm simultaneously joined their palms and addressed the Buddha in unison:

“If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), are able to constantly and sincerely hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, we shall always follow them with reverence and protection, ensuring that no calamities or afflictions may invade or distress them.”
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are themselves bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

By virtue of being bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they cause all sentient beings to forever sever the various perilous and evil destinies, such as those of the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, and the asuras.

By virtue of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all devas, humans, yakṣas, nāgas, and others shall be forever freed from all calamities, epidemics, poverty, hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and other such sufferings.

Because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all devas, humans, asuras, and others shall forever be free from various unfavorable circumstances; wherever they dwell, the clash of arms shall forever cease, and all sentient beings shall regard one another with hearts of loving-kindness.
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the ten paths of wholesome action;
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
and the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature.
From suchness up to the inconceivable realm; from the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm;
the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
The gates—whether it be the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; whether it be the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma stage;
whether it be the five eyes or the six supernormal powers; whether it be the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the nature of constant equanimity; or whether it be all the dhāraṇīs...

The doors of liberation, the doors of samādhi, as well as all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

it is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world great clans of kṣatriyas, great clans of brahmins, great clans of householders, great clans of laymen, various minor kings, universal monarchs (*cakravartin*), and their attendant ministers and officials.

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Control over Others' Emanations; the Heaven of Brahmā’s Retinue up to the Heaven of Ultimate Form; and the Heaven of Infinite Space up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception.

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world those who are candidates for and those who have attained the fruit of stream-entry; candidates for and those who have attained the fruit of once-returning; candidates for and those who have attained the fruit of non-returning; candidates for and those who have attained the fruit of arhatship;

and candidates for and those who have attained the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood. It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and cultivate the various sublime practices of a bodhisattva.

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there appear in the world Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, and deliver immeasurable multitudes of beings.
"Because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there exist in the world the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, which bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.
World-Honored One!"

For this reason, we—the hosts of devas, asuras, nāgas, yakṣas, and all powerful humans and non-humans—should constantly follow, revere, and protect these bodhisattva mahāsattvas, ensuring that no calamities or afflictions may harm them, and that their activities of hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, practicing, reflecting according to the truth, and transcribing the Prajñāpāramitā remain uninterrupted at all times.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra and the others, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

If sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), are able to constantly listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere heart, you should know that these sons and daughters of good family are indeed Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. Because of these Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, all sentient beings are enabled to forever sever the evil destinies, and even the Three Jewels appear in the world to bring great benefit to all sentient beings.

Therefore, you gods, nāgas, spirits, and those of great power—both human and non-human—should constantly follow, revere, make offerings to, honor, praise, and diligently protect this bodhisattva mahāsattva, so that no calamities or afflictions may harm them.

If you are able to reverently make offerings to, respect, praise, and diligently protect such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, you should know that this is equivalent to making offerings to, respecting, praising, and diligently protecting me and all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions.

Therefore, all you gods, nāgas, yakṣas, ṛṣis, asuras, and so forth, should constantly follow this bodhisattva mahāsattva, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, praising, and diligently protecting him, so that no calamities or afflictions may invade or distress him.
"You should know this!

Suppose the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas were to fill the entire Sahā world-system of three thousandfold thousands of worlds, like a dense thicket of reeds, sugarcane, bamboo, rice, hemp, and thickets, with no space between them. And suppose there were sons and daughters of good family who, throughout their entire lives, venerated, made offerings to, honored, and praised those fields of merit with immeasurable kinds of supreme and exquisite articles of enjoyment.

Furthermore, if there is another person who, for even a brief moment, respectfully makes offerings to, honors, and praises a single Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has newly resolved their mind and does not depart from the six *pāramitās*, the former accumulation of merit compared to this mass of merit would not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor even one *upaniṣad* (infinitesimal) part.
Why is this? It is not by means of the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world;
rather, it is solely by means of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there appear in the world the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

Therefore, all you gods, nāgas, and humans or non-humans of great power, should constantly guard, revere, make offerings to, respect, and praise these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, ensuring that no calamities or afflictions may harm them. By virtue of the mass of merit you shall thereby obtain, you will always enjoy peace and happiness among gods and humans, until you realize ultimate nirvāṇa and perform great benefit for others throughout the limits of the future.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How truly marvelous and extraordinary!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, with sincere hearts, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, correctly contemplate, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, thereby embrace such benefits in the present life as these:”
They bring sentient beings to maturity and adorn and purify Buddha-fields; they travel from one Buddha-field to another to attend upon and serve the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.

Regarding superior roots of goodness, according to what they delight in, by means of reverently making offerings to, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, they are able to cause them to grow and quickly reach fulfillment.

From the presence of the Buddhas, they hear and receive the True Dharma, and until they attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, they never forget the essential points of the Dharma they have heard. They are swiftly able to acquire the perfection of lineage, the perfection of parents, the perfection of the physical body, the perfection of retinue, the perfection of the marks and signs, the perfection of radiance, the perfection of eyes and ears, the perfection of voice, the perfection of dhāraṇīs, and the perfection of samādhis.
Furthermore, by the power of skillful means, they manifest bodies like those of a Buddha, traveling from one world-system to another until reaching a land where no Buddha resides;
there they praise and expound upon the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom,

praise and expound upon the emptinesses from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and praise and expound upon everything from suchness up to the inconceivable.

Regarding the elements (*dhātu*), he praised and expounded upon the element of abandonment up to the unconditioned element (*asaṃskṛta-dhātu*); he praised and expounded upon the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
he praised and expounded upon the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;

he praised and expounded upon the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; and he praised and expounded upon the eight liberations and the nine successive [attainments].
In meditative concentration, he praised and expounded upon the gates of liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he praised and expounded upon the Stage of Pure Observation up to the Stage of the Tathāgata; he praised and expounded upon the Joyful Stage up to the Cloud of Dharma Stage;
he praised and expounded upon the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; and he praised and expounded upon the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They praise and speak of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;
they praise and speak of all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi; they praise and speak of omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;
and they praise and speak of the Buddha-jewel, the Dharma-jewel, and the Saṅgha-jewel.

Furthermore, by the power of skillful means, he proclaims the sublime Dharma for all sentient beings, establishing them within the vehicles of the Threefold Dharma as appropriate, so that they may be forever liberated from birth, old age, sickness, and death, and realize the realm of nirvana without remainder;
or else he rescues them from the sufferings of the evil destinies, causing them to experience various exquisite joys among gods and humans.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"This Prajñāpāramitā is truly rare. If one can embrace such Prajñāpāramitā, then one fully embraces all six pāramitās, and by extension, up to and including all-aspect omniscience; furthermore, one fully embraces the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of pratyekabuddhas, the entire conduct of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.

If one can embrace this *prajñāpāramitā*, then one fully embraces all six *pāramitās*, and by extension, everything up to and including all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 502 (and 503). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The Third Division: Chapter Five, Part Two, "The Manifestation of Stūpas.

"Furthermore, Kauśika, if sons or daughters of good family are able to hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere heart, you should listen attentively and reflect well upon the benefits these sons and daughters of good family will obtain in the present life and in the future; I shall analyze and explain them for you."
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
"Indeed! We pray that you will speak."
"We would like to hear it," they said. The Buddha replied, "Kauśika!

If there are various evil heterodox practitioners and brahmins, or various evil Māras and their retinues, or others who are violent, cruel, and conceited, who wish to perform various harmful acts against this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, as soon as they give rise to such thoughts, they will swiftly encounter calamity themselves; their intentions shall surely be extinguished and their wishes shall not be fulfilled.
Why is this? Kauśika!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing non-apprehension as their skillful means, constantly cultivate the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, taking great compassion and vows as their primary guide.

If sentient beings have long been stingy and greedy, giving rise to various conflicts and disputes, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of generosity.

If there are sentient beings who, throughout the long night, have violated the precepts and committed various evil deeds, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external things and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*).

If there are sentient beings who, throughout the long night, harbor anger and resentment and mutually inflict harm upon one another, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to cause them to abide securely in the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).

If there are sentient beings who, throughout the long night, have been indolent and have abandoned all wholesome deeds, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes everything regarding internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of diligence.

If there are sentient beings who, throughout the long night, have minds distracted and preoccupied with clamor and agitation, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to cause them to abide securely in the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā).

If there are sentient beings who, throughout the long night, are deluded and do not know good from evil, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
If sentient beings wander through birth and death, their minds entangled by greed, hatred, delusion, and so forth,
thereby committing numerous harmful deeds, this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva employs skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) to cause them to subdue and extinguish the causes and conditions of birth and death—
namely greed, hatred, and delusion— or to establish them in the four [immeasurables].
They cause them to dwell in the dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; or they cause them to dwell in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
or they cause them to dwell in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
or they cause them to dwell in the eight liberations and the nine successive attainments; or they cause them to dwell in the various bodhisattva...
On the bodhisattva stages, they may cause them to abide in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence;
or cause them to abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm; or cause them to abide in the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm;
or cause them to abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; or cause them to abide in...
From the Stage of Pure Observation up to the Stage of the Tathāgata, they may cause them to abide in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
or cause them to abide in the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
or cause them to abide in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity; or cause them to abide in all dhāraṇīs.

the doors of liberation and the doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi*); or causing them to abide in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
or causing them to abide in the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddhabodhi*);
or causing them to abide in all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; or causing them to abide in the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas.
They cause others to attain equal enlightenment, or to abide securely in various other mundane and supramundane wholesome dharmas. "Kauśika,

these are called the benefits in the present life for bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*."

“Kauśika! By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in a future life; he will turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes, establishing sentient beings according to their original vows, causing them to reach the ultimate consummation in the training of the three vehicles, even unto the realization of nirvana without remainder.”

“Kauśika! These are called the future benefits for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, with a sincere mind, listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, with sincere hearts, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, then in that place, even if there are evil Māras and their retinues, or various non-Buddhist brahmins and others who are violent, malicious, and arrogant, who harbor hatred and jealousy toward the Prajñāpāramitā and desire to create obstacles, to censure, to resist, and to cause it to quickly disappear—despite having such intentions, they shall ultimately never succeed."

Because they have briefly heard the sound of the Prajñāpāramitā, their manifold evils gradually perish and their merits gradually arise; subsequently, by relying on one of the three vehicles, they shall reach the end of suffering, or escape the evil realms to be reborn among gods or humans.

“Kauśika! Suppose there were a wondrous medicine called Mākṣī; by its majestic power, it can neutralize all poisons. Wherever this wondrous medicine is located, various venomous insects cannot approach it.”

There was a large venomous snake that, driven by hunger, went about seeking food; encountering a living being, it desired to sting and devour it. That creature, terrified of death, fled toward a wondrous medicine. Upon smelling the scent of the medicine, the snake immediately retreated and fled.
Why is this? Kauśika!
Such a wondrous medicine possesses great majestic power; it can benefit life and body, and it can subdue and eliminate all poisons.

One should know that the Prajñāpāramitā possesses great majestic power in this same way. If good sons and good daughters listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to circulate widely, then whatever evil deeds the Māras and their like intend to commit against these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas shall, by the majestic spiritual power of this Prajñāpāramitā, be naturally extinguished in that very place, rendering them powerless to act.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because this Prajñāpāramitā possesses great majestic power, being able to destroy all evils and increase wholesome dharmas.
"How is it that the perfection of wisdom can destroy all evils and increase all virtues?"

That is to say, this *prajñāpāramitā* extinguishes greed, hatred, and delusion; from ignorance up to the entire mass of suffering; hindrances, obscurations, latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), entanglements (*paryavasthāna*), stains, and fetters; the view of a self, the view of a sentient being, up to the view of a knower; the view of annihilation, the view of permanence, the view of non-existence, the view of existence, and various other evil views; stinginess, immorality, anger, sloth, distraction, and folly; the notion of permanence, the notion of pleasure, the notion of self, and the notion of purity; as well as all other forms of greed, hatred, delusion, pride, doubt, and the activity of views—it extinguishes them all without exception. It also extinguishes attachment to form up to attachment to consciousness, and even extinguishes attachment to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) and attachment to enlightenment and nirvana.
Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all such unwholesome dharmas and is able to increase all wholesome matters.
Therefore, the Prajñāpāramitā possesses immeasurable and great majestic power.

Furthermore, Kauśika, if good sons and good daughters wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will be constantly protected by the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śakra Devendra, the Lord of the Sahā World, Mahābrahmā, the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, and other benevolent deities throughout the trichiliocosm. These beings shall not be afflicted by any calamities or misfortunes, and whatever they seek in accordance with the Dharma shall be fully realized.

The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions also constantly protect and mind them, causing evil to gradually diminish and wholesome dharmas to gradually increase—namely, causing the growth of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom—and likewise causing the growth of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). By means of non-apprehension as their expedient, that which is cultivated and that in which they abide never undergoes decline or diminution.

Kauśika! By virtue of these causes and conditions, the speech of this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is majestic and solemn, such that all who hear it feel respect and affection; his words are measured and his speech is free from frivolity; he steadfastly serves virtuous friends and deeply understands how to repay their kindness; and his mind is not obscured by stinginess, envy, anger, resentment, concealment, vexation, flattery, deception, arrogance, or the like.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally abstains from taking life, encourages others to abstain from taking life, correctly extols the dharma of abstaining from taking life, and joyfully praises those who abstain from taking life.”

In this way, up to and including: one is able to abandon wrong views oneself, and also encourages others to abandon wrong views; one unerringly extols the dharma of abandoning wrong views, and joyfully praises those who have abandoned wrong views.

Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice giving up to the perfection of wisdom himself, and also encourages others to practice giving up to the perfection of wisdom; he correctly extols the dharma of practicing giving up to the perfection of wisdom, and joyfully praises those who practice giving up to the perfection of wisdom.

In this way, they themselves cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); they also exhort others to cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; they unerringly praise the dharma of cultivating all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; and they joyfully laud those who cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, and dedicates [the merit] together with all sentient beings equally toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects:
"If I am unable to practice the perfection of generosity, I shall be born into a state of poverty and lowly station;
if I am unable to practice the perfection of ethical discipline, I shall close the gates of humans and devas and fall into the various evil destinies."
If I am unable to practice the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), my faculties will be deficient and my physical form will be ugly, and I shall not possess the perfect body of a bodhisattva;

if I am unable to practice the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*), I shall be unable to cultivate the supreme path of a bodhisattva, as I will constantly harbor indolence and fail to accomplish any undertaking;

if I am unable to practice the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*), I shall be unable to cultivate the supreme samādhi of a bodhisattva, as my mind will remain perpetually distracted and my aspirations will not be fulfilled.
If I am unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, I shall not be able to attain the skillful means by which I transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

If one possesses such conditions as poverty and the like, they lack the power even to bring sentient beings to maturity, nor can they purify a buddha-field; how much less could they attain the knowledge of all modes!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects:
"I must not follow the power of stinginess and greed; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of giving would not reach fulfillment.
I must not follow the power of breaking the precepts; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of pure ethical discipline would not reach fulfillment."
I should not follow the power of anger; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of patience would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of laziness; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of diligence would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of distraction; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of meditative concentration would not be fulfilled.
I should not follow the power of delusion; for if I were to follow that power, my perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) would not be fulfilled.
If my six perfections are not fulfilled, I will ultimately be unable to attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listens to, receives, upholds, recites, diligently studies, reflects upon according to the principle, writes down, explains, and widely disseminates this *prajñāpāramitā*. They thereby obtain such present-life and future-life mundane and supramundane merits and benefits.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This Prajñāpāramitā is most marvelous and rare; it is able to discipline the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they may leave behind prideful hearts, and furthermore, it is able to dedicate them toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika,

how is it that the *prajñāpāramitā* is so marvelous and rare, being able to discipline the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they abandon arrogance, and further enabling them to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*)?”
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the mundane perfection of giving, if they bestow gifts upon the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, the destitute, the aged and infirm, travelers on the road, and beggars, they then form this thought:”
"I am able to give to the Buddha and even to beggars"—

because this bodhisattva mahāsattva lacks skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), although they practice the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*), they give rise to a sense of superiority and are unable to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*).
When the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the mundane perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they form this thought:
"I am able to cultivate ethical discipline up to and including the perfection of wisdom."
They also form this thought:
"I am able to fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means, although they practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, they give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.

In this way, even when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), if they should form the thought:
"I am able to practice all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects."
They also think: "I am able to fulfill all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), although they practice all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects, they give rise to a conceited mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatājñāna*).
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bring sentient beings to maturity and adorn and purify Buddha-fields, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to bring sentient beings to maturity and adorn and purify Buddha-fields; others have no such ability."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva lacks skillful means, although they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, they give rise to a sense of superiority and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!

Such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, relying on worldly minds to cultivate various wholesome dharmas, because they lack skillful means and because their minds are disturbed by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ although they cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not attain it; thus they cannot subdue their arrogant minds, nor can they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñatā).”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of giving, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend a giver, they do not apprehend a recipient, and they do not apprehend the act of giving. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom while practicing giving, they are able to subdue an inflated mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, nor any phenomena whatsoever. Relying upon this perfection of wisdom, and practicing the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to subdue an inflated mind and is also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).

In this way, up to the point where when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not apprehend all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, or any phenomena whatsoever. Because these bodhisattva mahāsattvas rely upon the perfection of wisdom while practicing all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all-knowing (*sarvajñajñāna*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings sentient beings to maturity and purifies buddha-fields, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the maturing of sentient beings, the purification of buddha-fields, or any phenomena whatsoever. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom while bringing sentient beings to maturity and purifying buddha-fields, they are able to subdue haughty pride and also dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, I say: This Prajñāpāramitā is most marvelous and rare;
it is able to discipline the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas so that they abandon arrogance, and furthermore, it is able to dedicate them toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: "Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters can, regarding this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to principle, transcribe it, explain it, and cause it to circulate widely—these good sons and good daughters will experience peace and happiness in body and mind, and shall not be afflicted by any calamities or adversities."

If, while in the midst of military conflict or battle arrays, one recites this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere mind, maintaining compassion and protective mindfulness toward all sentient beings, one shall not be harmed or killed by blades or clubs. All adversaries will give rise to thoughts of loving-kindness; even if they harbor evil intentions, they will naturally retreat and be defeated. For such sons and daughters of good family, it is absolutely impossible that they should lose their lives or have their bodies destroyed by being wounded by swords or arrows in the midst of military service.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

Because these sons and daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* throughout the long night. Thus, they are themselves able to subdue greed, hatred, delusion, pride, evil views, latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), entanglements (*paryavasthāna*), impurities, and the various weapons of evil karma; furthermore, they are able to eliminate for others the various weapons of greed, hatred, delusion, pride, evil views, latent tendencies, entanglements, impurities, and evil karma.
