"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters, being able to engage with this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra without departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen to it with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently study it, contemplate it according to the principle, reverently make offerings to it, honor and praise it, transcribe it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated—then these good sons and good daughters cannot be harmed by any poisons, sorcery, malevolent spirits, curses, incantations, or spells; they cannot be drowned by water, burned by fire, or injured by blades, weapons, wild beasts, enemies, thieves, evil deities, various heterodoxies, or malevolent ghosts.

Why is this? Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is a great illuminating mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the mantra of the unequaled; this Prajñāpāramitā is the king of all mantras—supreme, most wondrous, and peerless. It possesses great majestic power, capable of subduing all things, yet it cannot be subdued by anything.
These sons and daughters of good family who diligently practice and study this king of mantras will not be harmed by themselves, nor harmed by others, nor harmed by both.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family who study this Prajñāpāramitā realize that neither self nor other can be apprehended.

Kauśika! When these sons and daughters of good family study this great king of spells, the Prajñāpāramitā, they do not apprehend a self up to a "seer," nor do they apprehend form up to consciousness; likewise, they do not apprehend anything up to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*). Because they do not apprehend a self and so forth, they are not harmed by themselves, not harmed by others, and not harmed by both.

“Kauśika! When these sons and daughters of good family study this great king of spells, the Prajñāpāramitā, although they have no attainment of either myself or the Dharma, they realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. They observe the differences in the mental activities of sentient beings and, according to what is appropriate, turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma for them, enabling them to obtain great benefit by practicing as taught.”
Why is this? Kausika!

The assemblies of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, future, and present have all diligently studied this profound Great Dhāraṇī King of the Prajñāpāramitā; they have realized, will realize, and are currently realizing unexcelled bodhi, turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, with respect to this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the practice of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen to it with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated—then those good sons and good daughters, wherever they dwell in kingdoms, cities, or towns, shall not be harmed by any calamities, misfortunes, or epidemics, whether caused by humans or non-humans."

Why is this so, Kauśika? Because wherever these sons and daughters of good family dwell, for the sake of this trichiliocosm and all other immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds throughout the ten directions— including all the gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, as well as the nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras— they will constantly come to protect, revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise them, so that no obstacles may arise to the Great Divine Mantra King, the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters write down this Great Divine Mantra King of the Prajñāpāramitā and place it in a pure location, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising it—even if they do not hear it, uphold it, read it, recite it, diligently practice it, contemplate it according to principle, nor explain or analyze it for others—nevertheless, in that dwelling place, city, district, or royal capital, humans and non-humans alike shall not be harmed by any calamities, misfortunes, or epidemics."
Why is this so? Kauśika!

Wherever this great king of mantra-kings, the Prajñāpāramitā, resides, for the sake of this trichiliocosm and all other immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds throughout the ten directions—including all the gods from the Cāturmahārājika Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, as well as the nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others—it will be constantly guarded, revered, honored, and praised, so that no obstacles may arise to this great king of mantra-kings, the Prajñāpāramitā.

“Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family merely write down this great king of dhāraṇīs, the Prajñāpāramitā, and place it in a pure location, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising it, they still obtain such benefits in the present life; how much more so for those who are able to hear it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, and extensively explain and analyze it for others!”
"You should know that such persons possess boundless merit; they will swiftly realize Bodhi and bring benefit to all beings. Furthermore, Kausika!

If good men or good women fear enemies, wild beasts, calamities, malevolent incantations, epidemics, poisons, spells, and the like, they should write down this Great Divine Spell King, the Prajñāpāramitā, and place it in a fragrant pouch according to their means, storing it within a precious tube. By constantly following it with their person, making offerings, paying homage, respecting, and praising it, all matters of fear will naturally be eliminated, for devas, nāgas, and spirits will constantly provide protection."

Kauśika! For example, if a person or even an animal of the animal realm enters the precincts of the Bodhi tree, or merely reaches the vicinity of those precincts, humans, non-humans, and others will be unable to harm them.
Why is this? Kauśika!

All Buddhas of the past, future, and present have sat in this very place and realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Having attained enlightenment, they bestow upon all sentient beings freedom from fear, freedom from dread, freedom from enmity, and freedom from harm, such that their bodies and minds abide in peace and happiness.
He establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to abide in the sublime conduct of the noble ones among gods and humans;
he establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to abide in the blissful sublime conduct of the three vehicles;

he establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to realize and attain for themselves the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship.
He establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings so that they shall realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
he establishes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings so that they may cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

All such supreme matters arise through the majestic power of the perfection of wisdom; therefore, all devas, nāgas, asuras, and others alike protect, revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise this place.

It should be known that it is likewise with this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*: wherever it resides, all devas, nāgas, asuras, and others will constantly come to protect, revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise it, so that no obstacles may arise for the *Prajñāpāramitā*.

“Kauśika! Wherever this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā may be found, you should know that this place is a true caitya; all sentient beings should pay homage to it, and they should honor, revere, respect, and praise it with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters transcribe this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and with various adornments respectfully make offerings to it, honoring, revering, and praising it; and further, make offerings to it with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, myriad wonders, rare curiosities, musical instruments, and lamps—[what would be their merit?]”

There may be sons of good family, daughters of good family, and others who, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, erect stūpas adorned with the seven precious jewels, place the Buddha’s śarīras within them contained in jeweled caskets, and offer them veneration, respect, and praise; furthermore, they provide offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incensed perfumes, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags and canopies, many wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.
"Between these two, which yields the greater merit?
The Buddha told Kauśika:
"I shall question you in return; answer as you see fit."
"What do you think?
By training and learning in what dharmas does the Tathāgata attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the body endowed with the marks and signs?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“The Tathāgata’s attainment of the knowledge of all modes and his body adorned with the marks and signs was gained by training in this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.”
The Buddha told Kauśika: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

Because I have studied and trained in this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, I have attained the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and the body endowed with the marks and signs of excellence.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is impossible for one who does not study the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! It is not merely by attaining the body endowed with the marks and signs that one is called a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; rather, it is by realizing the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) that one is called a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.”

Kauśika! The omniscient wisdom (*sarvajñajñāna*) attained by the Tathāgata arises precisely because it takes the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) as its cause; the Buddha’s body of marks and signs (*lakṣaṇavyañjanakāya*) serves merely as its basis. If one were not to rely upon the Buddha’s body of marks and signs, the omniscient wisdom would have no means of arising. Therefore, while the perfection of wisdom is the direct cause that gives rise to omniscient wisdom, in order to bring this wisdom into manifestation and maintain its continuity, one further cultivates and accumulates the Buddha’s body of marks and signs.

If this body of marks and signs were not the basis for omniscience, all devas, nāgas, asuras, and others would not offer it sincere worship and respect; however, because the body of marks and signs serves as the support for the Buddha’s omniscience, the various devas, nāgas, and asuras offer it worship and respect.
For this reason, after my parinirvāṇa, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others shall offer worship and reverence to my śarīras. “Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family merely pay homage, make offerings, revere, and praise this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, they thereby make offerings to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), to the Buddha’s body endowed with the marks and signs of excellence upon which that knowledge relies, and to the Buddha’s śarīra-relics after his parinirvāṇa.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because the knowledge of all modes, as well as the body endowed with the marks and signs and the śarīra relics, all have the perfection of wisdom as their root.

Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters merely pay homage, make offerings, revere, and praise the body of the Buddha and his śarīras, they are not making offerings to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) nor to this Prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this? Kauśika!
The physical remains of the Buddha's body are not the root of this *prajñāpāramitā* or of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Kauśika! For this reason, if any sons or daughters of good family wish to make offerings to the Buddha’s body, his mind, and his other virtues, they should first hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the truth, write down, and explain such profound sūtras as the *Prajñāpāramitā*. Furthermore, they should honor, revere, respect, and praise them with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, wonderful and rare objects, music, lamps, and lights.
"For this reason, Kauśika!

If any sons or daughters of good family write down this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and with various adornments respectfully offer it worship, honoring and praising it; and furthermore, offer it various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, garments, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, many wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—[they shall gain great merit]."

There may be sons of good family, daughters of good family, and others who, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, erect a stūpa adorned with the seven precious gems; they place the Buddha’s śarīra within a casket made of jewels and install it therein, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising it, further providing worship with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.
Of the merit obtained from these two, the former is greater by an immeasurable multiple.
Why is this so, Kauśika?
In this way, this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* can swiftly bring to fulfillment the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*;
from internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*);

from suchness (*tathatā*) up to the inconceivable realm (*acintya-dhātu*); from the realm of cessation (*nirodha-dhātu*) up to the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛta-dhātu*); and [the realization of] suffering...
the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path;
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments, and the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata.
From the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the Stage of Dharma-Clouds; the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;
all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi; omniscience and the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
The knowledge of all aspects matures sentient beings and purifies Buddha-fields;
it also accomplishes for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas the perfection of lineage, the perfection of physical strength, the perfection of wealth and treasures, and the perfection of retinues;
and it also accomplishes all the ten paths of wholesome action in the world, as well as making offerings.
Śramaṇas, parents, teachers and elders, as well as immeasurable wholesome dharmas such as generosity, ethical discipline, and cultivation,
can also bring about rebirth in the great clans of kṣatriyas, brahmins, householders, and gṛhapatis,
and even up to the heavens of the Four Great Kings and the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception.
It can also accomplish the fruit of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
It can also accomplish the [realization] of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Awakening can also accomplish the inconceivable, the ineffable, the unsurpassed and the most unsurpassed,
the unequaled and the equal to the unequaled— all-knowledge wisdom.
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"As for the people of Jambudvīpa who do not respectfully honor, make offerings to, revere, or praise this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, do they not know that by respectfully honoring, making offerings to, revering, and praising such a profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, one obtains various meritorious benefits?"
The Buddha said to Kauśika:
“I shall now question you; answer as you see fit. What do you think?”
Within Jambudvīpa, how many people have attained verified clarity regarding the Buddha, verified clarity regarding the Dharma, and verified clarity regarding the Saṅgha?
How many people are without doubt regarding the Buddha, without doubt regarding the Dharma, and without doubt regarding the Saṅgha?
How many people have reached the ultimate realization of the Buddha, the ultimate realization of the Dharma, and the ultimate realization of the Saṅgha?
How many people cultivate the ten paths of wholesome action?
How many people practice generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation?
How many people have attained the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment?
How many people have attained the three doors of liberation?
How many people have attained the eight liberations?
How many people have attained the nine successive meditative concentrations?
How many people have attained the four analytical knowledges?
How many people have attained the six supernormal powers?
How many people have permanently severed the three fetters and attained the fruit of stream-entry?
How many people have attenuated greed, hatred, and delusion and attained the fruit of once-returning?
How many people have severed the five lower fetters and attained the fruit of non-returning?
How many people have severed the five fetters of the higher realms and attained the fruit of arhatship?
How many people have resolved their minds and are certain to attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha?
How many people have resolved their minds and are certain to attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

"Within Jambudvīpa, there are some people who have attained pure faith in the Buddha, pure faith in the Dharma, and pure faith in the Saṅgha; likewise, there are even some people who have resolved their minds and are certain to proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

Within Jambudvīpa, there are very few people who attain the verified confidence in the Buddha, the verified confidence in the Dharma, and the verified confidence in the Saṅgha. Even fewer are those who have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha. Thus, even fewer are those who resolve their minds to definitely proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; even fewer, having already resolved their minds, diligently cultivate the practices leading to enlightenment; and even fewer, while diligently cultivating the practices leading to enlightenment, are able to become non-retrogressive and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Kauśika!

Among the classes of sentient beings wandering through birth and death, for immeasurable lifetimes they have mostly not seen the Buddha, have not heard the True Dharma, and have not drawn near to the Saṅgha; they have mostly failed to practice the ten paths of wholesome action, as well as generosity, ethical discipline, and meditative cultivation.
They do not hear of the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, nor do they cultivate the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom.

Likewise, they do not hear of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, nor do they cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.

Kauśika! By this cause and condition, you should know that within this Jambudvīpa, there are extremely few people who attain pure faith in the Buddha, pure faith in the Dharma, and pure faith in the Saṅgha; even fewer are those who have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha; and so on, until even fewer are those who resolve their minds to definitely proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; even fewer, having already resolved their minds, diligently cultivate the practices leading to enlightenment; and even fewer, having diligently cultivated the practices leading to enlightenment, are able to become non-retrogressive and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! I shall now question you; answer as you see fit. What do you think?
Setting aside all the human beings of Jambudvīpa,
how many sentient beings in this trichiliocosm offer worship and respect to their parents and teachers?
How many sentient beings make offerings to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas?
How many sentient beings practice generosity, observe the precepts, and cultivate various meritorious deeds?
How many sentient beings practice the ten paths of wholesome action?

How many sentient beings dwell amidst various desires with the perception of weariness, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of impurity, the perception of revulsion toward food, and the perception that all worlds are not to be relished?
How many sentient beings cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
How many sentient beings achieve pure confidence in the Buddha, achieve pure confidence in the Dharma, and achieve pure confidence in the Saṅgha?
In this way, up to how many sentient beings have resolved their minds to definitely proceed toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas?
And how many sentient beings, having already resolved their minds, are diligently practicing the conduct that leads to enlightenment?
How many sentient beings refine and nurture the mind directed toward enlightenment?
How many sentient beings skillfully practice the perfection of wisdom through expedient means?
"How many sentient beings abide in the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva?
How many sentient beings swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

"In this trichiliocosm, there are few sentient beings who offer worship and respect to their parents and teachers; likewise, there are but few sentient beings who swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
The Buddha told Kauśika: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

In this trichiliocosm, there are very few sentient beings who honor and respect their parents and teachers; even fewer sentient beings honor and respect śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; and so on, until there are even fewer sentient beings who abide in the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva, and even fewer sentient beings who swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

With my unobstructed, pure Buddha-eye, I survey the boundless worlds of the ten directions. Although there are immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings who have resolved their minds on bodhi and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, because they are far removed from the profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) and skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), only one, two, or three sentient beings manage to reach the stage of a bodhisattva’s non-retrogression; for the most part, they fall back into the lower intentions, lower practices, and inferior stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
Why is this? Kausika!

The merit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is boundless and extremely difficult to realize; for sentient beings of inferior wisdom, indolence, inferior diligence, and inferior resolve cannot attain it.

"Therefore, Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters who have resolved upon bodhicitta and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva wish to abide on the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without hindrance, they should repeatedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, inquire of their teachers, and delight in explaining them to others regarding this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā."

Furthermore, one should transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and honor, revere, respect, and praise it; moreover, one should make offerings with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes for scattering, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags and canopies, many wonderful and rare items, musical performances, and lamps.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should likewise hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, inquire of their teachers, and delight in explaining them to others, regarding all other excellent and wholesome dharmas that are subsumed within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; furthermore, they should copy them down, make offerings to them, and revere them.”
What are the other sublime and virtuous dharmas that are subsumed within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*? They are:
the *pāramitās* from generosity up to meditative concentration; the forms of emptiness from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature;
the realities from suchness up to the inconceivable realm; and the realms from the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm.
The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments, and the three gates of liberation;
the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma; and the five eyes, the six...
The superknowledges, the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha,
the quality of non-forgetfulness, the nature of constant equanimity, the doors of dhāraṇī, the doors of samādhi, all-knowledge,
knowledge of the aspects of the path, and knowledge of all aspects, as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-qualities— these are called...
This includes other excellent and wholesome dharmas within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. "Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family should also hear, receive, uphold, recite, and reflect upon according to reason those immeasurable dharma-gates—such as the aggregates, bases, and elements—that accord with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. They should not disparage them, thereby creating obstacles to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Kausika!
These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:

"When the Tathāgata formerly dwelt in the stage of a bodhisattva, he constantly and diligently cultivated and studied the dharmas conducive to awakening—namely, the *pāramitās* from wisdom (*prajñā*) down to generosity (*dāna*), and likewise up to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, together with other immeasurable dharma-gates such as the aggregates, bases, and elements that accord with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. By means of these, he realized the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening."
We who now seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should likewise train accordingly.

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* and all other excellent, wholesome dharmas that accord with it are certainly our true teachers; by training according to them, our aspirations shall surely be fulfilled.

They are certainly the true Dharma-seal of all Buddhas, for it is by training according to them that all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"It is also the true Dharma seal of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; by training in accordance with it, they all attain the ultimate further shore of nirvāṇa. "Therefore, Kauśika!"

All sons and daughters of good family, whether while the Buddha remains in the world or after his parinirvāṇa, should rely upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, extensively explaining it up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas and immeasurable dharma-gates such as the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense-bases (*āyatana*), and should constantly and diligently practice and study them.
Why is this so? Kauśika!

Because this Prajñāpāramitā—extending broadly to include all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā), as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, and immeasurable dharma-gates such as the aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and sense-bases (āyatana)—is the locus upon which all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and others, including devas, humans, and asuras, rely for their benefit and peace.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 501. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The Third Part, Chapter Five: The Appearance of the Stūpa, Section Three.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), should with a sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā* according to the truth; and should widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or should write it down, adorning it with various jewels, and furthermore offer it for even a brief moment with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, diverse rare treasures, music, and lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it—how much merit would these sons or daughters of good family obtain by reason of these causes and conditions?
The Buddha said to Kauśika:
“I shall now question you; answer as you see fit.

Suppose there were sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgatas, for the sake of making offerings to the Tathāgata’s śarīra, would erect stūpas made of the seven precious jewels, adorned with various rare and wonderful ornaments, one yojana in height and half that in width. Furthermore, throughout their entire lives, they would offer and honor them with various celestial flower garlands, powdered and scented incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags, canopies, manifold rare and wonderful things, music, and lamps, paying homage, respect, veneration, and praise.”
"What do you think?
By reason of this, would those sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very many, World-Honored One! Very many!”
“Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha told Kauśika:
“The mass of merit obtained by those sons and daughters of good family is far greater than this, immeasurable and boundless.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Set aside this one matter.

Suppose there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgatas, erect stūpas for the relics of the Buddhas out of the seven precious substances, adorned with various rare and wonderful ornaments, measuring one yojana in height and half that in width. Suppose they fill the entire Jambudvīpa, or the four continents, or a small thousand-world system, or a medium thousand-world system, or even a great trichiliocosm with these stūpas, and throughout their entire lives, they offer and honor them with various celestial flower garlands up to lamps, revering, respecting, and praising them."
"What do you think?
By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very much, World-Honored One!
Very much!”
“Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha told Kauśika:
“The mass of merit obtained by those sons and daughters of good family is far greater than this, immeasurable and boundless.”
Furthermore, Kauśika! Let alone one trichiliocosm.

Suppose all the sentient beings within a trichiliocosm, after the Tathāgata has entered parinirvāṇa, were each to erect stūpas for the relics of the Buddha out of exquisite seven precious gems, adorned with various rare and wonderful ornaments; these being one yojana in height and half that in width, filling the entire trichiliocosm without any gaps. Suppose they were to offer all kinds of celestial flower garlands, up to lamps and lights, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them for as long as their lives lasted.
"What do you think?
Would all the sentient beings in these three thousand great thousandfold world systems, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very much so,
World-Honored One!
Very much so!”
“Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha told Kauśika:
“The mass of merit obtained by those sons and daughters of good family is far greater than this, immeasurable and boundless.”
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying: “So it is,
World-Honored One!”
"So it is! Sugata!

If sons or daughters of good family offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that they are thereby offering worship, respect, honor, and praise to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present."

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many worlds throughout the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River were each to erect stūpas made of the seven precious jewels after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa for the purpose of making offerings to the Buddha’s relics. These stūpas would be adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures, measuring one yojana in height and half a yojana in width, filling every space throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each person would then hold various celestial flower garlands and even lamps and lights, making offerings, paying homage, showing respect, and offering praise for an eon or more than an eon.
“World-Honored One!
By this cause and condition, would those sentient beings obtain much merit?
The Buddha said:
"Very much so!
said Śakra, the Lord of Devas.

"If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they listen to, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra according to the truth; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or even transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and furthermore offer it for even a brief moment with various exquisite flower garlands and even lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it—then the mass of merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through these causes and conditions will be far greater than that [previous merit], being immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because this *prajñāpāramitā* is able to comprehensively encompass and store all wholesome dharmas, namely the ten...
The paths of wholesome action; whether the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; the three doors of liberation; the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments;
the five eyes, the six superknowledges; or the perfection of generosity, up to and including...
The *prajñāpāramitā*, whether it be from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature;
whether it be from suchness up to the inconceivable realm; whether it be from the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm; whether it be the contemplation of the four noble truths;
whether it be the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination; or whether it be from the stage of pure contemplation up to the stage of the Tathāgata.
Whether it be from the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the Stage of Dharma-Cloud; whether it be all the gateways of dhāraṇī or the gateways of samādhi;
whether it be the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the nature of constant equanimity; or whether it be omniscience, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the knowledge of all aspects.
"O Bhagavān, wisdom, as well as all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, are entirely subsumed within this profound Prajñāpāramitā."
This Prajñāpāramitā is the true Dharma-seal of all Tathāgatas, and it is also the true Dharma-seal of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have learned from this; they have realized, are realizing, and will realize unsurpassed bodhi.
All śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas have learned from this; they have reached, are reaching, and will reach the further shore of nirvāṇa.

For this reason, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), should with sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they should write it down, adorning it with various jewels, and further offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, even up to lamps, to honor, revere, respect, and praise it—the mass of merit obtained will be immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable, such that all other masses of merit cannot equal it.
Chapter Six: Praising Merit, Part Three; Section One of Chapter Six: Praising Merit. At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying:
“It is so! It is thus!”
So it is! It is just as you have said, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and with sincere hearts listen to, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon it according to the principle; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, or even transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and further offer various exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it—the mass of merit they obtain will be immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.
Why is this so? Kausika!
It is because by means of this prajñāpāramitā, one is universally able to accomplish all that pertains to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
It fully awakens to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
it can also accomplish the five perfections beginning with generosity; it can also accomplish internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
it can also accomplish suchness up to the inconceivable realm; and it can also accomplish abandonment.
From the realm of elements up to the unconditioned realm, they are also able to accomplish the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
they are also able to accomplish the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment;
they are also able to accomplish the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; and they are also able to accomplish the eight liberations and the nine...
The successive meditative concentrations can also accomplish the three gates of liberation;
they can also accomplish the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; they can also accomplish the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the Dharma-cloud;
they can also accomplish the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; and they can also accomplish the ten powers of the Tathāgata, up to...
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) can also accomplish the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāra*);
they can also accomplish the gateways of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇī-mukha*) and the gateways of samādhi (*samādhi-mukha*);
they can also accomplish the ripening of sentient beings and the purification of buddha-fields; and they can also accomplish [the paths of] śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and [bodhisattvas].
The Supreme Vehicle can also bring about the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Therefore, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) to wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and further offer various exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it—then compared to the merit previously created by constructing stūpas, this mass of merit [of the former] does not equal even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor even a *upaniṣad* (infinitesimal) part.
Why is this so? Kausika!
If this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā remains among the people of Jambudvīpa, then in this world the jewels of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha will never perish or disappear.
By virtue of these causes and conditions, the world constantly possesses the ten paths of wholesome action;
whether it be the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, or the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom,
and so on, even unto all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Wisdom—whether it be among the great clans of Kṣatriyas, Brahmins, householders, or lay-merchants;
whether among the gods from the Realm of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception;
whether among Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or the unsurpassed Mahāyāna; or whether it be the fruit of Stream-entry up to [the fruit of] Pratyekabuddhahood...
Awakening to bodhi: whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva maturing sentient beings, purifying buddha-fields, and practicing the various practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;

or whether it be a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha realizing unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, turning the sublime wheel of Dharma, and delivering classes of sentient beings—such supreme matters are ever...
"it shall not perish or vanish.

At that time, all the gods from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven within this Sahā world-system of three thousand great thousand worlds raised their voices in unison and addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"O Great Seer!..."

One should constantly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, study, reflect upon according to the principle, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise this profound Prajñāpāramitā.

Why is this? If one can, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then all unwholesome dharmas will diminish and all wholesome dharmas will increase; likewise, the hosts of devas will increase while the factions of the asuras will diminish; furthermore, the eyes of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha will never be destroyed, and the lineage of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha will never be severed.

Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, there exist in the world the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; there also exist internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, and so on extensively up to all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*); there also exist the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha-bodhi*); there also exist the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; and there also exist śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

Therefore, O Great Sage, you should always, with a sincere heart, listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, and offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise to this profound Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: "Kauśika!

You should, with a sincere mind, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, and make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise this profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
Why is this? If the asuras and their evil factions should give rise to such a thought:
"We shall wage war and dispute with the devas."

At that time, you and all your celestial retinues should each, with utmost sincerity, recite and contemplate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, making offerings to it, honoring it, respecting it, and praising it.
At that time, the evil intentions arising from the asuras and their factions were immediately extinguished of their own accord.
If any sons or daughters of the gods manifested the five signs of impending death, their hearts were struck with alarm and terror, fearing they would perish and fall into the evil realms.
At that time, you and your retinues of devas should stand before them and recite the profound *prajñāpāramitā* with utmost sincerity.

Then, by the power of their roots of goodness and because they have conceived pure faith in this *prajñāpāramitā*, those devaputras or devakanyās will see the five signs of decay vanish and their bodies and minds become peaceful and secure.
Should they eventually pass away and be reborn in their original place, they will experience celestial wealth and pleasure twice as great as before. Why is this?
It is because the power of the merit from hearing and believing the *prajñāpāramitā* is so vast.

“Kauśika! If any sons of good family or daughters of good family, or any devaputras or devakanyās, should even once hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* enter their ears, by the power of those roots of goodness, they will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Why is this so? Because all Buddhas of the three periods of time, together with their disciples, have studied this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; they have realized, are currently realizing, and will realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, thereby entering the realm of *nirvāṇa* without remainder.
Why is this? Kauśika!

Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* universally encompasses all factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*), fully including whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:

"The profound Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra, a great illuminating mantra, an unsurpassed mantra, a mantra equal to the unequaled, and the king of all mantras; it is most honored, most supreme, most excellent, and most wondrous, capable of subduing all things, yet itself never being subdued by anything."
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can extinguish all evil and unwholesome dharmas, and can fulfill all supreme wholesome dharmas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

Why is this? All Buddhas of the three periods of time have, by relying upon this profound Great Dharani King of Prajñāpāramitā, realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turned the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is by depending on the profound *prajñāpāramitā* that there come to be in the world the ten paths of wholesome action; whether it be giving, morality, and cultivation; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*; and so forth, extensively including everything from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), to the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! Based upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; based upon the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there are the ten paths of wholesome action, and so on extensively until the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha. It is also because of them that śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and perfectly awakened ones appear in the world."

For example, just as it is because of the full moon that medicinal herbs, stars, mountains, and oceans all flourish and increase, so too, because of the bodhisattvas, the medicinal substances of the ten paths of wholesome action—and by extension, all the qualities up to the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas—flourish and increase. Furthermore, all humans, devas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the noble ones who are in training or beyond training, like the stars, also flourish and increase; and all bodhisattvas, as well as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, like the mountains and the great ocean, likewise flourish and increase.

When the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have not yet appeared in the world, it is solely by virtue of the power of their great skillful means that the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas correctly expounds both mundane and supramundane dharmas for the sake of all sentient beings.

Why is this? All vehicles in the world—the vehicle of humans, the vehicle of gods, the vehicle of śrāvakas, the vehicle of pratyekabuddhas, or the unsurpassed vehicle—are accomplished through the skillful means of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; and all the skillful means possessed by bodhisattvas are accomplished through the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), they are able to fulfill the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). To speak extensively, they are able to fulfill everything up to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); they are able to attain the thirty-two marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*) and the eighty minor marks (*anuvyañjana*); they do not fall into the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields; they embrace the fulfillment of the bodhisattva’s lifespan, the fulfillment of requisites, the fulfillment of the pure land, the fulfillment of lineage, and the fulfillment of physical form and strength, until finally attaining the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatājñāna*).
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons and daughters of good family should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, they shall achieve the meritorious benefits of both mundane and supramundane qualities in the present and future lives."
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How do these sons and daughters of good family accomplish the mundane and supramundane merits and benefits of the present and future lives?”
The Buddha told Kauśika:

"These sons and daughters of good family will, in the present life, not be harmed by any poisons, malevolent incantations, or spells; fire cannot burn them, water cannot drown them, and various weapons such as swords and staves cannot injure them. They shall not even meet an untimely death from the four hundred and four diseases, except for those karmic results of past deeds that were fixed and must be experienced in the present life."

Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family encounter legal troubles or are oppressed by enemies and bandits, and they recite and contemplate the profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere mind, then when they arrive at those places, they will ultimately not be subjected to punishment or harm by them.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because the majestic power and influence of the profound Prajñāpāramitā cause phenomena to be thus.

Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family wish to go before kings, princes, ministers, and others, and recite the profound Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere mind, they will certainly be greeted with joy, questioned with courtesy, and honored with offerings by those kings and others.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family are always not separated from the minds of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity toward sentient beings.
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall attain the accomplishment of all such present merits and benefits as these.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family, wherever they are born, will never be separated from the ten paths of wholesome action. Whether it be generosity, ethical discipline, and cultivation; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; the six pāramitās—and to speak at length, up to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); or the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks—they shall not fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts, except when they intentionally go there by the power of their vows to take birth for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.”

In whatever place they are born, they will always possess all their faculties; their physical form will be upright and majestic, with no deficiency in limb or member. They will never be born into families that are impoverished, lowly, or of merchants, artisans, butchers, hunters, thieves, jailers, *caṇḍālas*, *pukkasa*s, or *śūdra*s—nor into any other such base and defiled clans. They will mostly be born through transformation from lotuses within the pure lands of Buddhas, where they commit no evils. They will never be separated from swift supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), traveling to various Buddha-lands at will to attend upon and make offerings to the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones. Therein they will mature sentient beings, adorn and purify Buddha-lands, hear the True Dharma, and practice according to its teachings, gradually realizing the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall attain the accomplishment of all such future merits and benefits as these.
"Therefore, Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters wish to obtain such mundane and supramundane benefits and merits in both the present and future lives,
and never be separated from them until they reach unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, [they should practice this]."
Regarding this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one should, without departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*),
listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it,
contemplate it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated.
Furthermore, they shall offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes,
robes, necklaces, precious banners, streamers, canopies, diverse wonders, rare treasures, music, and lamps;
they shall honor, revere, respect, and praise [the Buddha] without ceasing for even a moment.
At that time, a great multitude of non-Buddhist brahmins, desiring to challenge the Buddha, approached the place where he was.
When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw them, he thought to himself:
"Now these many non-Buddhist brahmins are coming toward this Dharma assembly seeking to find fault with the Buddha; could this not be an obstacle created by Prajñā?"
"I shall recite and contemplate the profound Prajñāpāramitā as I received it from the Buddha, so that those followers of heterodox paths may return by way they came.

Having thought this, he then recited the profound Prajñāpāramitā; thereupon, the many non-Buddhist brahmins offered their respects from afar, circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right, and returned by way they had come.
At that time, having seen this, Śāriputra thought to himself,
"For what reason has he just come and now departed?
The Buddha, knowing his thoughts, addressed Śāriputra:
“Those non-Buddhists came seeking my faults, but because Śakra, Lord of the Devas, recited the Prajñāpāramitā, they were made to depart.
Śāriputra!...”
I do not see even the slightest trace of white dharma in those non-Buddhists; they have come to me solely out of malice, seeking to find fault with me. Śāriputra!

I do not see any among the sentient beings of all the worlds—whether they be gods, Māras, or followers of external paths—who, when the Prajñā is being taught, would harbor a rebellious or evil mind and come seeking an opportunity to cause harm.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because all the celestial hosts of this trichiliocosm— including śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and buddhas, as well as all nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others endowed with great power— collectively protect this profound perfection of wisdom, so that no followers of heterodox paths may create obstacles.
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because all these devas are born through the power of the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and so forth, throughout all the world-systems of the ten directions—each as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—jointly protect this profound Prajñāpāramitā, ensuring that no followers of heterodox paths may create obstacles."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because those Tathāgatas and others are all born through the power of the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, Māra the Evil One secretly thought to himself:
"Now the Buddha is surrounded by his fourfold assembly from front to back, and the devas of the desire and form realms have all gathered to hear him proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā."

"In this assembly, there are certainly great bodhisattvas who have personally received the prophecy of enlightenment from the Buddha; they shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, thereby emptying my domain. I must go there to destroy their vision."
Having formed this thought, he manifested the fourfold army and, displaying fierce and sharp valor, approached the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw this and thought to himself:
"Could it not be that the Evil Māra has manifested these things, wishing to come and disturb the Buddha and create obstacles for the Prajñāpāramitā?"

Why is this? Such an array of fourfold armies, adorned with such extraordinary splendor, cannot be matched by the fourfold victorious armies of King Bimbisāra of Magadha; nor can they be matched by the fourfold victorious armies of King Prasenajit of Kośala; nor can they be matched by the fourfold victorious armies of the Śākya kings of Kapilavastu; nor can they be matched by the fourfold victorious armies of the Licchavi kings of Vaiśālī; nor can they be matched by the fourfold victorious armies of the Malla kings of the Auspicious Reed Land (*Śibira*). Observing this, it is certain that these fourfold armies have been conjured by the Evil Māra.

For a long night, Māra has sought out the Buddha’s shortcomings and seeks to destroy the sublime accomplishments cultivated by sentient beings; I shall now recite and contemplate the profound Prajñāpāramitā as received from the Buddha, so that this evil Māra may be sent back on his way.

Then, having thought thus, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, recited the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Thereupon, the evil Māra departed by the same path, compelled by the power of this great king of dhāraṇīs, the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

At that time, all the deities from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven within the assembly simultaneously manifested various exquisite celestial flowers, fragrant garlands, and other kinds of offerings. Leaping into the air, they scattered them over the Buddha, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha in unison:
"May this Prajñāpāramitā long abide among the people of Jambudvīpa."

Why is this? One should know that as long as the *prajñāpāramitā* circulates among the people of Jambudvīpa, the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha shall never perish or disappear in that place. This is likewise true for this trichiliocosm and even for the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless buddha-fields throughout the ten directions. For this reason, the sublime practices cultivated by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can also be understood.

In whatever region there may be sons or daughters of good family who, with pure faith, write down, uphold, and make offerings to and revere this Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that in such a place there will be wondrous radiance that dispels darkness and gives rise to all manner of supreme merit.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the assembly of devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

As long as the *prajñāpāramitā* circulates among the people of Jambudvīpa, you should know that in those places the Treasures of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha shall never perish. To speak more extensively, wherever there are sons or daughters of good family who, with pure faith, write down, uphold, and venerate the *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that in those places there will be sublime radiance that dispels darkness and gives rise to supreme merit.
At that time, the assembly of devas again each manifested various exquisite celestial flowers, fragrant garlands, and the like, scattering them over the Buddha, and addressed him once more, saying:

"If sons and daughters of good family can, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, no evil Māras or their retinues will be able to find an opportunity against them. We, the assembly of devas, shall also constantly follow and diligently protect them, ensuring they suffer no harm or affliction."
"Why is this? Because we, the assembly of devas, revere the Dharma; we honor him as we would the Buddha, or as we would a disciple held in high esteem by the World-Honored One.
Then, Śakra, Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"These sons and daughters of good family are not able to accomplish this task through meager roots of virtue; they must have, in previous lives, accumulated many roots of virtue in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas, made many true aspirations, extensively made offerings to the Buddhas, and served many virtuous friends, so that they are now able to listen with a sincere heart to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated."

"Bhagavān! If sons or daughters of good family wish to attain the omniscience of all Buddhas, they should study the Prajñāpāramitā; if they wish to attain the Prajñāpāramitā, they should study the omniscience of all Buddhas."
Why is this? Because all the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) attained by the Buddhas arises from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā);
and all perfections of wisdom arise from the knowledge of all modes attained by the Buddhas.

Why is this? The omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas is not different from the perfection of wisdom; the perfection of wisdom is not different from the omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas. One should know that the omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas and this perfection of wisdom are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Therefore, the merit and majestic power of the Prajñāpāramitā are most marvelous and rare.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

For what reason do the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha not extensively praise the names and merits of the five pāramitās beginning with giving, up to and including the name and merit of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), but instead extensively praise only the name and merit of the sixth, the prajñāpāramitā?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"The sixth, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), serves as the sovereign and the guide for the previous five perfections, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā). Therefore, I have extensively praised only the name and the merit of the perfection of wisdom."
"Furthermore, Ānanda, what do you think?

If one practices generosity— and so on, as extensively described, up to the knowledge of all aspects— without dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes, can that be called truly practicing the perfection of generosity, up to the knowledge of all aspects?"
Ānanda replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The Buddha said to Ānanda:

"Only by dedicating [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) while practicing generosity—and so forth, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—can it be called the true practice of the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects."

Therefore, I say that the sixth *prajñāpāramitā* is the sovereign and the guide for the preceding five *pāramitās*, and indeed for everything up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*); thus, I have extensively praised only the name and the merits of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How does one dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna) while practicing the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and so on, up to the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"By means of non-duality as a skillful method, by means of non-arising as a skillful method, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one should dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects."
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“By means of what non-duality as a skillful means, what non-arising as a skillful means, and what non-apprehension as a skillful means, should one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"By means of the non-duality of form up to the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one should dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects and cultivate the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects."
At that time, Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“How, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding everything from form up to the knowledge of all aspects, should one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and how should one cultivate the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Form is empty of the nature of form, and so on, up to the knowledge of all aspects being empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

This is because the nature of form up to the knowledge of all aspects is empty, and thus it is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to the knowledge of all aspects.

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of the perfection of wisdom that one can dedicate [merit] toward omniscience; and because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to bring the perfection of generosity—and so forth, as extensively explained—up to the knowledge of all aspects to ultimate fulfillment.”

Therefore, among the perfections such as generosity, and so forth up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is the sovereign and the guide; for this reason, I have extensively praised only the perfection of wisdom.
“Ānanda, you should know this!

Just as when seeds are sown in the great earth, they grow through the convergence of various conditions; you should understand that the great earth serves as the basis for the growth of the seeds and acts as their support.”

Thus, this perfection of wisdom and the omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) toward which it is dedicated serve as the basis for, the foundation of, and the cause for the growth of the perfections beginning with generosity and extending through all aspects of knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*). Therefore, this perfection of wisdom is the sovereign and the guide among the perfections beginning with generosity and extending through all aspects of knowledge; for this reason, I have extensively praised only the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has not yet finished expounding the meritorious benefits and supreme advantages of this Prajñāpāramitā.”
Why is this? Because the merit and benefits of the perfection of wisdom that I have received from the World-Honored One are exceedingly profound and vast, their measure being without limit.

All sons and daughters of good family who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and further make offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps and illumination, shall obtain merit that is likewise boundless.

If sons or daughters of good family, with a sincere mind, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, they will thereby embrace all the Buddha-dharmas.

By reason of this causal condition, there appear in the world the ten paths of wholesome action; whether it be generosity, ethical discipline, or cultivation; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments; the six pāramitās up to the knowledge of all aspects; the fruit of stream-entry up to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; the great clans of kṣatriyas up to the great clans of householders; the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; and all other superior worldly matters—none fail to appear.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: "Kauśika!
I do not say that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses only the meritorious benefits previously described."
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is endowed with boundless merits and benefits, such that its detailed exposition can never be exhausted.

Kauśika! I do not say that those sons and daughters of good family who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and furthermore offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps as an offering, will possess only the aforementioned merits and benefits.
Why is this? Kausika!

If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they wholeheartedly hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and furthermore offer various kinds of excellent flower garlands up to lamps for worship; [they will gain great merit].

These sons and daughters of good family will accomplish immeasurable and preeminent aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation.
“Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family are like the Buddha. Why is this?

Because it upholds the unsurpassed path of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present; because it resolutely leads toward the Bodhi of the Buddhas; because it brings benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings without end; and because it transcends the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

Kauśika! The aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do not equal even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor even a *upaniṣad* part of the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by these sons and daughters of good family.
Why is this? Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family transcend all inferior mental states of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; they never praise the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, for there is nothing among all phenomena that they do not know—meaning they are able to correctly know that "there is nothing."

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and with sincere hearts listen to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to be widely disseminated; and furthermore, offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps to it, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it—I declare that they shall obtain immeasurable and boundless meritorious benefits in both the present and the future.”
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“We devas shall constantly follow and protect these sons and daughters of good family, ensuring that they are not harmed by any humans or non-humans through various adverse conditions.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:

"If sons or daughters of good family, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), should receive, uphold, read, and recite this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, then at that time immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras will assemble there to hear the Dharma; they will rejoice and leap for joy, reverently receiving this profound *prajñāpāramitā*."

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha), proclaim such teachings corresponding to this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), at that time immeasurable devaputras will all assemble. By their celestial power, they will cause the Dharma-preacher’s eloquence to increase so that he may proclaim [the teaching] exhaustively.”

“Kauśika! When good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension, proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, immeasurable sons of the gods will assemble there out of reverence for the Dharma. By their celestial power, they will cause the eloquence of the Dharma-preacher to be unimpeded, such that no obstacles or hindrances shall be able to interrupt it.”

“Kauśika! Those sons and daughters of good family who, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen to, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and further make offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps—these shall, in the present life, obtain boundless merit and benefits, and neither Māra nor his hosts shall be able to afflict or harm them.”
