"Furthermore, Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, among the fourfold assembly, proclaim the *prajñāpāramitā*, their minds will be free from fear and they shall not be overcome by any polemical challenges."

Why is this so? Because they are sustained by the great king of mantras, the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and because within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā* all phenomena are extensively analyzed—namely, wholesome phenomena and unwholesome phenomena; determinate phenomena and indeterminate phenomena; contaminated phenomena and uncontaminated phenomena; conditioned phenomena and unconditioned phenomena; mundane phenomena and supramundane phenomena; common phenomena and uncommon phenomena; the phenomena of Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas. All such immeasurable and boundless gateways of differentiated phenomena are subsumed herein.

Furthermore, because these sons and daughters of good family are well-established in the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, they do not perceive anyone who can raise an objection, nor do they perceive anything that is being objected to, nor do they perceive any Prajñāpāramitā that is being taught.
For this reason, Kauśika,
because these sons and daughters of good family are sustained by the great king of mantras, the profound Prajñāpāramitā, they cannot be overcome by the polemical challenges of any heterodox teachers.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, regarding this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, copy it, explain it, and cause it to circulate widely, then these good sons and good daughters will always have minds that are not startled, not terrified, and not afraid; their minds will neither sink nor be filled with sorrow or regret."
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family do not perceive any dharma that could cause them to be startled, terrified, or even to feel regret. Kausika!

If sons or daughters of good family wish to obtain these present, boundless merits and benefits, they should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, write down, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra; furthermore, they should offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it without ever ceasing for a moment.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), are able to wholeheartedly hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice, reflect according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra; and furthermore, offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it;

These sons and daughters of good family will always be held in respect and affection by their parents, teachers, elders, friends, kings, ministers, as well as śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; they will also be protected and remembered by the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas of the infinite worlds in the ten directions; furthermore, they will be guarded by the devas, māras, brahmās, humans, non-humans, asuras, and others of the world.

These sons and daughters of good family will achieve the most supreme and uninterrupted eloquence; at all times they will be able to practice the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom—and as extensively explained, up to the knowledge of all aspects—maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields without ever becoming weary or negligent.
These sons and daughters of good family will achieve the sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, traveling through all buddha-fields with sovereign ease and without obstruction;
these sons and daughters of good family will not be overcome by any heterodox arguments of outside paths, but will themselves be able to overcome those heterodox arguments.

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters wish to obtain such benefits and merits that are uninterrupted and inexhaustible in both the present and the future, they should, regarding this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen to it with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to reason, copy it, explain it, and cause it to spread widely; furthermore, they should offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
If good sons and good daughters write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, adorn it in various ways, and place it in a pure location to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise;

At that time, all those from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Vast Fruit throughout this trichiliocosm and other boundless worlds in the ten directions who have already resolved upon unsurpassed bodhicitta will constantly come to this place to behold and pay homage to, read and recite, offer worship and respect, honor and praise, and circumambulate clockwise with palms joined before departing;

likewise, all the gods of the Pure Abodes will also constantly come here to behold and pay homage to, read and recite, offer worship and respect, honor and praise, and circumambulate clockwise with palms joined before departing.

Nāgas of great majesty and power, yakṣas, and so forth, up to humans and non-humans, also constantly come here to behold, prostrate to, recite, offer worship, show reverence, honor, and praise [this], and then circumambulate it to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and depart.
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:

"Now, all the devas, nāgas—and as it is extensively explained, even including humans and non-humans—from this trichiliocosm and the other infinite worlds of the ten directions, constantly come here to behold, pay homage to, read, recite, and worship this profound Prajñāpāramitā that I have transcribed; they honor, revere, respect, and praise it, circumambulate it to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and depart. By this, I shall have already provided them with the gift of Dharma."
Having formed this thought, they will rejoice and leap for joy, causing the merit they have obtained to increase twofold. “Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family, because of this, will be constantly followed and protected by the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others from this trichiliocosm and the infinite worlds of the ten directions; they shall not be harmed by any humans or non-humans, except for those karmic causes of fixed evil deeds from past lives that must ripen in the present, or those heavy evils which are transformed so as to be experienced lightly in the present life.”

Kauśika! By the great majestic power of this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, these sons and daughters of good family shall obtain such various merits and benefits in the present life; that is to say, those among the devas who have already resolved upon unexcelled bodhicitta, or those who, relying on the Buddha-dharma, have attained extraordinary benefit and happiness, will—out of reverence for the Dharma—constantly follow, protect, and increase their strength.
Why is this? Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family have already resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they do so constantly for the sake of rescuing and delivering all sentient beings, constantly for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity, constantly for the sake of never abandoning all sentient beings, and constantly for the sake of benefiting and gladdening all sentient beings.
Those devas shall likewise do so; by this cause and condition, they will constantly come to protect and guard [the practitioner], ensuring that no calamities or misfortunes can afflict them.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 502. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 503.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part Three, Chapter Six: Praising Merit, Section Two.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān! By what signs may these sons and daughters of good family know that the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others from this trichiliocosm and the infinite worlds of the ten directions have come to their place to behold and pay homage to, read and recite, offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to, and circumambulate with palms joined to the right while joyfully protecting and mindful of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* they have written and upheld?”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying:

"If these sons and daughters of good family see a sublime radiance wherever this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā* is located, or if they smell a rare and fragrant incense at that place, or again hear the sound of subtle music, they should know that at such a time, devas, nāgas, and others of great supernormal power and blazing majesty have come to that place. They observe, pay homage to, read, and recite the profound *Prajñāpāramitā* as it is written and upheld there; they make offerings, show respect, honor, and praise it, joining their palms, circumambulating it to the right, and joyfully protecting and mindful of it."
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

When these sons and daughters of good family cultivate pure conduct and adorn their dwelling, and with a sincere heart make offerings to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that at that time, devas, nāgas, and others of great supernatural power and blazing majesty will come to that place. They will observe and pay homage to, read and recite, and make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the profound *prajñāpāramitā* written and upheld there; they will join their palms, circumambulate it to the right, and joyfully protect and keep it in mind."

“Kauśika! Whenever gods, nāgas, and others possessed of such great supernormal powers and blazing majesty come to that place, all the malevolent spirits and heterodox deities therein will be struck with terror and disperse, none daring to remain.”

By virtue of these causes and conditions, the minds of these sons and daughters of good family will become vast and give rise to pure resolute conviction; the wholesome karma they cultivate will become doubly more radiant and clear, and all their undertakings will be free from obstacles.

"For this reason, Kauśika! Wherever this profound *prajñāpāramitā* may be located, one should thoroughly clear away all filth and refuse, sweep and scrub the area, apply ointments, and sprinkle it with scented water. One should arrange a precious throne and install [the scripture] there;

burn incense, scatter flowers, and set up canopies and awnings. Adorn the space with precious banners, pennants, and bells, as well as various exquisite and rare objects, vessels of gold and silver, clothing, necklaces, music, and lamps—decorating that place with all manner of variegated ornaments."

If one can make such offerings to this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, then immeasurable devas, nāgas, and others—possessing great supernormal powers and blazing with majestic virtue—will come to that place. They will observe and pay homage to it, read and recite the profound Prajñāpāramitā as it is written and upheld there, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it; they will join their palms, circumambulate it to the right, and joyfully protect and keep it in mind.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If these sons and daughters of good family can thus make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will certainly attain a body and mind free from weariness, a body and mind at peace, a body and mind that are supple and compliant, and a body and mind that are light and agile."

With the mind bound to the *prajñāpāramitā*, when sleeping at night, one shall have no evil dreams but only auspicious ones; that is to say, one shall see the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, his body of true golden color adorned with the marks and signs, emitting great light that universally illumines all things, surrounded before and behind by śrāvakas and bodhisattvas. Standing amidst the assembly, one hears the Buddha preach the dharmas associated with the *prajñāpāramitās* of generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, up to and including unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). Furthermore, one hears the detailed analysis of the meanings associated with the *prajñāpāramitās* of generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, up to and including unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.

Or, within a dream, one may see a Bodhi tree, vast in height and breadth and adorned with various jewels, beneath which a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has gone to sit in the full lotus posture, having realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and is turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.

Or, within a dream, one may see an assembly of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of great bodhisattvas deliberating and discerning various meanings of the Dharma, namely: how one should thus bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, cultivate the bodhisattva practices, subdue the armies of Māra, sever the habitual tendencies of afflictions, and proceed toward the realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Furthermore, they may see in their dreams the worlds of the ten directions, each containing immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas, and they also hear their voices, saying: "In such-and-such a world, such-and-such a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and Śrāvaka disciples who pay him homage, is preaching such a Dharma."

Furthermore, they may dream that in each of the worlds of the ten directions, there are immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas entering parinirvāṇa. After each of those Buddhas has entered parinirvāṇa, there are donors who, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddhas' *śarīra*, construct with exquisite seven precious gems immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of great *stūpas*. Moreover, at each and every *stūpa*, they offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise through immeasurable ages, using countless supreme and wonderful flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, various marvelous and rare objects, music, and lamps.

“Kauśika! When these sons and daughters of good family see such auspicious signs in their dreams, whether asleep or awake, their bodies and minds are peaceful and joyful; the various devas augment their vital energy, causing them to feel their own bodies become light and agile.”

For this reason, he does not become excessively attached to food, drink, medicine, clothing, or bedding; his mind remains light and subtle toward these four types of offerings. Just as a yogin who has entered a sublime meditative concentration finds his body and mind nourished by the power of that samādhi, such that even upon emerging from meditation and encountering exquisite food, his mind remains light and subtle—this is likewise the case here.
Why is this so? Kauśika!

It is because these sons and daughters of good family are protected and sustained by the compassion of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others who possess great supernormal powers and supreme majesty throughout this trichiliocosm and the infinite worlds of the ten directions; they secretly infuse their bodies and minds with wondrous vital essence, causing their resolve to be courageous and their physical strength to flourish.

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family wish to attain such various present benefits and merits, they should give rise to the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), and with a sincere heart listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, though unable to hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, or reflect upon this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and unable to extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings, nevertheless writes it down, adorns it with various jewels, and further offers it worship, respect, honor, and praise with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, up to lamps and illumination, they too shall obtain the various merits and benefits as previously described.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because these sons and daughters of good family are able to extensively bring benefit and happiness to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), should with a sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and furthermore make offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands up to lamps and so forth; [they shall gain immeasurable merit]."

The mass of merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family is immeasurable and boundless; it surpasses that of other sentient beings who, throughout their entire lives, provide all manner of superior and exquisite food, drink, clothing, bedding, medicine, and requisites as offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas in all worlds of the ten directions. It also surpasses the merit of those who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddhas of the ten directions and their disciples, erect stupas made of the seven precious jewels—high, vast, and magnificent—to enshrine their *śarīra*, and further offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise with immeasurable celestial flower garlands, up to lamps and lights, for the rest of their lives.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because all the Buddhas of the ten directions and their assemblies of disciples are born and grow by means of this very profound Prajñāpāramitā.
Chapter 7: The Relics of the Buddha, Part Three. Chapter Seven: The Relics of the Buddha. At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

Suppose this Jambudvīpa were filled with one portion consisting of the relics of the Buddha, and another portion consisted of the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā written down—of these two portions, which would you take?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
"I would rather take up this profound Prajñāpāramitā. Why is that? Because..."

It is not that I lack faith, devotion, worship, respect, honor, or praise for the *śarīra* relics of the Buddhas; rather, it is because the bodies of the Buddhas and their *śarīra* relics are all born from this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, and are all cultivated by the power and influence of the merit of the *prajñāpāramitā*, that they are worshipped, revered, honored, and praised by all the worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras.
Then Śāriputra said to Śakra: “Kauśika!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics (*animitta*). Since a dharma that is without characteristics cannot be grasped, how can you grasp it?”

Why is this? Kauśika! The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without grasping and without relinquishing; it is without increase and without decrease; it is without accumulation and without dispersal; it is without benefit and without harm; it is without defilement and without purity. It does not bestow the dharmas of the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, or śrāvakas, nor does it discard the dharmas of foolish ordinary beings (*bālapṛthagjana*). It does not bestow the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*), nor does it discard the conditioned realm (*saṃskṛtadhātu*). It does not bestow the various emptinesses (*śūnyatā*), nor does it discard the various realms of existence (*bhava*). It does not bestow the *pāramitās* up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor does it discard any dharmas of affliction (*saṃkleśa*).
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied to Śāriputra: “So it is! So it is!”
It is exactly as you have said, Venerable One!

If one knows the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it truly is—formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely the characteristic of being without characteristics; if one neither grasps nor abandons, and even does not associate with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), yet does not discard any phenomena of affliction (*saṃkleśa*)—this is the true grasping of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and this is the true practice of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Why is this? Because the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity do not follow a dualistic course, as they are devoid of dual characteristics.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
It is as you have said:
from the profound *prajñāpāramitā* down to the *dānapāramitā*, they do not follow dualistic courses, because they are devoid of dual characteristics.

Kauśika! Those who would wish for the profound perfection of wisdom, up to and including the perfection of generosity, to have two distinct characteristics, would likewise wish for true thusness, up to and including the inconceivable realm, to have two distinct characteristics as well.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, up to and including the *dānapāramitā*, and the *tathatā*, up to and including the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The profound Prajñāpāramitā should be wholeheartedly prostrated to, circumambulated to the right, honored, revered, respected, and praised by the world with its devas, humans, asuras, and others."

Why is this? Because all the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, through diligent cultivation and study of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
“World-Honored One!

Just as when I am seated upon the throne of the Lord of Devas in the Sudharma Hall of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, preaching the True Dharma for the assembly of devas, immeasurable sons of gods come to my presence to listen to what I say; they make offerings, show reverence, respect, and praise me, circumambulate me to the right, prostrate, join their palms, and then depart.”

If I am not present at that Dharma-seat, the sons of the gods will also come to that place; though they do not see me, they will pay homage and make offerings just as they did when I was there, all saying:

"This is the seat where Śakra, Lord of Devas, expounds the Dharma for the sake of the devas; we should all treat it as if the Lord of Devas were present, making offerings, circumambulating to the right, and prostrating before departing."
“World-Honored One!

If this Prajñāpāramitā is thus written down, received, upheld, recited, and widely proclaimed and disseminated for the sake of sentient beings, you should know that at such a place, there will always be those from this land as well as from the infinite worlds of the ten directions—countless and immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others—who all come to assemble.”

Even if there were no one to preach it, because of their reverence for the Dharma, they would likewise offer worship, honor, respect, and praise at that place, prostrating themselves before departing. Why is this?

Because all the requisites for happiness belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all sentient beings, are obtained by depending upon the Prajñāpāramitā.
The *śarīra* of the Buddha likewise receives offerings because it has been perfumed by the merit of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
"World-Honored One!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* serves as the cause, the condition, the basis, and the means of elicitation for the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and for the attainment of all-knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*). Therefore, I say: "

Suppose this Jambudvīpa were filled with relics of the Buddha as one portion, and a profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā were written down as another portion; between these two portions, my inclination would be to take the profound Prajñāpāramitā.
“World-Honored One!
When I uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, because my mind accords with the Dharma, I do not perceive any signs of fear whatsoever.”
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without marks, without characteristics, without speech, and without expression.

Since the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without marks, without characteristics, without speech, and without expression, the five *pāramitās* beginning with *dhyāna*, and so forth up to all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), are likewise without marks, without characteristics, without speech, and without expression.
“World-Honored One!

If the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possessed characteristics, marks, words, or explanations, rather than being without characteristics, marks, words, or explanations, then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha would not have realized that all phenomena are without characteristics, marks, words, or explanations, nor would he have attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and taught all sentient beings that all phenomena are without characteristics, marks, words, or explanations.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible—rather than possessing signs, marks, or verbal expression—the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, knowing all phenomena to be signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible, has realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and for the sake of all sentient beings, he teaches that all phenomena are signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible.”
“World-Honored One!

For this reason, this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā should be received with offerings, reverence, respect, and praise of immeasurable kinds of supreme and exquisite flower garlands, up to lamps and illumination, by all the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others.”
"Bhagavān! If there should be those who, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite,
diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, write down, and explain this profound Prajñāpāramitā..."
They shall cause it to be widely disseminated and further honor, revere, respect, and praise it with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and lights;
they will certainly never again fall into the various evil destinies, nor among the borderlands, the barbarians, or the mlecchas,
nor will they fall into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but will surely proceed toward [Buddhahood].
Regarding unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, they constantly behold all Buddhas, perpetually hear the true Dharma, and never part from spiritual friends;
they adorn and purify Buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity,
traveling from one Buddha-land to another, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising all Buddhas with immeasurable kinds of supreme and exquisite requisites.
"Bhagavān and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas!

Furthermore, Bhagavān, suppose one portion were the relics of the Buddha filling the trichiliocosm, and another portion were this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā written down; between these two portions, my inclination would be to take the profound Prajñāpāramitā."
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the *śarīras* of the Buddhas throughout the trichiliocosm, are all born from the Prajñāpāramitā;

furthermore, because the *śarīras* of the Buddhas throughout the trichiliocosm have been perfumed and cultivated by the power of the merit of the Prajñāpāramitā, they receive the offerings, reverence, respect, and praise of devas, humans, asuras, and others.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, if sons or daughters of good family make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the *śarīra* of the Buddha, they will certainly not be born in any of the perilous or evil realms; they will always be born in the auspicious realms to enjoy various riches and pleasures, and according to their aspirations, they shall ride upon the Three Vehicles and ultimately realize the *nirvāṇa* of the Three Vehicles.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If various sons and daughters of good family should see the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, or should see this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, these two merits are equal and without distinction."
Why is this? Because the profound perfection of wisdom is equal to, non-dual with, and indivisible from all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If there is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who abides in the three miraculous displays (*prātihārya*) and proclaims the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings—namely, from the *sūtras* up to the *upadeśas*—and if a son or daughter of good family likewise receives, maintains, recites, and extensively explains the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to others, these two merits are equal and without distinction."

Why is this? Because whether it be those Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, or their three modes of miraculous display, or the twelvefold teachings they have proclaimed, all are born from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the worlds of the ten directions, abide in the three modes of manifestation and proclaim the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings—namely, from the sūtras up to the treatises—and if sons or daughters of good family receive, uphold, recite, and extensively explain this profound Prajñāpāramitā to others..."
These two merits are equal and without distinction. Why is this?

Because all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the worlds of the ten directions; their three modes of miraculous manifestation; and the twelvefold teachings they proclaim—all arise in dependence upon the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

Suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, with immeasurable varieties of exquisite flower garlands and even lamps and lights, offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to as many Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the worlds of the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River;

and suppose there are other sons or daughters of good family who copy and uphold this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, and furthermore offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to it with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands and even lamps and lights."
These two merits are equal and without distinction. Why is this?
Because all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are born from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

"Furthermore, Blessed One, if sons or daughters of good family wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, write down, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they shall not fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts in the future, nor shall they fall into the stages of the śrāvaka or the pratyekabuddha."
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family will certainly abide in the stage of non-retrogression, remaining far removed from all calamities, epidemics, misfortunes, and fears.
Just as a debtor, fearing his creditor, immediately seeks the protection and service of a king, and through the king’s power escapes that fear;

so too, the *prajñāpāramitā* is likened to the king, and those sons and daughters of good family to the debtor. By relying upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, they attain liberation from all misfortune, affliction, and fear.
"World-Honored One!
It is just as when a person, by relying upon a king and being taken under his protection, is honored, revered, respected, and praised by all people of the world;

so too are the relics of the Buddha, for they have been perfumed and cultivated by the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and thus are honored, revered, respected, and praised by devas, humans, asuras, and others."
The King is a metaphor for the *prajñāpāramitā*, and the Buddha’s *śarīra* (relics) are a metaphor for that which relies upon the King.
“World-Honored One!

The omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas is also accomplished in reliance upon the *prajñāpāramitā*. For this reason, I say that even if this trichiliocosm were filled with the Buddha’s *śarīra* as one portion, and there were a written copy of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra as another portion—of these two portions, my intention would rather take the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

Why is this? Because the Buddha’s *śarīra* (relics) are firmer than adamant and possess various colors; because his body is adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics; and because the ten powers of a Tathāgata, and so forth up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), are all accomplished through the *prajñāpāramitā*.
The five pāramitās, beginning with generosity, all reach the "other shore" by virtue of the name Prajñāpāramitā. Why is this?
Because without Prajñāpāramitā, generosity and the others cannot reach the other shore.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

Whether it be the royal capitals, cities, towns, or villages within this trichiliocosm or in other worlds, wherever there are sentient beings who uphold, recite, transcribe, explain, and reverently make offerings to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the sentient beings in those places shall not be harmed or afflicted by any humans or non-humans, except for those whose suffering is determined by the inevitable ripening of their own evil karma. Within these places, sentient beings will gradually train in the correct practice of the Three Vehicles, and according to their aspirations, they shall even attain the *nirvāṇa* of the Three Vehicles."
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* brings great benefit to the trichiliocosm and possesses great supernormal power; wherever it resides, there is a Buddha performing the various works of a Buddha, namely, bringing benefit, peace, and joy to all sentient beings."
World-Honored One!

It is like a priceless great divine jewel, endowed with immeasurable kinds of supreme and wondrous majesty and virtue; wherever this divine jewel resides, humans and non-humans can never cause harm or affliction.

Should there be a man or a woman possessed by a ghost, suffering physical and mental distress, if someone were to show them this divine jewel, the ghost would immediately depart by the power of the jewel.

Whether there be fevers caused by wind, phlegm, or heat; or diseases resulting from the confluence of wind, phlegm, and heat—if one ties this divine bead to the body, none of these ailments will fail to be cured.

This jewel can provide illumination in the darkness; it cools when it is hot and warms when it is cold. Wherever this divine jewel is located, the seasons remain harmonious, being neither too cold nor too hot.
If this divine jewel is present in a locality, snakes, scorpions, and other venomous creatures will not dare to remain there.

Should there be a man or a woman who has been bitten by such venom and finds the pain unbearable, if they are made to see this divine jewel, the poison will be instantly neutralized by the power of the jewel.

If any sentient beings are afflicted with leprosy, malignant sores, swellings, blisters, dizziness, cataracts, or other diseases of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, throat, body, or various ailments of the limbs and joints, all these illnesses shall be healed by wearing this divine jewel.

If the water in various ponds, pools, springs, or wells is turbid and foul, or is on the verge of drying up, and one casts this jewel into it, the water immediately becomes full, fragrant, pure, and clear, endowed with the eight meritorious qualities;

if one wraps this divine jewel in a garment of various colors—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, azure, or green—and casts it into the water, the water takes on those various colors according to the hues of the cloth.

Thus, the majestic power of this priceless, great jewel-god is boundless and cannot be fully described; even when placed within a casket, it causes that vessel to be fully endowed with boundless majesty. Even if the casket is empty, because the jewel once resided within it, the vessel remains cherished and honored by all people.
The Venerable Ānanda asked Śakra:
"Is such a divine jewel possessed only by the gods, or do humans have it as well?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
"This jewel exists both among humans and in the heavens. If it is among humans, its form is small and heavy; if it is in the heavens, its form is large and light.

Furthermore, the characteristics of the jewel among humans are not fully complete, whereas those in the heavens are perfectly round and complete. The majestic power and virtue of the divine jewel in the heavens is infinitely superior, exceeding that of all human jewels by countless multiples."
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is likewise so; it is the root of all virtues and can extinguish immeasurable evil and unwholesome dharmas. In whatever place it resides, it causes the physical and mental suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings to be entirely eliminated, such that humans, non-humans, and others cannot cause them harm."

“World-Honored One! This priceless great jewel of divine power that you have described is not merely a metaphor for the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; it is also a metaphor for the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and likewise for the *dhyāna-pāramitā* down to the *dāna-pāramitā*. It is also a metaphor for the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) down to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*). It is also a metaphor for the four applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) down to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*). It is also a metaphor for suchness (*tathatā*) down to the inconceivable realm (*acintya-dhātu*). It is also a metaphor for the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*). It is also a metaphor for all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). It is also a metaphor for all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi, and it is a metaphor for the immeasurable and boundless qualities of a Buddha.”

Why is this? Such merits are all brought forth and manifested by the Great Divine Mantra King that is the Prajñāpāramitā; these merits are profound, vast, immeasurable, and boundless. Because the Buddha’s śarīra has been perfumed and cultivated by these various merits, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, it is worthy of receiving the offerings, reverence, respect, and praise of all the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others.

"Furthermore, World-Honored One, because the Buddha’s *śarīra* (relics) are the vessel that serves as the support for the most perfect, supreme, and pure *pāramitās* of wisdom (*prajñā*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), diligence (*vīrya*), patience (*kṣānti*), ethical discipline (*śīla*), and generosity (*dāna*), and so forth, up to the permanent severance of the continuity of the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of afflictions and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, they are worthy of receiving all offerings, veneration, respect, and praise from the world of gods, humans, and asuras after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa."
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

Because the *śarīra* of the Buddha is the vessel that supports the *pāramitās* of the most perfect, supreme, and pure precious qualities; because it is the vessel that supports the *pāramitās* of the most perfect, supreme, and pure—unstained and unpurified, unborn and unceasing, non-entering and non-exiting, non-increasing and non-decreasing, non-coming and non-going, non-moving and non-stopping, and without this or that; because it is the vessel that supports the *pāramitās* of the true nature (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena which is most perfect and supremely pure—it is worthy of receiving all offerings, reverence, respect, and praise from the world of gods, humans, and asuras after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa."
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

Setting aside the relics of the Buddha within the trichiliocosm, suppose there were one portion consisting of the relics of the Buddhas filling as many worlds in each of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and another portion consisting of the written profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā; between these two portions, my intention would be to take the profound Prajñāpāramitā."

Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as their śarīras, are born from the Prajñāpāramitā; because they have all been cultivated by the Prajñāpāramitā; and because they serve as the vessel upon which the Prajñāpāramitā relies, they are worthy of receiving the offerings, reverence, respect, and praise of all the worlds, including devas, humans, and asuras.
“World-Honored One!
If good sons and good daughters make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the relics of the Buddha, they will enjoy all manner of wealth and happiness among devas and humans without end.”

Among human beings, this refers to those of great clans such as the Kṣatriyas up to the Vaiśyas; among the devas, it refers to those from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven. By means of such distinguished roots of goodness, one attains the end of suffering in one's final body.

“Bhagavān! If sons or daughters of good family listen with a sincere mind to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, copy it, explain it, and contemplate it according to the principle, they will swiftly bring the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to full completion.”

Because the profound perfection of wisdom is brought to fulfillment, it further causes the perfection of meditative concentration, and so forth, down to the perfection of generosity; and likewise the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, to be brought to fulfillment as well.

By means of this, one is further able to transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enter the bodhisattva's state of rightness and departure from birth (samyaktva-niyāma), and attain the bodhisattva’s sublime and wondrous supernormal powers (abhijñā).

Riding upon these supernormal powers, they travel through the various Buddha-fields, proceeding from one Buddha-land to another, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-fields, and manifest various bodies through the arousal of supreme thoughts and vows.

For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, they may become a Great Wheel-Turning King, or a Lesser Wheel-Turning King, or a great king, or a minor king; they may become a Kṣatriya, or a Brāhmaṇa, or Vaiśravaṇa, or Śakra, Lord of Devas, or Brahmā, or other such forms, thereby bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
Therefore, World-Honored One!

It is not that I lack faith, joy, worship, respect, reverence, and praise toward the *śarīra* relics of the Buddhas; however, the merit obtained from worshiping, respecting, revering, and praising the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* is far greater than that. For this reason, I would rather take up the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters, etc., make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they thereby increase all Buddha-dharmas and also receive and sustain the sovereign mastery over mundane and supramundane wealth and happiness; thus, they have already made offerings to, revered, respected, and praised the *śarīra* relics of the Buddhas, as well as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Chapter 3: The Accumulation of Merit, Section 8-1. At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If sons or daughters of good family wish to constantly behold the Dharma-body and form-body of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the infinite and incalculable worlds of the ten directions, they should, with a sincere mind, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.

When these sons and daughters of good family have attained the constant vision of the Dharma-body and form-body of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the infinite and incalculable worlds of the ten directions, they shall gradually practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā until it is swiftly perfected; at that time, they should cultivate the recollection of the Buddha through the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
“World-Honored One!
The nature of all phenomena is briefly of two kinds:
first, the conditioned.”
The second is the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). What is called the nature of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma-tathatā*)?

It refers to the wisdom of the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; the wisdom of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the wisdom of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena; the wisdom of determinate and indeterminate phenomena; the wisdom of contaminated and uncontaminated phenomena; the wisdom of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena; the wisdom of faulty and faultless phenomena; the wisdom of mundane and supramundane phenomena; and the wisdom of defiled and purified phenomena. All such immeasurable gateways of wisdom are collectively designated as the nature of conditioned phenomena.
What is called the nature of unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛta-dharmatā*)?

It refers to all phenomena being without arising and without cessation, without abiding and without change, without defilement and without purity, without increase and without decrease, without marks and unconditioned, and without nature or self-nature; this is what is called the nature of unconditioned phenomena.
These sons and daughters of good family should practice the recollection of the Buddha toward the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas by means of these two kinds of dharmatā.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!
All Buddhas of the past, future, and present rely upon the Prajñāpāramitā; they have realized, will realize, and are currently realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

The śrāvaka disciples of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present have all, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, already attained, shall attain, or are currently attaining the fruits of srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, and arhat;
the pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, and present have all, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, already realized, are currently realizing, or shall realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because within the secret treasury of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the teachings corresponding to the three vehicles are extensively expounded.

However, these explanations are given with non-apprehension as the means, with the absence of intrinsic nature and the absence of marks as the means, with neither arising nor ceasing as the means, with neither defilement nor purity as the means, with neither creation nor volitional action as the means, with neither entering nor exiting as the means, with neither increase nor decrease as the means, and with neither grasping nor relinquishing as the means; all such explanations rely upon the conventional, not upon the ultimate truth.

Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is neither *prajñāpāramitā* nor non-*prajñāpāramitā*; it is not this shore, nor the other shore, nor the middle stream; it is not land, nor water; it is not high, nor low; it is not equal, nor unequal; it is not with signs (*sanimitta*), nor signless (*animitta*); it is not mundane (*laukika*), nor supramundane (*lokottara*); it is not with outflows (*sāsrava*), nor without outflows (*anāsrava*); it is not conditioned (*saṃskṛta*), nor unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*); it is not wholesome (*kuśala*), nor unwholesome (*akuśala*); it is not determinate (*vyākṛta*), nor indeterminate (*avyākṛta*); it is not of the past, nor of the future, nor of the present.

“Kauśika! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not bestow the qualities of the Buddhas, nor the qualities of Bodhisattvas, nor the qualities of Pratyekabuddhas, nor the qualities of Śrāvakas; yet it does not abandon the various qualities of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*).”
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“The profound perfection of wisdom is a great perfection; it is the unsurpassed perfection; it is the unequaled perfection.”

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, although they know the distinctions among the mental activities and spheres of all sentient beings, they do not apprehend a self, nor do they apprehend a sentient being, up to and including a knower or a viewer. Furthermore, they do not apprehend form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, nor do they apprehend the various feelings produced with the six contacts as conditions. Likewise, they do not apprehend the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, and so on, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? It is because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not manifest with respect to all phenomena based on the apprehension of existence. Why is that?

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is entirely devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended, because the nature and characteristics of the grasper, the grasped, and their two bases are all empty and unapprehendable.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

By taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* throughout the long night; yet they do not even apprehend 'awakening' (*bodhi*) or a 'being' (*sattva*), much less a 'bodhisattva-mahāsattva'!"
Since one cannot apprehend a bodhisattva mahāsattva, how could one apprehend the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
If one cannot even apprehend the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, how much less can one apprehend the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas!
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas only need to cultivate the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or should they also cultivate the other five perfections?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying:
“All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, fully cultivate the six perfections.”
When practicing generosity, one does not apprehend the gift, the giver, or the recipient;
when practicing pure ethical discipline, one does not apprehend the discipline, the observer of the precepts, or the violator of the precepts;
when practicing patience, one does not apprehend patience, the patient person, or the angry person.

When practicing diligence, one does not apprehend diligence; in not apprehending diligence, one does not apprehend indolence; one does not apprehend the tasks to be performed through diligence, nor does one apprehend that which can perform them, whether by body or mind.
When practicing meditative concentration, one does not apprehend concentration; in not apprehending concentration, one does not apprehend distraction.

When practicing wisdom, one does not apprehend wisdom; in not apprehending wisdom, one does not apprehend those possessed of sublime intelligence, nor those possessed of faulty intelligence, nor the specific characteristics and distinctions of the phenomena observed by wisdom.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

For all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the profound perfection of wisdom serves as the illumination and the guide; they cultivate all the perfections without attachment, causing them to be swiftly fulfilled."
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

For all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by taking non-apprehension as their skillful means and with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as their illumination and guide, they contemplate all phenomena without attachment, thereby causing their cultivation to be swiftly brought to fulfillment. That is to say, by taking non-apprehension as their skillful means and with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as their illumination and guide, although they contemplate the aggregates (*skandha*), the sense bases (*āyatana*), and the elements (*dhātu*), and so forth at length up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they remain without attachment."
By this causal condition, that which is cultivated will swiftly reach fulfillment. Kausika!

Just as all the trees in Jambudvīpa—whether their branches, trunks, flowers, leaves, or fruits differ in various forms and colors—their shadows are entirely without distinction; they possess great merit and are the refuge for all beings. In the same way, although the first five perfections each have their differences, because they are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, dedicated toward the knowledge of all modes, and employ the method of non-apprehension, no distinct characteristics can be apprehended at all; they possess great merit and are the refuge for all beings.
Then Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“The profound *prajñāpāramitā* accomplishes vast and sublime merit; it accomplishes all sublime merits; it accomplishes perfect and sublime merits; it accomplishes immeasurable sublime merits; it accomplishes incalculable sublime merits; it accomplishes boundless sublime merits; it accomplishes peerless sublime merits; it accomplishes inexhaustible sublime merits.”

If good sons or good daughters write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, uphold it adorned with various jewels, read and recite it, make offerings to it, revere, respect, and praise it, and reflect upon it according to reason as taught in this sutra.
There may be sons of good family or daughters of good family who write down this profound perfection of wisdom, bestow it upon others, uphold it, and cause it to be widely disseminated.
"Of these two accumulations of merit, which is greater?
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas:
"I shall question you in return; answer as you see fit."

If a son or daughter of good family receives from another the relics of the Buddha and places them in a precious casket at a high and eminent location, further making offerings of various exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them;

and if there is another son or daughter of good family who receives from another the relics of the Buddha and distributes even as much as a mustard seed’s worth to others, causing them to receive it with reverence and install it according to the Dharma, further making offerings of immeasurable exquisite flower garlands up to lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them.
"What do you think?
Between these two accumulations of merit, which is superior?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
"As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, of these two accumulations of merit, the latter is superior. Why is that? "

Because there are those among the class of sentient beings who are to be liberated by making offerings and paying respect at the *śarīra* (relics) of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, when the Tathāgatas are about to enter parinirvāṇa, they employ the power of the *vajropama-samādhi* (diamond-like concentration) to crush their diamond-like bodies into pieces the size of mustard seeds. Furthermore, through the empowerment of their profound, vast, and great compassion, they bless these *buddha-śarīra* so that after the Tathāgata has passed into parinirvāṇa, anyone who obtains even a single grain the size of a mustard seed and makes offerings or pays it respect shall obtain boundless merit; they shall experience many superior joys among gods and humans, and ultimately reach the end of suffering. Therefore, giving [these relics] to others brings forth the most excellent merit.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śakra, King of Devas, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

Regarding the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, whether one personally upholds, makes offerings to, and honors it, or transfers it to others so that it may be widely disseminated— the latter of these two accumulations of merit is greater."
Why is this? Because by giving to others, one enables immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings to obtain benefit and happiness. "Furthermore, Kausika!

If there is one who, regarding the meaning and intent of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, correctly analyzes and explains it for others so that they attain right understanding, the mass of merit obtained by them is hundreds of thousands of times greater than the merit of bestowing [this teaching] upon others for their circulation.
One should revere this Dharma Master as one would revere a Buddha, and likewise serve him as one would serve a venerable fellow-practitioner of the holy life. Why is this?

Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is itself all Buddhas, and all Buddhas are themselves the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is not different from all Buddhas, and all Buddhas are not different from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas of the three periods of time, by diligently practicing and studying the *prajñāpāramitā*, have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

you, O Noble Practitioner of Brahma-conduct, should know that these are Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abiding on the stage of non-retrogression, and these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas likewise, by diligently practicing and studying the *prajñāpāramitā*, have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

A person of the śrāvaka lineage also trains with diligent application in the perfection of wisdom and attains the fruit of arhatship; a person of the pratyekabuddha lineage also trains with diligent application in the perfection of wisdom and attains the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;

and a person of the bodhisattva lineage also trains with diligent application in the perfection of wisdom, transcends the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enters the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, gradually practices all the bodhisattva deeds, and dwells in the stage of a bodhisattva who is irreversible.

For this reason, Kauśika, if any sons or daughters of good family wish to offer, revere, honor, respect, and praise the Buddhas of the present with immeasurable and exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps, they should write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā sūtra and offer, revere, honor, respect, and praise it with immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps.
“Kauśika! When I first attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, I contemplated this meaning and thought:
‘Upon whom shall I rely for my dwelling?’”
"Who is worthy to receive my offerings and respect?
While he was reflecting thus, he did not see anyone among the devas, Māras, Brahmās, humans, or non-humans who was his equal, much less his superior!
He further reflects:

"Relying upon this Dharma, I have realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; this Dharma is profound, tranquil, and subtle. I shall dwell in reliance upon this very Dharma, honoring and revering it—that is, the profound Prajñāpāramitā."

“Kauśika! Even though I have already attained Buddhahood, I still rely upon, make offerings to, and revere the Prajñāpāramitā; how much more so should sons and daughters of good family who seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment not rely upon this profound Prajñāpāramitā to practice with diligence, making offerings to, revering, honoring, and praising it!”
Why is this so? Kauśika!

It is because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* gives birth to the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; from these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas arise all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; and it is by depending upon those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas that Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas come into being.
For this reason, Kauśika, whether they belong to the bodhisattva vehicle,

the pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the śrāvaka vehicle, all sons and daughters of good family should diligently study and train in the perfection of wisdom, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it with immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps.

Why is this? Because those of the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, and Bodhisattva vehicles must rely upon the Prajñāpāramitā, practicing and studying with diligent effort, in order to reach the ultimate goal.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! Suppose a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa, causing them all to abide securely in the ten paths of wholesome action. What do you think?"
"By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family obtain much merit?
Śakra, Lord of Devas, replied: "Very much!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha told Kauśika:

“If good sons and good daughters were to transcribe this profound Prajñāpāramitā sūtra, bestow it upon others, recite it, or transcribe it again and cause it to be widely circulated, the mass of merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters would be far greater than the former.”
Why is this? Kausika!
Within the secret treasury of the profound Prajñāpāramitā, all untainted dharmas are extensively expounded; therein, sons and daughters of good family have studied, are studying, and shall study.

There are some who have entered, are entering, or will enter the state of correct determination and departure from birth within the lineage of the Śrāvakas, gradually proceeding until they have attained, are attaining, or will attain the fruit of Arhatship;

there are some who have entered, are entering, or will enter the state of correct determination and departure from birth within the lineage of the Pratyekabuddhas, gradually proceeding until they have attained, are attaining, or will attain the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha;

and there are some who have entered, are entering, or will enter the state of correct determination and departure from birth within the lineage of the Bodhisattvas, gradually practicing all the bodhisattva deeds, having attained, are attaining, or will attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! All the untainted dharmas taught within the secret treasury of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* refer to the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*, as well as internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*).”
...up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; whether it be suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
whether it be the realm of cessation up to the unconditioned realm; whether it be the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; or whether it be the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four [formless attainments]...
The concentrations of form, whether the eight liberations or the nine successive attainments; the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the Dharma-cloud;
and the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.

Whether it be the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant equanimity; whether it be all the doors of dhāraṇī or the doors of samādhi; whether it be omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects; or whatever other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas there may be—all these are the untainted (anāsrava) dharmas spoken of herein.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 503; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 504.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The Third Division, Chapter Eight on the Accumulation of Merit, Part Two: "Furthermore, Kauśika,

if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to instruct a single sentient being to abide in the fruit of stream-entry, the accumulation of merit obtained would still surpass that of instructing all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa and causing them to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action."

Why is this? Those who abide in the ten paths of wholesome action are not exempt from rebirth in the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of hungry ghosts; yet, if sentient beings abide in the fruit of a Stream-enterer, they attain eternal liberation from all perilous and evil destinies—how much more so for the mass of merit obtained by teaching others to abide in the fruits of a Once-returner, a Non-returner, or an Arhat! That [merit] would surely surpass the former!

Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa so that they all abide in the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, the mass of merit they would obtain would not equal that of someone who instructs a single sentient being and causes them to be established in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.
Why is this? Because the merits possessed by the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha exceed those of a stream-enterer and others by many hundreds of thousands of times, Kauśika!

If a son or daughter of good family were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa, causing them all to abide in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, the mass of merit obtained would not equal that of someone who instructs a single sentient being to aspire toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? If one instructs sentient beings to incline toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, then one ensures that the Buddha-eye in the world is not severed. Why is this so?

Kauśika! Because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there exist the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; and there are also Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas achieve their accomplishment by relying upon the Prajñāpāramitā.

For this reason, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family writes out this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā and gives it to others for reading and recitation, or transcribes it and causes it to be widely disseminated, the mass of merit they obtain will surpass the previous mass of merit, being immeasurable and boundless.

Why is this so? Within the secret treasury of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the mundane and supramundane wholesome dharmas are extensively taught. Based on these wholesome dharmas, there exist in the world great clans of *kṣatriyas* up to great clans of householders; there exist the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception; there also exist the perfection of giving up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); there also exist the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the enlightenment of pratyekabuddhas; the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; and there also exist the designations of stream-enterers up to those of all Buddhas.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, suppose a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach all the sentient beings of the four great continents and cause them all to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action. What do you think?"
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside the sentient beings of the four great continents."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings within a small thousandfold world-system and cause them all to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action, what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kausika! Setting aside all sentient beings in a small thousandfold world system."
If a son or daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings within a medium chiliocosm and cause them to abide securely in the ten paths of wholesome action, what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside all sentient beings in the intermediate thousandfold world system."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings throughout a great trichiliocosm and cause them all to abide securely in the ten paths of wholesome action, what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside all sentient beings within the great trichiliocosm."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach and transform all sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in each of the ten directions, causing them all to dwell securely in the path of the ten virtuous actions—what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kausika! Let alone the sentient beings in each of these worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach and transform all sentient beings throughout all worlds in the ten directions, causing them all to abide securely in the path of the ten wholesome courses of action—what do you think?
The rest is as explained above. "Furthermore, Kausika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvipa, causing them all to dwell securely in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers—what do you think?"
“Would these sons and daughters of good family, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of Devas, replied: “Very much!”
"O Bhagavān!
It is very much so! O Sugata!"
The Buddha told Kauśika:

"If good sons and good daughters transcribe this profound Prajñāpāramitā sūtra and bestow it upon others for reading and recitation, or if they transcribe it further and cause it to be widely circulated, the mass of merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters will be far greater than the former."
Why is this? Kauśika!

Within the secret treasury of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all untainted (*anāsrava*) dharmas are extensively expounded; therein, sons and daughters of good family have studied, are studying, and will study. Some have entered, are entering, or will enter the state of correct nature and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*) within the lineage of the śrāvakas, gradually proceeding until they have attained, are attaining, or will attain the fruit of arhatship.

There are some who have entered, are entering, or will enter the state of rightness and departure from birth within the lineage of the Pratyekabuddhas, gradually proceeding until they have attained, are attaining, or will attain the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha;

and there are some who have entered, are entering, or will enter the state of rightness and departure from birth within the lineage of the Bodhisattvas, gradually practicing all the bodhisattva deeds, having attained, are attaining, or will attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! All the untainted dharmas taught within the secret treasury of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*—namely, from the *dānapāramitā* as extensively explained up to the *sarvākārajñatā*, as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas—all these are the untainted dharmas taught therein.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son or daughter of good family were to teach a single sentient being to abide in the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpatti), the mass of merit obtained would still surpass that of teaching all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa and causing them to abide in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers."

Why is this? Those who dwell in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers are not exempt from rebirth in the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of hungry ghosts;

whereas if sentient beings abide in the fruit of stream-entry, they immediately attain permanent liberation from all perilous evil destinies—how much more so for those taught to abide in the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship! How could the mass of merit obtained thereby not surpass that [of the former]?

Kauśika! If a son or daughter of good family were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa so that they all abide in the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, the mass of merit obtained would not equal that of someone who instructs a single sentient being and causes them to be established in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.
Why is this so? Because all the merits of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha exceed those of a Stream-enterer by many hundreds of thousands of times, Kausika!

If a son or daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa and cause them to abide in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, the mass of merit they would thereby acquire would not equal that of someone who teaches a single sentient being to aspire toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? If one instructs sentient beings to incline toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then one ensures that the Buddha-eye in the world is not severed. Why is this so?

Kauśika! Because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there exist the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; furthermore, there are Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas achieve their perfection by relying upon the Prajñāpāramitā.
"For this reason, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family writes out this profound Prajñāpāramitā sūtra and gives it to others to read and recite, or copies it further so that it may be widely circulated, the mass of merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless, surpassing the previous mass of merit."

Why is this? Within the secret treasury of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the mundane and supramundane wholesome dharmas are extensively taught; based on these wholesome dharmas, there come to be great *kṣatriya* clans in the world, and so forth, up to the fact that even the various Buddhas can be established and attained.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, suppose a son or daughter of good family were to teach all the sentient beings of the four great continents, causing them all to dwell securely in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers. What do you think?"
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside the sentient beings of the four great continents."

If a son or daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings in a small thousandfold world-system, causing them all to dwell securely in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers—what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside all sentient beings in a small thousandfold world system."

If a son or daughter of good family were to cause all sentient beings within a medium chiliocosm to abide in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers—what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside all sentient beings in the intermediate thousandfold world system."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings throughout a great trichiliocosm, causing them all to dwell securely in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers—what do you think?
The rest is as explained above.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Setting aside all sentient beings within the great trichiliocosm."
