"World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the *pāramitā* of non-attachment."
"So it is, Subhūti! Because they have transcended the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
“World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the non-conceptual *pāramitā*. “It is so!”
"Subhūti! Because all conceptualization is unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!"
"This profound perfection of wisdom is a measureless perfection. "So it is, Subhūti!"
"Because the limits of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the *pāramitā* that is like space."
"So it is, Subhūti! Because there is no obstruction regarding any dharma."
“World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the *pāramitā* of impermanence, suffering, and non-self. “So it is!”
“Subhūti! It is because one does not grasp at any phenomena, as they are subject to destruction and are driven away.
“World-Honored One!”
"The profound perfection of wisdom is the perfection of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
"So it is, Subhūti!"
“One realizes that all phenomena are entirely non-existent, for they are devoid of all marks and are beyond being an object of aspiration.
“World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the *pāramitā* of emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*)."
"So it is, Subhūti! For one knows that the dharmas which are empty are unattainable."
“World-Honored One!
This profound perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the four applications of mindfulness, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

"So it is, Subhūti! One knows that body, sensation, mind, and phenomena are all unapprehendable; this is explained at length up to the point of transcending the dharmas of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
“World-Honored One!
This profound prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the Tathāgata. “It is so!”
“Subhūti! Because you are able to speak of all dharmas according to reality.
“World-Honored One!”
“The profound perfection of wisdom is the self-arisen perfection. “So it is, Subhūti!”
"Because it exercises sovereign mastery over all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the *pāramitā* of perfect enlightenment (*samyaksaṃbodhi*)."
"So it is, Subhūti! Because he has attained perfect awakening to all aspects of all phenomena."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 507; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 508.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirteen: Dhāraṇī, Part Three; Dhāraṇī Chapter, Thirteen, One.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had this thought to himself:

"If good sons and good daughters should hear even the name of such a profound Dharma-gate as the *Prajñāpāramitā*, it should be known that they have in the past already drawn near immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; they have made great vows and planted various roots of goodness, and have been sustained by many spiritual friends. How much more so if they can write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to principle, explain it to others, or even practice according to the teaching to the best of their ability!"

It should be known that such a person has already approached, served, made offerings to, and honored immeasurable Buddhas in the past; they have planted many roots of virtue, heard the *prajñāpāramitā*, and having heard it, have upheld, contemplated, recited, and explained it to others, practicing according to the teaching. Or, they are able to question and answer regarding this sutra; by the power of their prior merit, they now accomplish these matters.

If sons or daughters of good family have already made offerings to immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their merit is pure and refined, then upon hearing this profound Prajñāpāramitā, their minds will not be startled, terrified, or afraid; having heard it, they will believe and rejoice in it, practicing according to the teaching. It should be known that such persons, in the past, before immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Buddhas, made great vows and practiced the pāramitās from generosity up to wisdom; therefore, in this present life, they are able to accomplish these matters.
At that time, Śāriputra also addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If sons or daughters of good family, upon hearing this profound meaning and purpose of the Prajñāpāramitā, their minds are not startled, terrified, or afraid; and having heard it, they write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to principle, explain it to others, cause it to be widely disseminated, and practice according to the teaching—then one should know that such persons are like great Bodhisattvas who have attained the stage of non-retrogression."

Why is this? Because the meaning and purpose of this *prajñāpāramitā* are exceedingly profound and extremely difficult to believe and understand; if one has not practiced the six *pāramitās*, such as generosity, for a long time in previous lives, how could one possibly believe and understand it upon merely hearing it for a brief moment!

"Bhagavān! If sons or daughters of good family, upon hearing the profound meaning and intent of the Prajñāpāramitā, disparage and revile it, one should know that in previous lives these persons also once disparaged this profound Prajñāpāramitā."

Why is this? Because when such foolish people hear the profound meaning and purport of the Prajñāpāramitā, due to the power of their past habitual tendencies, they lack faith and joy, and their minds are not pure.
Why is this? Because such foolish persons, in past lives, have never drawn near to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, or other noble sages, nor have they ever inquired:
"How should one practice the six pāramitās, such as generosity?"
The detailed exposition continues up to: "How should one train in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
Therefore, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they disparage, revile, do not believe, and take no pleasure in it, for their minds are not pure.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, said to Śāriputra:

“The meaning and purport of this Prajñāpāramitā are so profound and extremely difficult to believe and understand that it is not at all surprising if those who have not long since begun to practice with faith and joy the six pāramitās, such as giving, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, upon hearing this profound meaning and purport of the Prajñāpāramitā, are unable to believe and understand it, or even give rise to slander.”
"Venerable One!
I now pay homage to the profound Prajñāpāramitā; if I pay homage to the profound Prajñāpāramitā, it is as if I were paying homage to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.
To pay homage to the Prajñāpāramitā is to pay homage to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Why is this?

Kauśika! This is because the omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas, as well as all other immeasurable and boundless merits, are accomplished in reliance upon the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to abide in the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes, they should abide in the perfection of wisdom;
if they wish to give rise to the omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects of all Buddhas, they should study the perfection of wisdom.

If one wishes to sever the continuity of the habitual tendencies of afflictions, realize unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings, one should study the Prajñāpāramitā.

Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family wish to attain the fruit of a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, they should study the perfection of wisdom.

Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to properly establish individuals of the śrāvaka lineage in the śrāvaka vehicle, individuals of the pratyekabuddha lineage in the pratyekabuddha vehicle, and individuals of the bodhisattva lineage in the unsurpassed vehicle, they should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to subdue all māras and crush the dark factions of the non-Buddhists, they should study the Prajñāpāramitā.
Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to gather and sustain the community of bhikṣus and bring them to excellent discipline, they should study the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), how do they abide in form?”
How does one dwell in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
How does one cultivate form?
How does one cultivate feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
The detailed exposition continues up to: "How does one abide in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
How does one cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!
It is because you now rely upon the Buddha’s spiritual power that you are able to question the Tathāgata regarding such a profound meaning.”
"You should listen attentively!
I shall explain it for you. Kausika!"
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, if they do not dwell upon nor cultivate form (*rūpa*), this is their dwelling upon and cultivation of form;

if they do not dwell upon nor cultivate feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*), this is their dwelling upon and cultivation of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness;

and so on in detail, up to: if they do not dwell upon nor cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), this is their dwelling upon and cultivation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Why is this? Kauśika!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not find anything in form (rūpa) that can be dwelled upon or practiced; they do not find anything in feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), or consciousness (vijñāna) that can be dwelled upon or practiced; and so it is explained at length until they do not find anything in the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) that can be dwelled upon or practiced.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, if they neither abide nor do not abide in form, and neither cultivate nor do not cultivate it, this is called abiding in and cultivating form.

If they neither abide nor do not abide in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, and neither cultivate nor do not cultivate them, this is called abiding in and cultivating feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."

To speak at length, up to and including: if one neither dwells nor does not dwell in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and neither practices nor does not practice them, this is called dwelling in and practicing the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Why is this? Kausika!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they observe that from form up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, the prior, posterior, and middle limits are unobtainable.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is most profound.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!

Because the suchness of form is profoundly deep, the perfection of wisdom is most profound; and so on, up to: because the suchness of the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha is profoundly deep, the perfection of wisdom is most profound.”
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is thus difficult to measure.
The Buddha said:

"It is so! Because the suchness of form is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure; and so on, up to: because the suchness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure."
“World-Honored One!
Thus, this prajñāpāramitā is most immeasurable.
The Buddha said:

"It is so! Because the suchness of form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is also immeasurable; and so on, up to: because the suchness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is also immeasurable."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, if they practice the profound nature of form (*rūpa*), they are not practicing *prajñāpāramitā*; and so on, up to: if they practice the profound nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), they are not practicing *prajñāpāramitā*."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the profound nature of form is not form itself, and so on, up to the profound nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not those eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they practice the immeasurability of form, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom; and so on, up to: if they practice the immeasurability of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the unmeasurable nature of form is not itself form, and so on, up to the unmeasurable nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not itself those eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they practice the immeasurability of form (rūpa), they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom; and so on, up to: if they practice the immeasurability of the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma), they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the immeasurable nature of form is not form itself, and so on, up to the immeasurable nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not those eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Since this Prajñāpāramitā is thus most profound, immeasurable, and difficult to fathom, it is difficult to believe and understand; it should not be spoken before those who have newly begun their training in the Mahāyāna bodhisattva path."
Why is this? Lest they, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, become startled, terrified, or doubtful, or perhaps give rise to slander and fail to attain faith and understanding.
It should be taught only before those bodhisattvas who abide in the stage of non-retrogression. Why is this?

Because when they hear such profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their minds are not startled, terrified, or filled with doubt; they do not give rise to slander, but instead possess deep-seated faith and understanding.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Śāriputra:
"What fault is there in speaking of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* before a bodhisattva who has newly set out in the Mahāyāna?"

Śāriputra said: "If one were to speak of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* before a newly initiated bodhisattva mahāsattva, that person would hear it with alarm, terror, and doubt; they would be unable to believe or understand it, or might even give rise to slander. By this, they would create and increase karma that leads to rebirth in the evil destinies, sinking into the three miserable realms to undergo great suffering for a long time, making it difficult to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Therefore, one should not speak of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in their presence."
Then Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again asked the Venerable Śāriputra:

"Is it possible that there might be a bodhisattva who, though not yet having received the prophecy of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, does not become startled, terrified, or doubtful, and does not give rise to slander, but instead possesses deep faith and understanding?"
Śāriputra said: “There is, Kauśika!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva shall before long receive the prediction of great enlightenment. Kausika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom, is not startled, terrified, or filled with doubt, and does not give rise to slander but instead develops deep faith and understanding, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already received the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
"If they have not yet received it, they will do so after no more than one or two Buddhas; they shall certainly receive the prediction of great enlightenment.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra: "It is so!"
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Śāriputra."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long studied the Great Vehicle, long generated the great vows, long practiced the six perfections and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, made offerings to many Buddhas, served many spiritual friends, and upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their mind is not startled, terrified, or doubtful; but rather, with deep resolve, they believe, understand, uphold, recite, contemplate according to the principle, and explain it to others, or further transcribe it and practice in accordance with what is taught.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to offer a brief analogy; I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion, will grant me leave to speak.”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra, “Speak as you wish. Śāriputra replied:

"Just as those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle may, even in their dreams, practice the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, up until they sit upon the sublime seat of awakening—one should know that such persons are already close to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; how much more so for a bodhisattva who, while awake, practices the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity in order to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and yet does not swiftly realize that sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!"
"Blessed One!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long sit upon the sublime seat of awakening, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and contemplate it according to the principle, one should know that these persons have long studied the Mahāyāna, their roots of goodness are matured, they have made many offerings to the Buddhas, served many virtuous friends, and planted many roots of merit; thus they are able to accomplish such a feat.”
“World-Honored One!

If good sons or good daughters hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and believe in it, understand it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, explain it to others, and contemplate it according to the principle, you should know that such persons have either already received the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*), or are close to receiving the prediction of great enlightenment.”
“World-Honored One!

These sons and daughters of good family will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, just like bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in the stage of non-retrogression. By virtue of this, they shall hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and will be able to believe and understand it with deep faith, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to principle, practice in accordance with the teaching, and expound it for others.”
“World-Honored One!

It is as if there were a person traveling through a vast wilderness who, after traversing a perilous path of one hundred yojanas, or two, three, four, or five hundred, sees the preliminary signs of a city or royal capital—namely, herdsmen, groves, fields, and the like.”
Having seen these various signs, he thought to himself:
"The cities and royal capitals are not far from here.
Once he had this thought, his body and mind became composed and at ease; he felt no fear of wild beasts, bandits, hunger, or thirst.

"Bhagavān! It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, uphold it, recite it, contemplate it according to reality, and give rise to deep faith and understanding, you should know that before long they will receive a prediction of enlightenment or have already received it; they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will have no fear of falling into the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

Why is this? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already seen, heard, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, which is the precursor sign of unsurpassed enlightenment.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.
Relying on the Buddha's power, you should speak further.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is like a person who wishes to behold the great ocean; traveling toward it gradually over a long period of time, they do not see mountains or forests and thus think:
'Judging by these signs, the great ocean is not far away.'"
Why is this? Because the ground near a great ocean must gradually slope downward and be devoid of mountains and forests.
At that time, although that person has not yet seen the sea, seeing these proximate signs, he leaps for joy:
"I shall surely and swiftly behold the great ocean; how joyful it would be to fulfill my original vow!

World-Honored One, it is the same for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate according to principle, and give rise to deep faith and understanding, then although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet received a face-to-face prophecy from a Buddha:
"You shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment after such a number of kalpas in a future world.
Thus, one should know for oneself that the bestowal of the prediction is not far off. Why is this so?

This is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already obtained the vision and hearing of, paid reverence and made offerings to, upheld, recited, and reflected upon according to reason upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, which is the precursor sign of unsurpassed enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!
It is like the flowering and fruiting trees in the springtime; their old leaves have already fallen and their branches are lush and moist. When people see them, they all think:
‘It will not be long before new flowers, fruits, and leaves emerge.’”
"Why is this? Because these signs have first appeared upon these trees—their new flowers, fruits, and leaves.
Having beheld these signs, the men and women, the great and small, of Jambudvīpa were filled with joy and leaped for gladness, all thinking thus:
“World-Honored One! Just as we shall before long behold these flowers and fruits flourishing in abundance, so it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:

if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to principle, and give rise to deep faith and understanding, you should know that their roots of goodness from past lives have matured, that they have made many offerings to the Buddhas, and have served many virtuous friends; they shall before long receive the prophecy of great enlightenment.”
“World-Honored One!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva should form this thought:

‘I must certainly have possessed the power of superior roots of goodness in the past, which was able to draw forth unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; therefore, I now see, hear, make offerings to, and pay respect to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and I receive, uphold, read, recite, give rise to deep faith and understanding, contemplate according to the principle, and practice it to the best of my ability.’”
"World-Honored One!
Now, within this assembly, there are sons of the gods who have seen past Buddhas preach this Dharma; they leap for joy and all deliberate together, saying:

'In the past, when bodhisattvas heard the preaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, they immediately received their prediction [of enlightenment]. Now that these bodhisattvas have heard the Prajñāpāramitā, it is certain that before long they shall receive the prediction of Bodhi.'"

“World-Honored One! It is like a woman who has been pregnant for some time; her body grows increasingly heavy and she becomes restless in her movements. Her food, drink, and sleep all diminish; she takes no pleasure in much speech and grows weary of her usual activities. Because she suffers pain, all her affairs suddenly come to a halt.”
Just as a woman who has borne many children, upon seeing these signs, immediately knows that this girl will give birth before long;

so too, World-Honored One, it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Having planted roots of goodness in past lives, having made many offerings to the Buddhas, and having long served virtuous friends, because their roots of goodness have matured, they now hear the *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to the principle, give rise to deep faith and understanding, and practice and study it according to their capacity.
“World-Honored One!
By virtue of these causes and conditions, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long receive the prediction of unsurpassed, great bodhi.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śāriputra, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!
You have skillfully expounded this parable of the bodhisattva; you should know that it is entirely through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power that he has inspired such eloquence in you.”
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is most skillful in entrusting the bodhisattva mahāsattvas and most skillful in embracing the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.”
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.

Why is this? Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment for the sake of securing the benefit and happiness of many sentient beings, and out of compassion to bring welfare to gods and humans.

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas diligently train in the bodhisattva path, they embrace and sustain immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings for their benefit by means of the four articles of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*):
first, generosity (*dāna*).
Second, kind speech;
third, beneficial conduct;
fourth, cooperation.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally abides correctly in the ten paths of wholesome action and also establishes others, causing them to diligently train in the ten paths of wholesome action;

they personally practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, and also exhort others to practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they personally practice from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, and also exhort others to practice from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom.

By relying on skillful means through the perfection of wisdom, this bodhisattva mahāsattva, although he teaches sentient beings to realize the fruit of stream-entry up to and including the attainment of pratyekabuddha enlightenment, does not himself realize them.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally exerts diligence to cultivate the bodhisattva practices and also encourages others to cultivate all bodhisattva practices;
personally abiding in the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva, they also encourage others to abide in the stage of non-retrogression;

personally exerting diligence to adorn and purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity, they likewise encourage others to adorn and purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity.
They personally and diligently give rise to the supernatural powers of a bodhisattva, and also exhort others to give rise to them;
they personally and diligently adorn and purify the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi, and likewise exhort others to diligently adorn and purify the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi;
they themselves are able to realize perfect eloquence, and also cause others to attain perfect eloquence.

They themselves are able to acquire a perfect physical body endowed with all the marks and signs of excellence, and they also encourage others to acquire a perfect physical body endowed with all the marks and signs of excellence;

they themselves are able to acquire the perfection of the conduct of a youthful celibate (*kumārabhūta*), and they also encourage others to acquire the perfection of the conduct of a youthful celibate;

they themselves practice the four foundations of mindfulness, and so on, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), and they also encourage others to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, and so on, up to and including all-aspect omniscience.
They themselves sever the continuity of the habitual tendencies of afflictions, and they likewise exhort others to sever the continuity of all afflictive habitual tendencies;

they themselves realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings, and they likewise exhort others to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is marvelous,
World-Honored One!”
"How marvelous!
Well-gone One!

These bodhisattva mahāsattvas have accomplished such a mass of great merit; for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, they practice the profound perfection of wisdom, seeking to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, desiring to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings throughout the entirety of the future."
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the profound perfection of wisdom swiftly attain fulfillment?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, does not perceive form as increasing or decreasing, does not perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as increasing or decreasing—and so on, in detail, up to not perceiving all-knowledge as increasing or decreasing, nor perceiving the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as increasing or decreasing—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain fulfillment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive this as a dharma or as a non-dharma; they do not perceive this as past, future, or present; they do not perceive this as wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate; they do not perceive this as conditioned or unconditioned; they do not perceive this as the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm; they do not perceive this as the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; and, to speak at length, they do not perceive anything from all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). It is by practicing the profound perfection of wisdom in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva swiftly attains full completion."

Why is this? Because all phenomena (*dharma*) lack intrinsic nature and characteristics; because they lack functional activity; because they cannot be transmuted; because they are false, deceptive, unstable by nature, and lack autonomy; because they lack sensation and perception; and because they are devoid of a self, up to and including a viewer.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“That which the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"So it is! So it is! What the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable."
"Subhūti, you should know this:

because form is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

To speak extensively, up to: because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, knows form as it truly is to be inconceivable yet does not give rise to the thought that it is inconceivable—and so on, in detail, until—knows all-aspect omniscience as it truly is to be inconceivable yet does not give rise to the thought that it is inconceivable, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its full completion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to notions of what is conceivable or inconceivable regarding form, up to and including all-aspect omniscience. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its full completion."
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“The meaning and intent of this Prajñāpāramitā are so profound; who is able to believe and understand it?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long cultivated the six perfections, long planted roots of goodness, made many offerings to the Buddhas, and served many virtuous friends, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will be able to give rise to faith and understanding in this profound prajñāpāramitā."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"To what extent should it be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long cultivated the six perfections, long planted roots of goodness, made offerings to many Buddhas, and attended upon many spiritual friends?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding form; they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

They do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of form; they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."

One does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the nature of form; one does not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

To speak at length, up to: they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding all-knowledge; they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

They do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of all-knowledge; they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

They do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the nature of all-knowledge; they do not give rise to conceptualization or discursive differentiation regarding the nature of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is that? Because form, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects, are all inconceivable. Subhūti!

Based on this, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long cultivated the six perfections, long planted roots of virtue, made extensive offerings to the Buddhas, and served many spiritual friends.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"This Prajñāpāramitā is most profound.
The Buddha said:
"It is so! Because form is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound;

and so on, in detail, until: because all-knowledge is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“In this way, the perfection of wisdom is a great treasury of jewels.
The Buddha said:
"It is so! Because it can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of merit.

This great treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā* can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the ten paths of wholesome action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers; it can bestow upon sentient beings the six *pāramitās*, such as generosity, and so forth, up to the jewel of all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*); it can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; and it can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the turning of the wheel of Dharma. For this reason, the *prajñāpāramitā* is called a great treasury of jewels."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“This profound prajñāpāramitā is a mass of purity.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all these dharmas are a collection of purity.
Subhūti, you should know this!"

Because form is pure, this profound perfection of wisdom is a collection of purity; and so on, as extensively explained, up to: because the knowledge of all aspects is pure, this profound perfection of wisdom is a collection of purity.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is marvelous,
World-Honored One!”
"How marvelous!
Well-gone One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is so exceedingly profound that it encounters many obstacles; yet now, as it is being extensively taught, no obstacles arise."
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is beset by many obstacles; however, through the spiritual power (*ṛddhibala*) of the Buddha, although it is now being extensively expounded, no obstacles shall arise.

Therefore, sons and daughters of good family who belong to the Mahāyāna and who wish to write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, or explain to others this profound *sūtra* of the *prajñāpāramitā*, should quickly write it down and so forth, up to its explanation.

Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles; one must ensure that no difficulties arise—ranging from the act of writing it down to its exposition—that would prevent its ultimate completion.

“Subhūti, you should know that if these sons and daughters of good family wish to complete the transcription of this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within one month, or two, or three, up to one year, they should apply themselves with diligent effort and focused mindfulness to the transcription,

so as to bring it to completion within that time. If they wish to complete the upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and explaining to others of this profound *sūtra* of the *prajñāpāramitā* within one month, or two, or three, up to one year, they should apply themselves with diligent effort and focused mindfulness to the upholding and so forth, up to the explaining, so as to bring it to completion within that time.”
"Why is this? Because the great jewel of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How rare! World-Honored One!
How marvelous!"

"Sugata! This great jewel of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is beset by many obstacles; yet, for those who write it down, uphold it, read it, recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it to others, Māra will not create obstacles to prevent them from writing it down, up to and including explaining it."
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"Although Māra, the evil one, may wish to create obstacles so that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is not written down, nor even expounded, he lacks the power to create such obstacles as to prevent that bodhisattva from accomplishing what he has set out to do."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"By whose spiritual power is it that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct these bodhisattvas in their activities such as copying [the sūtras]?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“It is by the supernatural power of that Buddha that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct those bodhisattvas in their activities such as copying [the scriptures].
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”

Furthermore, it is through the spiritual power of all Buddhas in the worlds of the ten directions that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct or hinder the Bodhisattvas in their activities such as transcribing [the scriptures].
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas collectively protect and keep in mind those bodhisattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they ensure that Māra cannot obstruct or hinder those sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, preventing him from stopping them from copying, or even explaining, this profound perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Śāriputra, all the Buddhas,

the World-Honored Ones, together protect and keep in mind the wholesome deeds performed by those bodhisattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom, so that those evil Māras cannot create obstacles for them.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If bodhisattvas are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, it is the natural law that they shall be protected and remembered by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma throughout the worlds of the ten directions."
If one is protected and remembered by the Buddhas, it is the natural law that evil Māras will be unable to create obstacles.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,

if there are sons of good family with pure faith who are able to write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, they should form this thought:

"This current transcription and even the exposition of the profound Prajñāpāramitā are all due to the protective mindfulness and spiritual power of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently teaching the Dharma in all worlds throughout the ten directions."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“If sons or daughters of good family are able to copy, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, all of this is due to the compassionate protection and mindfulness of the Buddhas of the ten directions. It causes those superior roots of goodness performed by them to be unable to be obstructed by any hosts of evil Māras.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

If sons or daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that all such instances are due to the protective mindfulness and spiritual power of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If sons and daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, all the Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who are currently preaching the Dharma will collectively recognize them; by virtue of this cause and condition, they will joyfully protect and mindfully sustain them."

If sons or daughters of good family are able to transcribe, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, they will constantly be perceived by the Buddha-eye of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones currently preaching the Dharma in all worlds of the ten directions. By virtue of this cause and condition, those Buddhas will protect and mindfully regard them with compassion, such that every virtuous deed they perform will be accomplished without exception.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.

If good sons and good daughters write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and expound this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will always be seen, known, and mindfully protected by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently teaching the Dharma throughout all worlds in the ten directions; these Buddhas will behold them with their Buddha-eye. Thus, no evil Māras shall be able to harass them, and all the wholesome deeds they perform shall be swiftly accomplished.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that they have already drawn near to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and no evil Māras or adversaries will be able to obstruct them.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If sons and daughters of good family who are established in the Great Vehicle can write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and having done so, uphold, read, and recite it with various adornments, you should know that they have given rise to deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they are able to offer various sublime flower garlands, up to lamps and lights, to honor and revere this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, these sons and daughters of good family will always be seen, known, and protected by the Tathāgata’s Buddha-eye. By virtue of these causes and conditions, they will certainly obtain great wealth, great benefit, great fruit, and great retribution."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle can write down, uphold, read, recite, and reverently make offerings to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of these roots of goodness they will even attain the stage of non-retrogression; they shall never be separated from the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, constantly hear the True Dharma, avoid falling into the evil destinies, and be born among gods and humans in peace, security, and happiness."

These sons and daughters of good family, by virtue of these roots of goodness, shall never be separated from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—extending broadly even to all-aspect omniscience and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas—until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; through this, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi.

For this reason, sons and daughters of good family who wish to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should diligently copy, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, explain to others, and reverently make offerings of this profound sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, never abandoning it for even a moment.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, in which direction will this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā flourish?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā shall, after my parinirvāṇa, gradually flourish in the southeastern direction."

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who are firmly established in the Mahāyāna, and who, with deep resolve, have faith in and delight in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; they copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and expound it; furthermore, they honor and revere this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, they do not fall into the miserable realms; instead, they are born in the heavens or among humans, where they enjoy wealth, honor, and happiness.

Through this power, they augment the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) and cause them to be swiftly perfected. Consequently, they are able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Thereafter, according to their respective capacities, they rely upon the teachings of the Three Vehicles, practicing gradually until they attain liberation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall spread from the southeast to the south and gradually flourish there."

In that direction there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who are firmly established in the Mahāyāna; they are able, with deep resolve, to have faith in and delight in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and they copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it to others. Furthermore, they honor and revere this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by making offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, they do not fall into the evil realms, but are instead born in the heavens or among humans where they enjoy wealth and honor.

Through this power, they augment the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) so that they may be swiftly perfected; by means of this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Thereafter, according to their respective capacities, they rely upon the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, practicing gradually until they attain liberation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall further flourish, spreading from the south toward the southwest."

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who are firmly established in the Mahāyāna; they are able to believe in and delight in this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a deep heart, and they copy, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain it. Furthermore, they honor and revere this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by making offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and illuminations.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, they do not fall into the evil realms, but are instead born in the heavens or among humans, where they enjoy wealth, honor, and happiness.

Through this power, they augment the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) so that they may be swiftly perfected; by means of this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Thereafter, according to their respective capacities, they rely upon the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, practicing gradually until they attain liberation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā will, after my parinirvāṇa, gradually flourish and spread from the southwest to the northwest."

In that direction there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who are firmly established in the Mahāyāna; they are able, with deep resolve, to have faith in and delight in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and they copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate and contemplate it, and expound it. Furthermore, they honor and revere this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and lights.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, one does not fall into the evil realms, but is instead born among the gods or among humans to enjoy wealth and honor.

Through this power, one increases the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) so that they may be swiftly perfected; by means of this, one is further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to what is appropriate, gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles to attain liberation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall spread from the northwest to the north and gradually flourish there."

In that direction, there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who are firmly established in the Mahāyāna, who are able to believe in and delight in this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a deep heart, and who copy, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound it; furthermore, they honor and revere this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and illuminations.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, one does not fall into the evil realms, but is instead born in the heavens or among humans to enjoy wealth, nobility, and happiness.

Through this power, one increases the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) so that they may be swiftly perfected; by means of this, one is further able to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to what is appropriate, gradually practice the three vehicles (*triyāna*) to attain liberation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
This profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish and spread from the north to the northeast."

In that direction there are many bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who are firmly established in the Mahāyāna; they are able, with deep resolve, to have faith in and delight in this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and they write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate and contemplate it, and explain it to others. Furthermore, they honor and revere this profound Prajñāpāramitā by making offerings of various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and illumination.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, one does not fall into the evil realms, but is instead born among the gods or among humans to enjoy wealth and honor.

Through this power, one increases the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) so that they may be swiftly fulfilled; by means of this, one is further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to what is appropriate, gradually cultivate the teachings of the Three Vehicles to attain liberation.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years, this profound Prajñāpāramitā will perform great buddha-work in the northeastern region."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the Dharma revered by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is precisely this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra, this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā is protected and sustained by all Tathāgatas, Arhats,
and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

The unsurpassed True Dharma of the Vinaya, which is not a dharma obtained by the Buddhas, does not possess the characteristic of extinction or disappearance; rather, the unsurpassed True Dharma of the Vinaya obtained by all Buddhas is precisely this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.

Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna in the northeastern quarter, and who are able to have deep faith and joy in this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and who copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate and practice it, contemplate it, and expound it—for them I shall constantly protect and keep them in mind, ensuring they suffer no harm or affliction.

“Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna in the northeastern direction, and who are able to transcribe such profound sūtras as this Prajñāpāramitā, and further honor and revere them with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, up to and including lamps and illumination—I declare with certainty that by virtue of these roots of goodness, they shall not fall into the evil destinies, but will be born among gods and humans, constantly experiencing wealth and happiness.”

By the power of this, the six perfections are further increased and swiftly brought to fulfillment; because of this, one is further able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to what is appropriate, train progressively in the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to attain parinirvāṇa.

Why is this? Śāriputra, with my Buddha-eye, I behold, realize, extol, and praise the mass of merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family; likewise, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below, also behold, realize, extol, and praise the mass of merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family with their Buddha-eyes.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, during the later time, the later period, and the final five hundred years, will this profound Prajñāpāramitā be widely disseminated in the northeastern region?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra: “So it is! So it is!”
This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years, shall be propagated in the northeastern region.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

After my parinirvāṇa, in the future time, the final period, during the last five hundred years, those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna in the northeastern direction—if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep resolve, believe in and delight in it, copying it, upholding it, reading and reciting it, practicing it, contemplating it, and explaining it—then you should know that such individuals have long since generated the mind set on unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they have long cultivated the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they have made many offerings to the Buddhas; they have served many virtuous friends; they have long and extensively practiced physical discipline, mental concentration, and wisdom; and the roots of goodness they have planted have all reached maturity.

By the power of this merit, they shall hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep faith and joy, be able to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and reveal it for the sake of sentient beings.

At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

After the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, how many sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna will there be in the northeastern direction who, upon hearing this Prajñāpāramitā, will gain deep-seated faith and joy, and further be able to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it to others?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, although there may be immeasurable sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna in the northeastern region, few will hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with deep-seated faith and joy, and few will further be able to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it to others.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

When those sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna hear this profound Prajñāpāramitā, their minds are not startled, terrified, or frightened; they develop deep faith and joy, and they transcribe, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and expound it—this is truly most rare!"
Why is this? Śāriputra,

those sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna have already approached, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised immeasurable Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas, and have inquired about the profound meaning and intent of the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Those sons of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle will, before long, certainly fulfill the perfections from generosity up to wisdom; and before long, they will certainly fulfill all-aspect omniscience as well as the other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Because those sons of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle are protected by the mindfulness of all Tathāgatas, are sustained by immeasurable spiritual friends, and are upheld by superior roots of goodness, they seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment for the sake of benefiting many sentient beings."
Why is this? Śāriputra!

I constantly teach the Dharma associated with omniscience to those sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna; likewise, the Tathāgatas of the past also constantly taught them the Dharma associated with omniscience.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, those sons and daughters of good family will, in future lives, be able to again seek and proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and they will also be able to teach the Dharma to others as appropriate, causing them to proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Those sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna possess such stability of body and mind that even Māra, the Evil King, and his retinue cannot destroy their aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; how much less could others who delight in evil deeds and revile the *prajñāpāramitā* obstruct their minds or cause them to cease striving for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi!"

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when sons of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle hear me teach this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their minds attain the vast and sublime joy of the Dharma; they are also able to establish immeasurable sentient beings in the supreme wholesome dharmas, leading them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Sons of good family and others who are established in the Mahāyāna have now made this great vow before me:

'I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), to practice the various deeds of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and by manifesting, exhorting, encouraging, inspiring, and rejoicing with them, cause them to attain, at the very least, the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.'"
I deeply rejoice in that aspiration. Why is this? Śāriputra!

I observe that the great vows and the harmony between the mind and speech of such sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna will certainly enable them, in the future, to establish countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and to manifest, exhort, encourage, and gladden them, leading them to unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi and even to receive the prediction of non-retrogression.
These sons and daughters of good family also, in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, made this great vow:

"I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, lead them to unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression."
"The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past also deeply rejoiced in that vow.
Why is this? Śāriputra!"

The Buddhas of the past likewise observed that the great vows and the words of mind corresponding to them, made by such sons of good family who dwell in the Mahāyāna, will certainly enable them to establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings in the future, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and—by means of demonstration, exhortation, encouragement, and inspiration—to lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra! These sons of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle possess vast faith and understanding; they are able to practice vast giving based upon excellent forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles. Having practiced this giving, they are further able to plant vast roots of goodness. By means of these roots of goodness, they are able to acquire vast karmic results. Having acquired such vast results, they do so solely for the benefit of all sentient beings. Toward all sentient beings, they are able to relinquish everything internal and external that they possess. They dedicate these planted roots of goodness, vowing to be born in the Buddha-fields of other directions where Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently reside, in order to proclaim this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound Prajñāpāramitā."

Having heard this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is further able to establish countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings within that buddha-field, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). He demonstrates, exhorts, encourages, inspires, and rejoices with them as they cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, leading them to attain non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “How marvelous,
World-Honored One!”
"How marvelous!
Well-gone One!
There is no phenomenon among all those of the past, future, and present that the Buddha does not realize and know; regarding all..."

He realizes and knows the true suchness of phenomena (*dharmatathatā*) and the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), extensively explained up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), without exception;

he realizes and knows the distinctions in the meanings and purports of all teachings on phenomena without exception; he realizes and knows the distinctions in the mental activities of all sentient beings without exception;
and regarding the past Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and their buddha-fields, [he realizes and knows them] without exception.
There is nothing he does not realize and know regarding the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Buddha-fields of the future;
there is nothing he does not realize and know regarding the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Buddha-fields of the present;
and [there is nothing he does not realize and know] regarding all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas and the teachings they proclaim throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
“Bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, buddha-fields, and all such matters—there is nothing they do not realize and know.
World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to seek the six perfections with courageous diligence, never ceasing for a moment, will there be times when they attain these six perfections and times when they do not?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly apply themselves with courageous diligence toward the six perfections, seeking them with unceasing joy; at all times, there is nothing they do not attain.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly and tirelessly seek the six perfections with courageous diligence, and all buddhas and bodhisattvas always protect and keep them in mind.
Śāriputra said: “World-Honored One!
If those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not obtain sūtras associated with the six pāramitās, how can it be said that they have attained these six pāramitās?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva always seeks these six pāramitās with courageous faith, disregarding even body and life, it is impossible that they should at any time fail to obtain a sutra corresponding to them.”
Why is this? Śāriputra!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, seeking unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, manifest themselves to exhort, encourage, inspire, and gladden all sentient beings, causing them to receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and practice these sūtras associated with the six pāramitās. By virtue of these roots of goodness, in whatever place they are born, they always obtain these sūtras associated with the six pāramitās; they receive, uphold, read, and recite them, practicing with courageous diligence according to the teachings, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields, never for a moment ceasing until they have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Chapter 14: On the Works of Māra, Part Three. Chapter Fourteen: On the Works of Māra. At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

"The Buddha has already praised and described the merits of a bodhisattva who, with courageous and correct diligence, practices the perfections from generosity up to wisdom in order to realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, and who brings sentient beings to maturity and purifies buddha-fields. How should one recognize the obstructive works of Māra when those bodhisattvas set out for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and cultivate various practices?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in expounding the essential teachings of the Dharma, yet eloquence only arises after a long time, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva."
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason is it considered a work of Māra when a bodhisattva delights in preaching the essentials of the Dharma, yet eloquence arises only after a long time?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, because it is difficult for them to bring to fulfillment the perfections from wisdom down to generosity through these causes and conditions, those are said to be the works of Māra for that bodhisattva.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in expounding the essential points of the Dharma, but eloquence only arises at the very last moment, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva."
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason is it that when a bodhisattva delights in preaching the essentials of the Dharma, eloquence suddenly arises, yet this is declared to be the work of Māra?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, if they take pleasure in preaching the essential points of the Dharma and sudden eloquence arises such that they neglect their practice, this is the work of Māra."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When copying the profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if one yawns frequently, engages in idle laughter without cause, treats one another with contempt, experiences agitation of body and mind, misorders the words and phrases, becomes confused regarding the principles, fails to find its flavor, or if sudden calamities arise such that the copying is not completed—know that these are the deeds of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When one receives, upholds, reads, recites, contemplates, practices, explains, or listens to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if there occur frequent yawning and stretching; idle laughter without cause; mutual disparagement; agitation of body and mind; inversion of words and phrases; confusion regarding the meaning and principles; failure to find its flavor; or the sudden arising of untoward events such that what is undertaken is not accomplished—know that these are the deeds of Māra for a bodhisattva."
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"By what causes and conditions do sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing the teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, suddenly think:
'I find no flavor in this sutra; what is the use of listening to this sutra with such diligent effort?'"
Having formed this thought, he immediately departed; the same was true for his upholding, reciting, contemplating, practicing, copying, and explaining [the teaching].
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"These sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle have not practiced the six perfections, such as generosity, for long in past lives; therefore, they do not find flavor in this sūtra, their hearts do not delight in it, and they immediately abandon it."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, should think:
'We shall not receive a prophecy regarding this; what is the use of listening? "
"With a mind that is not pure, he rises from his seat and departs with a sense of weary detachment, having no lingering attachment; you should know that this is an act of Māra for a bodhisattva.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
“For what reason, within this profound sūtra, is he not granted a prediction [of enlightenment], such that those of his kind depart with weary detachment and no lingering attachment?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"A bodhisattva who has not yet entered the state of right determination (samyaktva-niyāma) should not be granted the prediction of great enlightenment (mahābodhi-vyākaraṇa). If such a prediction were granted, it would increase their arrogance and negligence; because it would cause harm rather than benefit, no prediction is given."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, should think:
'Our names are not mentioned herein; what is the use of listening to this? "
“With a mind that is not pure, he rises from his seat and departs in weary rejection, without any sense of lingering attachment; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
“For what reason is the name of that bodhisattva not recorded and proclaimed within this profound sūtra?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“It is the nature of things that a bodhisattva who has not yet received the prediction of great enlightenment should not have their name proclaimed. Furthermore, Subhūti!”
When sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear the teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, if they should think:
"In this [teaching], our birthplaces—cities, towns, and villages—are not mentioned; what is the use of listening to it?"
"With a mind that is not pure, he rises from his seat and departs in weary disdain, without any sense of regret or attachment; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason is it that, within this profound sūtra, the birthplace, city, town, or village of that bodhisattva is not recorded or declared?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"If the name of that bodhisattva has not yet been predicted, one should not speak of the distinctions regarding their place of birth. Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra being preached, depart with impure minds, then according to the extent of their steps taken while abandoning this sūtra with such an impure mind of aversion, they shall lose that many eons of merit and incur for that many eons the transgression of obstructing enlightenment. Only after having experienced those transgressions for that same duration of time, and subsequently exerting diligent vigor to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and practicing the difficult and painful austerities of the bodhisattvas, can they restore their original state.
Therefore, if a bodhisattva wishes to swiftly realize unsurpassed enlightenment, they should not weary of or abandon the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle abandon the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* and seek to study other sūtras instead, you should know that this is a work of Māra for bodhisattvas.

Why is this? Because these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, having abandoned the profound *prajñāpāramitā*—the very root of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)—instead grasp at the branches and leaves of other scriptures; they will ultimately be unable to attain the Buddha-bodhi.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What other sūtras are like branches and leaves, unable to bring forth the knowledge of all modes?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If one speaks of the teachings associated with the two vehicles, this refers to the four foundations of mindfulness, and so on, up to the eight branches of the noble path, the three doors of liberation, the knowledge of the four truths, and so forth."
