All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive cause all the sūtras, up to and including the treatises, that they uphold, contemplate, and recite to be thoroughly mastered and perfected. Through such dharmas, they always joyfully practice giving to all sentient beings, constantly reflecting:
"How may I cause all classes of sentient beings who seek the correct aspiration to have it fully satisfied?"

Furthermore, taking these roots of goodness from such dharma-giving, he shares them equally with all sentient beings; employing the method of non-apprehension, he dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"
"All non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattvas will never give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding the profound Dharma-gates spoken by the Buddha.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason do non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattvas never give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding the profound Dharma-gates spoken by the Buddha?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained non-retrogression do not perceive any dharma whatsoever that could give rise to doubt or hesitation."
That is to say: one does not perceive the aggregate of form, nor even the aggregate of consciousness; one does not perceive the sense-base of the eye, nor even the sense-base of the mind;
one does not perceive the sense-base of form, nor even the sense-base of mental phenomena; one does not perceive the element of the eye, nor even the element of the mind;
one does not perceive the element of form, nor even the element of mental phenomena; and one does not perceive the eye.
One does not perceive the element of consciousness up to the element of mental consciousness; nor does one perceive eye-contact up to mind-contact;
nor does one perceive the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition;
nor does one perceive the earth element up to the consciousness element; nor does one perceive causal conditions...
Up to the dominant condition (*adhipatipratyaya*), one does not perceive ignorance (*avidyā*) up to old age and death (*jarāmaraṇa*);
nor does one perceive the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

nor does one perceive inner emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*); nor does one perceive suchness (*tathatā*) up to the inconceivable (*acintya*).
Within the realms, one does not perceive the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, or the path;
nor does one perceive the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments; nor does one perceive the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path;
nor does one perceive the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
Furthermore, one does not perceive the eight liberations up to the ten spheres of totality;
nor does one perceive the stage of pure observation up to the stage of a Tathāgata; nor does one perceive the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the Dharma-cloud;
nor does one perceive the doors of dhāraṇī or the doors of samādhi; nor does one perceive the five [superknowledges].
One does not perceive the eye or the six supernormal powers; nor does one perceive the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
nor does one perceive great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity;
nor does one perceive the thirty-two marks or the eighty minor characteristics; nor does one perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness.

In the Dharma and the state of constant equanimity, one does not perceive omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
nor does one perceive the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
nor does one perceive any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva or the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.
One may harbor doubts or hesitations regarding this;
however, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive have accomplished physical, verbal, and mental actions that are disciplined, gentle, lovely, and delightful, and their minds are free from obstruction toward all sentient beings."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly accomplish loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; they initiate corresponding actions of body, speech, and mind, performing deeds that bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

The minds of all non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas never dwell together with the five hindrances, namely: the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, and the hindrance of doubt.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and marks, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already subdued all latent tendencies (*anuśaya*).
All fetters (*saṃyojana*), bonds, and the bonds of secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*) never arise again.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

All non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas enter and exit, go and return, with minds free from confusion or error. They constantly abide in right mindfulness and right situational awareness; it is likewise so regarding their dignified deportment in advancing or halting, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, and even in lifting or placing their feet. Wherever they travel, they invariably observe the ground; they proceed calmly, with focused attention and a direct gaze, their movements and speech always free from abruptness or violence.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

All bedding and clothing used by non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas are always fragrant and pure, free from any foul odors or impurities; they are also devoid of grime, oiliness, lice, nits, or similar insects;
their minds delight in purity and clarity, and their bodies are free from disease.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
The body and mind of all non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; they are not like the bodies of ordinary people, which are constantly being devoured by eighty thousand families of worms.

Why is this so? Because these bodhisattvas possess roots of goodness that are superior and transcend the world; their physical forms, both internally and externally, are pure, and therefore no insects or vermin can infest or consume their bodies.

As their roots of goodness gradually increase, so too do their bodies and minds become increasingly pure. By virtue of this cause and condition, the bodies and minds of these bodhisattvas become as firm and solid as a vajra, such that they cannot be harmed or disturbed by adverse conditions.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How does such a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly attain purity of body, speech, and mind?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"To the extent that the roots of virtue of this bodhisattva mahāsattva gradually increase, to that same extent the crookedness of body, speech, and mind is eliminated by the power of those roots of virtue; thus, they will never arise again throughout the limits of the future, and by this means, he constantly attains purity of body, speech, and mind."
Furthermore, Subhūti!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly manifest the three types of sublime conduct of body, the four of speech, and the three of mind, their body, speech, and mind are pure at all times. By virtue of this purity, they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, abiding firmly and immovably in the rank of a bodhisattva; through this, they constantly attain the purity of body, speech, and mind.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"

All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not value gain and offerings, nor do they pursue reputation; they do not give rise to attachment toward food and drink, clothing, bedding, dwellings, or material wealth. Although they may practice the twelve dhūta virtues, they place no reliance upon them.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas constantly cultivate the perfections from generosity up to wisdom, ultimately never giving rise to stinginess, greed, violation of precepts, anger, indolence, distraction, or delusion, nor to any other various minds associated with afflictions, fetters, or bonds.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

The awakening wisdom of all non-regressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas is firm and profound; they hear the True Dharma with reverence and faith, and contemplate its ultimate principles with focused mindfulness. Regarding all mundane and supramundane dharmas they have heard and received, they are able through skillful means to integrate them into the profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā. Furthermore, whatever worldly activities they undertake, they likewise rely on the Prajñāpāramitā to integrate them into the *dharmatā* (the nature of phenomena), such that not a single thing is seen to transcend the *dharmatā*. Even if there were something that did not accord with the *dharmatā*, they would still be able to skillfully integrate it into the profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, whereby nothing is seen to transcend the *dharmatā*.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

For all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive, suppose an evil Māra were to appear before them and manifest eight great hells; furthermore, within each of these great hells, he were to manifest immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, all of whom are being scorched by intersecting fierce flames and each undergoing bitter, agonizing, and poisonous great suffering. Having performed such a manifestation, he says to those non-retrogressive bodhisattvas:

"These bodhisattvas have all received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; therefore, they have fallen into such great hells and constantly undergo these various kinds of intense suffering."
"Since you Bodhisattvas have received the prediction of non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, you too shall fall into this great hell and undergo various intense sufferings."

"The Buddha has granted you the prediction that you shall undergo extreme suffering within the great hells; he has not granted you the prediction of non-retrogression toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Therefore, you should quickly abandon the mind of great bodhi, so that you may escape the suffering of these hells and be reborn among the gods or among humans to experience various sublime pleasures."
At that time, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive sees or hears this matter, their mind remains unshaken and free from alarm or doubt; they simply think:
"It is impossible for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has received the prediction of non-retrogression to fall into the realms of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, or among the asuras."

Why is this so? Because non-regressive bodhisattvas are certainly free from unwholesome karma, and they likewise possess no wholesome karma that would bring about bitter fruits; because all Buddhas are necessarily devoid of false speech; and because all that the Tathāgata speaks is for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, flowing forth from a mind of great compassion.
"What we now see and hear must certainly be the work and the teaching of an evil Māra; none of it is real.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, marks, and characteristics, one should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Suppose an evil Māra, assuming the form of a śramaṇa, were to come to an irreversible Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and say these words:

'All that you have previously heard regarding the need to cultivate the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom so as to bring them quickly to fulfillment, and even up to the realization of the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—all such things you have heard are false teachings; you should swiftly abandon them and not consider them to be true.'"

Furthermore, what you previously heard—that one should, regarding all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples of the past, future, and present, from their initial generation of the mind until the duration of the Dharma, rejoice in all their merits and roots of goodness therein, and having gathered them all together, share them equally with all sentient beings, employing the method of non-apprehension to dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—this which you have heard is also a false teaching; you should quickly abandon it and not consider it to be true.

If you abandon those false teachings you have heard, I shall instruct you in the true and pure Buddha-dharma, enabling you to practice and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"What you have previously heard is not the true word of the Buddha; it is a false compilation by a poet. What I have spoken is the true word of the Buddha.
Subhūti, you should know this!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such words, experiences agitation, fear, or doubt in their mind, it should be known that they have not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression; they are not yet determined regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and are not yet called a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such words, remains unmoved and neither startled nor doubtful, but dwells in accordance with the dharma-nature that is unconditioned, signless, and unborn—then whatever this bodhisattva mahāsattva undertakes, they do not rely on the words of others nor follow the instructions of others in practicing the perfections from generosity up to wisdom; nor do they follow the instructions of others in proceeding toward the realization of the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. You should know that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained non-retrogression regarding unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.”

Just as an Arhat whose outflows are exhausted acts with whatever purpose he may have—realizing the nature of phenomena through direct perception without relying on the words of others, free from confusion and doubt, and incapable of being shaken by any Māra—so too, an irreversible Bodhisattva Mahāsattva cannot have his mind broken, subdued, or made to feel despondent regarding enlightenment by any Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, non-Buddhists, or Māras.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva has definitely established themselves in the stage of non-retrogression; all their undertakings are preceded by careful reflection, rather than being initiated merely out of faith in others. Even regarding the teachings of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, they do not accept and practice them lightly or impulsively, let alone act upon the words of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, outsiders, or evil Māras!
It is impossible that this bodhisattva mahāsattva would perform any action without careful reflection, merely relying on the words of others.
Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma that could be trusted as something to be practiced.

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any form that can be practiced with conviction, nor does he perceive any feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness that can be practiced with conviction;

furthermore, he does not perceive any suchness of form that can be practiced with conviction, nor does he perceive any suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness that can be practiced with conviction.

To speak at length, up to and including not perceiving any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice as something that can be taken as a trustworthy practice, nor perceiving any unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as something that can be taken as a trustworthy practice;

furthermore, not perceiving any suchness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices as something that can be taken as a trustworthy suchness, nor perceiving any suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as something that can be taken as a trustworthy suchness.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
If an evil Māra, assuming the guise of a bhikṣu, should come to the place of any non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva and declare these words:
"What you are practicing is the dharma of saṃsāra; it is not the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor can the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening you seek be attained by means of this."
“You should now cultivate the path that brings an end to suffering, so that you may swiftly exhaust all suffering and attain parinirvāṇa.

At that time, Māra the Evil One immediately taught the Bodhisattva a counterfeit path resembling the cycle of birth and death—namely, the perception of bones, or the perception of bluish discoloration, or the perception of festering pus, or the perception of bloating, or the perception of being devoured by worms, or the perception of bloody putrefaction; or loving-kindness, or compassion, or sympathetic joy, or equanimity; or the first dhyāna, or even up to the fourth dhyāna; or the sphere of infinite space, or even up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—and he addressed the Bodhisattva, saying:

"This is the true path and the true practice; by means of this path and this practice, you shall attain the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha."
By means of this path and through this practice, you shall swiftly exhaust all birth, old age, sickness, and death; what need is there for you to endure the suffering of birth and death for so long?
You should even now feel weary of and abandon this present body of suffering, let alone seek to receive a body of suffering in the future!
"You should examine yourself and abandon what you previously believed.
"Sudhana, you should know that when this bodhisattva mahāsattva hears those words, his mind remains unmoved and he feels neither alarm nor doubt, but thinks only this:"

"This bhikṣu has benefited me not a little, for he has been able to explain to me a counterfeit path. This has allowed me to recognize that this path cannot lead to the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor even to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; how much less could it ever lead to the realization of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment I seek!"
Having formed this thought, that bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to profound joy and further reflects:

"This bhikṣu has been of great benefit to me; by skillful means he has explained to me the dharmas that obstruct the path. Now that I have recognized these obstructing dharmas, I shall freely train in the paths of the Three Vehicles."
"Subhūti, you should know that at that time,
the evil Māra, perceiving that this bodhisattva’s heart was filled with deep joy, spoke these words again: 'Ho!'"
"Noble son! Do you now wish to see those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have for a long time diligently practiced what is unbeneficial?

That is to say, throughout great kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, these assemblies of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have—with immeasurable varieties of exquisite food and drink, clothing, bedding, medicine, wealth, flowers, incense, and other such items—made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones."
Furthermore, at the sites of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they practice the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;

they train in and abide in the emptinesses from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; they train in and abide in the stages from suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
they train in and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; and they cultivate the four applications of mindfulness.
Abiding in [the factors] up to the eight branches of the noble path, they cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they cultivate the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they cultivate the eight liberations up to the ten totalities;
they cultivate the stages of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and they cultivate all dhāraṇī-gates.
...the doors of samādhi; they cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
they cultivate the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they cultivate great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;

they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity; and they cultivate the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order.
They arise to mature sentient beings, to purify Buddha-fields, and to cultivate the sublime supernormal powers of bodhisattvas,
up to and including the cultivation of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also drew near to and served Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, and in the presence of those Buddhas, they inquired about the path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, saying:
"How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abide securely in the Great Vehicle?"
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
abide in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm; and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path? Practice...
They practice the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; they cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they cultivate the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
they cultivate the eight liberations up to the ten totalities; and they cultivate the stages of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
They practice all the gateways of dhāraṇīs and samādhis; they cultivate the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they cultivate great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity; and they cultivate the twelve links of dependent origination.
How does one give rise to the contemplations of conformity and opposition, mature sentient beings, purify Buddha-fields, and practice the sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva,
up to and including the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have explained this in successive order according to your questions. Although these assemblies of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide and train according to the Buddhas’ instructions, and though they exert themselves with fervent diligence for immeasurable eons, they are still unable to attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek; how much less so can you, who are now merely practicing and training, attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!

"Subhūti, you should know that although this bodhisattva mahāsattva hears these words, his mind remains unchanged; he is not startled, nor terrified, nor does he harbor doubt or confusion. Instead, he becomes even more joyful and thinks to himself:

'This bhikṣu has greatly benefited me by skillfully explaining to me the dharmas that obstruct the path. Now I know that these obstructive dharmas will certainly prevent me from attaining the fruit of a stream-enterer, up to and including the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; how much less could I attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that I seek!'"

At that time, the Evil Māra, knowing that this bodhisattva’s mind was not discouraged and was free from delusion or doubt, immediately manifested the forms of immeasurable bhikṣus at that very spot and said to the bodhisattva:

"All these bhikṣus diligently sought unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in the past; they practiced various difficult and painful austerities for immeasurable kalpas, yet they were unable to attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they sought. Now they have all regressed and abide in the fruit of arhatship, with all outflows exhausted and having reached the end of suffering. How can you possibly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
"Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva has seen or heard this, they will immediately think:

'This must be Māra, the Evil One, who has manifested in the form of such a bhikṣu to disturb my mind. By teaching these counterfeit dharmas that act as obstacles, he intends to ensure that no bodhisattva mahāsattva ever reaches the stage of perfection in the practice of the prajñāpāramitā, nor realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, but instead falls back into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.'"
At that time, the Bodhisattva further thought:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom until reaching the ultimate stage, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

to speak at length, even if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects until reaching the stage of fulfillment, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!...”
All non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas constantly practice the perfection of wisdom and always maintain this thought:
"If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva diligently trains according to the teachings of all Buddhas,
they will never be separated from the sublime practices subsumed within the six perfections, nor will they ever be separated from the characteristics of the six perfections."
One should apply the mind, never being separated from the mental application associated with the knowledge of all modes;

constantly using skillful means, one should exhort all sentient beings to diligently practice and train in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. This is the certainty of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
They do not regress from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
they are certain not to regress from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; they are certain not to regress from suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
they are certain not to regress from the principle of the four noble truths; and they are certain not to regress from the four foundations of mindfulness.
Up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, they are certain not to regress from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they are certain not to regress from the three gates of liberation; they are certain not to regress from the eight liberations up to the ten totalities;
they are certain not to regress from the bodhisattva stages; they are certain not to regress from the *dhāraṇīs*.
They are certain not to regress from the gates of *dhāraṇī* and the gates of *samādhi*; they are certain not to regress from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
they are certain not to regress from the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they are certain not to regress from great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; and they are certain not to regress from non-forgetfulness.
By means of the Dharma and the nature of constant equanimity, they are certain not to regress from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path,
and the knowledge of all aspects, and will inevitably realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!...”
All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly practice the perfection of wisdom and always maintain this thought:
"If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva recognizes the deeds of Māra and does not follow those deeds;
recognizes evil friends and does not follow the words of evil friends; recognizes sensory objects and does not turn according to those objects—this bodhisattva..."
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is certain not to regress from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
certain not to regress from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence;
certain not to regress from suchness up to the inconceivable realm; certain not to regress from the principle of the four noble truths; certain not to...

They may regress from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, but they are certain not to regress from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they are certain not to regress from the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
they are certain not to regress from the eight liberations up to the ten totalities; they are certain not to regress.
The stages of all bodhisattvas consist of the dharani-doors and samadhi-doors from which they never regress;
the five eyes and six supernormal powers from which they never regress; the ten powers of a Tathagata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha from which they never regress;
and great loving-kindness, great compassion, and great sympathetic joy from which they never regress.
With great equanimity, they are certain not to regress from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they are certain not to regress from all-knowledge, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, and will inevitably realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, upon hearing the essential teachings spoken by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, experience profound joy in their hearts; they receive them with reverence and faith, skillfully understanding their meaning and intent. Their minds are as firm as adamant, unshakable and incapable of being led astray or deprived. They constantly and diligently practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and they likewise encourage others to train therein without weariness of mind.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Regarding such a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva, from what does he not retrogress that he is called ‘non-retrogressive’?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he retrogresses from the notion of the aggregate of form up to the notion of the aggregate of consciousness;
he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he retrogresses from the notion of the sense-base of the eye up to the notion of the sense-base of the mind.”
He is called "non-retrogressive" because he has turned back from the perception of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the perception of the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*);
he is called "non-retrogressive" because he has turned back from the perception of the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) up to the perception of the mind-element (*manodhātu*);

he is called "non-retrogressive" because he has turned back from the perception of the form-element (*rūpadhātu*) up to the perception of the phenomenon-element (*dharmadhātu*); [and he is so called] regarding eye-consciousness...
Because there is regression from the perception of the element (*dhātu*) up to the perception of the consciousness-element (*vijñānadhātu*), it is called "non-regression";
because there is regression from the perception of eye-contact (*cakṣuḥ-saṃsparśa*) up to the perception of mind-contact (*manaḥ-saṃsparśa*), it is called "non-regression";

and because there is regression from the various feelings and perceptions produced with eye-contact as condition up to the various feelings and perceptions produced with mind-contact as condition, [it is called non-regression].
They are called "non-retrogressive" because they do not retrogress from the perception of the element of earth, up to the perception of the element of consciousness;
they are called "non-retrogressive" because they do not retrogress from the perception of causes and conditions, up to the perception of dominant conditions;
they are called "non-retrogressive" because they do not retrogress from the perception of ignorance, up to the perception of old age and death.
One is called "non-retrogressive" because one turns back from the perceptions of greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as from the perceptions of various speculative views;
one is called "non-retrogressive" because one turns back from the perception of the perfection of generosity up to the perception of the perfection of wisdom;
and [one is so called] because one turns back from the perception of internal emptiness up to the perception of the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature.
They are called "non-retrogressive" because they have retrogressed from the notion of true suchness, up to and including the notion of the inconceivable realm;
they are called "non-retrogressive" because they have retrogressed from the notion of the four noble truths;
they are called "non-retrogressive" because they have retrogressed from the notion of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the notion of the eightfold noble path.
They may regress; because they do not regress from the conceptions of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, they are called "non-regressive.
Because they do not regress from the conceptions of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—they are called "non-regressive.
[They do not regress] from the conceptions of the eight liberations, up to the conceptions of the ten totalities.

Because they turn back, they are called "non-retrogressive. Because they may retrogress from the conceptualization of the Stage of Pure Observation up to the conceptualization of the Stage of the Tathāgata, they are called "non-retrogressive.
Because they may retrogress from the conceptualization of the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the conceptualization of the Cloud of Dharma Stage, they are called "non-retrogressive.
[They are also so called] because they may retrogress from the conceptualization of the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi.

Because they turn back, they are called "non-retrogressive"; because they have retrogression regarding the conceptualization of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, they are called "non-retrogressive";
because they have retrogression regarding the conceptualization of the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they are called "non-retrogressive";
[and likewise] regarding great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity...

Because they have the notion that there is regression, they are called "non-regressive"; because they have the notion that there is regression regarding the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics, they are called "non-regressive";
because they have the notion that there is regression regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity, they are called "non-regressive";
[and] because they have the notion regarding the fruit of stream-entry, up to the awakening of a pratyekabuddha...

One is called "non-retrogressive" because one has no conceptualization of retrogression; one is called "non-retrogressive" because one has no conceptualization of retrogression regarding the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha;
and one is called "non-retrogressive" because one has no conceptualization of retrogression regarding all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
They are called "non-retrogressive" because they do not regress from their conceptions of ordinary beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas,
or buddhas. Why is this so?

In this way, a non-retrogressive Bodhisattva Mahāsattva contemplates all phenomena as empty of their own characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnya*). Having entered the Bodhisattva’s stage of right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*), they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon that can be apprehended; because it cannot be apprehended, there is no volitional construction (*abhisaṃskāra*); because there is no volitional construction, it is called ultimate non-arising (*atyantānutpāda*); because it is ultimately non-arising, it is called the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); and by attaining such patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena, one is called a non-retrogressive Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 514, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three, Chapter Twenty: The Signs of Non-Retrogression (Part Two). "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

For all non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, even if an evil Māra should come to their place, wishing to cause them to become weary of and turn away from unsurpassed enlightenment, he might say:

"The knowledge of all modes is equal to space; its nature is the absence of intrinsic nature, and its own-characteristics are fundamentally empty. All dharmas are likewise equal to space; their nature is the absence of intrinsic nature."

Within the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics, there is not a single dharma that can be called the "realizer," nor is there a single dharma that can be called the "realized. The locus of realization, the time of realization, and that by which realization occurs are likewise unattainable.

Since all phenomena are equal to space, having non-existence as their nature and being empty of intrinsic characteristics from the very beginning, why do you undergo such fruitless hardship in seeking to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
"All those bodhisattvas you previously heard of who were said to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—this was all the speech of Māra and not the true word of the Buddha.

You should abandon the aspiration to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; do not, throughout the long night, laboriously undergo hardships for yourselves while vainly seeking the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings. Though you may practice various difficult and painful austerities, you will ultimately never attain enlightenment."
When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva hears such words of reproach and admonition, he is able to examine them closely, thinking:
"This is the work of an evil Māra, seeking to cause me to retreat and destroy my great mind of enlightenment; I must not now believe or accept what he says."

Although all phenomena are equal to space, having non-existence as their nature and being empty of intrinsic characteristics from the very beginning, sentient beings—throughout the long night of birth and death—do not know or see this; they act with perversion and negligence, creating various karmas and undergoing the suffering of birth and death.

I shall don the armor of merit, whose nature and characteristics are all empty like the great void, and swiftly proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For the sake of all sentient beings, I shall preach the Dharma as is appropriate, causing them to be liberated from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, so that they may attain the fruit of a stream-enterer, or the fruit of a once-returner, or the fruit of a non-returner, or the fruit of an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby being able to bring benefit and happiness to all throughout the future.

"From the moment this bodhisattva-mahāsattva first resolved their mind [on awakening], having heard this Dharma, their mind has been firm, unshakable, and irreversible. Relying upon this firm, unshakable, and irreversible mind, they constantly and correctly practice the six pāramitās, and have already entered the bodhisattva’s state of right nature and departure from birth."
Furthermore, by correctly practicing the six pāramitās, they gradually bring them to perfection and subdue all fetters; through this, they enter the stage of non-retrogression.
Therefore, although evil Māras may employ various means to cause their defeat, they cannot cause the Bodhisattva’s great mind of enlightenment to regress.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Is this bodhisattva mahāsattva called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not retrogress, or is he called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does retrogress?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not retrogress, and he is also called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does retrogress.”
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"In what way is this bodhisattva mahāsattva called 'non-retrogressive' by virtue of being non-retrogressive?"
"How is it that one is called 'non-retrogressive' even by virtue of retrogression?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"This bodhisattva mahāsattva has transcended the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and will no longer fall back into those two stages; for this reason, he is said to be non-retrogressive by virtue of being non-retrogressive."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, definitively relinquishing those two stages; for this reason, it is said that because he has "turned back," he is called "non-retrogressive."

Therefore, this bodhisattva receives two names; unlike those in other stages who are merely called "regressive," if a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, they will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and the armies of all evil Māras shall be unable to defeat them.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, wishing to enter the first dhyāna up to the fourth dhyāna, can enter them at will;
wishing to enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness up to the immeasurable state of equanimity, they can enter them at will."
He is able to enter them; whether he wishes to enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he can enter it at will;
whether he wishes to enter the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, he can enter it at will;
whether he wishes to enter the first liberation up to the liberation through the cessation of perception and feeling, he can enter it at will.
If he wishes to enter the first sphere of mastery up to the eighth sphere of mastery, he can enter them at will;
if he wishes to enter the first dhyāna concentration up to the cessation of perception and feeling (*nirodhasamāpatti*), he can enter them at will;
if he wishes to enter the first universal base (*kṛtsnāyatana*) up to the tenth universal base, he can enter them at will; if he wishes to enter emptiness, signlessness, or...
"May I enter the gates of liberation at will; may I manifest the five supernormal powers at will.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter the four dhyānas and even manifest the five supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), they do not experience their fruits.

For this reason, they are not born through the power of the dhyānas, the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the meditative attainments (*samāpatti*), up to the attainment of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*), nor through other meritorious qualities. Furthermore, they do not take up the fruit of a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, nor the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Rather, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, they assume whatever bodies are appropriate to be assumed according to their wishes; they are able to assume them exactly as they have vowed. Having performed what was to be done, they immediately relinquish them.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas accomplish the mental engagement of unsurpassed enlightenment and never depart from the great bodhicitta;
they do not prize the aggregate of form, up to and including the aggregate of consciousness; they do not prize the sense base of the eye, up to and including the sense base of the mind;
they do not prize the sense base of forms, up to and including the sense base of phenomena; they do not prize the eye element... [and so forth].
Reaching the element of mind, one does not prize the elements of form up to the element of mental phenomena;
one does not prize the element of eye-consciousness up to the element of mind-consciousness; one does not prize eye-contact up to mind-contact;
one does not prize the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition; one does not prize the earth element up to...
Regarding the consciousness element, one does not prize causes and conditions up to and including the predominant condition;
one does not prize the nature of all conditions or dependent origination; one does not prize the primary marks, nor the secondary characteristics;
one does not prize the bases, nor material and immaterial phenomena, nor visible and invisible phenomena, nor resistant and non-resistant phenomena.
He does not prize contaminated or uncontaminated dharmas; he does not prize conditioned or unconditioned dharmas;
he does not prize mundane or supramundane dharmas; he does not prize the self;
he does not prize sentient beings, nor even those who know or see; he does not prize his retinue, nor his kin, nor his rank and emolument.
One does not value wealth or treasures; one does not value the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
one does not value inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; one does not value suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
one does not value the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; one does not value—
Regarding the ten paths of wholesome action, one does not prize the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments;
one does not prize the five supernormal powers; one does not prize the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
one does not prize the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and one does not prize the eight liberations up to the ten totalities.
In this state, one does not prize the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata; one does not prize the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma stage;
one does not prize the gates of dhāraṇī or the gates of samādhi; one does not prize the five eyes or the six supernormal powers;
and one does not prize the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They do not value great kindness, great compassion, great joy, or great equanimity;
they do not value the quality of non-forgetfulness or the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity; they do not value all-knowledge, the knowledge of paths, or the knowledge of all aspects;
they do not value the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; they do not value any bodhisattva...
The practice of a bodhisattva does not prize the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; it does not prize the adornment and purification of buddha-fields;
it does not prize the maturation of sentient beings; it does not prize the frequent seeing of many Buddhas; and it does not prize the planting of roots of virtue.

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas realize that all phenomena are equal to space, having non-existence as their nature, and that their specific characteristics are entirely empty. They do not perceive any phenomenon that can be regarded as precious; the producer, the produced, the time of production, the place of production, and that by which production occurs—all these are unfindable.
Why is this? Because all these phenomena are equal to space; their nature and characteristics are all empty, for they lack the meaning of arising.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes the mental attention of unsurpassed enlightenment and never departs from the great bodhicitta. Whether moving or staying, entering or exiting, lifting or lowering a foot, his mind is never distracted. In walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, and in all movements and postures, he dwells in right mindfulness in whatever task he performs.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

All non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, manifest residence in the household life. Through skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), although they appear to accept the requisites for the five sensory pleasures, they do not give rise to attachment therein. All this is for the purpose of providing for sentient beings: that is to say, they provide food to those who need food, drink to those who need drink, clothing to those who need clothing, and vehicles to those who need vehicles; indeed, they provide everything that is required, thereby fulfilling their wishes.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally practices the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; they also encourage others to practice the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; they constantly and correctly praise the dharma of practicing the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom; and they joyfully extol those who practice the perfections from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom.

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva, while manifesting residence in the household life, by means of supernatural powers or the power of great vows, gathers various precious jewels and requisites to fill Jambudvīpa and even the trichiliocosm; he then uses these to make offerings to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and bestows them as gifts upon all impoverished sentient beings.

Although this bodhisattva-mahāsattva appears to dwell in a household, they constantly practice pure conduct (*brahmacarya*) and never partakes in the objects of exquisite sensual desire. Although they appear to acquire various kinds of precious wealth, they do not give rise to stained attachment toward them. Furthermore, when acquiring the requisites for sensual pleasure and precious wealth, they never coerce sentient beings to cause them grief or suffering.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive are constantly followed on their left and right by a Vajradhara Yakṣa King who secretly provides protection. He always thinks: "This bodhisattva-mahāsattva shall before long realize unsurpassed awakening;

may I constantly follow and secretly protect them until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. Throughout this time, the five families of Vajradhara Yakṣas shall constantly follow and protect them without ever abandoning them for a moment. Neither humans nor non-humans shall be able to harm them, and neither gods, Māras, Brahmās, nor any other beings in the world shall be able to destroy by means of the Dharma the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening mind they have resolved upon."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, these bodhisattvas, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, remain serene in body and mind and are never disturbed or afflicted.

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas never lack the five worldly faculties—namely, the faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body—and they likewise never lack the five supramundane faculties, namely, the faculties of faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s limbs are perfectly formed and adorned with the marks and signs, and his mental merits increase moment by moment until he reaches unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive are always superior persons and never inferior persons.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva come to be always a superior person and never an inferior person?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"For this bodhisattva mahāsattva, no afflictions ever manifest again; from moment to moment, wholesome dharmas increase until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and at all times his mind remains undistracted."
Therefore, I say that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is always a superior person and not an inferior one.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas accomplish the mental engagement of unsurpassed awakening;
they are never separated from the great mind of awakening, constantly cultivate a pure livelihood, and do not practice incantations or medicine."

One should not practice divination for various forms of wrong livelihood; nor, for the sake of fame or profit, should one recite mantras over spirits and deities to cause them to possess men or women so as to inquire about their fortune or misfortune.
Furthermore, one should not perform incantations or prohibitions to produce rare phenomena involving men, women, the young or old, animals, or ghosts;
nor should one practice physiognomy to predict the length of one's lifespan, wealth and status, or the birth of sons and daughters.
Regarding various matters of good and evil, they do not predict cold or heat, abundance or scarcity, fortune or misfortune, nor do they confuse sentient beings with likes and dislikes.
They do not practice incantations or prohibitions, compound medicinal decoctions, employ heterodox methods to treat illnesses, or cultivate alliances with the noble.
Nor do they act as messengers for others, assuming the guise of friends to pursue profit.
Even by name alone, he does not allow his mind to be defiled when observing men and women playing, laughing, or conversing, much less engage in other such matters!

Furthermore, he does not pay reverence or make offerings to spirits and deities; for this reason, I say that he is always an upper-class person (upapudgala) and never a lower-class person (adhama-pudgala).

Why is this so? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are empty. Within the emptiness of nature and characteristics, they do not perceive any marks; because they do not perceive such marks, they remain far removed from various wrong livelihoods, incantations, medical arts, and divination. They seek only unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, constantly bringing benefit to all sentient beings.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, though they have attained skillfulness in the various worldly arts and crafts, do not become attached to them. Why is this?

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva realizes that all dharmas are ultimately empty. Within ultimate emptiness, all worldly literature and arts are unobtainable; furthermore, all such worldly literature and arts are subsumed under frivolous speech and wrong livelihood. Therefore, the bodhisattva knows them but does not engage in them.

Subhūti, you should know that although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are well-versed in the secular treatises and scriptures of non-Buddhists, they do not take pleasure in them nor become attached to them. Why is this?

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva realizes that the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are empty; within this emptiness of nature and characteristics, no books or treatises can be found. Furthermore, the principles and matters explained in the secular and non-Buddhist (tīrthika) books and treatises often involve exaggerations and omissions; they do not accord with the Bodhisattva path and are all subsumed under frivolous conceptualization and impure speech. Therefore, bodhisattvas know them and take no pleasure in them.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
Furthermore, all non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess other practices, characteristics, and signs by which they are known to be non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"I shall analyze and explain this for you; you should listen attentively and reflect upon it very thoroughly!
Subhūti replied, "Indeed! I shall do so."
"Please speak!
We now focus our minds with the desire to hear.
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"All irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* penetrate the fact that all phenomena are non-existent; they never depart from the great mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*), and they take no pleasure in examining or discoursing upon the aggregates, the sense-bases, or the elements."

Why is this? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already well contemplated and thoroughly mastered the principle that the nature and characteristics of the aggregates, bases, and elements are empty.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing on various worldly matters. Why is that?
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already well contemplated and thoroughly realized the principle that all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature and characteristics.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing matters of statecraft.

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), and thus does not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of superior or inferior, noble or base.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing matters concerning thieves. Why is that?

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of self-characteristics, because they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of gain or loss, or of being given or taken away.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing military matters.

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), and thus does not perceive any phenomena as having characteristics of increase or decrease, or of aggregation and dispersion.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing talk of warfare. Why is that?

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells well in the principle of the emptiness of the true suchness (tathatā) of all phenomena, because they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of strength or weakness, or of attachment and aversion.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon men and women.

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of all phenomena (*dharmas*), and thus does not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of being beautiful or ugly, or of being objects of love or hatred.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing villages. Why is that?

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of all phenomena, because they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of increase or decrease, or of conjunction or separation.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon cities.

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of all phenomena (*dharmas*), and thus does not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as being grasped or ungrasped, nor as having the characteristics of good or evil.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon realms. Why is that?

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), because they do not perceive any phenomena as having the characteristics of belonging or not belonging to this or that.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon the marks and signs of physical excellence. Why is this?
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in the signless (*animitta*), and thus does not perceive any differentiated characteristics of beauty or ugliness among all phenomena.

“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon the notions that ‘this is a self,’ ‘this is a sentient being,’ and so on, up to ‘this is a knower’ or ‘this is a seer.’”

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) and do not perceive any distinction between the existence or non-existence of anything from a self (ātman) up to a knower (jñātṛ).

“Subhūti, you should know that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not delight in examining or discussing such worldly matters as these; they delight only in examining and discussing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is free from all marks (*nimitta*) and is able to realize unsurpassed, great *bodhi*.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!"

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is never separated from the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects; they practice the perfection of generosity while remaining free from stinginess and greed, they practice the perfection of ethical discipline while remaining free from transgressing the precepts, they practice the perfection of patience while remaining free from anger and contention, they practice the perfection of diligence while remaining free from laziness, they practice the perfection of meditative concentration while remaining free from distraction, and they practice the perfection of wisdom while remaining free from faulty discernment.
"Subhūti, you should know that although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the emptiness of all phenomena, they love and delight in the true Dharma and do not delight in what is not the Dharma;
although they abide in the emptiness of the unapprehendable, they constantly praise the merits of the Triple Gem."

“Subhūti, you should know that although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the single-taste characteristic of the suchness and dharma-realm of all phenomena, they delight in praising the various merits of that suchness and dharma-realm.”
"Subhūti, you should know that although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas realize that all phenomena are ultimately empty, they cherish virtuous friends and do not delight in evil friends."
Regarding "virtuous friends," this refers to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;

furthermore, those belonging to the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas who are well able to teach and establish sentient beings, leading them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, are also called virtuous friends.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva always delights in personally attending upon all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and in hearing the True Dharma.”

If they hear that a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is currently preaching the true Dharma in another world, they immediately take rebirth in that realm through the power of their vows, where they make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise him, and listen to and receive the true Dharma.

"Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva, whether by day or by night, is never apart from the mental engagement of mindfulness of the Buddha, nor is he ever apart from the mental engagement of hearing the Dharma. By virtue of these causes and conditions, wherever in any land a Buddha, a World-Honored One, is currently preaching the true Dharma, he immediately travels there to take birth through the power of his vows, or else travels there through miraculous power to hear the Dharma."

By reason of these causes and conditions, these bodhisattvas, in every place where they are born, are never separated from the Buddha and constantly hear the true Dharma without interruption or cessation.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

For the sake of constantly bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, although able to manifest the various profound meditative absorptions of the dhyānas and formless realms, skillfully employ expedient means to give rise to the mind of the desire realm and teach sentient beings the ten paths of wholesome action. Furthermore, by the power of their vows, they manifest birth in the desire realm within buddha-fields where a Buddha resides, making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, while listening to the true Dharma and practicing all sublime deeds.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
All non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
they constantly practice inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence;
they constantly practice suchness up to the inconceivable realm; and they constantly practice suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
The Noble Truths; constantly practicing the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
constantly practicing the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; constantly practicing the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
constantly practicing the eight liberations up to the ten totalities; and constantly practicing the sublime bodhi-qualities.
On the Bodhisattva stages, they constantly practice all *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates; they constantly practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
they constantly practice the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they constantly practice great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; and they constantly practice non-forgetfulness.

They abide in the Dharma and the nature of constant equanimity; they constantly practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they constantly practice all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and they constantly seek the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva never gives rise to doubt or uncertainty regarding his own stage, nor does he form such thoughts as:
‘I am non-retrogressive,’ or ‘I am not non-retrogressive.’”

Why is this? It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive even the slightest phenomenon that could be said to either regress from or not regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no confusion or doubt regarding the dharmas of his own stage. Why is that?
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already thoroughly understood and fully realized the dharmas of his own stage. Subhūti,

you should know that just as a stream-enterer abiding in the fruit of stream-entry has no confusion or doubt regarding the dharmas of his own fruit, so too do those who are once-returners, non-returners, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas— each abiding in their respective fruits— have no confusion or doubt regarding the dharmas of their own fruits.

In this same way, this bodhisattva mahāsattva also, regarding all the dharmas subsumed within the stage of non-retrogression in which he himself abides, knows them directly and sees them directly, without confusion and without doubt.

“Subhūti, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in this stage, they bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and cultivate all manner of meritorious virtues. When demonic activities arise, they are immediately able to recognize them; they do not succumb to the power of such demonic activities, but are well able to suppress and destroy various demonic deeds so that they do not obstruct the meritorious virtues they are cultivating.”

“Subhūti, you should know that just as for one who has committed an act of immediate retribution, that immediate state of mind constantly follows them, such that even until the end of life they cannot abandon it.”

Why is this so? Because the power of the entanglements (*paryavasthāna*) that give rise to the immediate karmic offenses (*ānantarya-karma*) operates with such predominant force that it continues to function constantly until the end of life, and cannot be suppressed; even if other states of mind arise, they are unable to obstruct it.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is also like this: dwelling securely in their own stage, their mind is immovable and free from conceptual discrimination; neither the gods, humans, nor asuras of the world can cause them to waver.

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess minds that are firm and steadfast, transcending all those in the world—gods, humans, māras, brahmās, and asuras—and have already entered the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, abiding on the stage of non-retrogression. Having attained the bodhisattva’s sublime supernormal powers, they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields. They travel from one buddha-field to another to offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and their disciples; they listen to the true Dharma, plant various roots of goodness in the presence of the Buddhas, and inquire about the meaning of the dharmas studied by bodhisattvas.

“Subhūti, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in their own stage, they are able to recognize as soon as demonic activities arise; they never comply with or follow after such demonic activities. Through skillful means, they gather all demonic activities and place them within the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), thereby eliminating them through skillful means. Thus, regarding the dharmas of their own stage, they have neither confusion nor doubt.”

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that all phenomena enter into the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); they have thoroughly penetrated that the limit of reality is neither one nor many, and within the limit of reality there is no conceptual differentiation. Since they are without delusion or doubt regarding the limit of reality, they likewise have no hesitation concerning the dharmas of their own stage.

“Subhūti, you should know that even if these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were to undergo further rebirths, they would never again regress from the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), nor would they ever give rise to a mind directed toward the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.”

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty; within this emptiness, they do not perceive any phenomenon that arises or ceases, or that is defiled or pure.

“Subhūti, you should know that even when this bodhisattva mahāsattva undergoes a transformation of rebirth, he will not harbor any doubt as to whether or not he shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has realized that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty, which is itself unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Subhūti, you should know this!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in his own stage and does not follow the conditions of others; regarding the dharmas of his own stage, there is none who can destroy them. Why is this?
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished unshakable and non-retrogressive wisdom, such that no adverse conditions whatsoever can cause him to waver.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
For all non-retrogressive Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, should an evil Māra assume the form of a Buddha and come to their place, saying:
"You should now seek the fruit of Arhatship, exhaust all outflows forever, and realize parinirvāṇa."

"You have not yet been worthy to receive the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*), nor have you yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). You do not yet possess the practices, marks, and signs of the stage of non-retrogression; therefore, the Tathāgata should not grant you the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Only when one is fully endowed with the practices, marks, and signs of the stage of non-retrogression may one receive from the Buddha the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment."
When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva hears those words, his mind remains unshaken; he does not retreat, nor does he sink into despondency, and he is without alarm or fear.
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva should realize for himself:
"In the presence of the Tathāgatas of the past, I have certainly already received the prophecy of great enlightenment."
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva who accomplishes such supreme dharmas is certain to receive the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas.
Since I have already accomplished such supreme dharmas, why does the World-Honored One not grant me that prediction?
"Therefore, I must have certainly received the prediction of great enlightenment from the Tathāgata in the past.
