In this way, up to and including: can that which is the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the non-alteration (*ananyathābhāvatā*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—be able to practice the profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?
"No, World-Honored One! Subhūti, it is not so. "World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]

Apart from the suchness of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; apart from the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—is there any dharma to be found that can practice the profound perfection of wisdom?
"No, World-Honored One! Subhūti, [it is not so]. "World-Honored One!"
If all such dharmas are unable to practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, how can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Do you perceive any dharma that is able to practice the profound perfection of wisdom?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Do you perceive this profound perfection of wisdom as the sphere of practice for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Is that dharma which you do not perceive obtainable as a dharma?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think? Can a dharma that is unapprehendable undergo arising?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"That which you perceive as the true nature of all phenomena is precisely the bodhisattva’s acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena, they are then worthy of receiving the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha— these immeasurable and boundless, preeminent virtues— is called one who practices with authentic diligence."

If one can practice with such diligence, it is impossible that they should not attain the wisdom of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, the knowledge of all aspects, great wisdom, and sublime wisdom.

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having already realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), shall experience neither regression nor diminution in the dharmas they have attained, up until their attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the non-arising nature of all phenomena?”
"No, World-Honored One! Subhūti, it is not so. "World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
"Do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the nature of arising of all phenomena? "No, they do not."
"Subhūti! "World-Honored One!

Do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of the Buddha's unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the nature of non-arising within the arising of all phenomena?"
"No, World-Honored One! Subhūti, it is not so. "World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]

Do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the fact that all phenomena are neither produced nor non-produced?
"No, Subhūti! The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“If that is so, how is it that the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are capable of receiving the prediction regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha?
The Buddha said to Subhūti: “What do you think?
"Do you see any dharma that receives the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment from the Buddha? Subhūti replied, "No!"

"Bhagavān! I do not perceive any dharma that is capable of receiving the prediction for the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; nor do I perceive any dharma that is able to realize the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. The time of realization, the place of realization, and that by which one realizes—all these are unapprehendable."
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.
Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not apprehend any phenomena, they do not form such a thought:

"I shall be able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; by means of this dharma, at such a time, and in such a place, I shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Because when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are free from all such conceptual discriminations.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is free from all conceptual discrimination; if one gives rise to conceptual discrimination, one is not practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This Prajñāpāramitā is most profound; it is difficult to see and difficult to realize, beyond the reach of discursive thought, transcending the sphere of conceptualization, and realized by those who are subtle, secret, wise, and sagacious, because it is ultimately free from all signs and discrimination.”

If there are sentient beings who, regarding this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, always delight in hearing it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, mastering it thoroughly, reflecting upon it according to reason, practicing in accordance with the teaching, and correctly explaining it to others—maintaining a mind free from all other mental states and mental factors until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—one should know that such sentient beings have certainly accomplished immeasurable roots of goodness and are capable of performing these deeds therein.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said, Kauśika! If there are sentient beings who,

regarding this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, constantly delight in hearing it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, mastering it thoroughly, reflecting upon it according to the principle, practicing in accordance with the teaching, and correctly explaining it to others— even until they reach unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment— without their minds or mental factors being mixed with anything else, you should know that such sentient beings have certainly accomplished immeasurable roots of goodness, and are thus able to perform these deeds herein."

Kauśika! Suppose all sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa, even throughout the trichiliocosm, were to fully accomplish the ten paths of wholesome action, or the four dhyānas, or the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments, or the five supernormal powers, and so forth—these immeasurable merits.

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, regarding this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, always delight in hearing it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, mastering it thoroughly, reflecting upon it according to the principle, practicing in accordance with the teaching, and correctly explaining it to others—the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family surpasses the aforementioned mass of merit a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold.
At that time, a bhikṣu in the assembly addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: "Kauśika!..."

If good sons or good daughters, with minds focused and undistracted, constantly delight in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, thoroughly mastering, reflecting upon according to principle, practicing in accordance with the teachings, and correctly explaining to others this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, and maintain such practice without being mixed with other thoughts or mental factors until they reach unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment—then the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters surpasses all the immeasurable merits of all sentient beings throughout Jambudvīpa and even the trichiliocosm who have accomplished the ten paths of wholesome action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, or the five supernormal powers.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied to the bhikṣu:

“The merit obtained by such sons and daughters of good family at the very first moment they give rise to a thought associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) already surpasses [the merit of] all those in Jambudvīpa, up to and including the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system.”
Even if all sentient beings in the great trichiliocosm were to fully accomplish the ten paths of wholesome action,
or the four dhyānas, or the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments, or the five supernormal powers—
possessing immeasurable merit many hundreds of thousands of times over— how much more so would this be the case for one who can [practice] this Perfection of Wisdom?
The merit obtained by one who, with a mind focused and undistracted upon the profound sūtras, constantly delights in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting,
mastering thoroughly, reflecting according to the principle, practicing in accordance with the teaching, and correctly explaining them to others—
maintaining no other thoughts or mental factors until reaching unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment— is immeasurable.
"Virtue can indeed be compared! Bhikṣus,

you should know that the merit and wisdom of these sons and daughters of good family not only surpass all the immeasurable merits— such as the accomplishment of the ten paths of wholesome action and the four dhyānas— of all sentient beings from Jambudvīpa up to the trichiliocosm, but they also surpass all the merits possessed by the gods, humans, and asuras of the entire world."

Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby bringing inexhaustible benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The merit and wisdom of these sons and daughters of good family not only surpass all the merit of the world’s gods, humans, and asuras, but also surpass the merit of all stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas.”

Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and their benefit and happiness for sentient beings will be inexhaustible.

“Bhikṣus, you should know that the merit and wisdom of these sons and daughters of good family not only universally surpass all the merits of stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas, but...
Furthermore, they surpass all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, while lacking the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*),
practice the perfections from generosity (*dāna*) up to meditative concentration (*dhyāna*),

abide in the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and abide in suchness (*tathatā*) up to the inconceivable (*acintya*).
Regarding the elements, they abide securely in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
they practice the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path; they practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they practice the eight liberations up to the ten totalities; and they practice emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
The gateways of liberation; the cultivation of the stages from the Ground of Utmost Joy up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma;
the cultivation of all dharani-gates and samadhi-gates; the cultivation of the five eyes and the six superknowledges;
the cultivation of the ten powers of a Tathagata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the cultivation of great loving-kindness and...
[They] cultivate compassion, great joy, and great equanimity; they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
they cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

they cultivate the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order; they bring sentient beings to maturity and adorn and purify Buddha-fields, practicing the deeds of all bodhisattvas.
[They shall attain] the qualities of the practices of a Mahāsattva and those of a Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because these sons and daughters of good family will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi, and their benefit and happiness for sentient beings will be inexhaustible.

“Bhikṣus, you should know that the merit and wisdom of these sons and daughters of good family also surpass all the merit possessed by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom while remaining distant from skillful means.”

Why is this? It is because these sons and daughters of good family will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and their benefit and happiness for sentient beings will be inexhaustible.
"Furthermore, bhikṣus!
You should know that these sons and daughters of good family are indeed bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it has been taught and possesses skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), they cannot be overcome by any in the world—whether devas, humans, or asuras—nor by other bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, or śrāvakas. They are able to perpetuate the lineage of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) so that it remains unbroken; they are never separated from the Buddhas and bodhisattvas, their true and pure spiritual friends. Before long, they shall sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), subdue all the hosts of Māra, realize unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma. They shall uproot the great suffering of birth and death for all classes of sentient beings and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in *nirvāṇa*.

"O Bhikṣus, you should know that because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom as it has been taught and possesses skillful means, they constantly train in the dharmas that bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to learn, and do not train in the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the Four Great Kings, each leading their own celestial hosts, come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, all saying: ‘Excellent!’”

"O Great Being! You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not study the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Just as the former Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas accepted the four bowls offered by the Four Heavenly Kings, you too shall accept them; and just as the Four World-Protecting Heavenly Kings of old presented those four bowls, I too shall present them to you."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas should train in, we, Śakra and the other devas, each leading our respective celestial hosts, come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying all together: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means and constantly trains in that which the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the devaputras Subhakāla, Sunirmita, Nirmāṇarati, and Vaśavartin each led their own celestial hosts to come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, all saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this way, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimanda), quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means and constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world-system, leading a host of Brahmā deities, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself to learning those dharmas that the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not learn those dharmas that Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you learn in this manner, you will quickly sit upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). I shall then go beneath the Bodhi tree and earnestly entreat you to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma for the benefit and happiness of infinite sentient beings."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the skillful means of profound prajñāpāramitā and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas should train in, the devas of the Ābhāsvara Heaven—extending through the detailed enumeration up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven—each leading their own celestial hosts, come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, all saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the dharmas that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means and constantly train in what the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train in, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, along with the devas, nāgas, asuras, and others, constantly follow, protect, and keep them in mind.”
By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva-mahāsattva cannot be harmed by any of the perils, hardships, or calamities of the world, nor by any physical or mental distress.

All diseases arising from the disharmony of the four great elements—namely, diseases of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and the various limbs and joints—all such four hundred and four types of illnesses shall forever cease to exist within his body, except for those heavy karmic retributions that are transformed and experienced as light.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means as taught, attains such present-life merits, and the merits for future lives will be immeasurable and boundless.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 519. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Third Division, Chapter on Skillful Means, Part Four. At that time, Ānanda had this thought to himself:

"Is it through his own eloquence that Śakra, Lord of the Devas, praises and speaks of such profound merits and benefits of the Prajñāpāramitā, or is it through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata?"
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, knowing the thoughts in Ānanda’s mind, addressed him, saying:
"Venerable One!
All the merits and benefits of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* that I have praised and described are entirely due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata."
At that time, the Buddha said to Ānanda: "So it is! So it is!"

One should know that when Śakra, Lord of the Devas, today praises and speaks of such merits and benefits of this profound Prajñāpāramitā, it is entirely through the spiritual power of the Tathāgata, and not by his own eloquence.

Why is this? Because the meritorious benefits and supreme virtues of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* are certainly beyond the capacity of any in the world—whether devas, humans, or asuras—to praise or describe.

Ānanda, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently studies, contemplates, and practices this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all the evil Māras in this trichiliocosm will give rise to doubt and uncertainty, thinking to themselves:

"Will this bodhisattva mahāsattva realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and thus regress to abide in the fruit of a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; or will he proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings?"

"Furthermore, Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from such profound prajñāpāramitā, all evil Māras give rise to great sorrow and suffering, their bodies and minds trembling as if pierced by poisoned arrows."
Furthermore, Ānanda!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, various evil Māras come to where he is and manifest all manner of terrifying things—namely, swords and blades, ferocious beasts, venomous snakes, and blazing fires erupting from all four directions—with the intent to cause the bodhisattva’s body and mind to be struck with alarm and fear, to lose the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and to cause his mind regarding his practice to become despondent, even to the point of giving rise to a single thought of distraction, thereby obstructing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete *bodhi*. This is the deep-seated wish of those evil Māras.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, are they all disturbed and distracted by Māra, or are there some who are disturbed and some who are not?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"It is not the case that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the profound perfection of wisdom are disturbed and distracted by Māra; rather, some are so disturbed while others are not."
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Which bodhisattva mahāsattvas, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, are disturbed and distracted by evil māras?”
“What kind of bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be disturbed by Māra?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, did not believe or understand it but instead disparaged and slandered it, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will be disturbed by Māra.”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, has believed in, understood, and praised it without giving rise to slander, then when that bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or confused by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom in a previous life, feels doubt and hesitation, thinking:
'Does it exist?'"
"Is it non-existent? Is it real or unreal?
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, has no doubt or hesitation at all in their mind and is certain that it truly exists, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or confused by Māra.

"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva distances himself from virtuous friends and is taken hold of by evil friends, he will not hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because he does not hear it, he cannot comprehend it; because he does not comprehend it, he cannot practice it; because he does not practice it, he cannot inquire about it; because he does not inquire about it, he does not act according to what has been taught; and because he does not act according to what has been taught, he cannot realize the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is then disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva associates with virtuous friends and is not influenced by evil friends, they will hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they hear it, they are able to understand it; because they understand it, they are able to practice it; because they practice it, they are able to inquire about it; because they inquire about it, they are able to act according to the teaching; and because they act according to the teaching, they are able to realize the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra, the Evil One.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva distances himself from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and instead embraces and praises what is not the true, sublime Dharma, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom and neither adopts nor praises that which is not the true, sublime Dharma, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they will not be disturbed or confused by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), disparages and slanders the sublime and true Dharma."
At that time, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:

"Now this bodhisattva is my ally; because he slanders the sublime and true Dharma, there will be immeasurable sons of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva Vehicle who will likewise give rise to slander against the sublime and true Dharma. By this cause and condition, my wish shall be fulfilled."

If these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, despite exerting diligent effort in cultivating all wholesome dharmas, should fall into the level of a Śrāvaka or a Pratyekabuddha—and cause others to fall as well—then when these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom, praises and accepts the sublime true Dharma, and likewise causes immeasurable sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva Vehicle to praise and accept the sublime true Dharma, the evil Māra will become sorrowful, anxious, and terrified. Even if these sons of good family in the Bodhisattva Vehicle do not apply themselves with diligence to cultivating wholesome dharmas, they will nonetheless certainly not cause themselves or others to fall back into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha; they will surely realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, he cannot be disturbed or confused by the evil Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, should speak thus:

'This principle of the *prajñāpāramitā* is so profound, so difficult to see and difficult to realize; what is the use of proclaiming, hearing, receiving and upholding, reading and reciting, contemplating, diligently practicing and studying, or copying and disseminating this sūtra?'"
‘Since even I am unable to fathom its source or its depths, how much less so for others of meager merit and shallow wisdom!

At that time, immeasurable sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, hearing these words, were all struck with fear and alarm; they then retreated from the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, falling instead to the level of a Śrāvaka or a Pratyekabuddha. When such Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā, they are thus disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.
If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they speak thus:

"The principle of this *prajñāpāramitā* is so profound that it is difficult to see and difficult to realize; if it were not proclaimed, heard, received, maintained, recited, contemplated, diligently practiced, written down, and circulated, it would be impossible to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

At that time, immeasurable sons of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, having heard what was said, were filled with joy and leaped for gladness. They then constantly delighted in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, mastering thoroughly, reflecting upon according to the principle, diligently practicing, explaining to others, and transcribing and disseminating this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Seeking to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, when practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on his own accumulated merit and roots of goodness, looks down upon other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, saying:
'I am able to practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, whereas you are not.'"
I am able to abide in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, whereas you are not able;
I am able to abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm, whereas you are not able;
I am able to abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, whereas you are not.
"I am able to practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the eight liberations up to the ten totalities, whereas you are not."
I am able to practice the wisdom of the stages from the Ground of Pure Contemplation up to the Ground of the Tathāgata, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the stages from the Ground of Supreme Joy up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, whereas you are not able.
I am able to practice the causes for the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity, whereas you are not.
"I am able to practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), whereas you are not.
I am able to practice calm abiding (*śamatha*) and insight (*vipaśyanā*), whereas you are not."
I am able to contemplate the factors of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order, whereas you are not.
I am able to observe the specific and general characteristics of all phenomena, whereas you are not.
"I am able to bring sentient beings to maturity and adorn and purify Buddha-fields, whereas you are not.
I am able to practice all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, whereas you are not;
I am able to train for the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, whereas you are not."
At that time, the evil Māra rejoiced and leaped for joy, saying:
"This bodhisattva is my companion; he will wander through birth and death with no time of emergence."
"When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra.

However, if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not rely on their own meritorious roots of goodness to disparage other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and though they constantly exert themselves in cultivating all wholesome dharmas, they do not cling to the marks of those wholesome dharmas, then when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra."

"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, relying on his own renowned name and lineage, looks down upon other bodhisattvas who are cultivating wholesome qualities; if he constantly praises his own virtues and disparages the faults of others; if, though actually lacking the practices, marks, and signs of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattva, he claims they truly exist; and if, giving rise to various afflictions, he praises himself and disparages others, saying:
'You all lack the name and lineage of a bodhisattva; I alone possess the name and lineage of a bodhisattva.'"
Because they, out of overweening pride, despise and revile the assembly of other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
at that time Māra the Evil One thinks to himself:
"Now this bodhisattva makes my realm and palaces not empty, but increases the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts."

At that time, Māra assists him with his supernatural power, causing his majesty, influence, and eloquence to increase further. Consequently, many people believe and accept his words; because of this, they are exhorted and incited to share his evil views. Having shared those evil views, they follow his false teachings; having followed those false teachings, their afflictions blaze up.
Because their minds are inverted, all the physical, verbal, and mental karmas they initiate are capable of bringing about undesirable, ruinous, and painful results.

By this cause and condition, the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts increase, causing the palaces and lands of Māra to become filled; because of this, the evil Māra rejoices and leaps for joy, and all that he undertakes proceeds according to his will and at his pleasure. When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are thus disturbed and distracted by the evil Māra.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely on his own false name and lineage to despise other bodhisattvas who cultivate goodness, remains free from overweening pride regarding his merits, never praises himself nor disparages others, and is able to skillfully recognize the deeds of evil māras, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he will not be disturbed or confused by evil māras.
"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva mutually disparages, contends with, or slanders those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the pratyekabuddhas."
At that time, having seen this event, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:
"Now this bodhisattva has distanced himself from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and has drawn near to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts."

Why is this? To mutually disparage, contend, and slander one another is not the path to bodhi; rather, it is the perilous path to the miserable realms of hell, the animal kingdom, and the realm of hungry ghosts.

Having formed this thought, he leaps for joy and exultation, causing the power and influence of this bodhisattva to increase further so that immeasurable people may grow in their evil karma; thus, when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is immediately disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not disparage, revile, or engage in conflict with those seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but instead skillfully guides and transforms them so that they may enter the Mahāyāna, or causes them to diligently cultivate the wholesome dharmas of their own respective vehicles, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva should engage in mutual disparagement, contention, or slander with other sons of good family who seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment..."
At that time, having seen this event, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:
"These two bodhisattvas are both far removed from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; they are both drawing near to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts."
Why is this? Mutual disparagement, contention, and slander are not the path to bodhi; rather, they are the perilous paths leading to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts.

At that time, having formed this thought, Māra the Evil One rejoices and leaps for joy, increasing his own power and causing the two factions to engage in incessant strife; thus, when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is disturbed and distracted by Māra the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not disparage, contend with, or slander those sons of good family who seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, but instead mutually instructs and exhorts them to cultivate all wholesome dharmas, they will swiftly proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; when such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment develops a harmful mind toward those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—engaging in strife, contending, despising, reviling, or slandering them—that bodhisattva mahāsattva shall, for as many moments as such unbeneficial thoughts arise, retrogress from the sublime practices previously cultivated for that many eons; for that long they shall remain far removed from virtuous friends, and for that long they shall again undergo the bonds of birth and death."

If one does not abandon the mind of great enlightenment (*mahābodhicitta*), then for as many eons as were previously donned in armor, one shall diligently cultivate sublime practices without interruption; only then will the lost merits be restored.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Regarding the suffering of the cycle of birth and death resulting from the evil thoughts generated by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, must they necessarily wander through saṃsāra for such a duration, or can they also attain liberation in the interim?"

Regarding the superior practices from which this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has regressed, must they diligently exert themselves for that many kalpas, donning the armor and cultivating all superior practices without interruption, before finally restoring the merits they had lost? Or does the restoration of the original state occur in the interim?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"I have taught for bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas the dharmas for the restoration of virtue through the expiation of offenses.
Ānanda, you should know this!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment should give rise to a mind of malice toward those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—engaging in strife, disparagement, abuse, and slander—and subsequently lack shame and remorse, harboring ill will without relinquishing it, and being unable to confess and repent according to the Dharma, I declare that for such individuals there is no possibility of emerging from their transgression or restoring their virtue in the interim; they must instead wander through birth and death for as many eons as were mentioned, remaining far removed from virtuous friends and bound by manifold sufferings.
If one does not abandon the great bodhicitta, one must don the armor for that many eons and diligently cultivate sublime practices without interruption; only then will the lost merit be restored.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment should harbor a harmful mind toward those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—engaging in strife, disparagement, abuse, or slander—and subsequently feel shame and remorse, such that their minds are no longer bound by evil and they are able to immediately confess and repent according to the Dharma, thinking:
"I have now obtained this human body so difficult to find; how could I allow myself to again give rise to such faults and evils as to lose this great, wholesome benefit?"
"I ought to benefit all sentient beings; how could I allow myself to instead cause them harm?
I ought to revere all sentient beings as a servant serves his master; how could I allow myself to instead give rise to arrogance, insult, or contempt?"
I should endure all beating and reviling from sentient beings; how could I allow myself to retaliate against them with violent or harsh physical or verbal acts?
I should reconcile all sentient beings so that they may respect and love one another; how could I allow myself to further give rise to perverse and evil speech to conflict with them?
I should endure the long-term treading upon me by all sentient beings, as if I were a road or a bridge; how could I possibly respond to them with further insult?

I seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in order to uproot the great suffering of birth and death for sentient beings and enable them to attain ultimate peace and happiness in nirvana; how could I possibly wish to inflict further suffering upon them?

From this day forth until the end of the future, I shall be like one who is dull-witted, mute, deaf, and blind; I shall make no discriminations regarding any sentient beings. Even if my head, feet, arms, and hands were severed, or my eyes plucked out, my ears cut off, my nose sliced away, my tongue cut out, or all the limbs and members of my body were sawn apart, I would never give rise to malice toward those sentient beings.

If I give rise to evil, I shall then fall away from and destroy the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that I have resolved upon; I shall obstruct the omniscience I seek and be unable to benefit and bring peace and happiness to sentient beings.

"Ānanda, you should know that for these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, I say there is also the meaning of emerging from transgressions and restoring their virtue even in the interim; they do not necessarily have to undergo the cycle of birth and death for such a number of kalpas, nor can evil Māras disturb them, as they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Ānanda! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should not engage in discourse with those who seek the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; even if they do engage in discourse, they should not dwell together with them; and even if they dwell together, they should not engage them in the formal determination of doctrinal points."
Why is this? If one were to engage in debate and deliberation with such persons, they might give rise to thoughts of anger and resentment, or cause harsh and abusive speech to emerge.

However, bodhisattvas should not give rise to thoughts of anger or resentment toward sentient beings, nor should they utter harsh or abusive speech; even if their heads, feet, or limbs were to be severed, they should still not give rise to anger or malicious words.
Why is this? All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should form this thought:

"I seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in order to uproot the manifold sufferings of birth and death for sentient beings and enable them to attain ultimate benefit and peace; how could I possibly turn such things into harmful acts toward them?"
"Ānanda, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of anger toward sentient beings and utters harsh and evil words, they will obstruct unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and also destroy the boundless dharmas of bodhisattva practice."
Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment should not harbor anger toward sentient beings, nor should they utter harsh or evil speech.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How should bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell together with other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, when dwelling together with other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, should regard one another as they would the World-Honored One.
Why is this? When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas look at one another, they should form this thought:”
"He is our true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra); he is our companion, traveling with us on the same boat.
In our training, in the precepts, and in the dharmas to be learned—whatever is studied through him, there is no difference whatsoever."
Just as they should train in the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in true thusness up to the inconceivable realm, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—I too should train in them.
Just as they should train in the eight liberations up to the ten totalities, I too should train in them.
Just as they should study the wisdom of the Ground of Pure Contemplation up to the Ground of the Tathāgata, so too should I study it.
Just as they should study the Joyful Ground up to the Cloud of Dharma Ground, so too should I study it.
Just as they should study the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi, so too should I study them.
Just as they should study the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, so too should I study them.
Just as they should train in the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, so too should I train.
Just as he should train in the causes of the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks, so too should I train.
Just as he should train in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), so too should I train.
Again, he thought: "Those bodhisattvas have taught us the path to great enlightenment; they are my true companions and my teachers."
If that bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in distracted attention, having departed from the attention associated with the knowledge of all modes, I shall not train in the same way as he therein.

If those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas remain free from distracted mental engagement and do not depart from mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, I shall always train therein in accordance with them.
"Ānanda, you should know this:
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, the provisions for awakening will be swiftly brought to fulfillment.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are said to train in equality with the assembly of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas."
Chapter 24: Training in Time, Part Three, Chapter Twenty-Four: Training in Time. At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“What is the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas? Why is it called ‘training in equality’ because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train therein?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"From internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, these are the equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in equality. Through this training in equality, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The emptiness of the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;

the emptiness of the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of the sense base of forms up to the sense base of phenomena..."
Emptiness is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of the eye element up to the mind element is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of the form element up to the phenomena element is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and the emptiness of the eye-consciousness element up to the mind-consciousness element is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The nature of equality: the emptiness of eye-contact through to mind-contact is the nature of equality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
the emptiness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition through to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition is the nature of equality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
the emptiness of the earth element through to the consciousness element is the [nature of equality] of the bodhisattva.
The equality of the mahāsattva is the emptiness of the causal conditions up to the dominant conditions;
the emptiness of ignorance up to old age and death is the equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom is the equality of the bodhisattva.
The equality of the Mahāsattva is the emptiness of internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
the equality of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is the emptiness of suchness up to the inconceivable realm;
the equality of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is the emptiness of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
The emptiness of the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path is the equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments is the equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is [the equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva].
This emptiness of the eight liberations up to the ten totalities is the equality of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
this emptiness of the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata is the equality of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
this emptiness of the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the cloud of dharma is the equality of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The equality of the Mahāsattva is the emptiness of the *dhāraṇī* gates and the *samādhi* gates;
the equality of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is the emptiness of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
the equality of the Bodhisattva is the emptiness of the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
The equality of the Mahāsattva is the emptiness of great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
it is the emptiness of the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty secondary signs;
it is the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.

Emptiness is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva;

the emptiness of the fruit of stream-entry up to the awakening of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddhabodhi*) is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; [the emptiness] of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas...
The emptiness of the practices of a bodhisattva and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is the sameness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called "the training in sameness," and through this training in sameness,
they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of form, and so on, up to training for the sake of the exhaustion of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from form, and so on, up to training for the sake of detachment from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of form, and so on, up to training for the sake of the cessation of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of form, and so on, up to training for the sake of the non-arising of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas—
is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

"Regarding what you have asked: 'If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion, detachment, cessation, and non-arising of form, up to and including the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?'"
"Subhūti, what do you think? Is the suchness of form,
up to and including the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, something that is exhausted, detached from, ceased, or abandoned?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The Buddha said to Subhūti:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this way regarding all suchnesses, they are training in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Subhūti, you should know that suchness is inexhaustible, non-separable, non-ceasing, uninterrupted, and cannot be realized as an attainment.”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in this way regarding all suchnesses, they are training in the knowledge of all modes. Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are training in everything from generosity up to wisdom.
Pāramitā, this is training in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature;
this is training in suchness up to the inconceivable realm; this is training in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
this is training in the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; this is training in the four dhyānas and the four immeasurables.
...the four formless absorptions; this is training in the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
this is training in the eight liberations up to the ten totalities; this is training in the wisdom from the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata;
this is training in the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma; this is training in the gateways of dhāraṇī...
The gateways of samādhi; this is training in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

this is training in the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; this is training in great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
this is training in the causes for the thirty-two marks of a Great Being and the eighty secondary signs; this is training in...

The quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity constitute the training in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they constitute the training in all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and they constitute the training in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.

"Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way— in the perfection of generosity up to and including the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas— they are training in the knowledge of all modes."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they reach the ultimate perfection of all training.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, no māras, celestial kings, or any non-Buddhist practitioners can overcome them."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will swiftly reach the stage of the bodhisattva’s non-retrogression.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they practice the sphere of activity of their ancestral fathers, the Tathāgatas.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they unfailingly conform to the Dharma that protects [beings], and they are able to perform the actions appropriate for dispelling darkness.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are well able to bring all sentient beings to maturity and skillfully purify their own buddha-field.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, it is said that they are training well in great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as in the other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma with its three turnings and twelve aspects; they are training to establish hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder and cause them to attain parinirvāṇa.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they train in not severing the lineage of the Tathāgatas; they train in opening the gate of ambrosia for all Buddhas; they train in establishing immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the three vehicles of the Dharma; they train in manifesting the ultimate, quiescent, and truly unconditioned realm for all sentient beings; this is the training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
Those who train in this manner are not capable of being trained by inferior sentient beings.
Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to skillfully deliver all sentient beings from the great suffering of birth and death, they should train in this way.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will certainly not fall into the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of King Yama; they will certainly not be born in border regions, among the Druṇa, or among the Mlecchas; they will certainly not be born into the families of Caṇḍālas, Pukkasa, or any other kind of impoverished, lowly, or unvirtuous families. They will never be blind, deaf, mute, or dumb; nor will they be crippled, lame, or have defective limbs; nor will they be hunchbacked, epileptic, afflicted with abscesses, scabies, leprosy, hemorrhoids, or malignant sores. They will be neither too tall nor too short, nor will they be dark-skinned, and they will be free from all manner of foul and loathsome diseases."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, in every birth they will always obtain a complete retinue; their physical appearance will be dignified and handsome, and their speech will be majestic and authoritative, such that all people love and respect them. In whatever place they are born, they will abstain from taking life up to and including wrong views; they will never embrace false or heterodox teachings, nor will they sustain themselves by means of heterodox teachings. Furthermore, they will not accept those who break the precepts, hold evil views, or slander the Dharma as their friends."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they will never be reborn among the long-lived devas of the heavens who are attached to pleasure and possess limited wisdom."

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*); by virtue of this power of skillful means, although they are able to repeatedly enter the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), they do not undergo rebirth under their influence.

Because they are sustained by the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they achieve such skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) that, although they constantly attain mastery in entering and emerging from all meditative concentrations, they do not, under the influence of those concentrations, take birth in the long-lived heavens (*dīrghāyuṣka-deva*) and thereby neglect the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they attain purity regarding all phenomena.
Because of that purity, they do not fall into the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"If all phenomena are pure by their very nature, how is it that when bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this way, they further attain purity regarding all phenomena?"
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.
All phenomena are by their very nature originally pure.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently trains in the profound *prajñāpāramitā* within this original purity of all phenomena, they skillfully master it through expedient means, such that the mind neither sinks nor is obstructed, remaining far removed from all afflictions and attachments. Therefore, it is said that when a bodhisattva trains in this manner, they further attain purity regarding all phenomena.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Although the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, ordinary beings do not know, see, or realize it.

It is for the sake of causing them to know, see, and realize it that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, and so forth, extensively practicing up to all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they will attain the fulfillment and ultimate purity of the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are able to penetrate to the ultimate further shore regarding the various mental activities of all sentient beings; through skillful means, they cause all sentient beings to know that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, thereby realizing the ultimate coolness of nirvāṇa."
"Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, on the great earth, precious things such as gold and silver are produced in small measure, whereas sand, stones, and rubble are produced in abundance. It is the same with all sentient beings: only a few are able to study the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, while the majority study the dharmas of the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
“Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, among those in the human realm, few are able to cultivate the karma of a wheel-turning monarch, while the majority practice the karma of minor kings; so it is with all sentient beings: few are able to cultivate the path to the knowledge of all modes, while the majority practice the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”
"Subhūti, you should know this:

among the multitudes of bodhisattvas who seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, few attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while many fall to the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha."

Subhūti, you should know that sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, if they do not distance themselves from the profound perfection of wisdom and skillful means, will certainly enter the stage of non-retrogression.
If one is devoid of skillful means regarding the profound perfection of wisdom, they will certainly regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattvas and wish to enter the ranks of those bodhisattvas who are non-retrogressive should diligently practice and study the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way in the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they will never give rise to a mind associated with stinginess, greed, breaking the precepts, anger, indolence, distraction, or wrong views; nor will they give rise to a mind associated with desire, malice, delusion, or pride; nor will they give rise to a mind associated with negligence, error, or other faults; nor will they give rise to a mind associated with attachment to the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness, and so on at length until: they will not give rise to a mind associated with attachment to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas."
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, do not perceive any dharma that can be apprehended.
Because there is nothing to be apprehended, they do not give rise to a mind that clings to the various phenomena associated with form and so forth. "Furthermore, Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way in the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they are able to encompass all perfections, gather all perfections, and lead all perfections."
Why is this? Because within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all *pāramitās* are contained.
Subhūti, you should know this!

Just as the false view of a self-body can universally encompass all sixty-two views, so too is it with the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), which contains and sustains all perfections (pāramitās).

"Subhūti! For example, when those who have passed away their life-faculty ceases, all their sense-faculties likewise cease to function; so it is with the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā): all the perfections that are studied follow along with it. If there were no perfection of wisdom, there would be no other perfections either."
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to reach the ultimate further shore of all pāramitās, they should diligently practice and study the profound prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to diligently practice and study this profound prajñāpāramitā, they are the most supreme and most excellent among all sentient beings."
Why is that? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to diligently practice and study the unsurpassed Dharma.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
"What do you think?
Are the sentient beings within this trichiliocosm many? Subhūti replied:
“The sentient beings within Jambudvīpa alone are already countless; how much more so must the sentient beings in a trichiliocosm be numerous!”
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.
Subhūti, you should know this:

suppose all the sentient beings in a trichiliocosm were to simultaneously attain human bodies; having attained human bodies, they were to simultaneously generate the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, practice the various deeds of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and having completed those practices, they were to simultaneously attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete buddhahood."

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, for as long as their lives last, are able to provide various kinds of supreme and exquisite articles of enjoyment to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
"What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit? Subhūti replied:
“Very many, World-Honored One! Very many!”
"Excellent, Sugata! The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle are able to constantly delight in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, thoroughly mastering, reflecting upon according to principle, practicing in accordance with the teaching, copying, and disseminating this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the merit they obtain will be far greater than the former, immeasurable and incalculable."

Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses great purpose and function, enabling the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

"Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to stand at the head of all sentient beings; wishes to universally benefit all sentient beings; wishes to act as a protector for those without protection, a refuge for those without refuge, a resort for those without a resort, eyes for those without eyes, and light for those without light; wishes to show the correct path to those who have lost it; and wishes to lead those who have not yet attained nirvāṇa to attain it—this bodhisattva should study this profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti, you should know this: if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; wishes to practice the sphere of activity traversed by all Buddhas; wishes to sport in the places where the Buddhas sport; wishes to let out the great lion’s roar of a Tathāgata; wishes to beat the unsurpassed Dharma drum of all Buddhas; wishes to strike the unsurpassed Dharma bell of all Buddhas; wishes to blow the unsurpassed Dharma conch of all Buddhas; wishes to ascend the unsurpassed Dharma throne of all Buddhas; wishes to expound the unsurpassed Dharma meaning of all Buddhas; wishes to resolve the web of doubts of all sentient beings; wishes to enter the nectar-like Dharma realm of all Buddhas; wishes to experience the subtle and wondrous Dharma bliss of all Buddhas; and wishes to realize the perfectly pure merits of a Tathāgata—this bodhisattva should study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and studies this profound perfection of wisdom in this way, there is no merit or root of goodness that they cannot attain."
"Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the locus upon which all kinds of meritorious virtues and roots of goodness depend.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice and study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, can they also attain the merits and roots of goodness of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"The merit and roots of goodness of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, these bodhisattva mahāsattvas are also able to attain; yet, within them, they neither dwell nor cling."
Having observed correctly with superior wisdom and vision, they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and enter the bodhisattva’s state of certainty (*samyaktva-niyāma*).
Therefore, there is no root of virtue or merit whatsoever that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot attain.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they draw near to the knowledge of all modes and will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they become a true field of merit for all the world—including its gods, humans, and asuras—surpassing the fields of merit of all worldly śramaṇas, brahmins, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas, and swiftly attaining the knowledge of all modes."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, wherever they are born, they do not abandon this profound perfection of wisdom, they do not depart from this profound perfection of wisdom, and they constantly practice this profound perfection of wisdom."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in this profound perfection of wisdom, you should know that they have already attained non-retrogression regarding all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), are able to correctly awaken to all phenomena, have distanced themselves from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and are drawing near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they might form such thoughts as:
'This is the perfection of wisdom; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation; I am able to cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom.'"
By means of this profound perfection of wisdom, and by relinquishing those things that ought to be relinquished, I shall certainly realize the knowledge of all modes!
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), nor can they comprehend the perfection of wisdom. Why is this so?"
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not form such thoughts as:

"I am this *prajñāpāramitā*; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation; this is the cultivator; these are the phenomena from which the *prajñāpāramitā* is detached; these are the phenomena illuminated by the *prajñāpāramitā*; and this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by the *prajñāpāramitā*."
"If one knows in this way, that is the practice of the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they form this thought:"

"This is not the perfection of wisdom; this is not the time for its cultivation; this is not the place for its cultivation; this is not the cultivator. It is not by means of the perfection of wisdom that one becomes detached from all dharmas that should be abandoned, nor is it by means of the perfection of wisdom that one is definitively able to realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Why is this so? Because all phenomena abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature—and as extensively explained, even up to the inconceivable realm—and herein, there is no differentiation whatsoever.
"Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom and will swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes."

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 523. Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Chapter 25: Seeing the Immovable. Part Three. Section One of Chapter Twenty-five: Seeing the Immovable. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had this thought to himself:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of generosity—and so forth, as extensively described, up to the knowledge of all aspects—already transcends all sentient beings, how much more so when they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!"
