If sentient beings, upon hearing the name of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), give rise to profound faith and understanding, they will still obtain the excellent benefits of human existence and attain the most supreme lifespan in the world; how much more so for those who resolve their minds toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, or who are able to hear this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)!

If any sentient beings are able to give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and hear this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, all other sentient beings should aspire to rejoice in them; the merit they obtain cannot be equaled by any in the world, including gods, humans, or asuras.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the mind of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed him, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have thought.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, leaped for joy and, taking exquisite celestial *mañjūṣaka* flowers, scattered them over the Tathāgata and the various bodhisattvas.
Having scattered the flowers, they made this aspiration:

"If there are sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle who seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, by the roots of goodness and merit produced by me, may their aspirations be swiftly fulfilled; may they quickly realize the knowledge of all modes; may the unsurpassed Buddha-dharmas they seek be swiftly fulfilled; may the dharmas of self-mastery they seek be swiftly fulfilled; may the true, untainted dharmas they seek be swiftly fulfilled; and may all the teachings they wish to hear be obtained according to their wishes."
"If there are those seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, I shall also cause their aspirations to be swiftly fulfilled.
Having made this vow, he addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If there are sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who have already resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, I shall never give rise to even a single thought of a contrary intention that would cause them to retreat from the mind of great bodhi."

I do not give rise to even a single thought of a contrary intent that would cause these bodhisattvas to become weary of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, or to fall back into the stages of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already developed a deep-seated aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I pray that his mind may increase even further, so that he may swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

May those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having witnessed the various sufferings within birth and death, give rise to various firm and great vows for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others, [vowing]:
"Since I have already crossed over the great ocean of birth and death myself, I shall also diligently cross over those who have not yet crossed."
Since I have already liberated myself from the fetters of birth and death, I shall also diligently strive to liberate those who are not yet liberated.
Since I have already attained peace and security amidst the various terrors of birth and death, I shall also diligently strive to bring peace and security to those who have not yet found it.
"Since I have personally realized ultimate nirvāṇa, I shall also diligently strive to cause those who have not yet realized it to likewise attain it.
"World-Honored One!
If good sons and good daughters, with a profound mind, rejoice in the merit of bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds for enlightenment, how much merit will they obtain?"
If one rejoices with a profound mind in the merit of bodhisattvas who have long since resolved their minds [on enlightenment], how much merit is obtained?
If one rejoices with a profound mind in the merit of bodhisattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, how much merit is obtained?
“If one rejoices with a profound mind in the merits of a Bodhisattva bound to only one more birth, how much merit will they obtain?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
The number of the four great continents may be known, but the measure of the merit produced by the mind of sympathetic joy of these sons and daughters of good family cannot be known.
Kauśika! While the number of small chiliocosms can be known, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sons and daughters of good family who rejoice together cannot be known.

Kauśika! While the number of two-thousandfold world systems may be known, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sons and daughters of good family who rejoice together cannot be known.

Kauśika! The number of two-fold units in this trichiliocosm of my world-system may be known, but the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sons and daughters of good family who rejoice together cannot be known.

Kauśika! Suppose the trichiliocosm were merged into a single ocean; if one were to take a single hair, split it into a hundred parts, and use the tip of one such part to touch the waters of that ocean, the number of drops could be known. However, the measure of the merit produced by the heart of sympathetic joy of these sons and daughters of good family cannot be known.
"Why is this? It is because the merit produced by the mind of sympathetic joy of these sons and daughters of good family is boundless.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If there are sentient beings who do not rejoice in the sublime virtues of the bodhisattvas, you should know that they are all possessed by Māra, bewitched by Māra, partisans of Māra, or those who have passed away from the celestial realm of Māra and been reborn here.

Why is this? If a bodhisattva mahāsattva seeks to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and cultivates the various practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, anyone who gives rise to the thought of deeply rejoicing in those merits will be able to destroy all the palaces, retinues, and armies of Māra.
“World-Honored One!

If there are sentient beings who, with deep hearts, revere and love the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who, wherever they are born, always desire to see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and encounter the Saṅgha, they should deeply rejoice in the roots of goodness and merit of all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
Having thus rejoiced, one should dedicate the merit toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, yet should not give rise to notions of duality or non-duality;
if one can act in this way, one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, benefiting sentient beings and destroying the hosts of Māra.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said,

Kauśika! If sentient beings, with deep resolve, rejoice in the roots of virtue and merit of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, those sentient beings will swiftly fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

If sentient beings, with deep hearts, rejoice in the roots of virtue and merits of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, those sentient beings will possess great power; they will always be able to serve all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and spiritual friends, and will constantly hear the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā, thereby skillfully understanding their meaning and intent.

Sentient beings who have accomplished such roots of merit through the virtue of sympathetic joy and dedication will, in whatever place they are born, always be honored, revered, respected, and praised by all the worlds—gods, humans, asuras, and others; they shall not see unpleasant forms, hear unpleasant sounds, smell unpleasant odors, taste unpleasant flavors, experience unpleasant tactile sensations, or contemplate unwholesome dharmas. They shall never be separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as they travel from one buddha-field to another, drawing near to the Buddhas to plant various roots of goodness, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields.
Why is this? "Kauśika!

These sentient beings are able to rejoice with a profound heart in the roots of merit and virtue of the countless bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds toward awakening for the first time, and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

One is able to deeply rejoice in the roots of merit and wholesome qualities of the immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas who abide in the first through the tenth stages, and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
One is able to deeply rejoice in the roots of merit and virtue of the immeasurable bodhisattvas bound to one more birth, and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
By virtue of these causes and conditions, the roots of goodness of all these sentient beings will increase, and they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Having attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they will be able to truly benefit immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings until the end of the future, establishing them in the realm of nirvana without remainder.

"For this reason, Kauśika, sons of good family and others who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should, with sympathetic joy, rejoice in the roots of merit and virtues of all bodhisattvas who have first resolved upon enlightenment, those who have long since resolved, those who dwell on the stage of non-retrogression, and those who are bound to only one more birth; they should dedicate them all toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

When rejoicing in [the merit of] birth and dedicating it, one should not be attached to rejoicing and dedicating as being identical to the mind or separate from the mind; one should not be attached to practicing as being identical to the mind or separate from the mind.

If one can thus remain without attachment, rejoicing and dedicating [merit] while practicing the various deeds of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and deliver all devas, humans, asuras, and others, causing them to escape birth and death and attain parinirvāṇa.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"As the World-Honored One has taught that all phenomena are like illusions, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of an illusory mind, attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Do you perceive the illusory mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"I do not perceive illusion, nor do I perceive a mind that is like an illusion.
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?"
"If there were no illusion and no mind that is like an illusion, would you see such a mind as being able to attain unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment? Subhūti replied, "No!"
"Blessed One!
I do not see any place where there is neither illusion nor an illusion-like mind, yet there is this mind that can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
In a state that is free from illusion and free from an illusory-like mind, do you perceive any such dharma that is able to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"I do not see any place apart from illusion and the mind that is like an illusion where there is any further dharma capable of attaining unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!
World-Honored One!"
I do not perceive any dharma that is either identical to or distinct from the mind; what dharma, then, could I say exists or does not exist?
This is because all dharmas are ultimately detached.
If all dharmas are ultimately detached, it is impossible to designate that "this dharma exists" or "this dharma does not exist."

If a phenomenon cannot be established as either existent or non-existent, then it cannot be said that one can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; for it is not by means of a non-existent phenomenon that enlightenment is attained.
Why is this so? Because all dharmas are non-existent; their intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended, and they are neither defiled nor pure. Why is this?
Because the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity are all ultimately detached;
because internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature are also ultimately detached;
because true suchness up to the inconceivable realm are also ultimately detached; and because the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are also...
Because they are ultimately detached, the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are also ultimately detached;
because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are also ultimately detached;
and because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are also ultimately detached; [and so on] up to the ten...

Because the spheres of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are also ultimately detached; because the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) up to the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) are also ultimately detached;
because the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi are also ultimately detached;
because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) are also ultimately detached; [and] because the ten powers of a Tathāgata up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha...
Because the Dharma is ultimately detached, and because great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are also ultimately detached;
because the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary characteristics are also ultimately detached;
because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are also ultimately detached; [and] because omniscience...
Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are ultimately detached;
because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas are ultimately detached;
and because the knowledge of all-knowledge is also ultimately detached.
“World-Honored One!

If a dharma is ultimately detached, that dharma should not be cultivated, nor should it be discarded, nor should anything be brought forth by it. Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is ultimately detached, one should not bring forth anything regarding dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

Since the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is ultimately detached, how can it be said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by relying on this profound *prajñāpāramitā*?”
"Bhagavān! The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is also ultimately detached. How can a detached dharma attain a detached dharma?
Therefore, it should be said that the perfection of wisdom cannot be described as attaining unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: “Excellent! Excellent!”
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
From the perfection of wisdom up to the perfection of generosity, all are ultimately detached; as explained at length, even the knowledge of all modes is ultimately detached.
Subhūti, you should know this:

because the perfection of wisdom is ultimately detached, and so on, up to the knowledge of all aspects which is also ultimately detached, it can be said that the bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes the ultimately detached, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.
Subhūti, you should know this:

if the perfection of wisdom were not ultimately detached, it would not be the perfection of wisdom; and so on, in detail, until: if the knowledge of all aspects were not ultimately detached, it would not be the knowledge of all aspects.

Subhūti, you should know that because the perfection of wisdom is ultimately detached, it is called the "perfection of wisdom"; and so on, in detail, until: because the knowledge of all modes is ultimately detached, it is called the "knowledge of all modes."
Therefore, Subhūti, it is not that bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not rely upon the profound perfection of wisdom to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti, you should know that although one cannot attain the state free from phenomena by means of something separate from phenomena, the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment does not occur without relying upon the profound perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should diligently practice and study the profound perfection of wisdom.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The meaning and purpose of the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are exceedingly profound.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"So it is! So it is! The meaning and purpose of the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is exceedingly profound."

Subhūti, you should know that bodhisattva mahāsattvas perform a difficult feat: although they practice such profound meanings and principles, they do not realize the dharmas of the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, the deeds performed by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not difficult; one should not say that they are able to perform a difficult task.”

Why is this? Because the objective meaning realized by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is entirely unapprehendable; the prajñāpāramitā that realizes it is also unapprehendable; and the realization itself, the one who realizes, the place of realization, and the time of realization are likewise unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
Since all dharmas are observed by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas to be unobtainable, what meaning or purpose could there be to be realized?
What Prajñāpāramitā could there be to serve as the means of realization?”
Furthermore, what can be established as the dharma to be realized, the one who realizes it, the place of realization, or the time of realization?
This being so, how can it be maintained that by means of this one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Even unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening cannot be realized, let alone the states of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha!
World-Honored One,
practicing in this manner is called the bodhisattva’s practice of non-apprehension.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice such a practice of non-apprehension, they will attain freedom from all obscuring darkness regarding all phenomena.
World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears these words and their mind does not sink, nor feel regret, nor experience alarm or fear, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
"Blessed One!

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this manner, he does not perceive various signs; he does not perceive 'I am practicing,' nor does he perceive 'not practicing. He does not perceive that the *prajñāpāramitā* is what he practices, nor does he perceive that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening is what he realizes. Furthermore, he does not perceive the place of realization, the time, or any such factors."
“World-Honored One!
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts as:
‘I am far from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.’”
For example, space does not form the thought:
"I am distant from or near to that object. Why is this so?
Because space is immovable, without differentiation, and without conceptual construction, so it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas:
when practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not form the thought, "I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening."
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
It is, for example, like an illusory person who does not form such thoughts:
"The illusionist and the illusory object are near to me; the phenomena that resemble illusions are far from me; and the assembly of followers is both near and far. Why is this so?
Because the conjured person is without conceptual discrimination,
so too it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom;
they do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is without conceptual discrimination regarding all phenomena.
For example, a reflected image does not form this thought:
"Because it appears due to that [object], it is near to me; because it does not appear due to those other factors, they are far from me. Why is this so?

Because the reflected images that appear are devoid of conceptual discrimination, so it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas as well: when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts as, "I am far from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
I am near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without discrimination regarding all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!...”
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* have neither attachment nor aversion.
Why is this? Because within the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and all phenomena, the intrinsic nature of attachment and aversion cannot be apprehended.

Just as all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have neither attachment nor aversion toward any phenomena, so too do Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā have neither attachment nor aversion toward any phenomena.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have severed attachment and aversion within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have forever severed all conceptual constructions and discriminations (*vikalpa*), so too do the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* subdue and sever all conceptual constructions and discriminations.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is without conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena.
Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
It is likewise for bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such a thought as:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena (*dharma*).
It is just as those who are emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not form such a thought:
"I am far from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

Because that which is emanated by the Buddhas is without conceptual discrimination, so it is likewise for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.
Just as when the Buddhas and others wish to perform some task, they manifest an emanation and have that emanation perform that deed, yet the emanated being does not form this thought:
"I am able to carry out such a work."

Why is this? Because those who are emanated have no discrimination regarding the actions they perform; likewise, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* also act with diligent cultivation for the sake of a specific purpose.
Having already trained and studied, although one is able to accomplish the tasks at hand, one does not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding those tasks.
Why is this? Because it is the natural law (*dharmatā*) of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* that it is non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.

Suppose there is a skilled craftsman or his apprentice who, for some purpose, constructs various mechanical devices—whether female or male figures, or elephants, horses, and so forth. Although these mechanical devices perform their respective functions, they possess no discernment whatsoever regarding those activities.

Why is this? Because the nature of mechanical devices is inherently non-conceptual, so it is with Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*: they establish [their activities] for the sake of what must be accomplished.
Once it has been established, although it can accomplish various activities, it remains entirely free from conceptual discrimination therein.
Why is this? Because it is the very nature (*dharmatā*) of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to be non-conceptual regarding all phenomena.
At that time, Śāriputra asked the venerable Subhūti:

"Is it only the perfection of wisdom that does not engage in conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena, or do the perfections such as meditative concentration likewise not engage in conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena?"

Subhūti replied, "It is not only the perfection of wisdom that is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena; the five perfections, such as meditative concentration and the rest, are likewise without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena."
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"Is it only the six perfections that are without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena, or are the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness likewise without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena?
Or are the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind [likewise without conceptual differentiation]?"
To abide in all phenomena without conceptual differentiation; to be without conceptual differentiation regarding the sphere of form up to the sphere of mental phenomena among all phenomena;
to be without conceptual differentiation regarding the eye-element up to the mind-element among all phenomena;
to be without conceptual differentiation regarding the element of form up to the element of mental phenomena among all phenomena; to be without conceptual differentiation regarding the eye...
The element of consciousness up to the element of mental consciousness is also non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena;
eye-contact up to mental-contact is also non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena;
and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition up to the various feelings produced with mental-contact as condition are also non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.
One does not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, from the earth element up to the consciousness element;

one does not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, from the causal condition up to the dominant condition; one does not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, from ignorance up to old age and death;
and one does not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature.
All phenomena are likewise without conceptual differentiation; even as suchness up to the inconceivable realm, they are without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena;
even as the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, they are without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena;
even as the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, they are without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
Being non-conceptual, they are also non-conceptual regarding all phenomena in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
they are also non-conceptual regarding all phenomena in the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and they are also [non-conceptual] regarding all phenomena in the eight liberations up to the ten totalities.
Being non-conceptual, one is without conceptualization regarding all dharmas from the Stage of Pure Observation up to the Stage of the Tathāgata;
being non-conceptual, one is without conceptualization regarding all dharmas from the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma;
being non-conceptual, one is without conceptualization regarding all dharmas concerning the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi. Being...
The five eyes and six supernormal powers are also without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena;
the ten powers of a Tathāgata, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are also without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena;
great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are also without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena; the three [refuges]...
The twelve marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs are also non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena;
the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity are also non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena;
and omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are also non-conceptual with respect to all phenomena.
For the sake of the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, one is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena;
for the sake of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, one is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena;
and for the sake of the conditioned realm or the unconditioned realm, one is likewise without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
"Are they distinguished?

Subhūti replied, "It is not only that the six perfections do not make any distinctions among all phenomena; from form up to the unconditioned realm, there is likewise no distinction among all phenomena."
"Why is this? It is because the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are empty and non-conceptual.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"If all phenomena are entirely without conceptual differentiation, how can there be the distinctions of wandering through the five destinies of saṃsāra?
Furthermore, how can there be the distinctions of the noble stages of stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, and the Tathāgatas?"

Subhūti replied: "Due to the causes and conditions of the afflictions of sentient beings' inversions, they initiate various actions of body, speech, and mind. From these, they experience the maturation of karma rooted in desire; based upon this, the distinctions of the five destinies—hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and devas—are established."
"Furthermore, as to what was asked regarding how there can be distinctions among the noble stages such as the fruit of stream-entry and so forth:

Śāriputra, it is because of non-conceptualization that 'stream-enterer' and the 'fruit of stream-entry' are designated; because of non-conceptualization that 'once-returner' and the 'fruit of once-returning' are designated; because of non-conceptualization that 'non-returner' and the 'fruit of non-returning' are designated; because of non-conceptualization that 'arhat' and the 'fruit of arhatship' are designated; because of non-conceptualization that 'pratyekabuddha' and 'pratyekabuddha-enlightenment' are designated; because of non-conceptualization that 'bodhisattva-mahāsattva' and the 'conduct of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva' are designated; and because of non-conceptualization that 'Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha' and the 'unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of a Buddha' are designated."
“Śāriputra! The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past can be designated as such because they are without conceptualization and have severed conceptualization;
the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the future can be designated as such because they will be without conceptualization and will have severed conceptualization.”

Furthermore, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently existing in the worlds of the ten directions are also established through non-discrimination, for they have severed all discrimination.

Śāriputra! By this cause and condition, you should know that all phenomena are without discrimination, because the non-discriminatory *tathatā*, the *dharmadhātu*, and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), serve as the definitive standard.
Śāriputra! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice this profound perfection of wisdom that is free from conceptual discrimination. Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice such non-conceptualizing, profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will be able to realize the non-conceptual, pure, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and will be able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings throughout the future.
Then, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, do they practice a solid dharma, or do they practice a non-solid dharma?"
Subhūti replied, “When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they practice that which is not a solid dharma; they do not practice that which is a solid dharma.”
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because the perfection of wisdom, up to and including the perfection of generosity, are not solid phenomena. Internally...
Because emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, is not a solid phenomenon;

because suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is not a solid phenomenon; because the noble truth of suffering, up to and including the noble truth of the path, is not a solid phenomenon;
because the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is not a solid phenomenon; [and] the four dhyānas and the four immeasurables...
Because the four formless absorptions (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) are not stable phenomena; because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not stable phenomena;
because the eight liberations up to the ten spheres of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are not stable phenomena;

because the stages from the Ground of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) up to the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) are not stable phenomena; and because the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi [are not stable phenomena].
Because they are not solid phenomena, the five eyes and six supernormal powers are not solid phenomena;

because the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not solid phenomena; because great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not solid phenomena;
[and] because the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary characteristics [are not solid phenomena].
Because they are not solid phenomena, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are not solid phenomena;
because they are not solid phenomena, omniscience, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are not solid phenomena.

Why is this? When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not perceive even the slightest non-solid phenomenon to be found within the *prajñāpāramitā* or up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), let alone perceiving any solid phenomenon to be found!
At that time, immeasurable sons of the gods from the desire realm and the form realm all had this thought:

"If good men and good women are able to resolve upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and practice according to the meaning as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, neither realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) nor falling into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas—for these reasons, these good men and good women are most rare and perform what is difficult; they should be paid homage."
At that time, Subhūti, knowing what the sons of the gods were thinking, addressed them, saying:

"That these sons of good family and daughters of good family do not realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), and do not fall into the level of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, is not particularly rare, nor is it yet considered difficult."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, knowing that all phenomena and all sentient beings are unapprehendable, yet gives rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, dons the armor of diligence, and vows to deliver immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to enter the realm of nirvana without remainder—this bodhisattva mahāsattva is truly most rare and is able to perform what is difficult to do.
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Although a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that sentient beings do not exist at all, they nevertheless resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and don the armor of diligence out of a desire to discipline the multitudes of sentient beings—just as if one were desiring to discipline empty space.”
Why is this? O sons of the gods!
Because space is detached, you should know that all sentient beings are likewise detached.
Because space is empty, one should know that all sentient beings are also empty;
because space is not solid or substantial, one should know that all sentient beings are also not solid or substantial;
because space is non-existent, one should know that all sentient beings are also non-existent.
For this reason, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are truly most rare and are able to perform what is difficult to do.
"O Son of Heaven, you should know!

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas don the armor of great vows because they wish to subdue all sentient beings; yet, since no such sentient beings exist at all, it is as if they were donning armor to battle with space."
“O Son of Heaven, you should know!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the great vow out of a desire to benefit all sentient beings; yet both those sentient beings and the armor of the great vow are ultimately ungraspable.”
Why is this? O sons of the gods!
Because sentient beings are detached, you should know that this great armor of the vow is likewise detached.
Because sentient beings are empty, one should know that this armor of the great vow is also empty;
because sentient beings are not solid or substantial, one should know that this armor of the great vow is also not solid or substantial;
because sentient beings do not exist, one should know that this armor of the great vow also does not exist.
“O Son of Heaven, you should know!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s activity of taming and benefiting all sentient beings is also unapprehendable. Why is this?
O sons of the gods!
Because sentient beings are detached, you should know that this act of taming and benefiting is also detached;
because sentient beings are empty, you should know that this act of taming and benefiting is also empty.
Because sentient beings are not solid and real, one should know that this work of taming and benefiting them is also not solid and real;
because sentient beings do not exist, one should know that this work of taming and benefiting them also does not exist.
"O Son of Heaven, you should know that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas likewise do not exist. Why is this?
O sons of the gods!
Because sentient beings are detached, you should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also detached;
because sentient beings are empty, you should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also empty.
Because sentient beings are not solid and real, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should know that they, too, are not solid and real;
because sentient beings do not exist, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should know that they, too, do not exist.
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such words, does not become despondent, is not startled, is not terrified, and feels no anxiety or regret, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? O sons of the gods!
Because the aggregate of form up to the aggregate of consciousness are detached, sentient beings are also detached; because the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind are detached...
Therefore, sentient beings are also detached; because the sense-base of form up to the sense-base of phenomena are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the eye-element up to the mind-element are detached, sentient beings are also detached; because the form-element up to the phenomenon-element are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the eye-consciousness-element up to the mind-consciousness-element are detached, sentient beings are also detached.
Because eye-contact up to mind-contact is detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the earth element up to the consciousness element is detached, sentient beings are also detached; and because the causal conditions up to the dominant conditions are detached.
Sentient beings are also detached, because they are detached from ignorance up to old age and death;
sentient beings are also detached, because they are detached from the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom;
sentient beings are also detached, because they are detached from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; [sentient beings are also detached] from suchness up to...
Because the realm of thought is detached, sentient beings are also detached; because the Noble Truth of Suffering up to the Noble Truth of the Path are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the Noble Path are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are detached, sentient beings are also detached.
Because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are detached, sentient beings are also detached;

because the eight liberations up to the ten totalities are detached, sentient beings are also detached; because the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
and because the stage of extreme joy up to the stage of the cloud of dharma are detached, sentient beings are also detached.

Because the *dhāraṇī* gates and the *samādhi* gates are detached, sentient beings are also detached; because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the Tathāgata’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
[because] great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and...
Because renunciation is detached, sentient beings are also detached; because the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are detached, sentient beings are also detached.
Because the fruit of stream-entry up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is detached, sentient beings are also detached;
because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas are detached, sentient beings are also detached;
and because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is detached, sentient beings are also detached.
"O Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the aggregate of form is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; and so on, up to: because the aggregate of consciousness is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length: because the aggregate of form is detached, even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is detached; and so on, up to: because the aggregate of consciousness is detached, even the knowledge of all modes is detached."
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the eye-base is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; and so on, up to: because the mind-base is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the eye-base is detached, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñājñāna*) is also detached; and so on, up to: because the mind-base is detached, the knowledge of all aspects is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) are also detached; and so on, up to: because the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) is detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length: because the sphere of form is detached, even the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is detached; and so on, up to: because the sphere of phenomena is detached, even the knowledge of all modes is detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the eye-element is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; and so on, up to: because the mind-element is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length: because the eye-element is detached, even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is detached; and so on, up to: because the mind-element is detached, even the knowledge of all modes is detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*) are also detached; up to and including because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak in detail, up to and including because the realm of form is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is also detached; up to and including because the realm of phenomena is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the eye-consciousness element is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; up to and including because the mind-consciousness element is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because the eye-consciousness element is detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is also detached; up to and including because the mind-consciousness element is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“O Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because eye-contact is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; and so on, up to: because mind-contact is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak extensively: because eye-contact is detached, even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is detached; and so on, up to: because mind-contact is detached, even the knowledge of all modes is detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; up to and including because the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is also detached; up to and including because the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the earth element is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; up to and including because the consciousness element is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak extensively, up to and including because the earth element is detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is also detached; up to and including because the consciousness element is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
"O Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because causes and conditions are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; even up to: because dominant conditions are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak extensively: because causes and conditions are detached, even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is detached; even up to: because dominant conditions are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached."
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because ignorance is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; up to and including because old age and death are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because ignorance is detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is also detached; up to and including because old age and death are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) is detached, the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*) is also detached; and so on, up to: because the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is detached, the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is also detached. To speak extensively, up to: because the perfection of giving is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is also detached; and so on, up to: because the perfection of wisdom is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because inner emptiness is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; up to and including because the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because inner emptiness is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is also detached; up to and including because the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because *tathatā* (suchness) is detached, the six *pāramitās* are also detached; up to and including because the inconceivable realm is detached, the six *pāramitās* are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because *tathatā* is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is also detached; up to and including because the inconceivable realm is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”

“Son of Heaven, you should know this! Because the noble truth of suffering is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the noble truth of suffering is detached, even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is detached; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are detached, even the knowledge of all modes is detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are detached, the six perfections are also detached; and so on, up to: because the eight branches of the noble path are detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length: because the four foundations of mindfulness are detached, even the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is detached; and so on, up to: because the eight branches of the noble path are detached, even the knowledge of all modes is detached.”

“Son of Heaven, you should know! Because the four dhyānas are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the four dhyānas are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is also detached; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”

"O Son of Heaven, you should know this! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the gate of liberation of emptiness is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is also detached; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached."
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the eight liberations are detached, the six perfections are also detached; even up to the point that because the ten spheres of totality are detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak extensively, up to the point that because the eight liberations are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is also detached; even up to the point that because the ten spheres of totality are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the Stage of Pure Observation (*śuddhādhyāśaya-bhūmi*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) are also detached; up to and including because the Stage of the Tathāgata is detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because the Stage of Pure Observation is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is also detached; up to and including because the Stage of the Tathāgata is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the Ground of Extreme Joy is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; and so on, up to: because the Ground of Dharma Clouds is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the Ground of Extreme Joy is detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is also detached; and so on, up to: because the Ground of Dharma Clouds is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the gateways of dhāraṇī are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the gateways of samādhi are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the gateways of dhāraṇī are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is also detached; because the gateways of samādhi are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”

“O Son of Heaven, you should know! Because the five eyes are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the six superknowledges are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the five eyes are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is also detached; because the six superknowledges are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because the ten powers of the Tathāgata are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; up to and including because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak extensively, up to and including because the ten powers of the Tathāgata are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is also detached; up to and including because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*) are also detached; because great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), and great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) are detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because great loving-kindness is detached, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is also detached; because great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the thirty-two marks of a great man are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the eighty minor marks are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including: because the thirty-two marks of a great man are detached, even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is detached.”
Because the eighty minor marks are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is also detached.
"Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is detached, the six perfections (ṣaṭpāramitā) are also detached; because the nature of constant equanimity is detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because the quality of non-forgetfulness is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached; because the nature of constant equanimity is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached."
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) are also detached; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because all-knowledge is detached, the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is also detached; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are detached, the knowledge of all-knowledge is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) are also detached; up to and including because the awakening of a solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddha-bodhi*) is detached, the six perfections are also detached. To speak at length, up to and including because the fruit of stream-entry is detached, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñatā*) is also detached; up to and including because the awakening of a solitary buddha is detached, the knowledge of all aspects is also detached.”

“Son of Heaven, you should know! Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are detached, the six pāramitās are also detached; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is detached, the six pāramitās are also detached. To speak at length, up to: because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are detached, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is also detached; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is detached, the knowledge of all modes is also detached.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Because omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) is detached, the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*) are also detached; and so on, in detail, up to: because omniscience is detached, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi*) of all Buddhas is also detached.”
“O Son of Heaven, you should know this!

If, when hearing it said that there are no phenomena whatsoever that are not devoid [of intrinsic nature], the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, not distressed, does not regret, and neither sinks nor desponds, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, the Blessed One addressed Subhūti, saying:
"For what reason and by what causal condition do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas not become despondent in their hearts regarding the profound perfection of wisdom?"
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Because all dharmas are non-existent, because they are all detached, because they are all quiescent, because they are non-existent, because they are without arising or ceasing, and because they are without intrinsic nature or characteristics, the minds of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas do not sink in despair regarding this profound Prajñāpāramitā.”
“World-Honored One!
By means of such various causes and conditions as these, the minds of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not sink in despair regarding the profound perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Because for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, that which might sink, that which is sunk, the place where one sinks, the time of sinking, and the one who sinks by virtue of this sinking—all these are unapprehendable, because all dharmas are unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this teaching, does not become despondent, nor is startled or terrified, nor feels sorrow or regret, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all phenomena are unapprehendable; it cannot be designated that "this is the sinking," "this is what sinks," "this is the place of sinking," "this is the time of sinking," or "this is the one who sinks by means of this sinking."
For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear such matters, their minds do not sink, nor are they terrified; they feel no sorrow and have no regret.

"Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this manner, Śakra, the lord of the devas, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the World, and others will constantly together pay him homage, make offerings, revere, respect, and praise him."
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this way, they will not only be constantly honored, worshipped, revered, respected, and praised by Śakra, the Great Brahmā King, the Lord of the World, and others."

Furthermore, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is constantly saluted, honored, revered, respected, and praised by those who have transcended these realms—the Ābhāsvara devas, the Śubhakṛtsna devas, the Bṛhatphala devas, the Śuddhāvāsa devas, as well as other devas, nāgas, asuras, and so forth.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they are also constantly protected and remembered by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as by the assemblies of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, throughout the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions.

Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will swiftly bring to fulfillment the perfections from generosity up to wisdom; as has been explained at length, they will even swiftly bring to fulfillment all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).

"Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will always be protected and remembered by all buddhas, as well as by bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, asuras, and others; they will swiftly be able to fulfill all meritorious qualities."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva should know the sphere of practice appropriate for a Buddha, and by correctly practicing the conduct of a Buddha, shall swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, becoming no different from a Buddha, the World-Honored One, in what ought to be known.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 521. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part Three: Chapter Twenty-five, "Seeing the Immovable," Section Two. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

The mind of this bodhisattva mahāsattva is as firm and solid as a diamond. Even if all sentient beings in as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges were to be transformed into Māras, and each of these Māras were further transformed into as many evil Māras as there are grains of sand in the Ganges—each of these evil Māras possessing immeasurable and incalculable supernormal powers—even with all their supernatural might, these evil Māras could not obstruct this bodhisattva mahāsattva or prevent him from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already attained the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and know that all phenomena are unapprehendable.

"Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes two dharmas, no evil Māras will be able to obstruct them, nor cause them to be unable to practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
What are these two?
First, observing that all phenomena are empty;
second, not abandoning any class of sentient beings.

"Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes two dharmas, no evil Māras will be able to create obstacles or prevent them from practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). What are these two? "
First, they are able to accomplish everything exactly as spoken.
Second, they are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in this way, the sons of the gods will constantly come to pay homage, draw near to offer worship, inquire, and exhort them, saying:
"Excellent! [Well done!]"
"O Mahāsattva!
One who wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should diligently abide in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is this?

"Noble son! If one diligently abides in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one can act as a protector for all sentient beings who have no protector; act as a refuge for those who have no refuge; act as a savior for those who have no savior; act as a destination for those who have no destination; act as a dwelling for those who have no dwelling; act as an island for those who have no island; provide light to those in darkness; and provide eyes and ears to those who are deaf and blind."
Why is this? Son of good family!

To dwell thus in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness is itself to abide securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; if one can abide securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can abide in such a manner within the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), then the Buddhas currently residing in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions will, amidst their great assemblies, spontaneously rejoice and proclaim the name, clan, and various merits of that bodhisattva mahāsattva—namely, the truly pure merits of abiding in the profound perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti, you should know this:

Just as I now proclaim the profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the assembly, I spontaneously rejoice and extol the names, lineages, and various merits of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Ratnaketu and Śikhin, as well as other Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who currently dwell in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha, purifying their brahma-conduct and abiding in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. These are the truly pure merits of those who abide securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

At present, in all the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the eastern direction, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas are proclaiming the profound Prajñāpāramitā for the sake of the assembly. Therein, too, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the pure conduct of brahmacarya without departing from the Prajñāpāramitā; those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas each, amidst their assemblies, spontaneously rejoice in and extol the names, lineages, and various merits of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—namely, their truly pure merit of not departing from the profound Prajñāpāramitā.
It is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.

"Subhūti, you should know that there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first production of the thought of enlightenment, practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, gradually perfecting the path to great awakening and gradually perfecting the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, until they attain all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). Furthermore, for these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions, amidst the great assemblies, spontaneously rejoice and proclaim their names, clans, and various merits—namely, the truly pure merits of practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."

"Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to perform what is difficult to do: they do not sever the lineage of the Buddhas, and they bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Which bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those whose names, lineages, and various merits the Buddha, the World-Honored One, spontaneously rejoices in and extols amidst the great assembly—those who are non-retrogressive or those who are retrogressive?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, abiding in the irreversible stage and practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, have their names, clans, and various merits spontaneously praised and extolled by the Buddha, the World-Honored One, in the midst of the great assembly."

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have not yet received a prediction [of enlightenment], practice the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, and are likewise honored by all Buddhas, who amidst the great assembly spontaneously rejoice and praise their names, lineages, and various merits.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha again, saying,
“What kind of bodhisattva is this that has been described?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, training by following the example of what was practiced when Akṣobhya was a bodhisattva, have already attained abiding in the stage of non-retrogression; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the natural joy of being praised and extolled by name, clan, and all their virtues by the Buddha, the World-Honored One, in the midst of the great assembly.”

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who train by following the practices cultivated by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as Ratnaketu and Śikhin; although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet received their prediction, they apply themselves with diligent vigor and practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* with skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), whereby they are also graced by the Buddhas, who, amidst the great assemblies, spontaneously express joy and proclaim the praise of their names, clans, and various merits.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; although they have deep faith and understanding regarding the non-arising nature of all phenomena,
they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) within this profound perfection of wisdom."
Although they have deep faith and understanding in the pāramitās, they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas;
although they have deep faith and understanding in the ultimate emptiness of all dharmas, they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas;
although they have deep faith and understanding in the quiescent nature of all dharmas, they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas. Regarding...

Although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are by nature detached, they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*);
although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are non-existent in nature, they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
although they have deep faith and understanding that all phenomena lack self-mastery, they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena.

"Endurance (kṣānti): although one has deep faith and understanding regarding the lack of solidity in all phenomena, one has not yet realized the endurance of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti). Subhūti!"
These and other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas likewise received the natural joy of the Buddhas as they proclaimed and praised their names, clans, and various merits amidst the great assemblies.

“Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva is spontaneously praised and extolled by name, lineage, and various merits by the Buddha, the World-Honored One, in the midst of the great assembly, that bodhisattva mahāsattva has transcended the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
"Subhūti, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom with skillful means, and the Buddha, the World-Honored One, spontaneously rejoices in and praises his name, clan, and various merits amidst the great assembly, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will certainly abide in the stage of non-retrogression; having abided in this stage, he will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the exposition of the meaning and purport of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, has no doubt, no confusion, is not deluded, and does not become despondent, but instead thinks:
'As the Buddha has taught this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, its principle is necessarily such that it is without inversion.'"

"Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has developed profound pure faith in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they will gradually hear the perfection of wisdom extensively from the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha and various bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and will develop deep faith and understanding regarding its meaning and intent."
Having gained faith and understanding, they shall abide in the stage of non-retrogression; having abided in this stage, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, merely by hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, can give rise to faith and understanding without engaging in disparagement, they will still acquire a great abundance of superior roots of goodness; how much more so if they can receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it, contemplate it with mindfulness according to the principle of *tathatā*, and dwell in *tathatā* while diligently practicing and training!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva shall swiftly abide in the stage of non-retrogression and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings throughout the future.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Since the true nature of all phenomena is entirely unapprehendable, how can it be said that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by dwelling in suchness and practicing with diligent application, will swiftly abide in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and be able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings until the end of the future?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“Just as a transformation being created by a Buddha abides in suchness and practices the various bodhisattva-mahāsattva deeds, they shall swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby performing great benefit for all sentient beings.”

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise thus: dwelling securely in suchness while practicing the various bodhisattva-mahāsattva deeds, they shall swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby performing great benefit for all sentient beings.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"That which is emanated by the Tathāgata is entirely non-existent; since phenomena are ultimately unattainable apart from suchness, who is it that abides in suchness to cultivate the bodhisattva practice?"
Who will abide on the stage of non-retrogression?
Who will realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Who will bring great benefit to sentient beings?

"Bhagavān! Since even suchness cannot be apprehended, how much less could there be one who abides in suchness to practice the bodhisattva path, who would swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and bring great benefit to all sentient beings?"
"If this were truly existent, such a thing would be impossible.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "It is so!"
"It is so! It is as you have said.

That which is emanated by the Tathāgata is entirely non-existent; since dharmas are ultimately unattainable apart from true suchness (tathatā), who could abide in true suchness to cultivate the bodhisattva practice?"
Who will abide on the stage of non-retrogression?
Who will realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Who will bring great benefit to sentient beings?

"Subhūti! Since even suchness cannot be apprehended, how much less can there be one who, abiding in suchness, practices the bodhisattva path, swiftly dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, rapidly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and brings great benefit to all sentient beings?"
If this were truly existent, it would be impossible.

Why is that? Whether a Tathāgata appears in the world or does not appear, all phenomena are by their very nature (*dharmatā*) inseparable from True Suchness (*tathatā*), the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the Dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).
